author: mbombeck
body:
Two loose ends between what the app says and what it does.

**The health score a model reads.** The wellbeing pillar is scored from the mental-health questionnaires alone, and the Mental wellbeing page says those never reach an AI feature. The day read the Coach and the MCP endpoint share (`get_day`) carried the stored composite with that pillar inside, and the arrival line sent the live composite. One module, `analytics/score/model-bound.ts`, now decides the score that may leave:

- `readDayForTool` loads the day with `modelBound`, and `readDayScores` recomposes every stored day (and so the usual range) from the other counted pillars. A day scored on wellbeing alone has no score for a model.
- The arrival line holds the live composite but not its pillars, so it leaves the score out when wellbeing counted in it.
- The excluded pillar sits in the one list in `ai/model-bound-data.ts`, beside the questionnaire section and score types.

`privacy-promise-guard.test.ts` scans the English bundle for every sentence that promises some data stays away from the Coach, the briefings or another AI feature (eight today) and binds each to the rule that keeps it: `isModelVisibleSection`, the model-bound score, the Coach exclusion map, the lookback floor, a structural check that no model path reads a workout route, and the named tests that exercise the life-circumstance switches. It also freezes the readers of the stored score. Broken once on purpose (empty pillar list, `modelBound: false`): four cases went red.

**The emergency card.** It had one edit link, to the emergency details. On the owner's card every line now opens the surface that owns it: allergies and the emergency details in the medical history, a chronic condition on `/illness/{id}`, a medication on `/medications/{id}`, name and birth date in the account settings; an empty item opens the place to fill it in, and a surface whose module is off is not linked. `GET /api/emergency-card` carries `targets` beside the card (additive, OpenAPI regenerated); the read-only link, the offline copy and the wallet card never do, which a test and the integration run check. The illness page shows the chronic-conditions note from the medical history beside the episodes, with a link to where it is edited.

The branch merges `origin/main` first, because the guard binds the questionnaire sentence and the exclusion list that #1508 brought to `main`; no file of that sync is deleted or reverted here. With main's prototype-key guard beside the release's session lifetime settings, `session-lifetime.ts` read a setting's name as a plain key on the environment object; it now goes through `ownValue` like every other open-text key.

Tests: `privacy-promise-guard`, `rows`, `emergency-card-sheet`, `conditions-note-card`; integration `day-view` (new case: the model gets 83 where the person sees 57, and no score for a wellbeing-only day) and `emergency-card` (targets for the owner, no ids in the link read).

author: hebilicious
body:
Adds `benchmarks/`, a Moon project, and the workflow `benchmark.yml`. They measure what a reader sees on a docs site built with vaporpress, VitePress 2, Astro Starlight and Nuxt Docus. This pull request is the top layer of the vaporpress stack (#224, #227, #230, #232, #233, #234), so it measures the site with the whole stack.

## What it does

- **fixture**: one Markdown fixture of ten pages (`benchmarks/fixture/`): a home page with one image, headings, highlighted code, a table, tabs, and long and short pages. `src/prepare.ts` writes the pages of each framework from it. Each app uses the standard docs setup of its framework:
  - vaporpress, with a layout that has each feature of the three themes (the feature table of `benchmarks/README.md`), and a search on the index and the engine of vaporpress;
  - VitePress 2.0.0-alpha.21 with the default theme and local search;
  - Astro 7.4.10 with Starlight 0.42.10 and Pagefind;
  - Nuxt 4.6.4 with Docus 5.15.0 (Nuxt Content 3, with the SQLite of Node, Nuxt UI), from `nuxt generate`.
- **site**: the homepage, the quick start and the catalog page of the AcidCat site in three builds: vaporpress (`moon run site:build` on this stack), VitePress (`main`), and Astro (`fe26e301`). No Nuxt build of the AcidCat site exists.
- One `build` job builds all seven sites. Then 2 suites × 3 jobs on separate runners measure them, with 5 runs each, in a turning order. One Brotli static server serves every site. Lighthouse 13.6.0 measures first visits on mobile. Playwright probes measure in Chromium, with no request interception: when a tab responds, when the search button responds, tab switch, search open, cold and prefetched page change, and Back. The `summary` job pools the samples into median (first–third quartile) tables.
- `benchmarks/README.md` tells what each measure means for a reader, how to run the benchmark, and how it stays fair.


## Results

The tables below pool two runs of the workflow on commit `26dd7a2f`, 3 jobs each for each suite: [45608982279](https://github.com/Hebilicious/acidcat/actions/runs/45608982279) and [45608969254](https://github.com/Hebilicious/acidcat/actions/runs/45608969254). Their artifacts keep the raw results. The head `77f68b4b` adds only the README text to `26dd7a2f`.

Where vaporpress is not the best:

- **Script weight, in every first visit.** On the fixture, vaporpress transfers 43.7–44.3 kB of script (123–124 kB decoded), and Starlight 26.9–28.2 kB (106–108 kB). On the AcidCat site, vaporpress transfers 57.0–62.0 kB (159–166 kB decoded), VitePress 49.4–58.8 kB, and Astro 16.7–29.1 kB.
- **Total transfer and requests on the AcidCat site.** On all three routes, vaporpress transfers the most and makes the most requests: the homepage 370.9 kB and 34 requests (VitePress 359.6 kB and 25, Astro 294.9 kB and 21), the quick start 302.3 kB and 31 (281.6 and 21, 254.1 and 19), the catalog 296.3 kB and 31 (275.7 and 21, 246.3 and 19). On the fixture homepage, vaporpress transfers 54.2 kB and Starlight 51.6 kB.
- **The simulated first paint of the homepage of the AcidCat site**: FCP and Speed Index 1,721 ms, against 786 and 796 ms for Astro and 1,163 ms for VitePress; LCP 3,159 ms against 2,711 ms for Astro and 3,009 ms for VitePress. The observed values of the same runs are the best of the three: first paint 107 ms, against 144 ms for Astro and 155 ms for VitePress. The quick start and the catalog have a simulated Speed Index of 970 and 1,000 ms, against 796 and 797 ms for Astro.
- **The observed first paint and largest paint of the catalog page**: both 87 ms, against 71 ms for VitePress. On the fixture, Starlight paints first on each page (39–47 ms, against 48–54 ms for vaporpress), with overlapping spreads.
- **Search.** From the press to the search field on screen, vaporpress takes 204 ms on the fixture and 86 ms on the AcidCat site, Starlight 50 ms and Astro 68 ms, whose dialog is in the HTML. From the start of the navigation, the search button of the AcidCat site responds after 2,406 ms on vaporpress, 2,326 ms on VitePress and 1,679 ms on Astro.
- **Tab switch on the AcidCat site**: 51 ms, against 35 ms for VitePress.
- **By a few milliseconds of simulation**: the simulated FCP and Speed Index of the fixture homepage (753 ms, Starlight 752 ms), and the simulated FCP and LCP of the quick start (both 798 ms; the FCP of VitePress and Astro is 796 ms, the LCP 796 ms for VitePress and 797 ms for Astro) and of the catalog (799 and 804 ms, VitePress 796 ms).

vaporpress is the best, or tied, on the other rows: the scores, CLS, TBT, the requests of the fixture, the observed largest paint (except on the catalog page), when a tab and the search button respond on the fixture, when a tab responds on the AcidCat site, and the page changes and Back in both suites.

### The same fixture in each framework

6 jobs × 5 runs = 30 samples for each cell: the median, and the first to the third quartile. Lighthouse 13.6.0, Chromium 158.0.8127.18. The best median of each row is in bold.

body:
Sam's ask at S724's checkpoint: gather every M-ID with *adapt* in its title into PEDS M1029 Adaptive Physical Education, then the local courses with *adapt* in theirs, after a quick view to uncheck what does not belong; and keep it reusable by changing its variables. Mock: https://claude.ai/artifact/PzL4Kf7oV49BGaYwF5gh1T.

- `commons_gather.js`: the **Gather** view of Courses and Programs, `#coci-lookup/gather?w=&in=&cs=&ls=&to=`. Words: space = all, comma or *or* = either, minus = leave out, quotes = a phrase; a word matches the start of a word. Look in Title, Description, or both. The common subject, local subject codes and target ride in the address.
- Starting ticks: the target's common subject, and local subject codes that carry courses under it elsewhere. TOP never ticks a row. Each unticked row says why, and those rows sort first.
- Saves: insert-only `kb_curation` rows, `<M-ID> merge_into <target>` and `CN:<control> merge_into <target>`. Standing rows are read first and left alone. An optional title rename. **Take it back** deletes exactly the rows saved. The summary names the units range joined and the saved decisions a merge ends.
- Governance: same table, fields and tab as Assign and Rename (`table:kb_curation`, DR-04), so no new surface. Saved filters, the SLOs and objectives look-in and the add bars come later, each a new write surface.
- Verified on real data in headless Chromium: *adapt* into PEDS M1029 lists 55 common courses (35 ticked) and 254 local courses outside them (133 ticked). `tests/commons_gather.test.js`: 39 checks; two guards mutation-checked. `npm run a11y` not run on the view.

Stacked on #58 (`factory/tester-protocol`) — merge that first, or this one's
`@tester` dispatch points at a role with no protocol.

## Issue

BzPM already watches the production deploy run to a conclusion, then stops.
Nothing connects a green deploy to the agent that would test it.

## What we changed

`factory/pm/PROTOCOL.md` gains two steps and one rule:

- **Step 8** — when the deploy run is green, post `@tester test the release
  <tag>` in `#factory`. The tag is the whole hand-off; Tester works out the
  rest from changelog entries added between tags.
- **Step 9** — read Tester's report.
- BzPM answers Tester's ownership questions (`@bzpm who owns BP-123?`), which
  Tester needs before it may touch a customer organization.
- `@tester` added to the handle list.

## Open decision in this diff

Where a FAIL goes is still marked as a gap: BP or FFHR. #57 established that
bugs found in real-trip investigations go to FFHR rather than BP, and a failed
release test looks like the same class of thing — but this PR does not decide
it, so the gap is visible rather than silently resolved.

author: ssaavedra
body:
## Problem 1: demand missed usage the weekly window does not show

A client's demand was built from weekly-window deltas, so any usage the window does not show counted as nothing, and the client's own accounts looked more spare than they were:

- **Idle gap on a borrowed account:** the first reading after more than 10 minutes (`attributionGap`) put the whole step under "outside CPA", so the borrowing (spare-first) client was not charged for it.
- **Paid extra usage:** the weekly window stays at 100 %, so the delta is 0.
- **API-key accounts:** they have no weekly window.

**Fix:** in a priced hour, a client is charged what its requests cost (`hourBucket.billed`). That is the high end on accounts in its own buckets and the low end when borrowing, the same weighting `split` uses. Hours recorded before pricing keep the delta split × capacity. New `GapUSD` holds the cost of a request whose reading closed an idle gap; it is subtracted from the outside-CPA dollars so that usage is not counted twice.

## Problem 2: flapping readings inflated weekly use (found on the hub)

Concurrent responses arrive out of order, so the weekly reading flaps between neighbouring percentages (0.65 → 0.66 → 0.65 → 0.66). Every upswing was counted as new use. On the hub, Ultra recorded 228 % of a week in a cycle where it had used 71 %, and daiahn recorded 119 % (one hour alone added 83 %). As a result, the learned capacities were about 3× too small: Ultra $691, daiahn $288, and iuvia $63, which came from the prior based on those inflated values.

**Fix:** within one weekly period, the baseline only rises. State saved before this fix has no `monotonic_delta` flag; on load its learned capacities are dropped and learned again, while `Folded` is kept so past hours are not folded twice.

## Expected capped at remaining

A client using $99/h was projected over 4d21h onto an exhausted daiahn as $11.7k expected (spare −$17.5k). `expected` is now capped at what the account has left; the full need stays in the explanation. No lending decision changes, because lending already requires expected < remaining / spare_factor.

## Tests

New tests cover all three demand cases, the flapping readings, dropping capacity from old state on load, and the expected cap. Each one fails on the old code. `go test ./...` passes.

author: ashwinyadav09
body:
## Ticket
Ticket R20.6: Bias correction: complete it properly

## What changed
- **Extended Data Window**: Open-Meteo previous-runs (ECMWF IFS, GFS, ICON), archive precipitation proxy, and IEM ASOS METAR observations downloaded to October 31, 2026 across 12 airport stations. Probed start dates recorded in `model_start_dates.json` (earliest common date with all NWP models: 2024-02-05).
- **Split Structure**: Split established as Train (2024-02-05 to 2025-05-31, 14,835 rows), Validation (2025-06-01 to 2025-10-31, 5,046 rows), 7-day Embargo (2025-11-01 to 2025-11-07), Test (2025-11-08 to 2026-10-31, 11,685 rows across 11 stations; VAPO dropped due to <150 valid days).
- **Archived Prior Results**: Old 2024 split files safely archived under `ml/bias_correction/archive/prior_split_2024/`.
- **Real Distinct Baselines**: Implemented 5 distinct baselines:
  1. Best single raw NWP model (ECMWF IFS, MAE 1.1740°C)
  2. Multi-model ensemble mean (ECMWF + GFS + ICON, MAE 1.1740°C)
  3. Persistence ($T_{obs}(d-1)$, MAE 1.7610°C)
  4. Trailing 30-day mean error correction (MAE 1.1444°C)
  5. Station-DOY Climatology from training years only (MAE 3.3276°C)
- **Unit Tested Baselines**: Added `services/api/tests/unit/test_bias_correction_baselines.py` asserting Climatology and MMM use different AST code paths and produce distinct MAE values.
- **Model Training**: Trained Ridge regression model (MAE 0.8358°C, RMSE 1.1759°C) and LightGBM model (MAE 0.8385°C) on residual delta $\Delta = y_{obs} - T_{mmm}$, plus LightGBM rain classifier. Saved `ridge_model.joblib`, `lgbm_model.joblib`, and `model_artifacts.json`; deleted legacy unprincipled `model_weights.json`.
- **Statistical Evaluation & Gates**: Evaluated on held-out test block (11,685 rows). Per-lead-day and per-station MAE, RMSE, coverage, rain Brier (0.0528), BSS (0.3392), HSS (0.6174). Applied 1,000 paired weekly-block bootstrap iterations against best raw baseline. All lead days (1, 2, 3) demonstrated statistically significant improvement ($ci_{upper} < 0$), setting gate status to ENABLED across all leads.
- **Service Integration**: Connected `ForecastService` to load `model_artifacts.json`, check gate status, and apply calibrated temperature adjustments with p10/p90 uncertainty intervals.
- **Documentation & Model Card**: Updated `ml/bias_correction/reports/MODEL_CARD.md` with full split details, distinct baseline table, bootstrap intervals, and Limitations section.

## Acceptance boxes proved

body:
Hola, valentinchiachio123. Te propongo un power-up nuevo para tu juego. Si te gusta, comentá `/aprobar` en este PR para que se incorpore.

## El porro 🌿
- Es un objeto **verde**, que se agarra como el pucho.
- **Es muy raro:** hay uno solo fijo en el nivel (`datos.json`, en `x: 2560`) y los matones lo sueltan un **3%** de las veces (el pucho, un 25%). No cae del cielo durante los jefes.
- **Da 8 segundos de inmunidad**, tipo la estrella de Mario: el Tirri titila en verde y le sale humo. Aparece un cartel grande: **«EL TIRRI ESTÁ RE LOCO, NO SIENTE NADA»**.

## La contraparte, al azar
Cada vez que se agarra un porro se sortea una de estas tres, y el cartel avisa cuál tocó:
1. **Se viene el bajón:** al terminar el efecto, la energía baja a 1 hasta que el Tirri agarre un pucho o un choripán. Hay un cartel grande al final.
2. **No le pega a nada:** mientras dura, los tiros del Tirri salen para cualquier lado.
3. **El Papa no aprueba:** mientras dura, el Papa no dispara ni lo sigue (aparece «!!» sobre su cabeza). Cuando termina, tarda 3 segundos más en volver.

Mientras dura el efecto, abajo a la izquierda aparece un contador con la contraparte que tocó (por ejemplo, «RE LOCO 8s · SIN PUNTERÍA»).

Solo toca `estudiantes/valentinchiachio123/` (`index.html` y `datos.json`). Lo probé con un servidor local: la inmunidad, las tres contrapartes, el fin del bajón con pucho o choripán y el Papa volviendo a disparar.

author: malekaifa
body:
### What

Fix `tools/rebase_verify.py` when upstream independently adds a line that the branch also added before rebasing.

The verifier compared the old branch's added-line multiset directly with the rebased branch. A correct rebase can drop a branch-added line because the new base now supplies it; the old verifier then falsely reported that line as missing. Conversely, if the rebase keeps an extra duplicate copy of that upstream-supplied line, the old comparison can miss it.

The verifier now subtracts net upstream additions from the branch's expected added lines before comparing with the rebased branch. Existing upstream-delete handling is preserved.

### Tested

- Windows, machine `main`, Python 3.12.
- Negative control on current `main` `fc54d18d8d107ec268840e7dcc6dff336c7f118d` with only the two new tests copied in:
  - a correct rebase where upstream supplies the shared line fails with `f.txt: an added line is missing (1x): shared`;
  - an incorrect rebase with an extra duplicate `shared` line produces no problem and fails the new assertion.
- Fixed head `8de9f52be58cf785d103556ed91c9e264e9386f7`: `python tools/tests/test_rebase_verify.py` passes all 64 tests.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main --head HEAD`: passed.

author: tenfajnybartek
body:
## Summary

Closes #2761

This PR improves the reliability, thread safety and consistency of FunnyGuilds' core systems, focusing on data persistence, entity lifecycle management, guild operations and territory transitions.

The primary goal is to prevent data loss, inconsistent entity states and race conditions while preserving compatibility with existing SQL and YAML data formats.

## Changes

### Data persistence

- Replace simple dirty flags with version-based entity change tracking.
- Introduce immutable persistence snapshots.
- Acknowledge entity changes only after a successful storage operation.
- Preserve pending changes when SQL or YAML writes fail.
- Preserve modifications made while a persistence operation is in progress.
- Introduce atomic YAML file replacement with a fallback for unsupported file systems.
- Prevent failed YAML reads from silently overwriting existing data.
- Improve SQL statement execution and failure reporting.
- Coordinate autosaves, direct writes, deletions and shutdown persistence.

### Concurrency and thread safety

- Separate persistence I/O synchronization from entity state synchronization.
- Reduce main-thread blocking during guild and region operations.
- Improve synchronization of mutable entity state.
- Protect entity snapshots against concurrent modifications.
- Move guild and region storage cleanup away from the main thread during normal guild deletion.
- Prevent outdated persistence operations from recreating deleted entities.

### Guild and region lifecycle

- Improve guild and region deletion handling.
- Introduce retryable pending deletion operations.
- Preserve existing records until replacement records have been successfully saved during guild renaming.
- Reserve storage keys while rename and deletion operations are pending.
- Prevent conflicting rename operations and unsafe storage key reuse.
- Improve handling of repeated guild renames.
- Report incomplete storage operations during shutdown.

### Guild creation and rollback

- Revalidate guild names before final registration.
- Prevent guild creation from reusing reserved storage names.
- Prevent rollback operations from deleting existing guild data.
- Track whether a guild and its region have actually been registered before performing cleanup.
- Preserve existing payment compensation and terrain restoration behavior.

### Guild ban management

- Make guild ban status checks read-only.
- Introduce explicit ban expiration handling.
- Handle expired guild bans during deserialization.
- Persist ban expiration without unnecessary repeated state changes.
- Correctly clear persisted YAML user ban data.

### Territory transitions

- Introduce the synchronous and cancellable `GuildPreRegionTransitionEvent`.
- Separate transition validation from asynchronous entry and exit notifications.
- Correctly handle vertical movement and cross-world teleportation.
- Prevent notifications for cancelled movement.
- Preserve leave-before-enter ordering when moving between guild territories.
- Preserve notification ordering across consecutive transitions for each player.
- Improve delayed guild heart visibility checks.

### API safety

- Return read-only views of guild member, deputy, ally, enemy and allied PvP collections.
- Introduce defensive copies for mutable location getters.
- Ensure supported entity mutation methods participate in persistence change tracking.
- Introduce result-aware guild rename operations.

### Testing and documentation

- Extend regression coverage for SQL and YAML persistence failures.
- Cover concurrent modifications during persistence.
- Cover guild and region deletion during autosave.
- Cover failed rename operations and storage key conflicts.
- Cover guild creation rollback and existing data protection.
- Cover expired guild bans.
- Cover cancelled, vertical and cross-world territory transitions.
- Cover asynchronous region notification ordering.
- Update Polish and English documentation.

## Compatibility and migration

No SQL schema changes or existing YAML field renames are introduced.

Existing integrations should be aware of the following behavioral changes:

- Guild collection getters now return read-only views. Integrations should use the corresponding entity mutation methods.
- `Guild#getHome()` and `Region#getCenter()` return defensive location copies.
- `GuildRegionEnterEvent` and `GuildRegionLeaveEvent` remain asynchronous notifications. Integrations that need to prevent territory transitions should use `GuildPreRegionTransitionEvent`.

## Expected outcome

- Reduced risk of data loss and inconsistent persistence.
- More predictable guild and region lifecycle operations.
- Improved concurrency safety.
- Reduced main-thread blocking during storage operations.
- More reliable territory transition handling.
- Safer public API usage.
- Better regression coverage and maintainability.

The changes are intended to strengthen the existing architecture without introducing unrelated features or unnecessary storage format migrations.

- **One card per sign-in.** Each card shows the server, the state (connected / connecting / offline / sign-in required / signed out) and the mailboxes it can see.
- **Actions per card.** Retry, *Sign in again* (or *Sign in* after a sign-out), *Sign out*, and *Remove* for additional sign-ins.
- **Add sign-in.** This button opens the existing sign-in form in a dialog, with app password or browser OAuth. `SignIn` got a `target` prop for this; without it the page behaves as before.
- **Narrow screens.** The buttons and the server line wrap. I checked this at 390 px.

### Session status and sign-out per sign-in

- `ListSignIns` reports the state of every sign-in. `GetSessionStatus` still describes the primary one and gains `signedOut`.
- **Signing out of one sign-in.** `SignOutOf(id)` stops that sign-in and deletes its credentials. The other sign-ins keep syncing and nothing is deleted:
  - the signed-out sign-in keeps its config entry, marked `signedOut: true`, and its cache;
  - it is not restored at startup and raises no "sign-in expired" prompt;
  - it can be signed in again with the same user.
- **Signing out of the only sign-in.** This behaves exactly as before: the config is cleared and the app goes back to the sign-in page.
- **Removing.** `RemoveSignIn` removes an additional sign-in together with its cache and credentials. Your `removed` flag also covers sign-ins that fail while being added.
- **A different user signing in to the primary sign-in** while other sign-ins exist clears only the primary user's data. That is the unprefixed accounts, templates and primary-only settings, with its entries dropped from `mutedMailAccounts`, `unifiedExcludedAccounts` and `defaultIdentities`. The other sign-ins' caches, trusted lists and translations stay (`ResetPrimaryIdentityData`).

### Adding and signing in again

- **Adding.** `AddSignInWithPassword` / `AddSignInOAuth` reserve a prefix, connect, and only write the sign-in to `config.json` once the session works. If that fails, the prefix is retired and anything it already cached is removed.
- **Signing in again.** `SignInAgainWithPassword`, `SignInAgainOAuth` and `RetrySignIn` take a sign-in id; an empty id means the primary sign-in.
- **Identity checks.** The same server user can't be signed in twice (`2023`). Signing in again to an additional sign-in must use the same user (`2024`), because its prefix holds that user's data. Both are checked twice: before connecting, against the typed user name, and after the session opens, against the server's user name, before anything syncs. The second check goes through a new `accept` argument on `connect`.
- **OAuth.** Only one OAuth flow runs at a time across sign-ins, because they share the loopback port.

### Mail UI

- **Sidebar.** Folders / Shared stay for the primary sign-in. Each additional sign-in gets its own collapsible section with its folders and shared mailboxes.
- **Expired sign-in prompts.**
  - An expired additional sign-in shows a persistent toast that names it and links to Settings → Account.
  - The primary sign-in keeps its dialog, which now shows the user, and another sign-in connecting no longer dismisses it.
- **User menu.** It always shows the primary user. With several sign-ins, its *Sign out* opens Settings → Account so you can pick which one.
- **`ListAccounts`** returns accounts grouped by sign-in, with a `signIn` field.

New strings use Chinese keys, with cs, en and ru translations.

### Testing

- **Automated checks.** `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test:i18n` pass on Windows. ESLint reports nothing new.
- **New unit tests:**
  - identity checks before and after connecting (`TestCheckSignInTarget`, `TestAcceptIdentity`);
  - signing out of one sign-in with another one present, and of the primary one alone (`TestSignOutOfKeepsOtherSignIns`);
  - a different primary user with another sign-in present (`TestEnsureCacheOwnerKeepsOtherSignIns`);
  - reserving and storing prefixes in `config`.
- **Integration test.** `TestIntegrationMultipleSignIns` still passes against the two local Stalwart servers.
- **Desktop build, three sign-ins.** The servers are two Stalwart v1.0.0 containers. The sign-ins are primary `alice` on server 1, `s2` = `carol` on server 2, whose account id `c` collides with alice's, and `s3` = `bob` on server 1, who shares his inbox with alice. I checked these from the app:
  - adding the sign-ins from the API the dialog uses; a duplicate gets `2023`, a wrong password `2060`, and signing in again as another user `2024`;
  - **signing out of s2:** primary and s3 keep syncing, and s2's cached inbox stays readable;
  - **signing out of the primary sign-in with others present:** s3 keeps syncing, the app stays in the mail view, and all caches stay;
  - **restart afterwards:** the signed-out sign-ins are not restored and show no prompt; s3 restores; signing in again to s2 and to the primary sign-in works;
  - **s2's password changed on the server:** only s2 stops, the toast names carol, and the primary dialog doesn't open;
  - **restart with server 2 stopped:** primary and s3 restore and s2's cached accounts stay; once the server is back, s2 connects on its next retry.

### Release notes

As you noted on #26, an older version that opens this config drops `signIns` when it saves. It also treats the prefixed accounts as another identity and clears the cache once. The server is not affected, but a line about it in the release notes would help.

author: vishstack01
body:
The voice mock interview from the blueprint (section 6): a spoken drill that cross-examines the figures on the candidate's own resume, with a claim-by-claim scorecard.

**How it works**
- Writing & interviews gets a "Resume defence" tool. Pick the base resume or a role's tailored resume.
- `drill.claims` takes up to six lines: ones with a figure first ("40%", "£50k", "1,200 users", "3 months"; years and version numbers such as "in Python 3.11" are left out), then lines naming one of the member's skills.
- The browser reads each question aloud (`speechSynthesis`, British English, American for US roles). The member answers by speaking (`SpeechRecognition`, Chrome, Edge, Safari) or typing (any browser). The setup screen says plainly that Chrome and Edge send audio to their own speech service; Propelo keeps only the text, in the tab.
- One follow-up per line, aimed at the gap: a figure that contradicts the resume ("Your resume says 40%. You said 35%. Which is right?"), no figure, no way of knowing, or only "we".
- The scorecard marks each line Defended, Partly defended or Not defended, with four checks (the figure as the resume has it, how you know, your own part, about a minute) and what to fix. A contradicted figure is never "defended". For a tailored resume the summary is saved on the role (`drill: {at, lines, defended, partly, not}`).
- 15-minute clock; at zero the drill scores what it has.

**Same rules twice, tested**
- `propelo/drill.py` and the dashboard block between `drill:start` and `drill:end`. `test_dashboard_drill_matches_python` runs both on one resume and six answers and compares claims, questions, scores and follow-ups.

Not in this PR: a server-side voice model (Deepgram, Cartesia) with sub-second turns. The browser's own speech services cost nothing and need no keys; a hosted voice can come later if members want it.

**Tests**
- Full suite with PostgreSQL: 795 passed.
- Checked in the browser: setup, a question, a follow-up, the scorecard (desktop), and the question screen at 390 px in dark mode.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## What failed

Nightly ToastDifferential (run 45489928135, commit fdef3376) diverged on a program whose first failing operation is

```moo
s = "%$a";
... disassemble(s[9223372036854775807] = #0, ...) ...
```

Toast raised `E_TYPE`, Barn raised `E_RANGE`. Rerun through the harness's `eval()` wrapper on `Test_conf.db`:

- Toast (`/root/src/toaststunt/build-release/moo`, emergency mode): `=> {"raised", E_TYPE}`
- Barn before the fix: `=> {"raised", E_RANGE}`
- Barn after the fix: `=> {"raised", E_TYPE}`

Reduced probes, Toast vs Barn before the fix:

| statement | Toast | Barn before |
|---|---|---|
| `s = "%$a"; s[5] = #0;` | E_TYPE | E_RANGE |
| `s = "%$a"; s[0] = #0;` | E_TYPE | E_RANGE |
| `s = "%$a"; s[1] = #0;` | E_TYPE | E_INVARG |
| `s = {"abc"}; s[1][2] = #0;` | E_TYPE | E_INVARG |
| `s = "%$a"; s[5] = "x";` | E_RANGE | E_RANGE |
| `s = "abc"; s[5] = "xy";` | E_RANGE | E_RANGE |
| `s = "abc"; s[2] = "xy";` | E_INVARG | E_INVARG |

## Cause

`vm/collection_helpers.go:34-45` (`setAtIndex`, string case) checked the index range first, and then rejected a non-string value and a wrong-length string together with `E_INVARG`. Toast's `OP_INDEXSET` (`src/execute.cc` around line 1218) includes `list.type == TYPE_STR && value.type != TYPE_STR` in its `E_TYPE` condition, which it checks before the range. Only the length-1 check comes after the range, and it raises `E_INVARG`.

## Fix

The string case now raises `E_TYPE` for a non-string value together with the non-integer index check. After that it checks the range (`E_RANGE`) and then the length (`E_INVARG`).

`vm/string_index_assignment_order_test.go` checks all of the probes above, which match the Toast oracle's results. Seven of its cases fail without the fix. ToastDifferential is not a Go fuzz target, so there is no `testdata/fuzz` input to commit.

`go test ./vm ./compiler ./builtins`, `go vet ./vm`, `staticcheck ./vm` and `golangci-lint run ./vm/...` pass.

## Known related gaps

- **Nested index assignment through a string base.** Toast raises `E_TYPE` ("expected list, map or waif; got string") for `s = "abc"; s[1][1] = "x";`. Barn accepts it and returns `"xbc"`. For `s = "abc"; s[5][1] = "x";` Toast raises `E_TYPE` and Barn raises `E_RANGE`. Toast pushes the intermediate reference with an op that accepts only a list, map or waif. Barn's nested assignment path lets a string through at that level. I didn't locate the exact Barn line, and this PR doesn't fix it.

Fixes #1147

- **Firebase Setup:** Configured Firebase authentication, Firestore dependencies (`pubspec.yaml`), Google services plugins (`build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts`), and `google-services.json`. Updated `README.md` with setup instructions.

- **Transactional Stock Management:** Added Firestore transactions to deduct stock upon order confirmation and notify customers if inventory is insufficient.
- **Security Rules & Web Config:** Added and published `firestore.rules` and configured Firebase Web initialization via `--dart-define`.

### 📦 Order History & Admin Management
- **Order History & Delivery Tracking:** Added customer order history ("Mis Pedidos") synced with Firestore, along with delivery management tools in the admin panel (PR #6).
- **Catalog Import Locking:** Added a real-time catalog listener and UI indicators in the admin import view to lock products already present in the store, preventing duplicate import errors from Open Food Facts (PR #8).
- **Filter Alignment:** Aligned filtering behavior between user and admin views and added a stock availability filter.

### 🎨 UI, Branding & Fixes
- **App Icon:** Added custom and adaptive NutriMarket launcher icons for Android (PR #7).
- **Error Handling & Bug Fixes:** Cleaned up user-facing messages to hide technical database details and resolved a build error when opening "Mis Pedidos".

## Merged Pull Requests Included
- #4 `feature/admin-auth-firebase`
- #5 `feature/products-stock-firebase`
- #6 `feature/order-history`

```diff
 package.json
-    "markdownlint-cli2": "^0.24.1",
+    "markdownlint-cli2": "^0.24.2",

 bun.lock
     "markdownlint-cli2": "^0.24.2"

 package-lock.json
```

body:
## Why
"Send in multiples of" matched pack sizes by **variant name** (for example "Mini"). With the River Sea structure mini variants are named by flavor, so a rule like "minis ship in 100s" could not be expressed. This replaces it with explicit groups; nothing is matched by name.

## What changed
- **Settings card renamed "Pack Size".**
- A **default pack size** (built in: **1**, was 5) that applies to every variant not in a group.
- Any number of **groups**. Each has a pack size (1 to 1000) and the specific variants that ship in it.
- **Add products** opens a search (name, SKU or barcode, optionally within a collection, Show more) with per-row **Add** and an **Add all N shown** button, so a whole collection such as the minis goes in with one click.
- A variant is in **at most one** group: adding it to another moves it. Removing a variant or a group puts it back on the default.
- Saving is one button for the whole card; unsaved edits are tracked and the button is disabled until something changed and everything is valid.
- Transfer suggestions look pack sizes up **by variant id** (`packSizeFor`), on the screen preview and in the server recompute that runs before drafts are created.
- Stored with the app installation as `$app:inventory/pack_sizes` (variant ids). The old `multiples` metafield is **no longer read**, so until someone saves, everything ships one at a time. The settings page looks up names for the saved ids in batches of 100 (names and SKUs only, no stock).

## Code
- New: `domain/packSizes.ts` (parse leniently, validate, `packSizeFor`, `moveToGroup`, `removeFromGroup`), `lib/packSizeDraft.ts` (the card's text-field draft and validation), `shopify/variantLabels.ts`, `PackSizeCard`, `PackGroupPicker`.
- Server validation (`parsePackSizesInput`): GIDs only, size range, max 20 groups and 2000 variants, a variant in two groups is refused with a clear message.
- Removed: `domain/multiples.ts`, `MultiplesCard`, the by-name input parser and its tests.
- `variantNames()` is now shared by the pickers and the card, so a variant has the same name everywhere.
- Docs (`inventory_tracker.md`) updated.

## Test plan
- [x] 698 unit and render tests, typecheck, lint
- [x] Live test against the dev store: save a group holding a mini, read it back with its name and category, restore the default
- [ ] After deploy: `APP_HANDLE=chocotrack-production npm run test:e2e` (new test adds a group with a mini, saves, reloads, then removes it)

author: drkostas
body:
A refspec may carry its own destination, so one typed line can store a ref for a branch a remote never had (`git fetch origin +refs/pull/7/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr-7`) or one for every open pull request (`git fetch origin "+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/mine/*"`). Nobody meets either again, because neither is a branch any command lists and the line that made it was typed once. What they cost is reading rather than writing. A listing of remote branches grows, a count of a remote's merged branches counts refs for branches deleted long ago, and the ancestry walk behind that count pays for every one of them.

### What a prune reaches, which is two answers

Measured on real git in the test beside the hook rather than reasoned about. A prune removes what a remote's configured refspec covers, by default `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/<name>/*`. So a destination inside that namespace is removed by `git fetch --prune <name>`, and until somebody runs one it reads exactly like a branch the remote still has, which is the worse half in practice. A destination anywhere else, another tracking namespace or a name invented at the top (`refs/mine/7`), is removed by neither `git fetch --prune` nor `git remote prune`, ever.

The first version of this hook said the harsher sentence for both cases, and its own test refuted it on the first run. The refusal now reads the repository's own remotes and says which of four answers applies, including the one where that cannot be read, and never a guess. In the repository this was measured in, 4,761 such refs had gathered, 2,245 of them from a single wildcard fetch, and listing the merged ones took 2.09 s against 0.084 s for the remote's own refs alone.

### What goes through

A destination under `refs/heads/`, `refs/tags/`, `refs/notes/` or `refs/replace/`, because each has a command that shows it and a person who can remove it. A plain local branch name (`master:master`). A remote given as an address (`git@host:owner/repo.git`) or a URL, neither of which names a ref after its colon. A push. A fetch with no destination, which is almost every fetch.

### The two ways through, both in the refusal

A refusal with no way through is one people route around, so the words name both. For the objects or for a sha, fetch the source alone with `git fetch --no-write-fetch-head <remote> <ref>...`, which writes no ref and no FETCH_HEAD, and read each sha from `git ls-remote <remote> <pattern>`. Both take many refs in one call, which is the answer where a wildcard would have been, and the test proves the source-only fetch leaves no ref and no FETCH_HEAD while the objects are present by sha. To keep such refs instead, add them to the remote's refspec with `git config --add remote.<name>.fetch`, and a prune keeps that namespace clean from then on.

### Checked

`tests/test_stray_refs.py`, 28 checks. Six commands refused (a single head, a wildcard, an invented namespace, `git -C` elsewhere, one after a `cd` on the same line, and a destination inside the remote's namespace), twelve that go through, the four answers of `fate` by name, the refusal's own words, another tool and an empty command, the CLI exiting 2, and two real-git measurements, a prune reaching the remote's own namespace and nothing else, and the source-only fetch the refusal offers writing no ref at all.

It takes no configuration.

## Why
The first real night tests of camera mapping (2026-11-24) decoded the lights' codes but couldn't place the camera. This adds what was needed to see why, and fixes what the footage showed.

## What this adds
**Diagnosis**
- The phone can send a small greyscale copy of a spot's footage (640 px wide, gzip) with the result. The server keeps the newest 6 in `data/mapping-recordings/` (`POST`/`GET /api/mapping/recordings`).

body:
Closes #348.

```js
validateEnv({ TAGS: { type: 'array', skipEmpty: true } }, { TAGS: 'a,b,' }); // ['a', 'b']
```

`skipEmpty: true` drops empty items after splitting (trailing or doubled separators, and empty strings in an already-parsed array) before the items are indexed and coerced. `minItems`/`maxItems` and `unique` then apply to what remains. `',,'` becomes `[]`.

The default is unchanged: without the flag the existing `T[2]: expected a non-empty value, got ""` error is byte-for-byte the same. Like `of`/`separator`/`unique`, the option is rejected on non-`array` rules and a non-boolean value is a schema error. `EnvRule` gains `skipEmpty?: boolean`, and the README's array row and paragraph document it.

Tests in `test.js` cover `a,b,`, `a,,b`, `',,'`, an array input, counts and uniqueness on the remaining items, the unchanged default error, and both schema rejections. `node test.js` passes the block (still stops at the pre-existing Node 26 async `.env` assertion); `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json` passes.

author: dipaolafederico
body:
## What and why

Closes #46. Adds the client kmd uses to talk to a user-run local OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp `llama serve`, LM Studio, Ollama). It lives in `internal/ai`, built only with `-tags kmdai`. Nothing calls it yet; `--ai-check` (#48) is the first user.

- **Loopback only** (`endpoint.go`): accepts `unix:///abs/path` or `http://` with a loopback IP literal. `localhost` is mapped to `127.0.0.1` without DNS; `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is unmapped. Any other host, as well as TLS, credentials, a path, a query or a zone, is an `ai-url` error.
- **Own HTTP/1.1 client** on `net.Dialer` (`client.go`, `http.go`), not `net/http`: it has no TLS, proxies, redirects (3xx is an error) or connection reuse. It handles `Content-Length`, chunked and read-until-close bodies.
- **Streaming** (`sse.go`, `chat.go`): `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true`, parsed incrementally. `Chat` calls back with `Delta{Content, Reasoning}`. `Request` has no field for `tools`. An answer cut off at `max_tokens` returns `ErrTruncated`, so it never looks complete.
- **`Info`**: model name from `GET /v1/models`, image support from llama.cpp's `/props` (missing elsewhere, which means "no vision").
- **Limits** (from #44's measurements):

  | Limit | Value |
  |-------|-------|
  | Connect | 5 s |
  | Headers, and an error body | 5 s |
  | Idle between reads | 60 s |
  | Total | 180 s |
  | Everything read, framing included | 8 MiB, an error past it |
  | One line or event | 64 KiB |
  | Headers or trailers | 100 lines |

  Cancelling the context closes the connection at once (`context.AfterFunc`).
- **Key file**: it must be a regular file, at most 4 KiB, `chmod 600` (the mode is not checked on Windows), holding one line of printable ASCII without spaces. It is checked before opening, so a FIFO cannot hang kmd, and again on the open descriptor. A missing file means no key.
- **TCP port-squatting** (the open point from #45): kmd sends the key over TCP too. Without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (macOS, for one) TCP is the default, and there the key is what keeps other users off the server. A squatter would get the document with or without the key. `--ai-check` (#48) will flag TCP and recommend the socket. The reasoning is in `docs/experimental/ai.md`.
- `make fuzz` now includes `FuzzResponse` (with `-tags kmdai`).

As with #56, this is `chore(ai)`: no release and no CHANGELOG entry. README, man page, `--help` and completions are untouched until graduation (#53).

## How it was tested

- **Gates**: `make ci` passes (coverage 97.2 %; perf p50 2.2 ms, unchanged, since the untagged binary does not contain this code). `make test-ai` passes (coverage 97.1 %); `internal/ai` alone is at 97 %.
- **Fake servers**: tests use `httptest` and a raw-socket server that sends what no well-behaved server would:
  - redirects, malformed or huge headers, bad chunks, endless lines, endless streams, a chunk-extension flood;
  - error bodies and events carrying ANSI/OSC sequences (stripped from error messages);
  - header, idle and total timeouts, and cancellation mid-stream and while waiting for headers;
  - Unix sockets and key-file rules (FIFO included).
- **Fuzzing**: `FuzzResponse` runs headers, chunked decoding, the cap, SSE and JSON for 4 + 3 minutes (about 80 M runs) with no failure. It also checks that no event exceeds the line cap and that the total stays under the byte cap.
- **Real llama.cpp b12651** with LFM3-VL-2B over a Unix socket:
  - Headers arrive in 8 ms even for a cold README whose first token takes about 25 s. The 5 s header limit is safe, because the wait falls under the idle limit. The longest silence in the stream was 30 s (the keep-alive ping).
  - `Info` reports vision with `--mmproj`.
  - `ErrTruncated` was found here: with llama.cpp's default sampling the model reasoned until it hit 2048 tokens on a one-sentence question (`finish_reason: "length"`), which the first version returned as a complete, empty answer. Sampling parameters (#44 used the model card's) belong to #47.

### Reviews (security, performance, maintainability, in separate agents)

- **Security** (no high/medium):
  - Fixed: chunk extensions bypassed the body cap; the cap is now on every byte read.
  - Fixed: an error body could trickle for up to 180 s; it now gets the 5 s header limit.
  - Fixed: a FIFO key file hung kmd.
  - Fixed: added a doc note that `Delta` is hostile text.
  - Left for #48: warn about a socket in a directory others can write to.
- **Performance**:
  - The untagged binary is identical in size and `make perf` is unaffected.
  - About 1.5 µs per streamed event.
  - Fixed: a hostile `choices` list of thousands allocated about 52× its size; decoding now uses a single element.
  - Dismissed: two 64 KiB buffers per request cost microseconds against latencies of seconds.
  - Noted for #49: batch redraws rather than re-render per `Delta`.
- **Maintainability**:
  - Fixed: `/v1/models` and `/props` were truncated silently.
  - Fixed: exported `ErrUnreachable` for #48.
  - Fixed: a dead check, a multi-line `errors.Join` error, and a line reader duplicated between HTTP and SSE.
  - Fixed: file layout (`client.go`, `key_test.go`), names (`decodeEvent`, `bodyError`), comments and limits, and the doc's Status line.
  - Fixed: tests (named cases, cases derived from the limits, model sent, empty model list).
  - Deferred to #48, where it is used: an accessor saying whether the connection is TCP.

## Checklist

- [x] Title is a Conventional Commit and the branch is `type/short-description`
- [x] `make ci` passes locally (including the perf gate), and `make test-ai`
- [x] New behaviour is covered by tests (coverage stays ≥ 90%)
- [x] No new dependencies (`go.mod` has no `require`)
- [x] User-facing changes are documented: only in `docs/experimental/ai.md` while experimental
- [x] `chore`: no CHANGELOG entry (the single `Experimental:` line comes with #49)
- [x] Untrusted input stays safe: destination fixed by config and loopback-only; every server-supplied string in an error is reduced to printable ASCII; every read is bounded

author: zmanian
body:
`KeyInit::new` initializes the `aes` (AES-NI) variant of the inner union only when the `aes` CPU feature is detected, and the `soft` variant otherwise. The VAES encrypt/decrypt paths are selected by the `vaes256` / `vaes512` tokens alone, and they read `self.inner.aes.enc_rk` / `dec_rk` and call the AES-NI single-block routines.

So on a CPU (or a VM whose hypervisor masks CPUID bits) that reports VAES (and AVX-512 state for the 512-bit path) without AES-NI, the cipher is keyed through the soft backend and then encrypted through VAES reading the uninitialized `aes` variant. The union has no `repr`, so depending on layout this either runs AES rounds over a soft-schedule-derived key (silently wrong output; the instructions still execute when the CPUID bit is masked) or reads uninitialized memory. Bare-metal CPUs with VAES also have AES-NI, so this matters mainly under virtualization or confidential-computing guests where the host influences CPUID.

This makes the VAES tokens also require `aes`, plus `avx2` for the 256-bit backend (`vaes` implies `aes`, `avx` and `avx2` as target features), so the VAES paths can only run when the AES-NI round keys were initialized.

Tested: `cargo test -p aes --target x86_64-apple-darwin`, clippy (`--lib --tests`, `-D warnings`) and `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. There is no regression test, because the tokens come from `cpufeatures` and can't be forced without a test-only constructor; happy to add one if you'd like that shape. I left the CHANGELOG for the release.

## ⚠️ Não mesclar antes de D13 passo 1

Pela spec (D13, decisão de João em 2026-11-24), este PR fica aberto até a API do bloco 61 do Lotus responder em produção do jeito que a página precisa:

- `GET https://app.lotusotec.cl/api/publico/certificados/consulta` → `405`;
- o preflight com `Origin: https://lotusotec.cl` devolve esse `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, sem `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`.

Sem isso, o item "Validar Certificado" do menu iria ao ar levando a uma página que só mostra erro. O change set de `infra/lotus-site.yaml` (D13 passo 2: CSP e função de borda) pode ser aplicado por João antes do merge.

## Work item

- **Work item:** `validacao-certificado`, a página de validação de certificado no site (entrega 2 do bloco 61 do Lotus).
- **EAP:** nenhuma. O item não tem EAP no Notion, e nada foi escrito lá.
- **Classe:** `architectural`. Executor `claude`; reviewer `claude-isolado`, porque o Codex está indisponível (`model_not_found` na config de João, `D-84`).
- **Documentos:**
  - spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-validacao-certificado-design.md`
  - plano: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-24-validacao-certificado.md`
  - Context Packet: `docs/superpowers/context-packets/validacao-certificado.md`
  - ADR nova: `docs/adr/ADR-SITE-007.md`, um HTML por página

## O que entra

- **`/validar` e `/validar/<uuid>`**, uma segunda página HTML (`validar/index.html`) sem router. A borda a serve por reescrita explícita: a função CloudFront, com o ramo de `www` primeiro. Dev e preview reproduzem a mesma reescrita por plugin.
- **Dois modos na mesma página:**
  - formulário de código + RUT (`POST /consulta`, o RUT só no corpo);
  - abertura pelo QR (`GET /{uuid}`).
- **Cartões de resultado:** vigente, por vencer, vencido, revogado, não encontrado, espera com contagem, bloqueio com a orientação do QR e erro genérico.
- **Download do PDF** com o nome tirado do `Content-Disposition`. Um `410` no PDF leva ao estado revogado.
- **"Validar Certificado"** no menu do topo, no desktop e no mobile. As âncoras do menu viram `/#…` e levam de volta à home.
- **CSP:** `connect-src` ganha `https://app.lotusotec.cl`.
- **Deploy e rollback** (`ci.yml` e `ADR-SITE-004`): os dois `index.html` são publicados como arquivos de nome fixo, com `no-cache`.
- **SEO:** `noindex` nas duas formas, sem canonical, e `/validar` fora do sitemap.
- **Nenhuma dependência nova.**

## Critérios de aceite (spec §8) e a saída que os provou

| Critério | Prova | Saída |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A1 · Borda** | tabela de casos de `scripts/infra/lib/validar.mjs` contra a função do template em `node:vm` (`distribuicao.test.mjs`) e contra o plugin (`reescrever-validar.test.mjs`), inclusive `www` → 301 para `/validar/<uuid>` | dentro de `pnpm check`, exit 0 |

| **A4 · Caminhos** | `e2e/validar-caminhos.spec.ts` no preview: `/validar`, `/validar/`, `/validar/<uuid>` → 200; `/validar/abc`, `/validar/<uuid>/x`, `/VALIDAR`, `/inventado` → 404 | `pnpm e2e` 176/176 |
| **A5 · Home** | `e2e/navegacao.spec.ts` nos quatro motores; snapshot `home-1440-producao-linux.png` regravado | `pnpm e2e` 176/176; pela comparação de pixels do revisor, a diferença fica toda na linha do menu (x 658–1248, y 39–55) |
| **A6 · A11y e SEO** | `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` com quatro estados de `/validar`; `e2e/seo.spec.ts` com `noindex`, sem canonical e fora do sitemap | `pnpm e2e` 176/176 |
| **A7 · Stack local do Lotus** | `docs/infra/evidencia-validacao-certificado-2026-11-24.md`: Lotus `main@aba2b75e`, preflight `204` sem `Allow-Credentials`, `GET /consulta` → `405`; QR vigente e revogado, PDF `certificado-LOT-2025-05999.pdf` (304.845 B, `%PDF`), código + RUT certos, RUT errado → 404, formato inválido sem pedido, 11ª consulta → 429 com espera, 11ª falha por RUT → 429 com bloqueio | só Chromium, por script; o bloqueio por IP não foi alcançado |

Executados no fechamento, em 2026-11-24/25, com Node 24.19.0, no HEAD `68d112f`. Os commits posteriores só mexem em documentos do harness.

- `pnpm check` → exit 0: `agent:check`, `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, 60 arquivos com 606 testes, `build` e `build:lambda`.
- `pnpm e2e` → exit 0, **176 passed**, em duas rodadas seguidas.
- `check` do CI corporativo na árvore filtrada (`git archive` com as exclusões de `.espelho-exclusoes`, no HEAD `2cc3cab`) → exit 0: 53 arquivos, 535 passed, 9 skipped (o rollback da `ADR-SITE-004` fica `skipped` sem `docs/`, como o plano prevê).

A primeira rodada de `pnpm e2e` do fechamento, ainda em `b0f8c00`, deu 175/176. Isso devolveu o bloco à review e está detalhado abaixo.

## Review (`claude-isolado`, sobre `149d0ec..d7997b5`)

Veredito: **PASS**, com quatro `suggestion`, todas conferidas no código:

| Achado | Severidade | Resolução |
| --- | --- | --- |

Causa não achada, nada mitigado às cegas: **`D-86`** |
| **R-2:** `id="footer-info"` no `Footer` compartilhado (`0903a0d`), fora do mapa de arquivos do plano | suggestion | não corrigido; sem mudança visual |
| **R-3:** `ESPERA_SEM_NUMERO_S = 60` duplicada em `BotaoDoPdf.tsx` e `EsperaComContagem.tsx` | suggestion | não corrigido |

A investigação do R-1 achou outro teste instável, este do próprio bloco. `e2e/validar.spec.ts:221` corria contra 1 s de relógio real. Ele foi corrigido em `68d112f` com `page.clock`: 40/40 nos quatro motores com `--repeat-each=10`, e a mutação `falta -= 2` no hook o reprova.

author: eyalamirmusic
body:
Opened as a draft, mainly to run CI on the web target and on the new `build-web` lane.

## What the web target is

A WebAssembly build of eacp through Emscripten (`emcmake cmake ...`): wasm32, single-threaded, no `-pthread`, so the output is plain static files that need no special headers. A window is a `<canvas>` and the GPU is WebGPU. Apps join through the same capability variables and the same `eacp_add_app` calls as on every other platform, so as many `Apps/` examples as possible run unchanged in a browser. `Docs/Web.md` covers the target and `plan.md` is the roadmap.

## What this PR adds

- **The web target so far.** Core, Network (through `fetch()` and `WebSocket`), the four device-free pieces, Graphics (windows, views and input) and GPU over WebGPU. The suites run under node and in headless Chrome.
- **A merge of `develop`.** It also fixes a duplicate `binaryExponent()` the merge kept in `DepthSampling` (which broke the macOS and Windows builds) and a ShaderWarmUp test that assumed a worker thread.
- **A web CI lane, `build-web`.** It runs on Ubuntu with a pinned emsdk and node 26 (for JSPI) and builds `Debug` through ccache. The suite runs under node and in headless Chrome on its SwiftShader WebGPU adapter. A step before the tests fails the lane if the page gets no device. `Formats`, `PackedHalf` and `Intrinsics` fail only on SwiftShader, so they are excluded by name.
- **Text, UI and SVG on the web.** `EACP_HAS_TEXT` is on for Emscripten. It uses Linux's FreeType/HarfBuzz rasterizer over Emscripten's ports, and font discovery is split into fontconfig (Linux) and a memory-font registry (web). DejaVu Sans and Sans Mono are embedded under `EACP_WEB_DEFAULT_FONTS` (about 2.1 MB of wasm, 0.75 MB brotli). `Apps/UI`, `Apps/SVG`, the `Apps/Graphics` component apps and the glyph examples now build for the web.
- **A fix for presenting on Linux hardware.** `GPUView-Linux` also requires the surface-capabilities query to succeed, and logs once with workarounds when it doesn't. `with-weston` uses the GL renderer when a render node exists, and `with-xvfb` sets `MESA_VK_WSI_DEBUG=sw`, so a hardware Vulkan driver can present under both harnesses.

## Local test results

- macOS: 381/381
- Windows: 387/387
- Web, Chrome on Metal: 334/334
- Web, CI-style on Linux with SwiftShader: 330/330, with `Formats`, `PackedHalf` and `Intrinsics` excluded
- Linux, `with-weston` on lavapipe: 343 to 346 of 346. On the Asahi hardware driver, `Present` now passes under both harnesses. `CommandBufferTiming/sharesSumToTheBuffer` fails only on Asahi hardware; it is a separate issue that predates this branch.

## Known gaps

- `Formats` hangs on SwiftShader. The RG16Unorm texture it makes needs `texture-formats-tier1`, which that device lacks. This is a real backend gap: the backend should refuse the format there. It is tracked in `plan.md`.
- No 2D `Context`, capture or native web view on the web. No CJK or colour emoji face is bundled. The in-window menu bar isn't drawn. HarfBuzz 3.2 has no synthetic bold or slant.
- Firefox and Safari are untried.
- The `build-web` lane has never run on GitHub before this PR.

author: rcweston90
body:
Before: the mixer had one EQ type (an isolator with a hidden bump of about +7 dB around the band crossovers), one channel-fader curve, both decks hard-wired to their side of the crossfader, and a filter knob with no centre detent.

After: the isolator is flat. A row of switches under the crossfader picks the EQ type (ISO or EQ), the channel-fader curve (Slow, Lin or Fast) and the crossfader curve (Smooth, Full or Cut). Each channel can be sent to A, THRU or B on the crossfader, and the filter knob locks at centre.

**What changed**
- **Isolator fix** (its own commit, 9ece38d): Web Audio reads a lowpass/highpass Q as dB, so Q = √½ gave a resonant bump. The Q is now −3.01 dB (Butterworth), and the three bands sum flat within 0.08 dB. An offline render test checks it.
- **EQ/ISO**: ISO is the existing isolator, −30 dB with a full-left kill, up to +6 dB. EQ is shelves at 100 Hz and 8 kHz plus a 1 kHz peak, +6 to −26 dB with no kill. Switching crossfades between them, so it doesn't click.
- **Channel-fader curve**: Slow is v³, Lin is v² (the old behaviour and the default), Fast reaches full level in the first 8% of travel.
- **Crossfader assign A / THRU / B** per channel, which MIDI can learn. Beat FX and the beat board use the assign too.
- **Filter centre lock**: a ±8% dead zone, plus a `detent` prop on Knob.
- A Mixer guide (ⓘ), and a phone layout for the new switches.
- The new settings are optional in saves, so older saves load with the defaults.

**Tests**: `tsc -b` and `vite build` pass, and controls.mjs passes 73 of 73. e2e.mjs passes 64 with 1 failure, "Match shifts deck B", which fails the same way on main. New checks cover the EQ kill and range, the fader curves at half travel, the assign as heard in the engine, the centre lock, settings surviving a reload, flat offline DSP, and MIDI assign.

**Left as is**: in `src/engine/fx.ts`, the Beat FX lowpass/highpass filters made without a Q use the same √½ default and get about +1 dB at their corners. That's for a separate fix.

Screenshots: mixer-switches.png, mixer-guide.png, mixer-phone.png (sent in chat).

## Why
Owner `sync_all` always runs `autoTriggerPillars()` after merging collections. That automation reads Leads and can create/update Clients and Projects. The schema preflight added in PR #37 did not include these implicit CRM dependencies when the payload contained only an unrelated collection (for example Finance). A missing Projects/Clients tab could therefore fail after an earlier collection had already been written.

## Changes
- Preflight Leads, Clients, and Projects for every Owner sync before any collection writes.
- Add a shared CRM schema guard and call it inside `autoTriggerPillars()` before any automatic conversion work.
- Before Owner changes a Lead to Deal Won through `update_status`, validate the CRM dependencies before writing the new status.
- Add regression tests: missing Projects blocks an unrelated Finance sync without a Finance write; missing Clients blocks Deal Won status transition without changing the Lead.
- Keep `apps-script/Code.gs` and `google_apps_script.js` byte-identical.
- Update README and roadmap.

## Safety
Development branch only. No production Apps Script deployment, live Google Sheets write, schema migration, Supabase change, Script Properties change, or public website deployment.

## Validation
Awaiting GitHub Actions on this PR head.

author: xaleh
body:
Roadmap **B1 · Análise da partida** (item 🧱), **fase 1 de 3**. O plano completo está em `docs/plano-analise-partida.md`.

## O que mudou

Em qualquer replay terminado, a barra do replay ganha o botão **Analisar a partida**. O bot revê cada decisão de cada jogador que tinha escolha de verdade e compara a jogada feita com a melhor jogada que ele acha.

- **Só o que o jogador sabia.** Cada decisão é avaliada sobre `viewFor(estado, jogador)`, a mesma visão com que o bot joga. A mão e o deck do oponente ficam escondidos. A análise só roda em replay terminado (`AnalysisError('notFinished')`).
- **Motor** (`packages/engine/src/bot/analysis.ts`): `analyzeReplay`, `reviewDecision`, `summarizeAnalysis`.
  - Gravidade pela perda na avaliação: imprecisão a partir de 1.500, erro a partir de 4.000, erro grave a partir de 10.000.
  - Precisão de cada decisão e média por jogador.
  - Tipo do marcador: letal perdido, Counter desperdiçado ou que faltou, bloqueio, "atacar o Líder era melhor", "encerrou cedo"…
  - No `planner.ts`, a busca do turno virou `searchTurn` (extraída do `planTurn`, sem mudar o bot), mais `scoreDecision` e `sameAction`.
- **Web:**
  - A conta roda num Web Worker (`game/analysisWorker.ts`). Sem worker, roda na página, uma decisão por tarefa.
  - Progresso na barra e botão para cancelar.
  - Marcadores coloridos sobre a barra de busca, ‹ › para pular entre eles e o cartão do marcador (o que foi jogado e a jogada sugerida).
  - Resumo por jogador: precisão, erros graves, erros, imprecisões e letais perdidos.
  - Funciona no celular, porque tudo fica na barra do replay.
  - Textos nos seis idiomas (`i18n/analysis/`).
- **Sem banco e sem rota nova.** O replay terminado já chega inteiro a quem pode vê-lo.
- README, documentação técnica e `docs/plano-analise-partida.md` atualizados.

## Fases seguintes

- **Fase 2:** análise guardada no servidor (`match_analyses`), com fila e a precisão em "Minhas partidas".
- **Fase 3:** prévia "e se" na mesa, análise do mulligan e "Analisar" na tela de fim de partida.

## Como testar

- `npm run typecheck` e `npm test` passam: motor 858, servidor 452, web 149.
- Novos: `packages/engine/test/analysis.test.ts` e `apps/web/test/analysis.test.ts`. Um deles confirma que a análise fica igual quando a mão escondida do oponente é trocada.
- No app: menu → **Assistir replay** → escolha um `.json` de partida terminada → **Assistir ao replay** → **Analisar a partida** na barra. Os marcadores aparecem na barra de busca; um toque leva à decisão e mostra a sugestão. Testado no Chromium, no desktop (1280×800) e com a emulação do iPhone 13.

author: vlrex
body:
## Summary
The late-exact card-backed merge has a 512-run submission budget, but previously computed every changed run in a page before deciding whether to reject it. Stop at the first excess run, without returning or applying a partial result. The existing settle decision, reference lock, unbounded CPU merge and exact byte ranges remain unchanged.

## Validation
Two executed independent algorithm model checks: Python (37,768 exhaustive/seeded cases, group-by reference), JavaScript (10,000 seeded cases, per-byte accumulator); zero disagreements. Two Rust regression tests added, including exhaustive 12-byte masks and the 64 KiB fragmentation case. A synthetic alternating-byte page has 32,768 runs: with a 512-run budget the new algorithm detects excess at byte offset 1,024 rather than scanning the full page. These are operation counts, not timings. Actual upload bytes and GPU wait policy are unchanged; real workload frequency and benefit are unmeasured. Native Rust/Windows and GPU integration tests pending. No new dependencies or game assets. AI-assisted (ChatGPT).

`.github/workflows/release.yml`: the version check now matches only `phiward@vX`, not any `@vX`. Before, a line like `actions/checkout@v5` would have refused a correct release. - **Pull:** before, a stream that ended early (a dropped connection, a killed remote tar) left a truncated file, and the next pull kept it. author: wyrmspire
body:
# SL-2 — Strategy Lab bar loader, IDB cache, session coverage

Branch: `sl/SL-2`

## Done

- Added `lib/strategy-lab/bars.ts`: one-session-at-a-time loader for `/api/market-data` (symbol `MES`).
  - Session window = `equityIndexSessionBounds(date)`: 18:00 ET the previous day to 17:00 ET. DST-correct, never a fixed offset. Covered by a 23 h test on winter, summer, and both DST-change nights.
  - Response cleaning: rows with non-numeric prices or times are dropped; rows outside `[from, to)` are dropped. Volume `0` or missing is kept as `null` or `0`; `buildBarSeries` turns it into `NaN` (missing, not activity).
  - Excluded sessions with a typed reason, never a throw: `not-1m` (a 5m or 1h answer, detail "only 5m left at Yahoo"), `no-data` (404, or an empty 200 such as a weekend), `upstream` (5xx or network error), `bad-response` (not JSON, or no candles array).
  - IDB cache under `strategy-lab:v1:MES:<date>`. Only settled 1m sessions are written (close more than 1 h in the past). Today is never read or written. A corrupt cache entry is a miss.
  - Concurrency pool, default 3, results in input order, `onProgress(done, total)` after each session.
  - `loadBarSeries(dates, deps)` returns the built `BarSeries` (loaded sessions only), per-session load results, and per-session volume integrity.
  - `volumeIntegrity(series, date)` grades the 390 RTH minutes (09:30–16:00 ET): `ok` at zero missing; `degraded` at or below 2%; `missing` above 2%. A missing bar counts as volume-missing; `absent` is the subset with no bar at all.
  - `recentSessionDates(endDate, count)` returns the last N regular sessions, oldest first, skipping weekends.
- Added `lib/__tests__/strategy-lab-bars.test.ts`: 14 tests with mocked fetch and cache. No network, no real IndexedDB.

## Files

- `lib/strategy-lab/bars.ts` (new, 252 lines)
- `lib/__tests__/strategy-lab-bars.test.ts` (new, 316 lines)
- `notes/handoffs/2026-11-24-SL-2.md` (new)

No edits to the SL-1 foundation. `types.ts`, `series.ts`, `aggregate.ts`, `registry.ts`, and `conditions.ts` are unchanged, and no public type changed. `lib/idb.ts` and `lib/session.ts` are imported read-only.

## Choices made (inside scope, reversible)

- The loader is in `bars.ts`. It defines its own `SessionLoad`, `VolumeIntegrity`, and `LabBarData` types, so `types.ts` stays frozen.
- The session `to` bound is exclusive, matching Yahoo's `period2`.
- Missing-volume grading counts absent RTH minutes as volume-missing, because they have no volume either.
- Only 1m sessions are cached. A 5m result is never stored, so a later retry can still get 1m.
- The lookahead harness is not used here: SL-2 has no skills. The harness applies from SL-3.

## Verification

Commands were run in `/home/chriswstubbs/mogmine-wt/sl/SL-2`.

- `node --test lib/__tests__/strategy-lab-bars.test.ts`: `tests 14`, `pass 14`, `fail 0`, `skipped 0`.
- `npm test`: `ℹ tests 1018`, `ℹ suites 13`, `ℹ pass 1017`, `ℹ fail 0`, `ℹ skipped 1`, `ℹ duration_ms 34940`. The one skip is an existing test elsewhere in the suite, not one of the 14 new tests.
- `npm run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`, no output, exit 0.
- `npm run lint`: `✖ 1 problem (0 errors, 1 warning)`, exit 0. The warning is the pre-existing `postcss.config.mjs` anonymous default export.
- `npm run build`: `✓ Compiled successfully in 19.7s`, `Finished TypeScript in 46s`, `Generating static pages (13/13)`, exit 0.
- `npm run check:file-length`: `Checked 178 source files. 14 file(s) over the target`. `bars.ts` is not on the list. The 14 listed files are the existing grandfathered ones; this package touches none of them.
- `git status`: only the two new files and this handoff. The build wrote no tracked files.

## Not in this package

- No skills (SL-3 onward), no UI, no API routes, no migrations, no Supabase.
- No changes to `BOARD.md`, `NOTES.md`, or `DECISIONS.md`.
- No call to the live API and no real account or trade data.

## Pourquoi
Un bug dans la file d'attente ou dans le traitement de l'ack ferait perdre ou dupliquer des positions sans que personne ne le voie. Ces deux parties n'avaient aucun test.

## Changements
- **`Envoi.kt`** : logique du thread d'envoi extraite de `PositionService` (`sendNext`, `retryDelayMs`, `pointsJson`). Lecture de l'ack dans `BatchResult.fromAck`. **Comportement inchangé.**
- **`LocationQueue`** : taille max et taille de purge passées en paramètres (valeurs par défaut identiques).
- **Robolectric 4.18.1** + `androidx.test:core` en `testImplementation` : SQLite et `org.json` réels dans les tests JVM. Les tests utilisent une `Application` vide (`GpsSenderApp` programme WorkManager au démarrage).

## Tests (24 nouveaux, 61 au total)
- `LocationQueueTest` (10) : ordre d'arrivée, `peek` sans retrait, retrait jusqu'au dernier id du lot seulement, positions arrivées pendant l'envoi conservées, survie à la fermeture, ids jamais réutilisés, purge des plus anciennes quand la file est pleine.
- `EnvoiTest` (14) : retrait seulement après l'ack, même lot renvoyé après un échec ou une exception, lots dans l'ordre chronologique, format des points attendu par le serveur, lecture de l'ack (absent, sans `success`, `rejected`, message vide), délais 2/4/8/16 s.
