author: jusso-dev
body:
## Summary

Finishes #219. PR #241 delivered the threat model itself. This PR covers what it deferred:

- **The pull request template checkbox.**
- **The `xtask threat-coverage` check.** It now runs in CI and blocks merges.
- **A status review.** Mitigations that merged after #241 are marked `implemented`, and each cites a test that exists on `main`.

One acceptance criterion cannot be met by an agent: a person other than the author has to review the residual-risk register. It is listed under Deferred as a manual step for the maintainer.

Closes #219

## In scope

Mapped to the open #219 checkboxes and to the items #241 deferred:

**Process**
- [x] **PR template checkbox.** `.github/pull_request_template.md` now asks: "Does this change a trust boundary or add a parser of untrusted input? If yes, the threat model is updated in this pull request." It links to the model's Process section.
- [x] **`cargo xtask threat-coverage`.** The code is in `xtask/src/threat_coverage.rs`, with 13 unit tests. It runs in a new `doc-checks` job in `ci.yml`, which sits behind the required `ci-ok` check. A matching row is in `xtask/src/ci.rs` STEPS and in `docs/ci.md`. The issue planned it as advisory until #230 lands. It is blocking from the start because the document passes it today. The check fails on any of these:
  - **Malformed STRIDE row:** wrong cell count, ID not `T-<component>-<nn>`, an unknown STRIDE letter, status, impact or likelihood, a reused ID, or an `N/A` row without a reason.
  - **Missing categories:** a component that does not consider all six STRIDE categories.
  - **Mitigation-table mismatch:** a missing row, a duplicate row, a row out of order, or an issue column that differs from the STRIDE row.
  - **Malformed verification entry:** every `;`-separated entry must be `TEST:`, `fuzz:` or `CI:` with backticked names, or a list of proposed `BYP-`/`RT-`/`FUZZ-`/`TEST-` IDs. A citation with a missing or mistyped tag fails, so it cannot slip past the existence check. A `TEST:` crate named without a test after it fails too.
  - **Unbacked status:** a threat marked `implemented` or `verified` with no `TEST:`, `fuzz:` or `CI:` citation, or a `verified` threat with no `BYP-*`/`RT-*` scenario. This is the rule the issue's design notes asked for.
  - **Stale citation:** any `TEST:` test function, `fuzz:` target or `CI:` command, on any row including `planned` ones, that does not exist. Test functions are found by tokenising every tracked `.rs` file of the named crate (`proc-macro2`, already an xtask dependency). Comments, string literals, `#[ignore]`d tests and the separate fuzz workspaces never count. Fuzz targets come from `xtask/src/fuzz.rs` `PROJECTS`, which a unit test already keeps in step with the fuzz `Cargo.toml` files. Commands come from every workflow's `run:` steps.
  - **Summary drift:** a "Summary by status" table that does not match the STRIDE tables.
  - **Undefined threat ID:** any tracked `.rs`/`.md` file, or the model itself, naming a threat ID of a known component that the tables do not define. On a line with a `threat:`/`threats:` annotation, any `T-…` token that is not defined fails, whatever its component or digit count. The defined IDs come from the same parser as the other rules.
  - **Blank or unrecognised rows:** every data row in the two tables is validated, not just rows starting with `T-`, and no required cell may be blank (preconditions and mitigation included). The issue's design notes ask for threat IDs to be greppable from code. This check makes those references trustworthy.
- [x] **`SECURITY.md`.** #244 already did the pointer. `SECURITY.md` links the threat model's Actors and claims table and its residual-risk register, so nothing changed here. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled: `GET /repos/jusso-dev/palisade/private-vulnerability-reporting` returns `{"enabled":true}`.
- [x] **Changelog.** Version 0.2.0 records this status review.

**Status update (the threat model's "status changes" review trigger)**

Each row now marked `implemented` cites tests that exist on `main`, and `threat-coverage` checks every citation. Where the caller, usually the agent, is still to be built, the residual-risk note says so. The status definition now says this too.

| Threat | Mitigation now on `main` | Cited checks |
|---|---|---|
| T-engine-05 | Deny-wins is the default. The mandatory-deny tier decides before every model, mode and override session. | `palisade-policy`: default and allow-wins warning tests, deny-wins property, mandatory-deny tests under every model and in every mode (#266, #270) |
| T-engine-10 | A path identifies an object only when no non-administrator can write it or any directory above it. Otherwise the criterion is unknown. | `palisade-policy` `ops::tests` ACL tests, implicit deny; `palisade-fileid` `fsctx::acl` writable-ancestor tests (#251, #248) |
| T-cache-06 | Hash cache records carry an HMAC tag. A tampered or moved record is rejected. | `palisade-fileid` `hash_cache` tamper and rekey tests (#261) |
| T-signer-02 | Domain-separation prefixes, and the signer refuses to sign outside a key's purpose. | `palisade-proto` `pki::tests` (#262) |
| T-signer-06, T-ca-08 | Trust-set key separation, anti-rollback and the fast-forward cap. These rows already cited tests; now marked `implemented`. | `palisade-proto` `pki::tests`, fuzz `trust_set_decode` (#262) |
| T-ca-05 | TLS 1.3 is preferred, `min_version = "1.3"` is available, and there is a strict profile. | `palisade-server` TLS integration tests (#255) |
| T-db-06, T-db-08 | Forced RLS, a fail-closed scope, and runtime-role checks through membership. | `palisade-server` Postgres tests, plus `CI:` the `postgres` job (#265) |
| T-ci-06 | **New rule in `check-workflows`:** every rust-cache step must set `save-if` exactly once (matched case-insensitively, as the runner matches input names) to `false` or the main-only expression. Small, but it fills the "nothing checks it" gap #241 recorded. | `xtask` `workflows::tests::rust_cache_must_only_save_on_main` |
| **T-engine-14 (new)** | A signer criterion only matches signatures whose status is valid. Signature, chain, timestamp and revocation checks fail closed. | `palisade-policy` signer test; `palisade-fileid` signature, chain and validity tests; three fuzz targets (#247, #256, #269) |
| **T-engine-15 (new)** | A catalog signature counts only when the catalog verifies under the trust config in force. Digests are used only in their own slot. | `palisade-fileid` catalog tests, fuzz `fuzz_ctl` (#268) |

T-engine-08 and T-engine-09 were already `implemented`. They now also cite the regex, chain, CRL and catalog limits, and the newer parsers' property tests and fuzz targets.

13 rows stay `planned` but gain citations of the partial code that exists. Each one's missing piece is named in its row:

- T-engine-03, T-engine-04, T-engine-06, T-engine-11
- T-driver-09
- T-agent-12, T-agent-15
- T-api-08, T-api-09
- T-db-01
- T-ca-02
- T-ingest-03, T-ingest-06

For example, T-engine-04 lacks volume GUID mapping and the agent's final-path facts (#54, #4).

Totals: 176 threats, 157 `planned`, 19 `implemented`, 0 `verified`. The VM harness, #26, does not exist yet. The residual-risk register is unchanged.

**Docs site.** The site is #27, being built in parallel. The document needs nothing site-specific. All 6 Mermaid blocks render with the Mermaid CLI, unchanged from #241. All links are relative. I coordinated with #27's implementer: the book includes `docs/security/threat-model.md` as-is, and this PR adds no new pages.

## Deferred

- **Second-person review of the residual-risk register, and the tabletop review.** These #219 acceptance criteria need a human other than the author, so an agent cannot do them. Manual step for the maintainer: review R-01 to R-17 in `docs/security/threat-model.md`, then add a changelog row naming the reviewer. If you prefer, that can happen after merge; the header and the register already say "independent re

author: handfulofluck-lab
body:
## 1. Restatement — what I understood the ask to be

> I understood the ask as: a rule the parent changes must take effect on the child within seconds, without a restart. B6 on the Flip4 showed a domain rule appearing only after the phone restarted, and staying applied after the parent removed it.

## 2. Item / issue

- Item: **#864** (beta-A blocker, `platform:android`, `K31`). Diagnosis posted on the issue at 05:52.

## 3. What changed and why

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `services/FirebaseMessagingSvc.kt:60-68` | `WorkScheduler.syncNow(applicationContext)` after the wake handler | a rules change reaches the child as a push, and nothing in that path asked for the rules |
| `test/…/RulesReachOnPushWiringTest.kt` | two wiring rows | `FirebaseMessagingService` cannot run on the JVM; the rows assert the call's **presence and position** |

**The diagnosis, because it is the whole PR:** the reload machinery was never the problem. `FilterVpnService` reloads on `ACTION_RELOAD`, after a command (`CommandDispatcher.kt:124`) and at the end of `RulesSyncWorker` (`:29`). What was missing is that nobody *asked* for the rules: `RulesSyncWorker` is scheduled **every six hours** (`WorkScheduler.kt:28`) and `WorkScheduler.syncNow()` — the only off-schedule fetch — has **exactly one caller, `PairingActivity.kt:1368`**. So a domain rule waited for the tick, a restart "fixed" it because boot reschedules, and the removal waited too — which is B6 steps 4 and 5 exactly.

**Two deliberate choices:**

- **Not keyed on a payload field.** `PushWakeHandler.onPushReceived` does not inspect `data` by design (its own docstring says so), and a key only the server knows today would fail silently the day it changes. Unconditional is the honest reading of the code we have.
- **Outside the wake budget.** `syncNow` is unique (`KEEP`) and network-constrained, so a burst of pushes collapses into one fetch; the wiring row also pins that the call sits *after* `PushWakeHandler`, because a rules fetch inside the 8-second wake budget would be cut off by the fallback and leave the phone waiting six hours anyway.

## 4. Gates I ran (raw output)

```
$ ./gradlew :app:testFullDebugUnitTest --tests "com.familyshield.agent.services.RulesReachOnPushWiringTest" \
    -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process --no-daemon
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 8m 14s
JUnit XML: tests="2" skipped="0" failures="0" errors="0"
```

**One failure on the way, recorded rather than hidden:** my first version of the test resolved its source file from the process directory and threw `NoSuchElementException` — the repo's existing wiring tests walk up from `user.dir`, and I now do the same. The row was red for a real reason (my bug), not a flake.

Not run: any device. **The row that closes #864 is on the Flip4**: add `youtube.com` from the parent, and see it blocked within a few seconds without a restart.

## 5. What the reviewer must verify (falsifiable claims)

1. `onMessageReceived` calls `WorkScheduler.syncNow(applicationContext)` — deleting it must redden the wiring row.
2. The call sits **after** `PushWakeHandler.onPushReceived(...)`, not inside its budget.
3. `syncNow` is still `ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP` and network-constrained, so a push storm does not become a fetch storm (`WorkScheduler.kt:62-72`, unchanged).
4. The command path is untouched: a block/unblock command still reloads the filter directly (`CommandDispatcher.kt:124`).

## 6. Open questions, assumptions, deliberately not done

- **Assumption:** any push is rare enough that a deduped rules fetch per push is cheap. Pushes today are rule changes, commands and token events; if the server ever pushes per-message, this needs a key.
- **Not done:** the killed-process case. A phone whose process is dead receives no push, so the six-hour worker remains its only path — that is #1085's world, and #1098's recovery tick is the natural place to also request a rules sync when it finds a gap. I left that out rather than growing this diff.
- **Worth a follow-up:** the server could send the rules version in the command-poll response; comparing it to `appliedRulesVersion` would bound the worst case to a minute with no new request. That is a server change and belongs with whoever owns the poll contract.

## 7. Discussion

- [ ] I have read the reviewer's point-by-point reply
- [ ] Every point is answered with evidence (or explicitly deferred with `needs-human`)
- [ ] Any change to my restatement in §1 is re-stated and agreed before merge
- [ ] The point-by-point exchange is in this PR's comments

— K31

author: claude[bot]
body:
## What failed

ToastDifferential (issue #1145, commit fdef3376) ran a program whose first effective call is

```moo
rindex("b", "%b\tb$\t", "aeaba\"", 9223372036854775807)
```

Toast raised `E_TYPE` for the whole program, Barn `E_INVARG`.

## Cause

Toast's `bf_index`/`bf_rindex` (`src/list.cc:1117-1147`) store the fourth argument in a C `int offset`, so only the low 32 bits count: `9223372036854775807` becomes `-1`. `rindex` accepts `-1` and returns 0 (the program then fails later with `E_TYPE` on `0.owner`), and `index` rejects it with `E_INVARG`.

Barn used the full 64-bit value: `builtins/strings.go:122` (`index`) and `builtins/strings.go:189` (`rindex`). So `rindex` raised `E_INVARG` for a positive offset, and `index` with the same offset returned 0.

## Fix

Truncate the offset with `int(int32(...))` in both builtins, the same conversion Toast's C assignment makes.

## Verification

Differential harness against the WSL Toast oracle (`/root/src/toaststunt/build-release/moo`, sha256 `61dd1799…613dd`, ToastStunt 2.8.0) on the issue's program plus 11 probes (offsets `2^63-1`, `2^32-1`, `2^32`, `2^31`, `-2^32`, `2^32+3` for both builtins):

- before the fix: 4 divergences, including the issue's `toast raised E_TYPE / barn raised E_INVARG`
- after: exit 0, `{"records": 12, ... "completed": 12}`, no divergence

The new `TestIndexOffsetKeepsLow32Bits` (expected values taken from Toast) fails without the fix (`index("b", "x", 0, 9223372036854775807) flow = 0 error = E_NONE, want E_INVARG`, …) and passes with it. `go test ./builtins` passes.

The issue's input wasn't added under `testdata/fuzz`. It is a differential-only divergence, and no native Go fuzz target fails on it, so `scripts/fuzz_red_green.py` would refuse it. The Go regression test above pins the behaviour instead.

## Known related gaps

- `index()` with an offset larger than the string length: Toast (`src/list.cc:1128`) passes `source + offset` and `len - offset` to `strindex` without bounds checking, so it reads past the buffer (undefined behaviour). Barn returns 0 (`builtins/strings.go:141`). No conformance expectation exists for it, and I did not change it.

Fixes #1145

body:
## O que
Requisito **essencial "parcial"** da tela 326 (blueprint `hub_projetos`): *"Portal com … painel de andamento da obra com as últimas atualizações"*.

A prévia do portal do cliente já mostra **avanço**, **fotos do diário** e **medições** em blocos detalhados, mas não havia um **resumo glanceável** no topo — o cliente (e a equipe conferindo a prévia) precisava rolar para entender o estado da obra num relance.

## Como (front-only, aditivo, sem núcleo)
- Faixa **"Resumo do andamento"** no topo da prévia com 3 mini-indicadores:
  - **Avanço** — % concluído;
  - **Última medição** — valor + competência/situação (a mais recente por `aprovada_em`/`competencia`);
  - **Último registro no diário** — data + atividade (o RDO mais recente).
- Derivado **só do que a tela já carrega** (`fn_obra_portal_avanco` / `_fotos` / `_medicoes`, page.tsx l.96-100) — **sem nova RPC, sem migration, sem tocar núcleo nem RLS**.
- Mostra só quando há algo a resumir (`resumo.temAlgo`); cada indicador degrada para `—` com texto "sem medição/diário ainda".
- **RD-95**: `?` (AjudaCampo) em cada indicador reusando as chaves **já publicadas** `obra.portal.avanco` / `obra.portal.medicoes` / `obra.portal.fotos` (nenhuma chave nova).
- **RD-96/RD-100**: linguagem e layout próprios. Mobile-first: `flex-wrap`, mínimos de 120px por indicador.

## Prova (RD-38)
Não há SQL nesta PR — é só render. As 3 chaves de ajuda reusadas existem publicadas em `erp_ajuda_campo` (`obra.portal.avanco`, `obra.portal.medicoes`, `obra.portal.fotos`, `status=publicado`). Os tipos consumidos (`Avanco.pct_conclusao`, `MedicaoPrev.valor_total/competencia/status/aprovada_em`, `FotoDia.data/atividades`) são os mesmos já usados nos blocos detalhados logo abaixo.

## 概要

本文に何を出すか（`PreviewTarget`）を、サイドバーの選択と一覧の行から導くのをやめ、窓ごとの意図（`PresentationIntent`）から決める。サイドバーは、その後で意図に合わせる。方針は ADR 0013（Accepted）で、移行の (a)〜(e)（TASK-930.1〜930.5）と、コードレビューの指摘への対応（TASK-930.6〜930.9）を含む。

ファイルを開いた直後に本文へフォルダー一覧が重なる不具合（#794 ほか 2 経路）が直る。

Closes #794

## 変更内容

### 意図の型と書き手（TASK-930.1 / 930.2）

- **`PresentationIntent`**（`befold/Viewer/PresentationIntent.swift`）: 窓ごとに 1 つ持つ意図。本文のビュー・capabilities・タイトル・履歴の記録が読む
  - 書くのは利用者の操作を受けた入口だけ。窓の生成、ファイル切替、開いている文書の選び直し、フォルダー行の選択、フォルダーへの移動、履歴の再生
  - サイドバー側の型（`SidebarNavigator` とその協力型、`FileListModel`）は参照を持たない。同期処理（取り直し・展開・レイアウト切り替え）からは書けない
- **削除**: `PreviewTargetResolver`、`FileListModel` の提示対象の導出と通知、`PreviewTarget.undetermined`
- **開き直し**: フォルダー一覧を出している窓で、開いている文書を CLI・Finder・最近使った項目・Quick Open から開き直すと、文書の提示へ戻る
- 窓の中でファイルを開く経路は `performFileSwitch` に集まる。「意図 → 本文 → サイドバー」の順は構造で決まっている

### フォルダーとディレクトリ（TASK-930.3 / 930.4 / 930.8）

- **フォルダーに入る・上へ移動する**: 記憶した選択や先頭行を自動で選ばず、移動先の一覧を出す（一覧の着地を待たない）。`SidebarSelectionMemory` を撤去した
- **`befold <ディレクトリ>`・Finder・Dock**: 中のファイルを開かず、その一覧を出す窓（文書を持たない `BlankTabWindowController`）を開く。空のディレクトリでもアラートではなく空の一覧を出す
- **同じディレクトリをもう一度開く**: 既存の一覧の窓を前面に出す（`--new-window` は常に新規）。規則は `BlankTabCoordinator.openFolder` に置き、再利用の表は文書の窓と `ViewerWindowOpenPolicy.reusableWindow` で共有する
- **サイドバーのフォルダー行**: 「新しいタブ/ウィンドウで開く」（メニュー・⌘クリック・⌘Return）は、中の最初のファイルではなくそのフォルダーの一覧を開く。フォルダー行ではスライドモードを出さない
  - 不要になった `containsSupportedFile` / `firstSupportedFile` を撤去した。一覧を取るたびにフォルダー行ごとに中を列挙していた処理も消える
- **CLI**:
  - `--compare` は、パスがすべてディレクトリなら `--diff` なしで通り、一覧の窓のサイドバーの git バッジに効く
  - 文書向けの指定（`--source`/`--preview`/`--diff`・行番号・`--line`）をディレクトリだけに付けると、標準エラーへ警告して窓は開く（終了コード 0）

### 履歴（TASK-930.5）

- 戻る・進むのエントリは、記録時の窓の意図を持つ。フォルダーに入ったときは、一覧の着地を待たず意図を書いた時点で記録する
  - これまでは着地前に別のファイルを開くと、フォルダーの訪問が履歴から落ちていた
- 再生では、記録した意図をサイドバーの同期より先に書く

### レビュー指摘への対応（TASK-930.6 / 930.7 / 930.9）

- **930.6**: フォルダー一覧の表示中にファイル切替が失敗したとき、選択を開いている文書の行ではなく、本文の意図に合わせて戻す（`SidebarPostSwitchSync.restoreSelection(on:)`）
- **930.7**: 一覧を出しているフォルダーが削除・改名で無くなったら、窓がキーに戻ったときと、その一覧の履歴へ戻ったときに、開いている文書へ戻す（一覧の窓は空タブの画面）
  - 判定はディレクトリの実在で行う
  - ADR 0013 の決定 2 に、この書き手を例外として追記した
- **930.9**: ADR 0013 の現状調査の見出しに調査日を入れた

### サイドバーの ⌘クリック（TASK-931）

- ⌘ / ⌘⇧ クリックで、新しいタブを開いたうえに起点のタブまで同じファイルへ切り替わっていた。SwiftUI の `List` が同じクリックで行の選択を書き戻し、それが「いまのタブで開く」経路（`commitSelection`）に入っていた。main にもある経路で、このブランチ由来ではない
- `FileListView.tableSelection` の setter で、書き戻しを起こしたイベントが修飾キー付きクリック（⌃ / ⌘ / ⌘⇧）なら確定しない（`acceptsTableSelectionWrite`）。判定はタップとの前後関係やフラグではなく、イベントそのもので行う。キーボードによる選択移動は従来どおり開く（#570）
- 確定しなかった回は表の選択を元の行へ戻す（`FileListModel.restoreTableSelection`）。戻さないとハイライトだけがクリックした行に残ることを実機で確かめた

### 文書と型グループ

- ADR 0013 / decision-14 を Accepted にした
- `docs/dev/native-app-design.md`・`viewer-ui.md`・`cli-launch.md`・`rules/product-code.md` を新しい挙動に合わせた
- 型グループの例外表は実測値へ更新した: `ViewerWindowController` 963、`SidebarNavigator` 406。`ViewerWindowManager` は閾値 400 以内に収めた（例外は足していない）

### 利用者に見える挙動の変化

- `befold <ディレクトリ>` は、最初のファイルを開かず一覧を出す。同じディレクトリを再度開くと、既存の窓を前面に出す
- リスト表示でフォルダーに入ると、そのフォルダーの一覧が出る（記憶していた選択の復元・先頭の項目の自動オープンはしない）
- ツリーで祖先フォルダーを畳んでも、本文は変わらない
- 一覧を出しているフォルダーが消えたら、開いている文書へ戻る
- サイドバーのフォルダー行の新しいタブ/ウィンドウは一覧を開く。フォルダー行のメニューにスライドモードは無い。⌘クリック・⌘Return もフォルダー行で効く
- `--compare` をディレクトリにだけ単独で付けられる。文書向けの指定をディレクトリだけに付けると警告が出る

## 検証

- **回帰テスト**: どれも修正を戻す変異を入れると落ちることを確かめた
  - `ViewerWindowFileOpenPresentationTests`（実ファイル、ツリー表示とリスト表示）。ファイルを開く経路、フォルダーへの移動、切替の失敗、フォルダーの消失を扱う
  - `ViewerWindowHistoryPresentationTests`。履歴の記録の時点、再生の順序、ファイルのエントリ、消えたフォルダーを扱う
  - `DocumentOpenerFolderTests`。ディレクトリを開く、再利用、`--compare` が git 取得の基準になる、フォルダー行を別の場所で開く、を扱う
  - サイドバーの修飾キー・⌘Return・メニュー項目のテストと、CLI の警告・`--compare` の検証のテスト
- **全件テスト**: `swift test --skip PDF` 2015 件、`--filter PDF` 103 件、CLI 85 件がすべて通過
- **静的検査**:
  - swiftformat の差分なし
  - swiftlint は変更ファイルで新規 0 件（`FileListEntry` の `id` の警告は main からの既存）
  - `scripts/check-type-group-size.sh --check` 通過
  - `xcodegen generate` の後に `xcodebuild build -scheme befold` が成功
- **実機確認**:
  - #794 の経路だけ確認した（TASK-930.1）。ツリー表示の ⌘P で、畳まれた `docs/` 配下のファイルを開いたとき、提示の変化は文書の 1 件だけで、フォルダー一覧の提示は 0 件だった
  - 930.2 以降は未確認（テストのみ）
- **TASK-931 の実機確認**（開発ビルドに一時ログを入れて測定。ログはコミットしていない）:
  - 修正あり: 1 タブで `b.md` ⌘ / `sub` ⌘ / `c.md` をクリックし、起点のタブは `a.md` のまま、いまのタブで開いた記録は 0 件、ハイライトは `a.md` に戻った。新しいタブは右端に開いた
  - 修正を無効化: `b.md` ⌘ と `c.md` ⌘⇧ で起点のタブが切り替わり、再現した
  - `swift test --skip Integration --skip FileWatcherTests --skip PDF` 1906 件通過。swiftlint は main とのベースライン差分ゼロ
  - 修正ありの版での ⌘⇧ クリックは記録できていない（無効化した版では、判定が ⌘⇧ でも確定しないことを記録した）
- **未検証**: 「変更のあるファイルのみ」が ON のとき、`--compare` 付きでディレクトリを開くと、絞り込みが一瞬空になるか

### マージ前に実機で確かめたいこと

1. サイドバーのフォルダー行の右クリックメニューにスライドが無く、新しいタブ/ウィンドウでその一覧が開く。⌘Return も同じ（⌘クリックは TASK-931 の実機確認で、起点のタブが変わらないところまで確かめた）
2. 新しいタブが背面に開く（ファイル行の ⌘クリックは TASK-931 で確認済み）
3. `befold <dir>` を 2 回実行すると、既存の窓が前面に出る
4. 一覧を出しているフォルダーを Finder で消してから窓に戻ると、文書に戻る
5. `befold --line 10 <dir>` で警告が出る

author: jhontmich
body:
## Qué cambia

Reduce el consumo de red, batería y escrituras en disco sin cambiar lo que ve la persona.

- **Sincronización:** con el tiempo real conectado, la recarga completa de la cuenta (unas 17 consultas) pasa de cada minuto a cada 5 minutos. Si el socket cae, vuelve a cada minuto, y al reconectarse se recarga una vez.
- **Caché y widget:** una recarga sin cambios ya no reescribe la copia local ni publica el widget (ni reprograma recordatorios o asistencia). Igualmente se escribe cada 5 minutos para que la hora de sincronización no envejezca.
- **Ubicación en segundo plano:** la comprobación periódica usa primero wifi y antenas (y reutiliza una ubicación de hasta 2 min). Solo enciende el GPS si la precisión no llega a 100 m.
- **Ubicación con la app abierta:** se comprueba al abrir y luego cada 5 minutos, en vez de cada minuto. Las geocercas siguen avisando al entrar y salir.
- **Almacenamiento:** la copia de la cuenta se guarda en su propio archivo de DataStore (`account_cache`), con una migración desde `user_preferences`.

## Pruebas

- `testDebugUnitTest` completo, con pruebas nuevas: `LiveUpdatesPollTest`, `SkipUnchangedTest` y precisión mínima en `AutoPlacesTest`.
- `compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin` y `assembleRelease` sin errores (APK de 5,33 MB).
- Pendiente en un teléfono real:
  - que la migración conserve la copia al actualizar desde 1.9.4;
  - que la detección de lugares siga siendo fiable con la precisión equilibrada;
  - que el tiempo real siga llegando al instante.

author: rpoyner-tri
body: `ProjectedGradientDescentSolver::SetProjectionSolverInterface()` stores a raw pointer to the interface it is given, but the Python binding did not tie the interface's lifetime to the solver. If the caller dropped its own reference, the interface was freed while the solver still pointed at it, and a later `Solve()` used freed memory: ```python solver = ProjectedGradientDescentSolver() solver.SetProjectionSolverInterface(ClarabelSolver()) solver.Solve(prog, None, None) # crashes ``` This stores the interface in a single attribute of the solver's Python object, in a way that Python's garbage collector can see. The same approach is used for `Simulator.set_monitor`. Setting a new interface, or passing `None`, releases the previous one. (`py::keep_alive` would also fix the crash, but it keeps every previous interface alive until the solver dies, and it hides reference cycles from the collector.) Found while surveying the issue "investigate uses of WrapCallbacks() for memory leaks" (#24162), but this is a crash fix and is independent of the other work there. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/RobotLocomotion/drake/25301)

author: willfrey
body:
The web app, stage 5 of `docs/build-plan.md`: the first point where a person can use the system. After this, `uv run airworthy` serves a fleet board on a fresh copy of the sample fleet.

## What a person gets

- **Fleet board** (`/`): each aircraft as cleared to fly or grounded, with the write-ups that ground it named, and per aircraft the open write-ups that still need a repair date and the ones whose repair date has passed. A summary line counts the cleared aircraft.
- **Aircraft page** (`/aircraft/{tail}`): each write-up with its severity, where it stands, and its full history, plus the actions its state allows: set a repair date, resolve, change the severity (with a reason), reopen. A form files a new write-up.
- **Past views**: either page takes `?at=` and shows what was known at that moment. A past view has no forms, since an action is always taken now.
- A form the domain refuses (resolving twice, a blank name, a date that isn't one) re-renders the aircraft page with a 400 and the reason. An unknown aircraft or write-up is a 404.

## Design

- No rule lives in the web layer. A form's text becomes an event through the same Pydantic models the store reads, the store's `append` checks it against the write-up's state under the write lock, and a `RefusedError` is shown as worded by the domain.
- Where a write-up stands (needs a repair date, scheduled, overdue, resolved) is one function, `standing`, in the write-up module. The board and the aircraft page both read it.
- The time of an action comes from a clock passed to `create_app`, so tests fix it. `main` takes the server as a parameter for the same reason.
- Templates are autoescaped; a test posts markup as a description and checks it comes back as text.

## Departures from the plan

- No `/work` page. The plan names it as the first thing to drop; the board carries its content as two columns (needs a repair date, overdue).
- `create_app(store, clock)` takes no suggester, because the AI triage stage is not built.
- A 400 re-render does not keep what was typed in the form.

## Checked

- `scripts/check`: 109 tests, 100% branch coverage. `scripts/mutation`: 581 mutants, 0 survived.
- mutmut does not mutate templates or module-level constants, so ten breaks were made by hand and each seen to fail a test: autoescape off; every aircraft shown cleared; the summary counting grounded aircraft; the overdue column listing unscheduled write-ups; the board link dropping the past moment; a past view offering forms; a resolved write-up offering a repair date; the aircraft status inverted; a POST route answering to GET; a missing aircraft answered with 400.
- The real server was started and driven with curl: board loads with 2 of 6 cleared, resolving the windshield write-up redirects with 303 and the board then shows 3 of 6, and resolving it again is a 400.

## Summary by Sourcery

Serve an interactive web application for monitoring aircraft readiness and managing write-ups through domain-validated actions.

New Features:
- Add a server-rendered fleet board and aircraft pages for viewing fleet status, write-up details, history, and current standing.
- Enable filing write-ups and performing state-allowed follow-up actions through web forms.
- Support historical fleet and aircraft views at a specified moment, with actions disabled for past views.
- Add a runnable `airworthy` command with configurable port and persistent database options.

Bug Fixes:
- Handle oversized write-up IDs as not-found records instead of database errors.
- Reject unsafe aircraft tail numbers and invalid historical timestamps with appropriate client errors.

Enhancements:
- Centralize write-up standing and follow-up eligibility so the web views consistently reflect domain state.
- Return clear validation and domain refusal messages while preserving HTML escaping for user-provided content.

Build:
- Add FastAPI, Jinja2, multipart form, Uvicorn, and HTTP client dependencies and expose the `airworthy` console script.

Documentation:
- Document how to run the web application with fresh or persistent fleet data.

Tests:
- Add comprehensive web application coverage for views, historical rendering, form actions, validation, refusals, routing, escaping, and server startup.

body:
Several documents said that an `npm run …` or `lint:…` script holds a rule. This repository has no such scripts.

**Rewritten where a check holds the rule**
- `contract/TRANSPORT-HTTP.md`: ids are held by the reader's identifier rules (`reader/lib/identifiers_rules.ml`, `make reader`).
- `specs/src/archivist/openapi.json`, `specs/src/client/timing.json`: the order of the waits is held by the reader's protocol rules (`reader/lib/protocol_rules.ml`).
- `contract/EVENT-BUS.md`, adding a channel: step 5 is `make validate` here and step 6 is `make generate` in the sdk repository, as step 1 already says.
- `specs/src/stack/README.md`: the launcher (`cli/internal/launcher/stack/read_test.go`) runs every case of `cases.json`.

**Removed where nothing runs the check the sentence named**
- `contract/WEAVER.md`, `contract/WORKER-SERVICE.md`, `contract/LIBRARIAN.md`: nothing holds the cases these documents name to the suites. Each still says a rule marked "Held by no case" is one nothing checks.
- `specs/src/stack/README.md`: nothing validates the launcher's fixture knowledge base, or holds a schema's properties to the types' fields.
- `specs/src/locales/registry.json`: nothing holds the translation files to the list.
- `specs/src/service-environment/variables.json`: nothing scans a Rust service's reads, or checks the launcher's boot golden.

These are gaps that a check could close later. No rule, shape or case changes; only prose and `$comment`/`description` text. `make validate` passes locally.

author: thep0y
body:
## Summary

Make `CarouselItem` hide only slides that are actually outside the visible range.

## Problem

- `index` is optional, but when it was omitted every slide got `aria-hidden="true"`.
- With multiple slides visible (`basis-1/2`), only `currentIndex` was exposed; the second visible slide was hidden from assistive technology.
- `aria-hidden` was applied even to slides containing focusable elements, so keyboard users could tab into content that screen readers could not announce.

## Changes

- Derive `visibleCount` from the measured item size and viewport size.
- Mark slides visible when their index is in `[currentIndex, currentIndex + visibleCount)`.
- When `index` is not provided, do not hide the slide.
- Add assertions for multi-visible layouts and for the no-index case.

## Verification

author: markgatcha
body:
## Summary

Three measured accuracy improvements to the hybrid retrieval pipeline, validated end-to-end on the repo's own harnesses (LoCoMo retrieval-only, bench-quality, bench-memory, bench-crossrepo, HotPotQA retrieval, eval:retrieval CI gate).

Headline numbers (LoCoMo retrieval-only, evidence-ID matching, fastembed/bge-small):

| Metric @10 | dev baseline | this PR (default) | this PR + local rerank |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hit rate | 65.6% | 67.5% | 70.2% |
| Evidence recall | 61.8% | 63.7% | 67.0% |
| All-evidence recall | 58.6% | 60.3% | 64.2% |
| MRR | 0.458 | 0.455 | 0.485 |
| nDCG | 0.484 | 0.486 | 0.519 |

With rerank on, every official LoCoMo category stays at or above the no-rerank baseline (adversarial 76.1 vs 74.6, multi_hop hit 46.5 vs 41.9, single_hop 67.5 vs 59.6, temporal 90.5 vs 87.3).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- **`src/memory.ts` — rerank ordering fix.** The canonical pre-expansion re-sort silently undid cross-encoder reranking: the reranker re-scores only the head with sigmoid-squashed CE logits while tail items keep fused scores, and the comparator re-sort interleaved tail items back above reranked head items. The reranker's ordering is now left untouched exactly like MMR output; detection is by array identity since every no-op path in `applyRerank` returns the input unchanged. (Rerank enabled, pre-fix: Hit@10 50.0%; post-fix: 70.9% pure-CE ordering.)
- **`src/memory.ts` / `src/types.ts` — `experimental.rerank.blend` (default 0.5).** Pure CE ordering is sharp but brittle on adversarially-phrased queries: literal-match traps outscore genuine evidence (adversarial Hit@10 −8.4 pts vs baseline). Blend mixes each head item's min-max-normalized fused score into the ordering key; at 0.5 no LoCoMo category regresses. `blend: 0` restores pure-CE ordering for maximum raw precision; `MEMOS_RERANK_BLEND` overrides for experiments. The emitted `score` stays the sigmoid CE score either way, so downstream gates see one scale.
- **`src/storage/sqlite.ts` — FTS AUTO backfill.** AUTO previously relaxed AND→OR only when AND matched *nothing*, so thin non-empty AND legs wasted candidate slots. Now a genuinely thin AND leg (<5 rows) is backfilled with the OR query's partial-term matches. Filler scoring is corpus-size aware: bm25 idf is meaningful only on larger corpora (≥200 nodes), where filler keeps its native rank; below that the single-rare-term pathology can outscore multi-term full matches (and fusion normalizes by score, not array position), so filler is remapped into a band capped at 25% of the leg's normalized range, strictly below every full match.
- **Tests updated** for the new contracts: AUTO ranks full matches first with partials below (`memos.test.ts`, `search-upgrades.test.ts`); rerank ordering tests pin `blend: 0` for pure-CE monotonicity and add `blend: 1` fused-order coverage (`rerank-local.test.ts`).
- **Refreshed generated bench artifacts** (bench-quality, bench-memory, bench-crossrepo results).

### Review round (commits `33fe947`, `837e3b8` — Devin Review findings)

- **`src/storage/sqlite.ts`** — AUTO backfill pagination fix: the AND/OR merge now runs unpaginated and slices exactly one page, so later pages can no longer repeat earlier hits or overshoot `limit`; filler is placed at exact normalized-cap targets so tied full matches cannot rescale filler above the 25% cap. Regression test asserts disjoint pages and limit compliance, and the AUTO backfill assertion is now unconditional.
- **`src/memory.ts` (endpoint path)** — partial endpoint responses no longer jump scored hits ahead of omitted hits: the whole head is merged by the blend ordering key (unscored candidates key as −∞, NaN-safe comparator, fused-position tiebreak), so `blend: 1` output keeps pure fused order end to end.
- **`src/memory.ts` / `src/context-pack.ts`** — ranking modulators (importance/Ebbinghaus) no longer re-sort by raw score when the reranker ran (score adjustments still apply in place), and context-pack trusts input order when any item carries `scores.rerank` instead of comparator-sorting mixed CE/fused scales.
- **`src/flight-recorder.ts` / `src/types.ts`** — the CE/fused blend is recorded in the trace config and replay recomputes the same blended key over the rerank window, so a no-override replay reproduces the recorded ranking instead of reordering by CE alone.

## Validation details

- `eval:retrieval`: PASS within tolerance of baseline (recall@5 0.9792 / mrr 0.9688 gate), re-verified after the review-round fixes.
- `bench-quality`: recall@5/10 100%, MRR 0.868 → **0.947**. Two caveats: this harness is noisy run-to-run on identical code (19 queries; observed recall@5 spread 0.79–1.0 across repeats), and the committed baseline artifact predates the bench's switch to the internal `bench-hash-v1` embedder — so treat the MRR delta as directional only. The deterministic evidence is LoCoMo / HotPotQA / eval:retrieval.
- `bench-memory`: recall@10 0.939 → **0.970**, precision@10 0.097 → **0.598**.
- `bench-crossrepo`: recall flat 0.970, precision 0.185 → **0.633**, p95 5ms → 3ms.
- HotPotQA retrieval-only (500 dev questions, fastembed): Hit@10 **99.8%**, EvRec@10 89.7%, MRR 0.883.
- Full Jest suite: 1480 passed; the single failure (`cli-completion` "passes bash syntax check") fails identically on clean `dev` — it shells out to `bash -n`, unavailable on this Windows runner. (`context-pack-audit` shows 4 failures on this runner from Jest's inability to `require()` the ESM-only `@yarflam/potion-base-8m`; byte-identical with this PR's changes stashed.)

```bash
pnpm test                    # pre-existing env failures only (bash -n; ESM require)
pnpm run typecheck           # clean
pnpm run lint                # clean
pnpm run eval:retrieval      # PASS within tolerance
pnpm exec tsx scripts/bench-locomo-noapi.ts --provider=fastembed --fail-on-embedding-fallback --topk=10
MEMOS_RERANK_LOCAL=1 pnpm exec tsx scripts/bench-locomo-noapi.ts --provider=fastembed --topk=10
```

- [x] All existing tests pass (except the pre-existing env failures, unchanged on dev)
- [x] I've added tests for new functionality (blend ordering coverage)
- [x] I've tested manually with a local MemOS instance (benchmark harnesses above)

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines (`npm run lint` passes)
- [x] I've updated the relevant documentation (JSDoc/doc comments on changed behavior)
- [x] My changes don't introduce any cloud dependencies or telemetry
- [x] I've reviewed my own diff before requesting a review

## Known environment issues (pre-existing on dev, not caused by this PR)

- `bench-haystack` and `bench-hotpot` crash with a V8 semi-space commit failure when other heavy node processes run concurrently on this memory-constrained runner; both run clean solo (hotpot results above). Reproduces byte-identically on clean `dev`.
- `bench-quality` run-to-run noise noted above.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- Grouped-turn ingestion (+5.3 Hit@10 on LoCoMo but −0.06 MRR): real tradeoff, needs a product decision on ingestion granularity rather than a silent default change.
- Widening PRF (`experimental.prfExpansion`) gates: with backfill active the keyword leg is rarely thin enough for PRF to fire; no measured gain.
- Relevance-gate cutoff semantics after rerank: blending can put a lower CE score on top, which lowers the gate's ratio reference. Escalated from review — needs a design decision on what the gate should reference post-rerank; tracked as a follow-up.
- `eval/retrieval-baseline.json` refresh: metrics unchanged within tolerance, so the baseline stands.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/68e2ab1f927944ea8ccd69d2c81eb005
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/68e2ab1f927944ea8ccd69d2c81eb005?variant=devin

author: chin0312
body:
## Summary

Continue the existing Phase 1 backend foundation on feat/backend-foundation. Changes remain inside backend/**; frontend PR #1, web/, design-system files, and the root .gitignore are untouched. This PR remains open and unmerged. Phase 1 stays in progress until review, merge, and acceptance.

## Backend foundation

- TypeScript, Fastify, PostgreSQL, Drizzle, Zod, and exact decimal strings backed by NUMERIC(38,18); no P&L engine or frontend calculation changes.
- Provider-neutral events, markets, instruments, fills, cash movements, settlements, position and cash snapshots, prices, source provenance/revisions, entity coverage, sync runs, and checkpoints.
- Two deterministic fixture adapters, independent stream contracts, authorized read APIs, OpenAPI, migrations, local setup, and a separate PostgreSQL 17 backend workflow. No live provider integration is claimed.

## Final integrity fixes

- **Snapshot recovery:** complete authoritative snapshots require full-refresh pagination. A saved cursor from an interrupted attempt is cleared atomically with the next run, which starts at page one. Only rows from that completed run can publish. Partial attempts preserve prior current state; complete empty snapshots clear it and retain a snapshot watermark. A failed finalization is recovered by the next full refresh.
- **Closed positions and stale snapshots:** zero positions remain as internal current tombstones while the active positions API omits zero quantity. Incremental records are checked against both the current observation and the complete-snapshot watermark. Complete empty snapshots still record their as-of watermark; older observations and older complete snapshots cannot restore holdings or balances. Rejected stale snapshots keep the prior successful timestamp and report stale_snapshot_rejected.
- **Independent event and market revisions:** eventSourceUpdatedAt and market sourceUpdatedAt are compared separately. An older event revision cannot overwrite current event metadata or block import of a new valid market/instrument. A stale market revision cannot replace that market. The test imports a new market and fill under an event whose stored revision is newer.
- **Entity-level success and coverage:** lastSuccessfulSyncAt advances only after the stream completes and the entity reports complete or partial data; complete-snapshot entities also require successful publication. Unknown/unavailable results and unpublished stale snapshots preserve the prior success time. Coverage start/end values are outer bounds across reports, not proof of continuous or lifetime history.
- **Migration:** 0003 adds snapshot watermarks, backfills them where a completed snapshot is known, and preserves a latest legacy zero position as an ordering tombstone.

## User-controlled data architecture

The current ownership chain is users → portfolios → provider accounts → source and financial records. A portfolio can contain multiple source accounts. The file_import account kind is only a starting boundary; no CSV import flow exists. Events/markets/instruments are provider-scoped shared metadata, while financial records and prices are account-linked.

Source payloads and financial records are plaintext to backend services and database operators. Payloads have no expiry/retention policy; provider credentials are not stored. Production authentication, source disconnect, user export/deletion, and credential management are not implemented. Database cascades exist for user-owned rows, while shared market metadata may remain.

The docs record the intended privacy-first direction without claiming technical guarantees: user-selected sources, public wallet tracking without treating an address as proof of ownership, verified read-only account scopes, canonical CSV normalization with import provenance, cross-device identity separate from provider identity, defined retention/export/deletion, and distinct disconnect versus delete semantics. Future market lookup should parse supported provider URLs and call trusted APIs only; hypothetical Scenario Lab positions need a separate model from real holdings. These product features remain planned.

## Validation

- npm run check passed: lint, production and test TypeScript checks, all 36 tests across four files, and production build. Tests include clean PGlite migrations, migration upgrade/backfill, nonempty multi-page recovery, stale closures/snapshots, event/market ordering, entity freshness, and coverage bounds.
- npx drizzle-kit check passed.
- npm audit --audit-level=high reported zero vulnerabilities.
- git diff --check passed.
- [GitHub Actions run 45563759544](https://github.com/chin0312/scevia/actions/runs/45563759544) passed on commit f01dd10 against PostgreSQL 17: npm run check, db:migrate, db:seed, built-server HTTP smoke test, and npm audit.

## PR #1 compatibility and remaining limits

PR #1 remains open and unmerged; its current state is mergeable. This change does not touch it. Its sample calculations use JavaScript numbers, date-only values, binary YES/NO sides, and a boolean fee-known field; this backend preserves decimal strings, UTC timestamps, provider-native outcomes, nullable marks, three fee states, buy/sell fills, and distinct transfers/adjustments. The coordinated mapping notes remain in backend/docs/FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md.

There is no production Polymarket/Kalshi/Predict.fun adapter, production identity, secret vault, CSV importer, market search, URL resolver, export/delete API, retention policy, background job system, trading, or custody function. This is not production privacy/security certification.

## Phase 2 handoff

Verify current official Polymarket documentation and sanitized responses for public wallet identity, endpoints, rate limits, pagination/order, fills/fees, cash movements, settlement/redemption data, position completeness/as-of, market/outcome identity, and price semantics. Add captured contract fixtures and reconcile a known wallet by source IDs and exact decimals. Start public market lookup as an account-independent adapter capability where provider APIs allow it. Keep unsupported history and discrepancies explicit; use no trading or custody permissions.

**Merge readiness:** the Phase 1 baseline is ready for maintainer review and merge: local checks and PostgreSQL 17 CI pass, and PR #3 is open and mergeable. No merge was performed.

- **Table:** `table__link`, and `table__cell--truncate` limited by `--table-truncate-width`.
- **Card:** `card__link`.
- **Stat:** `stat--interactive`; the applied filter is marked with `aria-current="true"`, matching the kit's attribute-based state rules.
- **Dropdown:** `dropdown__item--warning` (in `--warning-muted-fg`, readable on white) and `dropdown__menu--scrollable`.
- **Form:** `form__addon--btn`; `switch__text` and `switch__description` for a switch with a description; `radiocard`.

## Not added

- Lexicon's `table--sm`, `select--sm`, `card__content--empty`, `stat--active` and `toggle` map to existing kit classes or attributes (`table--compact`, `select input--sm`, `card__content--flush`, `aria-current`, `switch` with `switch__text`).

- `contentheader` and Lexicon's mobile-header and toolbar Go-button rules depend on Lexicon's own layout and stay there.

## Markup changes

None for existing sites: every change is an addition, and existing defaults are kept.

author: slaid098
body:
## Что сделано

Issue #115: единый порт БД с двумя реализациями, версионированные миграции,
импорт SQLite → PostgreSQL и PostgreSQL-набор в CI. Поведение продукта не
меняется: без `CONTENT_FACTORY_DATABASE_URL` сервис работает на прежнем
`app_data/db/db.sqlite3`.

- **Порт.** `db/connection.py` — единственное место с `sqlite3`/`psycopg`.
  Наружу `execute`, `executemany`, `commit`, `rollback`, `close`, контекстный
  менеджер, `rowcount`, строки по имени и позиции, `columns()` и
  `has_table()`. Ошибки драйверов переводятся в `db.errors`.
- **Выбор бэкенда.** `Settings.database_url` из
  `CONTENT_FACTORY_DATABASE_URL`; допускаются только `postgresql://` и
  `postgres://`, иначе `ConfigError`. Сигнатуры `connect(db_path)` /
  `connect_readonly(db_path)` сохранены; в режиме PostgreSQL путь SQLite не
  создаётся и не проверяется. `db_exists()` заменил `db_path.is_file()`.
- **SQL.** Плейсхолдеры остались `?`, PostgreSQL-адаптер переводит их в `%s`.
  `INSERT OR IGNORE` заменён на `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, `recent_titles`
  сортирует `created_at DESC, sha256 DESC`.
- **Миграции.** `db/migrations/0001_initial.py` создаёт финальную схему семи
  таблиц, включая `content_type`, `language` и частичный UNIQUE
  `videos(author) WHERE status='downloaded'`, и добавляет недостающие колонки
  старой dev-SQLite. Раннер применяет версии по одной транзакции под
  `pg_advisory_lock` / файловым lock, один раз на процесс при первом
  `connect()`. Вручную: `python -m content_factory.db.migrate`.
- **Импорт.** `python -m content_factory.db.import_sqlite --sqlite <path>`
  переносит все семь таблиц одной транзакцией с `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`,
  сохраняет `delivered_at`/`request_id` и печатает счётчики. Пустой, чужой или
  битый источник завершается ненулевым кодом без частичных записей.
- **CI и деплой.** `postgres:17` с healthcheck и `content_factory_test`,
  `CONTENT_FACTORY_TEST_DATABASE_URL`; `compose.yaml` передаёт DSN api и
  worker; `deploy/README.md` и `docs/database.md` описывают переключение,
  миграции, импорт, откат и границы.

## Проверки

- `ruff check .`
- `ruff format --check .`
- `mypy src main.py`
- `python -m pytest` — 1801 passed, coverage 95.95% (SQLite + PostgreSQL)
- `audit-gate --scope changed` — новых находок нет

## Границы

Выдача, формат стока и архива, API, поставщик, YouTube Kit, `video_gen`,
профили в `app_data` и файловые блокировки не менялись. Переключение прод-базы
и перенос данных на linux1 — отдельная задача после merge.

Closes #115

author: neffer77
body:
### A stance: before the first answer of a campaign fight, go in bold or guarded

Before: every campaign fight was fought the same way, with nothing to decide before the first question.

After: the power bar shows the knight's stance, even to begin with. Before the first answer a tap turns it bold (your blows a third harder, the foe's half again as hard) or guarded (the foe's blows halved, yours a fifth lighter), then back to even. Once anything is answered it is set for the fight. It rewards knowing which topics you are sure of.

How: a small Stance module that the power bar, the strike's multiplier and the foe's blow call. It lives only in the fight, so nothing new is saved. Verify checks every fight state and stance, play checks it on a phone, and 12 mutations are caught.

### A peddler: the third victory of a sitting meets one thing to buy at half price

Before: a sitting's victories paid gold and the fifth a sure chest, with nothing in between to look forward to.

After: on the third victory of a sitting, and every fifth after it, a peddler waits on the victory card with one thing at half the shop's price: whichever of a draught, an insight or a rune the knight carries fewest of. One sale a meeting, if the purse will stand it. It sells only what the shop sells.

How: a small Peddler module that the victory screen calls once the win is counted. The offer belongs to the sitting; a purchase goes into the pack as a shop purchase does, so no new save field. Verify checks every victory count and pack, play checks it on a phone, and 12 mutations are caught.

### The sky: each realm's omen this sitting, a gold moon, a fair wind or a mist

Before: every sitting's map looked the same, so there was no reason to pick one realm's road over another on a given day.

After: each sitting every realm has its own sky, shown on its heading on the map and said as a fight there starts. A gold moon pays a quarter more gold for every victory, a fair wind lands your blows a fifth harder, a mist has foes strike a fifth lighter, and now and then the sky is plain.

How: a small Sky module rolled once per realm per sitting, which the gold, the knight's blow and the foe's blow read in campaign fights. Play suites run under a plain sky unless they ask for one. Nothing new is saved. Verify checks every omen on every fight and a thousand rolls, play checks it on a phone, and 13 mutations are caught.

### A ballad: every victory card sings the fight in a line of its own

Before: every victory card said the same thing, the foe "falls before your blade", whether the fight was flawless, a scrape at a few health or a long slog through misses.

After: under that line the card sings the fight in one line of verse, read from what actually happened: a win from the brink of falling, a fight with no miss, a killing blow far past need, a long streak (with its length), a bold or a guarded stance, an omen overhead, or a win that took several misses to find. The moment most worth remembering is the one sung, and the wording turns with the foe, so the same feat reads fresh against the next one. It pays nothing and changes no fight; it gives each victory a story to look back on.

How: a small `Ballad` module picks the kind of verse in a fixed order from the fight's misses, longest streak, overkill, stance, sky and the knight's health as the foe falls (read before a level-up restores it), and picks one of three verses by the foe's name. `tools/verify.js` checks every combination of those for the right kind and filled-in words, and a new phone playthrough wins flawless, hard-won, brink, bold and plain fights. Nothing new is saved.

author: jcore9-bot
body:
## Why

Ship `v0.1.0-alpha.1`, and from M1 on let a tool set each version, tag and release notes from the PR titles. This clears B1 and B2 in #144: a ufw setting can remove Aphelion's isolation rules on reload, and the server reported `0.0.0`.

## What changes

- Preflight exits with status 1 when ufw is enabled and `MANAGE_BUILTINS=yes`, reading both files with `sh`, the way ufw does. The error and the install guide say how to fix it, and the guide warns that `ufw enable` or `ufw reload` while Aphelion runs can still remove the rules.
- The server version is `0.1.0-alpha.1`, No `CHANGELOG.md`: release notes live on GitHub Releases, as in T3 Code. The M0 notes go into the alpha.1 release PR and then the `v0.1.0-alpha.1` release. Other packages stay at `0.0.0`.
- From M1, release-please keeps a release PR open into `main` that bumps the version files and carries the release notes. Merging it creates the tag and the GitHub release. GitHub doesn't start CI on a PR a workflow opens, so you start CI on the release PR once before merging it. Decision 0061 and a release guide explain it.

Closes #192

## How to review

- Startup stops only when both settings are `yes`: [`deploy/host/preflight` lines 21–36](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/blob/beb40e7/deploy/host/preflight#L21-L36). Refused and passing cases: [`deploy/test/host-contract.sh` lines 165–223](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/blob/beb40e7/deploy/test/host-contract.sh#L165-L223).
- Version: `apps/server/src/version.ts` and `apps/server/package.json` both say `0.1.0-alpha.1`, and a test checks they match.
- [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/blob/beb40e7/.github/workflows/release.yml): runs only on pushes to `main`, may write only contents and PRs.
- [`release-please-config.json`](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/blob/beb40e7/release-please-config.json): `alpha` pre-releases, so M1 becomes `0.1.0-alpha.2`, not `0.2.0`. `skip-changelog` keeps notes out of the repo. Chores, CI and tests stay out of the notes.
- [Decision 0061](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/blob/beb40e7/docs/decisions/0061-release-please.md) and [the release guide](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/blob/beb40e7/docs/guides/releasing.md): check the tool choice, and the three one-time steps you do after the alpha.1 merge (the first tag, a repository setting, a re-run, in that order).
- Checked: `vitest run apps/server/src/cli`, the host contract test, a built image printing `aphelion 0.1.0-alpha.1`, actionlint, prettier, and a release-please dry run, which proposes `0.1.0-alpha.2`. It lists all 166 past commits because the `v0.1.0-alpha.1` tag doesn't exist yet.

author: clarkeyeh
body:
Fixes the two defects found in the first T12 live run (2026-11-25 09:50, stopped at the conclusion gate; nothing reached spike main, and cleanup verified clean).

## 1. Harness race: owner write before the ledger import
The backend created conclusion Issue #199 and opened its gate in the same second. The owner policy's `/approve` reached the guarded transport before the throttled (30 s) import had ledgered #199, so the transport threw "Object not in this ledger".
- New `joint/owner-write.ts` `ledgeredWrite`, used for every owner write on a backend-created object (today that's the `/approve` comment, the only one):
  - It first forces an import of the current poll, then writes.
  - On "Object not in this ledger" it imports fresh events (`events(live, id)`) and retries once; if the object is still missing, it fails as before. Other errors are never retried.
- Production `importObjects` keeps its 30 s throttle. It now remembers the workflow and short id, so the forced import can run.
- Offline tests (`owner-write.test.ts`) use a real Ledger and `guardedFetch` over a stub network:
  - the race reproduced;
  - a same-poll object imported before the write;
  - a fresh-events retry;
  - still missing after the retry, so it fails with exactly one retry;
  - other errors not retried.

## 2. Product: meeting reminder command ids contained spaces
`remind()` built `…/nudge/round 1/…`, and `meeting completion` had the same problem. runtime-orca's `marker()` rejects whitespace, so live meeting reminders never reached agents: in T12 the architect seat was dropped as absent without ever being reminded.
- `remind()` slugs the turn for the id only (`round-1`, `meeting-completion`); the body text is unchanged.
- Engine `commandId()` percent-encodes whitespace and `<>` in any part, as a safety net. Audit: all other engine id parts are fixed words, ULIDs, numbers, template stage or role ids, or attempt and gate ids that are themselves command ids. Planning item keys and template ids are covered by the safety net.

## 3. Test gap closed
- `assertMarkerCommandId` in `ports/runtime.ts` is the single rule. runtime-orca's `marker()` calls it, and so does the fake runtime for the operations Orca marks (openSession, prepareWorkspace, spawnAgent, send, answer).
- The shared RuntimePort contract checks that both runtimes refuse a spawn or send whose id contains whitespace. The runtime-orca synthetic tape for that test, `fixtures/orca/1.4.259/contract/synthetic/9208eff49ef3.json`, was generated offline from ContractWorld; no live Orca was involved.
- Engine `context.test.ts`:
  - `commandId` encoding;
  - every `command.issued` id across six meeting and planning scenarios, reminders and timeouts included, passes the marker guards;
  - the reminder id is `round-1` while its text stays `round 1`.

## 4. Fixtures, tapes and recordings
- No committed fixture, tape or recording carries an old `nudge/round N` id. The `round 1` hits in fixtures are message text only. Replays are unchanged; I didn't update or re-record anything live.
- The only deterministic update is the engine meeting snapshot (`nudge/round 1/` → `nudge/round-1/`, in 4 tests).

## DoD (Node v24.22.3, one run, per-step exit codes)
```
STEP 0 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
STEP 0 pnpm typecheck
STEP 0 pnpm typecheck:tests
STEP 0 pnpm -r build
STEP 0 pnpm lint
STEP 0 pnpm test --maxWorkers=2        (3809 passed, 10 skipped)
STEP 0 pnpm test:scripts
STEP 0 pnpm test:coverage --maxWorkers=2  (statements 98.62%)
STEP 0 pnpm depcruise
STEP 0 pnpm depcruise:selftest
STEP 0 pnpm contracts:check
STEP 0 pnpm check:bundle
STEP 0 pnpm fixtures:scan
STEP 0 pnpm docs:check
STEP 0 pnpm test:e2e                   (44 passed)
```
In an earlier DoD run, e2e `demo.spec.ts:141` (I-12 conclusion gate, the 409 refetch) failed once: the gate read `approved` where the test expected `open`. That test drives the fake backend's gate flow, not the code changed here. It passed on both reruns (44/44), so it looks like a timing flake.

body:
## Summary
- Add `GET /api/v1/me/dashboard` aggregating the authenticated learner's published mission count, own submissions, status counts, recent activity, assessment status/finality and progression.
- Keep XP/level/streak separate from rubric competency results. Dashboard exposes assessment status only; no unapproved scores/feedback are fabricated.
- Add `GET /api/v1/me/recommendations?limit=5` using deterministic career-goal keyword overlap against published mission title/summary, with an exploration fallback to recent unattempted published missions.
- Return basis, matched terms, selected goal and a human-readable reason. Suggestions are optional practice recommendations, not career-fit/job-readiness/employment predictions.
- Add PostgreSQL dashboard integration test, pure recommendation logic tests, OpenAPI coverage, README, task updates and ADR 0004.

## Validation
- `npm run check`
- `TEST_DATABASE_URL=... npm test` (28 tests across 10 files)
- `npm run db:generate` (no schema drift)
- `npm run db:migrate:local`
- `npm run openapi:export` (both new routes documented)
- `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities)
- `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run`
- Local smoke: DB health 200; protected dashboard/recommendation routes fail closed with 503 while Supabase JWKS/issuer is not configured.

## Scope boundary
- No AI recommender or career-fit prediction is introduced.
- Assessment scores and feedback are not shown in this slice; the dashboard only reports current assessment status/finality metadata.
- Reviewer policy, assessment finalization and Supabase remote auth remain separate decisions.

body:
## What

A stop-gap admin control for the per-ACOA lot and sample photo override.

- `backend/main.py`: Mk1's `PATCH /explorer/additional-coas/{config_id}` passes `lot_override` and `sample_image_url` to the Integration Service. A request that names either field (set or clear) from a non-admin gets 403. Branding fields stay open to all users.
- `SampleDetails.tsx` (`AdditionalCoaCard`): an override block with Lot override, Photo URL and a photo thumbnail. Admins edit. Everyone else sees the values read-only, and only once an override is set.
- The existing Regen button is unchanged.

## Why

The override is an exception to the COA display policy (DOC-0002 locks the photo and the received lot), approved per use. Until now it could only be set by an API call from inside the Integration Service container.

## Depends on

- ValenceAnalytical/accumark-integration-service#61
- ValenceAnalytical/coabuilder#41

**Deploy order: Integration Service and COA Builder first, Mk1 last.** An Integration Service without #61 ignores the two fields and still answers 200, so this panel would look saved and lose the value on reload.

## Verified

Stack: `acoaui` (devbox, all three branches mounted; destroyed after the walk).

- pytest `backend/tests/test_acoa_override_admin_gate.py`: 3 passed.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean. eslint and prettier clean on the changed lines.
- Admin set both fields in the panel and clicked Regen. New code RWRQ-5QU5 published with the override lot and its own stored photo; the old code was superseded and the primary COA untouched.
- Standard user: rows read-only (screenshot), PATCH of either field 403, website edit 200.
- Not seen: the photo thumbnail with a real image (the stack image URL is internal to the stack).

![ACOA override block as a standard user](docs/superpowers/e2e/acoa-override-readonly-2026-11-24.jpg)

body: ## What changed Bashkit checks the total value count, UTF-8 string and object key bytes, and nesting depth before invoking a registered TypeScript host callback. C, Wasm, and Python all use this dispatch path. The callback takes ownership of the checked arguments, removing a redundant clone. ## Why Binding conversions allocate host values outside the TypeScript VM memory meter. The dispatch budget bounds the input to those conversions. ## Before / After The bounded dispatch regression received a successful callback result above the value limit on main. With the fix it checks that ordinary arguments reach the callback and that dispatch rejects calls above the value, string byte, and depth limits. ## Risk - Medium. A registered callback can now receive a limit error for arguments above the documented budget. ## Checklist - [x] Tests added or updated - [x] Backward compatibility considered --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

body:
## Masalah
Rider terjadwal Siang yang clock-in 06:07 (Alam Sutera, 25 Nov) langsung mengisi Siang 2/10 padahal shift Siang belum mulai. Aturan 0067: rider dengan satu clock-in selalu mengikuti jadwal Orca, tanpa batas kewajaran.

## Perubahan (migrasi 0070, hanya `aktual_bo`)
Untuk rider dengan satu clock-in per DS per hari, shift dibaca berurutan:
1. Laporan Captain (`shift_dikerjakan`), sudah mencakup tukar shift dan backup/pengganti. Dipakai bila Captain mencatat tepat satu shift untuk rider itu.
2. Belum dilaporkan: jadwal Orca, hanya bila clock-in paling awal 2 jam sebelum jam mulai shift itu.
3. Selain itu: dari jam clock-in.

Rider dengan dua clock-in atau lebih tetap dibaca dari jam (long shift). Bentuk hasil tidak berubah; `aktual_bo_harian` tidak berubah. Tidak ada perubahan frontend.

## Tes
Tes baru: terlalu awal dibaca Pagi, Captain hadir menang atas jam, pengganti mengisi shift Siang, jadwal wajar tetap Siang. Satu tes lama disesuaikan (R3 terjadwal Siang clock-in 07:00 → 13:00, karena 07:00 kini memang Pagi). `npm test` 243/243, tsc bersih.

## Setelah merge
Jalankan 0070 di SQL Editor produksi. Perkiraan Alam Sutera hari ini: Pagi 10/10, Siang 0/10 sampai ada yang clock-in siang.

author: carlos0h
body:
## Task 01 - Dependência e configuração
Entrou o `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` e o `pom.xml` passou a importar o BOM do Spring Boot 3.5.15, que escolhe as versões compatíveis (Hibernate, Flyway, driver, JUnit). Por isso saíram as versões fixas: o Hibernate que veio é o 6.6.53.Final, porque o Spring Boot 3.5 não suporta o 7.4.2 que eu usava. No `application.properties`, `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate` (o Flyway cria as tabelas, o Hibernate só confere).

## Task 02 - O que ficou sem dono
Apaguei `GenericDao`, `GenericIDao`, `UsuarioDao`, `UsuarioIDao` e `JPAUtil`. Pelo mesmo motivo (o Spring Boot configura o banco e roda o Flyway sozinho) saíram também `ConfiguracaoBanco`, `MigracaoBanco`, `InicializadorBanco` e o `persistence.xml`. O commit `cfad7d3` só tem remoções: 11 arquivos, 484 linhas removidas (`git diff --stat` no README da pasta).

## Task 03 - A suíte
46 testes verdes (eram 51: saíram 9 testes das classes apagadas e entraram 4). O `UsuarioServiceTest` continua igual, sem subir o Spring. Mudanças nos testes em relação à `main`: apagados `GenericDaoTest` e `UsuarioDaoTest`; `FakeUsuarioDao` agora implementa o `UsuarioRepository` (mesmo nome e pacote, por isso o `UsuarioServiceTest` não mudou); novos `UsuarioRepositoryTest` e `src/test/resources/application.properties`.

## Task 04 - Consulta derivada
`existsByLogin` e `existsByLoginAndIdNot` no `UsuarioRepository`, usadas no `UsuarioService` no lugar do `loginEmUso`. Testadas com `@DataJpaTest` num H2 em memória.

## Task 05 - @Query
`buscarPorNomeOuLogin`, com JPQL (o nome derivado seria ilegível), e o teste dela.

## Decisões
- O `UsuarioRepository` estende `Repository<Usuario, Long>` e declara só os métodos que o Service usa, em vez de `JpaRepository`, para o dublê de teste continuar pequeno.
- O `UsuarioService` traduz qualquer falha do banco para a `FalhaPersistenciaException`, para as telas continuarem iguais.
- O `UsuarioRepositoryTest` usa o `application.properties` de teste (H2, sem Flyway), e roda em qualquer máquina, sem o PostgreSQL.

This is by an automated agent, not a human.

## Summary

Addresses the three requests from the source thread, plus the small configuration needed to support them:

1. **zh-Hans translation fix** — the "Active Sales Orders" dashboard widget now renders **活跃的销售订单** (previously 活动的销售订单), and its description renders **显示当前活跃的销售订单数量**. This matches the existing 活跃的采购订单 wording. Only `src/frontend/src/locales/zh_Hans/messages.po` changes.
2. **Windows startup scripts moved into the repository** — `contrib/windows/` now contains `启动 InvenTree.bat`, `停止 InvenTree.bat`, `开发模式.bat`, the shared `inventree_launcher.py` launcher and a Chinese README; they previously existed only in the local `D:\work\word_space\erp` folder. The launcher locates its runtime directory (`.venv`, `gtk`, `logs`, `.tmp`, `.browser-profile`) via `INVENTREE_APP_ROOT`, otherwise by walking up from the repository root, so the in-repo copy works with the local deployment layout (repository inside `project\`). `--stop`, `--dev` and `--no-browser` modes are supported.
3. **AGENTS.md in Chinese with a local-verification rule** — `AGENTS.md` (and the mirrored `CLAUDE.md`) translated to Chinese; new section `本机实测`: 新增功能时，必须在本机上真实运行并测试，确认无误后才能进入合并审核环节.
4. **Supporting configuration** — `.gitattributes` sets `*.bat text eol=crlf` (cmd.exe mis-parses a UTF-8 batch file with LF-only endings and executes fragments of the Chinese comments; reproduced locally), `pyproject.toml` adds a scoped `RUF001` ignore for full-width Chinese punctuation in `contrib/windows/*.py`, and `README.md` links the new scripts.

## Before / After (zh-Hans web UI)

Identical scenario in both captures: logged in as `admin`, dashboard at <http://localhost:8123/web/>, zh-Hans, light theme, 1440×900, same dashboard layout.

- Baseline: `erp_develop` @ 6afe9e258, frontend rebuilt from that commit without this change.
- After: this PR's head commit @ da23e1c99ea280ff8fb7f2f9234b3c61f143af8f, frontend rebuilt from this branch.

**Before — widget titled 活动的销售订单**

![Before: 活动的销售订单](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xzl197/dsh-superagent-erp/8dba1541686a296db0856e3c149c2b75c126386c/evidence/sales-orders-before.png)

**After — same widget titled 活跃的销售订单**

![After: 活跃的销售订单](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xzl197/dsh-superagent-erp/8dba1541686a296db0856e3c149c2b75c126386c/evidence/sales-orders-after.png)

The evidence images are stored on branch `agent/evidence-copy-startup-agents-ee85db57ae94` (not part of this PR); the links are pinned to commit `8dba1541686a296db0856e3c149c2b75c126386c`.

## Local verification (per the new rule)

Performed on the deployment machine (`D:\work\word_space\erp`), using the scripts from this branch:

- Rebuilt the frontend from the baseline commit (`yarn run compile`, `yarn vite build`, `manage.py collectstatic`) and captured the "before" screenshot; then applied the translation change, rebuilt, and captured the "after" screenshot.
- The compiled zh_Hans catalog contains 活跃的销售订单 and 显示当前活跃的销售订单数量, and the newly emitted zh_Hans chunk contains no 活动的销售订单.
- `停止 InvenTree.bat` stopped the running server (PID file + port fallback); `启动 InvenTree.bat --no-browser` resolved the app directory to `D:\work\word_space\erp`, started the server, wrote `logs\launcher.log`, and `GET /api/` returned 200.
- `开发模式.bat --no-browser` with `INVENTREE_LOCAL_PORT=8124` started the auto-reloading Django server; `GET /api/` on port 8124 returned 200, and the process tree shut down cleanly afterwards. The production server on 8123 stayed up.
- `ruff format --preview --check` and `ruff check --preview` (repository configuration) pass for `contrib/windows/inventree_launcher.py`; `python -m py_compile` passes.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

## Limitations

- The screenshot shows the dashboard widget title; the widget description is only shown in the "Add Widget" drawer (the sales widgets are already on this dashboard), so the new description was verified in the compiled catalog rather than visually.
- The Windows scripts are Windows-only and are not exercised by CI; verification was manual on the deployment machine.
- The old local copies under `D:\work\word_space\erp` were left untouched; the copies in this repository are now canonical and are what the README documents.

## CI status

- `Build` passes: it runs `yarn run compile && yarn run lib && yarn run build`, i.e. the frontend is compiled and bundled with this `messages.po`.
- `Style [prek]` fails on pre-existing files from the fork's earlier BOM-import work (`part/api.py`, `part/serializers.py`, `BomImportModal.tsx`, `BomTable.tsx`, `tasks.py`); the same failure is present on PR #1. Ruff-format/check, codespell, trailing-whitespace, end-of-file and mixed-line-ending report no changes to files in this PR.
- `Style [Documentation]` fails inside the third-party markdown link checker because it fetches `master`, which does not exist in this fork (base is `erp_develop`); it scans `docs/` only.
- The Playwright Chromium/Firefox jobs were still running when this PR was handed off. The Firefox shards also fail on the baseline (see PR #1); this data-only translation change does not touch their fixtures.

## Merge target

This PR targets `erp_develop` (head branch `agent/copy-startup-agents-ee85db57ae94`, based on `erp_develop` @ 6afe9e258). No merge CLI is configured, so a person merges this PR.

author: atimics
body:
The owner approved moving the two .dev deploy jobs to the self-hosted Fly runners, to skip the hosted-runner queue (2.5 min at the measured peak).

- **Switch:** setting the repository variable `DEV_DEPLOY_RUNNER=fly` runs `dev-plan` and `dev-deploy` on `[self-hosted, fly, cosyworld]` (infra/ci-runners). Unset, or any other value, keeps `ubuntu-latest`, so merging this changes nothing until the variable is set.
- **Main only:** these jobs run only for main's pushes, schedules and `dev` dispatches, never for a pull request, and the dispatcher refuses runs from other repositories.
- **GitHub CLI:** the Fly runner image has no `gh`, which both jobs call, so on a self-hosted runner they install a pinned release (2.63.2) first.
- **Not moved:** `dev-image` (Docker builds would need `dockerd` in the runner image) and `dev-checks` (many parallel jobs) stay on hosted runners.
- **Tidy-up:** removes three stale comments saying build.rs runs Node; it no longer does since phase 2.

**Before setting the variable:**
1. The dispatcher (`cosyworld-ci-dispatch`), its webhook and the GitHub App credentials from the old runner guide must be live.
2. The deploy token is then present on runner machines during these jobs; the runners otherwise hold no secrets.
3. If the fleet is down, a queued job waits for a runner and can't move to a hosted one. Set the variable back and re-run.

**Local results:** `test/infrastructure` passes (174, with a new test pinning both jobs' `runs-on` and the gh install). actionlint is clean on anchor-expanded copies. Change budget 41/400; comment ratchet -2; line ceilings ok.

- Compare RBI’s current repo rate with the dated policy history before calculating fresh call–repo spreads.
- Verify a mismatch against RBI’s Liquidity Adjustment Facility circular. Record its effective date and source when the circular and current rates agree.
- Keep the observed call money rate and liquidity visible while affected spreads and their five-day average are pending.
- Let validation publish the verified history during a hold and reject spread observations from the unresolved period.

## Verification

- 63 Python tests and 14 Node render checks passed locally.
- Rebuilt the dashboard from saved data with 61 series and 4,795 observations.
- Replayed RBI’s October rate change through the normal refresh. The real circular restored both derived spread series after a simulated hold.

author: ggpepperstech
body:
## ELI5

On the phone, if you close your last terminal tab at the same moment the desktop restarts that terminal, the phone could get stuck on a blank screen instead of showing "No tabs in this session" with a **Create Tab** button. Now the phone remembers every terminal that tab pointed to while the close is running, so it cleans all of them up and shows the empty-session view.

## What Changed

- **Before:** closing a terminal tab only cleaned up the terminal handle the tab had when you tapped close. If the host restarted the pane mid-close, the same tab ID got a new handle (`pty-1` -> `pty-2`). When the empty tab snapshot arrived before the close reply, nothing linked `pty-2` back to the closed tab, so it stayed the active handle and the session body rendered blank with terminal controls still enabled.
- **After:** the close records a `ClosingTerminalTab` (tab ID + set of handles) in `closingTerminalTabsRef` for as long as the request is in flight. It seeds the set from the tapped tab and the live tab list, and each applied snapshot adds any handle it maps to that tab ID (`rememberClosingTerminalHandles`). On success the close unsubscribes, drops terminal refs, and clears pending/active selection for every recorded handle. If a different terminal became active in the meantime, its selection is kept. The record is removed in `finally`, so it never outlives the request.

## Why

Tab IDs survive a host pane restart but terminal handles don't, and once the empty snapshot lands the current tab list can no longer recover the association. Recording handles as snapshots arrive is the smallest change that keeps the correct link without changing the host RPC contract.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #48646

Follow-up to #48613 ([review thread](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/48613#discussion_r4689416467)).

## Visual Proof

N/A for screenshots: the bug is a timing race (host pane restart landing between the close request and its reply), which can't be reliably staged on a device or simulator. The before/after is shown in the handler tests instead:

- **Before (main + new tests):** `clears the rebound handle after the last terminal closes` fails with `expected 'pty-2' to be null`, i.e. the phone stays on the rebound terminal (blank body). Extra probes for a double rebound and a pending pick of the rebound handle also failed on main (`expected 'pty-3' to be null`, `expected 'pty-2' to be null`).
- **After:** all pass; `activeHandle` becomes `null`, which renders the existing "No tabs in this session" view with **Create Tab**.

## Testing

- [x] Reproduced the race in `use-mobile-session-close-actions.test.ts` (rebound then empty snapshot before the close reply); it fails on main and passes with this change.
- [x] Added a guard test: when a different terminal (`pty-3`) becomes active during the close, it stays selected.
- [x] `vitest run src/session src/test-support` in `mobile/`: 9 files, 41 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit -p mobile/tsconfig.json` passes.
- [x] CI static gates on touched files pass: anti-slop oxlint, native code-quality oxlint, ast-grep, changed-code quality gate, oxfmt.
- Platforms: shared mobile session code (iOS and Android); verified via handler tests on macOS.

## Performance

Negligible. Snapshot application (runs on each tab-list publish, not per keystroke or terminal byte) now does one map lookup per in-flight terminal close, and the set is empty almost always. Measured with bun microbenchmark:

| Case | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Snapshot with 0 in-flight closes (typical) | ~15 ns |
| 1 in-flight close, 10 tabs | ~15 ns |
| 200 in-flight closes, 5000 tabs (adversarial) | ~2.6 µs |
| Starting a close with 5000 tabs | ~11.6 µs (one-time, on user tap) |

No new I/O, RPCs, polling, or timers.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

The riskiest part is matching handles: a wrong match could clear a newer terminal selection. Cleanup only uses handles observed for the closing tab ID, and still checks the live active tab ID before clearing, so another active terminal is preserved (covered by a test). No host RPC or saved-state changes, so older desktops and paired phones are unaffected. Back out with a plain revert.

## Review

Original fix by @ggpepperstech in #48648 (authorship preserved); maintainer follow-ups dropped the route-reset tracking and simplified the ref wiring.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why
- [x] I stated the risk and how to back it out
- [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason
- [x] Self-reviewed for correctness, security, and performance
- [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote, and path/shortcut impact considered
- [x] Targeted tests, typecheck, and lint pass locally; CI covers the rest
