author: dlroqa
body:
Test-only experiment, messages only. **Not for merge without separate owner approval.**

Refs #170.

## Question
Does the studio's own diagnostics port check collide with the replacement image engine's bind? This is the hypothesis for Windows R1b (`engine-slot` R1b: stand-in listen `EADDRINUSE` right after the studio's check said free), and possibly R2.

Code: `GET /api/diagnostics` → `getHealth()` → `checkPort(PORT_BACKEND)` really binds and closes the image port. R1b's sampler polls `/api/diagnostics` about every 40 ms during the replacement.

## Experiment (`e1-port-race.test.cjs`)
Each part repeats R1b's replacement (slot on; a settings change replaces the loaded engine). A test-only preload in the studio records every studio bind on the image port with its caller. The fake sd-server records its own listen and listen-error.
- **Control C:** the preload binds the port for 800 ms at the engine spawn. The replacement must fail with EADDRINUSE (R1b form), and the trace must name the overlap. This proves both the effect and the detector.
- **Arm A:** poll `/api/diagnostics` every 40 ms (R1b cadence).
- **Arm B:** poll `/api/backend-status` every 40 ms (no port check).
- Arms A and B are measured only. They report replacements, engine listen errors, studio binds by caller, overlaps (and which side lost) and the closest bind-to-listen distance.

## Local (Linux)
- **Control C:** 3/3 replacements EADDRINUSE and never ready; 3/3 overlaps named.
- **Arm A:** 8 replacements, 120 diagnostics probe binds, closest 0–5 ms to an engine listen, no engine failure.
- **Arm B:** only the product's own pre-spawn port selection, at least 141 ms away.

The Windows run is the point of this PR.

## Unchanged
The R1b and R2 tests and their assertions, startup timeouts, engine lifecycle, port ownership and all product code.

The polling uses R1b's existing 40 ms cadence, no faster. A local run takes about 2 minutes.

**Submitter note**

Harness: Claude Code

# 3 exact changes on record ad0f1322

## Parent and what this tree is

Parent: `ad0f1322-4cb0-4fa8-87d6-7119f1ab1683`, commit `f3332e8d09e093557ee3f585adf76b936820db3d`, the promoted record when this tree was built. Every file
not named below is byte-identical to that tree. Relative to the parent this entry edits:

- `crates/flock-core/src/gpu_commit.rs`
- `crates/flock-core/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/flock-core/src/zerocheck.rs`
- `crates/flock-core/src/zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized.rs`
- `crates/flock-prover/src/prover.rs`

## Changes of ours

Each change below is exact and is described with its files, its mechanism and the argument for byte-identical proofs; a change that has a kill switch names it.

### The GPU commit's gate environment reads kept once per process (`FLOCK_NO_GPU_ENV_ONCE`)

Files: `crates/flock-core/src/gpu_commit.rs` only (the switch `gpu_env_once_enabled`, five small environment helpers,
and the gate and trace sites that call them).

**The code this touches.** Several functions of the GPU commit read a variable from the process environment every
time they are called, and some are called many times per prove:

- `gpu_commit_enabled()` (the `FLOCK_NO_GPU_COMMIT` kill switch) is tested by the device accessor `gpu()`, by
  the zerocheck share selectors (`gpu_zc_ab_completion_share`, `gpu_zc_k_share`, `gpu_zc_t56_cap`), by
  `begin_from_z_first_pass_stream`, `commit_l0_or_fallback`, the warm-up helpers, and by the opening's
  `zfold_gpu_enabled`. A prove reaches it about fifty times.
- `gpu_commit_latched_on()` reads `FLOCK_NO_LAZY_GPU_CODEWORD` before it asks whether the warm-up latched the GPU
  path.
- The shared-table term `FLOCK_NO_GPU_TABLE_REUSE` is read in `final_leaf_selected`, in `g4x2_dead_lane_pass` and
  in the table share (`share_log`) of the three NTT tile encoders, once per encoded tile pass.
- The trace terms `FLOCK_COMMIT_TIMING` and `FLOCK_GPU_COMMIT_DEBUG` are read in `debug_enabled()`, in four timing
  sites of the commit and in `note_poisoned_lock`.

Each read is an `std::env::var_os` call, which takes the process environment lock and scans the environment block.
That is about sixty lookups per prove, on the threads that encode and drain the GPU work.

**The change.**

- Five helpers hold these terms: `gpu_commit_env_clear` (`FLOCK_NO_GPU_COMMIT` unset),
  `lazy_gpu_codeword_env_clear` (`FLOCK_NO_LAZY_GPU_CODEWORD` unset), `gpu_table_reuse_env_clear`
  (`FLOCK_NO_GPU_TABLE_REUSE` unset), `commit_timing_env_on` (`FLOCK_COMMIT_TIMING` set) and
  `gpu_commit_debug_env_on` (`FLOCK_GPU_COMMIT_DEBUG` set).
- With `gpu_env_once_enabled()` true, a helper evaluates its term once in a `std::sync::LazyLock` and returns the
  kept value afterwards. Otherwise it performs the same lookup as before.
- Every call site keeps its own logic and only takes the term from its helper:
  - `gpu_commit_enabled()` is still `GPU_COMMIT_DEFAULT && cfg!(..) && <env term>`, with the same short-circuit
    order;
  - `gpu_commit_latched_on()` still tests the environment term before `imp::gpu_commit_latched_on()`;
  - the `share_log` choice is still `0` with the variable set and `2` without it;
  - `debug_enabled()` is still "timing set or debug set".
- The three helpers that only the Metal module calls carry the crate's usual `allow(dead_code)` guard for other
  targets.
- `FLOCK_NO_GPU_ENV_ONCE` (any value; read once per process) restores the lookups on every call.

**Why the bytes are identical.** The worker never changes its environment while it runs, so a lookup returns the same
answer on every call of a process, and the kept answer equals the one a fresh lookup would return. Every gate
therefore selects the same arm as before, every encoder binds the same table share, and the trace terms print exactly
when they did. No kernel, buffer, dispatch, share rule or transcript value changes. Proofs from the harness worker,
run under the benchmark's Seatbelt profile, are byte-identical to the parent's for six seeds with the switch unset and
set.

**What it saves.** About sixty environment lookups per prove, each a lock plus a scan of the environment block. The
ranked worker's environment is small, so each lookup is short. This is a cleanup of repeated work, not a change of
any path.

**Where each helper is used.**

| helper | term | call sites |
|---|---|---|
| `gpu_commit_env_clear` | `FLOCK_NO_GPU_COMMIT` unset | `gpu_commit_enabled()`, which every GPU arm's selector tests first |
| `lazy_gpu_codeword_env_clear` | `FLOCK_NO_LAZY_GPU_CODEWORD` unset | `gpu_commit_latched_on()` |
| `gpu_table_reuse_env_clear` | `FLOCK_NO_GPU_TABLE_REUSE` unset | `final_leaf_selected`, `g4x2_dead_lane_pass`, the three `share_log` choices |
| `commit_timing_env_on` | `FLOCK_COMMIT_TIMING` set | `debug_enabled()`, four timing sites of the commit |
| `gpu_commit_debug_env_on` | `FLOCK_GPU_COMMIT_DEBUG` set | `debug_enabled()`, `note_poisoned_lock` |

`FLOCK_NO_GPU_FROM_Z_ZERO_COLUMNS` keeps its per-call read: its rollback is documented as uncached, and this change
leaves it alone. `ENV_GPU_COMMIT_FORCE` and the other switches that are read once already are not touched either.

**Checks.** The worker built from this tree was run through the harness path (cleared environment, the benchmark's
Seatbelt profile, the seed on standard input) for six seeds, with `FLOCK_NO_GPU_ENV_ONCE` unset and set; every proof
is byte-identical to the parent's, and the compile emits no new warning.

**Scope.** One file. No kernel, schedule, share rule, buffer, pipeline, wait, start-up step or protocol parameter
changes.

### The timing-trace environment reads kept once per process (`FLOCK_NO_TRACE_ENV_ONCE`)

Files: `crates/flock-core/src/lib.rs` (the switch `ENV_NO_TRACE_ENV_ONCE` and the helpers `phase_timing_env_on` and
`zc_timing_env_on`), `crates/flock-core/src/gpu_commit.rs`, `crates/flock-core/src/zerocheck.rs`,
`crates/flock-core/src/zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized.rs` and `crates/flock-prover/src/prover.rs` (the trace
sites that call them).

**The code this touches.** The prover prints optional timing traces. Each trace site decides whether to print by
reading a variable from the process environment:

- `FLOCK_PHASE_TIMING` (the phase-timing trace) is read in `prover.rs` by `prove_fast_core_with_commit_codeword`,
  `prove_fast_ligerito_from_witness_with_commit_codeword` and `commit_with_round1_ab_precompute`, and in
  `gpu_commit.rs` by `hybrid_cpu_tail_hash_join`, `retune_ranked_hybrid_with_exact_contention` and
  `zc_r2_drain_prefetch`.
- `FLOCK_ZC_TIMING` (the zerocheck trace) is read in `zerocheck.rs` by `prove_packed_padded_inner` and
  `stage_commit_tail_fill`, in `univariate_skip_optimized.rs` by
  `precompute_round1_ab_inner_packed_padded_body` and `round1_c_prelude`, and in `prover.rs` by
  `make_commit_tail_fill_hook`.

These reads run on every prove, whether or not a trace is printed. Each is an `std::env::var_os` call, which takes
the process environment lock and scans the environment block. Three further reads of `FLOCK_PHASE_TIMING` in the
GPU share selectors were already kept once per process in `LazyLock`s and are not touched.

**The change.**

- `phase_timing_env_on()` and `zc_timing_env_on()` in `flock-core` hold the two terms ("variable set"). With
  `trace_env_once_enabled()` true, each evaluates its term once in a `std::sync::LazyLock` and returns the kept value
  afterwards. Otherwise it performs the same lookup as before.
- The eleven trace sites listed above call the helper in place of their own lookup. Each site keeps it

author: jeffreycorro
body: ## Summary Cassie can record a new date when an applicant's interview or exam moves. The date already on the record stays in a short history (previous date → new date, reason, who recorded it, and when). Lists, the day view, the applicant, and print show the new date and a Rescheduled marker. An applicant with no reschedule looks the same as today. Nothing already stored is rewritten, and there is no database migration. The initial interview is the appointment that already has a date and a time, and the status list already included Rescheduled without a place to type the new date. That is where the Rescheduled date section sits, on the applicant, next to the initial interview. The same section also covers an exam date and a saved interview record (date only, no time) and a final interview when one is already stored the same way. Onboarding is the checklist after someone is hired, not an applicant appointment, so it is left as it is. Build id is **2026-11-25a** (the next id after 2026-11-24a on main). ## How Cassie uses it 1. Open Recruitment → Initial interviews, or open the applicant from the pipeline. 2. On a scheduled row, click **Reschedule**. On the applicant, use the **Rescheduled date** section. 3. Enter the new date. An initial or final interview also asks for the time. An exam or a saved interview record asks for the date only. 4. Reason is optional. Recorded by starts as the HR staff name; change it if someone else is entering the move. 5. Click **Reschedule** (or **Save rescheduled date** from the list). 6. The schedule list, the pipeline day view, the name on the pipeline, and the printed hiring file show the new date with a Rescheduled marker. Under the applicant, the history still shows the earlier date, the reason, who entered it, and when. Changing the date in the existing interview, exam, or interview-record field also keeps the earlier date in that history, instead of dropping it. ## Tests `npm test` in `hr-artifact`: **792 passed, 0 failed**. New coverage in `tests/concerns-2026-11-25a.test.js`: - Setting a reschedule stores the new date, the original date, the reason, who recorded it, and when. - A second reschedule appends. The first history line stays. - The same date is refused and does not add a history line. - An initial interview without a time is refused. - The day list, sort order, and applicant picker use the new date and show Rescheduled. - A legacy applicant with no reschedule data is unchanged: same date, no marker, no history keys. - An exam date and an interview-record date (no time) keep their own history. - Editing a saved date, or saving an applicant whose exam or interview date changed, records the move. A save that does not change the date does not invent a history line. This PR is not merged and not deployed. No production applicant data was written.

author: matheustimbo
body:
## Why
The GOTY 2026 page (the TGA Bolão plus the Seu GOTY wall) only existed on the web. App users now get the same page, with the same rules and data, without leaving the app.

## What changes
- **Route and entry point:** new `apps/mobile/app/(app)/goty-2026.tsx` screen in the authenticated Stack, with a dark/gold header. `GotyFloatingBadge` is mounted in `(app)/_layout.tsx`. On tab screens it sits above the tab bar, on stacked screens it sits near the bottom edge, and it is hidden on `/goty-2026`.
- **Deep link:** `nav-intent.ts` now resolves `/goty-2026` and `clubedojogo://goty-2026`, with an optional `?tab=bolao|seu-goty` that is validated. Existing `/jogos/:id` and `/perfil/:id` behave as before. `push-navigation.ts` is untouched.
- **Bolão GOTY** (`GotyBolaoTab`, `GotyBolaoAdmin`):
  - **Votação:** the 30 categories, filters (all, pending, answered, main, craft, genre, community_esports), search by category or nominee, and optimistic picks that roll back on error.
  - **Progress:** a fixed progress dock at the bottom of the screen opens the review sheet with **Confirmar / Reabrir palpite**.
  - **Placar:** podium and table built with `computeBolaoLeaderboard`. Tapping any member opens a sheet with their picks.
  - **Admin:** event status, `voting_closes_at` deadline (DD/MM/AAAA HH:mm, or no deadline), the `personal_voting_open` switch, the official winner per category, and a manual cover sync button.
- **Seu GOTY** (`GotyPersonalTab`, `GotyGamePickerSheet`): Meu GOTY is highlighted, followed by the other categories, each with choose / change / remove.
  - **Picker:** calls `GET /api/goty/search-games` with debounced search and an "Incluir outros anos" toggle. It shows the curated catalog in demo mode, or when the API fails, with a warning.
  - **Community wall:** top games mosaic, category filter, member showcases, and detail sheets. A game detail links to its club page when the game has a UUID.
- **Covers:** missing nominee covers are resolved in the background, in batches, via `POST /api/goty/resolve-covers` (same loop as `goty-experience.tsx`).
- **Data:** `packages/data/src/goty.ts` no longer reads `window.localStorage` directly.
  - `configureGotyDemoStorage()` takes a storage object, `undefined` (auto-detect `globalThis.localStorage`, the web default, unchanged) or `null` (memory only).
  - The app uses memory only and resets the demo state on each new demo session.
- **Hooks:** `apps/mobile/src/state/goty-queries.ts` has the React Query hooks. They use `getMobileSupabaseClient()` and the new `getMobileApiTransport()`, a shared Bearer transport added in `platform/api-transport.ts`.
- **Visuals:** fixed gold/dark palette regardless of app theme. Posters fall back to an editorial card with the full title, which wraps and shrinks instead of being cut off. `react-native-svg` is not installed, so the TGA emblem is drawn with native views (rotated blades and a border-drawn pedestal).
- **Not ported:** a comment or reason field on picks, because the web has none.

## Verification
- `npm run test:domain`: 38/38 pass.
- `npm run test:data`: 57 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped (they need a local Supabase). This includes 2 new tests: demo mode works with no `localStorage`, and injected or memory-only storage behaves as expected.
- `npm run test:mobile`: 156/156 pass. This includes the 10 new tests in `tests/mobile/goty.test.ts`: deep link, the badge visibility rule, Bolão filters and search, optimistic transforms, deadline parsing, batched cover resolution, and search fallback.
- `npm run test:api`: 48 pass, 1 skipped (needs a local Next server).
- `npm run typecheck --workspace @clube-do-jogo/mobile` and `npm run typecheck` (web) pass.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors. The 4 warnings are in files this PR doesn't touch.
- `npx expo export --platform android` bundles to Hermes bytecode without errors.
- **Not checked:** the screens have not been run on a simulator or emulator, so layout and interactions are untested on a real device.

author: thep0y
body:
## Summary

Use the documented controlled-state rule (`open !== undefined`) in SidebarProvider instead of treating the presence of `onOpenChange` as "controlled".

## Problem

`setOpen` only wrote the internal state when `onOpenChange` was absent. Therefore:

- `defaultOpen={false} + onOpenChange={log}` — the common "notify but do not take over" usage — could never open.
- A controlled provider without a callback wrote internal state even though `open` was supplied.

This contradicts the repository-wide controlled/uncontrolled contract.

## Changes

- Write `_setOpen` only when `open === undefined`.
- Always call `onOpenChange` when provided.
- Keep the existing cookie write.
- Add a regression test for `defaultOpen + onOpenChange`.

## Verification

- `bunx vitest run tests/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider/SidebarProvider.test.tsx`
- Full gates on `fix/sidebar-controlled`: 446 files / 5063 tests (statements 99.92 / branches 93.35); positioner 14 files / 216 tests; `bun run check`, `bun run check:branches`, `bun run build:positioner`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:build` all pass.

## Compatibility and risk

Behavior change only for the misclassified `defaultOpen + onOpenChange` case; that case now works as documented. Controlled usage with `open` remains callback-only.

Refs: `AUDIT_REPORT.md` P1-10.

author: tosinoladokun
body:
Closes #912.

## What
`SocialQueueWatchJob` runs weekdays at 9:00 and 9:45 America/Los_Angeles (after the 8:30 social job, and again once Buffer has had time). It raises one `social-queue` alert through the existing `Autopilot::Alert` (one email to hello@ plus a Sentry error, again only after 20 h) when, for today:

1. an approved row with `send_on` today (or earlier) is still a draft after 8:30, with the stopped-run reason when the 8:30 job gave one;
2. a row sent today is `failed` or `unknown` (unknown says to check the account);
3. a row is `queued` more than 30 minutes past its Buffer due time (the 5-minute sync should have read it back).

When none applies it calls `resolve!` ("back to normal", sent once if it was open). Skips weekends, holidays and channels that are Off. Owner is Infra (`lib/autopilot/owners.rb`).

## Safety
Read only: no sends, no mode changes. Alert text has row ids, platform and company slug only, never a post's words (tested). No migration, no `render.yaml` change (no Blueprint sync), no new dependency.

## Tests
8 new tests (each case, the reason text, Off, weekend, the schedule and owner); the autopilot and recurring-schedule tests pass; rubocop clean.

body:
## Motivation
The FIFO walker unconditionally records each visited command word and checks for control-flow words. Both history buffers are read only by diagnostic output. Add `GCM_FIFO_HISTORY=0` to skip this work during clean benchmarks. The default preserves existing fault-history dumps. `GCM_WORD_STATS` and `GCM_CIRCLE_DUMP` retain their branch history even when the full history is disabled.

## Scope
No changes to FIFO consumption, mapping, word budget, renderer mirrors, synchronization, flip recovery or guest progress. Set the option before launch. Raw memory around faults is still reported; the per-word history is intentionally absent in opt-out runs.

## Validation
Extend the existing NOP-run fixture to check recorded history and run the same FIFO/mirror/budget assertions in four fresh-process configurations (default, disabled, disabled with word stats, disabled with circle dump). Run `python tools/test_gcm_nop_runs.py` and runtime tests. Remote source/changed-file inspection performed; native tests and P5 performance measurements pending. Keep draft. No FPS improvement claimed.

author: xiajiexia
body:
## Summary by NightMe

停机期间主库的 WAL 会随最后一个连接关闭而重置，帧号重新计数，链上还没有的事务随之消失；备份端因此永远拿不到这批变更，且链条的 Sequence 依然连续，协议看不出缺口。本次改动让运行时自己承担这一半的连续性判定：关闭时先收口链条（补写 pending、补捕最后一轮之后的事务、发布段、越过屏障），校验链确实覆盖主库后再写下一条"链在位置 P 处是完整的"的干净关闭标记；启动时把标记与 driver 当前的 WAL 代际逐字段比对，代际未变或标记正好描述链的末端时链条跨代际延续，否则判定断裂，走既有重建路径并让备份端换基线。运行期发生的换代仍由 driver 判定，两者不重叠。

New Features:
- 干净关闭标记 `<Spool.Root>/<Protocol.DatabaseID>/peer.json`（内容为链末端的 `seq` 与 WAL 位置）：临时文件写入 → fsync 文件 → rename → fsync 目录，读不到或解析失败一律按"没有标记"处理。
- `Peer.Close` 的收口序列：停捕获与 GC 循环 → 补写 pending → 继续扫描 driver 直到没有新变更 → `Flush` → 屏障到期时 `Sync` → 校验完整性 → 写标记 → 关 Spool。校验要求 pending 为空且 durable ack 与 `CaptureCursor` 同代同帧，任一不满足则删除标记而不写新标记。
- 链条连续性的判定：链为空不判定；driver 尚不知代际时推迟到下一次捕获轮次；代际相同按位置续传；代际不同且标记的 `seq`/`pos` 与链末端完全相同则链条跨代际连续；其余一律判定断裂。

Bug Fixes:
- 停机期间 WAL 换代导致的静默不一致：判定断裂时沿用 `recoverChain`（`Reset` 提升 Epoch 并清空段链 → 主动取快照 → 置 `SnapshotRequired`），备份端拿到新基线，不再静默偏旧。
- 关闭时补捕最后一轮捕获之后提交的事务，消除"既不在链里、又随 WAL 复位消失"的那段洞。
- 重建与启动时链已不成立的情形下删除标记，避免过期标记让下一次重启被误判为连续。

Enhancements:
- 链条自启动以来没有推进时保留上一次干净关闭写下的标记，使"重启即换代、链未推进"这一常见情形零成本续传，而不必重新快照整库。
- 链不完整属于运行时状态，经 `Stats()` 的错误上报；`Close` 本身仍以 30 秒为界的超时执行收口，不因主库仍在写入而无限期挂起。

Tests:
- 新增 `source/marker_test.go`：`judgeChain` 表驱动覆盖四种判定情形，并覆盖标记的写出条件、Spool 打满与屏障未到时的不写出、半截文件按无标记处理、标记过期与失效、跨代际连续不触发重建、无标记/过期标记触发重建。
- `source/helpers_test.go` 增加重开 driver 的夹具，用于在测试里制造"重开后即为新一代际"的情形。

Documentation:
- `docs/source.md` 增补 The restart and the continuity 一节（标记内容、判定规则、停机顺序：停写 → 关 peer → 关 driver），并在 The chain that breaks 与 Not supported 中补上停机期间继续写入的条目。

Deviations from Issue #24:
- 连续性判定在首轮捕获轮次（`drv.Scan` 成功之后）执行，而不是在 `Open` 里读 durable ack 与标记 — driver 只在扫描后才知道 WAL 代际，`Open` 时尚无代际可比；R5 只要求"判定发生在 driver 已知代际之后"，这样执行才满足该约束。
- 关闭时的 `Sync` 只在屏障到期（`Pending().Due`）时执行，而非 R1 序列中的无条件 `sp.Sync(ctx)` — 屏障是否到期由 spool 判定；写标记仍要求 durable ack 与捕获游标同位置，未越屏障的链不会被打标，方向保守。
- 关闭序列在补写 pending 之后继续扫描 driver 直到没有新变更，超出 R1 列出的动作 — 只补写 pending 时，最后一轮之后提交的事务既不在链里又随 WAL 复位消失；不补捕会让每次重启都判定断裂、退化成整库重新快照。
- `Close` 保持返回 `nil`，收口失败经 `Stats()` 上报 — issue 未规定失败如何对外呈现；关闭时返回错误会让调用方把停机当作失败，而链是否完整是运行时状态。
- `Open` 在 spool 已报告链断裂时一并删除标记文件，判定流程图中没有这一步 — 该标记描述的链已不存在，留着会让下一次重启被误判为连续。

Risk: medium — 改动触及停机与重启这条数据一致性路径，`Close` 新增扫描、flush 与 fsync 且受 30 秒超时约束；判定失误的方向是重建（多一次快照）而非静默丢数据，但误判为"连续"会造成备份偏旧，故对标记比对采用逐字段严格相等。无 API、wire、配置或依赖变更，`driver`/`protocol`/`segment`/`spool`/`backup` 未改动。

Closes #24

body:
This round was a bug hunt: an independent review of the last four rounds' code, a chaos "monkey" test and a long-session memory check. Fixes:

- **Blank page on older Safari:** `Lines.fill` used a regex lookbehind, which Safari before 16.4 can't parse. Because the whole game is one script, the page would stay blank there. The behaviour is the same without the lookbehind. A new self-test check keeps the source free of lookbehind, optional chaining and nullish coalescing; the previous version on main contains the lookbehind it scans for, so the check would have caught it.
- **Title-screen overlap:** with storage full and no show in progress, the solid "Click anywhere to turn on sound" plate covered the storage-full warning. It now sits below it, with a gap.
- **Salvo running call:**
  - Names are compared case-insensitively, since a lowercase name gets capitalised at the start of a sentence.
  - A one-frame swap at the front no longer retires a correct "X is out in front"; the leader has to actually change.
- **Announcer voice:** a line taken off the bar, such as the countdown at the fire or a stale call, also stops the optional voice.
- **Title champion:** a duck that fails to draw can't leave the canvas transformed.
- **Reveal:** the lifted card settles when the pointer leaves the canvas or a finger lifts.

## Testing
- **Monkey test:** about 60 minutes in total, over 16 runs. Each run is a chaotic host pressing random keys (Space, R, S, T, M, N, P, Escape), clicking random buttons and canvas spots, using pause and settings, ticking roster boxes and resizing the window. Covered salvo and one-by-one, 1 to 40 ducks, with and without bonus ammo. Zero console errors and no stuck screens. One early "stuck" flag was a long but normal flight (salvo flights reach about 38 s of simulated time).
- **Memory:** 16 back-to-back shows in one page, drawn every frame. After GC the JS heap stays flat at about 7 MB; the only growth is the saved history, about 3 KB per show.
- **Each fix checked directly:**
  - capitalisation cases, including "…" staying lowercase;
  - the stale rule: a one-frame swap is not stale, a real change is, and the capitalised name is found;
  - the voice stops on retire;
  - the title canvas transform is intact after a duck that throws;
  - the pointer leaving clears the lift;
  - the storage-full title screenshot.
- **Self test:** all 46 checks pass.
- **Fast-forward sweeps:** 190 shows with no errors.
- **Distances:** the 2,000-flight signature is **identical to main**.
- **Harnesses:** reload, skip, replay and spotlight, music cues in both modes, reveal hover and quack, the champion walker and the roster panel all pass.

author: retracdev
body:
## Problem

The deploy for #24 failed in both attempts with:

> No artifacts named "github-pages-45533862567-2" were found for this workflow run.

The upload had succeeded, and the run's artifacts include both `github-pages-45533862567-1` and `-2`. `deploy-pages` listed artifacts about 0.4 s after the upload finished in the same job. At that moment it could only see one artifact: the previous attempt's, not the one just uploaded. So this is a timing race. The site build was fine. The earlier "Adjust image display in README.md" run failed at the same step.

## Fix

- Split the workflow into a `build` job (build, configure Pages, upload) and a `deploy` job that `needs: build`. This is the layout GitHub's own Pages workflow uses.
- The per-attempt artifact name is now passed from `build` to `deploy` as a job output. Re-running only a failed `deploy` job therefore still uses the artifact the build uploaded. Without the output, it would look for a name with the new attempt number.

## Testing

Nothing could be run locally. Merging this PR runs the new workflow on `main`.

author: xerial
body: ## Summary - `s.regexp_extract(pattern[, group])` now returns NULL when the pattern does not match, on every engine. Before, DuckDB, Hive, and the wvlet engine returned `''`, while Trino, Snowflake, and BigQuery returned NULL. - The DuckDB variant (which the engine also runs) and the Hive variant call `regexp_extract` only when the pattern matches, so a real empty match (`'b'.regexp_extract('x*')`) still returns `''`. - Hive's two-argument `regexp_extract` defaults to group 1. The Hive variant now passes group 0, so the default is the whole match as on other engines. - Adds the rule to the naming ADR's semantics list. Design note: `plans/2026-11-24-regexp-extract-null-on-no-match.md`. ## Decisions I made - Used `case when regexp_matches(...) then regexp_extract(...) end`, not `nullif(..., '')`, so an empty match is not turned into NULL. - The engine's bare `regexp_extract` SQL function stays DuckDB-compatible (`''`). Only the stdlib meaning changes. ## Validation - `EngineStdlibStringTest`: engine vs duckdb_jdbc 2.0.1 on no match, empty match, NULL input, and group forms. - `spec/basic/stdlib_string.wv` asserts NULL for no match and `''` for an empty match. It passes in RunnerSpecBasic (DuckDB) and RunnerSpecWvletEngine. - EngineBasicSpecTest, EngineStdlibCoverageCheck, and TyperCoverageCheck pass. The stdlib reference is regenerated; the catalogs did not change. - No prototype gate: this is not a UI change. ## Known limitations (follow-ups) - A capture group that is not part of the match (`'b'.regexp_extract('(a)|b', 1)`) still returns `''` on DuckDB and the engine, but NULL on Trino. - On BigQuery, the third argument of `REGEXP_EXTRACT` is a position, not a group, so the group form is wrong there today. ## Overview

Part of #3066 (the `XGBRFRegressor` / `XGBRFClassifier` items in the issue's deprecation list).

XGBoost deprecated `XGBRFRegressor` and `XGBRFClassifier`. Creating them now emits a `FutureWarning`, and the classes will be removed in a later release. That would break `TestExplainerXGBoost`.

Changes in `tests/explainers/test_tree.py`:

- The random-forest variants in `regressors` / `classifiers` are now `XGBRegressor` / `XGBClassifier` with `num_parallel_tree` and `n_estimators=1`, as the warning recommends. I copied the other parameters from the RF wrappers (`learning_rate=1.0`, `subsample=0.8`, `colsample_bynode=0.8`, `reg_lambda=1e-5`, 100 parallel trees), so coverage of boosted random forests is unchanged. With xgboost 3.4.1 and the same `random_state`, predictions are bit-for-bit identical to the old estimators for both the regressor and the classifier.
- Removed the `XGBRFClassifier` `NotImplementedError` check in `test_xgboost_multiclass`. The `XGBClassifier(num_parallel_tree=3)` check right after it hits the same branch (`num_stacked_models != num_outputs` in `TreeEnsemble.predict`).
- Added explicit `pytest.param` ids (`XGBRegressor-rf`, `XGBClassifier-rf`) so the test names stay readable.

## Testing

`pytest tests/explainers/test_tree.py -k TestExplainerXGBoost -W "error:.*XGBRF.*:FutureWarning"`: 13 passed (xgboost 3.4.1, Python 3.13, Windows).

author: gregoryharper84-ship-it
body:
Incident: #974

## Summary

November 24's final three-leg and five-leg proposals used eight different players but shared three games (BOS-WAS, VGK-EDM, DAL-DEN), and the five-leg card also held two Detroit players. Nothing held either card, because game exposure was only visible when the exact selection or the same player repeated. This PR records that retrospective and makes shared-game exposure fail closed.

## Changes

**`artifacts/wow-engine/v17/slip_research_preflight.py`**
- Pre-computes `(sport, official_event_id) -> proposed card IDs` over the whole portfolio, so a card is held even when the card sharing its game appears later in the payload.
- Holds every affected card and leg with `CROSS_SLIP_EVENT_EXPOSURE_UNVERIFIED` (`RESEARCH_HOLD`, `joint_probability=null`, `can_publish_as_certified=false`). The hold is absolute in this pure audit: a `cross_slip_joint_verification` receipt supplied in the same untrusted payload does not clear it, because the audit cannot authenticate it. No governed joint-artifact path exists yet.
- Normalizes caller confidence labels, so `STRONG CONFIDENCE`, `strong-confidence` and `Lock of the Day` are held exactly like `STRONG_CONFIDENCE`; previously only the exact underscore spelling matched.
- Removes the now-redundant `CROSS_SLIP_EVENT_HINGE_CONCENTRATION` threshold and its `max_distinct_slips_per_event` parameter. No in-repo caller passed the parameter.
- `cross_slip_event_exposure_counts` is now derived from the same portfolio map.

**`artifacts/wow-engine/v17/slip_construction_postmortem.py`**
- Adds sport+event exposure across cards, independent of player identity: per card `distinct_event_count`, `cross_slip_shared_event_legs`, `CROSS_SLIP_GAME_EXPOSURE_UNVERIFIED`, plus portfolio `cross_slip_shared_event_groups` and `cross_slip_shared_event_position_occurrences`. Still emits no joint probability, expected value or ROI.

**Fixture, doc and tests**
- `docs/wow/research/2026-11-24-dual-slip-postmortem.{json,md}`: eight unique picks, both final slips, reported scorecard, explicit evidence boundaries (no verified PrizePicks settlement, financial returns, final individual totals or WOW pregame receipts).
- `v17/test_nov24_dual_slip_postmortem.py`: exact three-leg + five-leg regression, scorecard reconciliation (4W/4L, 2/3, 2/5, NBA 3/6, NHL 1/2, MORE 3/6, LESS 1/2), no probability backfill, absolute-hold test.
- `v17/test_slip_research_preflight.py`: three pre-existing tests updated from order-dependent first-card-clean expectations to the symmetric hold; no assertion was relaxed.

## Acceptance - tests run

From `artifacts/wow-engine`:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  v17/test_slip_research_preflight.py \
  v17/test_nov24_dual_slip_postmortem.py \
  v17/test_slip_portfolio_optimizer.py \
  v17/test_session_exposure_card_shrink_p0.py \
  v17/test_nov22_chat_slip_postmortem.py \
  v17/test_slip_construction_postmortem.py \
  v17/test_postmortem_engine.py \
  v17/test_postmortem_shared_hinge_attribution.py \
  v17/test_niche_prop_research.py
```

Result: **184 passed, 1 warning** (upstream Starlette/httpx deprecation notice, unrelated).

Covered:
- Exact November 24 three-leg + five-leg cards held on both sides; 3 shared games; Detroit-only legs (Jenkins, Reed) carry no cross-card game blocker.
- A fully populated caller-supplied joint receipt does not clear the hold.
- Duplicate-thesis attribution stays single-sided while the game-level hold is symmetric.
- A third proposal on one shared game is held (the former hinge behaviour is subsumed).
- Zero backfilled probabilities, no invented ROI, `can_execute=false` throughout.

## Boundaries

No model, calibration, qualification floor, settlement or terminal-reducer change; `can_execute=false` and `V17_TERMINAL_REDUCER` authority unchanged; no deployment.

## Known gap

Every shared-game card stays held in research mode until a governed, authenticated joint-scenario artifact path exists. That requires fitted joint work and is deliberately not implemented here.

author: schereo
body:
## What

- **Every merge to `main`** builds a dev pre-release as before ("LocalVoice Test", `com.localvoice.dev`). It is now **signed with Developer ID and notarized**, so the `xattr` workaround is gone and macOS permissions carry over between updates.
- **Pushing a `v<VERSION>` tag** (made with `scripts/release.sh`) builds **LocalVoice** (`com.localvoice.app`), signs and notarizes it, and publishes the GitHub release with the changelog section as its notes.
- `dev-build.yml` is renamed to `build.yml`.

## How signing works

- `scripts/sign-app.py` signs every Mach-O file in the bundle one by one, with the hardened runtime and a secure timestamp: the embedded Python, all 200 or so `.so`/`.dylib` files from the wheels, and the helpers. The app itself is signed last. It doesn't use `codesign --deep`, which isn't enough for notarization.
- Entitlements are in `scripts/entitlements/`:
  - the app gets microphone and Apple Events;
  - the embedded Python gets those too, plus `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` (for ctypes/PyObjC closures) and `disable-library-validation`.
- `scripts/notarize-app.sh` submits with an App Store Connect API key, prints Apple's log if the app is rejected, staples the ticket and checks the result with `spctl`.

## Secrets

The workflow has two jobs:

- **`build`** has no secrets. It runs the checks, the pip installs and the build, then uploads the unsigned app as an artifact.
- **`sign`** runs on a fresh runner that runs no third-party code, in the **`release`** environment (only `main` and `v*` tags may use it). It imports the certificate into a throwaway keychain, signs, notarizes, deletes the certificate and publishes.

A tag build fails unless the tagged commit is on `main`. `docs/setup.md` lists the five secrets.

## Tested locally

- Built the portable app and signed all 201 Mach-O files with the Developer ID; `codesign --verify --strict` passes for each file and for the bundle.
- New unit tests for Mach-O detection and the signing plan; all 75 tests pass.
- Notarization of the full bundle: _waiting for Apple (first submissions with a new certificate take long)_.

**Shared layer**

**Prompts**

**Payloads and journeys**
- Kit detail: facts move to a rail beside the glass install panel; update and remove commands fold into a disclosure.

## Copy changes (presentation text only)

Payloads, install commands, URLs, redirects and machine files are unchanged (parity below).
- /prompts Best starting points intro: "Pick the job you have. Each card names one place to start and when to choose something else. Anything that changes code should run on a branch or a copy, never straight on production." becomes "Pick the job you have. Each names one place to start." The branch-or-copy warning now shows on each row that changes code: "Changes code: run it on a branch or a copy, never straight on production".
- Starting-point rows: the labels "Use when", "You get", "Requires", "Changes code?" are reworded as "Requires …", the mode label, and a disclosure titled "What you get and other options"; the Details button is removed (the pick's title links to the same page).
- /prompts area links: the three-title previews are removed.
- Area pages on phones: the selector reads "In {section} {area}".
- Kit detail: new disclosure label "Update or remove it".
- /fix: "Starts with {prompt}" removed from each symptom.
- /start: account invite moved below the steps (text unchanged).

## Verification (local `next build && next start`, against a local build of main 2087793)

- `npm run typecheck`: clean. Unit tests: 65 of 65 pass.
- Smoke: 82 of 82 pass (71 against the branch server, `account.smoke.mjs` 11 of 11 on its own fixture server). Two smoke checks were updated for the new markup: the area page now checks both the rail and the phone selector mark the current page, and the starting-point copy check targets Copy by role.
- `tests/qa/parity.mjs` against main: 426 pages, 308 redirects, 0 findings.
- `tests/qa/run.mjs --quick --ref main`: 4 new moderate findings, listed below; 117 moderate and 4 minor already on main. Two serious axe target-size findings on the area page's section link were fixed after that run; axe (WCAG 2.0–2.2 AA) is clean on /prompts, an area page, a prompt page, a kit page, /start, a step, /fix and /mcp-setup at 393 and 1440 wide.

## Not fixed, and why

- QA moderate touch-target: the kit links inside a starting point's "Requires" line are inline text links (17px tall). The interior spec's accessibility rule applies 44px to standalone controls and lets inline links use WCAG 2.5.8's inline exception; they pass axe's 24px target-size rule.
- From the spec, not done here: /skills keeps its horizontal kit jump bar instead of a 200px kit rail; /learn's start or resume is not lit (resume needs client state); collections do not light "New collection" when nothing is selected. Each can follow in its own PR.

Physical Safari, iPhone and iPad; signed-in collection pages beyond the account fixtures.

body:
The Solar tab gets a glare check, purchase steps (camping included), the golf course in the 3D model and the feeder cables. A new **Elpris nu** tab, in Swedish, for the staff on site shows quarter-hour prices and the month's peak.

**Solar tab**
- **3D model:** the golf course from OpenStreetMap under the buildings (ODbL attribution shown), buttons for each purchase step, and view presets (the buildings / the whole course / the camping). It starts close on the buildings; `?roofs=` and `?frame=` open a choice directly.
- **Purchase steps:**
  1. office + studio (29.7 kWp, ~34,100 kr/yr);
  2. + old office;
  3. + scout cabin;
  4. + the three cabins (75.3 kWp in all, ~77,900 kr/yr).

  Each step shows its value, payback, glare, what must happen first and why it may wait, plus the same steps **without the office's west roof**. The office building alone, without the west roof, is still worth it: 10.3 kWp, ~13,300 kr/yr.
- **Glare card:** hours when the panels' reflection reaches golfers' view along the line of play. It counts only **when golfers are out**, estimated from when cars are plugged in at the club's chargers, and the high season is weighted most. A month × hour table goes with it.
- **The cables between the buildings:** the feeders from the energy analysis, and the line losses for solar at the camping.
- **The camping roofs** (scout cabin, three cabins) are measured from Lantmäteriet's laser tile 62625_5350.

**Elpris nu tab (Swedish, for the staff)**
- The price per quarter hour from now on, with everything on top of spot, as cheap / normal / dear, and the cheapest three hours ahead.
- This month's peak so far, split into the facility and the estimated EV charging, what each kW above it costs, and the room under it hour by hour.
- It states that a peak from today shows only the next day: E.ON's values come a day late, until a HAN reader is fitted on the main meter.

| Roof (glare in golfers' view) | Jun–Aug, h | of it with golfers out, h |
|---|---|---|
| Office building, west roof | 22.3 | 12.6 |
| Old office | 27.8 | 4.6 |
| Office building, south + east | 13.0 | 0.5 |
| Studio, scout cabin, the three cabins | 0 | 0 |

<details>
<summary>The tools (tools/roof-solar), so all of this can be rerun</summary>

- `walkzone.mjs`: eye positions where golfers walk on any OSM hole. Each looks at the pin, at the line of play 150 m ahead, and in the walking direction.
- `glare.mjs`: the sun's reflection traced every 5 minutes of a year.
  - Takes any roof faces or planned arrays.
  - Classifies each hit by its angle to the view.
  - Counts it per period (high season ×3).
  - `--forest` lets the OSM forest block the reflection.
- `site-layers.mjs`: packs the course and the glare runs into `public/data/solar-site.json`.
- `simulate.mjs`:
  - runs the purchase steps (`SOLAR_STEPS` in `public/contracts.js`);
  - `--exclude kansli:W` writes `solar-effekt-nowest.json`.
- `roof_solar.py`: adds the camping buildings, and drops tree canopy over a roof from the face fit and the panel layout. This fixed the north cabin.
- `public/now.js`: the Elpris nu logic, tested in `server/now.test.js`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Caveats</summary>

- **The glare model:** flat ground, a clear sky every day; single trees and buildings in between are not modelled.
- **The scout cabin's roof** is blurred by the trees at the clearing's edge: check it on site.
- **Feeder data** comes from the energy analysis and still needs checking by the electrician (#40).
- **The merge with main** keeps this branch's regenerated `solar-roofs.json`, which already includes #38's studio slope.

</details>

Open items: #40.

author: awall451
body:
## What

The 11/24 brief and watchlist passed two fuel boards with "the move history says X, but the margin says Y":

> Weekly diesel KXDIESELW-26NOV30 … fuelscore --moves 6 --need -18 diesel: 0 of 56 windows (min -16.66c) -> the empirical distribution says YES T5.62 is cheap, but the 41.5c margin gap and the -22c HO settle say the fall accelerates … PASS.

> Monthly gas KXAAAGASM-26NOV30 3.50 … The empirical 6-print moves give about 0.6 YES, and margin reversion at 3.5420 gives 0.75+. Model-dependent, PASS.

Both tools already exist (`fuelscore.py --moves`, `futures.py margin`), but nothing joins them. Whether a wide margin has come before the big falls was left to judgment.

## Change

`python3 kalshi/fuelscore.py regular|diesel --moves K [--need C] [--since D] --by-margin` keeps the usual `--moves` lines and adds two more:

- **`# <grade> K-print moves by start margin (...)`** splits the same windows into thirds by their start margin. The start margin is the window's first print minus the newest RB/HO front-month settle dated before it, the same rule `futures.py margin` uses (it reuses `futures._settle_before`). Each third shows its margin range, n, median, and `need` hits.
- **`# <grade> latest margin M (day): …`** covers the windows that started at or above today's margin: n, the span of their start dates (marked "overlapping"), median, min, max, and need hits. If none started that high, it prints the widest start instead.

It also adds one prompt sentence under the fuelscore entry, with a pin. That sentence includes the warning that a tight `starts` span is one episode, not n independent draws.

## Live output (real journals, read-only)

```
# diesel 6-print moves by start margin (diesel - HO front month; 56 of 56 windows have a settle): low 1.3532..1.5387 n=18 median +0.01c need 0/18 | mid 1.5440..1.7699 n=19 median -8.79c need 0/19 | high 1.7716..2.0509 n=19 median -13.42c need 0/19
# diesel latest margin 2.1007 (2026-11-24): no window started at or above it (widest 2.0509 on 2026-11-05)
# regular latest margin 1.2095 (2026-11-24): 12 of 56 windows started at or above it (starts 2026-11-03..2026-11-18, overlapping): median -15.79c min -18.51c max -13.53c need 12/12
```

How to read it:
- **Diesel:** wider-margin starts have fallen more (median +0.01 → -8.79 → -13.42c by third). Still, no window, even from the top third, reached -18c. Today's 2.1007 is above every start in the history, so the history can't price the weekly.
- **Gas:** every window that started at or above today's margin fell at least the 11.49c the monthly 3.50 needs. But all 12 start between 11/03 and 11/18, so this is one episode. With `--since 2026-11-01`, all three thirds fall about 15c, so the margin effect is mixed up with November's falling-price regime. The line says that plainly rather than handing over a 12/12.

## Verification

- 10 new tests in a new file, `kalshi/tests/test_fuelscore_by_margin.py`. They cover start-margin arithmetic, thirds, the at-or-above line, the "none above" case, need per band, windows with no settle, a missing futures journal, usage errors, and the prompt pin.
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 852 passed.
- Ran live against `$DATA` (output above). It's offline and read-only; plain `--moves` output is unchanged.

author: dranto
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Dranto"} -->
_Requested by **Antoine** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01S7syvHk8sq5akdnkFPkyTb?thread=cmsg_01S7syvHk8sq5akdnkFPkyTbQyDvtzJFYbnBzq66GCyxNk)_

## Ce que fait la PR

- **Catalogues gettext** dans `godot/locale/` : `tree.pot`, `fr.po` (identique à la source), `en.po` (vide, pour la tâche B). 2 138 textes, dont 374 du code.
- **`Loc`** (`scripts/loc.gd`) : `Loc.t` / `Loc.tn` (pluriel) / `Loc.tc` (contexte) / `Loc.key` / `Loc.data` (textes des JSON) / `Loc.num` / `Loc.pct` / `Loc.game_name()`.
- **Données** : les JSON ne sont jamais réécrits. L'extracteur lit les champs de texte ; chaque nombre devient `{0}`, `{1}`… dans le catalogue, et il est réécrit selon la langue (1,5 / 1.5). Un chiffre réglé par F ne casse donc pas la traduction.
- **Textes composés** (noms de notables, mutations, élites, infobulles, résumé du build) : uniquement des gabarits traduisibles (`%s`), aucune concaténation.
- **`Settings.locale`** (`""` = langue du système, `"fr"`, `"en"`), enregistré dans `general/locale`. Ligne « Langue » dans l'onglet Jeu des options (Herbier, navigable au pad), bascule à chaud. Repli sur le français.
- **Pseudo-langue `xx`** (+40 %, accents, entre crochets), limitée aux textes du catalogue : un texte resté en français simple se voit tout de suite.
- **`tools/i18n.sh`** : extraction, `--check` (ajouté à la CI des tests de logique), `--coverage`, `--missing en`, `--lint`.
- **Tests** : `i18n_test.gd` (ajouté à `unit-tests.sh`) parcourt en pseudo-langue le titre, les 4 onglets des options, le HUD, la pause, la carte, l'arbre et les infobulles des 905 nœuds, et échoue si un texte visible reste en français. Il vérifie aussi que Cormorant a tous les glyphes. Nouveau scénario visuel `langue:1280x720` (poids 8).
- `TREE_LANG` / `--lang=` forcent la langue : les tests tournent toujours en français.

## Écart par rapport au brief

Le msgid est le **texte français lui-même**, pas une clé du type `node.<uid>.name`. Les références (fichier JSON, chemin du champ) sont en commentaires `#.` dans le catalogue. Pourquoi : `fr.po` reste identique à la source sans rien maintenir, les Controls de Godot traduisent seuls leur texte, et un texte partagé par plusieurs nœuds ne se traduit qu'une fois.

## Vérifications

- Tests de logique : tous verts (102 s).
- Tests visuels : rendu français identique au pixel. Seule `menu_options_3_*` change (nouvelle ligne Langue), plus les 4 nouvelles références `langue_*`.
- `tools/i18n.sh --check` : catalogues à jour, aucun texte du code hors traduction.

Note : une `Translation` écrite en GDScript, encore enregistrée à la fermeture, faisait planter Godot (code 134). La pseudo-langue n'est donc posée que pendant qu'elle sert, et retirée dans `Settings._exit_tree`.

- #1787 iOS 27 SDK 빌드가 실행 즉시 종료되지 않게 UIScene 생명주기 채택. 같이 실린 것: 버전 1.5.7, EAS iOS 이미지 `macos-tahoe-26.6-xcode-27.2` 지정, 배포 대상이 낮은 Pod를 앱의 16.4로 올리는 플러그인, Release 실행 검증의 테스트 단계 제한 15분.

- #1820 iOS에서 화면 제목의 자동 축소 끄기 — iOS 27 SDK 빌드에서 제목이 아주 작게 줄어든다.

- **네이티브 지문이 바뀝니다**(`app.json` 버전·플러그인 2개, `plugins/`). 이 승격 뒤의 `eas-release` OTA는 스토어 1.5.6 설치본에 닿지 않습니다. `store-build`(main)로 iOS·Android 운영 빌드를 새로 만들어야 합니다.
- **Expo SDK 55 + Xcode 27은 Expo 공식 지원 밖입니다.** Expo 문서는 SDK 57 미만에서 Xcode 27 이미지를 권하지 않습니다. #1787의 플러그인이 그 자리를 메웁니다.

  - #1787의 `testflight` 프로필 빌드 137(1.5.7)이 EAS 클라우드에서 성공했고 TestFlight 처리를 통과했습니다(내부 테스트 중).

body:
## Ringkasan
Rekap kehadiran siswa bulanan dalam bentuk PDF, dikirim otomatis oleh bot WhatsApp pada hari terakhir tiap bulan:
- **Grup tiap kelas**: PDF rekap kelas itu (format seperti rekap wali kelas di aplikasi).
- **Grup utama sekolah**: satu PDF berisi halaman ringkasan + semua rombel.
- Periode tanggal 1 s/d akhir bulan. **Semua tanggal** menjadi kolom; Sabtu, Minggu, dan hari libur diarsir abu-abu (dengan keterangan libur di bawah tabel).
- Libur: dari daftar yang diisi admin (`2026-11-10 Hari Pahlawan`, rentang `a..b`) dan otomatis untuk hari kerja yang tidak punya satu pun data absensi di seluruh sekolah.

## Yang berubah
- `supabase/migrations/20261125120000_wa_rekap_bulanan.sql`: kolom `monthly_recap_*` di `wa_bot_settings` (fitur **mati** secara bawaan).
- `server.js`: pengambil data (aturan sama dengan Absensi Wali Kelas), pembuat PDF (jsPDF + autotable, dimuat saat dibutuhkan), kirim lewat nomor utama, status per bulan (tidak kirim dobel, maksimal 3 percobaan, jeda 10 menit), penjadwal di tick 60 detik yang sudah ada (tanpa `setInterval` baru), susulan tanggal 1-3 bila bot mati di hari terakhir, `POST /admin/send-monthly-recap` (`requireAdmin`).
- `src/components/whatsapp/MonthlyRecapTab.tsx` + tab "Rekap Bulanan": pengaturan, kirim uji ke nomor/grup, kirim sekarang (dengan konfirmasi).
- Templat caption `monthly_recap_class` dan `monthly_recap_main` di `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` dan `WA_TEMPLATES`.

## Langkah setelah merge
1. Jalankan migrasi `20261125120000_wa_rekap_bulanan.sql` di SQL Editor.
2. Salin `server.js` ke `/srv/wa-bot/`, lalu `cd /srv/wa-bot && npm install jspdf jspdf-autotable` (opsional `sharp` agar logo non-PNG/JPG bisa dipakai), lalu `pm2 restart wa-bot --update-env`.
3. WhatsApp Bot → Rekap Bulanan: isi daftar libur, simpan, coba **Kirim uji** ke nomor sendiri, baru aktifkan.
4. Pastikan grup kelas sudah dipetakan (tab Grup Kelas), grup utama sudah dipilih (tab Rekap Grup), dan nomor bot anggota grup-grup itu.

## Pengujian
- `node --check server.js`, transpile TS lolos.
- Logika bot diuji dengan Supabase, jsPDF, dan autotable **tiruan**: data (siswa aktif, catatan terbaru menang, tahun ajaran), jenis tanggal (data/Sabtu-Minggu/libur/otomatis/mendatang), isi tabel dan warna sel, lebar kolom muat A4, paket PDF belum terpasang, kirim terjadwal, tidak dobel, gagal lalu coba ulang terbatas, uji ke nomor, susulan, saklar mati, endpoint.
- **Belum diuji di lingkungan nyata**: jsPDF asli (tampilan PDF), pengiriman WhatsApp sungguhan, dan layar tab di browser. Mohon cek PDF hasil "Kirim uji" sebelum mengaktifkan.

body:
Refs #1516, Part 3/3: the HK wiring the S line owns. Part 1 is the budget (#1535), Part 2 the service and contract (#1569).

**Red line: yes.** It adds a new worker relay, a cash-journal consumer (model and Gaode) and an auth surface. Base: main 80fa20cb. Head: 2283fb2fb9a4d56eb693fa88f2ea302afd8d2de0.

## What

**`deploy/hk/roadbook_relay.py`** (same pattern as nearby, hotel and transit)
- **Worker (`active_roadbook`)**:
  - Reads `CJ_ROADBOOK_INTERNAL_SUBJECTS_JSON`. It must be a non-empty, duplicate-free subset of the G2C@01–99 cohort (M4 entry 18, #1529/#1542/#1566), checked before suppliers are created. If it is unset, the route answers 403 `not_enabled`.
  - Builds `RoadbookService(GaodeNearby(CJ_AMAP_WEB_KEY, operations=AMAP_OPERATIONS), DashScopeRoadbook(CJ_MODEL_API_KEY), RoadbookBudget(HK journal), RoadbookPlaceBudget(HK journal), MemoryRoadbookCache())`.
  - Serves `/run/g2c-demo/roadbook.sock`: 0600, owned directory, 2 slots.
  - The owner is pinned and re-authorized by `RoadbookService` before every Gaode and model call.
- **API (`register_roadbook_routes`)**: `POST /v1/tools/roadbook/places` with one bearer and `no-store`.
  - Bodies are bounded at **16 KiB**: 20 places (the contract maximum) can exceed the generic 4 KiB plugin bound.
  - Replies are bounded at 512 KiB.
  - Relay timeout is **280 s**: uncached places run one after another, 1–2 Gaode calls plus up to 2 model calls each. The App is asked to wait 300 s or send smaller batches.
- `configuration.py`: `ROADBOOK_INTERNAL_SUBJECTS` is in the worker's optional secret names.
- `entrypoint.py`: registers the API route and enters `active_roadbook` in the worker.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `deploy/tests/test_roadbook_relay.py` (new, 11 tests) | PASS |
| `deploy/tests` (`CJ_ENV=local`, `PYTHONPATH=.:scripts`) | PASS, 1252 passed |
| Live HK smoke (one G2C@ account, one known POI) | UNRUN, after merge and deploy |

The new tests use the real Unix socket with the #1569 service and its fixture suppliers. They cover:
- 401 and 403, then a 200 with ready content.
- A cached repeat costs no supplier call.
- A 20-place body above 4 KiB is accepted.
- A body above 16 KiB gets 413; an invalid body gets 400.
- The closed state answers 403 with no supplier calls; an unreachable worker answers 503.
- The roster accepts the authorized cohort with both budgets wired, and refuses everything else.

Already done separately: the 41 template places were verified through `RoadbookPlaceBudget` on HK run -41 (41 `amap-roadbook.1` rows RECEIVED).

author: zhangming700
body:
/kind bug

## Change

After the first BF16 forward, converting the sharded weights to FP32 could leave the fused AllGather buckets and their unpack buffers configured for BF16. A subsequent forward read updated weights but rounded away their FP32 low bits. Both settings of `comm_fusion_zero_copy` were affected.

Refresh the cached gather layout when the effective parameter dtype or shard layout changes. Recreate incompatible unpack buffers with their unsharded parameter views. Validate flat-buffer views by storage, offset, size, dtype and contiguity before reusing a bucket. Retain each parameter’s resolved mixed-precision policy on reset.

## Verification

The original change on `c9e7fca` was validated on eight Ascend 910B3 devices with the full Qwen3-30B-A3B checkpoint. After a warm BF16-to-FP32 reset, all 49 gathers per rank used FP32. Rank-specific sentinels retained their low bits on all eight devices. With zero-copy enabled, the next forward issued 49 direct gathers and zero copy-ins or rebinds. With zero-copy disabled it issued 49 copy-ins.

Cold and warm resets produced identical per-rank losses and gradient norms with zero-copy enabled and disabled at gradient accumulation 1, 2 and 4. Meta initialization, an explicit BF16 communication policy and same-dtype storage replacement also passed. CPU offload with unpinned file-backed CPU weights passed forward and backward. A separate check on ordinary CPU shards observed both consecutive weight updates on every rank.

In one profiled FP32 training step per mode, median per-rank cumulative AllGather time over 98 calls was 1962 ms with zero-copy disabled and 1761 ms with it enabled. Step-time gains varied by accumulation setting.

The PR port targets `JT_dev` at `8d1e0d5` and preserves its per-parameter policy resolution. The eight-device measurements above were collected on the original test base.

author: vimkim
body:
https://jira.cubrid.org/browse/CBRD-28091

## Purpose

- `catcls_get_db_collation ()` 은 `_db_collation` 카탈로그의 행을 배열로 읽고, 행이 많으면 `db_private_realloc ()` 으로 배열을 늘립니다. 이때 realloc 결과가 아니라 항상 NULL이 아닌 인자 `db_collations` 를 검사해서, 확장 실패를 놓칩니다.
- AS-IS: 확장이 실패하면 NULL 주소에 `memset` 을 해 서버 기동이나 SA 모드 유틸리티가 SIGSEGV로 종료됩니다. 또 기존 배열의 유일한 포인터를 NULL로 덮어서 기존 배열을 해제할 수 없습니다.
- TO-BE: 확장이 실패하면 `ER_OUT_OF_VIRTUAL_MEMORY` 를 반환하고, 기존 배열은 호출자(`boot_restart_server ()`, `synccoll_check ()`)가 해제합니다.

## Implementation

- `src/storage/catalog_class.c` `catcls_get_db_collation ()`:
  - realloc 결과를 지역 변수 `new_collations` 에 받아 검사하고, 성공했을 때만 `*db_collations` 에 대입합니다.
  - 실패하면 `ER_OUT_OF_VIRTUAL_MEMORY` 를 `er_set` 합니다. `db_private_realloc ()` 의 lea heap 경로는 실패할 때 오류를 설정하지 않고 NULL만 반환하기 때문입니다.

## Remarks

- 확장 분기는 `_db_collation` 행이 256개(`LANG_MAX_COLLATIONS`)를 넘을 때만 실행됩니다. 정상 운영에서 이 분기에 도달하는 경로는 찾지 못했습니다.
- 확인 방법: debug 빌드의 `csql -S` 에서 gdb로 두 조건을 강제했습니다(fault injection). 배열 크기를 256에서 2로 낮추고, realloc 결과를 NULL로 바꿨습니다.
  - 변경 전 (`develop`): `memset` 에서 SIGSEGV가 발생합니다(`curr_coll = 0x98`). 기존 배열의 포인터도 사라집니다.
  - 변경 후: 함수가 `ER_OUT_OF_VIRTUAL_MEMORY` 를 반환하고 `*db_collations` 는 기존 배열을 그대로 가리킵니다. 호출자가 이 배열을 해제하고, 기동은 "Out of virtual memory" 오류로 끝납니다.
  - fault injection 없이 접속하면 정상 동작합니다(`_db_collation` 10행).
- 같은 함수의 `coll_name` 복사 경계 문제는 [CBRD-28095](https://jira.cubrid.org/browse/CBRD-28095) PR에서 따로 고칩니다. 두 PR은 서로 충돌하지 않습니다.

author: juliuspaulin
body: ## What this is A Planning tab, after Net Worth, for a year-by-year cash flow and net worth projection. It follows the approved layout: summary cards, assumption sliders, cash flow and net worth charts, life events, and a year-by-year table. Moving a slider recalculates immediately. Today's € and Future € switch the same projection between inflation-adjusted and nominal amounts. Compare overlays the other of the first two scenarios on the net worth chart. The numbers in the screenshots are a made-up example (a salary of 3 800 €, rent of 950 €, a 25 000 € net worth). Nothing in the branch is a real account or a real export. [Planning overview](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-8fb877c8-f6f4-55d6-ad39-0810870328ac/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fplanning-overview.png) [Net worth, compared with a keep-renting scenario](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-8fb877c8-f6f4-55d6-ad39-0810870328ac/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fplanning-networth-compare.png) [A custom event financed with a loan](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-8fb877c8-f6f4-55d6-ad39-0810870328ac/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fplanning-cottage-dialog.png) [The same tab in dark mode](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-8fb877c8-f6f4-55d6-ad39-0810870328ac/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fplanning-dark.png) ## How today's figures are filled in `GET /api/planning` reads the user's own data and returns it as `baseline`, plus `defaults` (the slider starting points with those figures already written in). - **Income, spending and rent** are a monthly average. The window is the last 12 calendar months through today. Spending is every expense except the Investments category, because that money is a transfer into the portfolio and the projection invests whatever is left over. Rent is the part of that spending in the Rent category. - A history that already covers the whole window counts empty months as zero and divides by 12. A history that starts inside the window is divided by the months actually on record, so two months of tracking are not diluted across a year. Nothing on record stays at zero. - **Investments and savings now** is the net worth the Net Worth tab shows (assets minus liabilities), rounded to a euro. An account you have not updated keeps its last balance, the same rule as that tab. - Age is not in the database, so a new plan starts at 30. The pension starts at 0. Both are editable. Reset fetches the baseline again and puts every assumption back to those defaults. Events are kept. The banner says what was actually used: the window, any Investments transfers left out of spending, and whether there are accounts yet. ## How a plan is stored One row per user in a new `planning_plans` table (`user_id`, `payload`, `updated_at`). The payload is the scenarios, the selected one, the euro unit, and whether Compare is on. Each scenario holds its assumptions and its events. All nine event types are stored, including a custom event with an optional loan and an optional asset value. The table is created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` inside the existing schema script, so an existing database gains the table and nothing already in it is rewritten. The row is removed with the user. `PUT /api/planning` replaces the document. A plan that does not check out is refused and the stored one is left as it was. The first visit with nothing saved opens one scenario, "Base plan", with the Balance figures and no events. The fictional events in the screenshots were saved through the API for the demo. They are not seeded for a real user. ## Tests `services/planning.py` is the projection. `static/js/planning-math.js` is the same rules, so the page does not round-trip on every slider move. When Node is installed, a test runs both and requires the same rows. The CI image has no Node, so that check is skipped there and the Python cases still run. Covered: the annuity payment (including the 90 000 € / 4.5% / 15 year cottage loan), inflation, the gap between retirement and the pension, financial independence, a home purchase that stops the rent, a custom cost with a loan and an asset, and the other event types. Route tests cover the empty baseline, a round trip of every event type, a rejected save that leaves the stored plan alone, and `init_db` adding the table without rewriting an existing transaction. `python3 -m pytest tests/` — 623 passed, 1 skipped (the pre-existing "no llama runtime in this checkout" skip). ## Deviations from the mockup - A new plan uses age 30 and a pension of 0. The mockup's 27 and 1 900 € were example numbers, and neither is in the database. - Spending leaves out the Investments category. Debt payments stay in spending. A loan that already exists is in the starting net worth and is not paid down unless it is modelled as an event. - The financial-independence target is that year's ongoing living and housing cost divided by the withdrawal rate. The one-off down payment is cash out of the portfolio that year and is not part of the target. That matches the mockup's own formula. - There is no way to delete or rename a scenario. The mockup did not have either. - The "Ideas for later" card is not in the tab. - Compare still means the other of the first two scenarios. The two lines are aligned by age, so a scenario that starts at a different age still lines up. - Chart animation is off, because the charts are rebuilt on every slider move. - Deleting an event asks in the app's own confirm dialog. - Event labels on the charts step onto another row when they would otherwise sit on top of each other. The mockup used two rows, which put "Car" and "First child" on the same line. - The event dialog keeps Delete, Cancel and Save on screen and scrolls the fields, so a short window does not hide the buttons. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: recursiverabbit
body:
Row 21 caught this within the hour and it was mine: with every pod torn down and **zero peer
lines in the intent**, the Router still held three accepts — the two resolver rules and the
world rule. Teardown left rules behind, and the Router also did not *"start with no
forwarding or transit rules"*, which the spec asks for at the other end of the same run.

The whole transit block is now a statement about the pods that are here. No peers, no
transit policy: one conntrack rule and a DROP policy.

**Measured both ends on z620, deployed at `8066cf66d888`:**

    with 4 peers      pod fetch by name          FETCHED
    after teardown    peers in the intent        0
    after teardown    Router FORWARD            -A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate
                                                RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

Nothing else changed; the egress path is untouched and still carries.

author: iammrcupp
body:
Closes #21

## Summary

A Twitch About panel that answers "what's running on screen?" — `twitch/panels/bench-tools.md` holds the four fields to paste (title, image, link, description), and the header image sits next to it as an SVG and its 320×100 PNG render.

Every line comes from the tool's own README or repo description. The chat line lists **megarohas_multichat**, the fork `multichat.service` runs, and credits megarohas's MIT original. duplexchat, its Go rewrite, gets a mention only: its default branch has only a README so far. bench-suite is in — "can I run it?" is the next question. homebrew-bench and bench-recon are out; the doc says why.

Twitch's help center gives the image limits (320 wide, 300 high, under 2.9 MB on the newer page; 320 × 600, under 1 MB on the older one — this fits both). It states no description limit, so the description is kept to 962 characters and the editor's counter is the final check.

`.gitignore` drops every PNG to keep bench frames out. One negation lets drawn panel art in `twitch/panels/` through; the rule still holds everywhere else.

## Test plan

- Rendered the SVG with `rsvg-convert` and checked the PNG at 3× — 320×100, 10 KB, nothing clipped.
- Counted the description block: 962 characters, 13 lines.
- No runtime change — CI runs the usual tests.

- [x] Tests pass (`python3 tests/test_*.py`) — not applicable: no code touched; CI runs them anyway
- [x] Checked on the bench, or says why not — not applicable: the panel goes on the channel page, not the bench

## Stream-safety check

- [x] No password, token or key, and nothing that prints one
- [x] No camera frame or screenshot from the bench — the image is drawn from an SVG in this PR
- [x] Nothing starts a stream or an output without someone pressing Start

author: mmastrac
body:
Upgrades row-major stacked BF16 matmuls (`n % 16 == 0 && k % 128 == 0`) from scalar per-warp FMA (`tessera_stacked_lanes`) to 16x16 2-pass exact BF16 Tensor-Core MMA (`tessera_stacked_lanes_tc`) by generalizing `fg_bf16_mm` with `w_stride` and `r0`. Keeps the scalar kernel as fallback for unaligned shapes.

### Verification
- `cargo nextest run -p tessera-device`, `cargo clippy -p tessera-device --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `stickler` (`comments`, `style`, `lint`, `simcheck`) pass.
- Direct CUDA GPU parity test on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (`batches=16, rows=8, n=256, k=512`): `max_abs_diff = 4.56e-2` (matches CPU BF16 reference `4.56e-2`).
- `nsys` on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (GLM-5.3 + DFlash2, `code_warm`):
  - `[16, rows, 512] @ [16, 256, 512]^T`: `4.85 us -> 4.16 us` (`-14.2%`, `4.1 us` median)
  - Larger batch (`gridY=48`): `26.37 us -> 9.30 us` (**2.84x faster**)
  - Combined time: `87.2 ms -> 77.0 ms` (`-10.2 ms`)

author: refusedguy
body:
## Summary

```diff
 type apiServer struct {
-	wiring      *wiring
+	services    apiServices
 	token       string
 	eventStream <-chan core.HarnessEvent
 	changes     *changeSubscribers
 }
```

`apiServices` holds `status` and `control` as interfaces with only the methods the handlers call. `serve` builds it from `w.status` and `w.control`. The loopback routes and their wire shapes do not change.

## Evidence

Before, `apiServer` held `*wiring`, which includes the dispatcher, SCM, harness and task services. After, its service fields expose only `apiStatus.Active` and the six `apiControl` methods.

Targeted test after the change:

```text
$ go test ./cmd/beacon
ok  	github.com/refusedguy/beacon/cmd/beacon	3.023s
```

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Reverting the commit restores the previous struct.

Blast radius: loopback API. A missing method on either interface fails at compile time, so a caller mismatch appears before merge.

author: vimkim
body:
https://jira.cubrid.org/browse/CBRD-28271

## Purpose

- serial 값을 받는 `NEXT VALUE` 가 페이지 공간이 부족해 실패하면, 장애 뒤 DB를 다시 시작할 수 없게 됩니다.
- AS-IS: `serial_update_serial_object` 는 새 serial 행을 redo 전용 로그(`RVHF_UPDATE`)로 먼저 남기고, 그다음에 행을 같은 slot에 덮어씁니다. 공간 확인은 debug 빌드의 `assert` 뿐이라, release 빌드에서 행이 들어가지 않으면 갱신은 실패하는데 redo 로그는 남습니다. 장애 뒤 restart recovery가 이 로그를 적용하다 같은 이유로 실패해, 재시작과 `checkdb` 가 매번 `LOG FATAL ERROR` 로 멈춥니다.
- TO-BE: 행이 들어가지 않으면 로그를 남기지 않고 `ER_QPROC_CANNOT_UPDATE_SERIAL` 로 실패합니다. 장애 뒤에도 재시작과 `checkdb` 가 정상으로 끝나고, serial 값은 마지막으로 커밋된 값입니다.
- redo 전용 로그: 되돌리는(undo) 기록 없이, 다시 적용할(redo) 내용만 남기는 로그입니다. 트랜잭션이 취소되어도 지워지지 않습니다.

## Implementation

- `src/query/serial.c` `serial_update_serial_object`: `assert (spage_is_updatable (...))` 를 release에서도 동작하는 확인으로 바꾸고, redo 로그를 쓰기 **전에** 실행합니다. 일반 heap 갱신(`heap_update_home`)과 같은 순서입니다.
- 확인에 실패하면 오류를 설정하고 기존 `exit_on_error` 경로(flush mark 종료, sysop abort)로 나갑니다. 로그와 페이지 모두 바뀌지 않습니다.

## Remarks

- 행이 커지는 이유: NUMERIC 값의 디스크 크기가 값에 따라 4~20바이트로 달라서(CBRD-26006), `current_val` 이 커지면 serial 행도 커집니다.
- 행이 들어가지 않을 때 `NEXT VALUE` 와 serial cache write-back은 이전처럼 실패합니다. 이 경우에도 성공하게 하는 폴백과 relocation된 serial 행 처리(CBRD-28272)는 CBRD-28292에서 다룹니다.
- 검증: JIRA 재현 절차(4K 페이지, `unfill_factor=0`, 실패한 `NEXT VALUE` 뒤 커밋하고 프로세스 강제 종료)를 release 빌드에서 실행했습니다.
  - 수정 전: SA 모드와 server 모드 모두 재시작과 `checkdb` 가 `LOG FATAL ERROR: log_rv_redo_record_sync ... data_length = 766` 으로 실패했습니다.
  - 수정 후: 두 모드 모두 재시작과 `checkdb` 가 성공했고, serial의 `current_val` 은 커밋된 값 1입니다.
- 회귀 테스트: `cubrid-testcases-private-ex` 의 `shell/_06_issues/_26_2h/cbrd_28271` 를 추가합니다. SA 모드와 server 모드에서 위 절차를 실행하고, 수정된 debug 빌드와 release 빌드에서 통과했습니다.

author: frunkq
body:
This is Alex's sea test: a rogue planet in a void with a helium sea that just works. Package log: `handover/packages/W-helium.md`.

## What
- **Liquid-only volatiles** (`sse-climate`): helium has no triple point. It now joins the volatiles from its lambda point, its saturated-liquid curve (ln p linear in 1/T) and its critical point, all from the data sheet (PR 475). Every volatile also carries `critical_k`.
- **Sea liquid by phase** (`sse-surface` `climate::liquid_by_phase`): when nothing names the liquid and water doesn't fit, the sea is the most abundant gas whose liquid is stable at the surface. That means above its triple point (helium has none), below its critical point, and with a vapour pressure no higher than the air's. The choice is logged in the climate's assumptions.
- **Wave damping**: each wave train carries `damping_s` = 1/(2νk²) from the liquid's own viscosity (Lamb 1932, art. 348). For the same wave, helium rings about 40 times longer than water.

## Test
`sea::helium_tests::a_rogue_planet_holds_a_superfluid_helium_sea` sets up a world with no orbit and no sunlight, at 1.8 K from its own heat (about 6e-7 W/m²), under 0.02 bar of helium. Nothing in the test names the sea. The climate picks helium, and the sea card shows:
- `superfluid` true;
- a 2.8 mm ripple cut-off;
- wave trains in every band;
- the damping ratio against water.

## Fudges logged
- Helium's latent heat is taken from the curve's end points, and its droplets are white.
- The curve is extrapolated below 2.18 K.
- The damping uses one viscosity, not the two-fluid model.

## Golden (on purpose)
One `contract.jsonl` line: the sea's trains gain `damping_s`.

## Checks, run locally after merging main

- the generated contracts diff
- both reference checks
- the harness

author: dahankzter
body:
Fixes a Section 3 item from the post-0.12 audit: `DmaFile::hint_extent_size` clobbers the file's other attributes.

**Hinting an extent size wiped the file's other flags and its project id.** `fs_hint_extentsize` set the hint with `FS_IOC_FSSETXATTR` on a struct built from zeros plus `FS_XFLAG_EXTSIZE`. That ioctl replaces every attribute it carries, so the call cleared every other xflag (NODUMP, NOATIME, APPEND and the rest), reset the project id to 0, which moves the file out of any XFS project quota it was in, and zeroed the CoW extent size hint. On XFS, a file marked NODUMP went from xflags `0x80000080` to `0x80000800`. I now read the attributes with `FS_IOC_FSGETXATTR` first and change only the extent size and its flag. `ImmutableFileBuilder::with_hint_extent_size` goes through the same call.

## Testing

- `an_extent_size_hint_keeps_the_other_attributes` (in `io::dma_file`): marks a file NODUMP with project id 7, calls `hint_extent_size`, and checks that both survive. On main it fails with `the extent size hint cleared NODUMP`. A variant of the fix that still resets the project id fails with `the extent size hint reset the project id, left: 0, right: 7`.

The test needs a filesystem that takes extent size hints, which in practice means XFS. Anywhere else it says so and checks nothing, so CI (ext4 and tmpfs) skips it. I ran it locally with `GLOMMIO_TEST_POLLIO_ROOTDIR` pointing at an XFS directory. The CoW extent size hint is preserved by the same read and write, but the test does not set it.

author: yuqi1129
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Add a daily, manually dispatchable workflow that warms a contributor fork's default-branch Gradle cache from `apache/gravitino:main`. It uses the same cache key as Fork CI, resolves external Gradle dependencies across all modules (plus Scala 2.13 for `:spark-connector:spark-3.5`, skipping historical `lanceSparkBundle_*` matrix bundles) on a cache miss, and fails fast if dispatched from a non-default branch. Document how to enable and run it.

### Why are the changes needed?

On a cold fork, parallel CI jobs download the same dependencies from Maven Central. HTTP 429 responses have stopped builds before tests could start. A default-branch cache can serve multiple PR branches with matching Gradle build files, and warming dependencies across all modules avoids locking PR branches into a partial cache when `actions/setup-java` hits the primary key and skips saving. [Example failure](https://github.com/yuqi1129/gravitino/actions/runs/45531881876/job/138929495605)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Contributors can enable **Warm Gradle cache** in their fork or run it manually from the default branch.

### How was this patch tested?

- Validated workflow YAML syntax and ran the exact `warmGradleDependencies` init script locally across all 98 subprojects (`-PskipWeb=true --max-workers=2`) and `:spark-connector:spark-3.5` with `-PscalaVersion=2.13`.
- On a GitHub-hosted runner, the fork’s default branch reported a cold Gradle cache, ran 110 `warmGradleDependencies` tasks and the Spark 3.5 Scala 2.13 pass, then saved the cache. [Cold-cache warm-up](https://github.com/yuqi1129/gravitino/actions/runs/45792609521/job/139815173051)
- On a fresh branch with no branch-scoped cache, the standard Fork CI compile check restored the same 4,761,062,791-byte archive (key ending in `2e488b77…3dfe62f`) and successfully ran `assemble -PskipWeb=true`. [Cross-branch restore and build](https://github.com/yuqi1129/gravitino/actions/runs/45794362869/job/139821766623)

author: rhtnddd
body:
## 🔗 관련 이슈

Closes #402

서버: nepyh/rooter-back#408 (rooter-back#405). **서버와 함께 배포해 주세요.** 서버보다 먼저 나가도 새 필드가 없으면 기존과 똑같이 동작합니다(없으면 COMPLETED 로 봄).

## ✨ 작업 내용

서버가 AI 계획을 **앞 구간(6~7일)만 먼저 만들어 응답하고, 남은 기간은 이어서 만들도록** 바뀝니다. 30일 계획의 첫 응답이 약 10초로 줄고, 60초 타임아웃 실패(rooter-back#400)가 없어집니다. 앱은 이 흐름에 맞춰 이렇게 바뀝니다.

- **진행 상황 반영:** 만드는 중인 플랜이 있으면 플랜 목록을 5초마다 다시 불러옵니다(`usePlanBoards`). 새로 만들어진 날이 생기면 할 일·캘린더를 다시 불러와 바로 보이게 합니다. 다 만들거나 실패하면 다시 불러오기를 멈춥니다.
- **홈 안내:** 고른 날짜가 아직 안 만든 날이면 마스코트 안내를 띄웁니다. 오늘 공부 설문 안내가 우선입니다.
  - 만드는 중: "이 날 계획은 루티가 지금 만들고 있어요. 다 만들면 자동으로 나타나요!" → 플랜 목록 보기
  - 실패: "이 날부터의 계획을 만들지 못했어요. 다시 만들어볼까요?" → 남은 계획 다시 만들기 (`POST /plan-generation/{planBoardId}/retry`)
- **알림:** `PLAN_GENERATION_COMPLETED`·`PLAN_GENERATION_FAILED` 를 누르면 홈으로 갑니다.
- **409 `PLAN_GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` 안내:** 만드는 중에 기간·과목을 수정하거나 아직 안 만든 날에 할 일을 추가하면 서버가 409 를 줍니다. 그 사유에 맞는 문구를 보여 줍니다.
- **생성 화면:** 바꾸지 않았습니다. 첫 응답이 빨라져서 바로 홈으로 갑니다.

## ✅ 체크리스트

- [x] 커밋 메시지 규칙을 지켰습니다.
- [ ] Prettier로 코드 포맷을 정리했습니다. — 저장소의 기존 파일도 `prettier --check` 를 통과하지 않아, 상관없는 줄이 바뀌지 않게 돌리지 않았습니다.
- [ ] 로컬에서 정상 동작을 확인했습니다. — 서버 rooter-back#408 이 아직 운영에 없어 기기 확인은 못 했습니다.
  - `tsc --noEmit` 통과
  - 바꾼 파일 `eslint` 통과
  - `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` 16건 통과 (신규 4: 생성 상태·안내 날짜·대표 플랜 우선·진행 요약)

## 💬 기타

- 플랜 수정 화면에서 만드는 중에 기간·과목 입력을 아예 막지는 않았습니다. 저장할 때 409 안내만 띄웁니다. 막는 게 낫다면 이어서 고치겠습니다.
- 서버 배포 뒤 확인할 것:
  - 30일 플랜을 만들면 홈에서 7일째 이후 날짜에 "만드는 중" 안내가 뜬다
  - 수십 초 안에 할 일이 채워진다
  - 완료 알림이 오고 누르면 홈으로 간다

## ➕ 추가 작업 (c815ce5)

- **홈 '일정 생성하기' 409 안내:** 사용자가 실제로 할 일을 추가하는 곳(`AddPlanBoardModal`)의 에러 문구 표에 `PLAN_GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` 가 없어 "일정 생성에 실패했습니다…" 가 떴습니다. 같은 안내("이 날 계획은 아직 만드는 중이에요…")를 상수로 두고 `useAddTodo` 와 함께 씁니다.
- **플랜 목록:** 만드는 중·실패한 플랜 카드 이름 아래에 "남은 계획을 만드는 중이에요"(회색)·"남은 계획을 만들지 못했어요"(빨강).
- **캘린더:** 아직 안 만든 날(generatedUntil 다음 날 ~ 기간 끝)에 "계획 만드는 중"·"계획 만들기 실패" 표시. 누르면 상세 시트에서 설명, 수정·삭제 버튼은 없음. 같은 날 여러 플랜이어도 하나만.
- **플랜 수정:** `GENERATING` 이면 기간 날짜를 막고 "남은 계획을 만드는 중이라 다 만들어진 뒤에 바꿀 수 있어요." 를 보여줌. 서버가 막는 건 기간뿐이라(rooter-back `PlanBoardApi` 409 설명) 이름·설명·대표는 그대로 수정됩니다. `FAILED` 는 서버도 막지 않아 열어 둠.

### 🧪 시뮬레이터 확인 (iPhone 18 Pro, Expo Go)

운영 API 앞에 로컬 프록시를 두고 테스트 계정 플랜의 `generationStatus`·`generatedUntil` 을 바꿔 가며 확인. 저장·추가·다시 만들기·알림 읽음은 프록시가 대신 응답해 운영 데이터는 바뀌지 않음.

- [x] 5초 새로고침, 완료·실패면 멈춤 / 다시 만들기 후 재개
- [x] 홈 안내(만드는 중·실패), 닫기, 플랜 목록 보기, 진행되면 할 일 다시 불러오고 안내 사라짐
- [x] 홈 '일정 생성하기'·할 일 추가·플랜 수정의 409 안내
- [x] 플랜 목록 상태 줄, 캘린더 표시·상세 시트, 플랜 수정 기간 잠금
- [x] 알림함의 계획 완성 알림 → 홈
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test:monitoring` 18건 통과

⚠️ **캘린더 날짜 칸이 main 에서 안 보입니다 (이 PR 과 별개, 1.2.0 에도 있음).** `app/Calendar/Calendar.tsx` 의 스와이프 `Animated.View` 에 `flex: 1` 이 없어 달력 칸 높이가 0이 됩니다(f5d3b36). 위 캘린더 확인은 로컬에서 `flex: 1` 을 넣고 했고, 이 PR 에는 넣지 않았습니다 → 따로 이슈·PR
