author: vishalkotak
body:
Fixes #994. Writes through a shared mapping of an O_APPEND file landed at the end of the host file. The host fd is now opened without O_APPEND, and the guest's own appends use RWF_APPEND, the same approach virtiofsd uses.

The new virtiofs-append test fails on main and passes with this. It also checks that appends don't overwrite data the host appended, which just dropping O_APPEND would break. Full integration suite and unit tests pass on aarch64 Linux.

macOS isn't affected since its pwrite() honors the offset on O_APPEND files. The bug is also on stable-1.19.x, if you want to cherry-pick it.

author: iamrgalisanao
body:
ADR-019 slice 3, part 2: ways back to trading for an expired or clock-locked shop. A revoked shop is **not** covered; it needs the owner's decision. Builds with no vendor key are unaffected.

**Pairs with** the `claude/unblock-shop` branch of `tindaflow-control-plane`. Merge this one first, then that one.

- **Defect fixed:** the control plane answers a certificate under 24 hours old with that same certificate, and the client resets its trusted time only on a new one. So an online renewal could not clear a clock lock for up to a day. A locked client now says so, and gets a new certificate if the last is over 1 hour old.
- **Renewal by file** for a shop with no internet, which until now had two extension codes and then nothing. The request is signed with the installation's own key; the reply is applied with the same checks as an online one.
- **A reply file never moves trusted time back**, so a reply kept for weeks cannot give that time again. Its tests fail if this rule is removed.
- **Drills** of each way back, real client against real control plane, on a database with a sale: nothing outside licensing changes, and the audit log only gains licensing entries.

**A decision to confirm:** a renewal by file restarts the count of extension codes, so a shop that never has internet can continue one file at a time. The provider decides each file.

**Still no way back** (listed in ADR-019): revoked; hardware changed; forked chain; a certificate the build no longer accepts or a lost identity file.

**Local:** unit and feature 439 pass, 2 skipped on Windows; database 1421/1423 (the two existing Windows line-ending failures); cross-repository 16/16; control plane 195/195 on PostgreSQL.

**Not verified:** nothing has run on a shop computer; the `docker compose cp` steps in the README have not been run. The drill makes a license old by re-signing it with the test key as 40 days old.

body:
## Summary

Adds two native UI features on top of the merged native dialog/toast infrastructure:

- `IQuasarDialogService.ShowMessageBoxAsync(...)` for simple confirmations
- a native `QuasarNotice` inline notice component

No page migration and no MudBlazor removal.

## Message box
`ShowMessageBoxAsync(title, message, yesText, noText, cancelText, options, cancellationToken)` returns `Task<bool?>`:

- `true` — Yes
- `false` — No
- `null` — Cancel, Escape, backdrop click, navigation, or canceled token

The Yes button is always shown. `noText` and `cancelText` hide their buttons when omitted. Title and message are rendered as plain text; labels and content are safely encoded. The host wires `aria-describedby` to the message body.

The box uses the existing native dialog host, focus handling, Escape/backdrop policy, sizing, and cancellation semantics.

## Notice

`QuasarNotice` provides:

- severity: Info, Success, Warning, Error
- variant: Outlined, Filled, Text
- dense spacing, optional class/style
- `status` role for informational/success notices and `alert` for warning/error
- `aria-atomic`

## Scope

- No page migration
- No MudBlazor removal
- `QuasarNotice` has no production callers yet; it will be wired by the first notice migration

## Qué incluye
- Control de 5 LEDs de recámaras con un 74HC595 (Q0–Q4) y LED de presencia (Q5).
- Presencia con PIR HC-SR501: calentamiento de 30 s y el LED sigue encendido 10 s tras el último movimiento.

74HC595: datos GPIO16, reloj GPIO17, latch GPIO21. PIR: GPIO26.

- `POST /api/lights/room?n=1..5&state=on|off|toggle`
- `POST /api/lights/all?state=on|off`
- `POST /api/lights/presence?mode=auto|off`

El estado aparece en `modules.lights` de `GET /api/status`.

## Cómo se probó
- [x] Las 5 recámaras se encienden y apagan una por una y todas a la vez
- [x] El LED de presencia responde al PIR y se apaga a los 10 s
- [x] Pruebas unitarias de la lógica (`pio test -e native`)
- [x] Cableado y documentación revisados contra el montaje real

Test files only. `d1-tests/bridge-placement` is unchanged. Its race cases already fail (8/9) when the bridge path's placement guard is removed. The earlier mutation changed `placementAssertionQueries`, and the bridge path never calls it: making that function throw still passes all 9 cases.

## What and why

Everything the branch holds that `main` does not. The newest part makes the loader read **Qwen3.5 hybrid decoders** (Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers alternating with gated full-attention ones), validated on the real Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base.

### This session's work

- **Qwen3.5 / `qwen3_5_text`**: layer types (`linear_attention` / `full_attention`), the `linear_*` geometry (key and value heads and dimensions, convolution kernel), partial rotary from `rope_parameters`, the attention output gate and the norm weight offset 1. The mixer tensors keep checkpoint `[out, in]` order; `conv1d` `[C, 1, K]` becomes `[C, K]`. The vision tower and MTP head are left out. Tested against the pinned 0.8B `config.json` and the names in its safetensors header (488 tensors).
- **Layered decoders** (Gemma 4): the layer layout derived from `config.json` (model-config 1.6.0), `gemma4_unified` bundles' text decoder, per-layer input tables sliced by column, routed experts restacked.
- **DeepSeek**: latent-attention and per-expert checkpoints, the absorbed latent-attention tables, the model-config 1.7.0 fields; renormalized greedy or group-limited routing and splitting a quantized projection are refused rather than guessed.
- Llama 3 RoPE scaling normalized, unknown `rope_type` refused.

### Inherited from the pinned base (`fa99d71`, not on `main` yet)

Eleven commits by the repository owner that the main project already pins: block-scaled E4M3 FP8 weights with validated scales (and the reference conversion), pinned Kimi FP8 metadata with bounded reads, GLM latent norms, packed experts and routing defaults, decoder activation and sliding-attention metadata, SmolLM3 per-layer rotary configuration, and an OLMo layer-count fix. Merging this PR brings them to `main` too.

## Purpose

- `catcls_get_db_collation ()` 은 `_db_collation` 카탈로그의 `coll_name` 과 `checksum` 값을 `LANG_COLL_COMPAT` 구조체의 고정 크기 배열에 복사합니다. 두 복사 모두 배열 크기 안에서 끝난다는 보장이 없습니다.
  - `coll_name`(32바이트): 복사 길이의 상한을 32로 두고 `coll_name[길이]` 에 `'\0'` 을 써서, 이름이 32자이면 배열 바로 뒤에 씁니다.
  - `checksum`(33바이트): 길이를 `assert (str_len == 32)` 로만 확인하므로, release 빌드에서는 길이 제한 없이 복사합니다.
- AS-IS: 32자 이름은 바로 다음 필드 `codeset` 을 덮어, 이미 읽은 값(예: UTF-8 = 5)이 0이 됩니다. 32자보다 긴 checksum은 구조체 끝을 넘어 배열의 다음 원소를 덮습니다.
- TO-BE: 이름은 최대 31자, checksum은 최대 32자로 자르고 `'\0'` 을 배열 안에 씁니다. 다른 필드와 다음 원소는 바뀌지 않습니다.

## Implementation

- `src/storage/catalog_class.c` `catcls_get_db_collation ()`:
  - `coll_name`: 복사 길이의 상한을 `sizeof (coll_name) - 1` 로 바꿉니다. 다른 콜레이션 이름 복사 코드(`COLL_NAME_SIZE - 1`)와 같은 기준입니다.
  - `checksum`: `assert` 뒤에 복사 길이를 `sizeof (checksum) - 1` 로 자릅니다. debug 빌드의 `assert` 는 그대로 둡니다.

## Remarks

- 현재 CUBRID가 만드는 콜레이션 이름은 최대 31자이고 checksum은 항상 32자입니다. 두 컬럼은 `varchar(32)` 이고 SQL로 `_db_collation` 을 고칠 수 없습니다. 그래서 일반 사용 경로에서는 재현되지 않으며, 메모리 경계를 지키는 방어적 수정입니다.
- 확인 방법: debug 빌드의 `csql -S` 에서 gdb로 id 5 콜레이션의 값을 바꿨습니다.
  - 32자 이름: 변경 전 (`develop`)에는 `codeset` 이 5에서 0으로 바뀝니다. 변경 후에는 이름이 31자로 잘리고 `codeset` 은 5 그대로입니다.
  - 40자 checksum (`assert` 는 gdb로 건너뜀): 변경 전에는 40바이트를 복사해 다음 배열 원소의 `coll_id` 를 덮습니다. 변경 후에는 32자로 잘리고 다음 원소는 바뀌지 않습니다.
  - 모든 주입 실험에서 기동은 이름 또는 checksum 불일치 오류로 끝납니다. 주입한 값이 로드된 콜레이션과 다르기 때문이며 예상한 결과입니다. 주입 없이 접속하면 정상 동작합니다.
- 같은 함수의 realloc 실패 검사 문제는 [CBRD-28091](https://jira.cubrid.org/browse/CBRD-28091) PR에서 따로 고칩니다. 두 PR은 서로 충돌하지 않습니다.

author: zlangbert
body:
The second of two stacked PRs that move the last crates' log calls to the rule, on top of `worker`'s, #2692.

The calls in `hub` were from before the rule: values in their messages, and no name to search by. Each of its 328 has a name, a fixed message and its values as fields now. It was the last crate to move, so the policy test holds every crate, and its list of those from before goes. Part of #2674.

**Less of what people write, and agents say, can reach the log,** which `docs/principles/observability.md` refuses:

- A report from an agent that's dropped, which was logged whole at `debug` and can hold its reply or a suggestion. Now what the report needs.
- A frame that couldn't be read, from a worker, a provider's adapter or a client, by an error whose words can quote what was in it. Now the kind of error and the column.
- A stored value that couldn't be read as JSON, an archive's metadata, and the providers' settings, whose `args` can hold a secret, for the same reason. `JsonProblem` in `crates/hub/src/error.rs` is that error without `serde_json`'s words, so what a client is told of one says less too.
- A paired device's name, and the username GitHub gave for a token of another user's. Now the ID alone.

**Levels that change,** to what the guide gives them:

- `error` to `warn`: the checks of the GitHub logins, and of whether the default can push, and keeping who GitHub says an account is, since each is tried again.
- `warn` to `info`: an instance is ending.
- `warn` to `error`: a second provider of the same name is left out, since it stays out until someone changes the settings.

**The fields are named alike:** `workspace_id` and `session_id` where a line had `id`, `workspace` or `session`. A line that had a workspace's name, which is a title someone can write, has its ID.

**Seven functions and a file are split,** since an event with fields takes more lines than `clippy` and the policy test let a function and a file have. Settling a workspace an earlier hub left part way through a move is `hub/workspaces/settling.rs`. Nothing in them does anything else.

**Where the state lives:** nothing is kept.

**Needs the owner:**

- `tools/policy/tests/policy/logs.rs`: `NOT_MOVED` goes, with the code that read it, so there's no list to add a crate to.
- `docs/principles/observability.md`: the policy test "holds every crate to it", in place of "every crate to it but those it lists", and that rule's *Not built* goes.
- The level of a second provider of the same name, above, which wasn't in what was agreed.

**Checked:**

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy on every target of `hub`, `policy` and `daemon`, the tests of `hub`, `logging` and `policy`, and the e2e tests of other builds and of stopping the hub.
- A new test that what a stored value holds isn't logged, read as a column's and otherwise. No test there had a value that couldn't be read.
- Tests that changed: three found a line by its wording, and find it by its event's name.
- Broken on purpose, with a test failing each time: keeping `serde_json`'s words of a stored value, read each way, and an event in `hub` without a name.
- The type of each ID newly called `workspace_id` or `session_id`, by reading it.
- The guide says nothing of these lines.

**Not checked:** the rest of the suite, what only another platform compiles, and the other crates on top of `hub`, left to CI. A real hub's log. No test covers a report that's dropped, a frame that can't be read, or the settings.

**Left open:** an `ApiError`'s message is for the person it's told to, so it can name an account, which may be an email address, or a file they attached, and about two hundred of these events have one as their error. It was so before this too. It's in #2674, with the check for secrets and email addresses.

+  test       npm ci -> build -> test

author: denchiklut
body:
Little Oa is Arc's Little Arc: a small window for one link or a quick search. It is a window style of the ordinary window with a sidebar container of its own, as in Arc, on Chromium's popup browser type.

Research: `docs/.local/research/arc-little-arc-static.md` (§12 and §13 reconcile it with live, §14 is the saved state, §15 the downloads tray, §16 the profile switch and traffic lights), `arc-little-arc-engine-static.md`, `arc-little-arc-live.md` (six live runs on Arc 1.174.2, the last partly on 1.174.3; §18 is the sixth; §16 is the tray, §17 the profile switch) and `arc-downloads.md` §18 (a download's source address). Feature page: `docs/features/little-oa/README.md`.

## Commits

1. **core** and four Chromium patches
   - 0026: the app's split view gets a disposition of its own (`SPLIT_VIEW`), so Blink's ⌘⌥ `NEW_SPLIT_VIEW` can reach the app as a background page, as ArcCore's.
   - 0027: `LITTLE_WINDOW` and the page menu's command (ArcCore's ID 53249), enabled for a valid standard link outside incognito.
   - 0028: a new tab stays in the browser it is asked of, so a popup holds several pages.
   - 0029: a popup's browser never asks for the last session.
   - Core makes `TYPE_POPUP` for a Little window, adds Open Link in Little Oa after Split View (fourth), and hands the menu's open to the app as an address, as it does for the incognito item.
2. **devkit**: `BrowserType` on `browser(windowID:type:)`, `PageEvent.openLinkInLittleWindow`, the stub's menu item.
3. **ui**: the window (an `NSPanel`), Arc's frames (490 × 329 bar, saved frame or 1185 × 832, +30/+30 cascade or about the pointer, 20 pt clamp), the 47 pt bar, entry points (⌥⌘N, page menu, ⌘⌥-click, links from other apps), reuse on the same entry address, pages inside, Open in (⌘O, green button, ⇧⌘O list), the profile chip with the per-host preferred profile, close and Archive with source `littleArc`, the permission card, the tip, the idle sweep, the link-open zoom on Peek's spring, and menu states.
4. **ui**: Settings ▸ Links rows under Arc's keys and defaults, the Carbon global hot key that follows the menu binding, and Air Traffic Control's Little Oa destination.
5. **docs**.
6. **ui** and **docs**: the saved state as Arc's (below).
7. **core**, **devkit**, **ui**, **docs**: the downloads tray (below), then two fixes and a docs commit for a download's source address.
8. **core**: a window's browser takes its type when it is made. **ui** and **docs**: the profile switch and Open in (below).
9. **core**, **devkit**, **ui**, **docs**: a page's profile, and the page Open in loses as Arc does (below).
10. The last differences from Arc, one commit each (below): **core** patch 0030 with **devkit** and **ui** for DevTools, then **ui** for the show path, the bar on losing key, the layout modes, the cards, the Open in list and the bar, two commits of corrections after a live look, the docked DevTools layout, and **docs**.

The plan had one commit per step; the UI steps share files, so they are two commits. The saved state's style change and its files are one commit for the same reason.

## Saved state

- The `little` sidebar context is gone. A window has Arc's `WindowStyle`: `standard(sidebarContext)` or `little(state)`.
- The state has Arc's fields: a session (id, entry point, preferred frame, start time), the profile, `shouldShowProfileIndicators` (more than one profile in use when the window is made; the chip shows only then), `modalState` and `downloads`. The first frame is placed from the session's anchor, and a reused window takes a new session.
- A Little window is written to `windows.json` as `style: {"little": …}` and its pages to a `littleBrowser` container in `sidebar.json`, under Arc's keys. The entry point is coded by Arc's table, the hot key's `{"externalLink": true}` included; a style that doesn't read back is a standard window's, as Arc's.
- Quit closes a key bar-only Little window first and closes or archives nothing else.
- At launch AppKit hands a Little window back (its saved state says `isLittleArc`) and it is refused. Its record goes at the first save. Containers with no window are removed after a window closes, not at launch, and the idle sweep also runs a second after launch and covers such containers.

This changes what a quit does to open Little windows: their pages are no longer archived. As in Arc they are gone once a window closes after the next launch, unless the sweep archived them first.

## Downloads tray

- **Core**: a download carries the registrable domain of its source address. The source address is ArcCore's: what the page that started the download shows while that page is open, else the file's own.
- **DevKit**: `Downloads.events`, a stream per caller with ADK's cases (`initialized`, `create`, `update`, `failed`, `cancel`, `paused`), and the starting page's address, title and session ID on `Download`. The stub emits the same events.
- **UI**: a Little window hears of every new download of its profile from the moment it is made, whichever window starts it, and keeps its own list, saved in its record as Arc's `DownloadData`. The tray is a row of 250 × 56 cards along the bottom of the page, oldest on the left, 20 pt in, which scrolls sideways and lets clicks and scrolls between the cards through to the page. A card has the file's icon with a ring while it runs, the name, and the Library's line. A click on a finished card opens the file; ✕, shown only under the pointer, removes the card and cancels the download unless it finished or was cancelled.
- Kept from Arc, faults included: a second click on the same card does nothing until another is clicked or the row changes; failed and paused events are ignored, so such a card stays as its last update left it; a paused download is saved in a form that doesn't read back; a new card isn't scrolled into view.

This also changes the Library's downloads page, which shares the line with the tray as Arc's does: "from ‹site›" names the registrable domain, and the site of the page the download was started from while that page is open (a file a page on example.com links to on a CDN reads "from example.com"); a paused row reads "Paused · from ‹site›"; a running one shows nothing while its size is unknown.

## Core's create call, the profile switch and Open in

- **Core**: `WindowBrowser::GetOrCreate` takes the browser's type, as ArcCore has a creator for each; the set of popup window IDs is gone. A page move or a page creation that finds no Browser makes a standard one: a Little window's Browser is always made with the window.
- **Profile switch**, as Arc's: a Little window's profile is its own stored one (the chip, making pages, the Open in target and the cross-profile check read it). A switch changes it, and the hidden Space's with it as Arc's file shows, and makes only the shown page again. The other pages go on in the profile and Browser they have. A window opened on a link writes the host's preferred profile; one from the menu, the hot key or a ⌘⌥-click doesn't. The downloads tray stays with the profile the window was made in.
- **Open in** always closes the Little window, and its other pages go to the Archive, as a control run in Arc showed. Before, a Little window with pages left stayed open.
- The traffic lights needed no change: Arc's bar also draws three buttons from AppKit's factory with the green one re-targeted, and shows the window's own only in full screen.

- **A page left in the old profile**, moved by Open in to a Space of the new one, is lost as in Arc: it shows in the standard window for a moment, closes with the Little window and is archived from that Space (reason manual), after the window's other pages. Core's `Page::GetProfileID` and DevKit's `Page.profileID` say which profile a page was made in. Doing this Oa's own way (loading the page again in the Space's profile) is #169.

## The last differences

Research for these: static §17, live §18 and `oa-little-arc-pixel-audit.md`.

- **DevTools**: ArcCore doesn

## What

This is the first slice of the social planner (build plan phase 3). The scope is the option chosen on 25 Nov: "Planner + Facebook auto-post".

- **`/social`**: month, week and 30-day list views in Malaysia time. A **Needs you** panel lists manual channels that are due, and failed Facebook posts with Retry.
- **Post editor** (`/social/[id]`): text, an optional link, up to 10 library images in the order you pick them, channels and a time. You can save it as a draft or schedule it. Once any channel has gone out, the post is locked and can't be changed or deleted.
- **Image library** (`/social/library`, `POST /api/social/image`): JPG and PNG up to 4 MB. Files go in the existing public `PAGE_IMAGE_BUCKET` under `social/`.
- **Facebook Page publishing** (`lib/social/facebook.ts`): a new `social` job in `schedule.yml` (`npm run social:run`).
  - The job claims a row before posting it, so two runs can't post the same thing twice.
  - Errors that look temporary are retried up to 3 times. Any other refusal fails straight away.
  - A post more than 12 hours late is never published on its own. Retry moves it to now.
  - A row cut off mid-publish is marked failed after 15 minutes and is not posted again, because it may already be live.
  - The job is skipped until `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID` and `FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN` are set.
- **Every other channel** (Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, X) is posted by hand and then marked posted, optionally with a link to the live post.
- Only `super_admin`, `management` and `marketing` can use the planner, and everything is audit-logged.
- **Migration 009** adds `sales.social_post`, `sales.social_post_channel` and `sales.social_media`, all in the `sales` schema only.
- Setup and behaviour are documented in `docs/social-planner.md`.

## Before it posts for real

1. Run migration 009 (`npm run db:migrate -- --apply`).
2. Add the GitHub Actions secrets `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID` and `FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN`. The token must be a Page token that can publish (`pages_manage_posts`).
   - I haven't confirmed whether the existing lead-ads token `META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN` has that permission, so it is deliberately not reused.
   - The Graph parameters used are `/feed` with `message`/`link`/`attached_media` and `/photos` with `url`/`caption`/`published`. Check them against Meta's current docs.

## Tests

- 23 new tests: 11 pure tests (time, calendar, state, and Graph calls with a fake fetch) and 12 DB tests. The DB tests ran against a local Postgres 16 with a stub `app_user`/`audit_log` and migrations 000 + 009, not the real CRM schema.
- `npm test` (no DB): 450 tests, 0 failing, 207 skipped. `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `next build` are clean.
- I checked the screens locally in a browser with demo data, using a temporary sign-in bypass that is not committed. I also checked that a refused schedule keeps what was typed as a draft.

author: abu-aska
body:
## What this adds

A research hub at `docs/hub.html` that rebuilds itself from the records on main, superseding #54. The curated results report stays at `docs/index.html` as the Pages homepage; this branch adds a single topbar link to the hub instead of rewriting the page, so it applies cleanly on top of the merged results-site stack.

The hub renders results parsed from `experiments/*/results.jsonl` by variant name, never from hardcoded KL values: Gemma E8 at 4.5 bits, the integer ball on three models, the packed ball file read back bit for bit, and the Hadamard turned E8 record. The Hadamard numbers come from the merged `e8-hadamard-real-weights-2026-11-22` record and are checked against its `results.out` table.

Roofline figures come from the Pillar 2 table and are labelled ceilings, not measurements; the summary sentence under that table is rendered from the parsed rows, not hardcoded. The hub also indexes every experiment folder and the open pull requests. The same numbers are in `docs/data.json`.

## How it stays current

`site/build_hub.py` renders the hub from `site/hub_template.html`. It exits non-zero on any missing or unparsable record, missing headline arm, or missing roofline row. `--check` verifies `docs/data.json` against the sources. PR titles and summaries are fetched live and normalized, so an em dash in an outside PR title cannot break the build.

`.github/workflows/hub.yml` runs the builder on pull requests that touch the experiment records, the builder, the template, or the hub files, and rejects a hand-edited `docs/data.json`. On pushes to main it rebuilds the hub, verifies with `--check`, and commits `docs/data.json` and `docs/hub.html` with `[skip ci]`. An actor guard stops the bot commit from re-triggering the workflow. Pages build settings are unchanged.

## Verification

The build ran from this branch against current main: 27 experiment folders, 8 open PRs, `--check` passes, and the generated `docs/hub.html` has no em dashes or unreplaced template placeholders.

author: ikrar06
body:
## What was wrong

- GitHub did not run the hourly schedule: after the reading at 15.01 WITA there was none at 15.20, 16.20 or 17.20. The page then put all 19 downloads of those three hours into the hour it was opened.
- When GitHub limits requests from a network (60 an hour without signing in), the page showed zeros.

## What changes

- **Schedule**: every ten minutes instead of every hour. GitHub runs schedules late in this repository (the daily calendar monitor has started 4 to 8 hours late), so more chances to run is what keeps readings close together.
- **Readings file**: a fourth column, `sejak`, the time of the reading before (when the old total was last seen). Rows written before stay readable.
- **Page**: a rise whose two readings are at most 30 minutes apart goes to its hour. Further apart, it is shared over the hours in between, drawn paler, and listed as a span ("antara 15.01 dan 18.06").
- **Fallback**: when GitHub will not answer, the page shows the last written-down totals and says so.
- **Branch `unduhan`**: a reading that only moves the time replaces the commit before it, so a quiet day is one commit, not 144.

## Checked

- `node --test` 23 pass (unduhan: 17).
- The save step run ten times against a throwaway repository: counts keep their own commits, time-only readings collapse, history stays whole (fetch depth 2; at depth 1 the replaced commit lost its parent).
- The page with made-up readings in a browser: the gap of today drawn as a span, a close reading in its hour, the 403 fallback.

## Not checked yet

- Whether GitHub really runs the ten-minute schedule here. That can only be seen after merge.

body:
`slimMessage` kept only `text`, reactions and files, so anything Slack puts in `blocks` or `attachments` never reached the model. A reply that posts a bullet list can come back with `text` holding only the first line, and the list items are gone.

## Change

- `blocks_text`: plain text rendered from the message's blocks (rich text sections, bullet and numbered lists, quotes, code, links, mentions, emoji, plus `section`, `header` and `context`). It is set only when it differs from `text`, so ordinary messages look the same as before.
- `attachments`: title, link, text (or fallback), `from_url`, `service_name`, and the attachment's own `blocks_text`.
- `slack_search_messages` matches also get `blocks_text`.

Mentions stay as `<@U…>` ids, same as `text`.

## Testing

No test runner in this package, so I checked the helpers against fixtures (a message with nested bullet and numbered lists, a plain message whose blocks match `text`, an attachment unfurl, and section/header/context/divider blocks) and ran `node --check index.js`.

Restart the `slack` server (`/mcp`) after pulling.

author: gabosarmiento
body:
## Change

End-to-end tests for the run's **own** tabs. The person can see and use those tabs too, so whatever page they leave in one is theirs. A new file, `chrome/e2e/owntabs.e2e.test.js`, has 7 tests and changes no extension code.

**Pass today:**
- **A click in the run's own tab:** the link the person clicks pauses the run. Its next read and act answer `paused_by_owner`, with nothing of the page.
- **A run tab dragged out of its group:** it stays the run's and stays fenced (its three rules). Only its own page is read, and an open off the run's sites is still `site_not_listed`.
- **A tab of the person's dragged into the run's group:** it never becomes the run's. It is not in the run's tabs and not fenced. An open of its exact address goes to the run's own tab, and nothing typed in it reaches a result. The run's Stop and the taf's next run leave it open.
- **Two runs of two tafs (two grants) at once:**
  - each has its own tab and its own group;
  - a read of one is `page_changed` in the other;
  - when both fill a field at the same moment, each value lands in its own tab;
  - one taf closing its run, and that taf's next run, leave the other's tab, group and fence as they were.

**Known bugs, kept as `todo` tests, each with its cause:**
1. **An address the person types in a run's own tab, on the run's sites, is read by the run's next `read`.** `runner.js` `onCommitted` takes every on-site commit in a tab of the run's own as the run's: it calls `noteAddress` with no `persons(d)` check and no `stepping` check. `read()` and `act()` only check a joined tab (`joinedNow`).
2. **The person's Back or Forward in a run's own tab: the run's next `read` reads the page they land on.** Same cause. The `forward_back` qualifier isn't checked there, and the page Back lands on is already in the run's trail.
3. **A second taf with the same name, under another grant, closes the first taf's kept tab.** A taf's finished run (`done`, `tafGroup`, `greying`) is keyed by the taf's name, not its grant.

`docs/chrome-e2e.md` lists the new coverage and the three known bugs. Under "Not covered yet" it notes that a drag is made with Chrome's own `tabs.group`/`tabs.ungroup`, because headless Chromium has no tab strip.

## Validation

- `cd chrome && npm run e2e`: 67 tests, 64 pass, 0 fail, 3 todo, three runs in a row. One more run with every core busy gave the same result.
- `node --test e2e/owntabs.e2e.test.js` alone: 4 pass, 3 todo, three times.
- `cd chrome && npm test`: 303 pass, 0 fail.
- `python3 scripts/public_text.py`: clean.
- Regression cases: the three `todo` tests fail on the current code with the causes above. Each starts to pass, and should drop its `todo`, once its fix lands.
- Not run: a real mouse drag of a tab, and a drag to another window.

## Compatibility and rollout

None. Tests and docs only; the extension's code is unchanged.

- [x] Public text, fixtures, logs, and screenshots contain no secrets or customer data.
- [x] Relevant tests and documentation are updated; Unreleased notes added when needed.
- [ ] Requested changes are addressed; a maintainer must review the final revision.

author: ceccec
body:
Three commits (ad1cd0a6c, eda87825d, 45f687427).

## What changes
- **The clay walk** (`clay { walk }`). k qubits hold a superposition of 2 ^ k states, and its cluster is every family formula that reaches it. Lean walks all 1000 qubit counts below the thousand-bit bound (`lean/tools/Thousand.lean`) and writes each formula with the theorem that binds it to its library notion. The door answers `walked: true`, `discovered: 100%`: 9509 cluster members, each held by a kernel theorem, none unclaimed. The register's 38 relations need 323 qubits, the NIST beacon board 512, the CERN checksum 32.
- **Each family formula bound** in `Qpu.General.Meaning`: twenty definitions carry the docstring of the notion they are. The meaning gate's list of standing violations shrinks from 1452 to 1431.
- **The kernel as a catalog** in the collections Payload's ecommerce plugin owns (`src/quantum/processing/catalog.ts`, `imagine { catalog }`). A product is a theorem; a variant is one worked example of it from one of the fourteen witnesses of the example's address. Every document is a receipt whose id is the UUID of its collection and content. A variant is ordered at no price, the public funding the work through the licence table's donation link; the order is one more receipt and names every variation of use it opens.
- **Served without Payload, seeded with it.** The site writes the catalog as Payload's REST API answers it (a find of each collection, each product with its variants joined) and a page for every product through VitePress's dynamic routes, with a schema.org Product that is free and has the donation as its action. Where Payload is installed, `seedCatalog` creates the same documents through the create its SDK and local API share, handing on the ids Payload gives; `recognisePayload` finds it absent here.
- **Ten missing proofs.** The code cited theorem names the kernel did not hold, nine of them in the NIST and CERN attest door. Asked through `imagine`, none was served, so each is written in Lean as the general law its check decides, proved from Mathlib, with its reflections. Two names remain in the standing list, both theorems of the unit's own tree.
- **Examples no hand writes**: one for each relation of the register, each family formula, and each textbook theorem no example named (evaluated at the first values that meet its premises). They are marked `made`: the audit replays them and the matcher does not weigh their words.
- **The work done by hand is the door's**: `settle`, `sync`, `ratchet`, `intake` (2.0 GB in 6 s), and `prose`, the check CI ran alone, now a step of the local chain.

## CI on this PR
- The first `build` failure was the prose check: three messages typed in TypeScript. Fixed in eda87825d, and the check now runs before every commit.
- The second was 1615 dead links: the file routing the product pages lay under `site/`, which git ignores. Fixed in 45f687427: the routes live in `site/.vitepress/catalog-routes.ts` and the seed writes the file that names them.

## What it does not do yet
- The catalog is walked but 48% discovered: about half of the products have no worked example yet, counted by module in the answer.
- The author's applications for public funding are not generated yet.

## Checks
- Every pre-commit and pre-push gate passed on each commit.
- New tests: the walk against the door's own integers and the kernel index; every catalog document's id recomputed, the pages walked, an order recomputed, a seeding through a stand-in; an intake of a temporary directory. The site was built and checked in a browser: 1625 product pages, the REST documents, no page errors.

author: aleche28
body:
The track repository page, as specified in [`docs/prd/068-track-repository.md`](docs/prd/068-track-repository.md). UI only: no API, migration or OpenAPI change. It also records #67 as done in the roadmap.

Closes #68.

## What changes

- **`/repositories/track` lists a linked account's repositories** from `GET /accounts/{provider}/repositories`.
  - With one account it is selected automatically. With several, a picker chooses one, and nothing is requested until then. The choice is kept in `?account_id=`, so a reload keeps it. An ID that names no linked account counts as no choice.
  - Accounts of a provider `GET /providers` no longer lists are left out.
  - An account with `needs_relink` gets a re-link link, and its repositories are not requested.
  - With no account, the page links to `/settings/accounts` and the public form stays usable.
- **The list.** Each row shows the name (linking to GitHub), public or private, the default branch, and *Track*.
  - Repositories already tracked show "Tracked". The page matches `provider` and `provider_repo_id` against `GET /repositories`, because the API's `tracked` marker is still only proposed.
  - The filter matches `full_name` as the user types, with no request.
  - An empty list explains that the app can't see any repository yet. The install link sits under the list.
- **Tracking** sends `POST /repositories` without `tracked_branch`, so the repository is tracked on its default branch. Changing the branch is #69.
  - Success: a banner "Tracking acme/docs on main." with a link to the repositories page. The row turns into "Tracked", and focus moves to the banner.
  - Each failure has its action: `409` says it is already tracked and refetches the tracked list; `404` links the installation when `install_url` is present; `403 forbidden` links a re-link of the account; `429` says how long to wait. Anything else shows `ApiErrorMessage`.
  - While a request runs, every *Track* button is disabled, and the one that sent it reads "Tracking…".
- **Public repository form.** One `owner/name` field, checked against GitHub's naming rules before any request, sent without `account_id`. A `404` explains that a private repository has to come from an account's list.
- **API hooks.** `useAccountRepositories` (in `accounts.ts`, keyed `['accounts', id, 'repositories']`, so unlinking drops it) and `useTrackRepository`. The mutation adds the new repository to the cached tracked list, and refetches that list on success and on `409`.
- **Entry point.** The repositories page placeholder links to the track page.

Where the code departs from the plan, the PRD's new *As built* list records it. The main points: discovery lives in `accounts.ts` to avoid an import cycle, the public form is GitHub only, and focus moves only after tracking from the list.

## Docs

- `docs/roadmap.md`: #67 and #68 are recorded as done in Phase 4. "Choose the branch" moved from the track page to the repositories page.
- `docs/prd/067-linked-accounts.md` status, the new `docs/prd/068-track-repository.md`, and the UI tests list in `AGENTS.md`.
- `docs/roadmap-stakeholders.md` is unchanged: tracking was already in *Now*, and the web app stays in *Next* until Phase 4 is finished.

## Testing

`make ci` passes, with 173 UI tests (69 new):
- The hooks: the request body with and without an account, the cached tracked list, what gets refetched on `409` and on other errors, and the account-repositories key under `['accounts']`.
- The account picker: auto-selection, several accounts, `?account_id=` kept and ignored, provider labels, unlisted providers, no accounts, `needs_relink`, and a failed load.
- The list: tracked rows, the filter with no request, the empty list, the install link, and each list failure (`app_not_installed` with and without a URL, `forbidden`, `429` with retry, others).
- Tracking: the request, the message, focus, the response's `full_name`, the disabled buttons, dismissal and replacement, and each failure.
- The public form: the parser's accepted and refused inputs, Enter, validation and its accessible description, `404`, `429`, and how the form and the list disable each other.

Not run in a browser yet. To check by hand (PRD → Risks):
- An account with a few hundred repositories, to see the list render and filter smoothly.
- The anonymous rate limit on the public form (#99).

- **Scheda persona** (RF-P3): saldo in evidenza e **storico con saldo progressivo**, dal più recente (`Ledger.timeline`, pura e testata). Toccando una voce si apre il movimento nel wizard oppure il rimborso (RF-P8).
- **Rimborsi** (RF-P4, RF-P7): «Registra rimborso» oppure «Ho restituito» se il saldo è negativo. L'importo proposto è il saldo intero, con le scorciatoie Tutto e Metà. Se il rimborso supera il saldo compare un avviso, ma si può salvare. Data, nota ed evento facoltativo (il campo evento appare solo se esistono eventi). Modifica ed eliminazione con conferma.

## Why

A fixed contract that moves the sender's money but is reached only from inside another, such as Uniswap's PoolManager, came up only at `pnpm report --render`, one result per run, and a review was enough to pass it.

## What changed

- `pnpm past-txs` (with `--record` and `--restudy` too) prints at once every address in the traces that moves the sender's money and whose code `verify` does not check: outside the registry, or registered but not reached through `dependsOn`. Each line gives the call, token, direction, count and an example hash. What `verify` checks is judged per trace, by the entries that transaction's own calls name. The run always says "nothing found over N traced, M not counted".
- `pnpm report --record` refuses, before any live read, while one is neither registered in `dependsOn` nor judged in `trace-addresses.json` beside the report (`not-fixed`, or `known-limit` with the change it needs; both with a reason and sources). It also refuses a judgement of an address no recorded trace names, and, for a template that moves money, a study with no counted trace unless the file says why (`"untraced": { "reason" }`). A template whose effects change no balance or allowance needs none.
- `pnpm test` parses every committed `trace-addresses.json` strictly. Its text follows `notes.json`'s rules, capped at 600 characters. URLs in both files may hold no user name or password.
- Where the card chooses among tokens on both sides, it also prints how many traced transactions moved each token on each side, so a one-direction sample shows.

## Scope

- Reuses `compareFlow` unchanged, so no recorded summary needs a new study.
- The rule applies at the next `--record`. `--render` and `--offline` do not read the new file, so main stays green with no judgement written. Making `--render` refuse is a documented follow-up, once every report is recorded again.
- No template, registry or verdict core change. The skill and `scripts/report.ts` are gate files, so the signer merges this.
- Left out: the judgement is on no page (the words of the report are verdict core), and a pool a bound call pays directly, an unregistered minter, `DELEGATECALL` code, and ETH sent by `CREATE` or `SELFDESTRUCT` are not named (Known limits). The JSON parser does not see a duplicate key, as elsewhere in this repo.

## Blast Radius

The research commands only. The next `--record` of `uniswap/swap` and `uniswap/swap-no-hook` is refused until PoolManager and `permit2` are settled. The Fluid deposits (0 traced, 97 and 154 not counted) and `eth/transfer` (no study) need traces or an `untraced` reason first.

## Verification

- `node scripts/report.ts uniswap/swap --record` refuses and names PoolManager and `permit2` at once; `cow/swap` passes the check.
- `past-txs --restudy uniswap-swap-usdt-v4` prints the same list and shows that only USDT to USDC is traced.
- A scan of every summary on main still names only those two addresses. Each guard was removed in turn (24 mutations); each made a test fail, after two added cases. `pnpm test` (1,516 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` pass.

body:
Add explicit synthetic protective-stop and liquidation policies to the offline USD50 paper model. Stops are frozen and established before logical opening, trigger on long Bid/short Ask, and fill only from causally eligible authenticated source rows under declared latency. Margin warning restricts new entries; stop-out is a separate pending liquidation. Missing/conflicting exits remain unresolved; negative balances and historical drawdown are retained.

Stacked on draft #49 at `e18f6c7c61b3caebef45085a74b2aa93ba7caded`, targeting `feat/iat-v3-paper-capital-v1`. All previous PRs remain unmerged. Session Engine work is untouched.

### Independent automated E4 review

This is adversarial technical review, not independent human approval. Defects reproduced before correction, in separate commits:

- HIGH E46-01: specifications effective after the original decision could authorize earlier modeled fills. Require effectivity at the decision as well as processing time.
- MEDIUM E46-02: delayed processing charged realized loss to the wrong UTC day. Use modeled fill date.
- HIGH E46-03: matching feed/dataset labels could conceal replaced source history. Authenticate the complete previously consumed producer prefix transactionally, excluding future rows.

No unresolved HIGH/CRITICAL finding from this review. External review remains pending. Ordinary v1 journal goldens are unchanged; corrected invalid inputs are intentionally rejected.

### Contracts and limits

- Explicit v1 synthetic structural-reference mapping; unknown E3 OHLC basis stays unknown. Exact tick/minimum-distance/geometry/source/specification validation; no stop tightening, upward volume rounding or risk escalation.
- Separate v2 account/journal, immutable prefix, source/policy/config hashes, resource rollback and cutoff reviews. E2 closed-bar predicates and existing capital thresholds are unchanged.
- Net-liquidation equity / frozen entry margin ×100, explicit zero margin, warning recovery and negative/exhausted accounts. Stop/liq share one fill only when their coincident policies imply exactly the same result; other conflicts remain unresolved.
- One source quote per receipt, existing freshness/gap/analysis-age checks unchanged. No generic cross-model reconciliation, live bridge, TP2/3, partial/trailing/timer exit or new strategy.
- Dashboard availability text only; no synthetic values mixed with live observations.

### Actual local verification

- Full Python3.11.9: **2,010 pass**,791.378s.
- Full Python3.12.14: **2,010 pass**,667.692s.
- 13 independent-review cases pass; v1 golden plus review:14 pass.
- Protection/scenario focus:46 pass on3.11.9 (53.101s) and3.12.14 (46.882s).
- Live view focus:36 pass. Provenance metadata hashes pass unchanged.
- PR CI matrix: **all four jobs successful**, no failures or skips in full discovery. [Verified run](https://github.com/gkraman9/Trading-ai/actions/runs/45582379350).

| Linux Python 3.11.9 |2,010 pass|46 pass|744.892s|

### Reproducible synthetic examples and benchmark

A–N cover normal/gap/delay/missing stop fills, warning/stop-out, conflicting exits, negative/exhausted account, minimum-lot rejection, repeated losses, recovery and missing intervals. Two complete14-case outputs are identical, canonical report hash `4db1653c4de538e7c98944feb5a8c5defc1287f971606861c5c9377861955a44`. Compact report: `config/examples/protection-v1.synthetic.json`.

Normal toy stop leaves USD49.5044; adverse gap USD47.9; coincident catastrophic stop/liquidation leaves USD-181.021, one fill/expense, two roles. Recovery retains drawdown. The isolated requested3500.15/3499.65/3498.90 arithmetic gives USD0.50 estimated price risk versus USD1.25 gross loss before costs. None is actual market data or profitability evidence.

14-case construction took18.044s/17.889s; prebuilt open0.0300s; stop settlement under allocation tracing0.0668s,555,542 traced peak bytes,25,806-byte journal;1,000 margin calculations0.0182s. These are descriptive Linux workspace measurements, not production guarantees.

body:
## Le puits éclairé sans à-coup (lot 47c, 1.56.0)

**Empilée sur #85** (`feat/regard-finitions`, elle-même sur #81) : tant qu'elles ne sont pas
fusionnées, ce diff contient leurs commits. À fusionner après elles. La tête de #85 (d403f2f, la
fabrique à trois temps venue de `dev`) est fusionnée ici.

Le but validé par l'utilisateur : le pire dessin du puits éclairé sous 16 ms (processeur ÷ 4,
390 × 844 à 3, et ÷ 6, 360 × 740 à 2), à chaque palier. Les règles et l'image ne changent pas.
**Atteint : 8,7 ms au plus.**

### Les vraies causes (mesurées image par image, avant tout code)

Le lot était demandé comme « la foudre et les éclats calculés par le GPU ». Chronométrée dans la
page, la frappe se compose en 1 à 2 ms, la casse en moins d'une ms : rien à gagner là. Les pires
images venaient de deux coûts de premier usage :

- **les images d'un mot** : le premier dessin d'une toile neuve (20 à 35 ms pour l'ancienne image
  avec halo, encore 5 à 10 ms pour trois toiles serrées), le contour surtout. Le coût revient à
  chaque toile neuve : préparer les seuls glyphes (premier essai de ce lot) ne l'enlevait pas ;
- **la première frappe d'une partie** : la cible du tampon de lumière, l'envoi des réservoirs
  d'éclats et d'éclairs, la vérification des programmes (13 à 30 ms ; 11 ms dans la Tour).

### Les corrections

- `WordPictures` (nouveau) : dès que la scène connaît sa palette et sa taille, les 19 grands mots
  qu'un effacement peut montrer (`FallingEffects.wordSamples` : RIFT!, DEEP RIFT!, ×2, ×3, combo
  jusqu'à ×12 et leurs cris, à la taille des effets calmes aussi) sont dessinés **un mot par
  tâche** (`scheduler.postTask`, sinon un délai nul), tramés tout de suite sur une toile de 1 × 1,
  puis gardés. Au ÷ 6, les 19 mots sont prêts en 0,3 s. `WellOverlay` ne fait plus que dessiner.
- **Partagés par scène** (`setWordPictures`) : le puits 2D et le calque du puits éclairé, la Tour
  2D et éclairée, tout le carrousel de l'accueil. Une autre palette ou une autre taille les refait ;
  une scène quittée arrête (`stop`). Un mot non préparé est fait à son image, comme avant.
- `LookRenderer.warm()`, `BoltLightPass.warm()`, `LitTowerPainter.warm()`, `TowerStrike.warm()` :
  chaque programme et réservoir sert une fois à la création, sans rien dessiner.
- Tests : `tests/falling/wellOverlay.test.ts` (9, dont 5 pour les mots faits d'avance, le partage,
  la palette changée et l'arrêt) ; `tests/falling/weight.test.ts` : chaque grand mot des scènes
  du ressenti est dans `wordSamples`, effets pleins et calmes (vu échouer en cassant la taille
  calme).

### Mesures (au calme, deux tours alternés, `npm run frame-time`)

Avant : #85 (b5b11de, même code de jeu que d403f2f). Moyenne / 95e centile / pire, en ms, sur les
cinq prises du puits ou les deux de la Tour. « Dessin » : le `render()` des peintres ; « image » :
le pas entier, avec l'IA qui joue.

| Palier                    | Dessin avant      | Dessin après      | Image avant        | Image après        |
| ------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ------------------ | ------------------ |
| Élevée, ÷ 4               | 0,76 / 1,9 / 28,7 | 0,71 / 3,2 / **8,7** | 0,92 / 2,8 / 29,1  | 0,88 / 4,1 / 12,5  |
| Moyenne, ÷ 4              | 0,71 / 1,7 / 27,6 | 0,61 / 1,9 / **5,0** | 0,87 / 2,7 / 28,0  | 0,78 / 2,5 / 13,6  |
| Basse, ÷ 4                | 0,77 / 2,3 / 30,0 | 0,62 / 2,0 / **4,9** | 0,93 / 3,4 / 30,4  | 0,79 / 2,7 / 11,2  |
| Basse, ÷ 6, 360 × 740 à 2 | 1,40 / 4,1 / 44,4 | 1,56 / 5,0 / **7,5** | 1,70 / 6,1 / 45,4  | 1,94 / 5,6 / 46,1  |
| Classique 2D, ÷ 4         | 0,63 / 2,1 / 68,0 | 0,59 / 2,7 / 80,0 | 0,77 / 3,6 / 68,0  | 0,75 / 3,4 / 82,7  |
| Tour, Élevée, ÷ 4         | 0,76 / 1,9 / 9,4  | 0,75 / 1,9 / 4,7  | 1,40 / 8,9 / 30,8  | 1,39 / 8,1 / 57,5  |
| Tour, Basse, ÷ 6          | 1,55 / 3,6 / 15,0 | 1,42 / 3,3 / 11,8 | 2,67 / 18,9 / 50,1 | 2,49 / 14,1 / 50,9 |

- Les pires images entières sont celles de l'IA qui décide un coup, pas du dessin.
- **Classique 2D** : une image de combo de 65 à 80 ms, avant comme après. C'est un `drawImage`
  d'un bloc déjà dessiné (`CrystalSprites`, 70 × 70) qui bloque environ 50 ms, sans lien avec les
  mots (ses FAILLES passent de 11–20 ms à 3–5 ms). Laissé à un autre lot.
- Mémoire des mots : 15 Mo de toiles à 390 × 844 à 3, 12 Mo à 360 × 740 à 2, une fois par scène.
  Serrer les boîtes à l'encre mesurée la diviserait par deux environ (autre lot).

### Images

34 images (combo, FAILLE, FAILLE PROFONDE, Tour ; 320 × 568 et 390 × 844), éclairé et Classique 2D,
comparées à #85 : écart moyen 0,07 / 255 et 0,14 % des pixels à plus de 8 niveaux (éclairé), pour
un bruit de 0,04 et 0,12 % entre deux passages de #85 (Classique : 0,06 et 0,13 %). Les pixels qui
bougent sont des étincelles, l'aperçu des pièces (animé en temps réel) et les pulsations de la Tour
2D (`performance.now`, même écart après contre après) : jamais un mot.

### Vérifié

- `npm run lint`, `format:check`, `typecheck`, `npm test` (126 fichiers, 1 490 tests), le rejeu et
  la garde des règles exactes (`golden.ts` inchangé), `npm run build` et `budget`.
- e2e éclairés (`litWell`, `litSand`, `litTower`, mobile et bureau) : 14/14 dans Chrome, 14/14 dans
  WebKit. Balayage responsive : 10/10 (le projet bureau ; le mobile les saute par conception).
- Lighthouse mobile, trois passages : 100 / 100 / 100 / 100 à chaque passage.

author: scopsy
body:
### What changed? Why was the change needed? Linear: [NV-9591](https://linear.app/novu/issue/NV-9591/ssrf-guard-lets-00008-and-other-reserved-ipv4ipv6-ranges-through) A report said the outbound SSRF guard treats `0.0.0.0/8` as public, so loopback is reachable through `0.0.0.1` on every guarded surface. The classification part is true. `private-ip-classification.ts` blocked only the single address `0.0.0.0`, so these all passed `assertSafeOutboundUrl`: - `http://0.0.0.1/` - `http://1/` (the URL parser turns it into `0.0.0.1`) - `http://0.1.2.3/` - `http://[::ffff:0.0.0.1]/` A DNS A record pointing at `0.x.x.x` passed as well. The loopback part did not reproduce. A service listening on loopback could be reached through `0.0.0.0` (already blocked) but not through `0.0.0.1`. On macOS that failed with "host unreachable". On Linux 6.10 it failed with "connection refused" through the Docker bridge network and "network unreachable" with no route. Since kernel 5.3, Linux routes 0/8 addresses other than `0.0.0.0` like ordinary addresses, so they go to the default gateway, not to loopback. That makes this a hardening fix, not a fix for a working exploit. This PR blocks: - `0.0.0.0/8` (previously only `0.0.0.0`) - `192.0.0.0/24`: IETF protocol assignments - `198.18.0.0/15`: benchmarking - `224.0.0.0/4`: multicast - `240.0.0.0/4`: reserved, includes `255.255.255.255` - `ff00::/8`: IPv6 multicast IPv4-mapped, NAT64 and 6to4 forms of these addresses are caught by the existing check, with no new code. Every caller of `isPrivateIp` gets the wider list: - the safe outbound HTTP client (webhooks, bridge, the HTTP request step, chat webhooks) - the SMTP target check - MCP OAuth discovery - file downloads for agent replies - client-IP detection in inbound mail ### How was this verified? - New spec cases check both edges of each range, the IPv6 forms, and a URL-level test for `http://1/`, `http://0.0.0.1/`, `http://0.1.2.3:8080/` and `http://[::ffff:0.0.0.1]/`. - The `@novu/shared` vitest suite passes: 451 passed, 8 skipped. - I searched the other specs and e2e tests for addresses in the newly blocked ranges. The only hit is a `CF-Connecting-IP` header in the human e2e test, which never goes through the classifier.
Expand for optional sections ### Special notes for your reviewer - **Compatibility:** proxy tools that use fake-IP DNS (Clash, Surge) and some corporate VPNs answer every lookup with an address in `198.18.0.0/15`. A self-hosted or local Novu behind one of these would now have outbound calls blocked. It can be unblocked by adding the hosts or that range to `NOVU_SAFE_OUTBOUND_ALLOW`. Novu Cloud is not affected. - **Sensitive spots:** this changes the outbound SSRF policy. It does not touch tenant isolation, secrets, endpoints, the hot path or edition gating. `isPrivateIp` is an in-memory `BlockList` lookup with no I/O.

Expands `isPrivateIp` to block additional special-purpose addresses: - Novu blocks more special-use IP addresses across its guarded paths. Adds range checks, IPv6 examples, and URL shorthand tests. No actionable issues were found. Tests were not run during this review. `scopsy` explicitly intends to block the listed ranges and acknowledges fake-IP DNS and VPN compatibility changes. The PR description gives `NOVU_SAFE_OUTBOUND_ALLOW` as the workaround. author: danielrispler
body:
Spec #477, parts A (Reader clarity) and B (Since you read). Part C (link evidence, #498, #499) waits on #475 and is not here, so this PR does not close the spec.

Closes #489
Closes #490
Closes #491
Closes #492
Closes #493
Closes #494
Closes #495
Closes #496
Closes #497

## Summary

What a brief's reader gains:

```diff
 <brief panel>                          ui/map-brief.ts buildPanel
+  Partial facts · N   (chip)            #491, from stored partial_facts
+  Main moved since this PR's base: …    #494, open PRs only, computed on open
+  Since you read <H1> · Full brief      #497
   <step>
+    not-confirmed mark → popover        #491, Esc closes it before the brief
+    copy icon (Could break, popover)    #493, prompt written by code, 4th toast
+    See the code (this step's parts)    #490, filtered before the 80-file cap
   <last step>
-    Also touched: model's lines
+    Also touched by kind, by code       #489 store, #492 reader
+      No part · Tests · Config/build · Docs · Ignored · Other
 <part sheet>
+  why it's fogged / stale / broken     #495, fog entries gain pr + why
```

What a new head H2 does after a read at H1 (`server/src/pr_briefs.rs` `push_of`):

```text
on new head H2
  not fully read at H1            → full brief, "Rewritten after a new push; you had read N of M"
  H1 missing                      → full brief, "Rewritten: the branch was rebased"
  H1 ancestor of H2
    main's merge base unchanged
      H1..H2 fogs nothing         → carry the read, "New push touched nothing on your map"
      else                        → "Since you read" story (pr-briefs/since/), full brief one click away
    merge base moved (main merged in)
      PR's own patches and whole PR diff equal → carry, "Main merged into the branch, nothing new in the PR"
      else                        → full brief, "Rewritten: main was merged into the branch"
    diff can't be gathered        → full brief, "Rewritten after a new push"
  not an ancestor
    same multiset of patch-ids    → carry, copy the brief to H2, "Rebased onto main, nothing new in the PR"
    else                          → full brief, "Rewritten: the branch was rebased"
```

Carrying moves every chapter read from H1 to H2 and leaves `lit` alone (`fog::carry_read`), so fog at merge runs from H2.

### Decisions the spec left open (Daniel may overturn)

- **See the code filters by part, not path list** (#490). The page never holds the PR's paths, so `pr_diff` takes `parts`, placed by the map at the PR head (default branch's map when the head has none). #492 added `paths` for a group, the final review added `base` so a story's See the code shows H1..H2.
- **Also touched** (#489, #492): "lit" means parts in chapter steps' `on`; lockfiles are `*.lock`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `Gemfile`, `Pipfile`, `requirements.txt`, `bun.lockb`; each group lists its files, and a tagged test file shows its law on its row. No-part group's copy icon uses its paths.
- **Partial facts wording** (#491): "The diff was cut: 64 KiB sent, 20 KiB not", "The claim check failed: <error>" (also for didn't run), "No extractor reads .py files, so their imports are not on the map".
- **Stale base** (#494): also names flows and "paths of <part>"; 3 names per kind then "+N more"; `main` as last fetched (opening a brief doesn't fetch).
- **Marks** (#495): fog line like "Thick fog from #418: paths, 2 files" then "+N more"; dates UTC `YYYY-MM-DD`; the staleness line moved to the sheet's top (plate hover and pre-flight keep the old wording); CI date is the run's `updatedAt`.
- **Copy** (#493): a lit part's changed paths are fetched through `pr_diff(parts)` when a copy-icon step draws; a failed fetch gives a prompt without files. A manual-fallback toast stays until ×.
- **Leave button** gets the panel's background (#490 fix): a taller step scrolls, and the scrollbar thumb under Leave failed contrast (1.47). It hides the thumb's top few pixels.
- **Known limits:** the tray's push note and the push verdict live in memory, so a restart drops the note (the carried read and copied brief stay on disk); which story chapters were read is page memory, so a reload restarts that count.

## Evidence

Screenshots (snap, headless Chrome, stubbed API) are on Daniel's machine in `local-evidence/2026-11-25-spec-477/screenshots/`: `490-mapBriefStepCode`, `491-mapBriefPartialFacts{,Open}`, `491-mapBriefWhy{,Esc,Decision}`, `492-mapBriefAlsoGroups`, `493-mapBriefCopied`, `493-mapBriefCopyByHand`, `494-stale-base-line`, `495-mapMarks{Thick,Thin,Stale,Broken}`, `496-tray-after-push`, `mapBriefSince`, and `review-fix-*` after the final review.

- **Before:** `mapBriefStory` failed after #490, `contrast: 1.47 < 4.5 on button.btn.quiet.brief-leave "Leave"`.
  **After:** passes, closest 5.03.
- **Before:** a merge commit that edits a PR file carried the read: `left: Merged, right: Rewrite(Some(MERGED))`.
  **After:** `merging_main_into_the_branch_is_judged_by_the_prs_own_commits_not_mains` passes; a plain merge still carries.
- Each Since-you-read row has a temp-repo test, plus a dropped commit, a missing H1, a partial read, fog at merge after a carry-over, and a read finished at H1 after the push was first judged.
- `npm run check` on `fad9a02c4`: Rust 1514/1514, node 608 passed, 0 failed.
- New frozen sample `pr-brief-v8` (`also_groups`); `v3`-`v7` still load (`@law: old-stored-files-load`).

## Correctness pass

Three reviewers on the whole branch (standards, spec, correctness), then a re-review of the fix commits. Fixed:
- a multi-chapter story could never be read to its end (the tray had one row);
- merging `main` into the branch was told as the PR's own push;
- See the code placed files by `main`'s map, so a part the PR adds had none;
- a push verdict made before the read finished, or during a git error, stayed cached;
- a gather error rewrote a read brief with no note;
- opening a PR in the since case didn't write the full brief;
- a story's See the code showed the whole PR diff;
- Also touched showed laws per group, not per file;
- `CONTEXT.md` still listed the dropped link-check input; Also touched, Since you read and Stale base added;
- three copies of the `pr_diff` arguments, now one helper;
- (re-review) a merge commit editing PR files carried the read;
- (re-review) a PR head without `system-map.json` lost See the code's files.

Rejected: a failed copy save after a carry was said to loop (it falls through to writing, `pr_briefs.rs:345-354`); `Shape.also` unused (the pre-flight reads it, `pre_flight.rs:170`). Left alone: `path_kind` vs `is_test` (the spec fixes the test rule; commented), splitting `pr_briefs.rs`, the manifest lists, SHA newtypes.

## Outside review

The review trial ran in place of the outside review, at Daniel's ask. Gemini quota at start: weekly 58%, 5h 12%.

- **medium:** review unavailable: the Gemini quota is used up (`agy`: "Individual quota reached… Resets in 2h5m").
- **subagents:** review unavailable: the Gemini quota is used up (same error, after it started four subagents).
- **high:** stopped by Daniel once the quota was gone; no result.

No findings, no `cost:` lines.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

New stored data is additive: fog entries' `pr`/`why`, `also_groups`, `pr-briefs/since/`. The old build ignores them, and drops `pr`/`why` if it rewrites `map-state.json`, which is harmless. A carried read moved to H2 stays moved after a rollback.

**Blast Radius:** briefs

The brief reader, the tray's Ready for review rows, the part sheet and `pr_diff`. Writing briefs no longer asks the model for `also` lines.

body:
## Summary
- Build a responsive Fex Practice teacher workspace with learner, submission and individual learning-progress views.
- Add a private student progress page at `/students/progress/` with module topics, individual completion, assessment history, teacher feedback and vocabulary review.
- Connect the five-module Retail learning path to the signed-in learner's saved module answers and progress.
- Add a Cloudflare Pages student progress API that verifies the student Access JWT and derives the learner ID server-side.
- Recalculate module quiz scores on the server rather than trusting client-supplied scores.
- Add spaced vocabulary review scheduling (Again, Difficult, Remembered, Very easy).
- Extend the protected teacher API to read per-learner progress and save teacher feedback against an active learner record.
- Add a D1 migration for learner identities, course enrolments, module progress, vocabulary items/reviews, assessment attempts and teacher feedback.
- Add regression tests and update the QA workflow to check both learner and teacher progress features.

## Privacy and security
- Student progress is scoped to the verified Access identity; client-supplied learner IDs/emails are not used to select records.
- The student API sits under the existing `/students/*` Access path.
- Teacher reads and feedback writes use the existing teacher JWT verification and protected teacher API.
- Written case-study drafts are not uploaded or stored in this first iteration; only the self-review completion flag is saved.
- Student pages are marked noindex and API responses are no-store.

## Infrastructure prerequisite
The repository does not currently contain a verified D1 binding. Before live persistent progress can work, create the Cloudflare D1 database, bind it as `FEX_DB` in the Pages project, and apply `migrations/0001_fex_learner_progress.sql`. Exact steps are documented in `docs/fex-practice-progress-backend.md`.

## Scope
- No Cloudflare database, binding, Access policy, production secret, live student record or production deployment has been created or changed by this PR.
- Draft PR for review; no merge or deployment is authorised.

## Latest QA correction
- Fixed module progress writes to calculate and validate the answer result on the server before saving; the client cannot supply its own score.

author: viet-wego
body:
## What

`FRANKY_REVIEW_FOOTER` accepts three literal placeholders so a review can show what produced it:

| Placeholder | Value |
|---|---|
| `{model}` | `FRANKY_MODEL`, else `default` |
| `{skill}` | the `--skill` name, else `review` |
| `{version}` | `v<n>` of the team plugin holding the skill (team `MANIFEST.json`: `skills[].plugin`, `installed.<plugin>.version`); empty if unknown |

- Plain `str.replace`; no other `{...}` is read.
- Each value keeps only `[A-Za-z0-9._:/@+-]`, max 80 chars, else dropped. `{version}` must match `\d+(\.\d+)*`.
- An empty value drops its separator (` · `, spaces) at the middle and both edges.
- The 500-char cap is checked on the raw value at start and again after substitution (config error before the container starts).
- The footer is computed once per run and passed to the skill and plain review paths. The ledger swap's `body.endswith(footer)` uses the same string, so it is unaffected. Nothing else parses the footer.

## Detection

No new capability field. A caller gates on Franky >= 0.4.8 (the next patch release, which carries this change). The version is not bumped here; `make release` does that.

## Verification

- New tests: substitution, sanitizing, unknown values, edge collapse, length cap, passthrough, and an end-to-end skill review with a manifest.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, private-terms: clean. Full suite: the same 36 failures as `main` (stale package metadata locally), none new. mypy is not installed locally.
- Docs: `docs/review.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Impl review: one Codex diff pass; both minor findings accepted and fixed.

Resource effect: none (string handling only; no image, RAM or CPU change; no effect on 2 or 4 concurrent jobs).

## 🚀 Rollout

1. Merge this PR, then release Franky (`make release`, 0.4.8).
2. Then merge the downstream PR that sends the placeholders, gated on Franky >= 0.4.8.

author: redrick
body:
margin-gui froze (no clicks, no scrolling) while the agent was writing output and the machine was busy.

**Cause:** every Wails event runs JS on the GTK UI thread, and Wails v3 keeps draining its event queue until it's empty. We emitted one `agent:data` event per PTY read, so a busy agent kept the queue full faster than the UI thread could empty it.

**Fix:** batch agent output and send it at most every 33ms. The first output after a pause still goes out immediately, so typing echoes right away. Reading from the agent pauses while 1 MiB is waiting to be sent, so memory stays bounded.

**Tests:** new `coalesce` tests cover batching, immediate first output and reading pausing; they pass under `-race`. The full suite passes.

author: possn
body:
## Dados e problema
A última publicação disponível do scanner continua a ser a de 24/11/2026 22:50 UTC, anterior à integração do PR #2048 às 00:30 UTC de 25/11; logo, **a melhoria de cobertura observada ainda não pode ser confirmada**. Aquele relatório tinha 1.311/1.616 séries verificadas nas 24 horas (81,13%), com apenas 347/400 séries avaliáveis no último slot.

A auditoria ao cálculo introduzido pelo #2048 encontrou dois erros concretos para universos acima do limite adaptativo:
1. `daily_coverage_capacity(1950)` dizia erradamente 100% porque contava as 25 ações da watchlist repetidas nos quatro ciclos como quatro conjuntos de nomes distintos; o limite de 500 pedidos/slot torna a capacidade ideal com 25 rechecks de apenas **1.925/1.950 = 98,72%**.
2. A seleção adaptativa rodava o universo inteiro, mas retirava a watchlist **depois** do offset; em 1.950 ações, 25 watchlist e quatro slots, isto cria sobreposições adicionais, levando a apenas 1.900 nomes no plano, em vez dos 1.925 possíveis.

## Correção operacional
- A contabilidade de capacidade distingue 25 rechecks reservados por slot dos nomes realmente distintos e marca explicitamente `planning_capacity_not_verified_ohlcv=true`, sem afirmar dados observados.
- O plano **adaptativo** roda agora diretamente sobre os tickers não pertencentes à watchlist e aplica um stride igual ao número de posições úteis do slot. Sem repetições evitáveis e sem exceder os 500 pedidos por execução.
- A seleção antiga de ≤1.600 ações permanece idêntica.
- Testes de regressão incluem universos de 1.616 e 1.950 ações, com e sem watchlist, quatro ciclos completos, contagens planeadas e limites de capacidade. Nenhum gate MA/VCP/swing, score, recomendação ou preço é alterado.

Este PR corrige capacidade e agendamento determinístico, **não comprova** cobertura OHLCV real, eficácia preditiva nem viabilidade de 100% para universos acima do limite técnico. Refs #1718 #2048.

Merge somente com Runtime JS, Unit Python completa, Architecture invariants, WebKit iPhone 1/2 aprovados no mesmo SHA, `behind=0`, `mergeable=true` e `expected_head_sha`.

author: juhy0987
body:
## 연관 이슈

Closes #644

## 구현 내용

> 요약: 프록시에 upstream (키) 이 없는 모델 provider 를 쓰는 에이전트가 배포 검증을 통과하고 첫 모델 호출에서야 404 로 드러났다 → 배포가 컨테이너를 띄우기 전에 프록시에 실제 중계 목록을 묻고, 없는 provider 를 쓰는 배포를 거절한다.

### 발생했던 문제

배포 검증은 설정 파일의 `runtime.egress_proxy.providers` 목록과만 대조했다. 프록시가 실제로 중계하는 provider 는 프록시의 키 env 로 정해지므로, 설정에 이름만 적고 키를 빠뜨리면 배포는 통과하고 에이전트는 healthy 로 뜬 뒤 첫 모델 호출에서 프록시가 `404 unknown provider` 를 냈다.

<details><summary>자세히</summary>

- 재현 (main `b1ada17`): 설정 `providers={anthropic, openai-compat}`, 프록시 키는 anthropic 만 → `openai-compat` 에이전트의 배포 검증 통과, 프록시는 `openai-compat` 에 404.
- 프록시는 중계 목록을 밖에 알리는 엔드포인트가 없었고, control plane 은 프록시에 HTTP 로 닿은 적이 없다 (에이전트 env 에 URL 을 주입할 뿐). 프록시 주소 `providers_url` 은 에이전트 내부 네트워크 alias 라 호스트에서 도는 control plane 은 풀지 못한다.

</details>

### 해결 방법

- 프록시가 `GET /v1/providers` 로 실제 중계하는 provider 이름을 알린다 (무인증 — 이름뿐).
- 배포마다, **선언을 읽기 전에** 프록시에 묻고, 원래 검증 자리에서 배포가 쓰는 provider (manifest primary · fallback, 노드 · 배포 override) 와 대조한다 — 없으면 기동 전에 `VAL_002`. 선언 읽기부터 점유까지 기다림이 없어, 묻는 사이 바뀐 선언이 검사를 비켜 가지 않는다.
- 프록시에 닿지 않으면 배포를 거절한다 (설정 목록으로 물러나지 않는다): 연결 실패 · 5xx 는 재시도 가능 `NET_001`, 총 마감 5초 초과 `NET_002`, 4xx · 모양 불일치 · 압축 응답 · 64 KiB 초과는 재시도 불가 `NET_001`.
- 새 선택 설정 `runtime.egress_proxy.control_url` — control plane 이 보는 프록시 주소. 비우면 `providers_url`. 에이전트 env 에는 싣지 않는다.

<details><summary>자세히</summary>

- `egress/providers.py`: `PROVIDERS_PATH` 라우트, catch-all `/{provider}/{path}` 보다 먼저.
- `runtime/deployments.py`: `_relayed_providers` (조회, `deploy()` 맨 앞) · `_check_proxy_upstreams` (동기 대조) · `_read_proxy_answer` (`accept-encoding: identity`, 압축 응답은 읽기 전에 거절, `aiter_raw` 로 받은 바이트 그대로 상한, `asyncio.timeout` 총 마감, 깊은 중첩 JSON 의 `RecursionError` 도 모양 불일치).
- `config.py` · `orchestrator/__main__.py`: `control_url` 과 배선.
- e2e (`test_egress` · `test_openai_compat`): 프록시 8081 을 호스트 loopback 18095 로 publish, `control_url` 로 설정 (control plane 이 호스트 프로세스).
- docs/en · docs/ko `api.md`, 규약 01 Contract Validation 10 · 03 Egress.
- 동작 변화: 프록시를 쓰는 설정에서 프록시가 닿지 않으면, 없는 그래프의 배포도 `NF_001` 이 아니라 `NET_*` 로 거절된다 (조회가 선언 읽기보다 먼저).

</details>

### 작업 분배

| 하위 작업 | 역할 | 티어 | 왕복 | 검수 결과 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 착수 전 검증 — 재현 · 경로 조사 | researcher | T2 (sonnet) | 0 | 재현 출력 원문 대조, 핵심 코드 위치 메인이 확인 |
| 구현 · 테스트 · 문서 | coder | T1 (opus) | 4 | ① 사용자 결정 반영 (`control_url` 추가 — e2e 가 control plane 에서 프록시에 닿지 못하는 문제) ② qa 지적 (선언 경쟁 · 응답 상한 · 압축 분류) ③ 압축 응답이 상한 전에 풀리는 문제 ④ 깊은 중첩 JSON / 별도로 `make check` 의 필드 커버리지 계약 실패 (퍼즈 문서 누락) 수정 |
| 독립 리뷰 | qa (Codex) | T1 | 1 | 1차 major 2 · minor 1 → 반영 / 재검 해소, 남은 minor 1 (깊은 중첩) 반영 |

### 핵심 결정

- **배포 검증이 프록시에 실제 목록을 묻는다** (사용자) — 버린 안: 에이전트 health 의 모델 컴포넌트가 상태를 보인다 (첫 태스크 전에 드러나지만 배포는 성공한다).
- **배포마다, 선언을 읽기 전에 묻는다** (AI 자율) — 버린 안: control plane 기동 때 한 번 (프록시 키는 재시작 없이 바뀐다) / 점유 직전에 묻기 (기다리는 사이 바뀐 선언이 검사를 비켜 간다 — qa 지적).
- **프록시에 닿지 않으면 거절** (AI 자율) — 버린 안: 설정 목록으로 물러난다 (이 이슈의 조용한 실패가 남는다).
- **질의 주소는 새 선택 키 `control_url`, 없으면 `providers_url`** (사용자) — 버린 안: 비우면 검사를 건너뜀 (설정하기 전까지 결함이 남는다) / 프록시 컨테이너 inspect 로 키 존재 확인 (control plane 이 API 키 값을 다루게 된다).
- **엔드포인트는 무인증** (AI 자율) — 버린 안: 인증 (돌려주는 것이 provider 이름뿐이고 비밀이 없다).

<details><summary>ADR — 배포 시점의 프록시 provider 확인</summary>

### 맥락
프록시가 중계하는 provider 는 키 env 로 정해지는데 배포 검증은 설정 목록만 봤다. 빠진 provider 는 첫 모델 호출에서 404 로만 드러났다.

### 결정
1. 프록시가 `GET /v1/providers` 로 중계 목록을 알린다.
2. 배포마다 선언을 읽기 전에 묻고, 배포가 쓰는 provider 가 없으면 기동 전에 `VAL_002`.
3. 프록시에 닿지 않으면 거절 (`NET_001` / `NET_002`).
4. 질의 주소는 `runtime.egress_proxy.control_url`, 없으면 `providers_url`.

### 근거
이슈의 완료 조건 (첫 태스크 전에 드러난다) 과 사용자 결정 (#644 코멘트). 실패 시 거절은 레지스트리 판정의 "판정할 수 없으면 거부" 와 같은 결 (01 Access Control). control plane 은 보통 호스트에서 돌아 에이전트 네트워크 alias 를 풀지 못하므로 별도 주소가 필요했다.

### 검토한 대안
- 에이전트 health 에 표시 — 배포가 성공해 버린다.
- 기동 때 한 번 조회 — 프록시 키 변경을 놓친다.
- 프록시 불통 시 설정 목록으로 물러남 — 원래 결함이 남는다.
- `control_url` 미설정 시 검사 생략 — 운영자가 켜기 전까지 결함이 남는다.
- 프록시 컨테이너 inspect — control plane 이 API 키 값을 다룬다.

### 결과·영향
프록시를 쓰는 배포는 프록시가 떠 있어야 성공한다. control plane 이 호스트에 있으면 `control_url` 을 설정하고 프록시 provider 포트를 그 주소로 열어야 한다 (e2e 는 loopback publish). 프록시가 늦게 뜨는 동안의 배포는 재시도 가능 에러로 거절된다.

### 되돌리기
커밋 revert. 설정 키 `control_url` 은 선택이라 남은 설정 파일은 revert 뒤 모르는 키로 거절된다 — 그 줄을 지운다.

</details>

<details><summary>검증 결과</summary>

- `make check`: 6696 passed, coverage 95.71%
- `pytest tests/integration/runtime -m integration`: 67 passed (9:16)
- e2e (`test_egress` · `test_openai_compat`): 수집만 확인 (5 tests) — nightly 에서 실행된다
- 뮤테이션 (사본 → 복원 → cmp): 조회를 점유 직전 await 로 되돌림 / 노드 override 대상 제거 / 배포 검사 호출 제거 / 라우트를 catch-all 뒤로 / encoding 검사 제거 / 상한 검사 제거 / `RecursionError` 처리 제거 → 각각 해당 테스트 실패. 총 마감 제거는 실패가 아니라 테스트가 멈추는 것으로 드러남. `aiter_raw` → `aiter_bytes` 단독은 encoding 검사를 지난 응답에서 같은 바이트라 구별 불가 (이중 방어).

</details>

## CI / 머지 게이트 점검

- [x] Lint
- [x] Type Check
- [x] Test (커버리지 ≥ 70%)
- [x] Integration Test
- [x] Commit Lint (`[카테고리]: 한국어 요약`)
- [x] PR Title Lint (`[카테고리#이슈번호] 제목`)
- [x] Linked Issue Check (closing reference)
- [x] Docs Sync Check (docs/en ↔ docs/ko 동기화)
- [ ] Review Presence (정보성)

## 변경 영향 범위 + 위험도

- 영향 범위: runtime (deployments), egress (providers), config, orchestrator 배선, e2e 하니스, docs, 규약 01 · 03
- 위험도: 중간 — 프록시를 쓰는 배포는 이제 프록시에 닿아야 성공한다. control plane 이 에이전트 네트워크 밖에 있는 배치는 `control_url` 설정이 필요하다 (없으면 배포가 `NET_001` 로 거절된다). e2e 의 변경은 nightly 에서 처음 실행된다.

## 롤백 계획

- 세 커밋 revert. 설정에 `control_url` 을 넣었다면 그 줄을 지운다. 데이터 · 스키마 변경 없음.

## Summary
Adds `GET /api/predictions/user/export`, an authenticated endpoint that streams the signed-in user's predictions as a CSV download.

## Changes
- New route in `src/routes/predictions.routes.ts` that returns `text/csv` with a dated `Content-Disposition` attachment filename.
- `PredictionService.streamUserPredictions` reads in keyset-paginated batches of 500 (newest first), so memory use stays flat for large histories.
- The stream waits on backpressure, stops when the client disconnects, and destroys the connection on a mid-stream error rather than returning a truncated file.
- New `src/utils/csv.util.ts` with RFC 4180 quoting and formula-injection guarding (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`; plain negative numbers untouched).
- Money columns use the existing 8-decimal string format.
- Registered in the route auth and parity registries; OpenAPI and Postman docs updated.

## Tests
- `csv.util.spec.ts`: quoting, dates, formula guarding, row format.
- `predictions-export.routes.spec.ts`: 401 without a token, headers, header-only output, row contents, user scoping, cursor paging, mid-stream DB failure.
- `tsc` is clean, and the OpenAPI and Postman sync checks pass.

## Notes
`route-parity`, `prediction.service` and `predictions.routes` have 5 tests that fail identically on a clean `main` and are unrelated to this change.

Closes #988

author: vursen
body:
Cleans up the pr-presentation skill: shorter instructions, fewer commands and less unused code, without changing its rules or its structure (chain, plan, reader, build).

## Changes

- `hunks.mjs plan` writes the reader's slide files when the plan has no problems. `hunks.mjs build` runs the whole build: `slides.json`, `build.mjs` and `check.mjs`. The `reader` and `slides` subcommands are removed. `check.mjs` exits 1 when a slide overflows.
- The coverage check (NOT SHOWN / PARTLY SHOWN) is removed. A slide line of only `...` matched every changed line, so the check passed on any deck with a skipped range. Once that was fixed, PARTLY SHOWN pushed the session to add changed lines that no fact of the chain needs, and NOT SHOWN repeats the plan's check that every code hunk is on a slide or omitted.
- SKILL.md: the checked limits are in one list. Review notes are defined in one place. Bullets that repeat the format examples are removed, and so are repeated sentences. Step 5 tells what to remove for a reader note.
- `references/slides-json.md` is removed: nothing read it, and it was out of date. The `omitted` field of `slides.json`, read only by the coverage check, is removed too.

## Testing

Two full local runs on web-components PR 13484, both successful:

| Run | Coverage check | Time | Turns | Cost | Slides |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | fixed, still in | 11.8 min | 98 | $3.84 | 12 |
| 2 | removed | 13.7 min | 97 | $4.08 | 13 |

In both runs the reader agents worked one slide at a time, the session stopped after two reader corrections, and the one-command build passed. In run 1, PARTLY SHOWN warnings caused about 12 extra turns. In run 2 the build passed on the first try. The final commit (no `omitted`, no `slides-json.md`) was checked by building run 2's work folder again.
