body:
Closes the P1 `work/ssiarith/main-red-a-tall-thin-cylinder-pairs-section-reads-limb-2-in-band-at-1e-12.md`.

## Finding: the refusal no longer happens on main

The row's tall thin pose is a radius 0.2 cylinder over z ∈ [−8, 8] passing through a radius 3 cylinder over [−1, 1] turned π/2 about y. I measured that pair alone on main `6003877ad8` (release build), with each op read through the row's own `differential::outcome`:

| ε | union | subtract | intersect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-12 | OK SOUND, pad 3.8e-12 | OK SOUND, pad 3.7e-12 | OK SOUND, pad 4.1e-12 |
| 1e-9 | OK SOUND, pad 1.7e-10 | OK SOUND, pad 1.2e-10 | OK SOUND, pad 1.7e-10 |
| 1e-6 | OK BAD, pad 5.8e-7 | OK BAD, pad 4.4e-7 | OK BAD, pad 5.8e-7 |

- **1e-12 and 1e-9:** the limb-2 `GermSectionUnbuilt` is gone, and every volume matches the closed form.
- **1e-6:** each enclosure is wider than the row's fixed pad budget. This is SPIRICARM's P1 class; I added the evidence to `work/spiricarm/main-red-three-cylinder-pair-volume-pads-pass-the-fixed-budget-at-1e-6.md`.

**The row as a whole had already moved past its pin.**
- The nightly of main `6a680cb845` (run 45332993102) was red at 1e-12 on an earlier pose: the skew pair's intersection, `Euler(DescriptionUncertified { … PeriodicView(Span { asked: … }) })`. That is SECTARMS' periodic-view class, already seen as `RebasedCarrier` at `b80352cd` (PR 7294's note on the row); I added the evidence to that row.
- On `6003877ad8` that stop is gone as well, and the whole row passes at 1e-12.

**Not bisected.** I did not name the merges that cleared the two stops. One hosted run of the row costs about 13 minutes, and the thing left to fix was the row's pin, not the kernel.

## Change (test and tracker only; no kernel code)

In `crates/sweep/tests/verbs_cylcyl_r1_review_probes.rs`:
- **The 1e-12 pin is removed**, so the row runs as written at 1e-12.
- **`"tall thin through short fat"` joins `answering`.** The row used to admit frontier refusals for this pose; it now holds the pose SOUND at the default ε and at 1e-12.
- **The 1e-6 pin is re-pinned on its new whole line.** On main the old digits had themselves moved: pad 6.7e-6 → 2.1e-6, and the volume is one digit off the old text. So the 1e-6 row was red on main before this branch. I first loosened the pin to the class; the review showed that a class pin would also accept a wrong volume, so it is the whole line again.

The issue file keeps its original body and closes in its own `## Closed` section. SPIRICARM's pinned line is updated to the new digits.

## Verified

- **Local, release, on this branch's merged head `37b5bc3373`:** the row at 1e-6 PASS (3 s), and at 1e-12 PASS (354 s). Before merging main in, on `6003877ad8`, the row also passed at 1e-9 (66 s).
- **Hosted gate, run 45594701363:**
  - The row passed at the default ε (slow-set step, 75 s). The gate's 1e-6/1e-12 step runs `--profile ci`, which skips the slow set, so the two pins had no hosted reading. That is CIW's `a-slow-rows-eps-pins-run-nowhere-on-the-pr-that-adds-them`; I added this PR as an instance.
  - The gate is red on one other test: `a_cylinder_wall_through_a_prism_corner_meshes_at_a_coarse_delta` at 1e-12 (`VolumeUncomputable`, `props_chart_junction_closed` margin 2.8e-12). That is main's own red, filed as TESSLIE's P1 `main-red-a-cylinder-wall-through-a-prism-corner-union-is-volume-uncomputable-at-1e-12` with the same margin. This PR changes no code it reaches.

## Review

A single STYLE review (Opus) plus four claims. Its verdict was mergeable after one MINOR, which I took (the whole-line 1e-6 pin), along with the SPIRICARM text, the restored item body, and naming the measurement base as a blind spot. The full disposition is in `work/ssiarith/log.md`.

body:
## Cause
Galaxus kids/toddler/Li-Ning lines never bought (349 attempts on Ugg Fluff alone, all parked as proxy_blank/size_grid).
- Kids products reject the US token (`?size=6Y`) and open the size picker.
- With the logged-in fr-fr/CHF session the picker reads "Sélectionnez du Size" ... "Annuler". `isSizeGridBody` only knew "Sélectionner la taille", so `resolveBuyPageSizeGrid` returned early, the empty-lane body was classified `proxy_blank`, and the pair was retried until parked. 394 dumps match this picker.
- In the EN guest/EUR session the tile price is `€111`; the EU tile regex only accepted CHF/Offer, so "EU 38 tile not clickable" (needs_review size_grid).
- ASICS Onitsuka line stayed `slug_unresolved`: Galaxus title has an extra brand word ("ASICS Onitsuka Tiger…") vs StockX "Onitsuka Tiger…".

## Fix
- `isSizeGridBody`: accept `Sélectionnez (du|la)? (Size|taille)`.
- `euSizeTilePattern` (pure, tested): EU tile with CHF prefix/suffix, €/$/£, EUR, or offer-only price; never matches a neighbour size. Used by the tile click.
- `galaxusTitleMatchesProductName`: allow up to 2 extra leading brand words (name must still match exactly and be unique).

## Not fixed
Li-Ning has no EU tab (US M tiles only) and no EU→US chart, so it now ends as a clear `size_grid` verdict instead of looping on proxy_blank.

body:
**Lỗi**: người dùng chỉ nghe được bài đầu tiên của mỗi playlist.

**Nguyên nhân**: khi một bài YouTube kết thúc, app hỏi `player.getPlaylist()` để biết còn bài nào không. Với Mix, YouTube thường trả danh sách rỗng, nên app hiểu là đã hết, ngay lập tức nạp lại link (cắt ngang việc YouTube đang tự chuyển bài tiếp). Kết quả là chỉ nghe lại bài đầu.

**Sửa**:
- Không dựa vào `getPlaylist()` để quyết định hết danh sách nữa.
- Với link là playlist / Mix: sau khi bài kết thúc, đợi 3 giây. Nếu YouTube tự chuyển sang bài mới (trạng thái đổi trong chưa đầy 1 giây) thì app không can thiệp. Nếu trình phát đứng yên ở trạng thái kết thúc thì mới chuyển sang link tiếp theo trong playlist của app.
- Video lẻ vẫn chuyển ngay khi hết bài. Bấm Dừng sẽ hủy việc chuyển bài đang chờ.
- Khi bài trong Mix bị chặn nhúng (lỗi 101/150) và YouTube không cho biết độ dài danh sách, app vẫn thử `nextVideo()` thay vì dừng.

**Kiểm tra** trên Chromium với YouTube IFrame API giả lập (`getPlaylist()` trả về rỗng, đúng như Mix):
| Tình huống | Bản cũ | Bản mới |
|---|---|---|
| Mix hết bài, YouTube tự phát bài tiếp | nạp lại link (sai) | không can thiệp |
| Mix hết thật, trình phát đứng yên | không chuyển link | sang link tiếp sau 3 giây |
| Video lẻ hết bài | sang link tiếp | sang link tiếp |
| Bấm Dừng khi đang chờ | vẫn tạo lại trình phát | không tạo lại |

Không có lỗi JS. Chưa thử với YouTube thật vì sandbox không truy cập được YouTube.

author: unurgunite
body:
## The report

```
com.intellij.psi.stubs.UpToDateStubIndexMismatch: PSI and index do not match.
Caused by: java.lang.AssertionError: Stub count (14) doesn't match stubbed node length (25)
  at CrystalMethodDefinitionImpl.getTypePath(CrystalMethodDefinitionImpl.java:62)
  at CrystalMethodLookup.getEnclosingClassName(CrystalMethodLookup.kt:170)
  at CrystalDotCallOverloads.ownedByReceiver(CrystalDotCallOverloads.kt:86)
  at CrystalTypeCheckInspection.resolveDotCallMethods(CrystalTypeCheckInspection.kt:141)
```

Triggered on `spec/support/fake_api_server.cr`, whose indexed stub tree held 14 stubbed nodes while the same text parses to 25.

## Two causes, both fixed

**1. Stale stub trees were never discarded (root cause).** `getStubVersion()` stayed at `4` after the 1.4.0 grammar rewrites — heredoc pairing, bare-call arguments, `record(` lexing. Those change where methods live inside a mis-parsed file, so an index built by an older build no longer matches the current parse. Bumped to `5`, which discards stale stub trees and rebuilds them with the current parser (same fix as the 1.1.0 `2 → 3` bump, and the rule already recorded in the changelog).

**2. The lookups had drifted from their own rule.** `getEnclosingClassName` was made stub-only in 1.2.1, then the `def Type.new` reopening fix put `method.typePath` back in front — and `getTypePath()` is a generated `PsiTreeUtil.getChildOfType` call that forces IntelliJ to build the AST of a stub-backed element. The method stub now carries `typePath`, `isStatic`, `parameterSignature` and `returnType`, written at index time:

| Lookup | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `getEnclosingClassName` | `typePath` off the AST | `stub.typePath ?: stub parent walk` |
| `getParameterSignature` | `parameterList` off the AST | `stub.parameterSignature` |
| `getReturnType` | `typeReference` off the AST | `stub.returnType` |
| `isStaticMethod` | `node.findChildByType(SELF)` | `stub.isStatic` |

Fixing only the reported frame would leave the inspection reproducible: `getInitializeMethods` calls `getParameterSignature` and `isStaticMethod` on the very same `StubIndex` hits, and both went through the AST. As a side effect a cross-file candidate (`.new` argument checks, project-method completion) no longer materializes the candidate's tree.

## Notes

- `gradle.properties` → `1.5.0` and `CHANGELOG.md` gets a `## [1.5.0]` section; CI requires both to match the `v1.5.0` base branch.
- `[1.4.0] — Unreleased` in the changelog dated to its tag (`v1.4.0`, 2026-11-19) so the file does not show two unreleased sections.
- Regression test: `CrystalMethodStubShapeTest` asks the stub index for the methods and checks the stubbed header facts, plus that `getEnclosingClassName` returns the header type for a top-level `def StubWidget.widget_reopen` and `null` for a plain top-level method.

## Checks

- `./gradlew test` — 1371 tests, 0 failures
- `./gradlew spotlessCheck` — clean
- `./gradlew detekt` fails locally with `Could not initialize class com.intellij.ide.plugins.PluginEnabler` on an unmodified `v1.5.0` worktree too, so it is an environment issue here and will be judged by CI.

author: samuelruizperez
body:
Adds ways to compare samples in the partition and RFD plots (`partition_or_rfd_plot.R`, `PARTITION_OR_RFD_PLOT`). So far samples could only be compared by eye from the mean profiles and their SD ribbons, which show how much initiation zones vary, not whether two samples differ.

- **Violin plots** of one value per initiation zone and sample ((downstream − upstream mean) / 2, since the values change sign across the zone), with paired tests between samples over the initiation zones: Wilcoxon signed-rank, or Newey-West with `--violin_test newey_west`.
- **Profile difference plots**: the mean paired difference of each pair along the distance axis, with a cluster-based permutation test of where the profiles differ.
- **Interquartile range** versions of the profile plots, next to the SD ones.
- **Window QC plots**: how many windows each sample loses (no reads, RPM cutoff, blacklist) and where.

Each plot comes with its tables. New options are set through `ext.args`; existing outputs are unchanged apart from the plot captions. The module environment now lists `r-sandwich` and `r-cowplot` (previously only indirect dependencies), with a rebuilt container.

`docs/output.md` gets a section describing all outputs of the module, with an example figure for each plot (mm39 SCAR-seq H3K27me3 and OK-seq). The section around it is renamed to "Partition, bias and replication fork directionality analysis".

Tested with a new `sample_comparisons.nf.test` (chr22 tables built as in `BAM_CREATE_PARTITIONS`, both tests) and the existing module tests, all passing on the new container with stable snapshots; also checked by hand on mm39 data. `nf-core pipelines lint`: 310 passed, 6 warnings (template TODO strings); `pre-commit` passed. The full pipeline test was not run, as the test profiles do not reach these plots.

## PR checklist

- [x] This comment contains a description of changes (with reason).
- [x] If you've fixed a bug or added code that should be tested, add tests!
- [x] Make sure your code lints (`nf-core pipelines lint`).

- [x] Output Documentation in `docs/output.md` is updated.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` is updated.

body:
Stacked on #157 (the zoom); its base is `viewer-zoom`, so the diff here is the material alone.

The viewer's left sidebar is now the system's material, as Finder's is. The folder's side, its toolbar, path bar and inspector stay opaque on the viewer's canvas.

## helder.os

- **`WindowBackdrop.Sidebar` (`backdrop="sidebar"`)**, by platform:
  - macOS: an NSVisualEffectView with the sidebar material (7). Its state follows the window's, so it dims while the window is inactive, as Finder's does.
  - Windows 11 22H2 on: Mica (`DWMSBT_MAINWINDOW`).
  - KDE: its blur, on Wayland and X11.
  - Elsewhere it reads `None`, as the other backdrops do.

  On macOS 26 Finder's sidebar is a floating Liquid Glass panel. This uses the sidebar material behind the whole window; a glass panel limited to the sidebar's rect is left for later.
- **`Settings.reducedTransparency`**, alongside `reducedMotion`:
  - macOS: `accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceTransparency`;
  - iOS: `UIAccessibilityIsReduceTransparencyEnabled`;
  - Windows: Personalization's Transparency effects (`EnableTransparency`);
  - false elsewhere (the web page's glue is left alone).

  TypeScript declarations regenerated.
- **Windows link fix.** `windows.Device`'s kernel32 functions are now declared as the rest of helder.os declares them: `GetModuleHandleW` fast, `GetProcAddress` not. Before, an app with a window that used `DeviceInfo` failed to lower on Windows.

## The viewer

- **Where it's asked for.** `Shell.material(os, version, desktop)` decides: macOS; Windows from build 22621; Linux when `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` has KDE. Not on Windows 10, GNOME, phones or the web.
- **The window.** It is made transparent with `backdrop="sidebar"`, and with `"none"` while Reduce Transparency is on. `clickThrough={false}`, so presses on the sidebar's empty space stay the window's.
- **Backgrounds.** The `window` view draws no canvas while the material shows (the window reads `Sidebar` back) and the width isn't a tablet's. The folder's side draws the canvas instead. The sidebar draws no background; its rows' hover and selection fills stay.
- **Where it doesn't take** (Windows 10, a desktop without it, reduced transparency): everything is opaque as before.
- **The full-size view** covers it opaque as before. The zoom's picture flies over the viewer, which fades in over the browser, sidebar included.

## Screenshots

macOS, a real window (HELDER_BACKGROUND=1, light appearance, the window inactive): the sidebar in Finder's material, its labels in the look's fg/fg2/fg3 and readable, the rest opaque. I can't attach images from here; it is in the session's scratchpad (`shot/macos.png`).

Not rendered:
- dark appearance: the system's setting, which I didn't change on your Mac;
- Windows: the cross build lowers, but linking needs the Windows runtime object this Mac doesn't have, and Wine/Docker is off-limits for heavy lanes. CI's Windows build covers the link.

## Tests

`apps/viewer/tests/viewer/Material.test.hx`:
- `Shell.material` across macOS, Windows 11 and 10, KDE, GNOME and others;
- with the material: the window and the sidebar clear; the folder's side, its panel, the inspector and the full view opaque;
- without it, and at a tablet's width: the canvas.

Lanes: viewer (101 pass), declarations, viewer-window (macOS).

Tester feedback (Vietnamese, verbatim topics):

| Feedback | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Tạo tk bị nhảy chữ | `Modal` re-ran its focus effect whenever `onClose` changed identity; pages pass an inline arrow, so **every keystroke** moved focus back to the first input (affected every dialog) | keep `onClose` in a ref; focus only on open. Reproduced on old code with per-key input (`xyz` landed in "Họ tên"), fixed on new code |
| TK trọng tài tạo ở Tài khoản không ghi nhận khi phân công | accounts created on `/accounts` belong to no tournament → absent from referee dropdowns, server rejects them | `POST /admin/users` accepts `refereeTournamentIds` (one transaction, logs `referee_create`); create dialog gets **Làm trọng tài giải**; dropdowns grouped Trọng tài / Ban tổ chức + hint when no referee |

| Thao tác admin load lại lâu | every action bumped a global `version` → reload tournament + whole match list + staff list; select snapped back meanwhile | `usePoll.mutate()`, `act(…, { local })`; optimistic referee assignment locking only its row; courts actions refresh only the board |
| Tìm kiếm (khách) | search showed the person's schedule inside the search box and the whole-tournament schedule below | two steps: typing shows **only the name list**; picking a name shows **only** that player's matches (Lịch) or groups (Bảng đấu); selection in URL `?p=` |

The **Log out** button on the profile page now logs the user out. It calls the existing backend logout endpoint, which invalidates the session and clears the `JSESSIONID` cookie. After that, the frontend clears the current user and navigates back to `/`, so the navbar shows the login button again.

author: ninotelephone1006-boop
body:
## Ce qui a été ajouté

Une couche de **vraies notifications du téléphone** (bandeau Android, bannière iOS 16.4+, notification bureau), **hors du jeu** : elles ne partent que quand le jeu n'est pas au premier plan. La cloche interne continue exactement comme avant.

### L'utilisateur choisit ce qu'il veut recevoir
- Fenêtre **« Quelles notifications veux-tu recevoir ? »** avec 8 interrupteurs : 🗺️ quêtes prêtes, 🏆 succès, ⭐ niveaux, 👥 demandes d'ami, 🪙 marché (vente, offre, pièces reçues), 🎲 défis pile ou face, 🎁 cadeau du jour, 📣 nouveautés/promos (**désactivé par défaut**).
- Question posée **une seule fois** à la première visite (jamais pendant une ouverture de pack ni par-dessus une annonce), plus un bouton **Tester**.
- Réglages accessibles à tout moment : **cloche → « Choisir »** et **Compte → Notifications du téléphone** (Activer / Réactiver / Désactiver / Tester).
- La permission du navigateur n'est demandée **que sur clic**. Sur iPhone/iPad, message expliquant l'ajout à l'écran d'accueil (iOS n'autorise les notifs que pour une PWA installée).

### Technique
- `push.js` : module autonome (catégories, préférences par compte en localStorage, filtres, enregistrement du service worker) — aucun changement de `firestore.rules`.
- `sw.js` : affiche les notifications et ramène dans le jeu au clic ; **aucun cache**, écoute déjà l'évènement `push` (branchement FCM possible plus tard sans toucher au jeu).
- `app.js` : déclencheurs quêtes / succès / niveau / ami / vente / pièces / offres / défis / cadeau du jour / nouveautés, toujours filtrés par les choix de l'utilisateur et par la visibilité du jeu.
- `server.js` et `firebase.json` servent `sw.js` avec `Cache-Control: no-cache` ; version de l'app incrémentée.
- Test dédié `tests/push-notifications.cjs` (ajouté à `npm test`) + section README.

### Limite assumée
Sans serveur de push (FCM + Cloud Functions), la notification ne peut partir que tant que le jeu est ouvert dans un onglet, même en arrière-plan — c'est là que les écoutes temps réel Firestore détectent amis / ventes / défis.

author: jstzwj
body:
Lean proof for L-quadratic-primes-cert-1153.

**Frozen statement.** `∀ n : ℕ, 1153 ∣ n ^ 2 + 1 ↔ n % 1153 = 140 ∨ n % 1153 = 1013` (complete sieve roots modulo 1153; the variable ranges over all naturals, no hypotheses, no estimates).

**Method.** Work in the prime field `ZMod 1153` (`Nat.Prime 1153` by `norm_num`). Since `140 ^ 2 + 1 = 19601 = 17 * 1153`, the class `140` is a root of `x ^ 2 + 1`, and `1013 = 1153 - 140` is its negative. In `ZMod 1153`, `x ^ 2 + 1 = (x - 140) * (x + 140)` because `140 ^ 2 + 1 = 0`, so a zero of `x ^ 2 + 1` makes one factor vanish (`mul_eq_zero` in a field), giving `x = 140` or `x = -140 = 1013`; conversely both classes are roots. Transport between ℕ and `ZMod 1153` uses `ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff` (`1153 ∣ n ^ 2 + 1 ↔ (n ^ 2 + 1 : ZMod 1153) = 0`) and `ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff` with `140, 1013 < 1153`. The two numeric facts are discharged by kernel `decide` before the `Fact (Nat.Prime 1153)` instance is introduced.

**Remaining assumptions.** None: unconditional, `import Mathlib` only.

**Local check.** Lean 4.36.0, pinned Mathlib `fc4f59e5`; `#print axioms` gives exactly `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`; no `sorry`, no `native_decide`; the repository's proof-file guard accepts the file.

author: freeesta
body:
## What changes
Three CLI robustness bugs reported by a lab user, each reproduced on synthetic data (`tools/wiff_riferimento.py`, `tools/wiff_grande.py`) and fixed with tests.

**Deliberate contract change (read this first).** `completeness` now runs on EVERY `sample list` (not only with `--probe`). A pair whose `.wiff.scan` ends before its index, or holds sections the index lacks, used to exit 0 (or 1 only with `--probe` and a short scan). It now exits **1** (a finished partial copy) or **8** (a member modified in the last `RECENT_S` = 10 s: it may still be written). The listing stays on stdout in both cases and the finding is logged with its evidence. `contract_verdict_tests.rs` changed accordingly: a freshly written cut copy is exit 8 (it was exit 1), and the same copy aged an hour is exit 1.

1. **Partial `.wiff` copy was not flagged.** `sample list` compares the `.wiff.scan` with its index (`mzlab_core::wiff::completeness`: `short` = scan ends before the index, `unlisted` = scan holds sections after the indexed part, found by their marker; padding is not an alarm; queued empty table rows do not hide an unindexed section). On a mismatch the JSON gets `consistency` {`status, scan_bytes, indexed_end, wiff_bytes, samples_listed, sections_unlisted, age_s, recent_s, still_writing`}; stderr gets ONE warning (the old `--probe` "cut" and "longer" lines are not repeated when `consistency` already says it) with the sizes, the age and the 10 s threshold. A modification time in the future counts as age 0 (just written). A whole pair carries no `consistency` key.
2. **`--json` stdout purity.** Not reproducible: on this base `sample list` already writes `listing FILE` with `err +=` (stderr), and no progress line moved from stdout to stderr in this PR, so no golden changed because of it. The reported stdout line is consistent with a shell that merges the two streams (`2>&1`). I audited every `--json` command instead and added `json_stdout_tests.rs`: a sweep derived from the commands catalog (every command that reads `--json` or prints JSON by default, given a missing file; a command added later is covered without an edit) plus 23 hand-written successful/warning/refused runs, each parsed as ONE document with `serde_json`. A guard test fails if a hand-written case names a command that left the catalog. The test needs `python3` and fails (does not skip) without it.
3. **`spectrum get` default MS level.** With one MS level other than 1, it is used and logged (stderr notice `warn.scan.levelOnly` and `evidence.level_auto` {`ms_level, levels, why`}, now a property of `spectrum-1.json`). With several levels and none at 1, the error is `err.scan.level` (exit 5) naming the levels and the hint `--ms-level N`. A file that has level 1 keeps the old default and logs nothing; `--ms-level` and `--scan` win.

The new stderr texts are catalogue keys (`warn.wiff.{short,unlisted}.{writing,idle,unknown}`, `warn.scan.levelOnly`, `err.scan.level`) in `lang/en` + `lang/contesto`, pinned by `the_warnings_are_catalogue_text_with_their_context_and_every_parameter_used`.

## Routes touched and parity
- CLI only: `sample list` (consistency, exit 1/8) and `spectrum get` (default level). The shared `samples_list/1` text is unchanged byte for byte for a whole pair; `consistency` is added only on a mismatch.
- **Technical limit for `consistency`:** the site's `native_samples` has no `consistency` key because a picked `File` is a snapshot with no modification time, so on a partial copy the site's listing bytes differ from the CLI's by exactly that key. `tests/test_samples_list_parita.py` (the wasm leg: it fails, not skips, in CI when cargo, wasm-bindgen or node is missing, via the `GITHUB_ACTIONS` guard) strips `consistency` with a regex, requires it on every `unindexed*` pair and on no other, and compares the rest byte for byte. Same sentence in `docs/agenti/wiff-sample-choice.md`.
- **Wasm modules: none touched.** `completeness`, `unlisted_sections` and `Completeness` live in `mzlab-core` (`wiff/growing.rs`, `wiff/unindexed.rs`) but are exported to no wasm entry point; no `crates/*-wasm` file and no `tools/moduli/*.toml` changed, so no cap is raised. The CI size step (`tools/ci_wasm_dimensioni.py`) writes its figures only to the `wasm-dimensioni` artifact of run 45603120272 (584 B zip), not to the job log, and the `rust-wasm` and `rust-wasm-guardie` jobs are green on this head; I did not read the per-module figures from the artifact, so none are quoted here.
- Goldens: none changed. The only behavior change besides the one above: `sample list --json` at exit 8 keeps its `samples_list/1` document on stdout (like the verdict exits) instead of an `error/1`; whole-run growing refusals stay `error/1`.

## Guards (none raised)
`commands --json` 31,078 B (< 33,000, unchanged); `flow steps --compact` 18,467 B (< 20,000, unchanged); `docs/agenti/cli-agenti.md` 25,443 B (<= 25,600, unchanged); `wiff.md` 25,516 B. No INDICE rows or subcommand names added. `sample list` HELP now names `consistency` and exit 8; the catalog exit list already had 8.

## Before the push
- [x] Area: I read the area file (docs/agenti/INDICE.md) and touched only what my prompt says
- [x] `origin/main` merged only on a real conflict (none); `python3 tools/pre_pr.py` green; `cargo test -p mzlab-cli --lib` 992 passed
- [x] Parity: CLI-only check, limit stated above
- [x] CLI route for agents: `--json` with stable keys, distinct exit codes (8 pinned in `contract_verdict_tests.rs`), data on stdout and progress on stderr, listed in the agent catalogs
- [x] English only; user-facing text through `lang/` keys
- [x] No real data and no forbidden surnames; synthetic data only
- [x] Generated files regenerated with their tool where one exists (`tools-1.json` unchanged; `sample-list-1.json` and `spectrum-1.json` are hand-maintained)
- [x] Risks: this PR does NOT touch Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, `.github/workflows/`, `.wasm` files, the CSP, `crates/mzlab-desktop/`

## Risks
The exit-code change for partial copies above (0 -> 1 or 8 for a pair that disagrees with itself); scripts that treated exit 0 as "whole" now see the evidence instead.

author: boldaxolotl
body:
Closes #4568

T3 Code creates, names and deletes worktrees (ADR 0082), so `booley worktree` keeps only `prepare`. This removes `new`, `list`, `rm` and `gc` with what only they used: the packaged `worktree_create.sh`, the last-used stamp the MCP server wrote, the evidence copy `rm` made, `[worktree].gc_older_than`, the dead pairing, setup, evidence and submodule helpers, and the Session handle rule that skipped numbers of `s<N>` worktrees and branches. Plan: `docs/plans/issue-4568-plan.md` (local, not committed).

Changelog: Removed `booley worktree new`, `list`, `rm` and `gc`, the last-used record, and the evidence copy `rm` made. T3 Code creates and deletes worktrees; run `booley worktree prepare` in a new one. Deleting a worktree deletes the Flow reports and build trees in it. `booley doctor` warns while `[worktree].gc_older_than` is still set in `booley.toml`; delete the key. Session handles no longer skip numbers of `s<N>` worktrees or branches.

## Size

A net removal: 381 added and 6,976 deleted lines overall. Non-test Python and config: 200 added, 2,285 deleted. Tests: 80 added, 3,927 deleted. Docs and other files: 101 added, 764 deleted (CI timing entries of deleted tests, whole deleted files, the rewritten `docs/user/WORKTREES.md`). About 113 of the added source lines are a mechanical move: `src/booley/harness/dashboard/git_worktrees.py` holds `worktree_registrations`, `Registration` and `count_uncommitted` from the deleted `worktree_list.py`, with the exception renamed `WorktreeListError` to `WorktreeGitError` and the unused `stdin` parameter of `_run`/`_git` dropped. It keeps the NUL-delimited, `surrogateescape` parse and the `inherited_git_environment()` runner, so an inherited `GIT_DIR` never redirects the read.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `booley worktree --help` lists only `prepare`: `tests/harness/test_worktree_cmd.py::test_worktree_requires_a_subcommand` (usage `{prepare}`) and `tests/harness/test_cli_vocabulary.py::test_recursive_command_inventory`.
- AC2: this search over the repository, excluding the CHANGELOGs and ADRs, prints nothing (checked at the PR head):

  ```
  git grep -n -I -E "booley worktree (new|list|rm|gc)|worktree_command=.(new|list|rm|gc).|worktree (rm|gc)\b|last-used|LAST USED|last use\b|\.last-used|worktrees/\.evidence|\.evidence/<name>|worktree_evidence_paths|record_worktree_use|stamp_worktree|worktree_create(\.sh)?\b" -- ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!**/CHANGELOG.md' ':!docs/adr' ':!changelog.d'
  ```

  Output: empty.
- AC3: the web Dashboard accepts any worktree Git registers and the main checkout: `test_linked_worktree_snapshot_lists_only_its_jobs` (a `git worktree add` outside `.booley/`, as T3 Code makes one) and `test_main_checkout_is_a_worktree_with_only_its_jobs`, and `test_unlistable_worktrees_are_a_503_without_jobs` (Git failure is a 503). All three now read Git's registrations through `harness/dashboard/git_worktrees.py`.
- AC4: `tests/audit/test_config_schema.py::test_ignored_setting_warns_with_its_fix` has a new case: `[worktree].gc_older_than` gives the `config.ignored-key` warning "booley.toml [worktree].gc_older_than was removed and is ignored", fix "delete gc_older_than from [worktree] in booley.toml". Doctor runs `audit_ignored_settings` for it through `_validate_booley_toml`.
- AC5: ADR 0082 Consequences, first bullet: uncommitted Paired Checkout edits, the Flow reports and the build trees kept in the worktree are lost without warning because nothing copies them out first, and commits survive on the branch. `docs/user/WORKTREES.md`, "Removing a worktree", says the same.
- AC6: Ruff check and format, pyright (0 errors), the packaged-copies, Markdown line-length and function-length checks pass; the broad suite runs in the pipeline's Verify stage.

## Receipts

- Red (base `origin/t3`): the 6 criterion nodes fail in their bodies for the recorded reasons (wrong usage text, inventory mismatch, `ModuleNotFoundError` for `booley.harness.dashboard.git_worktrees` in the three AC3 tests, `ValueError` unpacking zero findings for the new `gc_older_than` case).
- Green (head): the same 6 nodes pass.
- Affected: 6,773 tests collected from 146 test files and directories (every edited test file, every test file importing a changed module, `tests/docs`, `tests/test_site_contract.py`): 6,749 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed.

## Deviations from the plan

- The two AC3 tests that already accept a linked worktree and the main checkout would be green on base, and the red check needs every criterion node to fail. Each now also asserts that its worktree is among Git's registrations read through the new module, so both are red on base (`ModuleNotFoundError`) and green after.
- `tests/mcp_tools/test_handle_pruning.py::test_allocation_survives_a_branch_name_that_is_not_utf8` is deleted too: it tested the branch listing of the retired allocation rule.
- `tests/harness/test_booley.py::test_source_project_binding_required_dispatch` uses `["doctor"]` instead of the worktree command: `booley worktree prepare` already binds as independent of a Project, so it no longer reaches the source-checkout refusal.
- `tests/docs/test_config_reference.py`: `worktree` joins `MIGRATION_ONLY_TABLES`. `[worktree]` stays a known table so a leftover `chat` or `gc_older_than` gets one warning, but it has no documented setting.
- `tests/harness/test_worktree_cmd.py::test_prepare_help_documents_the_command` joins argparse's hyphen wrap ("post- setup") before it checks the text, because rewording the description moved the wrap.
- The architecture diagram's box subtitle reads "main checkout + one per T3 Code thread" (the plan had ", prepared by Booley" too, which does not fit the box); the `<desc>` and the alt text carry "which Booley prepares". `docs/user/assets/architecture*.svg` are regenerated by `website/illustration/build.py`.
- `tests/harness/test_setup_workspace.py`: the class is renamed `TestWorktreeSetup`; its CI timing keys follow.
- No `changelog.d` fragment, as the pipeline asks: the `Changelog:` line above is the entry.

## Decided autonomously (revisit)

- Session handle pruning still keeps an `S<N>` handle while `.booley/worktrees/s<N>` exists. Nothing creates such worktrees any more; a follow-up can retire the retention. The helper moved into `src/booley/mcp/handle_pruning.py` as a private function.
- AC3's behavior already held on base. Its red test comes from moving the Git reader off the retired module, as the deviation above explains.
- The `worktrees/` row of the Booley Directory classification stays: `prepare` still writes `worktrees/FUSESOC_IGNORE`, `.locks` and `.logs`, and existing Projects keep old worktrees there.
- Only the pairing-rollback test (4 cases) is ported from the deleted `new` tests to `prepare`. The rest of the indirect coverage that `new` gave to shared code `prepare` also runs (broken pairing sources, the left-out warning cap, the `FlowConfigError` branch, mount repair) is an accepted risk; that code does not change here.
- ADR 0082's note that T3 has no hook or dirty check to stop a deletion stands; a guard against deleting a worktree with a running Job (QA comment F-46) is not part of this PR.

author: sean-lai-sh
body: ## Summary Compacting OpenCode trials no longer abort the trace parse. OpenCode emits the compaction summary as a `step_start` in the same session, then a synthetic user text (`part.synthetic`, text starting "Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if") before the next `step_start`. That text is input. It does not open a step, and it does not raise `events_malformed`. The step it follows is a compaction step. `steps` is the number of main-agent calls that returned 200. Compaction steps are counted separately and their provider thinking tokens are not added to the main total. A text event in the gap after compaction is an `implicit_text_before_step_start` warning on `trace_warnings`. The trace is still written. A text event before any step, with no compaction behind it, is still `events_malformed`. Trial fields: `compaction_steps`, `summary_steps`, `synthetic_continue_messages`, `compaction_thinking_tokens`, `trace_warnings`. `summary_steps` is 0 here. Title and summary side calls do not emit a session step, and nothing else in the stream distinguishes a summary step from the compaction step the continue prompt marks. OpenCode's own `step_finish.tokens.reasoning` on the compaction steps is 0 in all six fixtures. That disagrees with the wire. `compaction_thinking_tokens` is the provider usage of the compaction calls paired with those steps, which matches the wire side totals exactly (325, 444, 352, 129, 1387, 0). The 0 from OpenCode is not written into the field. 871d15b8 did not compact. Rebuilding its trace from the committed events matches `trace-before-fix.jsonl` byte for byte, including against the uncommitted source `wire.jsonl`. `finish_trial` still returns `post_compaction_signature` for the two 4xx trials before it builds a trace, so a live re-run of those trials does not yet stamp `steps` onto the row. The parser counts for those streams are covered by the re-parse tests. The failed final 400s are not steps. ## Fixture sizes Committed under `obench/tests/fixtures/opencode-compaction/`. No `wire.jsonl`. Largest file is `871d15b8/trace-before-fix.jsonl` at 1,308,967 bytes. Event streams total 2,359,889 bytes. Each trial has `opencode-events.jsonl`, `row.json`, and `wire-summary.jsonl` (`call_index`, `call_role`, `side_kind`, `status`, `thinking_tokens`, null kept as null). `derive_expected.py` writes `expected_counts.json` from those summaries and records the sha256 of each source `wire.jsonl`. ## Tests `python3 -m unittest discover -s obench/tests`: 2574 tests, 1 failure, 81 errors, 6 skipped. The failure is `test_cli_publish_and_verify_e2e`. The 81 errors are the scrubber flagging hostname `cursor`. Same set as 75ab94b2. ## Checklist - [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s obench/tests` — same pre-existing failure and scrubber errors as 75ab94b2; no new ones. - [ ] `obench validate` — not run; no task files changed. - [x] No copied or licensed code in `tasks/` — `tasks/` untouched. - [x] Documentation updated (`TRACE_SCHEMA.md`, `RUNNER_TABLES.md`). - [x] Changes are focused. `data/`, tasks, deploy scripts, and the wire proxy are untouched. ## Notes for the reviewer Wire records are the source of thinking tokens, same as main steps. The event-stream reasoning counter on compaction steps stays out of the total because it is 0 while the paired usage is not.

author: runbotrobot
body:
Part of #4201 (not closing it: the cover figure with a real ghost remains, and fog on arrival is left out on purpose, see below).

Item 4 of the issue: when the product's model cannot be drawn (the template row is gone, or the file fails to load), the ghost is the outline of its size with its name on a small camera-facing label, never a filled block. A ghost that does get its model has no label. A tap on the label is a tap on the ghost.

- `addGhostName` draws the label on a canvas (rounded plate in the brand yellow, with a plain rect fallback where `roundRect` is missing); it frees its own texture and material only.
- `e2e/build-pending-restoration.test.mjs` feeds the ghosts a slot whose template is null (`__testSetRemovedGhostSlots`, same `window.__test*` convention) and asserts an outline that is named; the earlier assertions (model, tap opens the list) still hold. `npm test` (308 files) and build pass.

**Deleted/delisted items (item 1/2 of the issue):** none of them can leave a ghost today. `assertCatalogTemplatesDeletable` refuses to delete or delist a product while any placement, saved layout, version or backup of it exists, so a product with a placed copy is never deleted or delisted; the not-live cases that do leave an item behind are sold-out and a suspended seller, both of which the switch already covers. If delisting a placed product is ever allowed, the snapshot path needs to be extended at that time.

**Fog on arrival:** left out. Shop's and Build's arrival fog is built around the first load's level-of-detail hold-back (`src/build/arrival.js`); a ghost appears when a switch is flipped, which is a person's own action rather than the world loading, and wiring it into that machinery would cost far more than the effect is worth. Say so if the owner wants it.

author: babysurfer-cyber
body:
## Symptom
With mode 5 and a manually selected cruise setpoint >= 90 km/h, the high-speed path correctly chooses pure 4A3 navigation speed. But when a fixed camera's MapSource=2 announcement clears, the cruise setpoint may remain unchanged if the fresh pure 4A3 limit is identical to auto_prev_limit.

## Changes
- Preserve existing >=90 km/h auto_source_high latch, LinkClass precedence, 4A3-only source, tollgate, and 4BE logic unchanged.
- Remember a validated 4A3 camera announcement (MapSource=2), and distinguish it from section-control (fresh navSectionActive).
- When the announcement explicitly clears (MapSource != 2) and fresh 4A3 navSpeedLimit is nonzero, trigger the existing mode-5 speed-limit formula **once**, even if raw speed limit equals the previously recorded value.
- Respect physical/manual speed override while camera warning is active.
- Do **not** infer passage from time, distance estimates, loss of CAN validity, or unchanged MapSource=2; hold remains safe if the marker never clears.
- Add a diagnostic log on camera announcement and eligible fixed-camera clearance.

## Verification
Added five regression scenarios to selfdrive/car/tests/test_auto_mode_camera.py: fixed-camera release at same raw pure 4A3 speed, continued MapSource=2 hold, missing/stale or zero-speed data, section-control exit without reapplying same limit, and manual speed override. Tests have **not yet been executed on-device**; perform a bench/replay run before merge.

## Limitations
The underlying 4A3 metadata must explicitly indicate clearance; if the real vehicle continues to report MapSource=2 past the camera, the existing data does not prove passage and this change intentionally will not adjust the setpoint. Capture CAN/carState logs for that case. Also ensure SpeedFromPCM settings do not replace the computed openpilot setpoint.

**Draft only. Do not merge/deploy on the vehicle until reviewed and validated with replay logs.**

author: zannen
body:
Replaces the CSV logs and `schedule.json` with one SQLite database, `boiler.db`, using Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, so the package gets no new dependency. Startup no longer reads or repairs the whole log, and a power cut can no longer leave a damaged file. Logins, roles and the token signing key stay as separate files.

## Database
- **Tables:**
  - `samples`: one row per poll, holding `ms` and the raw ebusd value of each boiler value, one column each.
  - `summaries`: tier, ms, and the mean/min/max columns.
  - `changes` and `commands`.
  - `schedule` plus `schedule_periods`: the heating schedule.
  - `meta`: import progress.
- **Settings:** WAL mode with `synchronous = NORMAL`. A power cut can lose the last batch of writes, but the database stays consistent.
- **Writing:** `DbWriter` replaces `FileWriter`. It still runs in its own thread and still writes every `--flush-seconds`, now as one transaction per batch. Failed batches are kept and retried.
- **Startup:** loading the chart history, summaries, changes and commands is now a query on the time column, with no tail-reading and no header searching.
- **Schedule:** stored in tables rather than a JSON blob. The checks in `validate_schedule()` still run when it's loaded.

## Schema changes
- `migrations.py` holds an append-only list of migrations, each either a list of SQL statements or a function. Migration 1 is the starting schema.
- `db.migrate()` runs the pending migrations in one transaction and records the count in `PRAGMA user_version`.
- Before migrating an existing database it copies it to `boiler.db.before-vN` with `VACUUM INTO`.
- It refuses a database from a newer version, e.g. after installing an older deb.
- New `VALUES` or `SAMPLE_KEYS` entries need no migration: their columns are added at every start.

## Importing the old files (once)
- **Small files** (`schedule.json`, `.changes.log`, `.commands.csv`, `.1min.csv`, `.15min.csv`) are imported at startup, one transaction each. A `meta` row records each file as done.
- **`boiler.csv`** can hold months of data, so it is imported in the background while the app polls and serves the UI. Polling and heating control run from the first second. It works in batches of 5,000 rows; each batch's transaction also saves the file position, so a restart carries on where it stopped. Crash debris is skipped (NUL bytes, header lines from restarts, short rows), as the old repair code did. Columns from older header layouts are kept.
- **Summaries:** if a tier never had a summary file, its summaries are built from `boiler.csv` during the import, replacing the old one-off build at startup.
- **When the import finishes,** the hub reloads its chart history and summaries from the database, keeping newer rows it already holds, and sends every browser a fresh snapshot. The page already handles a mid-stream snapshot.
- The old files are left in place. The log says when they can be deleted.

## Removed
- `csv_files.py`, which held the CSV tail-reading, header search, cleanliness check and repair code.
- `file_writer.py`.
- The old one-off build of missing summaries at startup.

## Command line and packaging
- The positional argument is now the database path. Its default changes from a time-stamped CSV to `boiler.db`.
- `--import-csv`, `--changes` and `--schedule` name the old files to import. Their defaults are the same files the old version used.
- The service runs with `/var/lib/vaillant-boiler-ui/boiler.db`. The deb now suggests the `sqlite3` package.
- README: a new **Data** section covers the tables, how to query a copy of the database, the upgrade import and the schema change process.

## Tests (new)
`make test` runs pytest, and CI runs it after the Python lint. There are 18 tests:
- **Migrations:** a new database gets the latest schema; reopening changes nothing; a new migration runs once and makes a backup; a failing migration changes nothing; a newer database or a CSV file passed as the database is refused.
- **Import:** the small files are imported once and never doubled; an existing schedule isn't replaced by `schedule.json`; the background import handles debris and changed columns, builds summaries, reloads the hub and keeps live samples; an import stopped after two batches resumes with no duplicates or gaps.
- **Storage:** rows from the hub, poller and command log round-trip through `DbWriter`; rows are kept while the database is locked; the schedule saves and loads; a bad stored schedule stops the program.

## Manual testing
- **Large import:** I ran the app against a fake ebusd with old-version data: a 113 MB, 1.07M-row `boiler.csv` with NUL debris, plus the other CSVs and `schedule.json`. The small files were imported at startup, and the CSV in the background in about 30 s on my machine; a Pi Zero will be much slower. I stopped the service with SIGTERM at 40% and restarted it. It resumed and ended with exactly the 1,076,330 valid rows the CSV holds.
- **Recent data with no summary files:** a CSV covering the last 50 minutes. After the import, `/api/state` held 50 minutes of history and 50 one-minute summaries had been built. Saving the schedule, the override and the command log all worked through the API.
- `make lint`, `make lint-deb` and `make test` pass.

## Notes
- The database is somewhat bigger than the CSV it came from: 130 MB vs 113 MB in the test, because of the time index. Like the CSVs, nothing is deleted yet. A retention setting would be a good follow-up.
- I haven't run it on the Pi. The first start after upgrading will log the import progress every minute.

author: shyalon
body:
## Summary
The Nuclear E5 lesson omitted much of its 40-slide source. It is rebuilt against all slides: full theory blocks, worked examples, 20 quiz items, new original figures (beta spectrum, photon spectrum, EM bands, N-Z decay directions, X-ray spectrum) and substitution-ready formulas.

## Corrections
Checked against evaluated data (LNHB/DDEP, NIST):
- Po-210 decays to Pb-206 (the slide shows Pb-208).
- The Cs-137 1.175 MeV line is only the 5.43% minor branch.
- Na-22 and Cs-137 values, Q versus emitted alpha energy, Am-241 energies.
- The existing Compton arithmetic is fixed (1294 to 1324 keV; scattered photon 184 keV, electron 478 keV).

## Source coverage
A per-slide map (87 units, hashes and locators only, no source files or slide text) with an independent source review recorded and bound to the exact source, lesson, unit-map and figure-code hashes. This PR records the review. The release check that enforces it ships separately and is not part of this PR.

## Generated progress rules
`operations/firestore/progress.rules` changes only nuclear E5 (adds questions 19 and 20). Repository file only, not deployed.

## Tests
- Full `npm run build` chain on this branch as one command: exit 0 (browser, pwa, practice, mock-exam, papers, final-prep, figure geometry 85 OK).
- `npm test` 290/290.
- Progress-rules checks 17/17.

## Limits
- Checks prove structure and traceability, not meaning; the independent review is the semantic evidence.
- The geometry guard does not check curves against text.
- The licensed beta diagram, X-ray photos and the neutron row of the penetration figure are not reproduced and are listed in the map.
- Any later edit to the shared figures file needs the review refreshed.
- Other topics are still unaudited. No importer change.

This PR builds on #159 (and on #157 → #158) and targets `main`. Merge order: #157 → #158 → #159 → this one.

## What changes
- **`scripts/JfrToTrace.java`** now reads the whole stack of a `jdk.MethodTrace` event, as it already did for samples. Each pair of consecutive recorded frames becomes a `traced` relation, keyed by the upper frame's bci and line. Before, only the traced method's direct caller was recorded. Only the traced method itself gets an exact entry.

author: duncanmcclean
body:
This pull request fixes an issue where changing a setting on a linked field in the forms builder, then changing it back to the fieldset's value, would leave the setting in `config_overrides`. From then on, the field stopped picking up changes to that setting from the fieldset.

This was happening because the field inspector only ever added keys to `config_overrides` when a value differed from the fieldset's, and never removed them.

This PR fixes it by removing a key from `config_overrides` when its value matches the fieldset's value again.

body:
Refs #686

Implements **Pools: no warm pool** through the implement loop.

## Decisions

Readings and choices the loop made on its own. To override one, edit the issue (reopen it first if it is closed) and run the loop again.

- **fleet-promotion-panel**: The fleet dashboard keeps its two launch panels; the promotion panel's title and the module's docstring name the transition by the agent's own word, "promotion", and no longer say "warm pool". (The issue stops the warm gauge on this dashboard and nothing else. The lifecycle agent still knows the promotion transition until E6-23, and `tests/unit/dashboards/test_fleet.py` holds the two panels. The acceptance grep covers `fleet.py`, so only the words change.)
- **s7-spike-gauge-name**: `spikes/s7_drain.py` holds the name of the warm gauge as its own constant instead of importing `WARM_INSTANCES` from `rhi_scaler.metrics`; nothing else of the spike or of `tests/unit/spikes/test_s7.py` changes. (The grep forbids the constant in `services/scaler`, and the spike imports it, so the import must change for lint, types and its tests to stay green. The spike is not in the issue's list: reworking or retiring a measurement that tells a return to the warm pool is not asked here. It is named in the notes for the owner.)
- **scaler-edge-states**: Besides the `DescribeWarmPool` read, `aws_io.py` drops what only a warm pool produces: the `Warmed:*` states and the launch activities described as into or from a warm pool. A launch is an activity that starts with "launching", and every successful one reached service. The protection of an unprotected instance in service before a scale-in stays, with its reason reworded. (The deliverable is that the scaler's edge reads no warm pool, and the grep forbids the words in its code. Keeping branches for states that can no longer occur would leave dead rules to maintain; the protection step is behaviour the issue does not touch.)
- **field-and-fixtures-stay**: `warm_instances` stays in `rhi_common.pool_config`, in `config.example.toml` and in every test fixture that builds a pool; the lifecycle agent, `src/rhi/pools/hooks.py`, `release.py`, `dashboards/rhi_dashboards/objectives.py` and `tests/synth/test_parked.py` are untouched. (The issue says the entry gives the field until E6-21 and the agent keeps its two transitions until E6-23. The objectives named after the warm pool are outside the issue's list and its grep.)
- **policy-files**: Under `tests/policy/` only `acknowledged/pools_scaler.toml` and `acknowledged/pools_group.toml` change, to drop the entry for `autoscaling:DescribeWarmPool` and every sentence about a warm pool; no invariant and no other acknowledgement changes. (The issue names these two files (ADR 0001, decision 10). The role loses an action, so the change narrows what is acknowledged; an entry left for an action no statement holds would be a stale acknowledgement.)
- **group-metrics-kept**: The group keeps publishing its thirteen `Group*` metrics every minute; only the seven that count a warm pool are no longer asked for. (The fleet's alarms and the cost dashboard still read `GroupDesiredCapacity`, `GroupInServiceInstances` and `GroupTotalInstances`; the issue removes the warm pool's metrics among those the group publishes, not the collection.)
- **protected-paths**: protected paths the issue names are granted: tests/policy/acknowledged/pools_group.toml, tests/policy/acknowledged/pools_scaler.toml (a protected path changes only when the issue names it or the examiner approves a `protected_change` request)
- **s7-spike-reads-no-warm-gauge**: Accept the examiner's reading of D3: `spikes/s7_drain.py` no longer queries `rhi_scaler_warm_instances` or needs its samples. (The issue removes the warm pool from everything that reads it, and the spike read the gauge the scaler stops sending. An import-only change would have left every departure `unknown` and each cycle waiting for readings that never come. The spike now writes each departure's `scale_in` line once the scaler asks for none and every decision has its instances out of service and gone. The line has no `path`, `warm_before` or `warm_after`; `unknown` keeps the three reasons that do not rest on the warm count (`stopped_before_ask`, `not_read_out_of_service`, `not_asked`). A cycle is run again only if it read no departure whole or not the stream across a scale-in. The test stub's workspace refuses any query but the in-service gauge and the collectors' writes, so a read of another series fails the tests.)
- **s7-settle-wait-dropped**: The spike tells its departures as soon as they are read, with no five-minute settle wait. (The wait existed only so a late rise of the warm count could be seen. A stop is still read only after 90 seconds of silence from the instance's collector, and a stop a later read contradicts is still withdrawn while the cycle runs.)
- **old-launch-history**: `launch_history` treats every activity whose description starts with "launching" as a launch, and every successful one as having reached service. (A group without a warm pool gives no other launch description, and the acceptance grep forbids the phrase in `services/scaler`. One transitional effect: a successful launch into the warm pool still in the group's history from before the deployment now ends a row of abandoned launches. It can only under-count abandons that predate the deployment, and the next abandon counts normally.)
- **warmed-states**: `_supply` no longer treats a `Warmed:*` state in the group's own list as draining. (As planned: a group without a warm pool never gives that state. An instance in a state the supply does not list is still in `running`, so going to zero still names it.)
- **fleet-start-panels**: The fleet dashboard keeps its two start panels; the promotion panel is retitled "Promotion of a stopped instance: seconds per stage, per launch". (The issue stops the warm gauge on this dashboard, not the lifecycle agent's stage series; E6-23 removes the promotion transition. The old title said "warm pool", which the acceptance grep forbids in `fleet.py`. The docstring says the panel has no new launch to show.)
- **cost-one-count**: The cost dashboard reads one count, `INSTANCE_COUNT`, so the month's read and today's have the same shape (`$S / 60`). (With `WarmPoolPendingCapacity` gone there is nothing to add. Each pool's count is still reduced on its own, so a group that published nothing does not blank the bill's estimate over every pool.)
- **scaler-simulator**: The scaler's test simulator has no warm pool: every start is a new instance after `start_seconds` (300), and a drained instance is terminated. (It plays the group as it now is. The scenario tests keep their assertions; the wake after a long idle now asserts one launch of a new instance, and the scale-in scenario that the released instance is gone.)
- **runbook-panel-title**: Three runbooks that named the panel "Instances: desired, in service, warm" now name it by its new title; the unpark check reads zero for both counts instead of a filled warm pool. (This change renames the panel, and a runbook step that points at a panel that no longer exists cannot be followed. The rest of the runbooks' prose about the warm pool is left for a follow-up: the issue does not list it.)

Two buttons create an empty deck: "Create Deck" on the decks page (`src/app/[locale]/decks/page.tsx`, `handleNewDeck`) and "New Deck" in the header (`src/components/layout/HeaderDeckActions.tsx`, `useCreateFailureReport`). On `origin/dev` a French player whose request answered 500 read:

> Impossible de créer le deck — [createDeck] HTTP 500: Failed to create deck

and "— Failed to fetch" on a network error. That is diagnostic text, in English, from the deck client (`DeckApiError`). #1901 already keeps such text out of the AI panel; this PR applies the same split to deck creation (I-01).

What `POST /api/decks` (`src/app/api/decks/route.ts`) can refuse for an empty deck with a name and a format:

- 401 `Unauthorized` from `requireAuth`: the session ended. The player can fix this by signing in again, so it gets its own message.
- 400 `Invalid input`, a bad `Idempotency-Key`, or `name is required`: the client built the request, so the player cannot act on it.
- 500 `Failed to create deck`: may pass on a retry.

There is no deck-count limit, plan limit or rate limit on this route today, so nothing else is mapped.

## What changed

- `lib/deck/deck-create-failure.ts` (new, pure): `deckCreateFailureOf(error)` reads what creating a deck threw. A `DeckApiError` with status 401 is `signed-out`; everything else is `failed`.
- `hooks/useDeckCreateFailureReport.ts` (new): the one failure report both buttons share. It logs the raw error with `logger.error`, as before, and raises a toast with `common.nav.createFailed` or `common.nav.createSignedOut`. The toast never carries the thrown message.
- The decks page and the header's deck actions ("New Deck", and "Import" from a page without a deck) call that hook. The header's private `useCreateFailureReport` is gone.
- Locales: `common.nav.createFailed` no longer has a `{reason}` placeholder. en: "Could not create the deck. Please try again."; fr: "Impossible de créer le deck. Réessayez." New `common.nav.createSignedOut`, en: "Your session has ended. Sign in again to create a deck."; fr: "Votre session a expiré. Reconnectez-vous pour créer un deck." `common.nav.unknownError` and `deck.home.createFailed` had no callers left, so they are removed from every locale.
- Dormant locales (de, es, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh): `createFailed` keeps its existing translation, with the placeholder replaced by a full stop. The new `createSignedOut` is English, as the repo fills new keys in those locales today (see #1901).

author: satobloc
body:
## Purpose

Add a small, source-neutral formal result that turns the existing Coupling-Preserving Projection Gate (CPPG v0.1) joint-observable requirement into a candidate operational interaction signature. Add one source-grounded standard-reference example of an invertible contour-to-observable map.

The factor types W and T are abstract index domains; they do not assert that H(s)H has independently variable worldtube and timesheet carriers. The output V is a common additive observable space (or a product of separately typed channels).

Terminology is deliberate: Kestrel's historical Nathan-direct source explicitly preferred "intersection", "instantiating", or "observable slice" to "readout" (Science Made Stupid, conversation `6ab070ce-2384-83e9-b76f-4661c55867c4`, raw Git blob `100267f3f11f3cce09c7d802ce85ad03879d5744`, user-role message `77563549-2ae5-49e1-b95c-bc1fc7442586`). The module therefore uses "observable"; the CPPG term is retained only as an interoperability pointer.

## New formal results

### A. Source-grounded contour-to-observable equivalence

Barckicke, Falcon & Gissinger, *Kelvin wave propagation along vortex cores*, Nature Physics (published 10 February 2026), define

\[
\eta(z,t)=\frac{r(z,t,0)-r(z,t,\pi)}{2},\qquad
a(z,t)=\frac{r(z,t,0)+r(z,t,\pi)}{2}.
\]

The new Lean module formalizes the per-sample map
`(r₀,rπ) ↦ (η,a)` and proves its exact inverse `(η,a) ↦ (η+a,a−η)`. This establishes only that this two-coordinate change is invertible at a fixed sample; it is not an H(s)H projection, worldtube map, or physical equivalence.

Primary source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-026-03175-w, DOI 10.1038/s41567-026-03175-w, Methods / Measurement techniques, lines 234–237 in the author-hosted article PDF. Data availability: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30903347.

### B. Four-corner interaction contrast

For an observable O : W × T → V, define

\[
\Delta_{WT}O =
O(w_1,t_1)-O(w_1,t_2)-O(w_2,t_1)+O(w_2,t_2).
\]

The new module proves:

1. If O is additively separable as f(w)+g(t), every four-corner contrast is zero.
2. Given basepoints w₀,t₀, if every contrast is zero over the full Cartesian domain, O is additively separable.
3. One nonzero contrast rules out every additive-separable decomposition of that declared observable.
4. A constant additive detector offset cancels exactly.

This makes a nonzero contrast a possible witness of non-additive joint response, while preserving the distinction between a formal interaction term and physical coupling or causation.

## Candidate empirical use, not yet instantiated

The Nature experiment uses pump flow U and drain-hole diameter d as separate controls. It reports a 12.5 cm axial measurement window centred at z=22 cm, 300 fps / 30 s acquisition for spatiotemporal spectra, 60 μm px⁻¹ resolution, 0.5 mm contour width, and typical core-radius/position uncertainty about 0.1 mm. PIV uses a 37×23 grid at 2.7 mm resolution with circulation uncertainty about 0.005 m² s⁻¹; PTV reports vertical-velocity uncertainty about 0.05 m s⁻¹. The paper's data DOI is 10.6084/m9.figshare.30903347.

A future candidate contrast would be
`Δ_Ud O = O(U₁,d₁)−O(U₁,d₀)−O(U₀,d₁)+O(U₀,d₀)`,
computed separately for a selected, consistently calibrated observable channel (for example η, a, or a defined spectral observable). The published figures show one-factor sweeps, but a complete matched 2×2 factorial and raw phase-preserving file availability have **not** been verified from the Figshare files. The paper's power spectrum `S_X=|X̃|²/(LT)` is a later summary; do not assume phase information survives it.

The standard comparator is the paper's Rankine-core Kelvin dispersion relation, equation (2). Its Methods state that a₀ was measured, then Γ and v_z were fitted to the dispersion data and checked a posteriori against PIV/PTV values. A genuinely independent holdout should instead freeze a₀, Γ and v_z from independent measurements before predicting a held-out U,d condition; do not refit the holdout.

No dataset files have yet been downloaded or inspected, no 2×2 support confirmed, no covariance matrix recovered, and no H(s)H worldtube/timesheet map derived. Therefore there is no physical calculation, fit, H(s)H prediction, or numerical falsification threshold. The classical vortex's finite core is not automatically an H(s)H worldtube; its measured contour pair is not a timesheet. This is a standard-physics data candidate only. P2 remains HOLD.

A nonzero contrast beyond a pre-registered uncertainty region would reject the additive-separable observable class for that tested domain. It would not by itself establish H(s)H, causation, or departure from standard physics. Zero for one quartet is inconclusive; zero over the full domain is the theorem's stronger condition. Nonlinear calibration can create or erase apparent interaction, so calibration must precede the contrast. Heterogeneous channels must remain separately typed or be combined only through a dimensionally valid, frozen mapping.

## Existing-work relationship

- Builds on the proposed [Coupling-Preserving Projection Gate v0.1](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/COUPLING_PRESERVING_PROJECTION_GATE_V0_1.md), which requires a joint observable and coupling signature to survive projection.
- Complements Mercer's [dimensionally typed coupled-observable proposal](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/MERCER/2026-11-20T2336Z_H983_S3_DIMENSIONALLY_TYPED_COUPLED_READOUT.md); it does not replace channel typing, reference-scale or covariance requirements.
- Does not modify Kestrel PR #2323, Nadir PR #2397, Ravel PR #1133, Mercer PR #2236, or Sable PR #2327.

## Verification

- Lean 4.34.0 / Mathlib v4.34.0, using the existing pinned Lake project.
- New module: `FORMAL_VERIFICATION/HsHVerification/KestrelJointObservableInteraction.lean`.
- Root aggregator import added.
- No `sorry`, `admit`, custom axiom, new dependency, new workflow, or new tool.
- This PR targets the existing `infra/lean4-verification-20261023` formalization branch, not main.

**LEAN_VERIFIED / EXACT_PR_HEAD / BUILD_ONLY.** Actions run [#45594540078](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/actions/runs/45594540078) checked out exact head `a529bbc3ed3e12cc504c5b02a5733e038e619d3b` and completed the 8,948-job library build with Lean 4.34.0 / Mathlib 4.34.0. The five interaction-contrast theorems report `[propext]`; the two contour round-trip theorems report `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The earlier run #45593855251 failed because the real-valued definitions needed `noncomputable`; that was corrected in the current head. Tests, lint, leanchecker, nanoda and global axiom audit were skipped. `lake-manifest.json` is still not committed, so transitive dependency reproducibility remains incomplete. This build establishes only the formalized algebra and coordinate inverse, not their source-to-H(s)H translation or empirical truth.

## Factory Floor boundary

The geometry-first gate is not met: no H(s)H object-specific precision plot or independent hostile fidelity review exists. If Lean succeeds, this is eligible only for a clearly labelled **PRE-INTAKE HOLD / GEOMETRY_NOT_SUPPLIED / NOT FACTORY FLOOR ELIGIBLE / NOT AN H(s)H CANDIDATE / PHYSICALLY UNVALIDATED** record, not WORKSHOP/LIVE/ARTIFACTS/WEBSITE advancement.

body: Risky behavior now covered - STS verification rejects HTTP 300 even when the body contains an Arn, and does not echo the new secret. HTTP 299 with the same Arn still verifies, and the request stays on `https://sts.amazonaws.com/`. - An IAM `ListAccessKeys` body with `IsTruncated=true` and a `Marker` deletes only the oldest inactive key. It does not list a second page, send the marker, or delete the active key. - A Cloudflare create response does not store decoy tokens from `messages`, `result.secret`, or `result.token`. The stored value and derived secret come from `result.value` only. - A Backblaze key name or bucket id that contains a forged `capabilities` array stays one JSON string. `deleteFiles` is not added. - Two freshly scheduled targets draw jitter in config order. An unscheduled target between them does not consume a draw. Full negative jitter clamps to the base instant; the next draw lands two hours later. Test files added/updated - `src/provider/aws.rs` - `src/provider/cloudflare.rs` - `src/provider/backblaze.rs` (`create_key_body` is a behavior-preserving extract) - `src/scheduler.rs` Why these tests materially reduce regression risk These are the fail-closed checks around minting and trusting a credential. A status check that moves after Arn parsing would accept a redirect body as a live key. Following `Marker` would delete or request another page of keys. Reading a token from the wrong JSON field would store an attacker-controlled secret. String-building the B2 create body would let a key name grant `deleteFiles`. Sharing one jitter draw across targets would make a fleet rotate together. `cargo +stable test`: 50 passed in 4.01s. The five new tests re-ran 5 times, 0.00s. No production behavior change beyond the extract. Rust 1.83 cannot compile clap 4.6; `cargo +stable` is rustc 1.100.0.

body: The NHS unsocial hours calculator now answers overtime searches as well. From 26 Oct to 22 Nov 2026 the page had 1 click and 247 impressions at average position 32.4, and Google was testing it for queries such as "overtime calculator uk nhs" and "nhs overtime pay". ## What changed - Title, meta description, H1, Open Graph, Twitter and the WebApplication JSON-LD now lead with unsocial hours and overtime pay. The title is 57 characters. The meta description is 150. - A short section says what unsocial (unsociable) hours are under Agenda for Change, with the percentage table by band for nights, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. - A section on NHS overtime: hours above 37.5 in a week, time and a half for bands 1 to 7, double time on a general public holiday, and no overtime payments for bands 8 and 9 (band 8 includes 8a, 8b, 8c and 8d). Part-time staff stay on plain time until the week passes 37.5. The unsocial hours percentage is left out of the overtime sum. - Four questions, each answered in the first sentence, with FAQPage JSON-LD kept in step: the overtime rate, bank holiday pay, what unsocial hours are, and band 5 night shifts. - A short App Store prompt under the introduction, and the end button. Both use the existing campaign link `ct=tool-nhs-unsocial-hours` (the tool token already live on this page). Copy stays on what the site already says the app does: set up a shift pattern, see upcoming shifts, record hours and breaks, estimate pay from rates the user enters. It is described as a paid download. No price is hard-coded. - Internal link to `/journal/nhs-shift-rota-patterns.html`. That file, and the other pages in progress, were not edited. - `dateModified` is 2026-11-25. Sitemap `lastmod` for this URL is 2026-11-25. - The calculator script is unchanged. It still estimates unsocial hours on the shifts you enter, and the page says overtime is separate. ## Sources, checked 25 November 2026 - [NHS Terms and Conditions of Service Handbook, amendment 63](https://www.nhsemployers.org/system/files/2026-10/NHS-TCS-Handbook-version-63.pdf) (TCS Advisory Notice 04/2026, published 1 October 2026): section 2 (England), section 3 (paragraphs 3.1 to 3.7), section 10.1, section 4.2, Annex 4 and Annex 5. Wales and Northern Ireland section 2 tables show the same percentages. Scotland's section 2 differs for bands 1 to 3, and Scotland publishes its own handbook. - [NHS Employers, unsocial hours payments](https://www.nhsemployers.org/articles/unsocial-hours-payments) (reviewed September 2025), including the note that overtime in unsocial hours is paid at time and a half, or double time on a general public holiday. - [Section 3, overtime payments](https://www.nhsemployers.org/tchandbook/part-2-pay/section-3-overtime-payments). No current pay-point figures in pounds were added. £17.50 in the worked example is labelled as a rate you type in, not a band 5 pay point. ## Checks - Default example week (bands 4 to 9, £17.50): 36 paid hours, £630.00 basic, £252.00 unsocial enhancement, £882.00 total. Switching to band 1 changes the enhancement to £394.80. Adding and removing a shift updates the totals. An annual salary of 34000 converts to £17.39 an hour. - JSON-LD parses, and the FAQ answers match the visible text. - The page renders on a desktop width and at 390px, with no horizontal overflow.

author: bplatz
body:
Fixes #269.

## Case

The Sherwin-Williams EDS's US/Canada and California VOC tables restate a unit partway down for one column alone: `By wt`, bold and shaded as the header is, over `LVP-VOC | 0.0%`. `restated_header_rows` needed two names on the row, so `By wt` was read as a value under `K25W951 / LB/Gal`, and the `0.0%` under it was named `LB/Gal` as well.

## Layout class

A unit or sub-heading restated over the one column the rows under it fill, partway down a table: one name in a value column, the first column empty, set apart as a header is (bold, shaded, or names turned on their side), over a plain row.

## Fix

`restated_header_rows` (`table.rs`): a row with a single name now qualifies when three things hold:
- the name stands in a value column and the first column is empty. A name alone in the first column labels a group of rows, which `sub_headers` handles;
- `bold` holds with that one value cell bold. For rows of two or more names it still needs two or more bold cells, since one bold word beside a label is emphasis;
- at least one data row stands between the row and the header. Straight under the header, one name is the header's own label wrapped (`Body weight` over `(kg)`).

All the existing conditions still apply: no figure, code or repeat; a plain row under it; a row it shares a column with.

`docs/design/tables.md` describes it.

## Second example

The corpus A/B shows the same class in five other documents, each now naming its rows by the sub-heading over them:
- **HPE Hard Disk Drives QuickSpecs:** the server compatibility list sets `HPE ProLiant ML` over the ML servers, which were named `HPE ProLiant DL` (the previous sub-heading).
- **Google environmental report:** the goal `Maximize the reuse of finite resources …` heads the circular-economy rows, which were named by the water goal above.
- **Apple environmental report:** `Supplier facilities` heads its savings rows, which had no column header.
- **TI LM358 datasheet:** each revision-history block's `Changes from Revision X … to Revision Y` heads its bullets.
- **A partner evaluation package (requirements matrix):** `Non-functional requirements` heads the NFR rows, which were under `Functional requirements`.

The first A/B also caught two wrong changes, both now excluded by the "under a row of the data" guard:
- Eliquis `Body weight` over `(kg)`;
- a PMC table whose caption-like row sat straight under the header.

The unit test `a_single_bold_unit_over_its_column_restates_the_header` is synthetic: `in` restated over a millimetre column. It also checks that the row is not restated when set plain, when the name stands alone in the first column, or when it sits straight under the header.

## Measurements

Base is main at f2fd19d; rebased onto 0939f8d.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| bench tier 1 (`--md-links text`) | 0.915488 | 0.915488 |
| bench tier 3 | 0.946713 | 0.946713 |
| `eval/tough/check.py` | 2 failed (the new checks) | 0 failed (932 passed after the rebase) |
| `eval/tables/check.py` | 186/190 | 186/190 |
| `eval/tables/check.py eval/tables-full` | 8620/8642 | 8620/8642 |

- **Tough checks added** to `sherwin-williams-eds-restated-units`, both failing on main:
  - `single-unit-restated`: `0.0%` under `K25W951 / By wt`;
  - `single-unit-not-a-value`: `By wt` is no longer a value under `LB/Gal`.
- **Corpus A/B** (pdf-all, spec sheets, and the 704-PDF FinTabNet/PubTables/NIOSH sample, Markdown and DoCO): 6 documents change, all in DoCO only: the EDS sheet and the five above. There is no Markdown change.

## O que muda

**Cadastro livre com aprovação do gestor**
- Qualquer pessoa com o link cria a conta informando nome, e-mail e senha. A conta nasce **inativa e pendente**: não entra, não bate ponto e não envia justificativa (bloqueado pelas regras do banco).
- O gestor vê um aviso no Painel da Equipe e, em Configurações, **✅ Aprovar** ou **❌ Recusar**. Pendentes aparecem no topo da lista e não contam como colaboradores ativos.
- O pré-cadastro continua como atalho opcional: quem está nele entra já aprovado, com cargo, perfil e carga horária.

**Mensagens de cadastro**

## Como foi testado
- Schema aplicado sobre um banco criado com a versão anterior (PostgreSQL 16 imitando o Supabase): gestor e registros preservados; cadastro novo entra pendente.
