author: tomyan
body:
Entry 44, action 17: a long search field. The text now stays inside the field's content box, and the caret stays visible while typing, deleting, after blur and refocus, and on the first frame after a resize. Measured against the pinned Chromium 157.0.8103.0 (`scripts/chromium-field-scroll.mjs`). Design A′, agreed for Tom: the field element is its own horizontal scroll frame.

## What changes
- **User-agent sheet** (`crates/css/src/ua.css`): text inputs get `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; scrollbar-width: none`. Number fields are unchanged, and a number field set to scroll is still refused.
- **Clip** (`clip.rs` `content_clip`): a field whose text scrolls is clipped to its content box on x and its padding box on y. Chromium's ink stops at the same columns, 689 to 942.
- **Range and reveal** (`scroll_reveal.rs`):
  - The range on x is the run's text width, plus the 1 px caret, minus the content width.
  - On each settle where the caret or the laid-out content width changed, the field scrolls just far enough to show the caret.
  - On blur it scrolls back to 0.
  - A wheel scroll in between is kept.
- **Marks and text origin**: the field's run (its text box) now holds the marks and paints them in its own step, so they sit in the field's scroll frame. `paint_box` calls `text_paint` first, so the selection stays under the text. The kept text origin carries that frame, and the pointer and the IME read it from there.
- **Rounded corners**: a text field whose text scrolls may clip when its side padding is at least the corner radius less the border. Any other rounded clip is refused as before.
- **Bench**: `.search-input` drops `overflow: visible`, and the FLAGS row is updated.

## Tests (each failure observed)
- `crates/elements/tests/field_scroll.rs`:
  - Typing to 18–60 characters and deleting back to 59–19: the field scrolls exactly when Chromium's does, and once scrolled the caret is within a column of Chromium's 942/941. Failed on main: offset 0, caret at 951 to 1475.
  - The text is clipped to 689..943. Failed with the padding-box clip restored.
  - Blur scrolls back to 0, and focus shows the caret again.
  - Home scrolls back to show the caret at 689. Failed with the leftward reveal removed.
- `field_scroll_input.rs`:
  - A click places the caret under the pointer, in a scrolled field and after blur. Failed with the origin read through the field's outer frame.
  - A horizontal wheel scrolls a blurred field by 100, as Chromium does, and a vertical one passes it by.
  - The IME caret area is the painted caret. Failed with the outer frame.
  - A narrower window keeps the caret in the content box on its first frame, with no edit. Failed with the content width left out of the reveal.
  - A focused field's wheel scroll is kept across a relayout. Failed, snapping back from 433 to 533, with the reveal run on every settle.
- `clipping_refused.rs`:
  - A number field that scrolls is refused.
  - A rounded text field is refused when its padding does not clear the corners, or when it does not scroll.
  - It is drawn when its padding clears the corners.
- `gui-bench-app` `long_search.rs`: a 60-character search keeps its caret at 942 and its text under the content clip. Failed with `overflow: visible` restored: caret at 1475.
- Every new test runs in under 0.2 s.
- The compiler's counter snapshot is updated: the user-agent sheet's hash changed, and later rule indices move by 2.

## Coordination
- The placeholder stack (#584, merged) is integrated: `placeholder_paint` runs at the end of `paint_box`, as agreed with its owner. Its 15 tests pass.
- #621 also edits `topbar.wisp` line 17. Whichever lands second keeps both changes.

## Known gaps
- A selection's moving end is not scrolled into view. Chromium does this; vapors keeps the offset.
- Touch pan on a field is not compared with Chromium.
- Whether a field's text scrolls is decided in two places: style (text fields only) and layout (`scrolls_text`). They agree because a number field set to scroll is refused.

## Checks
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on 0aa9f3fb, 15 of 15 steps.
- Two independent reviews, of e460d0db/ba9237e1 and of the fix commit ef3ec80d. Every important finding is fixed, with tests.

author: edkief
body:
Closes #165. Part of #162.

Makes the web app's recorder (#164) survive a reload or a crash, and an expired sign-in. Adds a panel showing what waits to upload, cleans up local storage, and documents recording from the web app. Plan: https://github.com/edkief/convoscribe/issues/165#issuecomment-7159059552

## What changed

- **Recovery after a reload or crash.** Starting a recording now writes a *draft* to IndexedDB (database v2: `drafts`, and `draftLines`, one row per finished line). This happens before the WAV is opened. The tab holds a Web Lock `convoscribe-recording:<syncId>` while it records. A draft that no tab holds a lock for counts as interrupted. The upload panel then offers to **Recover** it or **Discard** it.
  - Recover runs the writer worker's new `recover`. It cuts the OPFS WAV to its last whole sample, writes the header's sizes and hashes the file. The saved lines are trimmed to the recovered audio, then the recording is queued.
  - On Stop, `promoteDraft` writes the upload and deletes the draft in one transaction.
- **Sign-in expiry.** Requests use `redirect: 'manual'`. A `401`, or an opaque redirect (authz-proxy sending the browser to sign in), throws `SignedOut`. The queue keeps its items and stops backing off, and the panel offers *Sign in again*, which reloads the page through sign-in.
  - The runner tries again every minute, when the tab is focused or becomes visible, and when the browser comes back online. Signing in from another tab therefore works too.
- **Upload panel on every page.** The sidebar or top-bar status line opens a panel listing every recording on this computer: date, length, size, then progress or the last error, saved as `lastError` and kept across reloads. A failed recording can be retried. Any recording not being sent can be deleted.
- **Clean-up.**
  - On start, the tab that sends removes OPFS recordings that are neither queued nor drafts, and drafts whose file is gone.
  - A queued recording whose WAV has disappeared now fails with a message instead of retrying for ever.
  - The runner stops sending a recording deleted meanwhile, for example from another tab, and creates no session for it.
- **Docs.** *Recording in the browser* in the server README covers browsers, what survives an outage and what doesn't, and the panel. The root README gets a paragraph in *Sync server*.

## Design

- **Drafts in IndexedDB beside the OPFS file**, not a sidecar file in OPFS. The queue already lives in IndexedDB, and one transaction can turn a draft into an upload, so a crash leaves exactly one of the two.
- **Web Locks tell a live recording from an interrupted one.** I rejected a heartbeat timestamp: it needs a timeout and gets it wrong in a throttled background tab. Without Web Locks every draft looks interrupted, but recovering one that is still recording fails harmlessly, because that tab holds the OPFS sync handle.
- **Sign-in goes through a page reload.** In api-key mode the expired cookie redirects to `/sign-in`; behind authz-proxy the proxy runs its own sign-in on the top-level navigation. One path works for both modes.
- **Left as it was:** a storage failure *during* recording still discards what was recorded (#164 behaviour). Keeping it for recovery would be a small follow-up.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`: clean.
- `vitest --pool=threads`: 59 files and 694 tests pass. New tests cover:
  - choosing interrupted drafts, trimming the lines, building the recovered item and finding orphans;
  - a fresh runner resuming after a reload, `401` and opaque-redirect sign-out with no backoff, `lastError` being saved, a missing WAV, a recording deleted mid-upload, and the error descriptions.
- `next build` compiles and emits both workers. Its exit status is non-zero because of a Next.js version check that fails the build after compiling, not this change.
- Headless Chromium: I killed the bundled writer worker mid-recording (3 s and 7 s of audio), and `recover` produced a correct header; its SHA-256 matched the file.
- I checked the panel's layout with the real `web.css` in a static page, wide (it opens upwards from the sidebar) and narrow (it opens down from the top bar).
- **Not run here:** the whole app end to end (no S3 or Postgres sign-in in this sandbox). Checklist for a real deployment:
  - [ ] Chrome and Safari: reload during a recording, then Recover; the session plays and its transcript is cut near the end.
  - [ ] Cut the network mid-upload, reload, reconnect; the upload resumes without a duplicate.
  - [ ] Behind authz-proxy: let the sign-in expire with an upload queued; the panel asks you to sign in again, and the upload finishes afterwards.
  - [ ] Delete a failed upload from the panel.

author: evilpatrick06
body:
Refs #4620

The sealed scroll swallowed every key even though the character list already has a native foreground check. This left the first screen impossible to finish without a mouse.

Scroll actions now use that same fresh-answer check. Enter or Space opens it, Space toggles its checkbox, and Tab or Shift Tab moves between the checkbox and Continue. Continue keeps its existing handler, choice timer and seat-request flow. The list hint now names arrows, 1-9 and Enter.

The seal and Continue have named button semantics and visible focus. Keys waiting for a native answer retain their scroll phase and focused control. An answer arriving after mouse navigation cannot turn an old opening key into a character pick or activate a different control. Repeat events and modified shortcuts cannot advance the scroll. Missing native proof keeps scroll keys inactive.

Validation:

- Actual page regression: 26 passed. The identical final regression against original Main passes 9 and fails 17. It covers both foreground answers, stale and unrelated answers, timeout, repeats, focus changes, mouse navigation during a wait, checkbox persistence and the existing native seat handshake.
- Existing start-screen checks pass 79, menu-choice 27, selection-focus 71 and start-focus 23. The old click-only assertions now cover the fresh native guard while retaining their mouse-route and logging assertions. author: qq399356807
body:
## Summary

Hardens the CFS-CTS 0.1.4 candidate across ledger validation, batch integrity, local-anchor handling, and filesystem write boundaries.

### Security changes
- Require complete event schemas and strict integer sequence values; reject boolean/non-integer sequence values.
- Fail closed for malformed event rows and missing/empty anchor histories.
- Validate checkpoint schemas, exact field sets, digests, ledger versions, and historical ledger-prefix continuity.
- Add cooperating-process advisory locking to ledger and local-anchor operations; refuse to extend corrupt history or anchor an invalid/stale cooperating-writer snapshot.
- Validate batch groups end-to-end: completeness, contiguous sequence/index order, consistent metadata, and recomputed batch digest; bound untrusted batch-size metadata.
- Reject duplicate JSON object keys and non-standard JSON constants.
- Normalize single-append payloads through canonical JSON so returned records match persisted records.
- Reject final-component symlinks and non-regular ledger, anchor, and lock files.
- Complete short writes and surface write/fsync failures instead of reporting success.
- Add regression coverage through SEC-38 and update 0.1.4 security/release documentation.

### Validation
- Latest CI: [run 45755217186](https://github.com/qq399356807/CFS-CTS/actions/runs/45755217186)
- 9/9 matrix jobs successful: Ubuntu, Windows, macOS × Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13.
- Current generated CI artifact: **45 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED / 0 INCONCLUSIVE**.
- Source checksum verification and compilation passed.

### Security boundary and release status
This is a hardened prototype, not a production tamper-proof logging system. The local anchor is not an independent trust root; SHA-256 is unkeyed. Final-component symlink checks do not pin every parent-directory component. A process crash, power loss, or filesystem failure can leave a partial JSONL record or batch; such tails fail closed and require forensic review, not automatic repair. File-lock/fsync semantics remain filesystem and platform dependent. No independently operated remote anchor, signed release, reproducible-build attestation, or independent security audit is included.

The 0.1.4 candidate is CI-green for the supported matrix, but production/security-compliance claims remain out of scope.

author: xiaoapple0
body:
> **风险等级：高（契约变更）。** 需要维护者审查和合并。

## 改了什么

M1 拆分后的第 1 个 PR：SDK 契约变更，对应 M1 方案第 1、2 条，已经你批准。之后又按你的补充要求做了适配，以支持第二个行情源——迅投 xtdata。SDK 从 0.1.0 升到 0.2.0，属于**不兼容**改动。

### 契约

- **证券列表**：`DataSourcePlugin` 新增两个必需方法，都返回新的 `schema.SECURITIES_SCHEMA`（`symbol`、`name`、`exchange`、`kind`、`list_date`、`delist_date`）：
  - `securities(*, include_delisted=False)`：证券列表，默认只含在市证券
  - `lookup_securities(symbols)`：查询给定代码，可以包含已退市或根本不存在的代码，只返回有记录的
- **声明能否直接列出退市证券**：`Capabilities` 新增可选字段 `lists_delisted`，默认 False
  - 为 True：平台调用 `securities(include_delisted=True)`，直接取完整名单
  - 为 False：平台用 `lookup_securities` 扫描代码区间，扫描结果由平台保存，不重复扫描
- **复权因子的定义**：`adj_factors()` 的 `factor` 是**累计后复权比例**，自除权除息日起生效，只能由该日及以前的数据决定（`schema.ADJ_FACTORS_SCHEMA`）
  - 后复权价 = 未复权价 × factor(t)
  - 以 T 日为基准的前复权价 = 未复权价 × factor(t) / factor(T)
- **`bars()` 的文档补充**：停牌日不返回这一行；已退市的证券也要能返回历史
- **枚举可以新增取值**：`kind`、`exchange`、`Freq`、`Capabilities.markets` 等枚举以后可能新增取值，新增取值属于**兼容改动**。使用方遇到不认识的取值要跳过、不能报错（规则写在 `plugins.md` 的“契约变更”一节）
  - 清单字段不在此列，因为清单受 `sdk` 版本范围约束

### 新增工具和检查

- `duohelm_sdk.adjust.factors_from_events(closes, events)`：根据每股派现、送转、配股和配股价计算复权因子；参考价取除权日**之前**的收盘价
- `duohelm_sdk.adjust.adjust_bars(bars, factors, mode, base_date)`：计算后复权，或以指定日期为基准的前复权
- `checks.check_securities()`、`checks.check_adj_factors()`、`schema.known_securities()`
- **隔离子进程**：
  - 允许行情源插件调用 `securities` 和 `lookup_securities`
  - 跨进程传递 `Capabilities.lists_delisted`
  - 解码时跳过不认识的 `Freq`：原来遇到新的频率会直接报错，违反上面的枚举规则

### 其他

- `.gitignore` 加入 `.claude/launch.json`：这个文件含本机的绝对路径

### 迁移说明

- 行情源插件实现 `securities()` 和 `lookup_securities()`
  - 能直接列出退市证券的，在 `capabilities()` 里设置 `lists_delisted=True`，并支持 `include_delisted=True`
- `adj_factors()` 按新定义返回，推荐直接使用 `factors_from_events()`
- 清单里的 `sdk` 改为 `">=0.2,<0.3"`
- 目前还没有官方参考插件；eltdx 和 xtdata 插件都会直接基于 0.2 编写

## 两个数据源如何对应到这份契约

> **说明**：
> - **eltdx** 一列是 2026-11-25 用 3.3.5 版连接真实主站实测的结果，详见 PR #9
> - **xtdata** 一列**只基于** `xtquant_250807` 的源码和 `doc/xtdata.md` 整理，**没有连接** MiniQMT 实测，标“待实测”的地方要在写插件时确认

| 契约方法 | eltdx | xtdata |
|---|---|---|
| `capabilities().lists_delisted` | **False**：代码表只有在市证券 | **True**：可以下载并列出过期合约 |
| `securities()` | `codes.all_a_shares()` 取当前代码表，代码从 `sz000001` 转换为 `000001.SZ`；代码表里没有上市日，`list_date` 由平台根据第一根 K 线补齐 | `get_stock_list_in_sector()` 取沪深京 A 股；`get_instrument_detail()` 的 `InstrumentName`、`OpenDate`、`ExpireDate` 分别对应名称、上市日、退市日（在市时 `ExpireDate` 的占位值转换为 null，待实测）。代码本来就是 `600000.SH` 格式 |
| `securities(include_delisted=True)` | 不支持，抛出 `NotImplementedError` | 先调用 `download_history_contracts()`，再从过期合约板块取退市股（板块名称待实测），合约信息同上 |
| `lookup_securities(symbols)` | `delisted_bars.get()`：有数据的代码，用第一根和最后一根 K 线的日期作为上市日和退市日（实测：不存在的代码返回空，在市代码也能返回）；退市股的名称取不到，为 null | 逐个调用 `get_instrument_detail()`，返回 None 的代码视为不存在 |
| `adj_factors()` | `corporate.capital_changes()` 中类别 1“除权除息”的记录：c1/10 → 每股派现，c3/10 → 每股送转，c4/10 → 每股配股，c2 → 配股价（单位已用公开分红核对），交给 `factors_from_events()` 计算。**不使用**服务器的复权价：它是线性变换，会出现负数价格 | `get_divid_factors()`：`interest` → 每股派现，`stockBonus` + `stockGift` → 每股送转，`allotNum` → 每股配股，`allotPrice` → 配股价，交给 `factors_from_events()` 计算。xtdata 自带的除权系数 `dr` 用来在插件测试里交叉核对；标记为股改（`gugai`）的记录，xtdata 说明有“特殊算法”，我们的公式没有覆盖，写插件时再决定怎么处理 |
| `trading_calendar("CN")` | 没有专门的接口：用 `sh000001` 和 `sz399001` 的日线推出沪深两市的交易日，取并集（实测：1991 年深市有周六交易；2000 年以后两市一致） | `get_trading_dates("SH")` 和 `get_trading_dates("SZ")` 取并集。xtdata 的日历只支持沪深，北交所沿用深市的交易日（2021 年开市以来两者一致，待实测） |
| `index_constituents()` | `helpers.index_members()`：只有**当前**成分和纳入日期；`in_date` 取纳入日期，`out_date` 全为 null。**没有历史成分**，平台从 M1 起每天保存快照 | `get_stock_list_in_sector(指数板块, real_timetag)` 能取**历史某天的成分**；特色数据“板块成分股变动历史”（`stocklistchange`）可以得到调入、调出日期。可以完整实现这个方法（指数板块的名称待实测） |
| `bars()`（参考） | 在市证券用 `bars.get()`，退市证券用 `delisted_bars.get()`，都是未复权。丢弃成交量为 0 的行（停牌股当天的占位 K 线） | `download_history_data2()` 之后用 `get_market_data_ex(period="1d", dividend_type="none", fill_data=False)` 取数；丢弃 `suspendFlag == 1` 的行。成交量单位（手还是股）待实测 |

**对 M1 其余部分的影响**：
- **历史指数成分**：xtdata 能提供 eltdx 缺少的数据，M2 的指数股票池可以有真正的历史成分。
- **历史 ST 状态（#11）**：xtdata 有 `get_his_st_data()` 和“ST 变更历史”特色数据，#11 可能可以用它来补。
- **两个插件的共同问题**：都通过原生扩展访问网络，xtdata 用的是 C 扩展连接 MiniQMT，所以 M0 的 Python 层网络拦截对两者都不起作用，见 #7。
- **许可要重新确认**：xtdata 的许可和服务条款要像 eltdx 一样确认后，才能写进 `data.md`。

## 验证

本地环境：Windows

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`：通过
- `pyright`：用 `--pythonplatform` 分别检查 Linux、Darwin、Windows，都是 0 errors
- `CI=true pytest`：202 passed

**你要求的测试**：`test_factors_unchanged_when_future_events_truncated`。用 3 组随机生成的历史数据（含停牌、派现、送转、配股），在多个截断日上检查：截断某日之后的除权记录和行情后，该日及以前的因子完全不变。另有同类测试检查前复权。

**破坏验证**：故意破坏以下逻辑，对应测试全部变红，恢复后全部通过。

| 破坏 | 变红的测试 |
|---|---|
| 因子按最后一天归一化（引入未来数据） | 截断不变测试 |
| 用除权日**当天**的收盘价计算参考价 | `test_uses_close_before_ex_date_not_on_it` |
| 前复权忽略 `base_date` | `test_qfq_uses_base_date`、前复权截断测试 |
| 除权日当天的 K 线仍用旧因子 | `test_hfq_is_continuous_across_ex_date` |
| 不检查代码后缀与交易所是否一致 | `test_invalid_securities` |
| 协议里缺少 `lookup_securities` | `test_protocol_requires_security_methods` |
| 不过滤不认识的 `exchange` / `kind` | `test_unknown_enum_values_are_skipped_not_errors` |
| 解码时遇到不认识的频率直接报错 | `test_capabilities_roundtrip_and_unknown_freq_skipped` |
| 跨进程传递时丢掉 `lists_delisted` | 同上 |

## 给审查者

- **除权事件的单位按每股计算**，由各插件负责换算：eltdx 是“每 10 股”，xtdata 本来就是每股
- **股改和送认沽权证等特殊事件**不在复权公式内，写插件时再定怎么处理：eltdx 的类别 14 是“送认沽权证”，xtdata 的记录带有 `gugai` 标记
- **`include_delisted` 是仅限关键字参数**：不支持的插件可以抛出 `NotImplementedError`，平台只会对 `lists_delisted=True` 的插件这样调用

author: sulaimonifeoluwa4-blip
body:
## Summary

Refreshes `contracts/.gas-baseline.json` as requested in #1507:

- adds gas/memory snapshot tests for **distribute**, **escrow**, **refund**, and **batch_claim**, which had no baseline coverage;
- teaches `scripts/gas-regression.sh` to harvest those four crates and stops harvesting the empty `callora-allowlist` stub;
- removes the stale `callora-allowlist` block and regenerates the baseline with `--update-baseline` (no hand-edited numbers).

The branch also contains the workspace build repairs that were required to compile and run the gas gate on top of current `main`.

Closes #1507

## New gas snapshot tests

Each file follows the existing `contracts/cold/tests/gas_snap.rs` pattern: deploy with a real Stellar Asset Contract, exercise the entrypoint, then read `env.cost_estimate().resources()` and print one JSON line per entrypoint.

| File | Entrypoints |
| --- | --- |
| `contracts/distribute/tests/gas_snap.rs` | `distribute`, `batch_distribute` |
| `contracts/escrow/tests/gas_snap.rs` | `create_escrow`, `release` |
| `contracts/refund/tests/gas_snap.rs` | `request_refund`, `approve_refund`, `process_refund` |
| `contracts/batch_claim/tests/gas_snap.rs` | `add_claim`, `batch_claim` |

The fixtures fund the contract (or admin) before measuring, so the numbers include the real token transfers rather than failing early on an empty balance.

## Harvester and baseline

`scripts/gas-regression.sh` now runs `cargo test -p callora-{distribute,escrow,refund,batch-claim} -- gas_snap --nocapture` and appends the JSON lines to the shared measurements file. The `callora-allowlist` harvest was removed because `contracts/allowlist/src/lib.rs` is still a one-line stub.

`contracts/.gas-baseline.json` was regenerated with:

```bash
./scripts/gas-regression.sh --update-baseline
```

Resulting new entries (CPU instructions / memory bytes):

| Contract | Entrypoint | CPU | Mem |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| callora-distribute | `distribute` | 246,972 | 1,596 |
| callora-distribute | `batch_distribute` | 433,706 | 1,820 |
| callora-escrow | `create_escrow` | 258,022 | 2,216 |
| callora-escrow | `release` | 261,739 | 2,680 |
| callora-refund | `request_refund` | 173,645 | 1,596 |
| callora-refund | `approve_refund` | 146,887 | 1,544 |
| callora-refund | `process_refund` | 378,302 | 3,160 |
| callora-batch-claim | `add_claim` | 199,937 | 1,668 |
| callora-batch-claim | `batch_claim` | 413,318 | 3,220 |

Also newly captured (harvested by the script but previously absent from the baseline):

| Contract | Entrypoint | CPU | Mem |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| callora-cold | `capabilities` | 11,385 | 104 |

**Moves greater than 5% vs. the old baseline:** none of the pre-existing keys (`callora-vault`, `callora-settlement`, `callora-revenue-pool`) changed — every new row above is a newly tracked entry, and the stale `callora-allowlist` rows were deleted. `callora-limits` still has no baseline entry; its rows were not written by the regeneration run, so the script treats its baseline as zero (it can never regress until it is seeded).

## Build repairs carried by the branch

These were needed to make the four test crates and the gas gate compile with the current tree:

- **yield limits (partially restored #1522 implementation):** `contracts/yield/src/limits.rs` referenced `read_window_ledgers`, `load_window_for_mutation`, `effective_window_state`, `read/write_window_state`, `read/write_window_limits`, `WindowLedgers`/`WindowLimits`/`WindowState` storage keys, and admin-gated `set_window_*` setters that did not exist. Restored the free functions, storage keys, TTL bumps, events, and auth checks; `contracts/yield/src/errors.rs` gains the matching error variant.
- **vault errors:** removed dead variants `InitialBalanceExceedsOnLedger` (17) and `PausedState` (37), and renumbered `TooManyIds` from 60 to 61 so it no longer collides with `Frozen = 60` (Soroban also caps a contract error enum at 50 cases).
- **settlement errors:** `PriceRegistryError` already used code 52/53 and `SettlementError` was at its 50-case limit, so `SystemFrozen` moved into a dedicated `FreezeError` enum at code 54. `check_not_frozen` now panics with that error, and `set_freeze_contract` takes `env`, requires auth, and returns `Result`.
- **refund:** restored `DEFAULT_DISPUTE_WINDOW_SECS = 604_800`, which existing rejection/dispute code already referenced but was never defined.
- **existing tests:** updated the vault `init` call in `contracts/limits/tests/auth_snap.rs` to the 9-argument signature, replaced the registry's removed `MockCatalog` registration with a plain catalog address, and updated vault/settlement error-code snapshots and `docs/ERROR_CODES.md` for the renumbering.
- **Cargo.lock:** regenerated by the workspace build.

## Verification

Run locally on this branch:

```text
cargo test -p callora-distribute -p callora-escrow -p callora-refund -p callora-batch-claim --no-run
  -> Finished successfully

cargo test -p callora-distribute -p callora-escrow -p callora-refund -p callora-batch-claim -- gas_snap --nocapture
  -> 9 passed, 0 failed
  -> emitted JSON lines match contracts/.gas-baseline.json exactly (values in the table above)

git diff --check
  -> clean
```

Not completed in this environment: the full `cargo test --workspace` run and a final no-flag `./scripts/gas-regression.sh`. Reviewers should let CI run the full gate; the measured rows above were reproduced directly from the test binaries.

## Notes for reviewers

- No workflow, build-output, binary, or `.vscode/` changes.
- The unrelated-looking yield/error-code edits are compile prerequisites, not gas optimizations; they are called out separately above so the gas change is easy to audit on its own (`scripts/gas-regression.sh`, the four new `tests/gas_snap.rs` files, and `contracts/.gas-baseline.json`).

On `main` (`0b0074e`), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` fails in `victory-gpu` on this machine (Windows 11, RX 6950 XT, Rust 1.98.1), with and without `--all-features`. Four lints (three of them were already there when I opened this; `shadow.rs` got the fourth since), none changing behaviour:

- `placed_filler_twins` (`resource.rs`) is read only by the diagnostics memory report (`copystat.rs`, which is built with the `diagnostics` feature only), so it was dead code without that feature: it is compiled with the feature now (`#[cfg(all(windows, feature = "diagnostics"))]`).
- `Rig::depth_written` (`indirect.rs`) is kept next to `depth_tested` but never read: renamed `_depth_written`, as the struct's other kept fields (`_kept`, `_target_heaps`) are.
- The scissor census in `draw.rs` sorts with `sort_unstable_by_key(|r| Reverse(r.1))` instead of `sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1))`.
- `shadow.rs` (the own-view write census): `n % 16384 == 0` is `n.is_multiple_of(16384)`.

**Checks:** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and the same with `--all-features`: clean. `cargo test --workspace --locked`: the crates before `victory-gpu` pass; in `victory-gpu` the library's tests pass apart from the intermittent failures that `main` has (the budget test, see #849; the crash of the test binary, see #850). author: sizumita
body:
Refs #513

## Root cause

Four sub-causes of the exec "type mismatch in interp conversion" family share one shape: a value's representation in the model legitimately differs from the declared type of the place it is compared against or stored into, and the comparison/write had no bridge between the two representations.

1. **`trait-upcasting/struct`** — comparing `*b` (`Rc<dyn Foo>`) against an `i32` reached `values_equal`'s `DynRef` arm with the Rc *handle aggregate* as the pointee (`Enum{0,[NonNull-wrapper, PhantomData, allocator]}`). The pointee does not live in the handle: it is field 2 of the `RcInner`/`ArcInner` aggregate ({strong, weak, value}) in the shared allocation.
2. **`osstring-str-equality`** — the `OsString` value is three nested variant-0 single-field wrappers around the byte list (`OsString` → `Buf` → `Vec<u8>` element form), one level deeper than `string_from_element_form` descended, so no string denotation was found.
3. **`type-ascription`** — a `Vec<u8>` in element form (its fields ARE the elements) compared against a byte-array literal (`Bytes`) matched no arm: the existing holder arm only covers a single-field ADT holding a `Tuple`/`Bytes`.
4. **`enum-clike-ffi-as-int`** — a fieldless enum returned through a transmuted function pointer is written into a `u32` destination place; `normalize_for_ty` saw `Enum{variant:1, fields:[]}` against `Uint(U32)` and errored. The discriminant (23) lives in the callee return type's table, which no runtime structure carried.

## Fix

- `dyn_pointee`: when the store-verified `rc_inner_id` identifies the base as an Rc/Arc handle, the pointee is field 2 of the allocation's `RcInner`/`ArcInner` aggregate. A `Box` handle has the same shape but its allocation holds the value itself, so the store check is the deciding evidence and Box behavior is unchanged.
- `string_from_element_form`: descend through nested single-field variant-0 wrappers to the element list. A byte vector's element list cannot itself consist of one aggregate, so a lone aggregate field is a wrapper, not an element; the per-element byte/UTF-8 evidence standard is unchanged.
- `values_equal`: new arm — a variant-0 ADT whose fields are all byte-valued (each possibly in a `MaybeUninit` one-field wrapper, via the new `element_form_byte` helper) against `Bytes` compares as the byte sequence the field list denotes.
- Return boundary: conversion bakes the return type's discriminant table into a new `ir::Body::return_discriminants` field (only when the return type is an enum whose variants are all fieldless, from the definition's shape + discriminant table). `exec_return` converts a fieldless-enum return value to its discriminant scalar when the destination place's declared type is an integer — the same boundary where the Vec real-form translation already happens.

All mechanisms are general (no per-test special cases). `values_cmp` was checked: it has no `DynRef` arm and no failing record names it, so it is untouched.

## Verification

- New driver regression tests (`crates/sparagmos-driver/tests/driver_value_equality.rs`, 4 tests, incl. negative controls and a negative-discriminant `repr(i32)` case): **all 4 fail on unmodified main, all 4 pass with this change** (verified by stash/rebuild both ways).
- `verify-gk3`: workspace **734 passed / 0 failed** (735 listed, 1 ignored), driver **1105 passed / 0 failed** (1105 listed; includes the 4 new tests). Recounted from raw `test result` lines and reconciled with `--list`.
- Subset before/after (13 records: the 5 named cluster records + 8 exec sanity records around dyn/Rc/String/Vec machinery; `--stages all`, measurement discipline, base binary vs fixed binary): **gain 4, loss 0**.
  - `tests/ui/traits/trait-upcasting/struct.rs`: unsupported → pass
  - `tests/ui/typeck/osstring-str-equality.rs`: unsupported → pass
  - `tests/ui/type/type-ascription.rs`: unsupported → pass
  - `tests/ui/enum/enum-clike-ffi-as-int.rs`: unsupported → pass
  - 7 sanity records pass → pass; `tests/ui/dst/dst-coerce-rc.rs` unsupported → unsupported (pre-existing, different cause: `RefCell::borrow` through a dyn reference).

## What remains (evidence on #513)

- **`enum-univariant-repr`** still fails: slice equality after `transmute(&[Univariant])` → `&[i32]`. The pair is `Enum{variant:0, fields:[]}` vs `Int(17)`. The slice's base is a `RefTarget::Value` constant aggregate — the storage element type is erased at the target, and every consumer site (builtin `generic_args` = the *reading* type `[i32]`, the FatRef, the resolved refs) carries only the reading side's type. The discriminant (17 for variant 0) is unrecoverable there; fixing this needs the constant/slice target to carry its element type, a conversion-side change. A direct element read (`ints[0]`) separately fails in `normalize_for_ty` ("expected Int(I32), found ADT value") — the same missing storage type on the read path.
- **`std/issue-3563-3`** does not share this mechanism (re-triaged): the failing write carries `Enum{0,[Uint(46),Uint(46),Uint(46)]}` (a 3-element aggregate) into a `Uint(U32)` place — a write-navigation defect, not a fieldless-enum discriminant.

author: jevonscode
body:
## What
Copy verified owner projects into the paired host and label locally served content with its source and last successful sync. The directory can include unavailable projects. Internal task selection, judgment and dreaming only receive locally actionable projects. The host reads profiles, operation receipts, history and Jefa's board at the owner. Conditional profile writes preserve the operation ID when the answer is lost.

The owner installs a verified permit before opening its project gate. A matching live permit and gate are both required for business actions. The host initializes a replica gate for every project it copies. Ordinary local captures and scoped journal writes continue while it holds an open replica. Inputs with unresolved effects still require the whole-space guard. PR #1129 supplies cross-store restore and native task protection and must land first.

## Why
A recent copy remains readable while its owner sleeps. A stale edit, an unknown delivery result and an unavailable board each require a different response. A directory entry must not make a remote project eligible for local work.

## Verification
Local tests cover directory filtering, forwarded console rejection, live owner and receipt HTTP responses, idempotent permit installation, stale permits and TLS delivery of history reads and updates. The disposable graph test checks capture on the host, rejection of writes to the replica, and unchanged copied records after a rejected import. CI runs the actual Provider and the platform suites on each submitted revision.

## Skills
Skills: N/A for this staged change. The final rollout updates operating-fuli with the owner-only live board, offline behavior and the human move workflow before these features are enabled.

## Before enabling project copies
#1130 owns the remaining write admission work for agent hiring, naming and executors, conversation triage, tags, scope edits, hard deletion, duplicate and preference maintenance, attention, worker runs, workflow observations, occupations and project memory usage. Whole-space writes while holding an open replica return `project_write_requires_owner_scope`. The rollout must verify local writes and reject copied targets in a real graph before enabling project copies. A project claimed by this host remains visible to task discovery during a naming conflict.

author: stonepower
body: ## Résumé Import des pages éditoriales de l'ancien site, à partir du kit déposé sur `stonepower-patch-2` (déplacé dans `reference/contenus-kit/`). - **34 pages** créées à leur `nouvelle_url` (`pages.json`, hors statuts « non reprise » / « redirection seule »), avec `SiteHeader`, `SiteFooter`, le carrousel, un `FilAriane` construit d'après la rubrique et le `h1` de `pages.json`. Le gabarit suit la capture `page-contenu-bureau.jpg`. Sur `/office-notarial/`, on retrouve la barre de sections et l'alternance gris/blanc. La page garde un seul `h1` : les titres de section du kit sont décalés d'un niveau. - **Les textes ne sont pas réécrits.** Au build, `src/lib/contenu.ts` fait seulement ceci : - remplacer les images par leur WebP, d'après une liste blanche ; - retirer toutes les autres images, donc **toutes les photos de l'équipe** ; - afficher l'équipe en liste « nom + fonction » ; - retirer les liens neutralisés du panier (`Ma sélection`, `Alerte mail`) ; - encoder l'espace de `juillet 2010.pdf` dans le lien ; - poser les cibles des ancres du lexique (`#A`…`#T`, absentes du kit). - **PDF** : les 58 fichiers sont déplacés (pas copiés) dans `public/documents/` et servis comme assets statiques. - **Images** : `etude_*` et `predecesseurs` (une façade, sans personne) sont converties en WebP dans `/images/contenu/` par `scripts/optimize-images.mjs`. Les originaux restent dans `reference/`. - **Correction du kit** : 4 caractères mal encodés dans `contact__plans-acces-horaires.html` (« T?l. » → « Tél. », « GR?OUX » → « GRÉOUX »). C'est le seul changement apporté au HTML source, et il est signalé dans le README du kit. ## Choix : prérendu statique (contenu Astro), pas de collection EmDash/D1 Les pages sont **prérendues au build** (`export const prerender = true`) à partir du HTML du kit. Elles sont servies comme **assets statiques** du Worker. Conséquences : - aucun contenu ni code de page dans le bundle du Worker ; - **aucun CPU ni requête D1 par requête** : important sur le plan gratuit (10 ms de CPU) ; - pas de back-office pour l'instant, donc rien à gagner à passer par une collection EmDash. On pourra migrer vers une collection le jour où un back-office sera ouvert. **Taille du Worker (gzip, `wrangler deploy --dry-run`) : 2402,65 KiB avant → 2410,81 KiB après** (+8 KiB : `urls.csv`, redirections, métadonnées du sitemap). C'est identique en staging et en production. ### Point technique : EmDash pendant le prérendu Le middleware d'EmDash s'exécute aussi pendant le prérendu. Il tourne alors sur la D1 **locale, vide et éphémère** du worker de build. En mode `check`, il écrivait la page 503 « Database migrations are required » à la place du contenu. `astro.config.mjs` force donc `EMDASH_MIGRATIONS_MODE = "auto"` **dans l'environnement Vite `prerender` uniquement**. Seule la D1 locale du build est migrée, rien de distant. Le Worker déployé reste en `check`. `tests/worker.test.mjs` le vérifie à chaque build : le bundle ne doit lire que `process.env`. ### Indexation (staging) Les assets statiques ne passent pas par le middleware `gate.ts`. Hors production, le noindex est donc assuré par deux mécanismes : - une meta `robots noindex` dans `Base.astro` (`SITE_ENV` est connu au build) ; - un `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` ajouté au `_headers` par une petite intégration. Il couvre aussi les PDF et les images. En production, ni l'une ni l'autre n'est présente (vérifié sur le build `production`). La page `/_design/` ne gêne pas : elle reste en place et en noindex. ## Menu, plan du site, sitemap - **Menu** (`src/data/site.ts`) : c'est le menu visible de l'ancien site. Les sous-entrées de « L'office notarial » pointent maintenant vers les pages séparées, comme avant ; « Historique » pointe vers `/office-notarial/#historique`. - **Pages hors menu**, comme sur l'ancien site : Situation géographique, Liste des coordonnées et Plans d'accès. Les 4 pages `/conseils/*` restent aussi hors menu, en attente de validation par l'étude. - **`/plan-du-site/`** (prérendu) liste toutes les pages, et un lien « Plan du site » est ajouté au pied de page. - **`/sitemap.xml`** remplace celui d'EmDash, qui ne listait que ses collections, vides ici. Il ne fait aucun accès à la D1. - Le lien « Les divers Droits » du pied de page pointe maintenant vers `/informations-juridiques/`. - Les liens vers `/annonces/`, `/contact/` et `/simulateur-pret/` répondent **404** pour l'instant, comme attendu. ## Redirections 301 Elles sont faites dans `src/middleware/gate.ts`, avant EmDash (pas de D1), d'après `reference/contenus-kit/urls.csv`. Seuls les chemins en `.php`, `.html` ou `.htm` sont examinés. - `product_info.php?products_id=N` et `-p-N.html` vont vers la page correspondante. Un id inconnu est une annonce et va vers `/annonces/` (règle générique du CSV). - `index.php?cPath=N` (y compris imbriqué, comme `16_18`) et `-c-N.html` vont vers la rubrique. `index.php` sans paramètre va vers `/`, comme `cPath=0`. - `allprods.php`, `CalcAmortEuR2.htm`, `simulateur-c-14.html` et `contact_us.php` (quel que soit le query string) suivent le CSV. Je n'ai inventé aucune destination. Un `cPath` inconnu reste en 404. ## Vérifications - `npm run typecheck` : 0 erreur. - `CLOUDFLARE_ENV=staging|production npm run build` et `wrangler deploy --dry-run` : OK. - `npm test` : 80 tests réussis. Le nouveau step `Tests` de `ci.yml` les lance sur le build staging. Ils couvrent : - chaque `nouvelle_url` reprise produit une page avec un seul `h1`, identique à `pages.json` ; - aucune image hors liste blanche ; - les ancres et les liens internes résolus ; - les redirections ; - le contenu absent du Worker ; - le mode de migration non forcé dans le Worker. - `wrangler dev --env staging` en local : - pages et PDF en 200 avec `X-Robots-Tag` ; - anciennes URL en 301 ; - `/annonces/`, chemins inconnus et `/_emdash/admin/` en 404. Aucune modification des workflows de déploiement, des secrets ni des migrations. Le déploiement staging se fera par la CI existante après le merge. Autres changements : - `FilAriane` : une rubrique sans page (par exemple « Droit de la famille ») s'affiche sans lien et sans `aria-current`. - Correction d'un sélecteur cassé dans `global.css` (`amain:focus`) : le soulignement des liens au survol est rétabli. ## Points à valider avec l'étude (repris du README du kit) 1. **L'équipe** (`/office-notarial/equipe/` et la section « L'équipe » de `/office-notarial/`) : les deux listes ne concordent pas. Il faut demander à l'étude la liste à jour, et son accord pour publier des photos. Les photos ne sont pas dans le kit ; en attendant, seuls les noms et fonctions sont affichés. 2. **Liste des coordonnées** (`/contact/coordonnees/`) : le contenu est périmé (il cite d'anciens collaborateurs). Les e-mails nominatifs y sont anonymisés en `prenom.nom＠notaires.fr`. Il faut une liste à jour. 3. **Tarifs** : ce sont des tarifs réglementés, à faire relire. 4. **Mentions légales** : l'hébergeur doit être mis à jour (Cloudflare) et une politique de confidentialité ajoutée (formulaire de contact). 5. **Pages orphelines** : « Mon entreprise », « Mon patrimoine », « Mon logement » et « Ma famille » (`/conseils/*`) ne sont dans aucun menu, alors que ce sont les textes les plus longs. Il faut décider si on les ajoute au menu. 6. **Doublons** : `/office-notarial/` regroupe Historique, Fonctions, Profession, Équipe, Lexique, Tarifs et Prédécesseurs, qui existent aussi en pages séparées. On garde les deux pour l'instant, comme sur l'ancien site. Plus tard : URL canonique ou fusion. 7. **Textes anciens** : plusieurs textes juridiques datent des années 2010. Une relecture éditoriale est recommandée. Autres remarques : - La page « Plans d'accès » contient des liens « Agrandir le plan » vers Google Maps, repris tels quels. Ce sont des liens sortants : rien n'est intégré et il n'y a aucun traceur. - Le build affiche « Unable to fetch the `Request.cf` object » pendant

body:
Round 3 slice r3-server-tools (v0.1.3).

Audit: `D:/tuffcode/.tuffcode-ops/audits/r3-server-tools.md` (gitignored, not committed).

## What landed

- `mcp/client.ts`: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio client with `initialize` (protocol 2024-11-05 plus `notifications/initialized`), `tools/list`, `tools/call`, a 10s per-request timeout, 64 KiB result cap, stderr suffix on failures, and a structural `spawnFn` seam so unit tests never spawn a real child.
- `mcp/service.ts`: server CRUD, a never-throwing `test`, a 60s `tools/list` cache cleared on upsert/remove/test, and a disabled-server refusal for `callTool`.
- `mcp/rpc.ts`: `registerMcpRpc(register, service)` for `mcp.list`, `mcp.upsert`, `mcp.remove`, `mcp.test`.
- `tools/extra.ts`: `createExtraTools(deps)` returning the `ExtraToolRunner` seam for `mcp` (list/call), `memory` (search/add with cwd-derived project scope) and `config` (provider.add, provider.model.add, mcp.add, settings.set with the D48 allowlist). Every failure returns a short string.
- `brain/service.ts`: the D49 kill switch now returns an empty slice, no injected ids and zero tokens including the always block; the assembly carries a `reasons` map for prompt preview.
- `brain/rules.ts`: `captureStandingRules` detects `always remember`, `from now on`, `never use`, `always use`, stores one rule per sentence, dedupes against active normalized rules, and derives the project from a thread id.
- `brain/handlers.ts`: `brain.link` stores typed edges and rejects missing ids and self links.

## Verification

```
pnpm --filter @tuffcode/server exec vitest run mcp tools/extra brain
Test Files  12 passed (12)
     Tests  94 passed (94)
```

```
pnpm --filter @tuffcode/server typecheck
(no diagnostics)
```

Full `pnpm check`, full `pnpm test`, lint and formatters were not run, per the shared brief.

## Glue dependencies (not wired here)

- Call `registerMcpRpc(register, service)` from `rpc.ts` with `createMcpService(repos)`.
- Call `createExtraTools({ repos, settings, providers, mcp, brain })` where `brain.search` is `searchMemory(store, input)` and `brain.add` is `store.upsert`.
- Call `captureStandingRules(repos, { text, projectId, threadId })` on the send path.
- `brain.link` is already registered by `createBrainRpcHandlers`.

author: ksycz
body:
## Summary

Roadmap item "End-to-end tests". Builds on #17 (the transfer page).

```text
e2e/transfer-day.e2e.ts            one new customer per test, so tests never share a day total
  RISK-TL-BOUNDARY   €3,000 + €2,000 → both sent, "Left today: €0.00"
  RISK-TL-PARTIAL    €4,999.99, then €0.02 → not sent, €0.01 left; then €0.01 → sent
  RISK-TL-INVALID    one test each for 0, -5, 12.345 → not sent, the typed text stays, nothing used
  RISK-TL-REMAINING  €1,250.50, reload → "Left today: €3,749.50"
```

```diff
 Stage 1 · Fast ─┬─ Stage 2 · Evidence ──────┬─ gate · can this PR merge?
                 ├─ Stage 3 · Smoke ─────────┤
+                └─ Stage 4 · End to end ────┘   installs Chromium, then npm run e2e
```

- `playwright.config.ts` has two projects: `smoke` (no browser) and `e2e` (Desktop Chrome). `fullyParallel`, because every test has its own customer.
- **When a test fails in CI:** each failed test keeps a trace (steps, page, network, console), and the run uploads the HTML report and traces as the artifact `e2e-report-and-traces` for 14 days. `actions/upload-artifact` is pinned to a commit SHA.
- **`eslint-plugin-playwright`** (recommended rules) on `e2e/` and `smoke/`. It fails lint on an assertion without `await`, which never runs and so always passes.
- Locators are all user-facing: label, role or visible text.
- `npm run e2e` shows **SKIP** with the install command if Chromium isn't installed locally. In CI it always runs.
- The Summary page gets a Stage 4 row and lists each end-to-end test.
- ROADMAP Later: accessibility checks with axe, and Firefox and WebKit.

Kept on purpose: `retries: 0` (a test that passes on retry is a flake to fix, not a pass) and Chromium only (speed; one line per browser to add later).

## Evidence

- `npm run gates`: 10 of 11 pass, mutation 97.81%, smoke 4 passed, **end to end 6 passed** in parallel. PR size warns because #17's lines counted while it was open.
- **Broken page:** "Left today" stops updating → `npm run e2e`: 2 failed (BOUNDARY, PARTIAL). **Real page:** all pass.
- **Missing await:** dropping one `await` → `npm run lint`: `'toHaveText' must be awaited or returned (playwright/missing-playwright-await)`.
- **Trace on failure:** a forced failure leaves `test-results/<test>/trace.zip` and `playwright-report/index.html`, the two folders the upload step keeps.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** CI time. Stage 4 downloads Chromium (about a minute), in parallel with Stages 2 and 3.

author: tr-evo
body:
`recap push --only betrieb/…` on the Schwärzwerk docs moved the chapter from third place to the top of the live sidebar. Article positions collided too. The sync route set `order` from the array position in the payload, and a scoped payload only holds the selection. `recap diff` does not report order, so nothing flagged it.

Server (`app/api/v1/projects/[slug]/sync/route.ts`):
- Accepts an optional `order` on chapters and articles (non-negative integer, otherwise 422 before any write).
- Without it, a full mirror still uses the array position.
- With `prune: false`, existing rows keep their stored order. New rows, and articles moved in from another chapter, are appended. This also fixes the already published CLI 0.5.1 without an upgrade.

CLI (`packages/cli/src/sync/payload.ts`): every item carries its position in the full manifest, also on a scoped push.

Behavior change: with CLI 0.5.1, a full `push --no-prune` no longer reorders existing items. The new CLI does, because it sends `order`.

Tests: 5 for the route, 3 for the payload; 7 of the 8 failed before the fix, the eighth pins the existing full-mirror behavior. `vitest` 298 passed (app) and 93 passed (CLI), `tsc --noEmit` clean for both, ESLint clean on the changed route and its test. Not run end to end against a real database.

Rollout: the server part needs a deploy, the CLI part an npm release (no version bump in this PR).

author: michaeljgrimm
body:
FR-09 of the [format-requests program](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/format-requests/burndown.md): a variable's declaration can say how much room it has.

## What changes

- **Schema.** A text variable takes `maxLength` and `maxLines`; a list variable takes `maxItems`. Each is an integer of at least 1. A limit on another kind of variable is a schema error.
- **Core.** `maxLength` counts characters as a reader sees them (grapheme clusters, `Intl.Segmenter`), exported as `visibleLength`. The new warning `opf/variable-overflow` reports `maxLength` and `maxItems` once at the declaration, and `maxLines` at each place the variable is drawn, from composition, naming the slide. `fill` and `resolveVariables` return the same overflow as a `variable-overflow` diagnostic.
- **CLI.** `opf fill` reports an overflow per record on stderr and in `fill.overflow` of its report before anything is written. The decks are still written, because the finding is a warning.
- **Editor.** `listTemplateFields` carries the limits and the Fill template panel shows the count ("12 of 48 characters").
- **MCP.** No code change: a model reads the limits from the schema, the docs page, the template's own declaration and `validate_deck`. One test covers the four.

MLM well-formedness checker (slice S2, increment 1)

## Summary
Adds a pure well-formedness checker for deep models in `src/model/mlm/checker/`. It implements Tasks 7a and 7–11 of plan `2026-11-17-increment-1`. The checker reads a `DeepModel` and returns sorted records (`rule`, `severity`, `element`, `related`, `message`). It does not touch Redux, the D/L layers or the canvas. The UI is wired to it in a later slice.

## What is included
- **Infrastructure:** record types and message templates (`records.ts`), a rule registry (`registry.ts`) and `runChecker(model, {increment?, only?})`. The runner builds the deep index once, gives a deterministic record order and lists the rules it did not evaluate.
- **Level rules WF-1 to WF-3:** each element is a member of exactly one level, each level has exactly one Model type (no typing cycles), and level numbering and range are correct.
- **Typing rules WF-4 to WF-8:** class match, the type is on a level above (default and range variants, and dangling type ids are reported), no instance of a potency-0 type, no direct instance of an abstract clabject, and multiple typing only with `isMultiType`.
- **Potency rules WF-9 to WF-11 and WF-18:** a stored potency is all-or-none, an instance's potency fits its type's, reach stays within the level's reach, and a warning when a feature's reach exceeds its owner's.
- **Field rules WF-12 to WF-17:** missing slot values, values on fields with potency ≥ 1, and data-type validation (WF-14). WF-14 derives the data type through the type-field chain and has a `noType` variant. The rules also report missing required fields, fields typed outside the owner's types, shared type fields and duplicate names.
- **S1 carry-over (7a):** tests for supers and types cycles and for delete order. `plannedFields` is extracted from `planInstantiate` and exported (S1 behaviour unchanged).
- **Fixtures and tests:** `scaleModel(n)` builds a large model for timing. The BC1 acceptance tests cover FR-8.2 and FR-8.3 and the registry. 193/193 MLM tests pass.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/release.yml`:

- `workflow_dispatch` takes a `tag` input. A manual run starts on `main`, so the fixed workflow file runs. Both jobs check out the tag. The tag must match `vX.Y.Z`.
- The release step keeps an existing release and replaces only the `.mcpb` file (`gh release upload --clobber`).
- A new step waits up to 5 minutes until npm shows the version, then the registry publish runs.

`docs/design.md` §13: the recovery note describes the manual run.

## Why

The 0.2.1 run published to npm with provenance. The registry step ran 9 seconds later, and npm did not show 0.2.1 yet (it took about 60 seconds), so the registry refused it. A re-run of the failed job would stop at `gh release create`, because the release exists. With this change, we finish 0.2.1 without deleting the release:

```
gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f tag=v0.2.1
```

author: zhezhe-agent
body:
This is by an automated agent, not a human.

## 问题

`POST /api/posts` 的图片 AI 审核是 `for...of` 串行 `await moderateImage(...)`。单张图片超时 30s、失败重试 2 次（退避 1s+2s），单张最坏约 93s；`MAX_IMAGES = 9`，因此在 vision 接口缓慢时，多图投稿最坏要等约 14 分钟才响应，前端长时间转圈，并可能诱发重复投稿。

Closes #19

## 改动

- `src/lib/ai-moderation.ts`
  - 新增 `moderateImages(images)`：固定并发上限（默认 3，`OPENAI_IMAGE_CONCURRENCY`）的并行审核，9 张图耗时从逐张累加降为约等于最慢一张，同时不会一次打满 vision 接口。
  - 任一张返回 `rejected` 后不再启动排队中的图片，尽快把拒绝结果返回给调用方；未启动位置返回 `undefined`，与入参顺序一一对应。
  - `withRetry` 增加可选 `retries` 参数；图片审核走独立的 `OPENAI_VISION_RETRIES`，**默认 0**，单张超时/接口失败直接降级为 `error` 进 pending 人工复审，不再退避重试拖满 3 次。文本审核重试策略保持不变。
- `src/app/api/posts/route.ts`：图片审核由串行循环改为调用 `moderateImages`，原有判定聚合逻辑（`rejected` 打回、`uncertain`/`error` 进 pending）保持不变。
- `.env.example`：补充 `OPENAI_VISION_TIMEOUT_MS` / `OPENAI_VISION_RETRIES` / `OPENAI_IMAGE_CONCURRENCY`。

## 效果

- 9 张图在接口正常时：由 9 次串行调用变为 3 批并发，耗时约 1/3。
- 单张接口超时/失败：最坏 30s 后即降级为 `error` 进人工复审（原为 30s×3 + 3s 退避 ≈ 93s）。
- 9 张图在接口超时/失败时：等待约 3 批 × 30s ≈ 90s 即可返回并进人工复审（默认重试 0）；改动前为 9 × 93s ≈ 14 分钟。

## 验证

- `npx tsc --noEmit`：通过
- `npm run lint`（变更文件）：通过；仓库其余文件的既有 lint 错误/警告与本次改动无关
- `npm run build`：通过
- 一次性验证脚本（mock `fetch`，未入库）确认：
  - 并发峰值恰为 3，不超上限；结果顺序与入参索引对应
  - 任一张 `rejected` 后不再启动后续图片
  - 图片失败时只发起 1 次请求（无重试），直接返回 `error`
  - 文本审核仍按 `OPENAI_MODERATION_RETRIES=2` 发起 3 次请求（行为未变）
  - 空图片列表返回空数组

## 行为与限制

- 默认并发 3 是为避免瞬时打满上游 vision 接口；可通过 `OPENAI_IMAGE_CONCURRENCY`（1–9）调整。
- 图片审核默认 `OPENAI_VISION_RETRIES=0` 是本次「快速降级」的取舍：偶发抖动会更多进入人工复审；如需提高自动化率可显式调大。
- 未实现「先返回 pending、后台异步审核」（issue 中标注为可选项），本次仍是同步审核，但最坏等待已从约 14 分钟降到约 1 批图片耗时。

## webserv — HTTP/1.1 server in C++98

Serveur HTTP/1.1 inspiré NGINX, en C++98 strict (flags: -std=c++98 -Wall -Wextra -Werror).

### Fonctionnalités
- 1 boucle d'événements select() — multiples clients simultanés, sockets non-bloquants, pas de thread par connexion
- Config NGINX-style : server/location, listen, root/alias, index, error_page, client_max_body_size, allow_methods/limit_except, autoindex, cgi/cgi_pass/cgi_ext, upload_store, return — routage par préfixe le plus long
- Méthodes : GET, POST, DELETE, HEAD
- Fichiers statiques (MIME, streaming), autoindex, pages erreurs, redirections (301), keep-alive
- CGI via fork() + pipes, env RFC 3875, multiples types (.py/.pl), timeout 504
- Uploads (multipart POST → 201, DELETE → 204, 413)

- Statuts : 200/201/204/301/400/404/405/413/500/501/502/504

author: zechengz
body:
A kit run could be reset and dropped, but not saved and brought back. Mirage's own workspaces have `snapshot`, `load` and `clone`; a kit run now has the same three, so an environment made of a workspace and its fakes can be saved, restored and forked whole.

- `GET /_kit/runs/<run>/snapshot` answers the run's world as one JSON document:
  - its SQLite file (`db`, base64), taken with `VACUUM INTO` on the run's own connection, so commits still in the `-wal` file are in
  - each tenant's clock, id counters, armed fault plans with how many requests each has served, and whether a reset seeded it
  - the fixture a bare `/reset` of the run reseeds from
  - the `service` and `schema` (the digest of the fake's Prisma schema) that can load it
- `POST /_kit/runs/<run>/load` with that document makes the run that world, replacing it or making it. The next id and timestamp it hands out are the ones the snapshotted run would have. A document is refused with 400 before the run is touched when:
  - it comes from another fake or schema
  - it names a fixture this fake does not have
  - its clock would stamp past the `Date` range
  - its `db` fails SQLite's `integrity_check`, run in a file of its own before the run is dropped
  - it does not parse, for example a fault plan on an undeclared route

  A load's body is bounded by the longest string Node holds, not by `maxBodyBytes`, so a run's own snapshot always loads back.
- `POST /_kit/runs/<run>/clone {"run": "<new>"}` loads the run's snapshot into a new run (201), which then diverges on a file of its own. An existing `<new>` is refused with 409, and an unknown `<run>` with 404.

Each waits on the run's request queue, as `/reset` and `DELETE` do, and a load fires the fake's `afterReset`. `/_kit/faults` now waits on that queue too, so a plan armed after a pending reset or load is armed on the run they leave. Under a `/_run/<run>` prefix the path must name the same run, as `DELETE`'s must.

Tests: a new section in the kit selftest (`pnpm run selftest`, in `integ-selftests`):
- a load restores the run, and the next card gets the id and timestamp it would have had
- a clone and its original diverge, each with its own fault plans
- a loaded run still refuses a tenant no reset seeded
- bad snapshots (truncated db, missing fixture, out-of-range clock) and clashing clones are refused, and leave the run as it was
- every load there is larger than the fake's `maxBodyBytes` (4096 in this test), and an API request past it still gets 413
- a plan armed while a load waits on the run fires on the loaded run
- `afterReset` fires on load

TypeScript only: the kit has no Python twin.

author: endynamoo
body:
**Found by the fresh install, not by the tests.** PR #153 shipped a card that could only say *"The stills setup script is missing from this installation"* — the installer does put `scripts\setup_engine.ps1` beside `Rhapsode.exe`, but `script_path()` looked under `config.APP_ROOT`, which in a frozen build is `_internal`. So `available` and `needed` were both false and the offer never appeared.

## What changed

- **`config.INSTALL_ROOT`** — beside the executable when frozen, the repository otherwise. `ASSET_ROOT` keeps its meaning (the packaged payload in `_internal`); things shipped next to the exe (`scripts/`, `licenses/`) use the new root.
- `enginesetup.script_path()` and the child's working directory use it.
- **`_adopt_profile()`** — when the script exits 0, the app saves and activates the profile itself. The script's last step imports `murmur` with the image interpreter, which only exists in a source checkout; in a packaged install that step fails silently and no `engine.json` is written.

## Verified

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` → **`Ran 445 tests in 36.123s` / `OK (skipped=4)`**, including a new test that a temp install root with `scripts/setup_engine.ps1` is found.
- The failing behaviour was reproduced first on the real artefact: `GET /api/engine` returned `"available": false, "reason": "The stills setup script is missing from this installation."` with `scripts/setup_engine.ps1` present in the install directory.

Rebuilt installer and a second clean run follow; the 5 GB setup itself is still to be exercised.

author: hacker-cb
body:
## What

`parseInZone` (public, and the path of every `Edm.DateTime` read from 1С) failed on years below 1000 with a raw `RangeError` — failing the whole collection read — rolled impossible values over (`2026-02-30` → `2026-03-02`, `24:00` → next day), and placed a wall-clock time a daylight-saving switch touches inconsistently: a skipped time moved **back** in `America/Sao_Paulo` but forward in `Europe/Berlin`; a time passed twice was the later instant in Berlin and the earlier in Sao Paulo. `formatInZone` wrote a year below 1000 without leading zeros (`999-05-01T…`) into filters, function-import arguments and written entities. The strict check lived only in MCP (`toDate` / `naiveInZone`).

Behaviour agreed with the coordinating session before building.

## Now

| case | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| year `0001`–`0999` (read) | raw `RangeError` | read correctly (incl. historic local mean time, e.g. Moscow +02:30:17) |
| year `0001`–`0999` (write, `formatInZone`) | `999-05-01T…` | `0999-05-01T…` |
| skipped time (clocks forward) | Sao Paulo: back an hour; Berlin: forward | forward by the gap, every zone (`Temporal`'s `'compatible'`) |
| time passed twice (clocks back) | Berlin: later; Sao Paulo: earlier | the earlier instant, every zone |
| `2026-02-30`, `24:00`, month `13`, year `0000`, not `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm[:ss[.fff]]` | rolled over / raw `RangeError` | `InvalidArgumentError` (a space for `T` still accepted) |
| unknown or missing zone | raw `RangeError` / host's zone | `InvalidArgumentError` |
| `formatInZone`: invalid `Date`, year outside 0001–9999 in the zone, past JS's range | garbage literal / raw `RangeError` | `InvalidArgumentError`; a `Date` from another realm (`node:vm`) is accepted |

New opt-in: `parseInZone(naive, zone, { disambiguation: 'reject' })` refuses a skipped time (a time passed twice is still the earlier instant — unlike `Temporal`'s `'reject'`). New public types `ParseInZoneOptions`, `ZoneDisambiguation`.

**Parser (`parser.ts`).** A field the schema types `Edm.DateTime` whose value names no real date-time — or is anything but a string or `null` — is a `ParseError` naming the field and the value (`dateMode: 'string'` still passes everything through). A field only the schema-less heuristic took for a date stays the string it came as. Only the exact empty date `0001-01-01T00:00:00` reads as `null` (any string starting with it did); that check still runs before `parseInZone`.

**MCP `register_query`.** Uses `disambiguation: 'reject'` instead of its own `naiveInZone`; a skipped naive time is still refused. A bare day whose midnight a switch skips starts at the switch itself (00:15 in `Asia/Kathmandu` 1986-01-01; still 01:00 in `America/Sao_Paulo` 2018-11-04) instead of always 01:00; a bare `periodTo` whose 23:59:59 is skipped ends at the day's last real second (`America/Nuuk` 2024-03-30); a day skipped whole, a year `0000`, and an offset period outside 0001–9999 in the server's zone are refused with `Invalid ISO date`. A naive year below 1000 is now read.

README: a paragraph on how daylight saving and impossible dates read.

## Checked against

- Live, read-only (BP 3.0 and Trade 11.5 test bases): no `Date` below year 1000 in `Document_РеализацияТоваровУслуг` / `Document_ПоступлениеТоваровУслуг` — the range is 1С's (`0001`–`9999`), so the read path must not crash on it, but none was seen.

## Testing

- `timezone.test.ts` — the year range both ways, every impossible value, minutes-only and space forms, unknown / missing / non-string zone, null options, message truncation, gaps (Sao Paulo, Berlin, Apia's skipped day), folds (Berlin, Sao Paulo, New York) under both modes, milliseconds across a gap, a `node:vm` `Date`, a wall-clock past JS's range.
- `parser.test.ts` — year 0202 in a typed field, empty date still `null` (typed and heuristic), exact-match empty date, a gap read forward, `ParseError` for an impossible typed date and a non-string one (and pass-through under `dateMode: 'string'`), heuristic non-date left as a string.
- `register-dates.test.ts` — year 0999, folds read earlier, Kathmandu day start, Nuuk day end, Apia skipped day (both ends), year 0000 bare / naive / via an offset.
- Project gates (runner): `biome ci`, `turbo typecheck`, `test:unit`, `test:integration:offline`, `test:e2e`, `package:lint`.
- Local review: Claude finders + Codex at the high rung, then a Codex reading of the fixes.

Changeset: `@1c-odata/client` **minor** with two `Breaking:` lines and the migration; `@1c-odata/mcp` **patch**.

Closes #193

## Scope
The user reported too many font sizes and weights. The trip page's ⋮ menu even mixed two styles: the screen's own items were Material's `labelLarge` (14sp medium), and the app's items were `bodyLarge` (16sp).

**Android** used 11 typography styles plus ad hoc weights. Now there are five:

| Style | Android | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | `titleLarge` | screen and card titles |
| Heading | `titleMedium` | sections, days, row titles |
| Body | `bodyLarge` | everything else; secondary lines are muted in colour, not smaller |
| Action | `labelLarge` (body size, medium weight) | every button and menu item |
| Badge | `labelSmall` | SHARED, CANCELLED and similar tags |

- New common rules **PRB-01–PRB-06** (pcall everywhere; `issecretvalue` before any operation and secrets recorded only
  as `secret`; no names or player GUIDs, `<player n>` / `<mob n>`; no network or CVar changes; run-time lookup of what
  the dump does not list; result format), the **context stamp** attached to every reading, and **P3b**: whether the
  client lets an addon *show* a secret value (`StatusBar:SetValue`, `FontString:SetText`) without reading it, which
  decides whether a display-only mode is an option if R2 bites.
- **`docs/spike/README.md`** (English): what `AzTw_Probe` is and why it is never distributed, the planned install
  (`tools/install_probe.py`, `tools/local.ini` from `tools/local.example.ini`, `<WoW folder>` only), the planned `/atwp`
  commands with the step that adds each, and the in-game procedure as a short table per context (solo, party, dungeon,
  raid, battleground).
- **SPEC-01 §2**: the dump puts `ShouldUnitThreatValuesBeSecret` / `ShouldUnitThreatStateBeSecret` in the `C_Secrets`
  namespace (not globals); the row now says so.

## Why

M0 exists to verify the threat APIs in the real client before any feature is promised (R1–R3, ADR 0004). M0.2–M0.6
need a precise target for each check, and M0.7 needs to know in advance what each verdict changes in the plan.

Findings from the dump worth noting for later steps: the second argument of the four threat functions is named
`mobGUID` but typed `UnitToken` (P2 tries both forms); `C_Secrets.HasSecretRestrictions()` tells whether the build uses
secrets at all; `Enum.AddOnRestrictionType`, `Enum.DamageMeterType` and `Enum.DamageMeterSessionType` are not
documented in the dump, so the probe enumerates them at run time.

## Not verified in the real client

command or procedure described here has been tried in game. No tests exist yet (the addon tests start in M1.3);

body:
## Summary Phase 3 trains and compares face-shape classifiers on **Kaggle niten19** (research use only, TD-14). It also prepares an **FFHQ subset for human labeling**, which has no labels yet because no annotators have been named. **Pipeline** (one command per step, seed 42): - `ml.datasets.build_features`: runs the Phase 2 pipeline on all 5,000 images. 2,977 pass the quality gates; the rejection reasons are reported. It also computes OpenCV Zoo **SFace** embeddings, used only to group images of the same person (average linkage at cosine 0.363, giving 250 groups). The embeddings stay local and are never logged. - `ml.training.train_face_shape`: compares the majority-class baseline, the Phase 2 rule baseline, rule prototypes fitted on train, RF, SVM, XGBoost and MLP. It holds out one identity-aware stratified fold as the test set (317 images) and tunes with identity-aware 5-fold CV on the remaining 2,660. Output: `metrics.json`, confusion matrices, feature box plots and the selected model (`ml/models/artifacts/*.joblib`, 68 KB). **Results from the run** (test macro-F1, 95% bootstrap CI): | Model | Test macro-F1 | |---|---| | Majority class | 0.066 | | Rule baseline (Phase 2) | 0.298 (0.243-0.346) | | Fitted rule prototypes | 0.389 (0.336-0.444) | | SVM | 0.447 (0.389-0.500) | | XGBoost | 0.476 (0.415-0.531) | | MLP (selected by CV) | 0.476 (0.417-0.530) | - The trained models are indistinguishable within CV noise. - 564 of the 586 images in niten19's own test split share a person with its train split, so that split is not used. - 46 identity groups contain one person labeled with more than one shape, which suggests label noise. There is no Diamond class and no male faces. The model's probabilities are uncalibrated. See `docs/model-card.md` and `research/results/phase3/kaggle_niten19/README.md`. **FFHQ prep (no labels):** - `ffhq_select` picks attribution or public-domain images, checked against NVIDIA's MD5s and the quality gates, and writes a license manifest. - `labeling_tool` builds an offline labeling page in Indonesian. - `agreement` computes Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa and keeps only consensus labels. - The annotator guide is in `docs/annotation-guide-id.md`. Decisions TD-21 to TD-24 are in `docs/technical-decisions.md`. ![Confusion matrices](research/results/phase3/kaggle_niten19/confusion_matrices.png) ---

body:
Ports ReiPan-PZ's gyro and over-the-shoulder walk changes to MikuPan, with release notes for **v0.1.4-over-shoulder** and **MikuPan PS5 v0.1.2**.

## Changes

- **Gyro Recenter Behavior** (Settings › Controls › Gyro, saved as `finder_gyro_recenter` under `[input]`). It controls the touchpad's right half while the Camera Obscura is up. Every option holds the gyro still while pressed so the controller can be re-gripped, then:
  - **Zero** (default): the view stays where it is.
  - **Level:** the view tips back to level.
  - **Level and back to start:** it also turns back to where Miku faced when she raised the camera.

  On PS5, Select is ignored while the right half is held, so the left half stays Select. The new strings are translated into German, Spanish, French and Italian.
- **DualSense gyro on PS5.** The PS5 controller driver now switches on the DualSense motion sensor and reports its gyro and touchpad fingers to SDL. This is the same driver change as ReiPan-PZ, so upstream's gyro aiming works on the console.
- **Over-the-shoulder walk after a camera cut.** Previously the old walk direction stuck until you let go of the stick. It now lets go when you steer the stick more than 50° away, and otherwise eases onto the over-the-shoulder camera's heading at 12° per tick.

## Testing

Builds for Linux (GCC Release) and PS5 (RelWithDebInfo). Not yet tested in-game.

## After merging

1. Run **Release** with version `0.1.4-over-shoulder`.
2. Run **PS5 Release** with `0.1.2`. The PS5 zip is built locally; attach it to the release.
