author: justyannicc
body:
## Problem

Basalt's upstream Executor pin is still `f69c6679` (2.0.0-beta.27). Every attempt to move it stalled: #1151 is about 2,400 commits behind main, conflicts in 25 files and edits a release layer main has deleted. Main's carries since then were never replayed on the newer pin.

## Change

This moves the pin to `2f4c398f3906e0570f0e25a16fa3602329baba29`, whose tree is identical to the release `executor@2.0.0-beta.38`. #1151's carries were reworked for this pin after it stalled, but that work was never pushed. This pull request is that work (547 carries) with today's main merged in, without rebasing, and the carries main added since.

- Every one of the 593 carries applies on the new pin, in order, exactly as preparation applies them.
- **Main's newer carries.** Nine carries that landed on main after that rework were cut against the old pin and are re-cut here: 0720, 0724, 0725, 0728, 0729, 0731, 0739, 0748, 0750. Each keeps its guarantee, shown by its own tests on the new tree:
  - 0725's check moves into the cloud auth core that carry 0098 creates.
  - 0724's cleanup retry reports a v2 job outcome.
  - 0750 keeps only its method names, because carry 0636 already shows the deferral sentence in the connect form.
  - 0748 keeps hosted step 24 under its id and name.
  - Carries that landed later are re-cut too: in 0782 and 0794 only the context moved. #2007's change to 0451 is carried onto the sync's version of 0451.
  - Carries 0778 and 0799 (#2048) apply unchanged. 0778's new custom endpoint provider app is regenerated on framework `.16`, like every other catalog app.
  - #2014's membership mirror test was written on the old pin, and its fixture built the app link table without v2's `linked_by` column. The fixture now builds that table as the sync's other membership fixtures do. Carry 0789 is unchanged.
- **Retired carries.** 0035, 0039 and 0050 retire because upstream merged them (#2439, #2453, #2462). 0714 retires because v2 navigation starts hosted pages from Organization settings. 0036 stays: upstream's #2446 covers three of its four files, and the remaining part keeps redacted native logs on Workers that export directly to Sentry or have no trace destination.
- **Fixes made after #1151.** The account check's partial notice now renders from the HTTP results (0643). The fixture fixes for tool availability, protocol 17 and the no-write connect proof come across. The protocol 18 scenario now asserts the deploy-time refusal: no approved framework release speaks protocol 18 (the registry holds 17, 25, 34, 39–41, 43 and 44) and deploy admission refuses any other, so no retained protocol 18 bundle can exist.
- **Accounts re-reading fix.** New carry 0787 fixes the Accounts directory never reading again after a missed change hint on v2: it kept showing stale accounts and never said it couldn't confirm them. Its three new tests fail without it and pass with it.
- **Carried catalog apps.** These pin framework `.16`. The Gmail and Google review digests move only because the served framework pin moves.
- **CI and records.** CI's new host-managed actions job gets v2's collector Bun. The migration list records hosted step 24. 0378, which patches Alchemy's Worker bridge, joins the dependency registry with its upstream issue (alchemy-run/alchemy#3780). 0138 leaves it: v2's Better Auth 1.7.16 passes all five security boundaries without its patch.

## Lint

The sync's own files had 55 owned-lint and Effect findings. All are fixed, with no baseline entry, disable comment or cast:

- Decodes go through `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect`, and error types are the real ones.
- Proofs that need PostgreSQL fail without `MIGRATION_TEST_ADMIN_URL` instead of skipping.
- The pool readiness proof uses the real `pg` client against that database.
- The six proofs that read the built framework are now `*.build-proof.ts`. Only `scripts/build.ts` runs them, after it builds what they read. Before, they skipped everywhere else.
- The catalog preview test passes its published feed inline, the seam every other catalog test uses.

The retained-release proof is deleted. It compiled independently rebuilt framework releases .14 and .15 to check that they reload unchanged through both retained formats, but no job builds those packages, so it never ran; retained serving at release time stays covered by the build's `closed-retained-serving` proof.

## Guardrails

The Guardrails "ship alone" check is red on this pull request, as expected: it wants changes to how releases are made to ship without product changes. But a pin move can't ship its re-cut Alchemy carries (0170, 0378, 0677, 0696, 0707, 0726, 0740) or the framework registry's `.16` ahead of itself, because those only apply on the new pin.

## Migrations

- The hosted step list is unchanged: steps 1–24, with step 22 explicit. A database that already recorded 24 is left alone, with the same row and the same function body.
- Upstream's Cloud steps 8–13 run as 14–19, after Basalt's 1–10. All six only create tables and an index, or add nullable columns.
- Executor storage stays at 4.0.30. The storage gate refuses an existing database below 4.0.29 before any DDL.
- `scripts/upstream-tests/migration-journals.json` lists every step in release order. The storage gate and Cloud bridge proofs now read their expectations from it.
- Proven on a local PostgreSQL 17.7 database built by main's own migration command, plus its change journal activation:
  - the sync's migration leaves the hosted journal row for row;
  - it records exactly Cloud 14–19 after main's 1–10;
  - a second run leaves the catalog fingerprint identical;
  - a run killed inside the first bridged Cloud step commits nothing, and its retry completes.

## Revoked native grants

No path lets a revoked native grant be used. The native grant code is the same as on main, and so are its two short windows:

- **Model requests through the pool:** an answer to an access check is reused for at most 3 seconds in each isolate. The isolate that made the revoke forgets it at once.
- **Tools-only devices revoked at the pool:** they keep tool access until the tools host's every-minute reconcile pass ends their grant, up to about 10 minutes. #1960 tracks making that immediate.

## What a release changes on production

Expected plan rows (a plan-only run on this head shows them):

- Every hosted Worker updates to the new upstream code with these carries.
- The only binding changes are a new plain `EXECUTOR_TELEMETRY_VERSION` on each Worker that exports telemetry, and `EXECUTOR_APPS_VERSION` on AppCompiler, from `.15` to `.16`. The `EXECUTOR_TELEMETRY` secret stays byte-equal (carry 0751).
- The migration command runs Cloud steps 14–19 once. Nothing else in any database changes.
- The pool's root container application does not change: nothing under `containers/` or `src/pool` changes.
- Only fix-forward after the Cloud steps record. A rollback across this release needs AppCompiler forced, because `EXECUTOR_APPS_VERSION` is secret text.

## Verification

- Every carry replays cleanly on the pin: 593 of 593, through preparation's own replay.
- Each re-cut carry's own tests pass on the new tree, as do 0787's three tests, which fail without it, and the tests #2014 added for 0789 and 0794.
- A migration proof on a local PostgreSQL 17.7 starts from a database built by main's own migration command and journal activation. It shows journals equal to the list, no change from a second run, and a killed run that commits nothing and then completes on retry. The storage-gate proofs (7) also pass.
- Local: typecheck, the production build and `check:startup` (every Worker within its startup budget), `check:upstream` with PostgreSQL, the fast lane's steps, fitness (157).
- On a Linux machine: owned unit suite, typecheck, style and lint, architecture and fitness.
- To read in this pull request's full Check: the pool-inventory job's scoped-change proof, which shows the Accounts view recovering after a missed hint end

author: claston
body:
## Summary

- Reject retired deterministic user tokens permanently; compatibility login/register now return expiring, revocable session tokens, logout revokes them, and the browser removes legacy credentials without migration.
- Bound XLSX archive expansion, grid size, decoded text and formatting; stream rows while preserving financial values and document identifiers. Reject unsafe authentication redirects and prevent caching private responses.
- Persist anonymous processing and session-creation budgets across API instances, independently of cookies. Update vulnerable runtime dependencies and run the API container as UID/GID 10001.
- Add an idempotent legacy-token revocation command and a maintenance-only mode in the existing API deployment workflow.

## Why

The security assessment reproduced reusable legacy credentials after logout, quota resets through new anonymous cookies, spreadsheet resource exhaustion, and external authentication redirects. The pinned multipart parser also had published security advisories. These changes close those paths and provide a production operation for invalidating already-issued legacy credentials.

## Type of change

- [ ] feat
- [x] fix
- [x] docs
- [ ] refactor
- [x] chore
- [x] test

## How to test

1. Full backend runner with an isolated PostgreSQL 16 instance: `backend/venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/test_backend.py --report-dir tmp/security-fix-validation --tb=short`, with `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointing to isolated local PostgreSQL (default full selection, runner-owned temporary directory). Final result: `5722 passed, 157 skipped, 2 xfailed` (575.14 seconds), exit code 0; PostgreSQL stopped and its exact temporary directory removed. The additional PostgreSQL plan-expiration and public-budget migration regressions passed (`2 passed`, 15.77 seconds) after updating the time-advance fixture to create a fresh session. Reproducible CI coverage explicitly includes `tests/test_public_budget_migration.py` in the PostgreSQL upgrade/rollback step.
2. Frontend: Node 24 with `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --pool=threads --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`. Final result: `80 files passed; 518 tests passed` (158.81 seconds). `npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit`: passed.
3. Real loopback HTTP using Uvicorn and synthetic data: `/convert` 200, report download 200, missing report 404, other owner 403, new-cookie quota bypass 429, old token 401, legacy migration 410, revoked token 401, expired token 401. `/analyze` is absent from this API; `/convert` is its current conversion endpoint.
4. `python -m ruff check backend`: `All checks passed!`; `python -m pip check`: `No broken requirements found.`; UTF-8/mojibake scan: no findings; `git diff --check`: clean.
5. PyPI advisory check on the 40 installed API runtime dependencies: zero reported advisories. `npm audit --omit=dev`: zero reported vulnerabilities. These checks do not audit deployed images or operating-system packages. Docker is unavailable locally; [API Runtime Image run 45614105563](https://github.com/claston/gettdone/actions/runs/45614105563) passed the image build, native/runtime/Textract checks and real HTTP startup as the configured non-root user. All checks passed on final revision `4f35ceb430ee30990fe945a8e22d4725fd8fcea1`: [Linux backend, PostgreSQL and browser suites](https://github.com/claston/gettdone/actions/runs/45614105628), CodeQL, and [worker image validation](https://github.com/claston/gettdone/actions/runs/45614105657). The worker suite reported `5718 passed, 161 skipped, 2 xfailed`; its built-image checks and HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability gate passed, with scan coverage verified for 21 OS packages and 23 Python packages.

Focused regressions include correctly signed retired tokens, expiration/logout, ZIP expansion, sparse and understated dimensions, renamed worksheet XML parts, decoded-text/format expansion, concurrent budgets, IPv6 prefixes, idempotent retries, cookie replacement, OAuth/browser redirect boundaries, and the reconciliation limit message. Network identifiers and operation keys are HMAC hashes; raw IPs are not persisted in these tables. Expired records are removed during enforcement. The downgrade intentionally retains the tables and counters, which the old API ignores.

The revocation operation raises `users.credential_version` to at least `2026112501`. It does not change passwords, account permissions or cookie sessions. author: martindrechsler
body:
**Home and flight are separate**
- Tapping TAP TO FLAP no longer shrinks the big home mushroom into the flying one; the flying mushroom is simply in its place.

**Out of breath**
- Two big buttons side by side: REST 1 MINUTE and WATCH AN AD. Nothing happens until one is tapped.
- Until then the mushroom sits knocked out: crossed eyes, head swaying round, cartoon stars circling.
- Choosing rest turns that button into a countdown ring; the ad button stays, to skip the wait.

**The recovery minute** (`RECOVERY` in `config/animations.ts`)
- 0 s: flops over, knocked out (tongue out, stars).
- 15 s: sits up and opens its eyes.
- 30 s: drinks a glass of water through a straw, gulp by gulp.
- 45 s: stands up and stretches.
- 60 s: a jump for joy with a burst, then home with 5 lives.
- Leaving mid-rest and coming back picks up at the right step.

**Notes**
- No save change: out of lives with 0 rest seconds left now means "not chosen yet" (`startRest`, `awaitingChoice`, `restProgress`).
- New moves: lie (down or back up), slump, daze, stars, drink. Squashes keep the stem's foot on the ground.

**Checks**
- `npm run check`: 142 tests pass.
- Phone flows: 47/47 on iPhone 13 and iPhone SE, no console errors. The harness now walks the choice, the whole recovery minute and the jump.

author: schadom
body:
## What

Addresses the review in the HACS default PR (hacs/default#13626): the aiohttp patches are now **strictly opt-in, off by default**, with a clear warning in the options. Bumps the version to **0.7.0**.

### Why it matters

The aiohttp layer replaces the private `ClientSession._request` and `TCPConnector._create_direct_connection` on the classes, so the wrapper sits in the HTTP path of **every** integration. If a future aiohttp release changes their signature, requests of every integration could break, not only this one. Failing open covers exceptions inside the tracer, but not a changed call shape.

### Changes

- **Default:** tracing uses only Python's public audit hook (`sys.addaudithook`). aiohttp is never touched.
- **New options dialog** (Settings › Devices & services › Security Monitor › Configure) with the switch **"Exact hostnames for HTTP requests (affects all integrations)"**:
  - off by default
  - a warning explains that it replaces private aiohttp methods for all integrations, and to turn it off first if integrations break after an update
  - saving reloads the integration, which switches the layer on or off
- **Panel:** the Connections footnote says where hostnames come from and points to the option when it's off. In English and German.
- **README:** "How it works" and "Known limitations" describe the default, plus a new section for the advanced option with a warning box.

### Impact for users

Home Assistant's own HTTP client resolves names with its own DNS library (aiodns), so the audit hook doesn't see `getaddrinfo` for its traffic. By default, those destinations now show a reverse-DNS name (e.g. `ec2-…amazonaws.com`) or only an IP, instead of the exact hostname. The integration is still attributed correctly. Hostnames for other libraries (`requests`, httpx, MQTT, websockets) are unchanged.

Request counts only appear with the option on; the table otherwise shows connections. Users who want the old behavior can turn the option on.

## Compatibility

- No migration needed. Existing installations start with the option off.
- Stored request counts expire after 7 days as before.
- Entities, Repairs issues and dismissed findings are unchanged.

## Testing

- New: aiohttp is left untouched by default, and requests are still attributed through the audit hook
- New: the options flow switches the layer on and off, and restores aiohttp's original methods when switched off
- Existing aiohttp-layer tests now run with the option on

author: mwangiiii
body:
## 1. `quantity_surveyor` role was impossible to assign

Migration `20261125120000_fix_quantity_surveyor_role.sql`.

The `role_name` enum already contained **both** `surveyor` and `quantity_surveyor`, but `public.roles` only had a row for `surveyor`. Since `user_roles.role_name` carries an FK to `roles(role_name)`, the value the whole application uses **could not be assigned at all** — `UserCreate.tsx:131` offers it, `RoleName` and `ROLE_PRIORITY` use it, `security.is_quantity_surveyor()` checks it, and the `/qs/*` guards expect it. 28 usages across 11 files, so the database moves rather than the app.

### Why the two existing `surveyor` users mattered

Not merely a cosmetic mismatch. `getPrimaryRole()` finds no match in `ROLE_PRIORITY` and falls through to `client` — but `security.is_client()` is **also false** for them, because they don't hold the `client` role. The result is a session with no recognised role, which therefore **passes** every policy written as `NOT security.is_client()`, including `chart_of_accounts_select` and `policy_categories_staff_read`.

They were unscoped, not restricted.

### Ordering is load-bearing

`user_roles.role_name` references `roles(role_name)` **`ON DELETE CASCADE`**. Deleting the old row before migrating its assignments would cascade-delete those `user_roles` rows and silently strip both users of all access. So: add row → migrate assignments → delete, guarded at each step, with a verification block that raises rather than leaving the lookup half-aligned.

The `surveyor` enum label stays — PostgreSQL can't drop enum values. Removing the lookup row is what prevents reassignment.

## 2. Leaving a project no longer dumps you on the dashboard

Module pages held the selected project in `useState`, so the URL stayed at `/finance/accounts-payable` whether you were on the picker or inside a project. Pressing browser Back — the natural way to leave — exited the module entirely and landed wherever you'd been before, usually the dashboard. The in-page back button also did nothing when `projectId` was supplied, because of the `if (!projectId)` guard.

`lib/useProjectSelection.ts` moves it into `?project=<id>`:

- Back returns to **that tab's picker**
- `?project=<id>` is deep-linkable and survives a refresh
- Back/Forward step between picker and project

Pages embedded for an already-chosen project leave the URL untouched, preserving the old guard's intent.

**Converted: Accounts Payable only.** The other 14 finance pages still carry the old pattern, pending confirmation that the interaction feels right before applying it fifteen times.

## 3. Repo cleanup

**Untracked, kept on disk** (working files, not source): `image_of_proof_stored/` — 17 screenshots, 14 MB, zero references in `src` — and the client quotation PDF.

**Deleted**: `PENDING_MIGRATIONS.sql` (generated for one migration run, now applied) and `bun.lockb` (a second lockfile alongside `package-lock.json` lets the two drift; this project uses npm).

**`.gitignore` rewritten.** It previously ended with two malformed entries — a bare `" ."` and `;supabase/.temp/storage-version`. Only `#` starts a comment in gitignore, so the `;` line was treated as a literal pattern and that file **was never actually ignored**. The seven individual `supabase/.temp` paths collapse to one directory rule.

## Deliberately not fixed

**Three users have no role and cannot log in** (`laveta3624@lawior.com`, `dennisjay43@gmail.com`, `thembrand@gmail.com`). Assigning one is a privilege grant and needs a human decision. The first is on a disposable-mail domain and looks like a leftover from when `/register` was open.

**`signUp()` and the `Register` import are dead code.** `/register` is commented out at `App.tsx:579`, so the client-side `user_roles` insert that RLS would reject can never run. Harmless; worth removing later.

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply the migration, then create a Quantity Surveyor via Admin → Users
- [ ] Confirm the two former `surveyor` users land on the QS dashboard, not the client one
- [ ] Confirm they no longer see the Chart of Accounts
- [ ] Accounts Payable → pick a project → browser Back → lands on the picker, not the dashboard
- [ ] `/finance/accounts-payable?project=<id>` opens that project directly

Typecheck: no new errors (64 pre-existing, unchanged).

author: valentinyeo
body:
## Why

An Antigravity worker waited on its own 8-minute CI timer after one push and burned the 45m print timeout (multiprompt PR 1216, and two hard timeouts in token-ladder PR 54). Briefs still tell workers to wait: "Push and read CI", "Stop when CI is green and the verifier has run", "sleep 240; gh pr checks". A worker that waits holds a lane and the chat does nothing until it dies.

## What changed

- `bin/worker-shims/sleep` refuses any duration over 30s and passes shorter ones to the real `sleep`.
- `bin/worker-shims/gh` refuses `pr checks --watch` and `run watch`; every other call runs the real `gh`.
- Both print one line, `worker shim refused: ...`, which `plan-pick`'s `shim_refusal()` now matches, so the run is recorded as `failure: environment` and never climbs a rung.
- `plan-pick --run` reads `brief.txt` before launching and refuses with exit 2 on CI-wait wording: stop when CI is green, wait/watch CI, until checks pass, read the PR checks, `gh pr checks`, `sleep N`. A negated line (`do not wait for CI`) passes. `PLAN_PICK_ALLOW_CI_WAIT=1` skips the check for reviewers only.
- README: "Workers never wait" rules under Worker lanes.

## Scope

Worker briefs only. No lane, rung or pace rule changes. No change to what the parent chat does after a red CI.

## Tradeoffs

The brief scan is a wording check, so a clever brief can slip past it. The shims are the hard backstop for `sleep` and CI watches. A worker that legitimately needs a 60s backoff inside its own script now fails fast instead of sleeping; 30s covers retry backoff.

## Blast Radius

Every `plan-pick --run` launch, because `bin/worker-shims` is prepended to the worker PATH. Reviewers and dry runs are unaffected. A brief that asks for waiting now exits 2 before any lane starts; the parent must rewrite the brief and rerun.

## Verification

Shim behaviour checked by hand: `sleep 240` and `gh pr checks --watch` refuse with one line, `sleep 30` and `gh pr view` run the real program. A real `--run` against a lane running `sleep 240` extended both guards end to end: exit 1, refusal line on stdout, and a `rung-attempts.json` finish with `failure: environment` and `refused: "sleep 240 (...)"`. `plan-pick --run` with the three real brief lines above exits 2 with one line naming the phrase; a brief that forbids waiting launches normally. `node tools/strip-comments.mjs --check` passes. The suite ran on GitHub Actions, not this server.

author: patrykkopycinski
body:
## Summary

The `enrich_report_core` step of the Threat Intel enrichment pipeline fails on Gemini models on Vertex AI with `status [400]. Error message: [Request contains an invalid argument.]`. Smaller structured-output calls (for example `assess_relevance`) succeed on the same endpoint.

The step's structured-output schema carries `maxItems` caps on three arrays: `approved_ioc_candidate_ids` (300), `behaviors` (100) and `artifacts` (200). Gemini rejects the schema when `behaviors` or `artifacts` carries `maxItems`. This is the same schema-complexity limit as elastic/kibana#297860 and elastic/kibana#297864.

## Change

- Remove `.max()` from the three arrays in `reportCoreModelOutputSchema` and from `approved_ioc_candidate_ids` in `iocAdjudicationOnlySchema`, so the tool schema sent to the model has no `maxItems`.
- Cap `behaviors` (100) and `artifacts` (200) in `enrichReportCore` instead, keeping the model's order and logging a warning when anything is dropped. Previously an oversized reply failed validation; now it is kept up to the cap, and the warning shows when that happens.
- `approved_ioc_candidate_ids` gets no replacement cap. Only ids of candidates in the reviewed batch (at most 300) are kept, and repeated ids collapse into one entry, so a long or repetitive reply cannot push real approvals out.
- Item-level bounds are unchanged: the candidate id range (0-4999), enums and per-field limits.

Dropping the tail of `behaviors` or `artifacts` narrows the enrichment output. It never broadens what gets hunted.

## Tests

`enrich_report_core.test.ts`:
- the JSON schema generated for both schemas contains no `maxItems` or `minItems`;
- both schemas keep every approved id the model returns, including repeats;
- `enrichReportCore` caps `behaviors` and `artifacts` in model order and logs one warning per capped field, and logs nothing when the reply is within the caps;
- an approved id listed after 400 repeats is still kept, and an id outside the reviewed batch is ignored;
- out-of-range candidate ids are still rejected.

Four of the new tests fail on `main`; all 20 tests in the file pass with the change. All `threat_intel/services` suites pass (606 tests).

## Verification

Direct Vertex AI probe (global endpoint): the tool schema generated from the Kibana code, after the inference plugin's Vertex schema sanitization, sent as a forced function call (`functionCallingConfig.mode: ANY`) with a minimal prompt.

| Schema | `gemini-3.5-flash` | `gemini-2.5-flash` |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (caps 300 / 100 / 200) | 400 (2/2) | 400 |
| This PR | 200, valid function call (2/2) | 200, valid function call |
| Only the `behaviors` cap | 400 | |
| Only the `artifacts` cap | 400 | |
| Only the candidate-id cap | 200 | |
| Adjudication-only schema, `main` and this PR | 200 | |

The 400 is `Request contains an invalid argument.`

Not verified end to end: the probe calls Vertex AI directly, not through Kibana and an Elasticsearch inference endpoint. The Elasticsearch Vertex AI request builder passes tool `parameters` through unchanged, so the probed request matches the one the pipeline sends.

author: samuelschlesinger
body:
Measure the cost of verifying a permutation by dividing the network's volume by the number of payload bits it delivers. A full-basis Boolean circuit for element distinctness gives such a verifier using the signed projection in [#8578](https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/pull/8578). This change proves two ways to lower-bound that cost. The [six-page derivation](https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/blob/4d473401b257beaf2f9a6caab9a35af1216a9176/notes/element-distinctness-routing.tex) gives the argument and its provenance.

Over a field without ports, lay the lists along rows and columns of a rectangle. Two permutation moves send a uniform starting position to an independent uniform destination. Charging the wires then gives a Poincaré bound for the verifier's graph. The graph obstruction forces the cost per bit to grow at least as fast as $\sqrt{h/\log h}$ for address width $h$, even when lists share arbitrary work. The single-list circuit proof needs just the row move. [Graph obstruction, #8571](https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/pull/8571).

Over a field with ports, choose a batch size at which no permitted replication factor more than halves the minimum cost per input bit of a hard signed computation. Compile its minimizing network once. A cheap tagged-permutation verifier would make the compiled computation cheaper than that very minimum. Lean checks normalization, substitution even along wires within a batch, and the choice of scale. The two inputs are an exact compiler for arbitrary normalized trivalent networks and a polynomial-size signed Boolean verifier with hard joint batches. OpenAI supplies these in [Proposition 14.1](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/3344da59991ed94f9ba711217b29c1d760badfa6/preprints/Euclidean-geometry-in-the-asymptotic-spectrum-of-tensors-November-24-2026/build/exact.tex#L11-L31) and [§12.1 and Theorem 12.1](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/3344da59991ed94f9ba711217b29c1d760badfa6/preprints/Circuit-lower-bounds-for-Hamiltonian-cycle-and-the-permanent-November-24-2026/build/model.tex#L18-L87). Native proofs for the source's constructions remain open in [#8448](https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/issues/8448).

From those two inputs, the [Lean transfer](https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/blob/4d473401b257beaf2f9a6caab9a35af1216a9176/CslibFrontier/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/ElementDistinctness/SourceTransfer.lean#L69-L91) derives the full list-volume bound and the circuit size bound at every sufficiently large record count, including eventual domination of every linear bound. The affected modules and six test modules built with warnings as errors. The headline proof terms use the three standard axioms. Codex assisted with the derivation, implementation and validation.

body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The arch22 HiSparse tests always used native ACL Host mapping, which fails before the intended operator checks on HDK without that capability. Select the Host allocator for the five affected test functions (25 parameterized cases):

- Query `aclrtHostMemMapCapabilities` after the existing NPU/arch22 guard. Prefer native ACL mapping when supported.
- If the query explicitly reports `ACL_ERROR_RT_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORT` or succeeds with no capability, allocate through the existing `allocate_mapped_host(..., memfabric=True)` backend from #22600.
- Do not skip for unavailable Host mapping. A missing/unusable MemFabric dependency or a MemFabric initialization/allocation failure fails the test. Unexpected capability-query errors and native registration failures also propagate; they do not trigger a backend retry.

Both backends use the same existing operator calls, inputs, accuracy assertions, graph replay, and cleanup. Parameter coverage stays at 117 cases, with the other 92 cases unaffected. This selection belongs to the test fixture; production backend selection remains explicit configuration and is unchanged.

Related A3 Nightly: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45572452710/job/139062732072

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Only the test file changes. Production allocation and operator implementations are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

```bash
python -m pytest -sv -rs tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_hisparse_arch22_ops.py
```

- Eleven focused CPU checks of the extracted fixture passed: native/MemFabric selection, unsupported capability responses, unexpected query/loader errors, unavailable MemFabric, and native allocation failure without retry. These are fixture-policy checks, not NPU kernel validation.
- A2 full-file negative-path regression on driver 25.2.0, CANN 9.3.0 and MemFabric 1.3.0: **92 passed, 25 failed, 0 skipped**. The failed set exactly matches the original 25 cases, with no new failures. All 25 reached MemFabric and failed with `Failed to initialize the MemFabric HiSparse Host pool: -1`; the installed AccOffload library reported `file too short`. This confirms unavailable backend support is surfaced instead of skipped; it is not a passing functional result.
- Hardware check used Ascend `7dcdb690caf879a17ab07382880d5773f5202e20` plus the current test file, vLLM `62d4bc3c7e33b1b6c906e233e6af2d3506c482ca`, and the existing prepared native extension/custom OPP. The original target test and Host-pool implementation match this PR's base `4f49ae332de1b1e572587bb9162cfb991eadf2ed`. This was not a full latest-main environment rebuild.
- AST comparison verified unchanged test bodies apart from allocator calls, unchanged parameterization, and the 25/92 coverage split. Targeted Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Repository-wide lint was attempted with actionlint excluded because its environment could not bootstrap locally. Ruff check, Ruff format and codespell passed in the available log; the complete repository check did not finish, so full lint remains for CI.
- A3 (Ascend910_9362), driver 26.1.0, CANN 9.3.0, MemFabric 1.3.0: **117 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** with MemFabric explicitly selected. Since this machine reports native capability available, a temporary validation copy replaced only the allocator fixture body with `partial(allocate_mapped_host, memfabric=True)`. All test functions, parameters and assertions remained unchanged. Runtime recording verified all 25 Host allocations used the real MemFabric backend. The run used this PR Python source, vLLM `62d4bc3c7e33b1b6c906e233e6af2d3506c482ca`, and previously built native extension/custom OPP artifacts; no full native rebuild was performed.
- The A3 result validates explicit MemFabric execution on the stack above, not automatic backend selection on the original HDK 25.5.1 Nightly runner. Exact original-runner validation and a full-file run of this revision through its default native selection remain pending.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: supported, absent and explicitly unsupported capability responses checked.
- [ ] **Regression test**: MemFabric full-file hardware run passed; default native-selection hardware run remains pending.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: both-backends-unavailable fails; unexpected errors are not hidden.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: original operator assertions and parameters are retained.

author: naimelijah
body:
Refs #162

## Problem

An independent review of #284's last commit found no bug. It found doc comments and docs that still described the code from before that commit:

- **Three Javadocs** still said a 400 item names a pointer or a parameter: `ProblemItem`, `ContractBreaks` and `ContractErrorHandler`. A whole-request item now names neither.
- **`architecture.md`** said `Problems` sets `instance`. Spring sets it, and `Problems.at` sets it only for `ErrorEndpoint`.
- **The filter's descriptions** left out its 400 for a path Spring can't parse. These are the `TraceIdFilter` entries in `architecture.md` and `code-structure.md`, and the `web` package-info.
- **Two comments** said Tomcat logs its parse line "once a day". The limit is once a day per connection processor: `application.properties` and `WebOverTomcatIT`.
- **One Javadoc sentence** in `ContractErrorHandler` had been wrapped by hand and was missing its verb.

## Approach

The wording follows the code and the contract's own phrasing: "or neither for the request as a whole".

## Trade-off accepted

None. The diff changes no executable line.

## What was done

8 files, comments and docs only: `ProblemItem`, `ContractBreaks`, `ContractErrorHandler`, `web/package-info`, `WebOverTomcatIT`, `application.properties` (`#` lines only), `architecture.md` and `code-structure.md`.

## How it was verified

- **`just core-check`:** Spotless `0 needs changes`; `Tests run: 3797, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0` (unit) and `Tests run: 796, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0` (IT); `BUILD SUCCESS`.
- **Comments only:** `git diff` was filtered for changed lines that aren't Javadoc, `//` or `#` lines, and none are left.
- **Clean diff:** `git diff --check` is clean, and no added line passes 100 columns except inline links.
- **The review panel** read the diff: code, tests, docs and security.
  - Tests, docs and security found nothing to block.
  - The code reviewer found three more stale sentences, now fixed: `ContractErrorHandler`'s log-line sentence, `package-info`, and `WebOverTomcatIT`.
  - The docs auditor asked for the ADR-142 decision 5 citation, now added.
  - The claims were checked with javap against spring-webmvc 7.0.10 and tomcat-embed-core 11.0.27:
    - Spring's return-value handlers fill a null `instance`;
    - `UserDataHelper` is an instance field of `AbstractProcessor`.

## ADR

None. ADR-140's decision 5 table still says a 400 item has "a pointer into the body or the parameter's name and place". That is a wording gap, not a changed decision: ADR-142 decision 5 already gives a 400 "one item for the whole request". Accepted ADRs are append-only, so it stays as written.

author: cheeenxiii
body:
Part of #182

## What changed

- `src/mhuc/quests/mibwrite.py`: `mib4_set_wave_monster(m, monster_id, wave=0, index=0)` — the
  original `.mib` with one large-monster definition's id patched **in place**. Every other byte
  (the texts, the pointer table, the blocks and their packing) stays; an unchanged id returns the
  file exactly. `mib4_build` remains the converter for other games' quests: it lays the blocks out
  again and shifts every offset, which the game's readers don't all follow.
- `src/mhuc/formats/arc.py`: `replace_entry(data, file_name, body)` — replaces one entry and
  reuses every other entry's original compressed stream (`write()` already keeps it), so only the
  patched stream moves and the table offsets after it change. A full repack (`mhuc arc pack`,
  which builds every entry from its file) compresses every stream again. The patch is the
  container-preserving path.
- `tests/test_with_game_files.py` (marked `game_files`):
  - every real MH4U quest's `.mib` patches in place byte for byte with an unchanged id, and a
    changed id moves only its four bytes;
  - replacing one quest inside a real archive returns the archive byte for byte when unchanged and
    keeps every other entry's compressed stream when changed.

## Why

The builder rewrote the whole `.mib` for the port's 125 quest (the texts compacted, 2,774 bytes
shifted), and the game's map/area init read a stale zone index (99) and never loaded the quest.
The in-place patch keeps the game's own layout.

## How it was tested

- `MHUC_DUMPS=… venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_with_game_files.py -k "patches_in_place
  or arc_patch_keeps"`: 2 passed (over every `rQuestData` of MH4U's RomFS archives).
- `venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`: 215 passed, 37 skipped; `/usr/bin/ruff check .`,
  `tools/check_specs.py`, `tools/check_no_game_data.py` pass.
- The patched 125 quest (original mib, one byte changed; arc 636,703 bytes against 636,716, every
  other entry's stream kept) was replayed in the headless harness.

## Left undone

- The correct-mib 125 quest still waits at the map/area init: the base quest's per-zone entry
  (the wave's monster id 1) finishes its load and the init walks zones 1..6; the ported id 125
  makes the same load's status never reach done, so the init stays in state 1, zone 0. That
  remaining resource load is #182's open item.
- The 124 (GU) replay is inconclusive: the 3U input route does not start the quest on the GU
  profile's save; it needs that profile's own route.

## What

- `@dx_test_tags_sources` used to walk the whole repo (about 42 s in the profile) and also wrote one `consumer.json`. Because of that, editing any consumer fixture reran every consumer test.
- The new `consumer_fixtures` repository rule in `tools/ci/repos.bzl` (repo `@dx_consumer_fixtures`) lists only the top level. It then walks `<lang>/tests/consumer` for each directory that has a `lang.json`. It watches each directory and file it reads.
- It writes one `<lang>.json` per language, plus `consumer.json` holding all languages for the cross-language readers: the in-graph prebuilt guard, `network_test` and the language docs test.
- `consumer_fixture_tests` in `tools/testing/consumer/fixtures.bzl` now depends on `@dx_consumer_fixtures//:<lang>.json`. `apple/tests:consumer_build_test` depends on `apple.json`.
- `@dx_test_tags_sources` no longer writes `consumer.json`, and its walk skips the bazelignored consumer directories again. `sources.json`, `files.json` and `all_paths.json` still need every BUILD and .bzl file, so that walk stays full-tree. Consumer tests no longer depend on it, though.
- `walk` takes `roots`, and `consumer_fixture_paths` groups paths by language. `repos_tests.bzl` covers both.

## Tests

- `tools/dx test //tools/ci/... //tools/testing/consumer/... //tools/docs/languages:languages_test //tools/docs/rule_names:rule_names_test //cli/tests/entrypoint:consumer_surface`: `Executed 76 out of 76 tests: 76 tests pass.`
- After a one-line edit to `lua/tests/consumer/hello.lua`, `tools/dx test //tools/testing/consumer:fixture_tests` gave `Executed 1 out of 55 tests: 55 tests pass.` The other 54 were cache hits. Before this change, all of them depended on the single `consumer.json`.

## Known limit: `--affected`

`tools/dx test --affected --since HEAD --output json` with the same edit selects `"targets":[]` both before and after this change. The plan event shows `widened: unowned lua/tests/consumer/hello.lua -> //lua/tests/consumer/...`.

The fixture directories are bazelignored, so they have no owning package. `dx affected` does not trace a file watched by a repository rule back to the targets that use that rule. The per-language manifests give per-language test-cache invalidation now. Making `--affected` select `lua_consumer_test` needs a dx change (for example, reading the repo `.marker` FILE/DIRENTS entries), which this PR does not include.

author: cgfixit
body:
## Proposed changes
If a page's inline `<script>` calls `document.forms[0].submit()` on a POST form while the page is still parsing, a `/browse` `navigate` to that page failed with `page.goto: Timeout 10000ms exceeded`. It should return an observation whose `held` list names the POST. The page route already held the POST and answered it `204`, so nothing was sent. But Playwright still counts that held load as the frame's pending navigation, so `domcontentloaded` never reaches `goto`. The model saw a navigate failure, and that failure counted toward the three-consecutive-failures stop.

`browser/sidecar.mjs`:
- New `loadStopped` hook. The page route calls it when it holds a top-level load (`topLevelLoad(request)`), or when it pauses one for the operator under takeover.
- `navigate` races `page.goto` against that signal. The signal counts only after this navigate's main frame has committed (`framenavigated`), so a load the old page starts before the commit does not end the wait early. Once the signal wins, the late `goto` rejection is swallowed.
- `settle(loadHeld)`: after a held load it waits on `document.readyState !== "loading"` instead of Playwright's `domcontentloaded`, which would burn its full 5 s. Measured: 5020 ms before this change, 505 ms after.

`src/common/browser_host.rs`, two fixtures on the same `/autosubmit` page (an inline parse-time submit to `/submitted`):
- `guard_holds` (takeover off) requires `held == ["POST {base}/submitted"]`, an empty `held_background`, the page text present, and no `POST` received by the fixture server.
- `takeover_with_policy` (takeover on, the shipped default) requires the same held row, the page text and no POST sent. It deliberately does not check whether the operator was asked: on `main` a page's own load is paused and refused, and after #1138 it is held without a question. The step holds either way.

`docs/Browser-Use.md`: the hold bullet now says a form a page posts mid-load is held and `navigate` still returns the page. The edit is word-neutral (527 of 530): #1138 also edits this guide and alone brings it to 530, so the merged file is 529.

`3b0c4f6` (from another Claude session) moved this branch's takeover bullet and routes to lines #1138 does not touch, so the two PRs now merge cleanly in either order.

**CodeQL on `main`** (operator asked for a review): `main`'s CodeQL run 45648983997 on `b769c23` (docs only) failed in both `Analyze` jobs, as did this PR's CodeQL, DevSkim and two comment jobs. In every case the scan finished, then the upload or the comment POST failed while GitHub's API was returning 500/502 (about 16:00–16:20 UTC). A healthy upload takes 7–9 s; the failed ones ran 23–28 s and logged no error. The workflow file and action pins are unchanged since the green run on `2f38a62`. Re-run attempt 2 of 45648983997 is green, with both uploads succeeding. So there is no workflow bug to fix and no alert to exclude, and this PR changes no workflow. I could not open the SARIF itself (the Actions artifact host is blocked from my session), so "no alert" rests on the green re-run, not on reading the results.

**Invariant / Governance Impact**: this touches the I6 browser paragraph's hold rule ("every request but GET and HEAD is held for the operator"). The rule still holds: the hold and the `204` answer are unchanged, and only the waiting around them changes. A page's own requests are still never asked about (takeover routing is unchanged; #1138 narrows it further, and the two compose). No `crate::agentic` reference, no write gate, no config, no core-path file.

## Types of changes
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Security (auth, encryption, certs, rbac,  privacy, injection, egress, redaction, or secrets)
- [ ] Invariant / Governance refinement (use this for changes that strengthen or evolve I6 isolation, write gates, or harness phases)
- [ ] Dependencies (updated, aligned between install methods, new deps added, removed, or bumped)
- [x] CI / Skills / AI infrastructure (skills, workflows, hooks, lint tools, ci/cd and tests/ additions or updates/trims, templates, checkers, etc)
- [ ] Refactor or clean-up (behavior-preserving, no new capability)
- [x] Documentation Update
- [ ] Other (none of the boxes above fit)

Scope: browser sidecar, its host fixtures and one bullet of `docs/Browser-Use.md`. The CI box covers the new guard and takeover fixture steps; no workflow file changes.

## Benefits / why
- A model browsing a page that auto-submits a form now sees the observation and the held row. The task ends as held for the operator, as it does for any other held page load, and no longer burns a failure on a 10 s timeout.
- The POST is still never sent: the fixture checks what the loopback server actually received.

## Risks to monitor
- Any held top-level load after commit now ends `navigate`'s wait, including one a late timer starts after the page fully loaded. The result is the same observation the model would have got, plus the held row, so I see no harm. The signal is the `held` row in the observation.
- A page can lie about `document.readyState`. The only effect is a shorter settle, bounded by the existing `networkidle` wait.
- Under takeover with a paused navigation (only reachable before #1138 merges), `navigate` now returns through `observe()`, which already waits on `pendingApproval`, instead of timing out. The new `takeover` step covers it with a Deny. An Allow of a page's own load is not covered; #1138 removes that question.
- `cargo test --all-targets` and `cargo deny check` were not run locally (per AGENTS.md, CI runs the suite; cargo-deny is not installed here). No dependency changed.

author: swordlash
body:
The first cut of #301 (what the first build of autocompletion left out): the two most noticeable cases of Enter in lists. Narrow by contract: an unusual place gets today's plain line break, never a wrong write.

## What changes

- **Enter in the middle of an item's first line splits the item.** The rest of the line moves to a new item of the same list directly below, written exactly as Enter at a line's end writes one (same indentation and bullet, the next number, `[ ] ` for a task); the item's later lines go with the new item. The spaces right after the cursor are removed, and the cursor stands at the start of the moved text.

  ```
  - Milk ‸and eggs        →   - Milk
                              - ‸and eggs
  ```
- **Later items are renumbered** when Enter adds an item to a numbered list (at a line's end or by a split), in the same transaction, so one undo takes back both. Only when the list was numbered one after another from the cursor's item: `1. 1. 1.` and lists with gaps are left alone.

  ```
  1. one‸         →   1. one
  2. two              2. ‸
                      3. two
  ```

## What stays a plain line break

The start of an item's text, a cursor among the marks or in a task's box, an item's later lines; inside code, math, a link, emphasis, an emoji's name, a mention, a spoiler, raw HTML left open, brackets left open; where the moved text would become a heading, a list, a quotation or a task box; a tab among the marks, CRLF, an item over 2,000 characters. Every split is read back by the parser: the two paragraphs joined must equal the old one inline for inline and everything else of the block must be unchanged, or Enter is plain.

## Choices

- **A number that grows a digit** (`9.` to `10.`): each item's later lines are left as they are; the renumbered text is parsed, and if its blocks differ, no number changes. A split whose new item's number is a digit wider, in an item with indented later lines, stays plain.
- **Renumbering is bounded by the 2,000 characters Enter reads**, not by a count of items: a list that goes on past that text gets no new numbers (the page shows the right ones anyway). On a long page the editor asks once more with a longer text and uses its numbers only when the change on the cursor's line is the same.
- The editor checks that every range still holds the text the answer was computed for before it writes; otherwise Enter is plain. A slide's row drops a renumbering that would reach past the row.
- The rule is pure (`Wiki.Core.Markdown.Enter.edit`); `web/src/editor.js` and `Editor/Browser.hs` carry the ask and the answer.

## Tests

Tables of splits, renumberings, UTF-16 offsets and 44 plain cases; properties over generated lists (the five marks, tasks, nesting, continuation lines, nested and loose lists; numbers consecutive, equal or with gaps): the exact text against a model, an independent read-back by the parser, apply then inverse gives the old text, the editor's two asks give the whole text's edit; over generic documents, a split read back or a plain break at any place. A cost test: a new item in the middle of a 1,000-item list stays under 100 MB of allocation natively. One browser example with an emoji before the cut and one undo. Two existing expectations changed on purpose: "leaves the numbers below" now renumbers, and `- on‸e` now splits.

## Verification

Run locally: `build-native`, `build-wasm`, `format`, `lint`; wiki-core's Enter (182), Complete and Starts groups; wiki-app's native Complete group; the browser Complete group (11) and the Editor's and slide rows' Enter examples. The test runs were on the first of the two commits; the second changed only the split's guards and their tests, whose group ran on the final head. Left to CI: the rest.

## Codex

- Round 1 (a927acdf): one finding. With a nested numbered list that begins on its outer item's first line (`1. 1. a`), the renumbering took the outer list for the cursor's and changed its numbers. Being fixed.

- Fixed in 4c239841: the cursor's list is found by the line and column of its item's mark, the item's identity, and the items after it are counted from that pair. The generator now puts lists on their outer item's first line (38% of cases); the property fails within 33 cases with the old lookup.

- Round 2 (4c239841): no findings.

author: maiiasleptcova
body:
## Summary

Search gets a local second stage (no LLM, no API key). The prompt hook recalls more memories and stops injecting unrelated ones.

- **Keyword channel.** `GraphStore.lexical_search` (non-abstract, default `[]`).
  - Embedded: an SQLite FTS5 table kept in sync by triggers, created and backfilled once for existing stores (one IMMEDIATE transaction, safe under racing processes). `recursive_triggers` is on, so `INSERT OR REPLACE` (restore, migrate) stays in sync.
  - Docker: a Neo4j full-text index on `Memory.content`, created by `initialize()`, or by a search that gets Neo4j's exact "no such fulltext schema index" error on an older store.
  - Superseded, invalidated and forgotten memories are excluded in the store query, which also filters project before its LIMIT. All engine filters (category, tags, session, user, dates, `valid_to`, `query.filters`) are re-applied to keyword hits.
- **Reranker.** The pool is RRF (k=60) of the dense top 50 and the keyword top 50, plus the best `limit` graph/entity-only candidates and the first-stage top `limit`. `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2` scores it, and the score is `(sigmoid(logit)·0.7 + min(graph,1)·0.3)·decay`, so graph links and temporal decay still count.
- **Relevance gate.** When no pool candidate reaches logit 0, the first-stage order is served. The reason is under Benchmarks.
- **Recall cutoff** (`[search] recall_min_score = 0.00002`). On the recall path only (`get_context`: the prompt hook and `collivind_get_context`), a memory whose cross-encoder score is below the cutoff is dropped, in whichever order was served. Recall can therefore return fewer than `limit` memories, or none, and the hook then prints nothing. Explicit search (`collivind search`, `collivind_search`) never applies it, because an explicit search that returns nothing is more surprising than a weak match. With the reranker off or unavailable it does nothing, and the existing `similarity_threshold` applies as before.
- **Hook depth and budget**: `[hooks] recall_limit = 20` (validated 1–50) replaces the hard-coded 5. `[hooks] recall_max_tokens = 2400` (validated 100–20000) replaces the hard-coded 800, and `hook user-prompt --max-tokens` still overrides it. No installed hook passes the flag, so plugins and `hook install` pick up the new default. See "Hook depth and tokens".
- **Where the model runs.**
  - Embedded: the cross-encoder lives in the resident embed daemon and loads before the socket binds. Hooks never load it in-process: no daemon means the first-stage ranking, and without a possible daemon the pool is not even built. With the daemon off (benchmarks, a long-lived process with `COLLIVIND_EMBED_DAEMON=0`) it loads in-process.
  - Docker: `POST /rerank` on the embeddings container, one try with a 3 s timeout and a 60 s backoff in-process. A pre-0.19 image returns 404, so rerank stays off until `collivind docker up` rebuilds it. The container limit goes 512M → 768M (measured about 455 MB resident with both models).
- **Fallback.** These all serve the 0.18.0 ranking unchanged: reranker missing, loading, slow, erroring, or returning non-finite scores; a graph-degraded search; no confident candidate without a cutoff. Nothing from the reranker raises out of search.
- **Config.** `[search]`: `rerank = true`, `rerank_model`, `rerank_pool = 50` (validated 1–200), `lexical = true`, `recall_min_score`. `rerank = false` reproduces 0.18.0 exactly and loads nothing. A golden test written against untouched 0.18.0 pins this, and on LoCoMo the rerank-off run returns the same ids as 0.18.0 on all 1,982 questions.
- **Daemon protocol.**
  - A new `rerank` op; `info` now reports `rerank_model`.
  - Daemon identity stays version + embedding model.
  - A daemon started without a reranker is replaced on the first rerank request.
  - A daemon serving a *different* reranker answers with a non-fatal error, and the client backs off for 5 minutes, so two configs cannot restart each other in a loop.
- **Benchmarks.**
  - LoCoMo: a strict score (the returned text must be an evidence turn's text) next to the chain-following one, plus `--search key=value` overrides.
  - LongMemEval: `benchmarks/longmemeval_engine.py`, a turn-level metric (`has_answer` turns) through `MemoryManager`, rerank on and off.
  - `search_bench.py`: an arm with the real cross-encoder.
- Version 0.19.0 (`version.py` and plugin manifests). README and BENCHMARKS updated, including the extra ~90 MB model download.

## Benchmarks (from the final commit: embedded mode, temp stores, daemon off, recall path with the default cutoff)

**LoCoMo, 1,536 non-adversarial questions, through `MemoryManager.search`:**

| Arm | strict hit@5 | strict hit@10 | hit@5 | hit@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.18.0 / `rerank = false` | 57.6 | 67.2 | 59.8 | 70.1 |
| rerank, `lexical = false` | 70.8 | 76.2 | 73.2 | 79.2 |
| **0.19.0 default** | **72.4** | **77.5** | **74.7** | **80.5** |

The target was ≥ 70 / ≥ 77. The offline estimate was 76.4 / 82.2. The gap breaks down as:
- Dedup: 2.3 / 2.9 points are questions whose evidence text was replaced by a near-duplicate at ingest.
- The relevance gate: about 0.9 / 0.6 points.
- The recall cutoff: 0.

**LongMemEval-S, the same 90-question sample (15 per type, seed 0), through `MemoryManager`:**

| Arm | session R@5 | turn hit@5 | turn hit@10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| rerank off | 97.8 | 74.4 | 83.3 |
| **0.19.0 default** | **97.8** | **75.6** | **83.3** |

**Why the gate.** Without it, LongMemEval turn hit@10 dropped 83.3 → 80.0 and session R@5 dropped 97.8 → 96.7. In those losses the cross-encoder scored every candidate near 0. They were indirect "preference" questions, and its order among texts it found irrelevant threw away a dense ranking that had the answer turn at rank 0–8. Indirect coding prompts look the same.

I declared two fixes before looking at pool data (the gate, and a fixed 0.5 cosine blend) and scored both offline on logged pools, with no sweep. Strict hit@5 / hit@10:

| Formula | LoCoMo | LME seed 0 | LME seed 1 (69 of 90 unseen) |
|---|---|---|---|
| first stage | 57.6 / 67.2 | 74.4 / 83.3 | 82.2 / 91.1 |
| plain rerank | 73.2 / 78.1 | 74.4 / 80.0 | 85.6 / 91.1 |
| **gate (shipped)** | 72.3 / 77.5 | 75.6 / 83.3 | 86.7 / 93.3 |
| cosine blend | 71.7 / 78.4 | 74.4 / 83.3 | 86.7 / 92.2 |

### Recall cutoff: how the default was chosen

Cross-encoder scores were logged for every returned candidate through the real engine. LoCoMo barely separates the two groups:
- Evidence turns: median 0.977, p10 0.087.
- Other turns from the same conversation: median 0.294, p10 0.0018.
- Category 5 (adversarial) questions are about the conversation too; their best-candidate median is 0.953.

So LoCoMo only bounds the cost. Strict hit@5 / hit@10, and how many of 10 results survive:

| cutoff | strict @5 / @10 (cat 1–4) | kept of 10 (cat 1–4) | no result | kept of 10 (cat 5) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 72.3 / 77.5 | 10.0 | 0% | 10.0 |
| **0.00002** | **72.4 / 77.5** | **10.0** | **0%** | **10.0** |
| 0.0001 | 72.5 / 77.3 | 9.9 | 0% | 9.9 |
| 0.001 | 72.3 / 77.0 | 9.5 | 0.2% | 9.0 |
| 0.01 | 71.2 / 75.0 | 8.4 | 1.2% | 7.0 |
| 0.1 | 69.0 / 71.5 | 6.5 | 3.5% | 4.7 |

**Coding-style sanity check**, because the reranker is MS MARCO-trained and LoCoMo is conversational. A synthetic store of 20 coding memories, 10 prompts each targeting one memory, and 10 prompts unrelated to all of them, at limit 20:

| cutoff | relevant: target kept | unrelated: mean kept | unrelated: nothing recalled |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (today) | 10/10 | 20 | 0/10 |
| 0.00001 | 10/10 | 20 | 0/10 |
| **0.00002** | **10/10** | **0.2** | **8/10** |
| 0.0001 | 10/10 | 0.1 | 9/10 |
| 0.001 | 8/10 | 0.0 | 10/10 |

Unrelated prompts sit on the model's floor, 1.1–1.4e-5. Indirect relevant prompts score low but above it: the lowest target was 0.00016.

I first tried 0.0001. It passed LoCoMo (72.5 / 77.3) but cost LongMemEval session R@5 **97.8 → 94.4** and turn hit@10 83.3 → 80.0 through the real engi

body: ## What Settlement generation 2 places hamlets, villages, towns, cities, rare capitals, and at most one metropolis per chunk. New worlds use it. A save that omits `settlementGen` still rebuilds generation 1, and `PackedWorld` is unchanged. Sites are scored (flat ground, coast, roads, preferred biome) instead of thrown as darts. Each footprint, including its farm ring, stays inside the class margin from the chunk edge. Towns and larger grow an irregular outskirts ring, drawn as a placeholder fill. Satellites sit on the roads out of those gates and take their role from the biome under them (farm, fishing, mining, logging, and the rest of §2.5). The map strokes the real quadrant outline at every map step, including close zoom. ## How to see it ``` npm ci npm run dev ``` Open the game, choose **New**. World Gen opens on seed **7741** (the default). - **Regions** — the belief map. Zoom with the wheel. Shots at 0.25, 0.6, 1.6, and 3.6 are below. - **Chunk** — the start chunk. Generation 2 draws roof-coloured footprints, a wheat-coloured farm ring, and the roads between them. Ashfen, Goldmere, Ironmarch, and Saltgate are still the named places. - **City plans** — the ward-cut overlay (class and seed). It is the cutter, not one town on the map. - Generation 1, for comparison: open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/?settlementGen=1` and choose **New** again. The chunk is the old nine places and a single road ring. Screenshots (seed 7741): - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-regions-gen2-z0_25.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-regions-gen2-z0_6.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-regions-gen2-z1_6.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-regions-gen2-z3_6.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-regions-gen1-z1_6.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-chunk-gen2.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-chunk-gen2-close.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-chunk-gen1.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-chunk-gen1-close.png` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/c1-city-plans-overlay.png` ## Counts over 200 continent seeds (world scale 1) | class | min | mean | max | worlds with one | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | hamlet | 11 | 20.6 | 34 | 200 | | village | 1 | 9.8 | 18 | 200 | | town | 2 | 3.0 | 5 | 200 | | city | 1 | 2.6 | 3 | 200 | | capital | 0 | 0.10 | 1 | 19 | | metropolis | 0 | 0.03 | 1 | 6 | 2,537 satellites. 1,147 of 1,150 towns-and-up have a farm ring. No world has two metropolises. ## Deviations - The no-settings island (`beginGeneratedWorld()` with no settings) stays on generation 1. Tools and the recorded Ashfen tests depend on that fixed map. New Game and World Gen use the default, which is generation 2. - Ashfen is never the metropolis. The rare upgrade is Saltgate (metropolis) or Goldmere (capital), so the start town stays one city-sized zone. - Outskirts are a separate tile list on the node and are not part of `node.tiles`. The 3D zone and `settlementZoneRect` stay the core. Layout and wards are C2 and C4. - Hamlet through city are clipped to a 32-fine-tile box. A 3×3 display city (48 tiles, about 56 in practice) baked in 4.5s instead of Ashfen's 0.5s, and the player-mesh round trip ran past its 7 minute limit. Capitals and metropolises keep the large footprint; splitting them into wards is C4. - On a 1× world a quadrant cannot be half a fine tile, so it is one fine tile. 16× worlds use the 8-fine-tile quadrant from the proposal. - Slope caps are looser than a gentle hillside. This height field is steep even on plains (often above 0.5 over 128 m). Sites are still ranked toward the flattest shelf, and cliff faces are rejected. - `?settlementGen=1` forces the new-world screen back to generation 1 so the before shot can be taken through the same UI.

author: freeqaz-openai
body:
A user can be redirected to an identity provider just as the API process that started sign-in exits. Extend the maintained PostgreSQL sign-in integration test to verify that a surviving API sharing the database can complete the callback for the original browser and return its session key once.

The test checks three distinct refusals. A different browser cannot complete the pending callback. A provider error without a code distinguishes live state from spent state, so a used provider code cannot mask a state-replay defect. Replaying the completed callback is also refused, and the established session remains valid.

The stock single-source PostgreSQL test command passed with 7 tests reported. Separate private launch wiring reran the same tests with older and current API processes in both orders, also passing. Both versions use the same authentication implementation. The test uses a simulated provider and does not exercise a real browser or rolling deployment.

The original surrounding runs failed whole-run cleanliness and formatting because the build generated source files. The same failure reproduced on the unchanged base. With a separate Console declaration fix applied, the unchanged PostgreSQL test passed again. Workspace checks, two builds, typecheck, lint and formatting also passed in that combined checkout. All temporary checkouts omitted one unrelated staging test.

Draft pending normal required checks.

author: octoalgo
body:
Fixes #861.

## Problem

On an **RTX 5090 (GB202)**, this fork faults at every world entry (Linux, Proton, vkd3d-proton, NVIDIA 620.73.04): NVRM Xid 13, "SM Warp Exception: MMU Fault", shader writes to unmapped GPU addresses. The same build runs clean on an RTX 5070 Ti in the same PC. On other NVIDIA cards the same cause costs video memory instead: Marvisak/VIctory#2143 reports GBs of VRAM reserved on an RTX 5080.

## Cause

`code_dword` (`crates/victory-shader/src/emit/lower.rs`) turns the program's code, starting at the lowest offset any load or descriptor names, into a constant array. A load at a computed offset names offset 0, so the array is the whole program. In 12 lighting computes reached at world entry, that is 4160–4596 dwords (16.3–18 KiB).

Under vkd3d-proton the array becomes a private one. NVIDIA's compiler keeps up to 16 KiB of such arrays in constant memory and copies a bigger one into each thread's **local memory**: 16–18 KB per thread in those 12 shaders. On GB202 this local memory faults.

## Change

This is a port of Marvisak/VIctory#2143 by @desplmfao: its two commits squashed into one, with desplmfao kept as the author. The only difference from upstream is the test module's import list.

The table now starts where the instructions end, because the program's constants follow its instructions and a computed load reads them. It keeps the old start if a load at a fixed offset reads below the end. A computed index below the start is clamped like one past the end, as before.

No follow-up change was needed. A 15-minute run logged all 1149 code-table reads in 114 programs:
- None is a fixed-offset load inside the instructions.
- Every `s_getpc_b64` + literal table base, as the translator computes it, sits at or after the instructions' end.
- So no real read falls below the new start. The 9 programs whose tables were 3200–4600 dwords now have 154–177 dwords.

## Evidence (RTX 5090 + RTX 5070 Ti, one PC)

- Nsight Aftermath dumps of the 5090 faults always named a shader whose NVIDIA compile uses local memory.
- Refusing every shader with local memory gave a clean 15-minute run, twice.
- Refusing only the 12 computes with 16–18 KB of local memory also gave a clean run, so they are the trigger. The other ~1000 shaders with 16–240 B of local memory are fine.
- A local switch with the same rule (table from the end of the instructions; it also kept a 256 B margin and a cap) gave two clean 15-minute 5090 runs with all shaders on and the world lit. It reached frames 3232 and 3272 with 0 Xid.
  - The executables' local memory, as reported by the driver, no longer reaches 16 KB anywhere (the largest compute uses 128 B, the largest pixel shader 192 B; before: 16–18 KB in 12 executables).
  - An A/B on the 5070 Ti, switch on vs. off, lit alike: mean luminance 0.161 vs. 0.162, and the per-frame difference is within run-to-run noise.
- **This branch** on the 5090: clean: full 15 minutes (frame 3059), 0 Xid, lit. The window scene's mean luminance is 0.141, vs. 0.143 with the local switch and 0.003 with the 12 computes refused. Local memory per the driver: at most 128 B (compute) and 192 B (pixel), over 997 compute and 782 pixel executables.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p victory-shader --lib` (Linux host): 172 passed, 2 ignored, including #2143's `the_code_table_starts_after_the_instructions`.
- `cargo build --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --release -p victory` (cross-built with xwin): OK. Also `--profile diag --features diagnostics`.
- One 15-minute RTX 5090 run of this branch, built with `--profile diag --features diagnostics`, with this PC's Linux-only additions on top (not part of this PR): the DXC fallback from #20 and the `VICTORY_NO_WATCHDOG` loader hook.

Credit for the fix goes to @desplmfao (Marvisak/VIctory#2143).

(Investigated and prepared with an AI coding assistant; all numbers are from runs on this PC.)

author: jaeyeol-yee
body:
A command started with `!` holds Pi until it ends, and nothing shows what is running. `/cl-run` starts the command in a multiplexer pane and returns at once.

![/cl-run and /cl-jobs demo](https://github.com/jaeyeol-yee/calliopi/blob/claude/friendly-babbage-g53r8m/assets/scenarios/cl-run.gif?raw=true)

## What it does

| Command | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `/cl-run <command>` | Runs beside Pi; focus stays in Pi. No confirmation. |
| `/cl-run -s <command>` | Runs in a background window that closes when done (tmux only). |
| `/cl-run -n <name> …` | Names the job. Default: the command's first two words (`npm test` → `npm-test`). |
| `/cl-run ? <words>` | The current model writes the command; it runs only after the user submits it in an editor (editable, Esc cancels). |
| `/cl-jobs` | Lists jobs with state and an output preview; pass output or the current screen to the conversation, go to the pane, stop, or forget. |

- When a job ends, Pi shows a notice and queues the exit code and the last 40 lines of output for the next turn. It does not wake the model.
- The rule for confirmation is who wrote the command: typed by the user → runs; written by a model → confirmed first. `??` is refused rather than run as a shell command.
- `?` sends the model file names in the working directory, package scripts, Makefile targets and earlier `/cl-run` commands there. No file contents.

## How

- A job is a directory (`$TMPDIR/calliopi-jobs-<uid>/<name>/`) with `meta.json`, `log`, `pid` and `exit`, so it is found by name without asking the multiplexer, and it outlives the Pi process.
- `bin/job-runner.ts` runs the command in its own pseudo-terminal inside the pane: the program still sees a terminal (colors, prompts, Ctrl+C) while its output is logged. `node-pty` moves from dev to runtime dependency of `calliopi-workflows` for this.
- The tmux adapter in `core` gains `openBackground`, `focus` and `capture`. They are optional on the `Multiplexer` interface; Rex and herdr do not have them.

## Demo recorder

The GIF needed two new scenario options:

- `multiplexer: tmux` runs Pi inside a private tmux server with its own config.
- `completions` answers one-off model requests an extension makes outside the conversation (the `?` inference).

The faux model now picks a turn's reply by the number of finished replies instead of the number of user messages, because messages an extension adds to a turn (a finished job's output) reach it as user messages too. `conversation` still records with this change; its committed GIF is untouched. The `demo` workflow installs tmux and fzf.

## Verified

- `npm run check` passes (workflows 39, core 34, ui 35, fanout 56, demo 12), including a test that drives `job-runner.ts` through the tmux adapter on a real tmux server.
- In a real Pi inside tmux 3.4: side pane, `-s`, completion notice, `/cl-jobs` share, screen share and stop.
- The demo recording runs the whole `?` flow against the faux model.

## Not verified

- `?` against a real model: the request was sent, but this environment has no model credentials. Reply handling is covered by unit tests and the faux model only.
- Rex and herdr: the side-pane path uses the same adapter call as `/cl-preview` but was not run with this command.
- macOS.

## Not in this PR

- A tool for the model to start jobs itself.
- Intercepting `!`.

author: seanhudson
body:
The runner side of #143, under Unreleased (to fold into 0.20.0).

- **Budget hook.** `RunnerOptions.budget(call)` is asked before each new answer (reused answers are free) with `{ runId, suite, operation, model, spentUsd }`. A returned reason stops the test with that reason as its error ("Stopped after 2 of 6 answers. Tests are stopped until 3:05…"), not "out of credits". A budget that throws lets the answer go ahead. `spendingBudget(spending)` builds one from an `EvalSpending`, so apps can drop the out-of-credits guard.
- **Stop between answers.** A running leg reads its run's status every `STOP_CHECK_MS` (2s); once it's not RUNNING it starts no more answers. Final run updates are guarded with `{ status: "RUNNING" }`, so a stop is never overwritten. `runner.stopTests(suiteKeys?)`; **Stop all tests** uses it when the app's `spending` has no `stopAll`.
- **Confirm.** Test every model asks for a second press above `CONFIRM_TESTS_USD` ($5) or when a price is unknown (`EvalApp.confirmTestsAboveUsd`).
- **After a deploy.** A failed test's row says "Test again: free, all 34 reused" / "~$0.10, 15 of 34 reused".

Example and starter wiring pass `budget: spendingBudget(spending)`; the example's `stopAll` calls `runner.stopTests()`.

Not done from #143: a per-test ceiling as a built-in (apps can do it in `budget`, which gets `spentUsd`), and folding per-search fees into `estimateCallCost`.

`npm run check` and `npm run e2e` pass; pages checked in NextGig on a local build.

author: groganz-bot[bot]
body:
The read tool `wordpress_site_tool_call` checks the catalog row it listed before it calls the site. The host resolves the call against its own catalog, which can change after the listing. Host pull request cinatra-ai/cinatra#4796 adds a guarded method, `invokeSiteToolGuarded`, that runs the call only when the row the host resolves now is still the listed row: same server, same raw annotations, and read class when asked. The host refuses with `catalog_entry_changed` otherwise. The same host refuses any `invokeSiteTool` call that carries a guard field (`guarded_call_required`). Today's connector sends `expectedRawAnnotations` through `invokeSiteTool`, so on that host every read would be refused.

What changes
- The read tool calls `invokeSiteToolGuarded` with the listed row's `serverId`, its `rawAnnotations` as `expectedRawAnnotations`, and `expectedClass: "read"`. It never calls `invokeSiteTool`.
- An unannotated known `ewpa/*` read on the default adapter server sends no `expectedClass`, because the host classifies a row without annotations as "write". The annotation guard (`{}` on the same server) still applies, so a row that gains annotations after the listing is refused.
- Host refusals become the tool's fixed refusals: `catalog_entry_changed` becomes "the site tool changed after it was listed", `catalog_entry_not_read` becomes the existing read-only refusal. Other errors pass on unchanged.
- `register.ts` binds the method with an inline presence test. On a host without it, the read tool is denied ("this Cinatra host does not enforce guarded site-tool calls") and nothing is sent. There is no fallback to the unguarded call.
- The guarded input type is declared in the connector's own deps type, so the connector builds against the published SDK. SDK imports stay type-only.
- The write tool and the post update helper keep `invokeSiteTool` and send no guard field. They sent none before this change either.

Host requirement and merge order
With this revision, the read tool needs a Cinatra host that has `invokeSiteToolGuarded`. On an older host the read tool is denied; listing and writing still work. Merge order: this pull request at any time, then host #4796, then the app pin of this revision after #4796.

Tests
- New `src/__tests__/site-tool-guarded-read.test.ts`: the read tool sends exactly the listed row's fields to the guarded method and never `invokeSiteTool`; without the method it is denied and nothing is called; `catalog_entry_changed` gives the tool's refusal and nothing else is called; the write tool and the post update helper send no guard field; `register(ctx)` denies on a host without the method and forwards unchanged on a host with it.
- The read-write split and passthrough tests now expect the guarded call.

Refs cinatra-ai/cinatra#3745

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **zams** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RiZpfzpFGLk8WJMKHzPkMJ?thread=cmsg_01RiZpfzpFGLk8WJMKHzPkMJSaBh8diW5wyJb6ffDGZL1a)_

## Qué cambia

En la vista de una colección del servidor:

- Junto a **Historia principal** aparece una insignia verde **✓ Completa** cuando todas las series de Kavita de esa sección tienen todos sus tomos publicados. Si la colección no tiene secciones, la insignia va bajo el nombre de la colección.
- Cada serie de la historia principal muestra debajo del título **✓ Todos los tomos** o **Faltan tomos · N de M**.

## De dónde sale

No se adivina por los títulos: que haya del 1 al 12 sin huecos no dice si la serie tiene 12 o 30 tomos. Se pregunta a Kavita (`/api/Series/metadata`):

- `publicationStatus = 2` (Completed): Kavita lo pone cuando la serie terminó **y** están todos los tomos (si terminó pero faltan, pone 4, Ended).
- `totalCount` y `maxCount`: completa si `maxCount >= totalCount`.

Si Kavita no sabe el total de una serie, no se muestra nada (mejor no prometer que está entera). La respuesta se guarda en localStorage (`yoru:kavita-serie-completa:v1`) para que la vista siga saliendo al instante y sin red; se refresca cada 6 h, como mucho 4 peticiones a la vez.

**Ojo:** en una biblioteca de EPUB, Kavita casi nunca sabe el total por sí solo. Para que se encienda la insignia hay que poner el *Publication Status* en *Completed* (o el total de tomos) en la ficha de la serie en Kavita.

## Archivos

- `frontend/utils/serieCompleta.ts` (nuevo): `estadoDeSerie` y el hook `useSeriesCompletas`.
- `frontend/utils/kavitaService.ts`, `frontend/types/integrations.ts`: leer `totalCount` y `maxCount`.
- `frontend/components/home/ServerViews.tsx`: insignia y texto por serie en `ServerCollectionView`.
- `frontend/components/home/yoru-shell.css`: estilo `.yoru-complete-badge` (tema oscuro y claro).

## Pruebas

- `tsc --noEmit` sin errores; `oxlint` sin avisos en los archivos tocados.
- Vista previa con Vite y caché sembrada: insignia en «Historia principal» con todas completas; sin insignia y «Faltan tomos · 2 de 3» cuando falta uno.
- Sin probar en teléfono ni contra el Kavita real.
