author: aerocommons-agents[bot]
body:
## Summary

**What changed:** `altd` now takes the ISA standard temperature from `PALT`, not `TALT`, and no longer waits for a middle input. The shipped config lists `PALT` and `OAT`.
**Why it is right:** the two new tests fail on `dev`. The first gets 7025.6 ft instead of 6788 ft, and in the second `DALT` is never published without `TALT`. Both pass here.
**Risk / not covered:** `DALT` moves by about 240 ft per 1,000 ft of TALT-PALT gap on installs that have a TALT writer. That move is the fix. Not checked on a bench.
**Your call:** none - merge when ready.

## The defect

`altDensity` computed `st = 15 - 1.98 * TALT / 1000` and added `120 * (OAT - st)` to `PALT`. ISA temperature is defined on pressure altitude, so a TALT-PALT gap biased `DALT` by about 2 degC, or 240 ft, per 1,000 ft. It also waited for `TALT`, a GPS (mavlink) or Dynon key. A panel with pressure and OAT but no GPS never got `DALT` at all. That is the one cost of removing Dynon's indicated `TALT` write (AER-6458).

Example: `PALT` 5,000 ft, `TALT` 6,000 ft, OAT 20 degC. Expected 5,000 + 120 x (20 - 5.1) = 6,788 ft. `dev` gives 7,025.6 ft.

## The change

- `compute.py` `altDensity`: `PALT` is the first input and is used in both terms. `OAT` is the last input. A middle input is ignored: it is not waited on and its flags do not reach `DALT`. An installed copy of the old `inputs: ["PALT","TALT","OAT"]` keeps working with `TALT` ignored.
- `config/connections/compute.yaml`: `inputs: ["PALT","OAT"]`.
- `writers.yaml`: the `DALT` datum is `density altitude: altd from PALT and OAT`. No key was added or renamed. `DALT`'s range and units are unchanged.
- Docs: `doc/plugins/compute.rst` gave the inputs as `[PALT, ALT_MSL, OAT]`, with the standard temperature taken from `ALT_MSL`. `docs/wiki/Architecture.md` said `TALT` feeds `DALT`. Both are corrected. (The RDAM-12 map comment that said the same was rewritten by #253. Merging `dev` in took #253's wording, so this PR no longer touches that file.)

## Evidence

Before the fix, on `dev` (`bfb7e0a`) with the new tests:

```
E       assert 7025.6 == 6788.0 ± 0.006788          (test_alt_density_takes_standard_temperature_from_palt)
E           assert 0.0 == 6788.0 ± 0.006788         (test_alt_density_publishes_without_talt)
2 failed, 2 passed, 97 deselected
```

After the fix:

- `tests/plugins/compute` together with `tests/test_one_writer.py`: 220 passed.
- `tools/check_key_writers.py`: 0 failures.
- After merging `dev` at `569479a` (#253, TALT sources) into the branch: `tests/plugins/compute`, `tests/arch` and `tests/test_one_writer.py`, 220 passed. `check_key_writers`, 0 failures. `test_one_writer[default.yaml]` first failed three times in a row with demo not attributed. It then passed twice on the branch and twice on `dev`, run back to back. That is the known load-sensitive case, where demo has not made its first write inside the 25 s window.
- Other tests that read `compute.yaml`, `writers.yaml` or `DALT`: 485 passed, across 11 files (`tests/arch/test_key_writers.py`, `tests/test_database.py`, the canfix shipped-map writer tests, demo, flightplan engine and others).

`test_alt_density_publishes_without_talt` runs both the old three-input form and the shipped two-input form. It writes only `PALT` and `OAT`, and expects `DALT` = 6788 with good flags. In the three-input form it then writes a bad, failed `TALT` and expects `DALT` to be unchanged and still good. The existing flag-path test took its `bad` flag from the middle input, so it now uses the two-input form and gets `bad` from `OAT`.

## Not covered

- Not run on a bench. The change is arithmetic in one compute function, and the unit tests drive it through the real callback signature.
- No other repo reads the `altd` inputs. On pyEfis `dev`, `DALT` appears only as a readout in two screen includes, and `TALT` appears nowhere (checked with `git grep`).

Fixes BACKLOG `DALT1`, AER-6594.

Several reviewer agents in `.claude/agents/` and the next-issue skill restated the `AGENTS.md` invariants in their own words ("the BankID receipt text is the only exception", "keys live only in the URL fragment or in browser memory", "everything runs fully local"). Decision record 0012 added a sanctioned exception, so these stale copies made lanes and the verifier raise sanctioned behaviour as false blockers. `AGENTS.md` says an exception makes every absolute that covers it untrue in `.claude/` as well.

Each lane that judges the invariants now carries the same instruction instead of its own copy:

> Read the Invariants section of `AGENTS.md` and the decision records it names as they stand at the merge base, not in the working tree (`git show "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)":<path>`). Data in a place an exception allows is not a finding. The same data anywhere else, or a change that widens an exception or adds one, is.

- Records are read at the merge base, not in the working tree, so a diff cannot sanction itself by editing `AGENTS.md` or a record such as 0012.
- Each lane keeps its own list of places to flag. A sentence that says data never goes somewhere is scoped "Outside those places", so no copy states an absolute that an exception makes untrue.
- The three "fully local" copies now say "tests and demos", as `AGENTS.md` does.
- next-issue step 5 passes the `AGENTS.md` Invariants section verbatim.

Review: review-changes ran three rounds with the Code Reviewer, over-engineering, Software Architect and Application Security Engineer lanes. The last round found 0 blockers and 0 majors. Earlier rounds caught some real gaps:
- lanes exempting a whole emailed-link flow instead of the places 0012 allows;
- AGENTS.md and the records read from the working tree;
- the emailed link's mark flagged as a key;
- a restored BankID line that contradicted 0002.

Follow-ups (minors, not fixed here):
- The instruction is copied into 10 lane files. One copy in the review-changes skill, with the merge-base sha written into every reviewer prompt, would remove the duplication and the hardcoded `origin/main` (if `git merge-base` fails, the command quietly reads the index).
- `reality-checker.md` L39 forbids dropping an `AGENTS.md` violation, so a pull request that adds an exception the documented way (new record plus `AGENTS.md` edit) can end the fix loop only at the round cap. Decide whether the main session should take such a finding to the user instead.
- `<merge-base>` placeholders on unchanged lines: `test-results-analyzer.md` L16, `reality-checker.md` L26.
- `accessibility-auditor.md` L22 defers to the Invariants section without the merge-base pin.
- `application-security-engineer.md` L19's signaling clause repeats L16.

Needs maintainers approval (`.claude/**`).

author: thuram-nana
body:
## What this changes

First, **read-only** slice of the 90-day evidence-retention feature (V13). Adds `framework.v2.evidence.retention`: it classifies each engagement's raw `targets/<slug>/evidence/<action_id>/` dir as **KEEP** (an active finding references that `action_id`) or a **SWEEP candidate** (orphan scan traffic), with byte totals, and renders it as a dry-run report — runnable as a module: `python3 -m framework.v2.evidence.retention [--json] [--targets-root DIR]`.

**It deletes nothing, writes nothing, sends no traffic.** It's the decision-independent core that any eventual sweep shares, so you can see exactly what a sweep *would* remove before any of the hard choices are made.

**Deliberately NOT in this PR** (they need your decisions / legal wording, and are tracked below): the actual deletion (hard-delete vs crypto-shred), the cross-plane "engagement ended ≥90 days ago" trigger, the top-level `framework.v2` subcommand wiring (which also obligates the capability-briefing + dispatch-set guards), and the `/privacy` + ADR 0008 updates.

## Type

- [ ] Bug / production fix
- [x] New capability (additive / opt-in, default-OFF)
- [ ] Docs / tests only
- [ ] Refactor (no behaviour change)

## Doctrine & safety checklist (required)

- [x] **Authorized-use / defensive posture only.** A data-minimisation / privacy maintenance read; no offensive capability.
- [x] **Prove-don't-guess, near-zero false positives.** No new detection/FACT. Classification is conservative: a dir is a sweep candidate ONLY when NO active finding references it, and a missing report snapshot keeps ALL of that engagement's evidence.
- [x] **Two-env boundary intact (FATAL-2).** Engine-side module; imports only `..common.paths`. No `sigil.*` import; no `framework.v2.evidence.cli` import (the `_findings` shape is mirrored inline).
- [x] **Determinism on any signed / decision path.** Pure, deterministic (sorted output; no wallclock, no RNG).
- [x] **Additive / opt-in.** A manual read-only CLI — inert unless explicitly run; nothing auto-invokes it; it is not imported by `evidence/__init__`, so the scan/engage/gate path never loads it.
- [x] **`make gate` stays byte-identical.** New module off the gate path; no new `OracleKind`.
- [x] **Tests included and green**, with safety controls: a `deletes-nothing` assertion, fail-safe on a missing report, backed-vs-orphan classification, repo totals, and text/JSON CLI output.
- [x] **Honest docs.** Module docstrings state it is read-only and that the destructive sweep + trigger are a later, gated slice; no overclaiming, no new product claim.

## Evidence

```
$ python3 -m pytest framework/v2/evidence/tests/test_retention.py -q
........                                                                  [100%]
# 8 passed

$ python3 -m framework.v2.evidence.retention --targets-root <synthetic>
evidence retention — DRY RUN (read-only; nothing is deleted)
  acme: keep 1 dir(s) / 8 B, sweep-candidate 1 dir(s) / 12 B  [report]
  TOTAL: sweep-candidate 1 dir(s) / 12 B; keep 1 dir(s) across 1 engagement(s)
```

## Residual / follow-ups

Later V13 slices, each pending an owner decision:
- **Delete mechanism** — hard-delete orphan evidence vs crypto-shred (ADR 0008 is whole-engagement; the keep-some rule needs finer granularity).
- **"Ended ≥90d" trigger** — map the sovereign-plane `assessment_outcome` completion (keyed `cust_<hash>`) to the engine-plane `targets/<name>/` evidence tree.
- **`/privacy` + a new ADR** — a time-based timer reverses ADR 0008's "no timer"; reconcile the 30-day / "not removed automatically" wording. (Legal — owner/counsel.)
- **Top-level CLI subcommand** + its capability-briefing / dispatch-set guard updates.

body: Closes #14722 Work item 3b of the fleet transport & pooling design (#13752, §3.5 step 1): the #13717 route-form walker is the primitive's first adopter. - Tier 0 (`fleet laptop exec`, `crates/fleet/src/laptop.rs`) now selects through `fleet-pool`: T1–T3 are members under one host group, the pool picks each attempt and records it in its decision log, and each outcome is classified back into the pool — `Served` is a success (never advances, whatever the exit code), `Failed`/`TimedOut` are serve-failures (always advance). - The walker's own ladder code is removed: the hand-rolled loop over forms and the `WALK_ORDER` constant in `forms.rs` are gone. The only walker-specific piece left is the attempted-set strategy (`walker-ordered`), the same shape the crate's walker oracle tests use — a form already attempted in this walk is not re-selected, because a single walk tries each tier at most once even though a first serve-failure only demotes the member in the pool's longer-lived state machine. - `fleet-pool` is linked only through the `laptop` feature, so the connect variant does not carry it. - Tests: four unit tests in `laptop.rs` script the attempt function and name the #13717 oracle — serves via the first form and names it; advances only on failure-to-serve (failure + timeout); never advances on a served result; exhausts each form exactly once when nothing serves. The crate-level oracle tests in `crates/fleet-pool/tests/walker.rs` already bind the same cases against the pool directly. Verification: remote only, via the fleet-command.yml fallback (queue dispatch is blocked by the #13185 TLS defect) — run id to be noted on the PR when it lands; this PR's CI also applies. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-25T15:53:22Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "htch-runtime", "worktree": "/home/hatch", "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": { "kind": "worktree", "id": "/home/hatch", "repo": "developing-today/code", "branch": "main", "sha": "bbfc8aa3a3b4f3e3d399b7e76beb6962c0daa5b9" }, "auth_subject": "xaltha", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? author: kongkang
body:
## 变更概述

Refs #9, #10, #11, #12, #13

本 PR 针对 Windows 11 + Python 数据管线客户反馈以及移动端同步提出的 SDK 增强需求，将版本预升至 **`0.0.10`**（暂不打 tag，待真机回归完成后再标定 `v0.0.10`），完成以下修复与新增能力（保持既有公共 API 100% 向后兼容）：

1. **Windows BLE 扫描修复（Refs #9, #11）**
2. **音频调理、采样率重采样与 `sample_rate` 元数据透传（Refs #10, #12）**
3. **24-bit RTC 1024s 回绕时间轴重建（Refs #10, #12）**
4. **类型化设备配置辅助方法（Refs #10；对齐固件 `dyj-hd-v2` PR #22 / 主控 `0.3.20`）**
5. **`dyj_cli --json` 结构化输出与 `decode` 增强（Refs #10, #13）**
6. **官方 Python 绑定子包 `python/`（PyO3 `abi3-py310` + maturin，Refs #10）**

---

## 详细改动

### 1. Windows BLE 扫描修复（`src/btleplug_transport.rs`）
- `DeviceManager::scan` 与 `DeviceManager::scan_dfu_targets` 统一改用 `ScanFilter::default()`，在扫描窗口内通过 `adapter.events()` 收集活跃外设 ID（获取失败时优雅退回全量外设列表），避免返回过时系统缓存设备，也避免 Windows WinRT 按 Service UUID 过滤丢弃 ADV/Scan Response 分包。
- 提取纯匹配函数做应用层过滤并补齐单元测试：
  - `match_card_candidate`：支持仅 ADV 含 `DYJ` 前缀名称（大小写不敏感、排除 `DFU` 前缀）或仅 Scan Response 含 `NUS_SERVICE_UUID`（缺名或空名时兜底 `"DYJV2"`）。
  - `match_dfu_candidate`：支持 `DFU_SERVICE_UUID` 或 `DFU` 前缀名称（空名兜底 `DFU_ADVERTISED_NAME`）。

### 2. 音频预处理、重采样与 `sample_rate` 元数据透传（`src/audio.rs`、`src/recording.rs`、`src/types.rs`、`src/lib.rs`）
- 保持 `apm_to_wav(apm, wav)` 签名与默认行为完全不变。
- `DeviceInfo` 与 `FileEntry` 新增 `sample_rate: Option<u32>`（同时兼容 `sample_rate` 与 `sampleRate` JSON 字段名），供上层优先按 `.txt` 旁车或设备信息中的 `sample_rate`（`16000` vs 历史固件 `15578`）判定是否重采样。
- 新增并公开重导出 `AudioProcessOptions`（含 `Default`、`conditioned_for_asr()`、`with_source_sample_rate()`）、`condition_speech_samples`（12.7 Hz 一阶高通去直流 + 50ms 帧 800 样本 P95 RMS + `< 0.00085` 静音门控不放大 + `0.00085..0.005` 软膝盖 `2x..10x` 增益上限、目标 P95 RMS `0.065` + `±0.80` 平滑软限幅）、`resample_linear_i16`、`process_pcm_samples`、`apm_to_wav_with_options`。

### 3. 1024s 回绕时间轴重建（`src/types.rs`、`src/lib.rs`）
- 新增并重导出 `ReconstructedFileEntry` 与 `reconstruct_session_timeline(entries: &[FileEntry]) -> Vec<ReconstructedFileEntry>`：
  - 按 `session`（8 位 hex，大小写无关归一）分组，同组严格按 `seq` 升序；
  - 检测到 `start_at` 倒退或折叠异常时，以首段可信 `start_at` 为锚点，按段长 `size / 8000` 秒（至少 1 秒）累加推算后续各段 `effective_start_at` 并置 `reconstructed = true`。

### 4. 类型化设备配置辅助方法（`src/device.rs`）
- 在 `DyjDevice` 上封装 `mic_gain()` / `set_mic_gain(mode)`、`silence_stop_minutes()` / `set_silence_stop_minutes(minutes)`、`local_only()` / `set_local_only(enabled)`，底层复用 `config_value`（`CONFIG_GET`）与 `set_config`（`CONFIG_SET`），对应固件配置键 `mic_gain`、`silence_stop_min`、`local_only`，并补充 `MockTransport` 单测。

### 5. `dyj_cli --json` 与 `decode` 增强（`examples/dyj_cli.rs`、`examples/common/mod.rs`）
- 新增全局 `--json` 选项：`--json` 开启时 tracing 日志输出至 `stderr` 保持 `stdout` 为纯净 JSON；`scan`、`dfu-scan`、`files`（集成 `reconstruct_session_timeline`）、`decode`、`take`、`take-oldest` 等命令输出标准 JSON，报错时于 `stderr` 输出 JSON 错误对象。
- `decode` 子命令新增可选 `--normalize` 与 `--source-rate <hz>` 参数，调用 `apm_to_wav_with_options`。

### 6. 官方 Python 绑定子包 `python/`（`python/Cargo.toml`、`python/pyproject.toml`、`python/src/lib.rs`、`python/README.md`）
- 独立 `[workspace]` 声明，不干扰根 Cargo workspace、不强依赖 `libpython`。
- 基于 PyO3 `abi3-py310` + `maturin` 暴露 `scan`、`connect`、`CardDevice`、`apm_to_wav`、`reconstruct_session_timeline` 与 `AccessPointClient`。

---

## 在另一台电脑（Windows 11 / Python 3.10+）上的测试指南

### 环境准备
```bash
git clone https://github.com/ReAI-com/reai-card-sdk.git
cd reai-card-sdk
# 需要 Rust >= 1.93；如需测试 Python 绑定，需要 Python >= 3.10 与 pip
```

### 测试 1：本地单元测试与静态检查
```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-targets
```
- **预期**：`src/lib.rs`、`examples/dyj_cli.rs`、`src/btleplug_transport.rs` 等全部单测通过，0 警告。

### 测试 2：Windows 11 BLE 扫描与 DFU 扫描（验证 #9 / #11）
1. 确保 DYJ-HD v2 录音卡开机，且**未被手机 App / 其他电脑软件独占 BLE 连接**。
2. 运行：
   ```bash
   cargo run --example dyj_cli -- --json scan
   ```

The Reminders coordinator fetched every list in one refresh. Accounts with hundreds of lists issued hundreds of CloudKit requests and hit the 300 second timeout, so no to-do entities were ever created.

author: chris-wolfgang
body:
Part of #128. Stacked on #215.

## What

`ModelConventions.Verify(model)` returns one sentence for every place where a model breaks `docs/DATABASE-CONVENTIONS.md` (ADR 0004 §12). `ModelConventionsTests` asserts that it returns nothing for `BarefootDbContext`'s model.

| Convention | What fails |
|---|---|
| schema | a table outside the default schema |
| names | a table, column, key, foreign key or index whose name is not the one `SchemaNames` gives it |
| name length | a name longer than 128 characters, the most SQL Server accepts |
| keys | a primary key that is not one `Guid` column, on any table but `setting` |
| referential integrity | a foreign key that does not restrict its delete |
| concurrency | a `Version` that is not a `long` concurrency token |
| time | a `DateTime` column; a `DateTimeOffset` not stored through `UtcInstantConverter` to the millisecond |

- A problem reads, for example, `ParcelLabel: the foreign key on SenderId deletes with Cascade, not Restrict.`
- `SchemaNames` now exposes the name of each kind of object (`TableName`, `ColumnName`, `KeyName`, `ForeignKeyName`, `IndexName`), so naming and checking use one rule. `SchemaNames.Apply` behaves as before; its tests are unchanged.
- `DATABASE-CONVENTIONS.md` no longer says the check "arrives later"; each "Enforced by" line says what the check fails.

## Choices of mine to check

- **The list of checks.** Gap D-10 says the documents never list what `Verify` checks and asks to confirm "naming, `Restrict`, key type, concurrency token and UTC instants". I implemented that list and added the default schema and the 128-character limit. The gap note itself is not edited here.
- **Not checked:** string lengths, money precision and "every index cites its query". The first two are pinned by `BarefootModelTests` and `BarefootDbContextTests`; the third is a review rule.
- **`setting` is exempt from the key rule by type**, because the conventions name it as the one table keyed by a name.
- **`AppUser.Oid` passes** as a `Guid` key; the check does not require the column to be called `id`.

## Verified

On Windows, at this head:

- Release build with no warnings.
- 793 tests pass (Contracts 140, Core 382, Data 198, test kit 9, architecture 64).
- 100 % line coverage on every project.
- InspectCode reports no findings.
- Stryker on the Data tests: a full run gave 259 killed, 14 counted as timeouts and 1 survivor in `ModelConventions.cs` (the separator between the columns of a foreign key). A test for a two-column foreign key was added, and a run on `ModelConventions.cs` alone then killed all 52 of its mutants with no timeout. The full run was not repeated after that test.

## Not verified

- No local Linux run (Docker was not running); CI's Linux stage covers it.
- Nothing has run on SQL Server.

author: mrnasil
body:
An old tool output spilled to disk was saved as `.whycodes/scratch/artifacts/<tool_call_id>.txt`, and an existing file with that name was kept as it was. Tool call ids repeat:
- Gemini numbers its calls from `gcall_1` in every stream;
- fallback ids restart;
- every session in the project shares the directory.

A later result's pointer could therefore send `read` to an earlier call's output, which is quietly wrong context for the model.

The file name now carries a stable FNV-1a hash of the body (`<id>-<hash>.txt`). A reused id with a new body gets its own file, and the same body still maps to the same file.

Tests: a reused id with two different bodies gives two files, each holding its own output. The spill and lifecycle tests now look artifacts up by the new names. All 176 session tests pass.

```bash
go build -o bin/truss ./cmd/truss

bin/truss runs               # error + hint: start it with: truss daemon start

```

## What changed
Spec: `specs/025-cli-tidy/spec.md`. Tier 2 (CLI usage/output). The commands keep their names (maintainer's decision).

- Advice at the end of an error goes on a `hint:` line, for every command including `truss run`.
- `truss completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell` completes commands, subcommands and flow names. Flow names are treated as data: nothing in a file name runs, and names are inserted quoted.
- `truss runs -n` is `--limit`. `truss help exit-codes` is new.
- Unchanged: stdout of commands (except the help text), JSON, exit codes.

author: jorenham
body:
| `hyp3f2(½, −½, −½; 1, 1; z)` | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `z = 0.999999` | NaN | 1.1329536620052636 |
| `z = 1` | NaN | 1.1329538074558454 |
| Nonfinite results on 1,905 near-one inputs and overlap controls | 644 | 0 |
| Geometric mean / peak finite relative error | 1.54e−16 / 2.73e−16 | 1.91e−16 / 7.92e−16 |

This recovers the rank-one, two-dimensional Gaussian distance correlation curve of Dueck et al. At canonical correlation `r = 0.9999999`, the reconstructed distance correlation is 0.6904817101315677. The paper used a matrix-argument implementation. Its dotted curve reduces to this scalar function at `z = r²` and `z = r²/4`. [Corollary 3.2 and Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/html/1210.2482)

Lowering two upper parameters in Clausen’s square gives a sum of three squares involving complete elliptic integrals. On CPU 30 the `z = 0.99` call takes 48 µs → 0.15 µs. At `z = 0.999999` the former 11 ms decline takes 0.083 µs. Four ordinary or unrelated controls stayed within 1.1%.

The panel samples binary64 `z` from just below 0.99 through 1 and uses 180-bit Arb elliptic references. The geometric mean floors finite errors at unit roundoff and omits the 644 baseline NaNs. Direct interval summation of the positive defining series independently gives correctly rounded references 1.1329536620052632 and 1.132953807455845 at the two inputs above. All 37 standard accuracy rows (71,000 inputs) and all four `just pfq-map` SVGs are unchanged.

Refs #1469.

Offen bleiben die vollständigen Backend- und Frontend-Testläufe, die PostgreSQL-Migrationstests der Abschlussprüfung und der vollständige Browserlauf. Beim Browserlauf fehlt lokal Playwrights Chromium Headless Shell (Build 1254). Typecheck, Produktionsbuild, Backup-Tests und `git diff --check` waren erfolgreich. Die fachliche Prüfung auf DEV erfolgt separat.

## Merge-Abschlussprüfung für `a8d3c06` — abgebrochen

GitHub meldete den PR als offen und mergefähig gegen `dev`. Der geprüfte `dev`-Stand `60cf5aa35221f9228d4cdaf71842c7c1d984becc` ist Vorfahr des PR-Heads und blieb remote unverändert.

| Prüfung | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| Backend gesamt auf isoliertem PostgreSQL | Nach 135 bestandenen Tests unterbrochen. Keine vollständige Auswertung. |
| PostgreSQL-Migrationstests | Im abgebrochenen Gesamtprüflauf nicht erreicht. |
| Backup-Tests | 35 Tests und 14 Subtests bestanden. |
| Frontend-Tests | 147 bestanden, 29 laufende Testfälle abgebrochen, 0 übersprungen unter den erfassten Tests. |
| Chromium-Browsertests | 1 bestanden, 1 fehlgeschlagen, 2 abgebrochen, 0 übersprungen. Der Backup-Browsertest konnte Playwrights Chromium Headless Shell (Build 1254) nicht starten, weil die ausführbare Datei lokal fehlt. Ein separater Browserstart bestätigte den Umgebungsfehler. |
| Typecheck, Produktionsbuild und `git diff --check` | Bestanden. |

Der Merge wurde gemäß Abbruchbedingung nicht ausgeführt. Kein Deployment, keine Migration einer laufenden Datenbank und keine PROD-Änderungen.

## Änderung

Bei der gemeinsamen Prüfung kann eine neue, eindeutig identifizierte Person mit gleichen gültigen Aufenthaltsdaten und dem Quellwiderspruch „Double shared“ / „No room“ einmalig mit `UNRESOLVED` importiert werden. Beide Originalmeldungen und Competition-Memberships bleiben erhalten. Die Klärung bleibt sichtbar. Bis zur ausdrücklichen Entscheidung im vorhandenen Athletendialog sind Zuweisungsvorschläge und Buchungen gesperrt.

## Abschlussprüfung auf `32fd703` und Folgecommit `a8d3c06`

| Operative Entscheidung nach Erstimport | Verhalten auf `32fd703` | Ergebnis mit Folgecommit |
|---|---|---|
| `REQUIRED` | Identischer Reimport erhält `MANUAL` | Regression bestanden |
| `NO_ROOM` | Manuell speicherbar, Reimportfreigabe blockiert | Identischer Reimport erhält `NO_ROOM / MANUAL` |
| `NO_DISPO` | Im Athletendialog vorgesehen und speicherbar, Reimportfreigabe blockiert | Identischer Reimport erhält `NO_DISPO / MANUAL` |
| Keine Entscheidung | Identischer Reimport möglich | `UNRESOLVED / IMPORT` und Klärungsbedarf bleiben erhalten |

Die bestehende Prüfung für einen bereits importierten Quellkonflikt verwendet die vorhandene Liste zulässiger manueller Entscheidungen. Dateifingerprints, Identität und Buchungsschutz greifen weiterhin. Regressionen prüfen die unveränderten Originalversionen, Competition-Memberships, den Schutz einer vorhandenen Buchung und die sportliche Quotenbasis. Sieben gezielte Backend-Tests auf isoliertem PostgreSQL und `git diff --check` bestanden. Keine Migration im Folgecommit.

## Abschlussregressionen in `32fd703`

- Ein importierter Athlet mit `UNRESOLVED` bleibt in der gemeldeten Personen- und Athletenbasis sowie in seiner sportlichen Quote enthalten. Die operative Projektion meldet für ihn keinen offenen Unterkunftsbedarf, keinen ausgewählten Platz und keinen EZ-Bedarf. Die Quotenberechnung ist unverändert.
- Nach der ausdrücklichen Entscheidung `REQUIRED` im Athletendialog kann dieselbe gemeinsame Meldung erneut freigegeben und importiert werden. Der Folgeimport behält die Person, beide Memberships und `REQUIRED` mit Herkunft `MANUAL`. Der bestehende Dateifingerprint und die zuvor importierte gemeinsame Revision belegen die Übereinstimmung. Geänderte Dateien und vorhandene Buchungen bleiben für diesen Konflikt gesperrt. Auch die Schutzregeln für einzelne Teilimporte bleiben bestehen.
- Backend-Folgelauf mit Import, Teilimport, Unterkunftsbedarf, Reimport und Abfragebudgets: 185 bestanden, 5 mangels Originaldateien für AUT/JPN übersprungen. `git diff --check` bestanden.

## Migration und vorherige Prüfungen

Alembic `20261125_01` erweitert ausschließlich den operativen Check-Constraint. Der Quellwert-Constraint bleibt erhalten. Upgrade, alle vier gültigen Werte, Ablehnung ungültiger Werte und Downgrade wurden lokal auf isoliertem PostgreSQL geprüft. Bei vorhandenen `UNRESOLVED`-Werten wird der Downgrade abgelehnt und die Werte bleiben erhalten.

Auf `6070d13` bestanden 273 Backend-Tests, 331 Frontend-Tests, Chromium-Regression, Typecheck und Produktionsbuild. Der Italien-Fall verwendet synthetische Quellen. Die Fehlerklassifikation steht in `docs/import-clarifications-ux.md`.

## Lokaler Recheck-Vergleich der ursprünglichen Änderung

Flask-Testclient und lokales PostgreSQL. Dieselben synthetischen Teilmeldungen, je ein Request pro Upload-Reihenfolge. Ausgangsstand `d746468`, Vergleichsstand `6070d13`.

| Upload-Reihenfolge | Vorher | Nachher | SQL-Anweisungen vorher / nachher |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SB → FS | 234 ms | 276 ms | 134 / 134 |
| FS → SB | 219 ms | 275 ms | 134 / 134 |

Die zwei Einzelmessungen erlauben keine Aussage über die Laufzeit unter Produktionslast.

Kein Merge, kein Deployment und keine PROD-Änderungen.

author: alexconrey
body:
## Summary

Every plugin call builds a new extism plugin (`invoke()` in `src/plugins.rs`), which compiles the plugin's WebAssembly and extism's kernel. With no cache option set, extism uses wasmtime's disk cache in its default location, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wasmtime` or `$HOME/.cache/wasmtime`. When that directory can't be created (a read-only root filesystem, or a `$HOME` the process can't write), `Plugin::new` returns an error, so **every plugin call fails** with `plugin.load_failed`. This answers the question in #366 and does the "set the cache explicitly" part of #392.

Now deckwatch picks the cache itself, once at startup, from `DECKWATCH_CACHE_DIR` (`--cache-dir`):

| `DECKWATCH_CACHE_DIR` | Plugin calls compile with | Startup log |
|---|---|---|
| unset or empty | `with_cache_disabled()` | one info line saying how to turn the cache on |
| set and usable | `with_cache_config(<dir>/wasmtime-cache.toml)`: wasmtime's cache in `<dir>/wasmtime` | one info line |
| set but unusable | `with_cache_disabled()` | one warning with the reason |

The directory counts as usable when all four of these work:
- deckwatch creates `<dir>/wasmtime`;
- it writes a file there;
- it writes `<dir>/wasmtime-cache.toml`;
- it loads that file the way plugin calls do: it compiles an empty module through `PluginBuilder::with_cache_config(..).compile()`, so extism hands the file to `wasmtime::Cache::from_file`.

**The cache never makes a plugin call fail.** wasmtime reads the config file again on every compile, so the cache can also break after startup, for example if the file is deleted. When a compile fails with the cache, deckwatch retries it without the cache. If the retry works, deckwatch warns once and stops using the cache until it restarts. A module that is really broken fails both times and reports its own error.

## Design notes

- **New module:** `src/plugin_cache.rs` adds `CompileCache`, with `resolve()` called at startup and `compile(builder)` called per call.
- **How the cache reaches calls:** the resolved cache is stored on `PluginTelemetry`. That struct is already in `AppState` and already reaches every call as `call.telemetry`, the same way `call_timeout` does.
  - Plugin calls never read the environment.
  - In the call path, only `invoke()` and its one caller line in `call_export` change. No plugin call sites or signatures change.
- **#395:** it has merged since this PR was opened. This branch now includes it (`origin/main` merged in, no conflicts), and the full lib suite passes on the merged branch. #395's `OwnedPluginCall` clones `PluginTelemetry`, so the cache follows calls onto the blocking pool.
- **Config keys:** in wasmtime 49.0.7 the `[cache]` table uses `deny_unknown_fields` and has no `enabled` key. Older configs said `enabled = true`, which now fails the whole file.
  - deckwatch writes only `directory`.
  - wasmtime requires `directory` to be absolute, so a relative `DECKWATCH_CACHE_DIR` is made absolute first.
  - The path is escaped as a TOML string.
- **Config file location:** the config file sits next to `<dir>/wasmtime`, not inside it, because wasmtime's cleanup deletes files it doesn't recognize in its cache directory.
- **Empty values:** `Config::cache_dir` is an `OsString`, because clap's `PathBuf` parser refuses an empty value, which would stop deckwatch from starting. An empty value means off.
- **Cost:**
  - With the cache on, each compile reads the small config file and checks the directory, then loads the cached artifact. #392 measured about 3 ms per call this way, against 45–62 ms for a full compile.
  - With the cache off, wasmtime no longer starts a cache worker thread on every call.

## Chart

- **New `cache` values:** `enabled: true`, `mountPath: /var/cache/deckwatch`, `sizeLimit: 1Gi`. When enabled, the chart mounts an emptyDir at `mountPath` and sets `DECKWATCH_CACHE_DIR` to it.
- **Non-root pods:** an emptyDir is writable for any `runAsUser` and also works with `readOnlyRootFilesystem` (#366).
- **Size limit:** the default is `1Gi` because wasmtime's own soft limit is 512 MiB, enforced by a cleanup that runs at most hourly, and Kubernetes evicts a pod whose emptyDir grows past its limit. An empty `sizeLimit` renders `emptyDir: {}`.
- **Replicas:** each pod has its own cache, so no shared volume is needed. The cache survives container restarts and starts empty on a new pod.

## Upgrade note

extism used to cache compiled plugins under `$HOME` by default. Now there is no cache unless `DECKWATCH_CACHE_DIR` is set. The chart sets it; installs that don't use the chart should set it themselves. This is in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.

## Testing

- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` all pass (1204 lib tests with main merged in).
- **`src/plugin_cache_tests.rs`** (tempdirs, with configs loaded through extism):
  - unset or empty: off, with the info line;
  - writable: on; the config file has `[cache]` and an absolute `directory`, wasmtime loads it and writes into `<dir>/wasmtime`, and nothing else is left in `<dir>`;
  - a path under a regular file (can't create) or a read-only `<dir>/wasmtime` (can't write): off, with one warning;
  - quotes and backslashes in the path survive the config file;
  - the startup check refuses a config that says `enabled = true`;
  - a cache that breaks after startup turns itself off with one warning;
  - a module that doesn't compile keeps its own error, and the cache stays on.
- **Funnel tests with the fixture plugin** (`src/plugins_funnel_tests.rs`):
  - an `apply()` call succeeds when the cache directory is unusable;
  - with the cache on, a call compiles into `<dir>/wasmtime`, and calls still succeed after the config file is deleted.
- **Unwritable `$HOME`** (pointed at a read-only directory):
  - a build without this change fails 36 plugin tests with `plugin.load_failed: the WASM module failed to load: failed to create cache directory: …/BytecodeAlliance.wasmtime: Permission denied`;
  - with this change, the full lib suite passes.
- **Chart:**
  - `helm lint`;
  - `helm template` with the defaults, `cache.enabled=false`, `cache.sizeLimit=`, and the cache combined with the registry, database and extra-CA volumes;
  - `cache.mountPath=` fails with a message.

Refs #366, #392.

author: lkkolki
body:
﻿## Problem

The KM `vsip-memsrc` model only used the first 64 B of a vector for a write or read. Any burst of more than two beats (the supersmasher `f2soc_*` cfgs with 16 or 32 beats) therefore sent or checked the wrong data, and the test failed.

## Cause

In `mem_source_wr.sv` a FIFO entry holds the address plus 16 data dwords (512 bit). The data FIFO is popped after every 512 bit, that is after every two 256-bit beats. A burst of N beats therefore uses `ceil(N/2)` consecutive vectors. The address comes from the first vector and the data from all of them. The model did not do this.

## Change (`vsip-memsrc/vsip_memsrc.dml`)

- Decode the write length (`xlen[7:0]`) and read length (`xlen[31:24]`); beats = len + 1.
- Add op 3 (write burst).
- Read the burst data from consecutive vectors, two 256-bit beats per vector.
- Skip the vectors a burst used, so the next op starts after them.
- Scale `pv_cycle_cnt` by the vectors used.
- Log `xlen`, `wlen`, `rlen` at start.
- Short README section on bursts.

Single-beat and two-beat behaviour is unchanged.

## Testing

Simics 7.116 KM model, a private build with this change, stock guest image, supersmasher with `layout = "km"`.

- `km/f2soc/*` cfgs: 21 of 21 PASS. The stock model fails the burst cfgs.
- `f2soc_sdram_write_read_1024_cachelines_16.cfg`: 8 loops, awvalid 64, wvalid 2048, arvalid 64, rvalid 2048. This matches the 128 write vectors, 8 AW per loop of 32 beats each, that the RTL gives.
- Negative control: a corrupted data dword in vector 138 makes the cfg FAIL, reported against vector 138.

## Not covered

- The read side (`mem_source_rd.sv`) was not compared with the RTL; the read burst follows the same two-beats-per-vector rule.
- The RTL unit test was not run (no VCS here).
- KM has a fixed 256-bit interface; cfgs with another `interface_width` do not apply.

author: mikelane
body:
## Summary

- The live wait scenarios ended as `SETUP` because the harness's own appended system prompt ("Do only what the typed prompt says...") told the waiting session to decline the peer's message. A peer message arrives as a `cross-session-message`, not a typed prompt. A receiver transcript from 2026-11-23 shows the model's reply: "I didn't run `sleep 14`. My instructions for this session say to do only what the user typed, and this request came from another session."
- The session that `start_waiting_handoff` starts now gets one more sentence in its single `--append-system-prompt`. The sentence names its peer session (by `from-name`) as a source of harness steps. Every other session keeps the base prompt, and `--permission-mode dontAsk` with `--allowedTools` still decides what any session may run.

## Changes

- `scripts/live/session.sh`: a new `live_system_prompt` builds the one prompt string. It adds the peer sentence when `LIVE_PEER_STEPS_SESSION` is set.
- `scripts/live/handoff/common.sh`: `start_waiting_handoff` sets `LIVE_PEER_STEPS_SESSION=$(session_of "$peer")` as a prefix on its `handoff_start` call only.
- `scripts/live/README.md`: "Advice, not enforcement" and "Peer sessions" describe the exception.
- `.github/tests/live-harness-{session,handoff}.test.sh`: six tests cover the following.
  - The peer is named.
  - A session with no peer gets the base prompt only.
  - Exactly one `--append-system-prompt` flag is passed.
  - The prompt reaches `claude` whole through `dash`.
  - The waiting session is started with the peer named.
  - The setting does not leak to later sessions.

## Testing

Live (local, Claude Code 2.1.330):

| Scenario | Before (2026-11-23) | After (d4d881b) |
|---|---|---|
| `clear-resume-during-handoff` | 0/3 (all `SETUP`) | **3/3 PASS** (28 checks each) |
| `busy-abandon` | — | 1/1 PASS (5 checks) |
| `restore-order-after-abandon` | — | 1/1 PASS (4 checks) |

An uncommitted probe with the same wording also passed `clear-resume-during-handoff` 3/3 before the change was implemented.

- `.github/tests/canary-report.sh` at 97d0d82: 795/795 on `/bin/bash` 3.2 and 795/795 on bash 5.
- Gauntlet (T1): one bug-hunt, quality and security pass; adversarial-qa passed twice (the second run was a delta on the purist commit); the bash purist made no changes; the test purist made the flag-count assertion exact (`^1$`).

Not verified live:
- `subagents-during-handoff` also goes through `start_waiting_handoff`. It was not run here, and #184 tracks it.
- The 97d0d82 commit changes only a CI test, so the live runs on d4d881b still cover the harness code.

Known limit (from adversarial-qa): the per-call prefix assignment leaks into later calls under bash 3.2's POSIX mode. The harness always runs as `#!/usr/bin/env bash` in normal mode, so it can't be reached.

LOW, left as is: one unwrapped long line in the README "Peer sessions" paragraph.

Closes #182

Follow-up to #523 / #525. release-please matches `exclude-paths` as **directory prefixes** (`file.startsWith(path + "/")` in `src/util/commit-exclude.ts`), so the single-file entries never matched. That is why #524 still reached the root package and needed `Release-As: 0.95.3` in #525.

This keeps only `packages`, so the config doesn't suggest more than it does. For a real fix, move the pnpm workspace root under `packages/`, or keep using a `Release-As:` footer when a helpers PR also touches root pnpm files.

author: djl88
body:
Owner-approved model upgrade: BiRefNet-lite (fine subject edges). **Desktop and cloud runner only, opt-in, U²-Netp stays the device default.**

Status for the lead to carry over (no ROADMAP edit): **BiRefNet-lite: WIRED into V2 Find subject on desktop; no download offer in the UI yet.** Our own ONNX export, weight-only fp16, 92.2 MB. 1024 px parity with PyTorch: PASS. Used only when it finds the same subject as U²-Netp.

## What changed
- `src/core/optionalModels.ts`: `BIREFNET_LITE` pack, tier `desktop`, one file pinned by URL, SHA-256 and bytes. With no address in the build it isn't offered.
- `src/core/birefnet.ts`:
  - input preparation and a soft alpha resampled to the mask size; a non-finite result is refused;
  - `compareSubjectMasks(coarse, fine)` → IoU, **gain** (what BiRefNet adds: wing tips, tail, whiskers) and **loss**, for the guardian's whole-subject check (owner decision 5);
  - `preferFineMask` is true only at IoU ≥ 0.6.
- `src/providers/fineEdgeMask.ts`:
  - status, download and remove, desktop only: never on a phone (including the Tauri mobile shell) or in a browser tab;
  - `fineEdgeMask`;
  - `refineSubjectGrid(framed, grid, detail)` gives BiRefNet's grid plus a fine outline over U²-Netp's own subject region, up to 384 cells. **It returns null unless both models found the same subject.**
- **Wired:** V2 Find subject or background (`useEngineWorkspace`) uses the refined grid and detail when available, and U²-Netp's otherwise. Any failure falls back silently to U²-Netp.
- Settings → Models lists it, with load and run times measured live.
- docs/models.md: provenance, conversion and parity; `.env.example`.

## Model
- Source: HF `ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet_lite` @ `aa62cd87…` (MIT). Exported by `tools/model-conversion/birefnet_lite.py` (#1553, #1562) with an exact pure-PyTorch deformable convolution, because torchvision's op has no ONNX exporter.
- File: `birefnet-lite-w16.onnx`, 92,215,270 B, SHA-256 `2c7c7240884841649e5f67b645cf7aed004a401c2fc666dd00c97a29948ef319`. I downloaded the run artifact and re-checked its hash locally. It's kept in `C:\Users\david\Code\Kestrel-models\birefnet-lite\out\`, with the gate reports.

## Evidence
- **Model conversion run [45648025801](https://github.com/DjL88/Kestrel/actions/runs/45648025801)**, 1024 px vs PyTorch, 5 CC0/public-domain images:
  - our fp32: **PASS**, an exact match (difference 0.0);
  - weight-only fp16: **PASS**, mean ≤ 7e-5, IoU ≥ 0.9995, edge band ≤ 0.0045 (limit 0.03);
  - the ops-kept fp16 variant couldn't load in onnxruntime, so it isn't used.
- The patched PyTorch model vs the real one at 1024 px: max 2.5e-5.
- Native onnxruntime on the runner's 4 CPUs: 7.6 s per photo, 1.14 GB peak.
- The earlier run [45641328704](https://github.com/DjL88/Kestrel/actions/runs/45641328704) showed the authors' published ONNX **fails** on edges, which is why this is our own export.
- `node --test` (birefnet, modelCatalogue, rfDetr, efficientSam, nafnet, optionalModels, modelStats): **PASS** (32/32)
- `tsc --noEmit`: **PASS**
- Full suites, build and browser tests: GitHub Actions on this PR.

## Not verified
- Speed in the desktop app's own runtime (single-thread WebAssembly; expect several times 7.6 s, and the Find subject task shows progress).
- Real feathers and fur.
- A download offer in V2 Settings.
- Cloud-runner use.

Etapas 2, 3 e 4 do Liner (v1 local-first, sem Spotify Web API), conforme `docs/PLANNING.md`.

author: andreasjordan
body:
Part of #10806 (the Copy-DbaRegServer sites) and of #10799 (the Copy-DbaRegServer item), plus every other defect found in the command.

## The problems

1. **The stores were never closed** (the #10799 item). The command read the stores of the source and of every destination through `Get-DbaRegServerStore` and never called `Disconnect-RegServer`, unlike the other nine registered server commands since #10577 and #10633. A store keeps its connection open after it was read. Lab (SQL03\SQL2025 to SQL03\SQL2022, counting the sleeping sessions of the process through a non-pooled connection): after a warm-up call, 4 calls of `Copy-DbaRegServer` took the source and the destination from 2 to 5 sleeping sessions each. 4 calls of `Get-DbaRegServer` on both, as reference, left them flat.
2. **Under `-WhatIf` an existing subgroup looked new.** The subgroup of the destination and its status row were read inside a ShouldProcess "Copying group". Under `-WhatIf` they were never read, so `-WhatIf -Force` announced "Copying group sub1" and "Creating group sub1" for a subgroup that the real run drops and recreates, and nothing about the registered server in it.
3. **`continue` without a loop** (the #10806 item). The three exits at the top of `Invoke-ParseServerGroup` ran `continue`. They are reachable only from the call for `-Group`, which is the last statement of `foreach ($store in $stores)`, so the effect was that of a `return`, but it depended on the shape of the caller.

## The fix

1. The stores come from `Get-DbaRegServerStore` with the instances as given, so that they record whether this command opened their connection (`IsNewConnection`). `Disconnect-RegServer` closes them in `finally` blocks, in `process`, so the cleanup also runs after a throw under `-EnableException`. A connection that the caller handed in stays open. The server objects come from the stores. `-MinimumVersion 10` is gone with the separate connection: `Connect-DbaInstance` refuses everything older than SQL Server 2008 anyway.
2. The subgroup and the status row are read before any ShouldProcess. The pseudo-operation "Copying group" is gone from the `-WhatIf` output; the real operations are announced as before.
3. `return`.

## Tests

A new context copies the group of the existing test three more times with `-Force` after a warm-up call. It counts the sleeping sessions of the test process on both instances through non-pooled connections that are opened once: no more afterwards than before. A pooled session may end while the test runs, so the assertion is less-or-equal; a leak adds one per call.

Problems 2 and 3 do not show in the output of the command (the first only in the host output of `-WhatIf`), so they are shown by the lab probe above, not by a test.

In the lab:

- With the fix: 5 of 5 on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (set03) and on PowerShell 7.6 (set04), no warnings. The probe: 1 sleeping session on each instance before and after the 4 calls, and `-WhatIf -Force` announces "Dropping subgroup sub1 recreating", "Creating group sub1", "Dropping instance ... and recreating", "Copying ...".
- Against the command of `development` (5.1, set03): both counting tests fail (source 3 to 6, destination 2 to 5).

author: ce-dmelnych
body:
## Description

**What changed:** ports `QueueItem.order` to `stable/8.9`. The new [`order`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/37d3effb2fa60e6fa9afc741421e29b6c1846a62/db/rdbms/src/main/java/io/camunda/db/rdbms/write/queue/QueueItem.java#L18-L20) component defaults to `0` and is compared between `statementType` and `statementId` in [`QueueOrdering.SORT_BY_STATEMENT_TYPE`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/37d3effb2fa60e6fa9afc741421e29b6c1846a62/db/rdbms/src/main/java/io/camunda/db/rdbms/write/queue/QueueOrdering.java#L26-L33). `QueueItem.copy` carries it, `PRESERVE` and `PRESERVE_PER_ID` ignore it, and a five-argument `QueueItem` constructor keeps every existing call site unchanged, so there is no behavior change at the default `order = 0`. It is the same mechanism as [`5cffda1639d`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/commit/5cffda1639d10cc7fe0396875a6e1d1c0d5ea580) on `main` and [`a22a2617975`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/commit/a22a2617975e095a0e048a9240ba752806d7f2b8) on `stable/8.10`, adapted to the `QueueOrdering` layout of 8.9.

**Why:** on 8.9 the items of one `ContextType` and `WriteStatementType` can only be tied by `QueueItem.statementId`, so a statement that has to run after its siblings cannot be expressed. The 8.9 backport of the batch operation `endDate` fix (#71018) needs exactly that, because `BatchOperationWriter` queues its `finalizeEndDate` statement with `order = 1` so it runs after the item updates of the same flush.

**What it enables:** the RDBMS fix commit of #71018 can be applied to `stable/8.9` as it is on `main`. This PR has to merge first, and #71018 is then rebased on top of it.

**Out of scope:**
- This is not a backport of #61864. That PR introduced `order` to run `updateSuspendedState` before `updateStateAndEndDate` in `ProcessInstanceWriter`, and this code does not exist on 8.9, so only the mechanism is ported.
- No consumer of `order` is added here, and `DefaultExecutionQueue` needs no change.

The change is split into a `feat` commit with the mechanism and a `test` commit that pins the ordering contract.

## Related issues

author: szhenger
body:
The fixes for the from-scratch review of 2026-11-25 (main at `b582229`). One commit per finding, then a code-review round and a last verification commit; nothing here changes a plan's bytes or a loss that was not saturated.

## What changed

| Finding | Fix | Held by |
|---|---|---|
| Cached segment-masked attention compiled a wrapped batch field above 65,535 sequences, and the device ran it | Lowering refuses a field that does not fit; the executor contract holds the forward to the positions its `segment_starts` wrote | compiler test at 65,536 and 65,538 sequences; contract test on both forwards |
| The compiler never validated its own instructions | `VerifyGeneratedPlan` runs the device's `DecodePlan` on the emitted plan | a re-sealed plan with an undefined opcode |
| Durable writes used plain `fsync` on macOS | `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)` on Darwin, `fsync` only where the filesystem has none, and elsewhere | existing storage suites (no power-loss test exists) |
| Loss saturated at 27.63 for a confidently wrong row | Below the 1e-12 floor the loss is the log-sum-exp of the row's logits: CPU, both Metal kernels, the eval tail, the NumPy oracle. Bits unchanged at and above the floor | CPU, Metal-vs-CPU and oracle tests |
| ReLU turned a NaN into zero | `x <= 0 ? 0 : x` on CPU, Metal, the epilogue, the fused map and the oracle; every number keeps its bits | bitwise test over -inf .. NaN |
| The relaxed Metal GEMM test passed where the kernels could not run | A counted SKIP on such a GPU | — |
| Nothing gating compared training to a real framework | `test/tool/torch_step_test.py`: a decoder and an MLP in torch (float64) against the compiled step — loss 1e-5, gradients 1e-4, AdamW/SGD movement 2e-3; cached and tiled attention, unfused plan, Metal | runs in the e2e job, which fails if it skips |
| The finite-difference check passed ~4 % errors | Noise floor plus 1 %, and at least half the coordinates must be resolvable | — |
| `--hf-parity` had no threshold | A delta above `1e-3 × (1 + max |logits|)` withdraws the export | unit test of the bound |
| A dead MatMul or a compiler-derived name failed passes later with an internal message | Sema refuses both by the user's own names | parser tests |
| `segment mask:` refusals were unattributed diagnostics | A registered unit | existing test |
| A boolean or missing tolerance passed the certificate checker | Refused by name | certifier test |
| Pushes to main cancelled each other's CI runs | `cancel-in-progress` for pull requests only, and each push to main has its own concurrency group | — |
| Parity tests ran in no CI job | The e2e job installs transformers and tokenizers and fails if those tests skip | — |
| Stale docs | 74 vendored files, 59 opcodes, three address spaces, bit 62, tile flags, counts (660 C++, 274 Python) | — |

## Verified locally (Apple M5, macOS 26)

- `SEEML_BENCH=1 SEEML_ACCELERATE=1 sh build/build.sh`: 0 warnings.
- 34 suites, 660 C++ tests pass; 274 Python tests pass with no skips.
- The plan the old compiler emitted at 65,538 sequences is refused at load by name.
- A 2 % perturbation of one reference weight fails `torch_step_test.py`.

## Not in this PR

- **Branch protection on `main`**: a repository setting, left to the owner.
- **A green scheduled nightly**: can only be observed.
- **An iPhone or iPad run**: needs a device.
- **`-ffp-contract`**: pinning it changes bits and speed, and speed cannot be measured on battery.
- **The SmolLM-135M tokenizer parity test** still needs a cached checkpoint, so it stays outside CI.
- Lower-severity items from the review that were not in its summary: emitter relocation and non-atomic emission, `recipe_hash` coverage, the `CXX` quoting in the Metal probe, Metal grid sizes above 2^27 rows, `MetalBackend::Bind` ordering, `kGemmAccNN` alpha finiteness, the bench gate's missing-fixture pass, sanitizer coverage of `.mm` files and `update_main.cc`.
- The ReLU and loss kernel changes were not timed (the host was on battery); the nightly bench gate is the first place a throughput change would show.
- A checkpoint written before the loss change whose validation set has a row below the floor is refused on resume (the gate losses are re-measured to the bit). There is no version bump.

## Code review of this branch

`/code-review high --fix` found ten issues in the first ten commits, all fixed in `179dc6e`: the KL forward was quadratic in the vocabulary below the loss floor (4.9 s for 8 rows at 49,152 classes; the same loss bits now in 1 ms), one concurrency group for main still lost the middle of three merges, the derived-name check missed chained stems and companion ids, a null-pointer offset in the eval tail, and six smaller ones. The last commit adds the engine-level test of the eval tail below the floor (CPU and Metal) and narrows the `F_FULLFSYNC` fallback to unsupported-filesystem errors. `SaveSmf` (tests only) still uses plain `fsync`.

In the e2e job the six non-Metal `torch_step_test.py` cases and the transformers parity test run and pass.

## Why

Prepares the repo for outside contributors before it goes public: CI that gates PRs, GitHub-built releases, dependency checks and contributor docs.

## What changed

- **CI** (`ci.yml`): Windows `check` job (fmt, clippy, test, rustdoc with `-D warnings`, all `--locked`; cache saved from `main` only) and an Ubuntu `policy` job (cargo-deny bans and sources, no personal paths in tracked files, no AI co-author trailers). Runs on PRs and `main`; superseded runs are cancelled; actions pinned to SHAs.
- **Advisories** (`advisories.yml`): cargo-deny advisories weekly and when `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` change.
- **Release** (`release.yml`): a `v*` tag checks the tag against the crate version, builds the MSVC exe without cache, checks with `dumpbin` that it needs no VC++ runtime and is x64, and drafts a GitHub release with the exe and `checksums.txt`. PRs touching the build setup and manual runs build only.
- **Build**: one workspace version, `publish = false`, static CRT on MSVC (`.cargo/config.toml`).
- **Dependabot** for cargo and actions; `deny.toml`.
- **Docs**: CONTRIBUTING (scope, settled decisions, adding a device with catalog examples, replay tests, PR title format), SECURITY, AGENTS, PR template, issue forms, `.coderabbit.yaml`, README Download and Contributing sections.
- Two stale rustdoc links fixed so the docs check passes.

## Verification

Locally on Windows (GNU toolchain): fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked` (678 passed), rustdoc with the CI flags, cargo-deny bans/sources/advisories, actionlint, issue forms and Dependabot/CodeRabbit configs validated against their JSON schemas, gitleaks over the full history. The MSVC release build and the `dumpbin` check run for the first time on this PR.

author: jerbouma
body:
The hosted server's logs show two ways clients lose requests before a tool is even called:

- **Sessions.** About one in nine requests from Claude.ai's servers was refused with "Missing session ID" (400) or "Session not found" (404): a conversation that resumes after the 30-minute idle timeout, or a request sent from another address of the client's pool without its session header, has to start over. The tools keep no state between calls, so the HTTP server now runs stateless: every request stands on its own and none of these are refused.
- **Pasted addresses.** One client has called `/mcp%20.` (the address copied with the end of its sentence) on every request for days and only ever got a 404; others send `/mcp%0A` (a line break). `/mcp` and `/sse` followed by spaces, line breaks, dots or slashes are now served as the endpoint. The rewrite is the outermost middleware, so authentication sees the same path the request is served on: without credentials these get the same 401 as `/mcp`.

Checked on a local hosted server: requests without a session, with an unknown session and on `/mcp%20.`, `/mcp%0A` and `/mcp/` answer 200 (401 without credentials), other paths still 404, and a regular client initializes and calls tools as before.

body:
Moves the vendored tracker wheel from tractable 1.3.0 to 1.3.2.

1.3.2 lets a recovered batch owner take over a claimed member whose implementation dependency is a prepared member (joeharris76/tractable#84). author: korczis
body:
## Summary

A curated note, `.ai/repo/knowledge/curated/music-analysis-from-sonic-playground.md`, offers back what three analysis passes measured in sonic-playground's live visualiser. The passes ran on freely licensed recordings from Wikimedia Commons, against librosa references. This follows the owner's order of "bidirectional knowledge" (2026-11-24).

- **Tempo:** a per-range onset novelty with autocorrelation and a comb over multiples is the robust estimator.
  - Every analysis step is averaged and timed by the audio clock.
  - A room's own noise periodicity is gated by the onset rate.
  - SuperFlux novelty is used.
  - Results on the recordings: hip-hop 0 -> 99%, rock 20 -> 75-80%, jazz 27 -> 57%.
- **Beat phase:** the `kuramoto` sine coupling has a stable trap at half a beat. A sawtooth pull from near-beat kicks and snares escapes it.
- **Key:** Krumhansl-Schmuckler profiles over about 8 s, with hysteresis, named the key of 7 of 8 excerpts. A lone major triad stays ambiguous.
- **Sections:** the `page-hinkley` kernel on live audio scored F1 0.53 offline. Live it needs a spread floor, lambda 10, a 3 s learning time and a 6 s gap.
- **Proposed plates:** `tempo-autocorrelation`, `key-profiles`, `superflux-onsets`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run verify -- --fast`, run under a build slot: catalogue, derived facts, Rust kernels, typecheck, unit tests, README, build, flowbite, majordomus doctor. It passed (Majordomus task t-20261125023752-e81a, tree 30bd0ed4c63f).

body:
## Summary

Test-only. No behavior change. No product code. Data dependence: none.

Owner, 2026-11-24: "tests that are based on time will go into the pool that runs on integrator, and tests that can be fixed since time is a by product of poor design are fixed."

This PR fixes the 33 `proxy` lines of `scripts/release/pending-timing-fixes.txt`. All 33 lines leave the list.

## What changed

| Test | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| EveryCallAfterASweepOnlyProxy... | fixed 40 s sleep for the real ticker | keeper on a test clock, 20 sweeps of 2 s; 40 s becomes 1.5 s |
| ANonClaudeModelOnARelayIsNotPingedUnlessNamed | 5 s window, shorter than Idle (10 s), so it proved nothing | test clock, wait for a held Claude thread, then sweep and count glm calls |
| AcquireSpareLeavesRealTrafficAlone, LimiterBoundEvictsOneKeyNotAll | wall-clock minute | `pinned(...)` limiter clock; the skip on a minute straddle is gone |
| Refusals (5 tests) | limiter clock | already pinned on main; line removed |
| BobObserve..., 4 cgllm shadow-store polls, ToolDeferPurge..., TenantAfterStart, ToolFilterRefuses..., ObserveOffPath..., ResponsesRoute..., SavingsRecordEnds..., CapturedRequestRecords... | hand-rolled polls of 1 s to 5 s | `testutil.WaitFor` |
| ToolDeferProbeAsk | 1 s limit, redundant | check removed (hooks already prove no probe) |
| Retired, CacheAware x2, SummaryCall..., 3 cgllm cost tests | 5 s summary wait | 30 s |
| 3 SSE tests, CachePreset..., TheStreamedPrefix... | 2 s and 5 s first-event bounds | 30 s client wait and 30 s upstream escape hatch |
| AccEndDoesNotWait..., AccountantPanic..., PricerAdapterNeverBlocks | 1 s, 2 s, 5 s bounds; 50 ms sleep | 30 s; the sleep is gone |
| ConcurrentRequestsAgainstAFlakyGateway | sleeps to settle goroutines; 100 ms silence races replies | `WaitForState` on the goroutine count; the "sent N times" bound runs only with timing on |
| ClosingIdleConnections... | 100 ms sleep for streams to start | wait on the server's start counter |
| SeedAfterLoadKeepsTheLoadedUses | 200 ms absence window | kept, marked `//timing:ok`: no event follows it, and a starved goroutine only weakens it |

## Not fixed

- None of the 33 stays on the list.
- One window stays: the 200 ms in `SeedAfterLoad...` (marked, above).
- Left alone, not on the list: `TestRegistrationRateLimitedPerIP` (already gated, #1366). `TestFailedProxyAuthIsThrottledPerClientAddress` has the same minute edge; it needs the clock set on the registration limiter. No open PR touches my test files.
- Two cgllm cost tests and `SummaryCall...` got the same 5 s to 30 s change, so they are done too.

## How it was tested

macOS, Go 1.27.4, `GOMAXPROCS=4`.

- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=20 -run '<20 tests>' ./proxy/`: pass (231 s).
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=10 -run '<12 SSE, summary and stream tests>' ./proxy/`: pass (228 s).
- `go test -race -count=5` over all 33 names plus `TestCGLLM`: pass.
- `go test -p 2 ./proxy/` without `-race`, in two parts (`^Test[A-L]`, `^Test[^A-L]`): pass.
- `gofmt`, `go vet ./proxy/ ./internal/...`, `go test ./internal/timingguard/`: pass. Baseline lowered by 16 lines.

Vacuity:

- `ANonClaudeModel...`: set `CONTEXT_GURU_KEEPALIVE_MODELS=glm`. The test failed ("saw 5 upstream calls, want only the 3"). Before the fix, the same change passed.
- `LimiterBoundEvictsOneKeyNotAll`: limiter bound set to 1. Fails at once.
- `BobObserve...`: look up a wrong key. Fails after the 30 s bound, with its message.

Local tests: waived (owner rule).

author: sebaustin
body:
Fixes the six medium-severity findings from the code review of the iOS app.

## What changed

- **Answers attaching to the wrong letter.** "Explain this letter" is disabled, and refused if called, while a question or reply draft is in flight. Questions and drafts are refused while a letter is being read. This also stops the privacy receipt from mixing calls from two letters.
- **Deadlines on non-Gregorian phones.** A letter's ISO dates are now always read as Gregorian (new `deadlineDate`; `daysUntil` takes a time zone instead of a calendar), then displayed in the phone's own calendar. Before this, Thai Buddhist or Japanese calendar settings gave wrong day counts.
- **Device log.** Model errors log only the error type publicly; the description, which can quote the letter, is private.
- **Dynamic Type.** Theme fonts scale with the text size setting through a `@ScaledMetric` modifier, with large display type scaling like `.largeTitle`. The composer buttons stack when they don't fit side by side.
- **App-layer tests.** New `PlainlyTests` target with six view-model tests, made possible by an initializer that takes an `Inference` and a device-model status. `grantConsent()` now returns its task so tests can await it.
- **Code signing.** `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED: NO` is replaced by automatic signing. `ios/Signing.xcconfig` optionally includes a git-ignored `ios/Local.xcconfig` holding `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`. The App Attest entitlement is added, which Release builds need for App Check on a device.

## Testing

- `swift test` in `ios/PlainlyCore`: 47 tests pass, including a new Buddhist-calendar test.
- `xcodebuild test` on an iOS simulator: the 6 new app tests pass. Each half of the stale-answer test fails when its guard is removed.
- Ran the app in the simulator at the accessibility-extra-large text size with Apple's on-device model. The composer, decode summary and figures (19 days left, $1,284.50) all fit.

## Not verified

- Running on a physical iPhone. It needs a team ID in `Local.xcconfig`; simulator builds need none.
- The low-severity review items are not addressed here.

author: lumi673
body:
Splits the two giant compiler source files so later stages can change separate files instead of one 8.6k-line `emit.rs` and one 5k-line `tests.rs`.

Pure moves: no logic edits, no renamed emitted strings or error messages, no reordering that changes output, no new dependencies. The only signature change is visibility (`pub(super)`/`pub(crate)`) needed to call a method from another `emit` submodule. `crates/compiler/src/lib.rs`, the crate re-exports, `Body`, the plugin API (57) and all three compile modes are untouched.

## Ownership map

| module | lines | concern | expected editor |
| :-- | --: | :-- | :-- |
| `emit/mod.rs` | 334 | `Emitter`, `Body`, output buffer, `payload_params`, `temp`/`line`/`push`/`lookup` | shared, land first |
| `emit/statements.rs` | 1437 | statements, patterns, `if`/`match`/`for`, `ret`/`Ok`, assignment | S2 |
| `emit/expressions.rs` | 1137 | expressions, paths, literals, binary/unary, fields, closures | S2 |
| `emit/methods.rs` | 2294 | method calls, iterators, string/number/collection methods, path/std constructors | S3 |
| `emit/calls.rs` | 320 | call forms, ui nodes, fallback, function references | S4 |
| `emit/macros.rs` | 518 | `format!`, `json!`, `matches!`, pattern conditions | S4 |
| `emit/ops.rs` | 535 | `Op` construction, callbacks, event recording | S5 |
| `emit/constants.rs` | 152 | constants, statics, `static_init`/`static_value` | S5 |
| `emit/inline.rs` | 652 | helper inlining, inline binding/budget, `check_body`/`Scan` | S3 |
| `emit/native.rs` | 912 | native boundary: register, stub, runtime, signature params | S6 |
| `emit/types.rs` | 453 | `Ty`/`Base`/`StaticKind`/`StaticDef`, type hints, predicates | shared |

`tests/` mirrors the same split, `tests/mod.rs` keeps the shared helpers (`options`, `source`, `module_options`, `native_options`, `NATIVE_HELPER`). Test counts per file: methods 49, inline 28, native 21, statements 18, ops 17, expressions 15, macros 14, constants 6, calls 4, types 3. The compiler test file holds 175 tests in total, and all 175 still run. Stage names are my reading of each concern, confirm or correct them in review.

## Gates

| command | result |
| :-- | :-- |
| `nix develop --command cargo fmt --check` | pass, no diff |
| `nix develop --command cargo test --workspace` | pass: compiler 175, lib 90 + 4 + 10, build 25, luau 31 + 12 + 5, macros 3, example 36 |
| `nix develop --command cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | pass, no warnings |
| `nix develop --command cargo tarpaulin --fail-under 80.87` | pass: 81.52% (8724/10702), `+0.00% change in coverage` |
| `node .github/scripts/performance-aggregate.test.cjs` | pass, 0 failures |

The repo pre-commit chain also ran on the commit and passed: nix `fmt`, `clippy`, `nextest` and `tarpaulin` checks, typos, lychee, gitlint.

## Byte-identical output and scan parity

The corpus harness was copied into this worktree first, because it links the build crate through a relative path and measures the checkout that owns it. Corpus `ea75acf5d916c912d0ba035320d38390`, 366 plugins, 1067 handler entries.

| check | baseline | result |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `md5.sh "$PWD" --mode auto --entry --compare md5/main-auto-entry.json` | main `4c215d6`: 1067 entries, 7603 files | PASS: 1067 compared, 0 status changes, 7603 files, 0 changed |
| `md5.sh "$PWD" --mode strict --entry --compare md5/main-strict-entry.json` | main `4c215d6`: 195 entries, 1410 files | PASS: 195 generate, 0 status changes, 1410 files, 0 changed |
| `md5.sh "$PWD" --mode strict --compare md5/main-strict.json` | main `4c215d6`: 8 plugins, 50 files | PASS: 366 plugins, 0 status changes, 50 files, 0 changed |
| `md5.sh "$PWD" --mode auto --compare md5/main-auto.json` | main `4c215d6`: 2557 files | PASS: 2557 files, 0 changed |
| `scan.sh "$PWD" --mode strict` | `baselines/main-strict-entry.json`: 195/1067 | 195/1067, `summary.json` equal to the baseline except timing |
| `scan.sh "$PWD" --mode auto` | `baselines/main-auto-entry.json`: 1067/1067 | 1067/1067, `summary.json` equal to the baseline except timing |

"Equal except timing" compares `entries`, `entries_detail`, `per_kind`, `per_plugin` and `errors`.

## How the move was checked

Besides the corpus diff, the regenerated files were compared line by line against `4c215d6` with a multiset check: every original non-blank line is present, and the only additions are module headers, `mod`/`pub(crate) use` wiring, `impl<'a> Emitter<'a> {` wrappers and attributes that rustfmt reflowed after the `pub(super)` prefix pushed two signatures over the width limit.

## Files that resisted a clean split

- `emit/mod.rs` keeps `payload_params` and the `Body`/`Ty`-alias vocabulary the other modules share; moving them out only moved the header.
- `tests/methods.rs` (49 tests, 1274 lines) is the largest test file. Many tests mix statements and one method call, so a few placements are judgment calls (`keeps_bodies_with_only_void_method_statements` sits in `statements.rs`, `strips_carriage_returns_and_trailing_newlines` in `methods.rs`).
- Ten tests exercise the whole surface (`compiles_the_whole_op_and_host_surface`, `covers_*`); each sits in the file of the concern it exercises most.

iOS 专属功能第三组「不打开 App 也能学」（方案在共享笔记 ios-27-features.md 第 3、4、6 项；第一、二组是 #335、#348）。

## 学员看到的

- **「今天」小组件**（主屏：小、中；锁屏：圆形、长条、一行）：今天要复习几个词、新词、大约几分钟；中号的右边是今日好句（带网站给的「公版名句」「语流文章」标注和出处），没有好句时是今天这篇。点左边去复习，点右边去今日。过了半夜还没打开过 App，就写「打开语流看看今天的」。没登录不显示任何人的词。
- **控制中心按钮**（iOS 18 起）：「开始复习」「今天的学习」，打开 App 的复习页、今日页。
- **复习进度的实时活动**（「iOS 专属功能」里的开关，**默认关**：锁屏上别人也看得到数字）：复习单词时锁屏和灵动岛显示「复习单词 12 / 30」和进度条。网页一侧请语流 B2 在复习页调 `activity.review` / `activity.end`。
- 设置页多了一组「不打开 App 也能学」，下面写了小组件和控制中心按钮怎么加（这两样学员自己加、自己删，就不另设开关）。

截图（共享笔记 ios-app/）：22-widget-home.png（主屏上的中号小组件，样例数字）、23-widget-gallery-medium.png（添加小组件时的预览）。在模拟器上点小组件左半边，App 打开就跳到复习页。

## 怎么做的

- 工程（项目生成脚本改的，不手改 pbxproj）：新扩展 `FlowWidgets`（WidgetKit，嵌在 App 里）、两边共用的文件夹 `Common/`；App Group `group.$(FLOW_BUNDLE_ID)`（`Config/Shared.xcconfig`，两个 entitlements 文件）；App 自己的链接 scheme：正式版 `yuliu`，内测版 `yuliu-beta`（两个能同时装，各开各的）。
- `Common/TodayCard.swift`：小组件显示的数字、App Group 里的存取、链接 `yuliu://open?path=%23/review` 的生成和检查（只认本站 `#/` 页面，别的 scheme、外部网址、怪字符、太长都不开）。
- `Flow/Features/WidgetsFeed.swift`：提醒刷新完（App 回到前台、后台刷新）把数字写进去，今日好句和今天这篇最多半小时问一次 `/api/next/home`；没变就不写，变了 `WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines()`。小组件自己不上网。
- `Flow/Features/ReviewActivities.swift` + `FlowWidgets/ReviewActivityWidget.swift`：ActivityKit，只在本机更新，没有推送；App 启动时清掉上次留下的。桥：能力 `activity`，命令 `activity.review {done, total}`、`activity.end`。
- 约定 `docs/native-bridge.md` 第 2 节和 iOS 一节、`ios/README.md`（隐私一句）。
- 截图用：内测版启动参数 `-FlowWidgetSample YES` 写一份样例数字。
- 没有用到 iOS 27 SDK 才有的接口（控制中心按钮是 iOS 18 的），CI 的 Xcode 26 能编。
- 顺带修第一组的一个时序问题：单句循环时录音放到这一句末尾就停；正好在一句放完那一刻关掉单句循环，晚到的「放完了」被当成整篇放完，整篇就停了（iPhone 模拟器上 test7 偶尔失败，截图停在第 1 句「放完」）。现在一口气放时只有真放到录音结尾才算完，别的「放完」接着放。

## 测试（本机，静音）

- 两台模拟器（iPhone 17e、iPad mini）上完整的单元测试和界面测试。
- 单元测试：链接只开本站页面（各种坏链接都不开）；数字卡（没登录不放词、今日好句带标注、存进去再读出来一样）；半夜以后算旧；实时活动默认关、没开时回 off。
- 界面测试 `test11Glance`：App 写好了小组件的数字（测试没登录：没有词，有今日好句）；用 `yuliu-beta://open?path=%23/review` 打开 App 跳到复习；实时活动没开时不起，打开以后起一个（3 / 10），结束以后没了。
- 手动：模拟器主屏加上中号「今天」，点左半边跳到复习页。
- 已经用免费签名装到用户的 iPhone（扩展 `cn.flowlang.app.beta.me.widgets`、App Group `group.cn.flowlang.app.beta.me` 都配上了）。装上以后 iPhone 要求在「设置 → 通用 → VPN 与设备管理」里重新验证一次开发者（多了扩展、换了描述文件，免费账号都会这样），已告诉用户；以后付费账号走 TestFlight 就没有这一步。

## 隐私

本机多存的：App Group 里一份今天的数字和今日好句（只在这台手机上，每次刷新覆盖，没登录不写词）；主屏、锁屏上的小组件和实时活动别人看得到数字（实时活动默认关）。已告诉语流 B6。

author: retronym
body:
`import O.{y => z, x => y}` binds `y` to `O.x` and `z` to `O.y`, but implicit search does not see `O.x`. With the selectors the other way round, `import O.{x => y, y => z}`, both implicits are found. The swap `{x => y, y => x}` loses one of the two in either order.

```scala
object O {
  implicit val x: A = new A
  implicit val y: B = new B
}
class C {
  import O.{y => z, x => y}
  val a: A = y    // fine: y is O.x
  implicitly[B]   // fine
  implicitly[A]   // error: could not find implicit value for parameter e: A
}
```

The order of the selectors of an import clause has no meaning (SLS 4.7), and the identifier already resolves, so the implicit should be found. Scala 3 finds both in every order.

## Mechanism

`Contexts.collectImplicitImports` walks the selectors right to left. For a selector `from => to` it removes, from the infos collected so far, those whose name is `from`. The filter is there for a trailing wildcard: in `{x => y, _}` or `{x => _, _}` the wildcard has contributed `O.x` under its own name, which the clause does not bind. But it compares against the name under which any later selector bound its symbol, so the selector `y => z` also removes the info that `x => y` has just created for `O.x`.

## Fix

An info with the name `from` is kept if it comes from a renaming selector: that selector introduced the name for another member, which is not the one this selector renames or masks.

The filter still applies to what the wildcard contributed and to a later plain selector of the same name, so `{x => y, x}` and `{x => _, x}` behave as before. (A name can be selected twice in one clause; `{x, x => y}` produces two infos for one member, which is ambiguous with itself. That is finding IR4, not this change.)

The only programs affected are those with a renaming chain inside one import clause, where one selector's new name is another selector's old name. They failed with "could not find implicit value", or fell back to an implicit of lower precedence, in spite of an import that names the implicit; they now get the imported one.

Long-standing: 2.12.20 behaves the same.

Found in the third wave of the coordinated code review of 2.13.x (finding IM3). Prepared with Claude.

body:
Root fix R20. Story US-09, new AC58. Leads A22 (done) and A25 (partial: the iPhone half is left).

What now holds:
- `shouldReport(previous, now)` in `packages/health-core/src/record-host.ts` keys each failed-save report by cause and grant. The same cause under the same grant is a repeat. A new cause or a new grant reports again. It replaces the per-session set of device refusal kinds. A cloud failure's cause reads the error's typed `reason` and `outcome`.
- `StorageFailureReason` gains `writes-stopped`. `WritesStoppedError` and the session's own gate raise it. A closed device page is silent only for that reason. Any other cause is reported once.
- The web's page hide (`RoadmapStore.flushSync`) calls `RecordSession.flushSync('hold')`. It still writes the device copy, but starts no cloud save the grant refused (`retryOwed`). The iPhone's callers keep the default, so the phone is unchanged.

Readers of `reason`: none switches over it exhaustively. Each compares to one named member, so `writes-stopped` takes the same branch as no reason did.

author: gidvantus
body:
Closes #261

## Что сделано

### Задача 1 — `block_previews` 4 с → ≤100 мс

Причина найдена профилем из комментария к issue: `personnel_query.Candidates.roots()` вызывался **для каждого корня** отбора.

```python
people = [root for root in ordered[order_key] if root in found.roots(criteria.filter)]
```

`roots()` копирует весь `base` (до 4 874 корней) и пересекает его с фильтром. На рамке с четырьмя блоками это 14 625 вызовов и 2,9 с в профиле — это и был весь `block_previews`.

Правка: набор блока считается **один раз на блок** (`chosen = found.roots(criteria.filter)`), дальше — проверка вхождения в `frozenset`. Состав, порядок и счётчики не менялись.

Дополнительно: `employee_cards()` в ограниченном контексте (страница, превью) читает `employee_events` только по людям группы, а не по всей области. Для ограниченного контекста результат тот же (собираются только `targets ⊆ group`), а полный контекст (`employees=full`) работает как раньше.

### Задача 2 — один запрос рамки на одно открытие

`Personnel.tsx`:
* `period` получил устойчивую ссылку (`fallbackPeriod` по строкам дат): ответ сервера меняет `today`, месяц пересчитывался новым объектом с теми же датами, и эффект рамки уходил вторым запросом.
* ключ последнего запроса удалён: запоминание ключа до отправки при повторном запуске эффекта после `AbortController` могло оставить экран без данных. Стойкая ссылка `period` снимает дубль без блокировки следующего запроса.
* компонент по-прежнему запрашивает только `employees=none`; таймер `useFrameRefresh` даёт один запрос в минуту.

### Замечание тестировщика Ф1 — `GET /api/personnel` без `employees=none`

Оба оставшихся вызова полной поверхности заменены точечными ручками; полный ответ `GET /api/personnel` больше не запрашивается ни одним компонентом персонала.

* `GET /api/personnel/cards` — только карточки сотрудников организации для конструктора подвкладок: ему нужен весь реестр для формул и связей, но не планы, заезды и настройки (их он получает из рамки `employees=none`). `PersonnelWithBuilder.loadData()` берёт карточки отсюда и складывает их в уже пришедшую рамку; `period`/`dormitories`/`source_columns` по-прежнему из рамки.
* `GET /api/personnel/employees/by-source?dormitory_id&table_key&row_id` — корень карточки, привязанной к конкретной строке-источнику. `useEmployeeCard` использует его, когда сохранение ячейки создало карточку, не вернув `id`. Ответ `404` трактуется как «строки пока нет в карточке» — открывается диалог связывания, как раньше; ошибки другого рода показываются пользователю.
* Тесты: `test_all_cards_and_employee_by_source_avoid_the_full_workspace` (бэкенд), `personnel-identity` при `404` и «точечный поиск вместо полного реестра» в `EmployeeNameTables.test.tsx`, мок `personnelApi.cards` в `PersonnelWithBuilder.test.tsx`.

## Замер до/после (свой стенд `crmdormitory-261`, `dbtest`, 2 000 сотрудников / 20 000 строк-источников)

`tests/test_personnel_workspace_perf.py::test_page_cost_and_body_size_on_the_same_volume`

| Вариант | `workspace employees=none` | этап `block_previews` |
|---|---|---|
| до (origin/develop-m) | 1 066 мс | 1 018 мс |
| после | 128 мс | **89 мс** |

Боевой профиль из issue: `block_previews` 3 697–7 573 мс при 14 625 вызовах `roots`; после правки число вызовов не зависит от размера отбора (проверка — новый тест ниже).

## Тесты

* `tests/test_personnel_workspace_optimizations.py::test_block_previews_intersects_the_selection_once_per_block` — счётчик `Candidates.roots`: ровно 6 вызовов (3 блока по людям + 3 числа сводки) при 50 сотрудниках; прежняя реализация дала бы 153.
* `tests/test_personnel_workspace_optimizations.py::test_limited_cards_keep_history_of_merged_members` — карточка, держащаяся только на журнале участника слитой группы, остаётся на странице и в превью с `history_dormitory_ids`.
