author: patrickhuetter
body:
## Was ändert sich?

Befunde eines Nachtests von 0.15.0 an Voranmeldung, Zusammenfassender Meldung und USt-IdNrn. der Partner, jeder zuerst als fehlschlagender Test:

- **Korrekturen aus der Zeit vor 0.15.0 sind unbestätigt.** Das Update auf 0.15.0 (`set_the_basis_of_overrides`) gab jeder bestehenden Korrektur den Betrag ihrer Zeile vom Tag des Updates als Grundlage. Hatte eine späte Buchung diesen Betrag schon vorher geändert, verdeckte die Korrektur sie weiter, ohne dass `KORREKTUR-UEBERHOLT` anschlug. Welche Grundlagen der Patch geschrieben hat, hielt er nicht fest. Der neue Patch `mark_the_bases_of_earlier_overrides_unknown` markiert deshalb jede Korrektur eines Belegs, der vor dem Lauf des früheren Patches angelegt wurde, mit „Grundlage unbekannt“: Zeilen der Zusammenfassenden Meldung, Kennzahlen der Voranmeldung und Zeilen der Jahresmeldungen, nicht die Zeilen von Hand. Eine so markierte Korrektur hält ihren Beleg mit `KORREKTUR-UEBERHOLT`, `ZM-KORREKTUR-UEBERHOLT` oder `SB-KORREKTUR-UEBERHOLT` an, auch bei gleichem Betrag, bis eine Änderung von Betrag oder Begründung sie gegen den Betrag bestätigt, den die Zeile dann zeigt. Eine Berichtigung übernimmt die Markierung. Beim Speichern eines Jahresbelegs übernimmt die Zeile jetzt auch die Grundlage, die `restored` berechnet; bisher blieb dort die alte stehen, sodass eine geänderte Korrektur sie nicht bestätigte.
- **Steuernummer und ERiC.** `EricPruefeSteuernummer` lief beim Speichern mit einem Protokollverzeichnis, das es nicht gab; ERiC startet dann nicht, und die Prüfung gab still keine Antwort. Der Worker legt das Verzeichnis jetzt an, wie beim Prüfen, auch für die Versionen der Bibliotheken, und die Prüfung schreibt ihr Protokoll unter `logs/eric/steuernummer` der Site. Gibt die Prüfung trotzdem keine Antwort, sagt eine orange Meldung „Steuernummer nicht geprüft“ beim Speichern, warum (keine Laufzeitumgebung, Datenschutzhinweise nicht bestätigt, keine Antwort von ERiC). Eine Steuernummer nur aus Nullen lehnt schon das Format ab, ohne ERiC. Das Feld sagt in seiner Beschreibung, wann ERiC prüft.
- **Stornierung über den Monatswechsel im Abgleich mit den Registern.** Mit dem unveränderlichen Hauptbuch stand der stornierte Beleg im Monat seines Datums und die Stornobuchung im Monat der Stornierung, beide als Differenz mit Erklärungspflicht, obwohl die Meldung die Stornierung am Tag des Belegs zählt. Der Abgleich lässt einen stornierten Beleg und seine Stornobuchung jetzt auf der Seite des Hauptbuchs ganz weg, wie die Berichte die stornierte Rechnung; ohne das unveränderliche Hauptbuch war das schon so.
- **Automatische USt-IdNr.-Prüfung.** Die Beschreibung der beiden Einstellungen, der Schritt von „Steuerbote einrichten“ und `docs/ust-idnr-pruefung.md` sagen, nach welchen Partnern die automatische Prüfung fragt: nach denen, mit denen das Unternehmen über ein eigenes Konto oder eine gebuchte Rechnung zu tun hat, und für das Standardunternehmen der Site auch nach jedem Partner, der mit keinem Unternehmen zu tun hat. Das Verhalten ändert sich nicht.
- **Anrede.** Die Befunde der Voranmeldung und der Zusammenfassenden Meldung, die überholte Korrektur und ein Satz der Übersetzungen siezten nicht; sie tun es jetzt. Ein Test liest die deutschen Übersetzungen, die Texte der Module und die Vorlagen auf Du-Formen.
- **Ausgangsrechnung.** Eine deutsche USt-IdNr. mit falscher Prüfziffer nennt die Prüfziffer wie das Formular des Kunden, nicht die Regel, dass das BZSt keine deutschen Nummern bestätigt. Die Warnung bei Kz 21 sagt den nächsten Schritt.
- **Berichtigung der Zusammenfassenden Meldung.** Der Befund einer Zeile, die die Berichtigung unverändert wiederholt, steht als Hinweis mit dem Satz, dass er nichts anhält; die Berichtigung hielt er schon vorher nicht an.
- **Kleineres.** Empfänger der Erinnerung, die über die API als Liste statt als Text kommen, lehnt das Speichern mit einer Meldung ab statt mit einem Serverfehler. Die Dokumentation beschreibt die Wartezeit auf BZSt und VIES so, wie urllib sie zählt.

### Nach `bench migrate`

- Der Patch markiert die Korrekturen der Belege, die vor dem Update auf 0.15.0 angelegt wurden. Jeder Entwurf mit einer solchen Korrektur zeigt nach dem nächsten „Berechnen“ den Fehler `…KORREKTUR-UEBERHOLT` mit dem Satz, dass die Korrektur aus einer Version stammt, die ihre Grundlage nicht festhielt. Für jede: gegen das Hauptbuch prüfen und Betrag oder Begründung ändern, oder die Korrektur löschen. Auch eine Korrektur, die erst unter 0.15.0 an einem älteren Beleg eingetragen wurde, ist einmal so zu bestätigen, denn keine Aufzeichnung trennt sie von denen des Updates. Abgegebene Belege tragen die Markierung nur, damit eine Berichtigung sie übernimmt.
- Bisher hat ERiC eine Steuernummer beim Speichern der Einstellungen nicht geprüft. Ein „Prüfen“ einer Meldung je Unternehmen zeigt, ob die gespeicherte stimmt; eine geänderte prüft ERiC jetzt beim Speichern.

### Nicht umgesetzt, Entscheidung offen

- Ein Partner ohne eigenes Konto und ohne gebuchte Rechnung fällt bei der automatischen Prüfung dem Standardunternehmen zu. Vorschlag: Die automatische Prüfung fragt nur für Unternehmen, mit denen der Partner zu tun hat, und ein Partner ohne solche Beziehung wartet auf die Schaltfläche, die Rechnung oder die tägliche Erneuerung, sobald er eine hat; oder der Rückfall gilt nur auf einer Site mit einem Unternehmen.

## Quelle

- ERiC-API-Referenz 44.3.6.0: `EricInitialisiere` endet mit `ERIC_GLOBAL_FEHLER_INITIALISIERUNG` (610001083), wenn es `eric.log` nicht anlegen kann; `EricPruefeSteuernummer`, ERiC-Entwicklerhandbuch 44.3.6.0, Kap. 6.3.3.
- ELSTER, „Wo ist meine Steuernummer?“, Aufbau der Steuernummer (`steuerbote/elster/steuernummer.py`).
- ERPNext 16: `make_reverse_gl_entries` (`erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`), Sales Register und Purchase Register listen nur gebuchte Rechnungen.
- § 18a Abs. 10 UStG, Anleitung zur ZM IV.12.2 (Berichtigung mit der vollständigen Summe); UStAE 3a.2 Abs. 9 (qualifizierte Bestätigung bei sonstigen Leistungen); UStAE 18e.1 Abs. 1.

## Checkliste

- [x] Tests zuerst: Jede Änderung hat einen Test, der ohne sie fehlschlägt. Kein Test wurde abgeschwächt.
- [x] Die Dokumentation unter `docs/` und im README passt zum Code.
- [x] Keine echten Steuernummern, Zertifikate, PINs, Zugangsdaten oder Belegdaten in Code, Tests, Fixtures oder Screenshots.
- [x] Geldbeträge sind `Decimal`, nie `float`.
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` und `pytest` laufen lokal durch.

author: pzelasko
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds the `voicearena_monsoon` benchmark: transcription of conversational Indian English (2,102 clips, 1,444 speakers) and Hindi (753 clips, 468 speakers) from the public test splits of VoiceArena Monsoon, recorded on phone handsets. Each language is one profile and both run by default. English is scored by corpus word error rate with the Open ASR Leaderboard normalizer. Hindi is scored by corpus OIWER (the lattice-aware error rate the dataset card prescribes, from the `voi-oiwer` package), because each Hindi reference is a lattice of accepted spellings per span, not one string. The benchmark runs on the existing `audio_eval` resources server, which finds the new scorer by name (`++eval_type=nemo_skills.dataset.voicearena-monsoon.scorer::MonsoonASREvaluator`).

**Why.** Indian-English and Hindi phone speech with code-switching is a hard, practically important ASR condition that no benchmark in the catalog covers. Both datasets are public under CC-BY-4.0.

Related issue: none; a new benchmark on the existing `audio_eval` server.

## What changed

- `benchmarks/voicearena_monsoon/`: `config.yaml`, `manifest.yaml` (`domain: asr`, `licensing: CC-BY-4.0`, experimental), `prepare.py`, `profiles.json`, `README.md`, `data/.gitignore`.
  - `prepare()` reads the two pinned dataset revisions, checks each split's row count, id uniqueness, speaker count, language column and duration, validates every Hindi lattice, converts the clips it needs to 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV (parquet row groups are read on demand) and checks each WAV against the source duration. `max_samples_per_profile` keeps the first N rows of each profile and is validated at the start (a positive integer or `None`).
  - The Hindi `expected_answer` is the first spelling of each lattice span and is informational; the score uses `reference_lattice`.
- `resources_servers/audio_eval/_scoring/dataset/voicearena-monsoon/scorer.py`: the evaluator and metrics. English uses `resources_servers.asr_with_pc.open_asr_normalizer` and the server's `word_error_counts`. Hindi calls `voi_oiwer.oiwer` (version pinned to 0.1.4, checked at first use) and checks that its score equals 100 x errors / reference words. Metrics are corpus micro `wer` or `oiwer` with substitution, insertion and deletion counts, `coverage` and `missing_predictions`; they refuse to mix WER and OIWER rows. `voi-oiwer==0.1.4` is already declared in the server's `pyproject.toml`.
- Tests: `tests/unit_tests/benchmarks/test_voicearena_monsoon_benchmark.py` (declaration, profile contracts, census checks, row building, audio conversion, offline `prepare()` against small parquet shards built in the test, row-cap validation) and `resources_servers/audio_eval/tests/test_scoring_voicearena_monsoon.py` (evaluator, metrics, name-based lookup of the profile contracts, an end-to-end `score_rows` run).
- The root `README.md` benchmark-table row and the `benchmarks.mdx` bullet are not in this PR; a follow-up docs PR adds them for all of the new benchmarks, to avoid conflicting edits between parallel benchmark PRs.

This PR depends on `asr_with_pc` (merged) for the English normalizer. No change to the server, its lock file, the root `pyproject.toml` or `.github/`.

## Validation

- `gym env test --resources-server audio_eval`: 225 passed (22 of them in the new scorer test file).
- `tests/unit_tests/benchmarks` plus `tests/unit_tests/tooling/test_benchmark_shared_modules_packaging.py`, in the core environment without `setuptools`: 1345 passed, 10 skipped. (`tests/unit_tests/tooling/test_component_dependencies.py` needs `git ls-files` and cannot run in the sandbox container, which has no `.git`; it is not affected by this change.)
- Mutation checks: 13 deliberate edits each fail at least one test: English reference not normalized, the `voi-oiwer` version pin removed, the OIWER score/count invariant removed, deletions left out of the error count, deletions not pooled across rows, WER and OIWER rows allowed in one profile, missing predictions not counted, the speaker-census check removed, the lattice first-spelling rule changed, the row-cap check removed, the audio duration tolerance widened, the Devanagari instruction dropped from the Hindi prompt, the loop-cleanup setting dropped from the profile. One edit survived at first (pooling of deletions); a test with several rows was added and kills it.
- `gym env validate` on the benchmark config is valid. A capped `gym eval prepare` against the real data (3 rows per profile; 6 rows written) succeeded, and `gym env publish voicearena_monsoon --kind benchmark` passes (4 verifier cases). The real `voi-oiwer` 0.1.4 was also called on a small hand-made lattice (alternative spelling scores 0 errors, a missing word 1 deletion, an extra word 1 insertion).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed Python files; the repo's pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files (including `guardwords-check`). The secrets hook passes with the unchanged baseline.
- A throwaway merge with `main` is clean.

## Rollouts

### What ran

- **Model:** the public Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe BF16 checkpoint (`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B`), served with
  vLLM 0.32.0 and the NeMo-Speech vLLM plugin on one H100 (the model-card stack, MTP speculative decoding with 2 tokens).
- **Data:** the **first 100 rows of each** public split (`--max-samples-per-profile 100`): Indian English (`en-in`) and Hindi (`hi-in`),
  200 rows in all. Request settings from the profiles: greedy, thinking off, `max_output_tokens: 256`, verbatim transcription prompt.
- **Path:** the standard Gym path: `gym eval prepare`, `gym env start` (the `audio_eval` environment with this benchmark's profiles) and
  `gym eval run --no-serve --agent voicearena_monsoon_simple_agent`.

### Run health

- 200 of 200 rollouts completed and were scored: coverage `complete: true`, 0 masked, 0 failed, 0 request errors. All responses have
  status `completed`; none is empty and none reached the 256-token limit (27 output tokens on average, 90 at most).
- Both profiles report `coverage` 100.0.

### Metrics

| Profile | Metric | Value | Errors / reference words | Substitutions / deletions / insertions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `voicearena-monsoon.en-in.public` | `wer` | 3.51 | 69 / 1,966 | 41 / 10 / 18 |
| `voicearena-monsoon.hi-in.public` | `oiwer` (orthography-aware WER) | 10.72 | 190 / 1,772 | 133 / 22 / 35 |

`num_entries` is 100 for each profile.

### What the rollouts show

- **English:** cased, punctuated transcripts of the right kind (`I feel more positive and refreshed.`); none of the 100 English
  outputs contains Devanagari.
- **Hindi:** 99 of 100 outputs are in Devanagari with English words in Latin script, as the references are; one output is Latin
  only. The prompt does not ask for translation and none of the outputs is a translation. One output starts with `Sorry,` where the
  reference has `सर` ("sir"): a misrecognition, not a refusal.
- The scorer works on the Hindi lattice-style references (`oiwer`), whose errors are mostly substitutions (133 of 190), consistent with
  spelling variants and word-boundary differences that the orthography-aware rate is designed to forgive only in part.

### Limitations

- 100 rows per split, one repeat, one model: a smoke result, not comparable to full-split numbers.
- The substitution-dominated error profile of the Hindi rate was read from the counts, not audited word by word.

### Commands (generic form)

```bash
gym eval prepare --config benchmarks/voicearena_monsoon/config.yaml +prepare_script_args.max_samples_per_profile=100
gym env start --config benchmarks/voicearena_monsoon/config.yaml \
    --config responses_api_models/vllm_model/configs/vllm_model.yaml --model-type vllm_model \
    --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B --model-url http://<host>:<port>/v1
gym eval run --no-serve --agent voicearena_monsoon_simple_agent \
    --input benchmarks/voicearena_monsoon/data/voicearena

author: abdelaziz-mahdy
body:
On shutdown, `ThreadPoolAgency.stop()` calls `shutdownNow()`, which interrupts every running task, but nothing waits for them. Pool threads are daemons, so the JVM exits while a task is still in its interrupt handler, and work it meant to undo, such as a cron rolling back what it half wrote, stays half done.

```
Task that catches InterruptedException, then cleans up for 300 ms
  ThreadPoolAgency.stop() returns at once; JVM exits mid-cleanup    <- before
  ThreadPoolAgency.stop() returns after 303 ms, cleanup finished    <- after
Task that swallows every interrupt (shutdownTimeout 1500 ms in the test)
  ThreadPoolAgency.stop() gives up after 1505 ms                    <- after
```

Fix: `ThreadPoolAgency.stop()` waits up to `shutdownTimeout` (default 10 s, Docker's default stop grace period) for running tasks after `shutdownNow()`, and logs a warning if some are still running. Tasks still in the queue are dropped by `shutdownNow()` and never run. `reload()` keeps its old behaviour and does not wait.

The cron scheduler's own loop runs on `threadPool` and ignores interrupts on purpose, so that a cron timeout or a pool reload does not kill it. It now ends when its pool's `stop()` begins (a `stopping` flag only `stop()` sets); otherwise every shutdown would wait out the timeout for it.

Please check the stop order: services stop in `HashMap` order (`Boot.java:39`), so a service a task's cleanup needs, such as a JDBC connection pool, may already be stopped when the thread pools wait. Should the thread pools stop before other services?

DOS-5985

body: **Stacked on #1579** (decode each RAW once). Its base is `claude/v2-raw-decode-once`; I'll retarget to `main` when #1579 merges. **Problem:** a 45 MP RAW is about 270 MB as RGB16. Since #1494, every RAW JPEG, PNG, TIFF and format output frames and edits that full-size picture on the main thread, so the app froze for seconds per output. That matters most on desktop, which owner decision 14 makes the full app. **Change** - `master16.ts`: `frameAndEditRgb16(picture, turn, edit, framing)` is the frame and edit step (crop, quarter turns, straighten, then `editRgb16` with the lens centre), unchanged maths, now in one function. - New `raw16EditWorker.ts` runs exactly that function off the main thread. - New `raw16Edit.ts` `frameAndEditOffThread`: - A shared decode (#1579's per-photo cache) is copied. An owned one is transferred, so there is no extra 270 MB copy. - It passes the view's offset and length, because the decoder's buffer starts with an 8-byte header. - Cancelling an export terminates the worker at once, so its memory is freed instead of the job finishing in the background. - Without workers (unit tests, very old browsers) it runs on the main thread as before. - `rawMaster16.ts` `editRaw16` works out the turn on the main thread (that needs the shown ``), then hands the frame and edit to the worker. The callers (`renderRaw16`, the TIFF and PNG masters, `scheduledPhotoExport`) are unchanged. Still on the main thread: the RAW decode itself in the browser (wasm; on desktop it runs in Rust), the resize to output size, and encoding. **Tests (`raw16Edit.test.ts`, 5 new)**, using a stand-in worker that hands buffers over the way `postMessage` does: - Pixels are identical to the main thread's for a decoder-shaped buffer with its header, at turn 0 and 90. - A shared picture is left untouched; an owned one is transferred (its buffer detaches). - Cancelling terminates the worker and rejects. An already-cancelled export starts no worker. - A stopped worker reports in plain words. - The no-worker fallback gives the same pixels. **Checks** - Laptop, targeted: `raw16Edit`, `rawSourceCache`, `master16`, `raw16Working`: 40/40 PASS. `tsc --noEmit`: PASS. - Browser tests: NOT RUN on the laptop. `tests/v2-raw-develop.spec.ts`'s 16-bit TIFF and PNG master tests go through `editRaw16`, so the real worker runs in Chromium on CI. GitHub Actions is the check of record. - No new wording. No ROADMAP edit. **Not verified:** how long a real 45 MP NEF takes in the installed desktop app, and whether the UI stays responsive during an export. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: joshuata
body:
## What A new `Popover` component in `ilw-ui/svelte` and `ilw-ui/react`: a button that opens a non-modal panel anchored to it, for filter panels, "?" help buttons and secondary actions. The toolkit has no popover, so this is a new gap item (E18 on the roadmap, uiuc-csid/ilw-ui#9). ```html
…
 ``` ## How - **Native first.** The panel is a native auto popover opened by `popovertarget`. The browser handles Escape, clicking outside, one open at a time, focus return, the implicit `aria-expanded`, and putting the panel next in the Tab order. The markup works from a server template with no script. - **APG disclosure, not a dialog.** Opening it leaves focus on the button. - **Placement.** `popover.css` places the panel with CSS anchor positioning (`position-area` + `anchor-scope`, 4px off the button) and flips it above or below when there's no room. Six placements: `bottom-left` (default), `bottom-center`, `bottom-right`, `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`. - **What the component adds:** - `open` state: bindable in Svelte; in React, optional `open` plus `onOpenChange`. - Closing the panel when focus moves outside it. - Placing the panel by script in browsers without anchor positioning. - **Shared code** is in `src/core/popover.ts`, used by both `Popover.svelte` and `Popover.tsx`. `src/react/use-next-id.ts` is the `useNextId` hook from the React plan. ## Stories and tests - `Overlays/Popover` in both Storybooks: Fixture, Open, Phone, Toggle, Placements. - Controls: `label` and `placement` drive the demo page's Filters popover. - A Phone / Tablet / Laptop viewport list; the Phone story checks the panel fits at 375 px. - Play functions are shared (`stories/plays/popover.ts`), and both frameworks compare against the same contract files. - `tests/e2e/popover.spec.ts` covers Enter, Tab into the panel, Escape with focus return, Done, Tab past the end, Shift+Tab, clicking outside, and the script fallback. It passed `--repeat-each 20` on all four projects (480/480), and the stories passed `--repeats 10`. - `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` (641 tests) pass, both Storybooks build, and `compare-index` passes. Re-run after merging main's Storybook 11.0.0-rc.0 migration. ## For reviewers - **Escape and click-outside are only tested in the keyboard spec.** The stories' simulated keys and clicks don't trigger the browser's close-on-Escape or close-on-click-outside. - **`react-ssr.test.ts` now ignores the case of attribute names.** React's server render writes `popoverTarget="…"`, which browsers parse as `popovertarget`. - **The script fallback switches off `position-area` inline.** Otherwise, where anchor positioning exists but the script places the panel (the spec stubs `CSS.supports`), its `top`/`left` are offsets inside the anchor area. - **The screen-reader checks in `docs/at-smoke.md` still need a person to run them.** - Docs: a README section with the DOM contract, roadmap row E18, and the plan with an outcome section in `docs/old-plans/2026-11-25-popover.md`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sbarczyk
body:
**Stack 3/5 · relationship search.** Base: #60 · Next: #58.

The editing side of relationship search: a stage where the question is drawn and an inspector where each part is set up. These components are not opened from anywhere yet; #58 puts them in a modal.

### Stage
- `PatternStage.tsx`: the question drawn as a small graph on dotted "analysis paper". Nodes can be dragged and links drawn between them. Known entities show in their type's colour, a group of known entities appears as stacked sheets, link arrows point the way the relationship runs, and once there is an answer each sought node shows its match count.
- `StageToolbar.tsx`, `AddEntity.tsx`, `KnownSearch.tsx`: add a sought node or find a known entity. Name matches show on every keystroke from a cached pool, and search by meaning runs once typing settles.

### Inspector (docked under the stage)
- `NodeEditor.tsx`: a sought node's type, part of its name and minimum number of links.
- `LinkCountEditor.tsx`: "co najmniej N powiązań [relacja] z [typ]", edited as a sentence whose parts open their choices.
- `KnownGroup.tsx`: the entities a known node stands for, and how many of them a match must be linked to (one, at least N, all).
- `EdgeEditor.tsx`, `DirectionPicker.tsx`, `HopsInput.tsx`: a link's relationship (only those the space has between the two types), its direction, its length in hops, and whether it is required, optional or must not exist. When a mode isn't allowed, it says why in the user's terms.
- Small building blocks: `Chips`, `Stepper`, `Row`, `NodeButton`, `SoughtTag`.

### Tests
No new unit tests: the logic behind these components is in #60. Checked with `tsc`, ESLint and the existing suite.

author: solomonic
body:
Automated pin bump: re-vendors the [ai-price-index](https://github.com/RoninForge/ai-price-index) dataset to `v2026.11.25-430e96e`.

## What changed

- `internal/pricing/PINNED_TAG` -> `v2026.11.25-430e96e`
- `internal/pricing/index/**` + `PROVENANCE.json` re-vendored from that tag (sha256 provenance refreshed)
- `internal/pricing/table_gen.go` regenerated from the new vendored data
- `internal/pricing/refresh/testdata/**` refreshed to the same release's published signed bundle, so the fixture and the compiled table stay in step (a frozen fixture eventually reads as a rollback and fails the refresh tests)

## Why this is safe to auto-merge

The pricing was already human-verified upstream in the dataset repo, which is the source of truth and owns the daily pricing audit. This PR does not introduce a new rate by hand; it only re-vendors the already-verified data into the binary's embedded table.

CI proves the embedding is faithful before this can merge:

- `pricing-codegen` regenerates `table_gen.go` from the vendored artifacts (offline) and fails on any drift, so the embedded table provably matches the dataset.
- the golden-vector and point-in-time pricing tests in `internal/pricing` ran green in this job and run again in CI.

BudgetClaw stays zero-key, zero-latency, and fully offline: the price table is embedded at build time, there is no runtime network access.

## No forced migration

Pricing is point-in-time. A new rate adds a new interval and does not change rows already priced at their then-effective rate, so this routine refresh does not require users to run `backfill --rebuild`. Only a correction to a past rate would.

Opened by `.github/workflows/pricing-bump.yml`.

author: milind-soni
body:
## What

Publishing a bot or department template to the community now scrubs personal details automatically, before anything leaves the computer, and credits the publisher with an optional **Published by** name.

### Automatic scrub (`shared/publish-scrub.ts`)

One dependency-free function (the MausBot Admin runs the same file as a backstop) rewrites every text the template carries:

| What | Example | Becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home folders | `/Users/janedoe/WorkSpace/acme`, `/home/bob`, `C:\Users\John Smith\Docs`, `C:/Users/bob` (also `C:\\Users\\…` as quoted YAML writes it) | `~/WorkSpace/acme`, `~`, `~\Docs`, `~` |
| The app's data folders | `~/.openmausbot-profiles/default/workspaces/<uuid>/out.md`, `…/task-workspaces/<bot>/<thread>/x` | `<workspace>/out.md` |
| Email addresses | `jane.doe@acme.io` (not `git@github.com:`, `icon@2x.png`, `you@example.com`, noreply) | `<email>` |
| Phone numbers in clear formats | `+1 (415) 555-0132`, `415-555-0132`, `+44 20 7946 0958`, `+919876543210`, `020 7946 0958` | `<phone>` |
| Key/token shapes | `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `github_pat_…`, `xox?-…`, `AKIA…`, `AIza…`, a random `Bearer` token, private key blocks | `<secret>` |
| The publisher's own names | this computer's user name, and the profile name when it isn't the credit. A full name is replaced anywhere; a one-word name only as a handle or folder (`@jane`, `~jane`, `/srv/jane/`), so a user name like `will` doesn't wreck prose. Never common words like `root`/`node`, never inside an id | `<name>` |

Timestamps and ids stay (`anchorAt: 1794748391525`, ISO dates, IPs, versions, UUIDs, cron). Only matched spans change, so Markdown, code fences and YAML stay as they were. It is deterministic and idempotent; `shared/publish-scrub.vectors.json` holds the input→output vectors both repos test, and a scan over every template in the community repo shows only real paths, emails and phone numbers changing.

### Where it runs

- **Make template** scrubs the folder it writes, so the bot's folder and Details already show the cleaned text.
- **Publish** scrubs again (the bot may have edited the folder) and writes the cleaned folder back.
- **Save folder / your GitHub repo / team library** get the scrubbed files too.
- **A key blocks publishing.** If anything key- or token-shaped is in what the template carries (checked before the existing masking, connections excluded), Publish is refused and nothing is sent, even masked.

### What the person sees

- One line on the card: "We removed 3 local paths and 1 email before publishing" (distinct values, with the locale's list format).
- With a key: one red line, "It holds a key or token, so it can't be published. Remove it from the bot, then update the template.", and Publish is disabled.
- One optional field, **Published by**, above Publish. It starts with the session's own profile name, never the OS user name and never a shared workspace owner's profile. The person can edit or clear it, and empty publishes as `Community`. A name with `@` is refused.
- After publishing, the card says "Published by <name>". The Templates gallery shows the same line from `catalog.json`'s new `author` field, once the community repo copies it. Placeholder credits ("Community", "MausBot user") are never shown.

A bot publishing through the share tool uses the name last chosen on the card. With none chosen, it uses `Community`, so a name the person never saw is never published.

No new settings, dialogs or flags; `server/index.ts` is unchanged. Strings are added in en and pt-BR.

## Checks

- `server/cloud-team-templates.e2e.test.ts` passes
- `server/share.e2e.test.ts` (isolated fixture: make template from chat, check the saved folder is scrubbed, card counts and the key block)
- `scripts/testing/team-template-ui.e2e.test.ts` fails the same way on origin/main (a "Sales crew" managed section); it's unrelated
- `tsc -b`, `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` (8 GB heap), `tsc -p packages/phone-protocol/tsconfig.json`, `oxlint --deny-warnings .`, `node scripts/generate-locale.mjs --check`
- Tests (Vitest): `shared/publish-scrub.test.ts` (vectors, leaked shapes, timestamps, hostile 1 MB inputs), `server/share.test.ts` (scrub on make and publish, a key blocks, credit flow, names), `server/share-team-templates.test.ts` (HTTP body), `server/team-library.test.ts` (catalog author), `src/components/TemplateCard.test.ts`, `src/lib/template-share.test.ts`, plus the size ratchet and vocabulary guards

author: teamleaderleo
body:
The nightly-next `cmux-next quality report / report` has been red since 11-20. Its most recent failure is in the v2 gate home: `v2.pr04.chat_stopped_reader: the gate did not report a measure` (runs 45640200374 and 45594073290).

Cause: the god worker fails `row 1 after the resume: left: None`. The reference `View` keeps only the newest 4096 row ids and drops the lowest id first. The god side streams about 1.2M rows, so row 1 (the chat's opening row, which every window still carries) is evicted. The resumed reader's window then has a row the reference no longer holds. The small side streams 2048 rows and never evicts, so it passes.

Fix (test only): the reference view pins the ids a window delivered, so they are never evicted. It still holds 4096 rows plus the pinned ones, so the memory measured on the god side does not change in any meaningful way.

Base-red sweep, lane-9 fallback row "cmux-next quality report / report". Leo's words via the brief: "No new guard".

body:
Closes #601

## Summary

Follow-up to merged PR `#607` (`c0b516020`), this change shards wallet projection external sorting, draining, and SST emission across two-byte key-prefix partitions while bounding open merge descriptors and scaling default sort budgets from container memory:

- **Key-prefix sharded variable-value sorter (`crates/zinder-rocksdb-bulk-load`):** Adds `ShardedKeyPrefixSorter` / `ShardedKeyPrefixWriter` / `ShardedSortedVariableValues` (`bulk_load/variable_value_sort.rs`, `bulk_load.rs`, `lib.rs`) with independent per-shard buffers, `SharedMemoryTracker` bounded credit (flushing all local buckets before direct fallback pushes), `SharedTempFileBudget` enforcing `2×` merge-pass headroom and `TemporaryFileLimitBeforeFinish` on pre-finish spills, explicit `per_shard_merge_fan_in_cap` enforcement across all open shards, and parallel partition flushing/merging.
- **Sharded wallet outpoint merge & address-transaction drain (`crates/zinder-wallet-rocksdb`):** Updates `projection_load.rs` and `accumulator_hashing.rs` (`BranchHashingPool::split_many` / `split_secondary`) so both outpoint merges and secondary address-transaction drains partition and emit disjoint non-overlapping SST ranges across workers, enforces `(address_index_push_shards * address_index_per_shard_fan_in) + (address_transaction_shards * address_transaction_per_shard_fan_in) <= active_merge_fan_in`, caps cumulative pipelined SST queue memory (`PIPELINED_SST_TOTAL_QUEUE_CAP_BYTES = 16 MiB`), adds `RetainedUndoCollector`, and verifies ingest/digest parity against serial builds across `[2, 3, 4, 8]` shards.
- **Container-proportional build defaults & docs (`crates/zinder-runtime`, `services/zinder-projector`, `docs/`):** Adds `wallet_build_outpoint_sort_memory_bytes_for`, `wallet_build_secondary_sort_memory_bytes_per_sorter_for`, and `wallet_build_reorg_undo_memory_bytes_for` (`memory_budget.rs`, `env_var_docs.rs`, `services/zinder-projector/src/bin/zinder-projector/config.rs`, `tests/integration/cli.rs`), safely clamping tiny containers while leaving headroom on `2 GiB`, `6 GiB`, `10 GiB`, and `64 GiB` envelopes, and updates ADR-0005, `configuration.md`, and `bulk-catchup-resource-tuning.md`.

## Validation

- Verified on commit `ac11d7ac6` (rebased onto `origin/main` `c0b516020`):

body:
AIStor can encrypt data at rest with a drive key held in the KMS store. Add the client side of its admin API so callers can manage it.

- AdminClient methods to enable and disable cluster encryption, rotate the drive key, read the status (with the key state of every node), look up the encryption of one object version, and start, stop, pause, resume and query the encryption job.
- DistJobTypeClusterEncryption, with wire value 4 and name "encrypt-at-rest". The name stays because it names the job's checkpoints on the drives.
- BucketUsageInfo and DataUsageInfo report the versions not encrypted at rest and their on-disk size. The scanner counts them whether or not cluster encryption is enabled. The fields are omitted when zero.

Rotate and the job calls (start, stop, pause, resume) never retry. The server may act before it answers 503, so a repeat could apply the change twice. Enable and disable are safe to repeat.

author: danielezonca
body:
## Why

The **Model detail** table on *My usage* only showed total tokens per model, so a user could not tell an input-heavy model from an output- or cache-heavy one without scrolling to *Recent transactions* and adding rows up by hand.

**This came from a user request, not an internal idea:** a dashboard user asked for the input/output/cache split to be shown there, "similar to what we already have in the recent transactions section below".

## What

`internal/dashboard/account.html` — the Model detail table gains four columns and the old token column becomes Total:

| before | after |
|---|---|
| Model · Type · Requests · **Tokens** · Spend · Share | Model · Type · Requests · **Input · Output · Cached · Cache write · Total** · Spend · Share |

- Same header labels, `title` tooltips, `tok-in` / `tok-out` / `tok-cached` / `tok-cache-write` / `tok-total` colours and `compact()` formatting as *Recent transactions*, so the two tables on the page read identically. No new CSS, class names or wording — the second table is pointed at what the feed already defines.
- `Total` keeps the `tokens` sort key (still ordered by `total_tokens`), so nothing is lost versus the old column.
- `colspan` updated to 10 in all three `#model-rows` placeholder rows (loading, empty, load-failure) so no state renders a ragged row.
- No API change: `GET /api/v1/me/usage/models` already served `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_tokens` via `storage.ModelSummary`, in both the raw `GetDashboardModels` query and `rollupModelsSQL`. No backend, schema or migration change.
- `internal/dashboard/cluster_parity_test.go`: refreshed the `account.html` golden hash, as required for any intentional page change.

## Semantics

Cached and Cache write are **subsets of Input**, not siblings — prompt tokens already include them (see `costUSDExpr`). So `Input + Output == Total`, and adding the four split columns up will overshoot. This mirrors the recent-transactions feed exactly; the `Total` tooltip states "Input + output tokens". Rows without prompt caching legitimately show `0` in both cache columns.

## Testing

- `go test ./...` green against `postgres:16`, run in a `golang:1.26` container in the same shape as `.github/workflows` (`gofmt -l .` → `go vet ./...` → `go test ./...`): `cmd`, `config`, `dashboard`, `handler`, `k8s`, `maasapi`, `pricing`, `storage` all ok.
- `TestClusterModeBytesMatchMain`: `account.html`'s golden hash is refreshed in this commit (page has no `MODE:` markers, so cluster-mode bytes are the file's sha256) — this guard failed before the refresh, i.e. the PR would have been red on CI.
- `node --test tests/ui/*.test.cjs`: 17/18 pass. The one failure (`identity-less self fallback uses personal usage…`, `local-review.test.cjs`) also fails on `main` with this change stashed and does not touch `account.html`.
- Adversarial review (GLM) before submission; its one real finding — a third `#model-rows` `colspan` in the load-failure path — is fixed here.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Model detail has no token-colour legend and no sticky header, unlike the feed's `.recent-scroll` wrapper — worth aligning both cards in a separate change.
- Dimming zero cache cells (`—` instead of `0`) in both tables, to cut visual noise on models that never use prompt caching.
- No test covers this table; a small `internal/dashboard` test counting the `<th>`s against every `#model-rows` `colspan` would have caught the missed cell.

author: moofone
body:
## What changes

When a Live TV channel times out, stalls or ends, the error screen used to show fixed text, e.g. "did not present channel video before the startup time limit", even when Plozz's loopback relay had seen the provider fail. The failure report now carries the relay's evidence and explains itself from it:

- **A refusal or network error the relay recorded** (any 4xx/5xx, time-out, DNS, TLS) uses the existing provider messages. Unknown statuses read "The provider refused the stream (HTTP n)."
- **The channel request was never answered:** "The provider did not respond to the request for this channel."
- **The request was answered with no data:** "The provider accepted the request but sent no data for this channel."
- **A playlist arrived but its segments delivered no bytes:** "The provider sent the channel's playlist but no video."
- **A stall or an ended stream** only blames the provider's *recent* requests, never a segment error the stream recovered from earlier.
- **Inconclusive evidence** (segments arrived, or the root was a master playlist) keeps the generic text, so a decode problem is never blamed on the provider.

The Details/support text now includes the upstream request evidence for these failures too. There are no URLs or hosts in it; a test checks this.

Audio-without-video was already the typed `videoNotDecoded` failure on main, so nothing changes there. The AMC 4K report came from a build without it.

## Other commits

- **iOS build fix:** `PrototypeLayout.rulerFontSize` was tvOS-only, so the iOS app target failed to compile (found by `tools/l10n-sync.py`).
- **Catalog sync:** `tools/l10n-sync.py` adds the new strings, plus about 117 source keys that earlier Live TV changes never synced. Translations are still to follow through the reviewed pipeline; `--check` reports these keys missing in every language, as it did before for the older ones.

## Checks run (tvOS Simulator)

- **CoreModelsTests:** 3257/3262 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped.
- **FeaturePlaybackTests:** 1370/1378 passed. The 2 failures, `NextEpisodeCoordinatorTests` runtime labels, are unrelated to this change.
- **ProviderIPTVTests:** 256 passed, 0 failed, including the new proxy-driven test. The run then wedges in `LiveTVLaunchUnderTenSecondsTests` and the watchdog kills it; it wedges identically on main + #6 without this change. Two later classes, `SavedGuideScheduledProbeTests` and `StorageSuspensionTests`, did not run.
- **App build:** deployed to the owner's tvOS simulator, and the guide opens normally. The new messages have **not** been seen on screen against a real failing channel yet.

author: thiagocalazans-dev
body:
Closes #455

## Summary

As três cópias da busca de contato viram um componente só, `ContactSearch`, com uma prop `variant` que diz como ele se comporta em cada tela. Nenhuma mudança visual. Duas mudanças de comportamento, aprovadas por Laboratório na rodada 1 da revisão (sugestões do revisor aplicadas): setas e "carregar mais" passam a funcionar no Enviar contato, e contato sem telefone fica sempre desabilitado (inclusive durante a conferência do Novo chamado).

```text
frontend/src/components/
├── ContactSearch.tsx          # NOVO: a busca, o resumo do contato e a tabela `variants`
├── NewConversationSheet.tsx   # usa ContactSearch variant="new-conversation"
├── PhoneRegistrationSheet.tsx # usa ContactSearch variant="phone-registration"
└── SendContactDialog.tsx      # usa ContactSearch variant="send-contact"
```

A tabela `variants` no topo de `ContactSearch.tsx` define cada tela:

| Variante | Filtros | Foco na busca | Setas entre contatos | Pagina ao focar o último | Contato sem telefone | Espaço nome/telefone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `new-conversation` | sim | não | sim | sim | desabilitado | não |
| `phone-registration` | não | não | sim | sim | desabilitado | não |
| `send-contact` | sim | sim | **sim (novo)** | **sim (novo)** | fora da lista | sim (2 px) |

O botão "Novo contato" aparece quando a tela passa `onRegister` (Novo chamado e Registrar por telefone). As outras props são `checking`, `onChoose` e `selectedId`/`selectedRow`. A regra de desabilitar é `disabled={checking || !contact.phone}`.

O resumo do contato (`ContactSummary`) também deixou de estar duplicado em Novo chamado e Registrar por telefone.

## Evidence

- **Antes:** capturas da jornada `busca-contato` na `develop` `90f0110` (pasta `antes-90f0110`).
- **Visual do Enviar contato:** no `74e591e` faltava o espaço de 2 px entre nome e telefone (apontado na revisão). Corrigido no `9ffaa9d`; posições medidas iguais às da `90f0110` (topo das linhas 412,22 / 470,97 / 529,72 px, altura 57,75 px) e guardadas por uma asserção geométrica em `send-contact.spec.ts`. Capturas do `9ffaa9d` no comentário de evidência.
- Lint: `make lint` → 0 erros (4 avisos pré-existentes em `TicketPage`/`TicketHistory`); `tsc -b` sem erro.
- Ponta a ponta no `e6fcaf6`, sem mudar asserção existente: `conversas-nova`, `phone-registration`, `send-contact`, `form-dialogs`, `accessibility`, `quotes-screen` e `chamados-acoes` → **85 passed** (82 de antes + 3 novos).
- Testes novos: setas + Enter no Enviar contato; foco no 20º contato carrega a página 2; contato sem telefone aparece como "Sem telefone" e não pode ser escolhido no Novo chamado.
- CI no `e6fcaf6`: Lint, Código gerado, Testes do backend e Testes ponta a ponta verdes.

### Critérios de aceite

| Critério | Evidência |
| --- | --- |
| As três telas usam o mesmo componente | `ContactSearch.tsx`, importado nas três, cada uma com sua `variant`; sem cópia local |
| Cada tela mantém paginação, foco, rolagem, seleção e cadastro | tabela de variantes acima; `send-contact.spec.ts` cobre Voltar com rolagem/foco/página e o teclado; `form-dialogs` cobre o foco da busca |
| E2E das três telas passam sem mudar asserção | 85 passed, asserções antigas intactas, 3 testes adicionados |
| Screenshots antes e depois nas três telas | capturas `01`–`03` de `antes-90f0110` e `busca-contato` (`9ffaa9d`) |
| Nenhuma mudança visual | posições das linhas medidas iguais à `develop`; asserção do espaço de 2 px |
| CI verde | 4 jobs verdes no `e6fcaf6` |

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — refatoração de frontend sem migração nem mudança de contrato; reverter é só voltar os commits.

**Blast Radius:** três janelas do frontend (Novo chamado, Registrar atendimento por telefone, Enviar contato). O backend não muda.

## Out of scope

- A busca da tela de Contatos (cadastro) e o `useContactOptions` não foram mexidos.

author: nakita628
body:
## Why

On `provider = "mysql"`, MyXQL gives `PrismaJson.load/1` two shapes for the same `Json` value. MySQL's `JSON` column is decoded by the driver, so a JSON string `"42"` arrives as the binary `42`. MariaDB's `JSON` is `LONGTEXT`, so the same value arrives as the binary `"42"`, quotes included. The value alone can't tell the two apart. The owner's decision: keep #243's `load/1` as the default (decode when the text is valid JSON), and add an optional `mysqlFlavor = "mysql" | "mariadb"` for an exact read.

Closes #244

## What

- `mysqlFlavor = "mysql"`: `load/1` never decodes a binary. A MySQL string such as `"12345"`, `"true"` or `"null"` stays a string.
- `mysqlFlavor = "mariadb"`: `load/1` decodes every binary, and returns `:error` for text that isn't JSON.
- Unset: unchanged. `type/0` and `dump/1` are the same in all three.
- Any other value fails generation with a `GeneratorConfigError` (`mysqlFlavor of Hekireki-Ecto is "mysql" or "mariadb", not "percona".`). The option is ignored unless the provider is `mysql`.

## Where

`hekireki-ecto` only: `src/core/ecto.ts` reads and checks the option, `src/generator/ecto.ts` passes it on, and `ectoJsonType` / `mysqlJsonLoad` in `src/helper/ecto.ts` write the type. In the README, the option is in hekireki-ecto's row of the ORM table, and a sentence in the `Json` paragraph points MySQL users to it.

## Who

Users of `hekireki-ecto` on MySQL or MariaDB with `Json` fields who set the option. Not breaking: without it, the output is unchanged.

## When

next release

## How

New tests, all failing before the change:
- `src/helper/ecto.test.ts`: `load/1` for each flavour. The output for SQLite and PostgreSQL is the same whatever the option says.
- `src/core/ecto.test.ts` (new): the generator writes the MariaDB `load/1` for `mysqlFlavor = "mariadb"` and refuses `"percona"`.

- [x] `pnpm check`
- [x] `pnpm test`
- [x] `pnpm example`, when a generator's output changed (no diff)
- [ ] `pnpm lang`, when the generated code of a language changed (the harness doesn't set the option)
- [ ] `pnpm test:e2e` in `packages/hekireki`, when Studio (`src/studio/`) changed

author: juliamagan
body:
## Description

Adds a tool under `migration/` that migrates a Wazuh 4.14.x deployment to 5.0.x on the same hosts, for package installations (deb and rpm), all-in-one and clusters. It carries the agent registry and groups, API users and roles, the manager settings that still apply in 5.0, custom rules and decoders (through the ruleset migration tool `rmig`), indexer security, custom dashboards and the 4.x alert history, then upgrades the agents and closes the 4.x agent ports. Until the point of no return it can put the 4.x deployment back.

The tool is one file and one command: `bash builder.sh -m` builds `wazuh-migrate.sh`; the user copies it to the 4.x host (the master on a cluster) and runs `./wazuh-migrate.sh` until it prints `MIGRATION FINISHED`. Each run stops only where the person must decide (the rules review and any settings questions, the point of no return), with every question in one decisions file. A clean all-in-one takes 3 commands and 2 answer rounds; a cluster, 4 and 3.

This is a draft for early review. The tool is not ready for production use. The source must be the latest 4.14.x (4.14.11).

Related: wazuh/internal-devel-requests#7726

## Proposed Changes

- `migration/src/`: the tool. `migrate.sh` is the entry point (a cluster is detected on the master and driven over SSH, `migrate-cluster.sh`); `build-wazuh-migrate.sh` makes the single file.
- `migration/tests/`: unit tests (`bash migration/tests/run_tests.sh`). Tests that need the private ruleset tool skip unless `MIG_TEST_RMIG_DIR` and `MIG_TEST_STOCK_RULESET` are set.
- `migration/README.md`: what the tool does, the user session, the questions, exit codes and settings.
- `builder.sh`: new `-m` option that builds `wazuh-migrate.sh`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: add the entry under `v5.0.0` → `Added`.

## Testing Scope and Coverage

Unit tests from this branch, and end-to-end runs on AWS labs with real 4.14.11 deployments and the 5.0.0 nightly, using only the single file as a customer would.

### Execution Results and Evidence

| Test | Status | Evidence |
| :-- | :-: | :-- |
| Unit tests (`bash migration/tests/run_tests.sh`): 610 run, 22 skipped without the private ruleset tool | :green_circle: | Local run |
| All-in-one, Ubuntu 24.04, 4.14.11: one command to `MIGRATION FINISHED`; agents keep ids and keys; history proven | :green_circle: | Lab run |
| All-in-one: `back`, then the same command starts a new attempt; a killed 5.0 install is waited for; a stopped agent is named and the run waits | :green_circle: | Lab run |
| Ubuntu 24.04 cluster with ufw, from the master with a sudo SSH user: 4 commands and 3 answer rounds; whole-cluster `back` and a new attempt to the finish | :green_circle: | Lab run |
| RHEL 9 cluster (SELinux enforcing, firewalld): end to end on an earlier commit | :yellow_circle: | Rerun on this commit in progress |
| Closing the legacy ports for never-connected agents on a cluster from the decisions file | :red_circle: | Known issue, fix pending |

## Documentation Updates

`migration/README.md`. A user guide will follow.

## Review Checklist

- [ ] Code changes reviewed
- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] End-to-end lab runs pass on the final commit
- [x] CHANGELOG entry has the PR number

author: mumukshupanchal
body:
## What

The demo page, redone to look and behave like a product: a conversation in place of a form. Its guards hold: no framework, no build step, nothing loaded from another origin, no inline script or style, everything from the API written as text, links made in one checked place, nothing kept in the browser. One thing about them changed in how it is shown: what the page sends is said in one line whenever there is a conversation, with the whole notice and the list of questions in a fold.

## Why

The page is the first thing a visitor sees of the project, and it looked like a form from an exercise. What stands behind it (search with citations, a cache, follow-up questions) did not show.

## What a visitor sees now

- **A conversation.** Each question is a bubble, each reply a card in its own turn. The question box is docked at the bottom. Enter asks and Shift+Enter starts a new line (Ctrl+Enter and Cmd+Enter still ask); Enter asks nothing while a character is being composed, with an empty box, over the length limit, or while an answer is being written.
- **An empty state**: a short welcome, four example questions as chips (each a real question of the golden set, one of them a question the handbook does not answer, and the page says so), and the steps of what happens when you ask.
- **Sources as cards** beside the answer on a wide screen and under it on a narrow one: the number, the page's title path, a snippet, a short form of the address on a line that wraps, its host always whole, with the whole address as the link's title and in the passage's fold. Pointing at or focusing a citation number marks its card, and the other way round; pressing a number brings its card into view.
- **"How this answer was made"**: a strip of badges under each reply (passages found, sources cited, the model, the time to the first words and in all, the tokens, a follow-up rewritten, a stored answer and its tier), with everything the page showed before under "All details".
- **Every outcome has its own look and its own word**: an answer, a decline as a calm notice, a reply that was withheld or cut off, a failure with "Ask again", a stop. Stop shows only while an answer is being written.
- **A header** with two plain links to the README (how it works, how it is measured), light and dark themes that follow the system, the system font, shapes drawn in the markup for icons.
- **A phone layout**: one column, the controls under the conversation in about 190 pixels of an 844-pixel screen (192 measured), with the line that says what is sent, and the steps folded.

## What did not change

The API, the service and the page's security policy. The page still sends only the questions as they were searched for, keeps nothing in the browser, and says what it sends: in one line whenever there is a conversation, with the whole notice and the list in a fold.

## Tests

- **The guard tests hold the same rules on the new structure**, and some are stricter: the exact list of the page's own links (with `noopener noreferrer` on the two that leave the page); no part of a drawing that could fetch a file; no live region made by the script, by attribute, property, role or an `output` element (only the two in the markup announce); the script may make only elements from a fixed list, through `make` called by its own name, and may never set `src`, `srcset` or `style`, use `Object.assign` or write a style; the notice of what is sent and its controls are checked in the markup and the stylesheet; and a test of the stylesheet fails on the ways of hiding or cutting text it knows of (an ellipsis, a clamp, a height limit, a non-wrapping or inherited `white-space`, clipping by `overflow` or `contain`, `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, zero opacity or size, a transparent colour), set on the address line, on an element or attribute selector that could reach it, or on the card or what is around it, `!important` included. That test does not compute the cascade, and it does not know every way a style sheet can hide text. Class names fed with text from the API, names built from pieces, and `hidden` set on a line other than the address lines and the notice are not checked.
- **The script is run, not read.** `tests/test_demo_behaviour.py` runs the real script under node with a fake page that has nesting, classes, hidden flags and events, through a conversation that includes an answer, a follow-up, a decline, a withheld reply, a failure, a stop, a failed and an unusable rewrite, key presses, the example questions, "Ask again", copying, the found passages, the count past ten questions and the announcements. 117 faults planted in the script are each caught, among them the 40 a review planted, 37 of which the first version of these tests had missed; a source card or a found passage that is made to fail leaves the answer shown, the card still reached by its number; and the address under every source and found passage is checked as shown, not only as present. The test is skipped, with the reason shown, where node is not installed.
- 3,220 fast tests pass; ruff, the format check and mypy are clean.

## What is not done

- **No real screen reader, and no browser but one**, has been tried: the page was looked at in Chromium only. Contrast was checked by a script for both themes.
- **The pictures used while building were taken with a stand-in service** that returns saved real replies. The README's two pictures are from the real service, on 25 November 2026.
- **The number of passages on the badge** is what the page's own search call returns, since the API does not send how many the answer was given; for a stored answer that is today's search, and the page says so.
- **The hint and the links were chosen by taste**, as any look is; nothing measures whether a visitor finds the page clearer.

## Checklist

- [x] Lint, format, types and tests pass locally
- [x] No new dependency
- [x] The guard tests hold the same rules or stricter ones
- [x] The README's pictures from the real service

body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A note a conductor sends to its own worker on another crew cuts into the worker's running turn by default, as it does for a local worker.

A `session_send` with `crew=` forwarded `steer` only when the caller passed `steer: true`. Left out, the note queued behind the worker's turn, which can last hours. A local send to a session the caller created cuts in by default, so the same sender got two behaviours and had to remember a flag for one of them.

## Why it matters

A conductor that forgets the flag believes it corrected a worker. The worker never sees the note until its turn ends, and the person watching sees notes stack up unread.

## Not a goal

- Changing what the crew does with a steer (its guards, refusals and the queue fall-back are untouched).
- Folding earlier queued notes into a later steer.
- Any change to a send without `crew=`.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

A crew send reaches only a session the caller opened on that crew, so the target is always the caller's own worker: the case in which a local omitted `steer` already cuts in. `mcp_session_crew.run_crew_send` now sends `steer: true` unless the caller passed `steer: false`. The result line reports a fall-back to the queue with its reason for a defaulted steer too. Tool text, the user doc, the spec and the remote-dispatch reference say the new default.

## Backwards compatibility

A caller that left `steer` out on a crew send and relied on the queue now cuts in. `steer: false` keeps the queue. The hub route and the crew are unchanged, so an older crew behaves the same for the flag it receives.

## Tests

- `test/test_mcp_session_crew.py`: an omitted or null `steer` sends `steer: true`; an explicit false queues; a defaulted steer that fell back names why.
- `test/test_session_control_doc.py`: the tool text and the doc state the new default.
- 114 related test files: 5877 passed, 1 failed (`test_goal_conductor_steers_a_working_fleet_like_one_worker`, whose asserted phrase is in no skill file on the base either).

## Manual verification

On the hub, a send with `steer: true` to a busy worker on another crew landed in its running turn; a send without it had queued. After install, a send with `steer` left out is checked the same way.

## Screenshots / video

N/A — no UI change.

## Related Issues

N/A

## Sibling sweep

The other rule-8 arm (`_patrol_wake_admitted`) is unchanged and still needs its own setting. No other caller check reads the owner mark for `crew=`.

author: bucharitesh
body:
Adds a **Calendar event** content type (`calendar-event`): a static code holding one iCalendar `VEVENT` that phone cameras offer to add to the calendar. Refs #310.

## What changed

- **Encoder** (`apps/app/utils/calendar-event.ts`): writes `SUMMARY`, `DTSTART`/`DTEND`, `LOCATION`, `DESCRIPTION` and `URL`. It reuses `escapeIcsText`, `eventTimes`, `zonedTimeToUtc`, `formatUtcStamp` and `isValidTimeZone` from the hosted event block (`lib/landing/blocks/event-calendar.tsx`). That file is plain TypeScript with no imports, so I import it directly and didn't move anything. The block and its tests are unchanged.
  - **Bare `VEVENT`, no `VCALENDAR` wrapper.** ZXing's calendar parser starts at the `BEGIN:VEVENT` line, and the wrapper (`BEGIN:VCALENDAR`, `VERSION`, `PRODID`, `END:VCALENDAR`) adds about 65 bytes, which makes the code denser. QRdx's own scanner already accepts both and adds the wrapper itself for the `.ics` download. Apple doesn't document what the iPhone Camera reads, so the phone check is listed under Owner steps.
  - **Times in UTC (`Z`).** They're converted from the time zone they were typed in, so no `TZID`/`VTIMEZONE` is needed. A missing time zone means UTC. Times skipped or repeated by a DST change follow RFC 5545 §3.3.5 (the block's `zonedTimeToUtc`).
  - **All-day events** use `VALUE=DATE`, and `DTEND` is the day after the last day.
  - **Escaping:** `\\ \; \, \n` in TEXT values. A newline in a value can't start a new line or a new event.
  - **Line endings and folding:** lines end in CRLF and are **not folded**. Readers accept long lines, QRdx's scanner unfolds anyway, and folding only adds bytes.
  - **The link** goes in `URL` and also at the end of `DESCRIPTION`. ML Kit's calendar event, which many Android scanners use, has no URL field, so the link would otherwise be lost there.
  - **Checks:** a name and a start date are required, and so is a start time unless the event is all day. The end must come after the start (an event that runs past midnight needs an end date). The time zone must be a real one, and the link must be an http(s) web address. Without an end time, a timed event lasts an hour.
- **Form** (`content-forms/calendar-event-form.tsx`), built on `SchemaForm`:
  - Fields: event name, all-day switch, start date and time, end date and time, time zone, location, description and web page.
  - Two small additions to `SchemaForm`: a `time` field kind, and `row`, which puts a date and its time side by side. No other form uses `row`, so the other forms look the same.
  - The time zone picker starts in the device's zone (UTC in the server HTML, then the device's zone once the page has loaded, before anyone types). A stored event without a time zone shows UTC, the way the encoder reads it.
- **Long payloads:** past 300 bytes (the "keep it under 300 characters" guidance the Text type's page already gives), the form shows an amber note to shorten the description. It uses the same style as the URL form's warnings.
- **Labels** live in `en.json` (`editor.contentForms.calendarEventForm` and the `schemaForm.fields` keys). They're machine-translated into all 10 locales with `i18n:translate`. Only my own keys are kept; other people's pending strings were left alone.
- **Everywhere types are listed:**
  - In the app: type picker (Business category), `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` (and the `apps/docs/types` copies), `FORMS` in the playground and on the generator pages, `STATIC_ONLY_TYPES`, design_qr's schema map and field descriptions, `describeContent`, form examples, picker and generator icons (`CalendarAdd`), type mark (red `CalendarAdd`, not the event page's orange `Calendar1`).
  - On the marketing pages: the `/qr-code-generator/calendar-event` page copy (with the hosted **Invitation** page as the editable alternative), four sample tiles, a showcase entry. `facts.contentTypes` counts the new type from code.
- **Scanner:** an all-day `DTEND` is the day after the last day, but the result card showed it as the end. It now shows the last day, and no end for a one-day event (`components/scanner/parse.ts`).
- **No new MCP payload tool.** The `qr_payload_*` tools are written by hand, not generated from the type list. design_qr and list_options pick the type up from `CONTENT_FORM_SCHEMAS`. A `qr_payload_event` tool is a follow-up.

## Done when (from #310)

- [x] Encoder with unit tests, including escaping and all-day events (`tests/encoders/calendar-event.test.ts`, 48 tests: escaping, all-day, time zones east and west, DST gap, checks, design_qr, long payloads).
- [x] Round trip: `"calendar-event"` sample in `tests/support/samples.ts`, so `round-trip.test.ts` encodes, renders, decodes and compares it at every error correction level. Also:
  - a hostile-unicode case there;
  - a seeded `parseScan` round trip in `tests/scanner/parse-roundtrip.test.ts`;
  - full render → camera-model decode → `parseScan` tests in the new suite.
- [ ] Scanned with the stock camera on an iPhone and an Android phone. **I can't scan with phones.** The decode is covered in tests; see Owner steps.
- [x] `bun x vitest run` in `apps/app` and `bun run --filter app i18n:check` pass (see Verification).
- [x] Screenshots of the form, desktop and mobile (below).

## Verification

Run locally on this branch:

- `bun x tsc --noEmit` in `apps/app`: clean.
- `bun x vitest run` in `apps/app`: the pre-push hook's run passed 663 files and 15,513 tests. That includes the new suite, `round-trip.test.ts` (every type at L/M/Q/H), `page-codes/scan-types.test.ts` (the four new sample tiles pass the scan score and the 160/320 px camera and crisp decodes) and `playground-samples.test.ts`.
- `bun run test:node`: passed, including the new scanner case in `components/scanner/parse.test.ts` and the event block's `event-calendar.test.tsx`.
- `bun run --filter app i18n:check`: "i18n catalogs OK". Each locale's 34 missing content strings were missing on staging too.
- `bun run lint:ci`: passed, with `ultracite fix` run on every changed file.
- The pre-push hook passed: engine build, both typechecks, `i18n:check`, lint and the affected tests.

### Screenshots

I took these with headless Chrome on `next dev --port 3111`, with a throwaway `.env.local` (an unreachable `DATABASE_URL`, no production keys; signed-out pages don't need the database). The repo's `e2e/cdp.mjs` filled the form through its labels. GitHub image upload needs a signed-in browser, so they aren't attached here. They're in the lane folder on the owner's Mac, `~/Desktop/Work/qrdx/.git/lane-briefs/issues-nov25/shots-calendar/`:

- `calendar-event-generator-desktop.png`: `/qr-code-generator/calendar-event` at 1440 px. Date and time sit side by side, the time zone picker starts in the device's zone (here `Asia/Calcutta`), and the live code is on the right.
- `calendar-event-generator-mobile.png` and `-mobile-2.png`: the same page at 390 px, rows stacked.
- `calendar-event-playground-desktop.png`: `/playground?type=calendar-event` with a long description. The red calendar type mark is in the picker, the amber note says the code is dense, and the scan score drops to 65.

The first phone screenshots showed date and time side by side cutting off their values ("17/04/202", "06:00 P"). The second commit stacks them below the `sm` breakpoint, and the screenshots above were taken after that fix. No console errors on either page.

## Overlap

No open PR touches these files. Lane D (Micro QR, #384) also adds strings to `en.json` and the catalogs; all my edits there are additive.

## Follow-ups

- The cloud repo's marketing site (`qrdx-cloud/apps/site`) has its own copy of `lib/qr-types-content.ts` and the type-mark colours. `/qr-code-generator/calendar-event` needs the entry mirrored there, and the core pin bumped, before it shows on qrdx.dev.

_Requested by **Laurence** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0195VUSTsEaVtaQxpYuLUV6S?thread=cmsg_0195VUSTsEaVtaQxpYuLUV6SJHbhtP6xcZbvsoGpVm8oyo)_

## What this does

This is the supply-side half of Antigravity's #280, rebuilt as a pre-registered lane (`planning/lanes/SUPPLY_corporate_capital_channel.md`). The pre-registration is the first commit; the outturn is appended below the line.

For a `CorporateTaxPolicy` with a statutory rate change, the FRB/US-Lite dynamic view now adds the output change that comes from the C-corporation capital stock. It uses the textbook user-cost channel, and every input is a file the repository already ships:

- **EMTR on C-corporation capital**: CBO publication 53724, `tp_emtr_capital_business_c_corp`, scaled by Δτ/τ₀. That scaling is an approximation and the lane says so.
- **C-corporation share of capital (0.44)**: read back from CBO's own capital-weighted aggregate EMTRs.
- **α, δ, K/Y**: `CAPITAL_SHARE` and the OLG calibration's BEA targets.
- **Path**: the capital stock closes the gap at the Solow rate `(1−α)(g+δ)`, with `g` taken from the vintage's own real GDP path.

No new constant is introduced, and a test fails if the module types a float other than 0, 1 or 100, or reads a scorecard target.

## Results (FY2026–2035, February 2026 vintage)

| Preset | Feedback before | Feedback after | Dynamic total before | Dynamic total after |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Biden Corporate 28% | −$86.6B | **−$248.8B** | −$1,085.9B | **−$923.7B** |
| Trump Corporate 15% | +$96.5B | **+$235.5B** | +$1,390.3B | **+$1,251.3B** |

All four figures land inside their ±$1B pre-registered bands. For the 28% preset, the long-run output effect is −0.84% of GDP, and −0.29% of it is reached by FY2035.

## What does not move

- **Conventional scores**: unchanged on every surface.
- **Validation artifacts**: `cold_holdout.py --json`, `run_validation_dashboard.py` and `run_loo.py --donor-matrix` are byte-identical to `main`.
- **Every other dynamic view**: a sweep of every preset under both adapters found only the two corporate FRB/US-Lite views changed.
- **Tariffs**: stay demand-only, as `HSC_h8_tariff_feedback.md` decided.
- **The Simple Keynesian adapter**: stays demand-only.

## Why #280's version was not used

- Its constants (−0.075% per point; −0.95 × tariff revenue) had no source, and its docstring and code disagreed.
- It typed in GDP as $28T.
- Its tariff drag reversed a recorded finding.

## Not predicted

The two older vintages (Feb 2024, Jan 2025) do not carry CBO's housing EMTR, so the capital share cannot be read back from them and the channel is off there. The app's default vintage is unaffected.

## Surfaces

These now say the one supply channel is the corporate capital stock, for corporate rate changes only:
- the Streamlit dynamic tab
- the site's dynamic tag and Economic effects note
- the Ask tool
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `METHODOLOGY.md`

The Streamlit tab also carries a Decision 6 caption that computes the demand-only feedback from the same run. `site_data` is regenerated for the two corporate presets only.

## Still open

The long-run figure has not been checked against a published dynamic score (Tax Foundation, PWBM), because those sites are not reachable from this environment.

## Checks

- pytest: 5,378 passed, 8 skipped (key unset)
- ruff and the mypy gate: clean
- web: tsc clean, tests pass

author: yonnock
body:
When GitHub drops a push event, `refs/heads/<branch>` moves but the PR's `headRefOid` and its CI stay on the old sha. Seen in practice: babysit's push barrier timed out with "is someone else pushing to it?" (nobody was), and the rerun warned about the mismatch, skipped CI ("no CI checks reported; continuing"), spent a full review on the stale head and then failed with "the review is for X but the branch is at Y".

- Startup: for a PR target whose fetched branch head differs from the PR head, wait (same 180s window as after a push) for GitHub to catch up, and stop if it never does. Branch-only targets keep the warning.
- Push barrier and startup share `staleHeadError`: when `ls-remote` shows origin already has the sha, the error names the dropped push event and the resync (push a new commit); otherwise the existing other-pusher message stays.
- `headPoll`/`headSettle` timings so tests can shorten the wait.

Design choice: fail fast rather than proceed on origin's head. Reviews, CI and auto-merge all follow GitHub's PR head, so no step can be trusted while it lags. Pushing an empty commit automatically was rejected; that's a commit on someone's branch the user should choose.

Not changed: `ChecksNone` still continues. Path-filtered workflows legitimately produce no runs, and the stale-head case can no longer reach the CI wait.

Checks: `make check` green; new tests in `internal/loop/pr_head_test.go`.

author: pzelasko
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds the `cs_fleurs` benchmark: transcription of the four test sets of CS-FLEURS, a code-switched speech corpus (113 language pairs over 52 languages; read speech plus concatenative and generative TTS), scored by mixed error rate. It uses the `audio_eval` server that is already on `main` (#6249) and carries no scorer code of its own: the generic audio evaluator already implements the mixed error rate for rows marked `use_mer`.

**Why.** Code-switching, where a speaker mixes two languages in one utterance, is a failure mode that monolingual ASR benchmarks do not test. A mixed error rate counts characters for scripts without word boundaries and words for the rest, in the same utterance, so one number is meaningful across Chinese-English and Hindi-English alike. Part of a series of speech and audio benchmarks, one benchmark per PR, each reusing `audio_eval`.

Related issue: none; a new benchmark.

## What changed

- `benchmarks/cs_fleurs/`: `config.yaml`, `manifest.yaml` (`domain: asr`, `licensing: CC-BY-NC-4.0`, experimental, `determinism: unknown`, placeholder reward range because `audio_eval` is evaluation only), `profiles.json` (four profiles), `prepare.py`, `README.md`, `data/.gitignore`.
- `tests/unit_tests/benchmarks/test_cs_fleurs_benchmark.py`: 22 tests, offline against a mock of the dataset repository; two of them (the server accepts the profiles; a prepared Thai-English row is scored as a mixed error rate) run only where the scoring libraries are installed.
- The root `README.md` table row and the fern `benchmarks.mdx` bullet are not part of this PR: they will be added by a follow-up docs PR, to avoid conflicting edits between the parallel benchmark PRs.

Nothing else is touched: no change to `audio_eval`, to `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`, to any `pyproject.toml` or lock file, or to `.github/`.

**Preparation.** `prepare()` reads each test set's `metadata.jsonl` from the pinned `byan/cs-fleurs` revision (`0cdbf166c5517ae4b6eb1c54248522eedec53017`), checks its SHA-256, row count, id uniqueness and audio-path uniqueness, and downloads the clips unchanged (about 150 hours of 16 kHz audio, tens of GB). It fails if a clip is missing after the download. `max_samples_per_profile` (a positive integer, checked first) keeps the first rows of each test set and downloads only their clips. Rows carry the matrix and embedded language, and a flag for grapheme-cluster segmentation (Thai, Lao, Burmese and Khmer).

**Profiles and metrics.** `cs-fleurs.read` (5,818 rows), `cs-fleurs.mms` (14,932), `cs-fleurs.xtts-test1` (11,321) and `cs-fleurs.xtts-test2` (17,226): 49,297 rows. One fixed prompt, the `greedy` request preset, generation-loop cleanup before scoring. Scoring is the generic evaluator's `Multilingual-ASR` task with the multilingual normalizer (combining marks kept). Published as `audio/<profile>/pass@1/*` and `audio/<profile>-<pair>/pass@1/*`: `wer` is the mixed error rate (stored under the `wer` key, so it is not a word error rate), `wer::<pair>` the per-pair value, and `cer` a parallel character error rate computed after lowercasing and removing punctuation (`lower_nopunct`). As in the other audio benchmarks, `no_answer` is half the share of empty generations.

## Validation

All run on this branch, on top of `upstream/main` at `677841e230`:

- `tests/unit_tests/benchmarks/test_cs_fleurs_benchmark.py` in a CI-like core environment without `setuptools`: 20 passed, 2 skipped (the two that need the scoring libraries). The same file inside the `audio_eval` server environment: 22 passed.
- Wider core suites that scan every benchmark (`tests/unit_tests/benchmarks`, `tests/unit_tests/environment`, `tests/unit_tests/tooling/test_update_env_list.py`, `tests/unit_tests/tooling/test_benchmark_shared_modules_packaging.py`), without `setuptools`: 2149 passed, 12 skipped, 1 failed. The failure, `test_environment_validation.py::test_resolve_config_servers_logs_unresolvable_configs[recursive_alias-ConfigError]`, concerns config alias resolution and no file of this PR; it was not compared against a run on plain `main`. The container has no `.git` directory, so the suites that need git (`tests/unit_tests/tooling/test_component_dependencies.py`) were not part of this run.

author: khallilb
body:
## What changed

Browser checks on pull requests now start as soon as a small **Check: scope** job has decided they are needed, instead of waiting for **Check: code** to finish. The two slowest browser jobs are also split so their halves run in parallel:

- **Test: site** keeps Storybook navigation, recipe and component documentation, the deployment dry-run and the production artifact. Its Chromium and WebKit journeys and form-control fixtures move to a new **Test: journeys** job.
- **Test: stories** no longer runs the overlay suite; that is now **Test: overlays**.

`scripts/validate-site.sh` gains `overlays`, `built-site` and `built-journeys` stages for those jobs. `built` and the no-argument run still execute every check locally, in the same order as before. **Gate: validation** now also requires **Check: code**, so a passing gate still means every check passed. `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the deployment guide describe the new jobs.

Checks run locally: all 146 tests in `scripts/` pass, including the updated workflow and stage tests. Those tests were written first and failed against the old workflow and script. A real `bun run validate:site built-journeys` run passed (33 journey tests and 10 control tests), which shows that stage works without the steps that moved to the site job. Biome passes on the changed files. `built-site` was not run locally; it is the previous `built` sequence with the journey steps removed. This pull request's own CI run is the first end-to-end check of the new job graph.

## Why

Recent runtime pull requests took 13 to 15 minutes. Almost all of that was **Test: site** (about 10 minutes, with two roughly 4-minute Playwright suites running one after another) plus about 2 minutes spent waiting for **Check: code**. With the split, the longest browser job should be **Test: layouts** at about 6 minutes, so runtime PRs should finish in roughly 6 to 7 minutes. That is an estimate from step timings in earlier runs, not yet a measurement.

The trade-offs: documentation-only PRs wait a few extra seconds for the scope job before **Check: code** starts. Browser jobs keep running when **Check: code** fails, which uses more runner minutes. Each job still builds its own packages, so no artifacts are shared between browser jobs.

## Summary
At each handover, `kernel_automate_prepare` now keeps an earlier backlog line only while its ticket is still listed by one of its playbook's own poll triggers. It drops a closed or off-filter ticket and names it in a new `dropped` field with a reason. When the ticket's source can't be read, the line is kept and named in `unverified`. The owner gets a **Retire** action on the Tasks screen's Parked run card, so an old run's unfinished items stop being carried without anyone moving a run file by hand.

## Changes
- **`kernel/src/automate/carry-check.ts`** (new): `verifyCarried` works out a ticket's source from its link and re-runs that source's `poll` triggers (only those linked to a playbook) through `fetchPollItems`. It reads `ticket_closed` (from one closed-issue probe per GitHub repo) or `filter_no_longer_matches`, and `unverified` when it has no trigger, a fetch fails, the listing may have been cut (`found >= MAX_POLL_ITEMS`) or a poll spec can't be parsed. It only reads. `CARRY_DROP_REASONS` is the closed set of drop reasons.
- **`kernel/src/automate/retired-runs.ts`** (new): one writer and the readers for the append-only `automate_run_retired` event.
