body:
## Qué hace

Distribuidor 3/3: **compras y reabastecimiento**, más el formulario de proveedores y el arreglo del RNC.

- **Órdenes de compra** a suplidores (OC-00001): se editan en borrador, se envían (PDF para mandarlo por WhatsApp o correo) y se cancelan si no tienen recepciones.
- **Recepción total o parcial:** suma existencia en unidad base (2 cajas de 24 = 48), registra el movimiento de entrada y deja como último costo el costo por unidad (caja ÷ 24). No deja recibir más de lo pendiente, ni aunque dos personas reciban a la vez; una venta simultánea no se pisa. Una línea a costo 0 (bonificación) no cambia el costo.
- **Factura del suplidor desde la orden:** el servidor calcula bienes e ITBIS de lo recibido y aún no facturado y crea el gasto del 606 (tipo 09) enlazado a la orden. No se puede facturar dos veces la misma mercancía. El gerente puede deshacer una factura mal registrada y la orden libera esas cantidades. Desde Gastos se pueden corregir NCF, fecha de pago, forma de pago y descripción, pero no los montos.
- **Sugerencia de compra:** productos bajo mínimo agrupados por suplidor, con lo que falta hasta el máximo (o 2 × mínimo) menos lo pendiente de recibir, en el empaque de la última compra y redondeado hacia arriba. Nada se crea sin confirmar. Productos sin suplidor aparte; con variantes, "revisar a mano".
- **Vista "Compras"** en Gestión de Almacén (permisos `purchases` y `purchases-view`; la factura del suplidor con `finance-expenses`).
- **Proveedores:** tipo de proveedor (Empresa, Persona física, Informal, Del exterior) e identificación con formato de RNC (`1-01-12345-1`) y cédula (`001-1234567-8`), guardada solo con dígitos; campo de persona de contacto; el error real del servidor llega a la pantalla. Las apps instaladas siguen guardando proveedores como hoy.

## ⚠️ Arreglo que ya afecta producción

**El dígito verificador del RNC estaba mal** (también en el formulario de clientes de la 1.1.20): rechazaba entre 2 y 3 de cada 11 RNC reales (ej. `101010632`). Corregido con la fórmula de referencia (python-stdnum) y probado con RNC reales.

## Recortes aprobados por el dueño

Sin envío por correo (solo PDF), sin "empaque de compra por defecto" (la sugerencia usa el de la última compra), sin compras de productos con variantes.

## Base de datos

Migración `20261126000000_compras`: tablas `purchase_orders`, `purchase_order_items`, `purchase_receipts`; `expenses.purchaseOrderId` e `invoiceLines`; `suppliers.supplierType`. Datos: los proveedores con 11 dígitos pasan a persona física, los que tienen letras a exterior, y se quitan guiones de las identificaciones numéricas. Antes de desplegar: respaldo y ensayo contra una copia del respaldo en el servidor.

## Verificación

- 73 archivos de prueba corridos uno por uno: pasan 72; falla `shipmentsView` (ya fallaba en `main`).
- `vite build` con Node 22, `prisma validate` y `node --check` pasan.
- Revisión por tarea, revisión final de toda la rama y una ronda de correcciones revisada.

## Pendiente / no probado

- Un usuario con rol "admin" que no es el dueño no puede deshacer una factura de compra (el dueño y el gerente sí).
- La exportación de datos de la empresa todavía no incluye las compras.

author: n-resmini
body:
## Summary

A message the model's context window cannot hold is now refused before it is sent and left out of the conversation. Before, it was sent, rejected and sent again on every later turn. The CLI's context indicator never reads over 100%.

## Why

- **A 3.5 MB paste (~1.17M tokens):** compaction summarized the history and the request still went out, so the model returned a 400. The overflow recovery sent the same request again and got a second 400. Every later message ("what happened?") sent the paste again and failed, so the conversation was dead.
- **A ~600k-character paste over a 150k window:** compaction paid a summary of a single greeting, and the summary came out longer than the greeting. The request was sent anyway. The model accepted it, but the indicator showed `context 135% · compaction in ~0 tokens`, then 128% on every later turn.

Causes: no compaction step shortens a user message. An old paste stayed protected as the first message or in the verbatim tail. The overflow retry sent the request again even when compaction had not changed it. A summary was kept even when it was no shorter than the text it replaced.

## What changed

- A message that alone exceeds the window (together with the system prompt, tool definitions and turn context) ends the turn with `RequestTooLong` before any model call. Later requests carry a one-line note in its place saying a user message was not sent (`Compactor.oversized`, `leave_out`, `CompactionRecord.excluded`, re-applied by `replay`).
- After compaction, a request whose total is still over the window is not sent. The current message is left out if the rest fits; otherwise the turn ends with `ConversationTooLong` (`refuse_over_window`). The indicator shows this same total, so it cannot pass 100%.
- The CLI's refusal says where the window comes from: `context_window` in `config.yaml`, or the 150k the CLI assumes when the endpoint reports none (`Repl._window_hint`).
- After a "too long" rejection from the provider, the request is retried only if compaction changed it. Otherwise an earlier oversized message is left out and the request retried once, or the turn ends with `ConversationTooLong` (`tool_use.py`).
- Compaction can now summarize an old paste. A first message larger than the tail budget is no longer protected (`_head_size`), and an older request larger than the tail budget is not pulled into the tail (`_cut_point`). A conversation broken before this fix recovers on its next message.
- `two_phase` drops a summary that is no shorter than the text it replaces.
- The CLI's messages:
  - At the threshold, the indicator shows `context N% of W` instead of "compaction in ~0 tokens".
  - "Still over the limit" now points to `/clear` instead of telling the user to summarise.
- Docs: `guides/context-compaction.md`, `guides/llm-providers.md`, `AGENTS.md`.

## Breaking changes

None.

## How it was tested

New tests:
- `test_compaction.py`: `TestAMessageNoWindowHolds`, `TestALargeOlderRequestCanBeSummarized`.
- `test_two_phase.py`: `TestASummaryThatSavesNothing`.
- `test_compaction_cli.py`: `TestAMessageLargerThanTheWindow`. The provider-rejection tests are rewritten, because a request compaction did not change is no longer sent again.

By hand with `domyn run`, against an OpenAI-compatible gateway that reports no window (150k assumed):

| Paste | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ~600k characters (~197k tokens) | sent; indicator at 135%, then 128% | refused in 0.1 s, nothing sent; the next message goes out at 7.5k tokens |
| 3.5 MB (~1.17M tokens) | two 400s per turn; every later turn failed | refused in 0.2 s, no 400; the next message gets an answer, and the model explains the paste was not sent |

## Not in this pull request

- The window of endpoints that report none. The CLI still assumes 150k, so a message between 150k and the model's real window is now refused, where before it went through. Setting `context_window` to the real value fixes it.
- Resuming a conversation broken before this fix was not tried by hand (covered by unit tests).

## Checklist

- [x] It implements an accepted issue, or it is a small fix, or I am a maintainer
- [x] One change per pull request, with nothing unrelated in it
- [x] If a coding agent wrote it: it followed `AGENTS.md`, and I checked the whole diff and what it implies
- [x] `make check-all` passes
- [x] Tests cover the new behaviour (for a bug, a test that fails without the fix)
- [x] The pages under `docs/docs/` say what the change does to them (a page added or retitled also needs its line in `domyn-docs/SKILL.md`)
- [x] No secrets, private URLs or customer data in code, tests or examples

body:
Codex and Antigravity paused next-message suggestions at 90% usage even though suggestions account for roughly 1% of quota, Claude had no off switch (only an off-by-default early-pace override), and the standalone Suggestions section sat below disabled agents on the Providers page.

Changes:
- Raise the shared prompt suggestion usage ceiling from 90% to 100% so Codex and Antigravity pause only once a relevant usage window is spent, and align Antigravity's unknown-model fallback with remainingPercent checks.
- Replace Claude's pace-only setting with a live Claude suggestions on/off switch (default on) that updates CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION in-session, drops in-flight suggestions when off, hides existing Claude suggestions in the composer, and accurately reports promptSuggestions on session.configured and query spans.
- Move the Claude, Codex, and Antigravity suggestion switches to the top of each provider's Configuration tab (noting shared scope when multiple accounts exist), remove the standalone Suggestions section, keep Settings Search live switches working, and auto-open the matching provider row to Configuration on place-link arrival.

author: agit8or1
body:
The first batch (P0-1) of the UI/UX initiative: an audit of the running console, baselines for the §28 workflows, standalone requirements and a phased roadmap. It also includes a few small, reversible fixes the audit found.

There is no migration, API change, agent change or visual redesign. Nothing here is evidence about endpoints.

## Docs: `docs/ux/` (10 pages, not in the in-app bundle)
- **UX_AUDIT.md**: 25 ranked findings (F-1 to F-25) from a Playwright walk of the scratch docs stack.
  - Coverage: 45 pages, in light and dark, at 390, 1280 and 1920 px, for 270 loads.
  - Also measured: axe-core 4.11 at 1280 px, 120 s idle traffic on five pages, and code grep counts.
  - Nothing was configured on the stack (no signer, PSA, peer, AI, SMTP), so this was also the standalone walk.
- **WORKFLOW_BENCHMARKS.md**: B1 to B13 for every §28 target.
  - Each row gives starting conditions, clicks and security steps counted separately.
  - Times are machine-driven (3 runs each), so they are floors, not what a person will see.
- **UX_ROADMAP.md**: P0-1 to P0-8, P1-1 to P1-18 and P2, plus the deferred-feature list and eight owner decisions.
  - It is linked from `implementation-status.md` (relative link) and `readiness.md` (GitHub URL, because readiness.md is in the bundle).
- UX_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md, STANDALONE_REQUIREMENTS.md, SHARED_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md (with a WCAG contrast table), design-tokens.json (draft 0), CROSS_APP_UX_CONTRACT.md, CLIENTST0R_HANDOFF.md and COMPONENT_INVENTORY.md.
- The ClientSt0r shared spec is not yet published. These pages were checked against clientst0r main `2d26c30`, and Clientst0r itself was not modified.
- `docs/ux/` is not bundled: `gen-docs-bundle.mjs` reads only top-level pages, and a comment there says why.

## CLAUDE.md
A new section: *Standalone first, shared design, optional integration*.

## Fixes
- **History tab (F-1).** The ClientSt0r *AI summary* section is no longer drawn with no peer configured. Its stale "holds no AI provider key" text is corrected.
- **Create ticket (F-2).** The button and its reason notice are no longer drawn with no PSA connector. The server already refused the request.
- **Titles (F-14).** The browser title is "Rem0te" with a `%s · Rem0te` template. `/download` shows the portal's branding title instead of "Reboot Remote".
- **Accessible names (F-15).** `aria-label` added to the icon-only buttons axe flagged (Users row menus and filter, monitor, level and window *Remove*, audit pagination, status refresh).
- **Contrast (F-15).** The sidebar version line was the one contrast failure on every page. It is now 12 px in the ordinary muted colour.

## Checks run locally
- `check-versions.mjs` and `check-security-invariants.mjs` pass.
- Web `tsc --noEmit` passes, and eslint passes on every changed file.
- `gen-docs-bundle.mjs` regenerates cleanly.
- e2e-ui's History-tab assertion runs with a peer configured, so the section still renders there.

Not merged, not deployed.

body: ## Story / Task - Story: TS-30 - Description: HU-19 - Navegar al comentario desde el listado y la línea de tiempo, y eliminar los comentarios propios. ## What changes **Backend** (`docs/specs/backend/HU-19.md`) - `DELETE /api/v1/comments/{comment}` (`whereUuid`, `auth:auth0-api`, `can:delete,comment`) → 204. - 404 si el comentario no existe, si el id no es un UUID o si su versión, canción o producción está borrada (`Comment::resolveRouteBinding` con `whereHas('version')`). - 403 para el artista, para un rol desconocido y para un productor que no es el autor. - `CommentPolicy::delete`: solo el autor puede borrar. `isProducer()` y `Comment::isAuthoredBy()` quitan la comprobación duplicada en `create`, `viewAny` y el Resource. - `is_mine` en el listado (`CommentResource`, solo si `author` está cargado). - Los comentarios no se pueden editar: no hay ruta PUT ni PATCH, y un test lo comprueba. **Frontend** (`docs/specs/frontend/HU-19.md`, marcos 16–18 de TS-88) - Saltar a la marca: la marca del listado y los marcadores de la barra son botones que llevan el audio a ese punto y lo reproducen, aunque estuviera en pausa (`VersionPlayer.seekTo`). - Si la URL se está renovando, el salto pasa por `resumeAt`. - Si la URL caduca en el salto, la resuelve el `onError` que ya existía. - Un marcador agrupado salta al primer comentario del grupo. - Marcadores de 24 × 24 px con nombre accesible y en el orden de Tab. La pista sigue con `aria-hidden`. - Eliminar los propios: la papelera solo aparece donde `is_mine` es verdadero. Usa el `AlertDialog` de confirmación con el mismo patrón que `SongList`. - Tras borrar se invalida el listado, aparece «Comentario eliminado.» y el foco va al encabezado «Comentarios» (`finalFocus`). - Si falla, sale el aviso de error, el comentario sigue y el foco vuelve a la papelera. - Un 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` cuenta como borrado. ## How it was tested - [x] Automated tests added or updated - Backend: `CommentDestroyTest` (nuevo), `CommentIndexTest` (`is_mine`) y `ApiRouteProtectionTest` (inventario y UUID). Suite: 816 tests (813 passed, 3 skipped). - Frontend: `CommentList.test.tsx` (#7–#14), `CommentTimeline.test.tsx` (#5–#6, sustituye «es decorativa» de HU-18) y `VersionPlayer.test.tsx` (#1–#4: salto con la URL caducada y durante la renovación). Suite: 567 tests en verde. - Revisión C3 (cada test probado en rojo): - backend: 27 mutaciones, todas en rojo; - frontend: 38 mutaciones, todas en rojo tras añadir el caso «404 con otro `code`», que cubría la única que sobrevivió. - [x] Verified locally: `pint --test`, PHPStan nivel 5 y Pest; `format:check`, `lint` (0 errores), `test` y `build`. ## Review checklist (required) ### Screenshot of Component or Code Working ### CI - [x] Pipeline is green - [x] Lockfiles committed if dependencies changed (no cambian dependencias) ## Notes for the reviewer - Sin migraciones: `comments` ya existe desde HU-17. - `is_mine` es la fuente de verdad del cliente: la papelera no depende del rol. Cuando la parte B de HU-21 permita comentar al artista, sus comentarios mostrarán la papelera sin tocar el frontend. - Fuera de alcance, para decidir en una rama `fix/` aparte: un PUT o PATCH a `/api/v1/comments/{id}` responde 500 en lugar de 405, porque el handler de D3.1 no mapea `MethodNotAllowedHttpException`. - Los marcos 16, 17, 17b, 17c y 18 de HU-19 están en la página «TS-88 · Ampliación» de Figma.

body:
Closes #1835

## 根本原因
1. **上流**: \	ag_property_integrity\ (\data_validator.py\ / \pi.py\) および \un_ttl_expired_recrawl.py\ が \PropertyTypeDetector.detect_from_object(item)\ の粗いMLカテゴリ名 (\partment\) で \PropertyEvaluation.property_type\ を保存・上書きしていた。結果として \KenbiyaInvestmentBuilding\ (\pp3\, \id=1473\) が \property_type='apartment'\ で保存されていた。
2. **下流**: \send_recommendations.py\ の \_match_model_for_company_and_ptype\ が単一モデル (\KenbiyaInvestmentApartment\) のみを返し、URL未発見時に URL 一致検証なしで \id=1473\ フォールバックを実行したため、別テーブル \kenbiya_investment_apartment\ の同一連番 \id=1473\（足立区北加平町 9,990万円）が \e_4814675p1h\（新宿区舟町 2.58億円）の評価レコードに誤結合され、75.1% 割安のお宝物件として誤通知された。

## 修正内容
- **上流**: \esolve_canonical_eval_property_type\ を追加し、\	ag_property_integrity\ / \un_ttl_expired_recrawl._apply_eval_entry_mutation\ / \pi._run_stage1_eval\ で実モデル名由来の正確な \property_type\（例: \investmentbuilding\）を保存・維持するよう修正。
- **下流**: \send_recommendations.py\ で全候補モデルを順に \pageUrl\ 照会し、\property_id\ フォールバック時は \UrlMatcher.is_same_url\ による同一URL検証を必須化。さらに \_dispatch_single_recommendation\ に通知直前の URL 一致ガードを追加。
- **水平展開**: \ecover_sekisan_prices.py\ の \property_id\ 参照にも \UrlMatcher.is_same_url\ ガードを追加。
- **テスト**: \	ests/unit/test_issue_1835_property_url_mismatch.py\ を追加し、関連テスト + \	est_architecture_harness.py\ 計72件全通過を確認。

author: jamesashbourne-lawhive
body: Two vertical merges can start in the same row and end in different rows. The row height plan takes one span length per head row, so the shorter merge's head sized its own row. When that row has a fixed height, the head was clipped at it. Court forms put labels in such merges, under head rows 2 to 6pt tall. The labels disappeared, and only their boxes showed. We found this in two court forms. In one, a cell with six short paragraphs started in a 5.65pt row and covered five fixed rows, 85pt in all. It painted nothing, because its first line started below the 5.65pt row. The editor's search still found the text. ## Behavior - A shorter merge (`w:vMerge`, `CT_VMerge`, ECMA-376 Part 1, §17.4.84) joins a head row that already has a plan, when every row it covers has an exact height (`w:trHeight`, `CT_Height`, §17.4.80; `ST_HeightRule`, §17.18.37). Its head flows through its own rows like other accepted heads, and is clipped at their bottom. - No row height changes. A fixed row keeps its height whatever its cells hold, so the plan's earlier measurements stay valid. - A shorter merge over a row without a fixed height is still declined. That row's height would depend on where the head goes. - Tables in headers, footers, and other tables get the same result, through the one-pass path. - `docx-fidelity.mdx` narrows the "Merges clipped at the first row" entry. This is separate from #2130, which changes the height of a row whose cells all start or continue merges. Both came from the same court forms. ## Tests - `table-vmerge-same-head-row.test.ts` adds 7 layout tests with the fixed measurer. - 5 fail without the source change: all lines of the shorter merge, a head with space before its first line, the same lines as a merge that ends with the longer one, clipping at the bottom of the fixed rows, and a footer table. - 2 pass before and after: every row keeps its fixed height, and a merge over a row without a fixed height keeps its head row. - With the same change on 2.39.0, both court forms show every label in the editor. - `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `check:docs`, `check:parity`, `check:lane-boundaries`, `check:license-headers`, `api:check`, `i18n:validate`, `reference:check-citations`, `collaboration:check`, and `openspec validate typed-ooxml-paragraph-editor --strict` pass. - `test:changed` ran 3054 files: 35068 tests pass. 5 Vue test files timed out under load, at about 300s each. All 62 of their tests pass when run alone with `run-parallel.mjs --only`. ## Collaboration `no-impact` decision in `.collaboration/changes/same-row-merge-spans.json`. The change is in table row layout only. Shared state, operations, and synchronization are unchanged. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: trejgun
body:
Speed-up the balance session asked for (540 map levels x 20 seeds took >10 min).

- `path::Tree`: one Dijkstra from the walker answers routes to every cell. `path::find` is now Tree + route, with identical results. lure's fighting spot builds one tree per decision instead of one search per candidate cell.
- rayon: matrix seeds, map-level seeds and the level lists run in parallel. Results are collected in order before summing, so output is identical on any core count.

Bench (60 map levels, 10 rooms, 20 seeds, 10 cores): 111 s -> 11.8 s (tree) -> 2.3 s (tree + rayon). The output is byte-identical to the old build. `reports/design-guard.txt` is unchanged.

Verified: `cargo fmt --check` and clippy are clean, `cargo test` 53 passed.

author: florianheysen
body:
Follow-up to #218. Images without `f_` or with `f_auto` are encoded in a format picked from the client's `Accept` header and served `public, max-age=31536000`, with no `Vary`. A shared cache in front of a self-hosted instance (nginx, Varnish, a CDN) could hand Chrome's AVIF to Safari 15.

- Core: `TransformService.transform` adds `Vary: Accept` whenever the format was negotiated, on both cached and freshly transformed responses.
- Cloud Worker: the R2 hit path does the same. The miss path already passes the container's headers through. Dashboard thumbnails are skipped, since their format does not depend on the client.
- A named format (`f_png`) sends no `Vary`, so it stays one shared entry.

Tests: the f_auto test now checks the header on both clients and its absence on `f_png`. `packages/core` 213/213, cloud server tests pass, both typecheck.

## The form

The key takeaway, as with THEORYs. SYNTHESIS titles come in three kinds:

- **An integrating claim** gets the claim itself: `Records secure traceability, not correctness`, `Seeing splits categories, acting merges them`.
- **A map of an open question** says what is open: `When networks acquire structure is still open`.
- **A map of a line or an exchange** names it and what it holds: `Learning-and-inquiry: eight parts, no sequence`, `First Contact RL exchange: the self thesis mapped`.

author: juandroo1
body:
## What

- New tool `plan_trip` (AK-2.1 to AK-2.4):
  - Parameters: `from` and `to` (name or ID), `via` (up to 2), `datetime` (local Swiss time), `time_is` (`departure` or `arrival`), `transport_types[]` (string enum), `limit` (1–8, default 4).
- Stop resolution (`StopResolver`, shared with `get_departures` in 2.3):
  - An ID is used as is.
  - A name is searched via `/locations?type=station` and then matched in this order:
    - an exact match, where case and accents are ignored and each language of a bilingual name counts
    - otherwise the only candidate starting with the name, or the only place-level one among them ("Basel" → Basel SBB, "Fribourg" → Fribourg/Freiburg)
    - otherwise the name is ambiguous ("Buchs", "Zürich")
  - An ambiguous name returns the candidates with their IDs instead of connections.
  - If no candidate starts with the name, the tool returns an error that lists similar stops ("Genf" → … 8501008 Genève).
  - The resolved stop is always named in the result.
- Compact format:
  - Each connection gets a summary line: date with weekday, departure → arrival, duration and number of transfers.
  - Each leg gets a line with line, direction, stops, times, platforms, `(now 8)` for a forecast platform change and `(+N min)` for a delay.
  - Walks and transfer times are shown, and an arrival on the next day carries its date.
  - Output lines always end in `\n`.
- Snapshot tests: 11 files in `tests/Perron.Mcp.Tests/Snapshots`. A difference writes a `.received.txt` file, which is git-ignored.
- Token cap: 400 characters per connection with up to 2 transfers, estimated at about 115 tokens. The longest recorded block has 315 characters. There is no API key yet, so the count with `count_tokens` follows in phase 3.
- `find_stops` now uses the same ambiguity rule. Its hint points to `plan_trip`.
- CI, README and Bench tests now expect `find_stops,plan_trip`.

## Decision log

- The resolution rule for stop names, including the fixtures that motivated it.
- The token cap as a character limit, to be confirmed with `count_tokens` in phase 3.

## New fixtures

- Four `/locations` searches, stations only: Basel, Fribourg, Genf, Zürich.
- They were recorded 3 s apart and are listed in the manifest and the README.

## Testing

- `dotnet build -warnaserror` shows 0 warnings, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean, `dotnet test` passes 193/193. No test calls an API.
- Snapshots cover:
  - a direct connection, `now`, arrival time, one via, two vias, trains only, a transfer at Zürich HB
  - French names, a bus leg with a walk, no connections, an ambiguous `from`
- Other tests:
  - the matching rule against the real stop searches
  - how the request is built
  - every invalid input
  - datetime parsing, including summer time and an offset
  - a constructed connection with a delay, a platform change, a walk and an arrival after midnight
  - over HTTP: the `tools/list` schema (snake_case names, `enum` values as strings, `from` and `to` required) and `tools/call` with string enums
- Docker:
  - `mcp` is healthy.
  - `bench check --expect-tools find_stops,plan_trip` printed `OK … tools (2): find_stops, plan_trip`.
  - One live `plan_trip` call (Fribourg → Bern, 2026-11-26 08:00) resolved to Fribourg/Freiburg (8504100) and returned 2 connections.

author: rootulp
body:
Dependabot opened one pull request for each cargo major version update. This change puts all cargo majors in one `rust-major` group, so cargo version updates arrive as at most two pull requests a month. The Go entries also move from weekly to monthly, so every ecosystem uses the same schedule.

<details>
<summary>Opus 5.5</summary>

Changes:

- `.github/dependabot.yml`: add the `rust-major` group (`applies-to: version-updates`, `update-types: [major]`). The ignore rules for consensus-sensitive majors stay as they are. Change the two `gomod` schedules from `weekly` to `monthly`.
- `xtask/tests/dependabot.rs`: add two tests. One checks that every `interval:` is `monthly`. One checks that the `rust-major` group exists.
- `docs/security.md`: describe the new grouping and the schedule.

Limits:

- Security updates do not follow the schedule. Dependabot opens them when an advisory is published. They are already grouped per ecosystem (`rust-security`, `go-security`).
- The recent burst of `go_modules` pull requests (#593, #594, #598, #599) came from Go modules that `dependabot.yml` did not list. Those modules used the repository-level default grouping. #597 fixed that, so new Go advisories now arrive as one `go-security` pull request.
- If one crate in a grouped major update breaks the build, the whole group pull request fails. To merge the other crates, ignore that crate with `@dependabot ignore <crate> major version`.

</details>

author: bidaboss
body:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01C3Xjz6dXDsL7K9MbGqCPeL

## Quoi
Première des deux PR de la photo d'une idée (« Ajouter une idée », capture E11). Le prototype prévoit une « Photo (facultative) ». Cette PR ne contient que le côté serveur. L'écran viendra dans la PR suivante.

La photo d'une idée reste **privée à son auteur**, comme l'idée elle-même.

- **storage.rules** : nouveau dossier `notebooks/{memberId}/photos/{fichier}`.
  - Seul le propriétaire du carnet lit, envoie et supprime.
  - Pas de remplacement d'un fichier existant.
  - JPEG uniquement : ≤ 512 Ko pour la photo, ≤ 64 Ko pour la vignette `-thumb`.
- **firestore.rules** : `isValidNotebookIdea(e, memberId)` accepte un champ `photo`.
  - Ce champ vaut null, ou bien un chemin `notebooks/<propriétaire>/photos/<id>`.
  - Le chemin d'un autre membre ou d'un autre dossier est refusé.
- **Fonction `onNotebookEntryWritten`** : quand une idée perd sa photo, change de photo ou est supprimée, l'ancienne photo et sa vignette sont effacées avec `deleteItemPhoto`. Une photo d'un autre dossier n'est jamais touchée (`droppedNotebookPhoto`).

## Limite connue

author: behdad
body:
Makes `wasm_runtime_set_instruction_count_limit()` work in the Fast JIT, so that a host can have both the limit and JIT speed, and closes the ways around the limit that a review of the first version found. 21 commits on main (fd3c104f).

This is for review in the fork. Nothing has been sent upstream: no issue, no pull request.

## Why

HarfBuzz runs a font's WebAssembly shaper under an instruction limit, which on main only the interpreters enforce. The heavy example shapers need seconds per paragraph there. With this branch and an experimental HarfBuzz copy that uses the Fast JIT, 600 characters of the Nastaliq example shape in 0.6 s under a limit, where the interpreter of the same runtime build takes 13.2 s under the same limit.

## What it does

- **The Fast JIT stops at the limit** (commits 1 to 8). A new IR instruction charges each straight-line run of opcodes when the run starts: one count per wasm opcode, as the classic interpreter counts. The count is kept in a register and shares one countdown in the exec env with the interpreters, armed at the outermost call, so nested calls (host, wasm, native, wasm) count against one limit.
- **A limit of 64 bits** (12): `wasm_runtime_set_instruction_count_limit64(exec_env, int64_t)`. The `int` setter is unchanged. The Fast JIT counts opcodes, about twice what the fast interpreter counts for the same work, and real shaping calls pass `INT_MAX`.
- **A limit on the instance** (13): `wasm_runtime_instantiation_args_set_instruction_count_limit()`. It covers what the runtime runs by itself, which no exec-env limit could reach: the start function, `__post_instantiate`, `__wasm_call_ctors`, and the module's own `malloc`/`free` when the host allocates in the instance. It is opt-in.
- **The module's own `malloc`/`free` run during a limited call count against it** (16). In builds without hardware bound checks they ran on an exec env of their own, without a limit.
- **Threads** (15): a thread that the module creates gets half of what its creator has left, so a chain of threads ends.
- **Size counts** (17, 18): `memory.fill`, `memory.copy` and `memory.init` add bytes / 64, the table instructions elements / 8, and a call adds the bytes of the function's local variables / 64. One count for a `memory.fill` of 64 MiB made the limit worthless as a bound on time.
- **Multi-tier JIT mode ignores the limit from the first call** (11), and says so. Before, a call was limited until its function tiered up to LLVM code and then silently was not.
- **`wasm_runtime_is_instruction_count_limit_enforced(module_inst)`** (4) tells a host whether the limit means anything in the instance's running mode.
- **The interpreters keep one indirect jump per handler** (9). The first version of the nested-call change made Clang fold the fast interpreter's dispatch into three shared jumps.

Enforced in `Mode_Interp` and `Mode_Fast_JIT`. The LLVM JIT, the Multi-tier JIT and AOT ignore the limit and the query returns false there. With metering compiled out there is no API change and the classic interpreter's binary has the same size as main's.

## Bugs outside metering, fixed because the tests hit them

- The Fast JIT's lazy-compile stub went on through `fast_jit_func_ptrs`, which in a multi-tier build can already point at LLVM JIT code (10).
- The Fast JIT left the frame's stack pointer short after `call_indirect` of an imported function, so the next call through `fast_jit_invoke_native` could yield 0 instead of its result (20).
- Both interpreters crashed on `return_call` of an imported function from a function that the host had called (21).

## What a count is

One per wasm opcode in the classic interpreter and the Fast JIT; the fast interpreter counts its own, fewer, instructions, as on main (a loop that costs 9009 in the first two costs 4004 there). At the end of every straight-line run the Fast JIT agrees with the classic interpreter. When a trap happens inside a run the JIT has already counted the rest of it; if a native function swallows that trap, the call goes on with the difference. That is documented, not changed.

## Tests

- 20 build configurations with `-Werror`: GCC and Clang, each interpreter and the Fast JIT with and without metering, threads, no hardware bound checks, multi-tier, LLVM JIT, tail calls, 32-bit x86.
- Unit tests: all suites in classic-interp (536) and fast-interp (209). The metering suites: 86 in each interpreter, 169 in the Fast JIT, 106 in the LLVM JIT, 210 in multi-tier, also 32-bit and Clang. Each new test was seen to fail, or crash, without its fix.
- Spec tests with metering compiled in: 85 of 85 in fast-jit, multi-tier-jit, classic-interp and fast-interp.
- Differential test, classic interpreter against Fast JIT under every limit: 5 builds, 3 modes, 7,329 calls, about 83,000 limits tried per run, no mismatch. A second one written by a reviewer: 41,940 calls from 2,000 random modules, none bad with the size counts switched off (its oracle counts opcodes only).
- Each of the 13 commits after the first eight builds without warnings and passes its metering tests on its own.
- Formatting and the coding-guideline check pass for all 21.

Two new unit suites: `tests/unit/instruction-metering/sw-bound-check` (the same tests without hardware bound checks) and `tests/unit/instruction-metering/thread`.

## What it costs

- Fast JIT with metering compiled in, against compiled out, user-mode instructions: +5% to +40% on eight small benchmarks (calls and tight loops the most), +19% to +20% per shape for two real shaper modules. In cycles the same benchmarks range from -3% to +40%.
- Interpreters, against main, which already meters them: within noise with GCC 15 (0.97 to 1.16 of main's cycles across six programs). With Clang 21 the fast interpreter is at 0.91 to 1.04, and one program (crc) at 1.44. That one is where two indirect jumps land in the binary: moving them four bytes gives 0.98. Nothing in the source controls it.

## Known gaps

- The LLVM JIT, Multi-tier JIT and AOT are not metered. Work on the LLVM JIT and AOT was started and is not in this branch.
- The instance limit is opt-in, and a thread's instance starts in the runtime's default running mode.
- The size terms are a calibration. `memory.grow`, `table.grow` and atomic wait still count 1, and time inside native functions is not counted.
- Compile time and the size of generated code are not limited. A crafted module compiles slowly on main as well (most of the time is in `gen_commit_values` and `clear_values`).
- There is no call to read what a call consumed.
- A lock-order problem in lib-pthread that is on main (`wait_lock` then the cluster's lock in `pthread_create_wrapper`, the other order in `wasm_cluster_set_exception`) can deadlock when a thread hits the limit while another is being created. Not fixed.
- The Fast JIT is x86-64 only. Built and tested on Linux with GCC 15 and Clang 21. The project's CI has not run on this.

## Building and running the tests

```
cmake -S product-mini/platforms/linux -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DWAMR_BUILD_FAST_JIT=1 -DWAMR_BUILD_SIMD=0 -DWAMR_BUILD_INSTRUCTION_METERING=1
cmake --build build
```

The metering tests are in `tests/unit/instruction-metering` and run in every mode that directory is built for.

## If this goes upstream

The project asks for an issue before a feature, and for pull requests of about 300 to 400 changed lines, squash-merged. This is 39 files and about 3,500 lines, so it would go as a series: the three fixes outside metering first, each on its own, then the Fast JIT limit, then the 64-bit setter, the instance limit and the rest. The commits have no `Signed-off-by`; the project does not require one.

author: raicevic
body:
Closes #150.

Table-based e-mails had text centred that Chrome left-aligns. Cause: browsers map `<td align="center">`, `<div align="center">` (and `<center>`) to `text-align: -webkit-center`, which unlike `text-align: center` a `<table>` resets to its initial value (Blink's StyleAdjuster). The e-mails centre their layout tables with an outer `<td align="center">` and rely on that reset for the text inside. AngleSharp computes `-webkit-center` too, but lets it inherit into tables.

- `ComputedStyle.TextAlignFromAttribute` marks a `-webkit-*` alignment. `BoxBuilder.AttributeAlignment`: an element that does not set `text-align` itself (AngleSharp's `ComputeExplicitStyle`; only queried for `-webkit-*` values) takes its parent's resolved alignment, and a table resets it to `start`. Author `text-align` (also `center`) still inherits into tables, and cells with their own `align` or `text-align` keep it.
- The UA style sheet gives `<center>` `text-align: -webkit-center` (as Blink's html.css), which fixes the cerberus e-mails wrapped in `<center>`.
- Local comparison with Chrome's references (words within 2 pt, before → after): postmark-welcome 7 → 133 of 162, postmark-receipt 52 → 159 of 163, cerberus-fluid 20 → 134 of 235, cerberus-hybrid 101 → 151 of 374, cerberus-responsive 207 → 269 of 374. postmark-invoice is unchanged (it differs in page count: another cause).
- Tests: 11 alignment cases (cell, nested table, through a div, right, nested cell with own align or text-align, author override inside, CSS centre inherits into tables, `<center>` with a table and a paragraph, `div align`), standards mode. 6/7 mutations caught (the 7th is equivalent: the flag after a reset changes nothing). The test helper `Flatten` now also descends into table cells.
- Baseline update follows from this PR's Fidelity artifact.

author: vipulbhavsar94
body:
Follow-up to #131 (TECH-8828).

## The problem
When the app finds this PC's registration on a fresh install, it tries to store a registration of its own. If that fails (offline, a server error), the app uses the found one for now and marks it to try again on the next start.

It set that mark before checking whether the user had already moved on to register by hand, and registering by hand didn't clear it. So for a user who registered by hand, the next start:
- sent the automatic registration again (the server just returned the manual one, since it has the same app instance ID);
- waited up to 20 s for the hardware serials first;
- logged a second `registration_completed`, marked `auto`.

## The fix
- The mark is set only once the app actually goes on with the registration found: storing its own failed, or the PC couldn't be read.
- A registration by hand clears it.
- Its key (`PENDING_AUTO_REGISTRATION_KEY`) moves to `registration-context.service.ts`, which both pages use.

One small change in behaviour: when the PC can't be read, the app still uses the registration found, as before. But it now also tries again on the next start, where before it never did.

## Tests
- New:
  - sending fails after the user moved on: nothing left to retry;
  - the PC can't be read: retried on the next start;
  - registering by hand clears a pending retry;
  - a failed registration by hand keeps it.
- `ng test`: 299 of 299 pass.
- Not re-tested end to end on staging.

author: rifont
body:
## Summary

use_skill startup latency, step **T3** (`docs/research/use-skill-startup-latency.md`, "Migration and decision rule").

**Stacked:** on #2843 (T2), which is on #2841 (T1). The base is `main`, so this diff also shows T1 and T2 until they land. This PR's own commits are the last three.

- **Status** comes from the run phase and the command in flight: `ChatSessionStore.getChatStatus` / `selectVisibleChatStatus`. It reads `submitted` from dispatch until the log folds the run, `streaming` while the run runs, and `ready` otherwise. The store announces each change on the chat topic. The composer, the CAD client, the tour, the resume gate and the liveness snapshot all read it. No SDK status or error callback feeds the store any more, and the live SDK error is no longer a visible-failure source; the log and the saved error own failures.
- **Watches are no longer armed.** A dispatch holds its run until the log ends it, pauses it, or another run becomes current. A reattached run opens no stream. The SDK watch recovery (`#recoverPresentation`) and its retry bookkeeping are gone.
- **Usage** (`getHistoricalUsage`) is `usageOf(selectTranscript(projection))`. It is synchronous and cached per snapshot.
- **Composer trays** settle from the fold.
- **First-text timing** reads the run's answer (its tail message) in the displayed transcript.
- **Seed owner:** the seed is cleared once the projection with display authority holds a user turn. This is the rule the SDK materialization kept, and it never reads a fold kept from before a reset.

## Carry-forward risks (attempt 1)

1. **Legacy `chat.json` history.** No chat can have history only in `chat.json`. `chat.json` never stores `messages`: `chatRecordSchema` omits the field (P26), and the file store's `hydrate` returns either `[]` or the one `startupRequest` message, which is the seed. The old IndexedDB chats store was dropped with no migration (A31/I15), the same as before T2. No change is needed.
2. **Seed owner.** Resolved: see the last bullet of the summary. It is covered by `should not consume a seed from a previous session's cached user before a fresh empty host read`.
3. **Steering with live-only text.** Verified in the harness: pi-agent-core injects steering only after `streamAssistantResponse` (the answer's `message_end`) and `turn_end`, and every listener is awaited. New test: `session.test.ts › steering while an answer streams`.
4. **Untested replay cases.** Added the Foreign run case through `remote.views` (Run D from a peer segment) and the cost check on the largest fixture (`kinetic-regenerate-resume.jsonl`, 428 rows): one delta reduces one chunk.

## Tests (testing policy §14)

The SDK status, watch, usage, delivery, approval and live tests now assert on `session.messages` and `getChatStatus`. The SDK presentation recovery suite (`chat-session-store.recovery.test.ts`) is retired with its owner. The T2 "No SDK" replay case is its successor.

## Checks

- `nx typecheck ui`, `agent-host`: pass.
- ui vitest (whole project): 11921 passed. Six fail:
  - The MessageQueue drift gate (see below).
  - Five that fail the same way in this checkout regardless of this change: `vite-module-graph` (an unbuilt `esbuild.wasm` asset), `headless-image` x2 and `channel-diagnostics`. The `headless-image` service failure also fails on the T2 base.
- oxlint and ESLint on the changed files: no errors.

## Formal drift

`MessageQueue` needs a re-pin; the change note is in `MessageQueue.tla` and `README.md`. **Not re-pinned**: that is the coordinator's call:

```
FORMAL_UPDATE=1 pnpm nx test ui --watch=false -- specs/message-queue/message-queue.conformance.test.ts
```

author: righi
body:
Nothing on the way to the five `Main` theorems reads six fields of `Formalism.BasicNotions.NTypes` or four of `Formalism.BasicNotions.NBC`. This PR removes them, their entries at every construction site, and what only they used: 120 lines in 17 files, all deletions apart from three edited lines.

The fields:
- `NTypes`: `Mray_gal`, `Mray_ab`, `Mray_unr`, `bc_pos`, `bc_sum`, `AmbPar`;
- `NBC`: `multAU`, `satAU_card`, `infW_card`, `embAV_inj`.

Also removed:
- The `LocTy` and `LocBC` fields that only supplied them: `LocTy.bc_pos`, `LocTy.bc_sum` and `LocBC.embAV_inj`. The two proof steps in `locTy_exists` that proved the first two go with them.
- The `mult` fields of `GlobalTheory.HeightCounting.AUSide` and `Formalism.L2.AUTied`, whose types mention `multAU`. Both structures are already unreachable from `Main`.
- These declarations, which only the removed fields used:
  - `GlobalTheory.AutQuot.infOf_card` and `satOf_card`;
  - `Formalism.L2.NG.multRep` and `NG.AutRep.mult`;
  - `mult_eq_of_iso`, which was also already unreachable.

Removing an unread field only weakens an assumption, so no statement gets stronger. `Main.lean`, `Challenge.lean` and `Statements.lean` are unchanged.

Found with the field-liveness analysis in https://github.com/righi/riemann_fieldlive (claimed in #151). Both structures are in `DataN.lean` next to `NTh` (#2400), but the edits do not overlap.

I used Claude Code to find and make these changes. I reviewed the change myself.

body:
Closes #1577.

`POST /statistics` with a FeatureCollection currently returns 204 for the whole collection when one feature has no assets. The valid features lose their statistics too.

The loop in `geojson_statistics` now catches `NoAssetFoundError` per feature and continues. Features without assets keep empty `statistics` and `used_assets`; the other features are returned as before. If no feature has assets, the endpoint returns 200 with empty statistics for each feature instead of 204.

Added tests for a mixed collection and for collections with only features without assets. `pytest src/titiler/mosaic -q` passes (11 tests).

author: tannevaled
body:
The global pre-push guard now refuses a push whose new commits add a path matching `(^|/)\.[^/]+\.atomicwrite-[0-9]+$`, naming each path. Escape: `GITSAFE_ALLOW_ATOMICWRITE=1`.

Motivation: a mutsweep temp file was committed and released twice (go-fde/veracrypt v0.8.0, go-filesystems/smb v0.17.2). mutsweep itself now refuses to start with one present; nothing stopped it being committed.

Paths come from `rev-list --objects` and `log --diff-filter=A`, so a file added and deleted within the push still counts and a temp with the same bytes as another file cannot hide. Tests: a refusal (tip clean, earlier commit adds it), a clean push, the escape, and the pattern edge cases.

author: davidwendt
body:
## Description
Improves the performance of `cudf::string_view::compare` for strings of 8 or more bytes by comparing 4 bytes per step instead of 1. This speeds up sorting and searching wide strings, which spend most of their time in this function.

Strings in a column are rarely 4-byte aligned, so each string is read with aligned 32-bit loads and its bytes are realigned with `__funnelshift_r`. Every loaded word contains at least one byte of the string, so no load crosses an allocation boundary. On the first mismatching word, the two words are byte-swapped with `__byte_perm` so that an unsigned integer compare gives the lexicographic byte order. The remaining tail bytes, and strings shorter than 8 bytes, use the existing byte loop. The word path is compiled only under `__CUDACC__` since the header is also included by host-only sources.

The documented return value (`0`, `<0` or `>0`) is unchanged; a mismatch found by the word loop returns `-1` or `1`.

Adds a test that compares strings at all 16 combinations of 4-byte alignments, with mismatches at every position (including bytes `>= 0x80`) and with prefixes.

Benchmark results for an RTX A6000 and an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell are in a comment below.

## Checklist
- [x] I am familiar with the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudf/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] New or existing tests cover these changes.
- [x] The documentation is up to date with these changes.

author: adityakuchhal
body:
Implements FT-006 ([SI-25](https://serious-ish.atlassian.net/browse/SI-25)): the server's clock is the only one that counts, and every swipe and message carries a request ID so a retry never repeats the action.

## What's in it

- **Migration `20261125000100_server_time_requests.sql`**
  - `public.server_time()`: the database clock to the millisecond. Members only; signed-out callers can't run any of our functions (inventory rule), so before sign-in the app uses each reply's `Date` header.
  - `private.quota_period(kind, at)`: the limit period containing a time, as UTC bounds. Likes and rewinds reset at local midnight, SuperLikes at Monday midnight, in `app_config.daily_quota_timezone` (America/Toronto, with Toronto as the fallback). Working in local calendar days keeps resets at midnight on the 23- and 25-hour daylight-saving days. FT-055 uses this as the `usage_counters` period key.
  - `private.lock_request(member, request_id)`: a second copy of a request that arrives while the first is still running waits for it, then finds its stored row and returns the original result without charging a limit again. The pattern `record_swipe` (FT-030) and `send_message` (FT-042) must follow is written at the top of the file. Missing IDs are refused (`REQUEST_ID_REQUIRED`); an ID reused for a different action is refused (`REQUEST_ID_REUSED`).
- **`apps/mobile/src/lib/serverClock.ts`**: `serverNow()` and `timeLeftMs(deadline)` for countdowns. Elapsed time comes from the monotonic clock (`performance.now`), matched to the server by every reply's `Date` header, so changing the phone's clock or time zone never moves a countdown. After a failed call or a return to the foreground, the next reply sets the clock afresh.
- **`api.ts`**: feeds every reply's `Date` header to the clock (errors included), `newRequestId()` for one ID per action, and `syncServerClock()` for millisecond precision through `server_time()`.
- **Error catalogue**: `REQUEST_ID_REQUIRED` and `REQUEST_ID_REUSED` map to G02, as only an app bug can send them.
- **Tests and CI**: `supabase/tests/storage-api` is now `supabase/tests/api` and `pnpm db:test:storage` is now `pnpm db:test:api` (CI step renamed to API tests). `postgres` 3.4.9 is a new dev dependency so a test can hold two database connections at once.
- **README**: a "Server time and duplicate requests" section.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it is met |
| --- | --- |
| Changing the phone's clock or time zone doesn't change any countdown or deadline | Countdowns use the monotonic clock plus the server offset. Jest: a phone clock moved a day ahead and the same deadline in three time zones give the same time left. Deadlines are only stored and checked on the server. |
| The same swipe request twice → one swipe, one quota debit, at most one match | pgTAP with a stand-in that follows the pattern: a repeat returns the original swipe, stores nothing new and charges nothing. Two-connection test: a copy arriving mid-flight waits and gets the same swipe; 10 simultaneous copies give one swipe and one like. Both fail with the lock removed. **Match creation comes with `record_swipe` in FT-030.** |
| The same message request twice → one stored message | pgTAP with a stand-in `send_message`: one message, the same ID returned. The real function comes in FT-042. |
| After a reconnect, the offset is refreshed from the next reply | Jest: after a failed call or a return to the foreground, the next reply resets the clock (an hour's jump while the monotonic clock paused). |
| Tests cover a daylight-saving change and a phone clock set one day ahead | pgTAP: Toronto midnight on the spring (23 h) and autumn (25 h) change days, both 1:30 a.m.s, and a week crossing the change. Jest: countdowns across both changes, and the phone clock a day ahead. |

## Verified

- `pnpm db:test`: 127/127 (26 new). `db lint` on public and private: no errors.
- `pnpm db:test:api`: 13/13 (2 new), cleaning up after itself.
- `pnpm check`: type-check, lint, format, 427 app tests, public variable check.
- Generated types are up to date.
- iOS simulator (iPhone 16 Pro, fresh dev build): replies carry the `Date` header, the clock synced from it (64 ms off), re-synced after a return to the foreground (336 ms off), and the monotonic clock kept counting while in the background.

## Decisions and assumptions

- **SuperLike week starts Monday 00:00 Toronto time.** The docs say "a week" without a start day; to be confirmed with Parveen.
- `server_time()` is for signed-in members only, to keep the "no functions for signed-out callers" rule.

## Not done or not verified

- Real `record_swipe`, `send_message`, server-side deadline checks and match creation belong to FT-030, FT-036 and FT-042.
- `syncServerClock()` isn't called anywhere yet; countdown screens (FT-035/036) will call it.
- Not checked on a real phone: changing the device clock, and the clock while the phone is asleep. The simulator always uses the Mac's clock.
- Dev builds made before #11 lack `expo-crypto` and crash on start; anyone with an older dev build needs to rebuild it.
- After merge: push the migration to staging and production.

Refs: SI-25

_Requested by **Eric** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01SGEzGjUnRawkmyRzYxJfL9?thread=cmsg_01SGEzGjUnRawkmyRzYxJfL95VWaJ3hVc1W9M3uUvKSaz8)_

## What this changes

Roadmap X109 part (b). Read `docs/user-guide/settings.md` first.

- **New page `docs/user-guide/settings.md`.** It covers every field of `ModelSpec`, `CrossFitting`, `Targeting`, `Inference` and `Runtime`. Each row gives the keyword, the default, the kinds of fit that read the field (point, over time, exact times, trial, dose curve) and what the field changes. The page also has a table of each typed method's own options, and a table of every place a method or design replaces a default.
- **New test `tests/unit/test_documentation_settings.py`.** It ties each of those cells to the code:
  - fields, against `dataclasses.fields`;
  - defaults;
  - keywords, against `SHORTCUTS`;
  - "used on", derived by translating a method that changes the field, plus `_READ`, `ATMLE_FIELDS` and `DOSE_RESPONSE_FIELDS`;
  - method options;
  - changed defaults, as a generic diff of each method's translation against the default method with the same groups.

  It also checks that no point or longitudinal translation accepts a setting it does not read. Ten deliberate-mutation controls run each check on a doctored page or method.
- **Behaviour change:** a point-treatment fit now refuses `pseudo_learner`, `censoring_learner` and `competing_learner` instead of silently ignoring them (`methods.py`). The new check found this.
- **Docstrings:**
  - `Inference.simultaneous` and `ModelSpec.survival_model` now state the C-TMLE and DR-TMLE defaults on an event outcome over time.
  - `ModelSpec.screen_threshold` and `min_retain`, and `CorrelationScreener`, now describe what the screen does today: a p-value cut, and `min_retain=None` keeps every covariate. Fix-20 changes that rule and will rewrite these rows.
- **`methods-learners.md`:**
  - a method table, and a C-TMLE strategy table with its interval rules;
  - a "Pool the correction or run it per fold" section;
  - links to the new page;
  - wording fixes (`cluster=`, the `repeats` mean for learned rules, fold evaluation).
- **`capabilities.md`:**
  - the dose-response row now names `DoseResponseCurve`, because #763 routed it through `CausalStudy`;
  - the Targeting row links the settings reference.
- **Shared-test edits:**
  - a `PRELUDES` entry for the new page;
  - `BUDGETS["settings"] = 2750` in `scripts/render_for_reader_review.py`. The page is a lookup reference whose table rows count as main-path words. The budget was re-set to the measured page plus about 10%, on the accuracy reviewer's advice.
  - the writing-for-readers owner row for argument defaults now names this page and its test.

- **Part (c), after merging main.** Main gained the outcome screen from Fix-20 (#772) and the engine options that X123 part (a) routes through the method objects (#762). The page now lists `hazard_library`, `censoring_library`, `norm`, `bootstrap_interval`, `variance`, `cluster_variance` and `max_memory_bytes`. It also drops `screen_threshold` and describes the outcome screen. The test samples the new fields, and a companion setting may now come from another group. This covers roadmap X109 part (c), and X109 moves to the delivered items. The screening paragraph links the "Covariate screening" reference section, and the `cluster_variance` row says only longitudinal TMLE takes the jackknife.

## Evidence

- **Reader review.** Two accuracy reviews (fix then pass, all fixed) and three persona rounds. The quiz answers were correct in each round. After round 3 the remaining blocking flags were fixed: the TMLE, hazard and score glosses, the `effect` link, and the word "pointwise". Per the guide, round 3 is the stop, so no fourth persona read those fixes.
- **Not changed, by choice:**
  - the placement of `q_bounds`, which the quickstart covers;
  - which learner slots a basic fit needs, which "Learner choices" owns;
  - the screening rows, which Fix-20 rewrites.
- **Tests:**
  - targeted doc tests (settings, capability map, links, prose, runtime, API): 5545 passed;
  - every unit test file that passes the three over-time learners, plus the refusal codes: 8442 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed. These ran before the rebase onto main.
  - I did not run the full suite in the cloud.
- **Lint and docs:** `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/cleverly/methods.py` and the docs build (`sphinx-build -W --keep-going`) pass. `python -m tests.prose` shows no unjudged findings.
- **Validation studies:** none regenerated. The only behaviour change is a new refusal of settings that no fit read.

A notebook test, `test_tutorial_semantics_at_documented_size[docs/examples/longitudinal-survival.ipynb]`, fails locally on main at c76cec15 as well as here, so this PR did not cause it.

## Checks

- [x] `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass
- [x] `mypy` passes (changed module)
- [ ] `pytest -q -n auto --dist loadgroup` passes (CI; targeted suites run locally)
- [x] `python -m tests.prose` findings are fixed, or carry `accepted: <reason>` in `tests/prose-report.md`
- [x] `nox -s docs` passes (same sphinx-build command)
- [ ] `python -m build`, strict Twine validation, archive checks, and clean install checks pass (CI)
- [x] regenerated artifacts: none
- [x] `docs/roadmap.md`: X109 moves to `docs/roadmap-delivered.md`

author: zoomrmc
body:
Libinput configuration events echo back settings Triad just sent. Without request tracking, `set_tap`, `set_drag`, `set_drag_lock`, and `set_dwt` can form a feedback loop and leave the device flipping between values.

Triad now tracks current and requested values per device, skips redundant setters, and clears pending requests when River reports the new state or rejects the change. Live input checks are documented in `docs/live-testing.md`.

author: hcal-coder[bot]
body:
## **TLDR:**
mintd's readers stop trusting three things dvc never writes, or reads differently: a cached folder list whose bytes don't match its name, a file list that names one path twice, and a producer's pointer read as YAML 1.1.

## Problem
1. **A cached folder list is trusted even when its bytes don't match its name.**
   - **Before:** the cached list of a folder's files (`.dvc/cache/files/md5/…/<md5>.dir`) is damaged and drops `p2.csv`. `mintd data pull`, import rescue and the push's pin proof take it as whole, and the folder lands without `p2.csv`, reported complete.
   - **After:** mintd hashes the list, sees it doesn't match its name, and treats it as not cached. It fetches the list again, or the pull stops naming it.
   - **What dvc does:** it trusts a read-only cache object as it is (dvc leaves its cache read-only), and re-hashes only a writable one. So where mintd falls back to `dvc pull`, the file can still go missing. A strict-xfail Target test records that.
2. **A file list naming one path twice is read differently by different readers.**
   - **Before:** a hand-resolved merge conflict leaves `data/final.dvc` listing `survey.csv` twice, with two md5s, and mintd's readers disagree on which entry counts.
   - **After:** every reader stops: `data/final.dvc is cut short or damaged: the file list of final lists a path twice, which dvc never writes`.
   - **What dvc does:** it never writes such a list. Given one, `dvc checkout` silently keeps the last entry (tried with dvc 3.67.1).
3. **`mintd check` reads a producer's pointer at a pin as YAML 1.1.**
   - **Before:** a producer tracks a folder per country, and `dvc add NO` (Norway) writes `path: NO` unquoted. `mintd check --upgrades` read the producer's pointer with PyYAML, took `NO` as the value false, never matched the output, and said it couldn't tell whether it changed.
   - **After:** it reads `NO`, as dvc does.
   - **What dvc does:** it reads and writes YAML 1.2. Tried: `dvc add NO` writes `path: NO`; YAML 1.1 reads `False`, and dvc's reader reads `'NO'`. mintd's local readers already read YAML 1.2.

## Solution
- **The hash check:** `read_cached_dir_manifest` returns None unless the list's bytes hash to its name. Its callers already treat None as "not cached" and fetch or route.
- **The twice-listed check:** one check, `refuse_a_path_listed_twice` in `_dvc_state`, called by every reader of a file list:
  - `_check_out` (the `.dvc` and `dvc.lock` readers);
  - `_listed` (cached and fetched folder lists);
  - pin proof's `_out_entries`;
  - import rescue's read of the producer's pointer;
  - check's `_out_identity`. In check such a list counts as unreadable (`drift_unknown`), never as a pick of one entry.
- **YAML 1.2:** check reads the producer's `.dvc`, `dvc.lock` and `dvc.yaml` at a pin through `_producer_doc` (`load12`).

## Reviewer notes
- **Where to look:** `_dvc_state.py` (`refuse_a_path_listed_twice`, `read_cached_dir_manifest`), then each caller in `check.py`, `_pin_proof.py` and `_import_rescue_ops.py`.
- **Tests, each with a mutation that turns it red:**
  - **Hash check:** a cached list with an entry dropped, and with an md5 swapped. Dropping the comparison turns both red.
  - **Twice-listed check:** a case in each of the `.dvc` and `dvc.lock` parser tables, a cached list, a list from storage, import rescue, pin proof, and check. Making the check a no-op turns all 7 red.
  - **YAML 1.2:** a producer's `NO.dvc`, unchanged (`up_to_date`) and moved (`drift`). Reading it with `yaml.safe_load` again turns both red.
- **The Target:** `test_a_pull_never_returns_normally_with_a_file_its_cached_tree_dropped` is strict-xfail. dvc's fallback pull trusts the read-only list; that's follow-up work.
- **A fixture:** one data-pull fixture filed a cached folder list under a made-up md5. It now uses the md5 of its bytes, as dvc does.
- **Not in this PR, both follow-ups:**
  - import rescue still reads the producer's pointer with PyYAML, the same YAML 1.1 bug as change 3;
  - `imports.py` reads a consumer's own import pointer that way too, so an import kept at a folder named `NO` raises a ValidationError in check.
- **Overlap with #162:** none in meaning. #162 changes how `.dvc/config` remote settings (`version_aware`, `worktree`) are read and refused, in `_storage_state`. This PR changes the readers of file lists, cached folder lists and producer pointers. They share `_dvc_state.py` and `vocab.md`, not functions, and merge cleanly either way.
- **What ran, at `295a6f9`:** `tests/test_check.py`, `test_fast_sync.py`, `test_import_rescue.py`, `test_pin_proof.py`, `test_pointer_cut_short.py`, `test_harness_contract.py`, `test_data_ops.py`, `test_dvc_state.py`, `test_substrate_rules.py`, `test_src_size.py` and `test_test_shards.py`: pass, with the expected xfail above. ruff and mypy pass. Stories: not run locally; CI's stories job runs them at this head.
- **Lines:**
  - Reuse: looked for a YAML 1.2 reader for fetched producer files and a place every file-list reader passes through; used `load12` (wrapped as `_producer_doc`, since `read12` makes an empty file and a parse failure the same None), `_check_out`, `_listed` and `PointerCutShort`. The one new helper is the twice-listed check, which pin proof, import rescue and check call too, because they read file lists past `_check_out`.
  - Size: src/mintd +28/-0 (`check.py` +14, `_dvc_state.py` +9, `_pin_proof.py` +3, `_import_rescue_ops.py` +2), in `tests/src_size_budget/readers-refuse-what-dvc-never-writes.txt`.
  - Vocab: updated (the `_dvc_state` readers paragraph).
  - Skill: no change.

author: aaronepinto
body:
On macOS, Discover finds the PS5 and pairing completes, but **Browse Console Saves** stops with:

```
[error] OSError: [Errno 65] No route to host
[error] download backend exited with status 1
```

This happens with GarlicTransfer switched on under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network**, and after restarting the app.

## Cause

The macOS build runs with `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false`, so electron-builder skips signing and the bundle keeps the linker signature of Electron's prebuilt binary:

```
$ codesign -dv /Applications/GarlicTransfer.app    # v0.3.13 release DMG
Identifier=Electron
CodeDirectory v=20400 size=513 flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed) ...
```

The system log shows Local Network privacy resolving the process by that identifier (`LocalNetwork: found bundle id Electron by PID`). Re-signing the same bundle with its own bundle identifier is enough to make the same traffic succeed (table below), and adding `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` without re-signing is not.

## Change

- `build/mac-sign.cjs`: a `mac.sign` hook that calls electron-builder's own `@electron/osx-sign` with the identity electron-builder found, or ad hoc (`-`) when it found none. The per-file options, `build/entitlements.mac.plist` and hardened runtime are the ones electron-builder passes in.
- `package.json`: `build.mac.sign` points at the hook.
- `tests/mac_sign.test.cjs`: signs ad hoc when there is no identity, keeps an identity that was found, and checks the build configuration uses the hook. The first test fails if the ad hoc fallback is removed.

A Developer ID certificate, if one is configured later, is still used. electron-builder skips signing for pull-request builds, so this only affects the tag and manual builds in `build.yml`.

## Validation

macOS 27.0.1 on Apple silicon, PS5 on firmware 14.23, GarlicTransfer allowed under Local Network.

To test without starting a transfer, I ran a small probe inside each bundle with `open -n -a <app> --env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 --args probe.cjs`, so macOS attributes its traffic to that app. The probe starts a Python child, as the backends do, which sends the DDP `SRCH` query to the PS5 on UDP 1006 (the first packet the download backend sends) and opens a TCP connection to another host on the LAN. The Node process also opens one TCP connection to that host.

| Bundle | Signing identifier | PS5 `SRCH` (Python) | LAN TCP (Python) | LAN TCP (Node) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.3.13 release DMG | `Electron` | No route to host | No route to host | `EHOSTUNREACH` |
| v0.3.13 with `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` added | `Electron` | No route to host | No route to host | `EHOSTUNREACH` |
| v0.3.13 re-signed ad hoc | `com.earthonion.garlictransfer` | `HTTP/1.1 200 Ok` | ok | ok |
| This branch, built with the CI command | `com.earthonion.garlictransfer` | `HTTP/1.1 200 Ok` | ok | ok |
| This branch, app inside the built DMG | `com.earthonion.garlictransfer` | `HTTP/1.1 200 Ok` | ok | ok |

- Built with `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false npx electron-builder --mac --publish never`, as in `build.yml`. The log shows `executing custom sign ... identity=none`. `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes. The app and its four helpers are signed as `com.earthonion.garlictransfer` and `com.earthonion.garlictransfer.helper[.GPU|.Plugin|.Renderer]`, with the entitlements from `build/entitlements.mac.plist`. The app is universal (x86_64, arm64).
- The built app starts normally: the main, GPU, network and renderer processes keep running and no crash report is written.
- `npm run check`, `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` (534 passed, 2 skipped), `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` (121 tests OK) and `git diff --check`.

With the v0.3.13 build, downloading and uploading a GTA VI save on this Mac worked only when the app was started from Terminal, which applies Terminal's Local Network permission instead.

Not tested: a full Browse and Upload on the PS5 with this build, and a Mac on which GarlicTransfer has never been allowed under Local Network.

author: nittin-murthi
body:
Part 7 of the DiskGraph-only OmniSage stack. Depends on #536.

## Summary

Add a DiskGraph end-to-end test that exercises all six OmniSage data requirements in one model batch. Query graphs use scored walks. Supplied positives, neighbors drawn by score, and positives drawn from future actions each get a graph at the owning query's cutoff. Graphs expose fixed-shape feature columns and point-in-time degrees. The runner reads Parquet datasets and anchor tables through local files or S3.

The comparison loader calls the same native DiskGraph sampler on the same immutable index. It preloads the example's static vectors, primary-key map and anchor columns into RAM, then samples temporal neighborhoods and degrees per batch. Both loaders are checked against the input Parquet rows. Their random selections can differ.

The training check directly imports Pinterest's `GraphSageV6AlphaTransformerAggregator` from an external checkout of `omnisage/model.py`. Recorded runs used revision `4cd0d60676803bbb1ded4897df94d459e663674e`, a one-layer, 32-wide CPU configuration, and a benchmark-specific in-batch contrastive loss with SGD. This measures the data path and a training step. The three-objective training benchmark follows in the next PR. [Pinned Pinterest model](https://github.com/pinterest/atg-research/blob/4cd0d60676803bbb1ded4897df94d459e663674e/omnisage/model.py)

## Change map

[Review the file-by-file change map.](https://github.com/NVIDIA/kumo-engine/pull/537#issuecomment-7173100285)

## Testing Done

An independent full-epoch oracle checked keys, candidate offsets, scored edges, fixed vectors and degrees against each anchor time. The end-to-end tests exercised local Parquet and loopback S3, and a separate S3 check verified index reuse. The historical focused regression run passed 112 tests.

Recorded synthetic CPU results used 32,768 Pins, 4,096 anchors, one DiskGraph thread and loopback Moto S3. The custom loader preloaded 150 MiB of arrays. Following one warmup epoch, the loaders ran five alternating warm trials. Throughput is anchors per second.

| Batch size | Package loader | Custom loader | Package with training | Custom with training |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 953 | 2,142 | 286 | 344 |
| 64 | 1,040 | 2,270 | 313 | 368 |

The benchmark and tests are in the diff. These measurements were recorded separately in `omnisage-end-to-end-benchmarks.json`. To reproduce from `packages/experimental/kumo-pytorch`, set `PINTEREST_ATG` to the pinned checkout and run:

```sh
python -m tests.e2e.omnisage_throughput --storage s3 --model-file "$PINTEREST_ATG/omnisage/model.py"
```

## Checklist

- [x] Breaking changes reviewed. This PR adds a benchmark and tests.
- [x] Added the benchmark invocation to the package README.
- [x] Added local and S3 end-to-end correctness coverage.

author: bh5msu-coder

_Requested by **Brad** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01XJiGoqYPqTnKtzFhEEWahQ?thread=cmsg_01XJiGoqYPqTnKtzFhEEWahQ2cy471hSv75ktkrsJ8cudk)_

## Why

The intro from #9 only rendered on the sign-in screen and only once per device, so anyone already signed in never saw it.

## What

- **Intro on every open.** `<Intro />` now sits above every screen in `PoolApp` (loading, sign-in, the pool). It plays once per browser session (`sessionStorage`), so a reload or the sign-in redirect does not replay it, but each new open of the site or the installed app does. Still tap-to-skip, and still skipped for reduced motion and data saver.
- **Wide screens.** The clip is portrait, so on landscape windows it is shown whole and centred instead of cropped.
- **Install app.** New `InstallApp` component on the sign-in screen and in the menu (replaces the iPhone-only tip). Chrome and Edge get a one-click "Install app" button via `beforeinstallprompt`. Safari on Mac gets "File, then Add to Dock"; iPhone gets "Share, then Add to Home Screen". Hidden when already running installed.

The branch includes a no-content merge of the old #9 branch history so it could be pushed without a force push.

## Checks

- `tsc --noEmit`, eslint on `src/components`, and vitest (269 tests) pass.
- Local dev server in Chromium at 1280x800: intro plays over both the signed-in app (demo mode) and the sign-in screen, removes itself, does not replay on reload, and plays again in a new session. A simulated `beforeinstallprompt` shows the button, clicking it calls `prompt()`, and the button then goes away.
- Not tested: a real install in Chrome or Safari on a Mac, a real iPhone, or the wide-screen layout after the last CSS change.

author: zz-plant
body:
## Why

Production holds 1 of the 11 secrets the Worker reads (`WHETHER_CRON_SECRET`). Since 2026-11-02:

- every one of the 22 `whether-regime-history-refresh` runs, and `brief-freeze-2026-11-23`, errored with `GITHUB_TOKEN is not configured`. `data/published_briefs.json` stops at w46.
- the failure notice could not go out, because `WHETHER_OPS_EMAIL` is unset.
- `/api/health` answered `"status":"ok"`, because it only judges the data.

## What changes

- **`lib/runtime/deploymentSecrets.ts`** lists every secret the Worker reads and what is lost without each one. Each secret is required by the lane switch it serves: `GITHUB_TOKEN` wherever a data Workflow is switched on, `WHETHER_OPS_EMAIL` wherever the lane has the `EMAIL` binding. A Worker Preview or a dev server switches neither on, so it never reports a missing secret.
- **`lib/delivery/runOutcomes.ts`** records how each run last ended (both crons and both Workflows) under `ops:last-run:<run>`. It stores failed step names only, never the error text, because `/api/health` is public. Records expire after 14 days.
- **`/api/health`** adds:
  - `dependencies.automation`: `ok`, `unconfigured`, `failing` or `unknown`
  - `missingSecrets`
  - `failingRuns`

  `unconfigured` and `failing` both make the overall status `degraded` (still HTTP 200).
- **`bun run secrets:check`** compares the list with `wrangler secret list`, judged against production's switches in `cloudflare.config.ts`. It exits 1 when a required secret is missing; against production today it names `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `WHETHER_OPS_EMAIL`.
- **Docs:** the runbook now points to the list and the script. Its VAPID section described the push feature removed in #1833, so it is deleted.

## Verification

- `bun run check`: all tasks pass; 4,075 tests across 502 files.
- New tests: `tests/deploymentSecrets.test.ts` (production requires exactly those two secrets, a Preview requires none), `tests/runOutcomes.test.ts`, and three new cases in `tests/apiHealthRoute.test.ts`.
- Ran `bun run secrets:check` against production: exit 1, with the two required secrets listed as missing.

## After merge

Production's `/api/health` will report `degraded` / `unconfigured` until the two secrets are set:

```
npx wrangler secret put GITHUB_TOKEN --name whether
npx wrangler secret put WHETHER_OPS_EMAIL --name whether
```

author: labcoder
body:
The Windows anchor lookup behind `hold_product_folder` and `profile_root` checked the held anchor, then opened the child by its absolute path. The held handles don't deny rename, so between that check and the open the path could be redirected to a replacement folder. A `Missing` result could then describe the replacement, not the admitted anchor.

**Change**
- A new `open_child` opens the name with `NtCreateFile`, relative to the held anchor handle. It requests the same access, sharing and no-follow as the path open did. `check()` still compares the child's final path with the expected one, so a moved anchor is refused rather than yielding a held child.
- Only `STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND` and `STATUS_NO_SUCH_FILE` count as absent. Every other status is an opaque failure, since translating a status first folds unrelated ones, such as a missing object ID, into not-found.
- Storage's `windows-sys` gains the `Wdk_Foundation` and `Wdk_Storage_FileSystem` features. `Cargo.lock` is unchanged.

The architecture note says how the child is opened.

**Checks** (reviewed locally, on main)
- `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy -p kumochi-storage --all-targets -- -D warnings` on Linux, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (also with `gate-identity`, and release lib) and `aarch64-apple-darwin`
- New tests: one moves the held anchor and plants a replacement holding another child, and checks that the held folder's own child opens while the planted one is not found; the other checks which statuses count as absence.

author: sagzy
body:
no ref

The "Migration export (SQLite → MySQL)" check has failed on every pull request since Ghost 6.79.0 was released, with `user_accounts: row differs`. It fails on unrelated changes too, e.g. https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost-CLI/pull/2480 and https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost-CLI/pull/2481.

## Why it fails

The check installs the latest Ghost, exports its SQLite database, loads the export into MySQL and compares every row.

Ghost 6.79.0 added the Better Auth tables, whose date columns are `DATETIME(3)` in MySQL. MySQL prints those with three fractional digits, while the check expected every date at second precision:

```
actual:   2026-11-25 18:06:20.000
expected: 2026-11-25 18:06:20
```

So the first row with such a column never matched.

## The fix

The check now reads each column's `DATETIME_PRECISION` from `information_schema` and compares dates at that precision. Columns without fractional seconds are compared as before.

The precision has to come from MySQL: Knex creates a `dateTime` column with a precision as a plain `datetime` on SQLite, so the SQLite file doesn't carry it.

## What this doesn't change

The export itself is untouched. It still writes dates stored as epoch milliseconds or ISO strings at second precision, as it does for every other date, so the milliseconds Ghost stores in these new columns on SQLite are dropped on the way to MySQL. The data loads, and the difference is under a second on fields like a session's expiry, but it may be worth a follow-up if those values should survive exactly.

author: jonathanong
body:
## Problem

`vouchington storybook-browser-runner` kills a stalled suite with `no semantic test progress for 120000ms; terminating terminal mid-suite stall`, but nothing says which story module or test was running. In vouchington/vouchington run 45676922101 (job 139430845661, `storybook`), the last marker was seq 1401, the module-end of `design-system/scroll-area.stories.tsx`, and the renderer was at 43% CPU. The hung story could not be identified, so the stall could not be fixed downstream.

## Change

- New bounded `ProgressTracker` reads every progress marker line (not just the latest per chunk) and keeps the last 10 markers, the modules that started but did not end (cap 64 tracked, 10 reported), the running test per module, and the last ended module.
- On a semantic stall the watchdog logs one JSON line before SIGTERM and records the same line in the diagnostics artifact:
  `[storybook-browser] semantic stall in flight: {"hangMs":120000,"collectedNotStarted":[],"inFlight":[{"module":"...","runningForMs":120000,"test":{"name":"...","runningForMs":120000}}],"lastEnded":{"endedAgoMs":120000,"module":"..."},"recentMarkers":[{"agoMs":..,"event":"..","module":"..","seq":..,"test":".."}]}`
- `createVitestStorybookProgressReporter` also emits `test-start` / `test-end` markers (test name capped at 160 chars, marker still under 512 bytes). They name the running test only and are not progress: `latestStorybookProgressSequence` still matches only `module-*`.
- Not changed: the 120s threshold, retries (a semantic stall is still not retryable), and what counts as progress. Progress was not wrong; it was just not attributed.

Limitation: if a stall happens before the next module's `module-start` (for example while it loads), no module is in flight, and the line shows `lastEnded` plus `recentMarkers` only. `collectedNotStarted` names modules that were collected but not started.

## Evidence

Reference: vouchington run 45676922101. Unit tests cover the tracker (in-flight, test-end, bounds, replay, split lines, bad escapes), the reporter markers, and an end-to-end stall that checks the stderr line and the written diagnostics file. `pnpm run lint`, `typecheck` pass; all 687 test files pass; the new files are 100% covered.

Includes changeset and README note.
