Based on one observed case. Not yet verified after deployment. A router that reports neither field would show every device as not connected.

body:

_Requested by **Juanra** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BP5zdXXtjWJBjLwvcstqMy?thread=cmsg_01BP5zdXXtjWJBjLwvcstqMyFBcVYbxopCgouPo8ZVmHaJ)_

## Qué cambia
Velocidad de reacción pasa a ser una escena, construida desde la plantilla común v1.1 con los bocetos v2b aprobados:

- **Reacción**: balón de vidrio sobre placa con termostato, termómetro y cronómetro que se para al terminar; el balón se tiñe con C (gas de color). Modelo en círculo de radio 222, panel de estado con la curva de velocidades y la tira de velocidad de toda la reacción.
- **Comparar**: dos balones con su modelo, mando de la variable bajo cada uno, «Igual en los dos» y sello «¡TERMINA ANTES!».
- **Choque**: moléculas grandes que se giran arrastrando, panel con las dos condiciones y «Tus choques».
- Retos (5) y álbum de 6 sellos, con `?retos=1`. Mismos parámetros de URL.
- Física igual (Eₐ, orientación, catalizador) en el círculo; reloj simulado reescalado una vez (22 pasos = 1 s).
- Símbolos: división «/», multiplicación «·». Solo en español (traducciones aparte).

## Pruebas
`probar.mjs` (escritorio 1366 y móvil 390, cuatro temas, cinco idiomas): sin errores de consola ni desbordes. Comprobado también girar y lanzar en Choque, los tres modos de Comparar y 57 fps con 30 A, 30 B y 6 K.

## Nota
El reto «sin catalizador en menos de 60 s» no es alcanzable (la vía térmica tarda minutos simulados), así que pasa a «en menos de 30 s» (con catalizadores) y «lo mismo con temperatura Baja o menos».

author: the-goat-solution
body:
## What changes

The evidence for step 11 (`TENANT_SCOPE=enforce`) was failing and couldn't see it (audit C0), and it covered too little of the app (C0b). This fixes the evidence. The 7-day clock restarts after this merges **and** migrations `0012` and `0013` have run on production.

**The report (`scripts/shadow-report.mjs`)**
- A day is clean only when **every** check (`settings`, `routing`, `tenant-reads`) has a clean result that day and none has a `differ` or an `unavailable` one. Before, a day counted as clean when any one check was clean, and `unavailable` was ignored.
- A day with nothing recorded isn't clean. Today is left out until its heartbeat has run.
- `--since YYYY-MM-DD` (the day the clock started) and `--need N` (default 7). Exit code 0 only when the gate is met.

**The daily heartbeat (`lib/shadow-log.ts`, roster cron)**
- The row-level-security probe skips a club-owned table whose migration hasn't run yet, and names it on the record (`skipped`). Before, one missing table made the whole check `unavailable`. `verify.mjs`, run after every migration, still reports a missing table as a problem.
- The probe gets the unscoped pool. Under `enforce` the cron's scoped pool made the "no club named" half see the club's rows: a false alarm every day (audit, Medium).
- With the app's own login (`APP_DATABASE_URL`) there is no owner to compare with, so the probe checks from the inside: no row of another club with the club named, none with no club named.

**Shadow reads (`lib/database.ts`)**
- In `shadow` mode, Drizzle's reads (`orm()`, every repository) and reads on connections from `sql.connect()` (transactions) are now sampled and compared like `sql\`…\`` and `sql.query()`. The statements themselves run exactly as before, once, as the owner.
- A comparison started from a held connection never waits on the pool: it only runs when a connection is spare at that moment, otherwise it is skipped. A test holds every connection and proves nothing hangs (it caught one real hang while I wrote this: the club-id lookup).

**What members could notice:** nothing functional. In production (`TENANT_SCOPE=shadow`) one in ten Drizzle and transaction reads now also runs the comparison, as one in ten plain reads already does.

**Not merged without the owner's OK**, because it changes the database client every production request uses.

## Checks

- `tests/shadow-log.test.ts`: 9 new verdict tests, including production's state on 25 Nov (settings `differ`, probe `unavailable`, routing clean → not a clean day).
- `tests/tenant-scope.test.ts`: missing table (probe reports, heartbeat skips and records it); scoped pool gives the false alarm, unscoped doesn't; the probe from a login with no rights; shadow covers Drizzle, Drizzle transactions and `connect()`; no deadlock with the pool exhausted.
- Full `pnpm --filter web test` locally: everything passes except `schema drift`, which needs Postgres 18 (local is 16; CI runs it). Typecheck and lint clean.
- Nothing was run against production.

## Availability

- [ ] This ships or changes something people can use, and I updated its line in `apps/site/content/availability.ts` (and the wording that depends on it). The Luvallplay website's badges and status notes read from that list.
- [x] Not applicable: nothing user-facing became available, limited or unavailable.

author: rayakame
body:
The hub now releases through the shared workflows from `libre-bots/.github` v0.1.0.

- `release.yml`: run `release` on `main` and pick `patch`, `minor` or `major`, optionally as a release candidate. `prepare` checks that `CI Done` is green, computes the version, builds and tests the Python client and the image (amd64 and arm64), and creates the tag. `pypi` uploads the client with trusted publishing from the `release` environment. `finish` attests and tags the image, writes the GitHub release, and checks PyPI and GHCR.
- `ci.yml`: `CI Done` uses the shared action. Runs on `main` are grouped per commit, so a pending run is never cancelled. Actions are pinned to commits, and every job only reads.
- `image.yml` is gone; the image is built by the release.
- The client's version in `pyproject.toml` is `0.0.0`; the release sets the real one.
- Release note categories, the shared Renovate preset, and a short Releases section in the README.

Before the first release, PyPI needs a pending trusted publisher for `librebots-hub` (workflow `release.yml`, environment `release`) and the repository needs the `release` environment.

author: consolexe-lucifer
body:
## Bugfix: устаревшая обложка при переключении треков (P1/P2 исправлены, работа приостановлена)

Связан с Issue [#6](https://github.com/consolexe-lucifer/ConsoleXAll-Rust/issues/6). Обновление **существующего Draft PR #9**; новых PR/Issues нет, merge не выполнялся.

**HEAD:** `848ea03158b9a2a0680668ad7390f401529ff98e`
**Статус:** работа приостановлена до завтра. P1/P2 из последней проверки Codex исправлены, тесты/сборки проходят; ждём повторной проверки.

### P1 — чужая обложка после выхода из pending

Причина: проверка «хэш принадлежит другому треку» выполнялась только в `pending`. После подтверждения A возврат к A и поздний thumbnail B принимались как новая картинка.

Исправление: защита от известных чужих/stale thumbnail работает и для уже подтверждённой текущей обложки — поздний чужой thumbnail отклоняется, не заменяет и не скрывает корректную обложку. Действительно новая картинка того же трека (неизвестный хэш) по-прежнему принимается.

### P2 — общая обложка после вытеснения истории

Причина: история хранила только `track_key → hash`; при вытеснении записи A (общая обложка с B) возврат к A не находил подтверждения, а B считался чужим треком, поэтому правильная общая обложка отклонялась бесконечно.

Исправление: запись истории теперь содержит `track_key + hash + album + source`. Хэш, подтверждённый для другого трека того же альбома/источника, считается допустимой общей обложкой; чужие уникальные обложки по-прежнему отклоняются. Лимит истории 16 не увеличивался.

Оба дефекта сначала воспроизведены падающими тестами на HEAD `c94835c`:
`returned_track_survives_late_thumbnail_of_another_track`,
`shared_album_cover_is_accepted_after_history_eviction`.
После исправления проходят, добавлены тест на вытеснение уникальной обложки и published-`MediaState` тест на поздний чужой thumbnail.

### Сохранённое поведение

- Абсолютные быстрые проверки 0/250/700/1500 мс, медленная проверка ~10 с, force по `MediaPropertiesChanged`.
- Pending-заглушка, same-album без мерцания, A → B → A / A → B → C → A, смена источника, отсутствующий/битый thumbnail, поздняя правильная обложка.
- Декодирование только при смене байтов; WinRT в worker; UI не блокируется.
- Rust 1.80.

### Проверки

| Команда | Результат |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check` | exit 0 |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| `cargo test` | **160 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored** |
| `cargo build --release` | успешно |
| `cargo +1.80.0 check --locked` | успешно |

author: noise64
body:
Fixes for the review of #1 on `golem-bash-tool`.

- External commands: the arguments, `argv[0]`, the program path and the exported values go to the OS as the bytes the shell value stands for (`rawbytes::to_os_string`), in `compose_std_command`, so `exec` gets the same. Before, a value from `$'\xff'` reached `env printf` and `env` as the marker character `f4 8f bf bf`.
- `[[ =~ ]]` with a back-reference: the match is on the shell string, so its captures are copied as they are. Before, each raw byte in `BASH_REMATCH` was decoded a second time and became four marker characters. The other match path still decodes, because it matches the encoded bytes.
- Arithmetic read and assignment through a nameref to an element (`declare -n r='a[i]'`; `$((r))`, `(( r += 1 ))`, `let`) go through `read_element` and the element assignment, so the subscript is evaluated with its side effects, and an associative key stays as written. Before, `i`, `i+1` and `j++` read and wrote element 0.
- `return` builds without `builtin.exit`: the status operand helper moved to `status_operand.rs`, enabled by either feature. The two features stay independent.
- A heredoc delimiter inside `$( )` is unquoted with `tokenizer::unquote_str`, as the shell does. Before, every backslash and quote was removed, so `<<E\\F` looked for `EF` and read past the closing `)`, and `<<'A"B'` did not parse.
- The substitution printer prints a connection's commands from a work list, and `Command` has a `Drop` that frees a chain of connections from a work list. Printing or freeing a long flat list or pipeline (`$( :; :; … )`, `declare -f`) no longer overflows the stack. `connect_async` no longer moves the chain by recursion.

Checks on Linux x86_64, toolchain 1.98.1, oracle GNU bash 5.2.37 on the same host:

- each new test fails on `518bd2f0` and passes here: the compat cases for raw-byte arguments and values, raw-byte back-reference captures, the nameref subscript in reads and in assignments, and the heredoc delimiters; the `regex.rs` and `word.rs` unit cases; the `comsub.rs` long-list test, which also fails with the work-list printer and a recursive drop
- `cargo check -p brush-builtins --no-default-features --features builtin.return`: fails on `518bd2f0`, passes here; `builtin.exit` alone and both together pass
- `cargo test --test brush-compat-tests`: the same failing and known-failing set as on `518bd2f0`, plus the new cases, which pass
- `cargo test -p brush-parser --lib` and `cargo test -p brush-core --lib`: pass
- `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip2 -p brush-shell --no-default-features --features minimal` under wasmtime 51: the heredoc forms and a 20000-command flat list match bash
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean; `cargo clippy --no-deps` reports nothing in the changed files. The `too_many_lines` and other errors it reports in `declare.rs`, `hash.rs`, `read.rs`, `expansion.rs`, `interp.rs`, `env.rs` and `callstack.rs` are also on `518bd2f0`

Not changed: a long `elif` chain is nested, not flat, and its printing still recurses. Bash 5.2.37 on this host rejects 20000 `elif`s with a syntax error.

## Self-review fixes

Parser and tokenizer:

- `case` in a substitution is read only where a command starts. The check looks for `case` first, so long words and many adjacent quoted fragments no longer take quadratic time
- arithmetic subscripts are read without recursion, and tokenizer nesting and here-document nesting are bounded, so deep nesting fails before the stack runs out
- a trailing backslash waits for more input. Quoted braces in a command in braces are ignored. A `case` pattern after a terminator is read as a pattern. The lookahead for a process substitution reports its errors
- a `$(...)` or `${ cmd; }` inside arithmetic is read as commands, and the arithmetic state is restored after every nested expansion, so `(( x = $((a)) << 2 ))` is a shift, not a here-document
- source text keeps its line continuations as bash does. Line-continuation removal in `[[ =~ ]]` and similar words takes the ends of `$(`, `$((`, `$[`, `${`, `${ cmd; }` and an in-word `<(`/`>(` from the tokenizer, scans each body on its own, and skips comments. A comment starts after a blank or an operator character, as in the tokenizer. The source offset table is built when first needed

Raw bytes, as bash keeps them:

- file names, `printf`, scripts and their names, arguments, the environment, tilde expansion, the default `HISTFILE`, `PATH` directories (also `type -P`, `command -v`, `.` and `compgen -c`) and `hash` listings. On WASI, `PATH` is split on bytes
- bytes that make a character are joined into it, in values and in patterns, as one run across all pattern pieces, including empty quoted pieces

Other:

- `PIPESTATUS` is kept across a trap action
- a persistent output substitution keeps running without a job scope
- printing an `elif` does not copy the clauses after it

Checks, with GNU bash 5.2.37 as the oracle on the same host:

- each new compat case fails on the head before its fix and passes here; the new cases match bash, and `declare -f` of them matches bash
- the full compat suite, with SIGINT and SIGQUIT reset, has the same non-passing set as before plus the new cases, which pass
- `cargo test -p brush-parser --lib` (including the stack-depth test) and `cargo test -p brush-core --lib`: pass
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `cargo clippy` reports nothing new; brush-parser is clean. One commit, `Read a process substitution in a word when removing line continuations`, has a `too_many_lines` error on its own, which the next commit removes
- the `wasm32-wasip2` minimal release build has no warnings and runs the new cases under wasmtime as bash does

Not changed:

- bash also matches a lone byte against part of a character (`[[ é == $a* ]]`); brush does not
- bash quotes the path and name in `hash -l`; brush does not
- bash counts parentheses inside `${...}` within `$((...))`; brush's tokenizer does not
- on WASI, a bare `wait` does not wait for a process substitution, because it is not a job
- the line-continuation scanner decides whether an in-word `<(` is a process substitution with its own copy of the tokenizer's rule, reads a `<(...)` at the start of a word as plain text, and does not track a `((...))` command inside a `$(...)`

Commits use plain subjects without the Conventional Commits prefix or Assisted-by trailer that CONTRIBUTING asks for.

author: aliromman
body:
# Three fair dice that neither of the proposed moves can change

Roll any two of these eight-sided dice. Each wins exactly 32 of the 64 possible rolls.

| Die | Face labels |
|---|---|
| A | 1, 2, 7, 12, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| B | 3, 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 22 |
| C | 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 17, 23, 24 |

Injo Hur and Yeansu Kim conjectured that two operations suffice to turn every fair triple into repetitions of a six-letter palindrome such as `ABCCBA`. For these dice, neither operation can even make a first change. This disproves Conjecture 1 of their journal article, numbered 3.5 in the preprint. [Journal article, §3](https://doi.org/10.1155/2021/6648248) · [Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.12866)

## Why the word is isolated

Read the die names in order of increasing face label.

```text
AABCCCABBCCABBBBCAAAABCC
```

The first operation exchanges a neighboring pair `xy` and a neighboring pair `yx` elsewhere. The only transitions between different letters in this word are `AB`, `BC`, and `CA`. None occurs in reverse.

The second operation slides a permutation of `ABC` across an adjacent segment containing equal numbers of all three letters. To check all possible slides, record the two differences $(\#A-\#C,\#B-\#C)$ after each prefix. A segment has equal counts exactly when the differences are the same at its two ends.

| Three-letter block | Number of letters before the block | Prefix differences there | All prefix lengths with those differences |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| ABC | 1 | $(1,0)$ | 1, 4 |
| CAB | 5 | $(0,-1)$ | 5, 8 |
| CAB | 10 | $(-1,-1)$ | 10, 13 |
| BCA | 15 | $(-1,1)$ | 15, 18 |
| ABC | 20 | $(1,1)$ | 20, 23 |

These are all the three-letter permutations in the word. Each row gives just the two ends of its block. A slide across a nonempty segment needs a third occurrence of the same differences. The word therefore stays fixed. It starts with two equal letters, whereas every proposed block starts with two different letters. The same obstruction works even if the order of the letters can change from block to block.

## Source and verification

Related work gives algorithms for listing words with the same scattered pair counts. Hur and Kim ask whether their two particular moves can connect fair triples. Searches for the conjecture, its moves, and this example found no prior refutation. OpenAI Codex found the word by searching cyclic sequences of letter runs and formalized the proof. [Lejeune, Rigo and Rosenfeld on pair-count equivalence](https://www.lirmm.fr/~mrosenfeld/LejeuneRigoRosenfeld.pdf)

From the repository root, run

```sh
lake exe cache get
lake build conjectures.HurKimFairDice.Solution
lake env leanchecker conjectures.HurKimFairDice.Solution
```

author: piercypixel
body:
Follow-up to #9042. That change merged the Guardrails calls around a held tool call into one circle and one card with titles of its own ("Checked what's allowed", "Guardrails step"). The row no longer matched the calls the session made, and the card hid what each call sent and got back.

It builds on #11268, which is merged; the diff here is the Guardrails work only.

## What changes

- **One circle per call, in order.** Each Guardrails call is its own circle again, under its real tool name, with the request and result it carried. The grouping code and its tests are removed.
- **A blocked call is shown as that call.** When the policy blocks a call, the proxy hands the client a `get_remedy_plans` call in its place, with the blocked call and the ruling as its arguments. Chat shows that step as the call the model tried: its tool name and icon, the arguments the model sent, a "Blocked" state, and the notice's result as the model got it. A `get_remedy_plans` call that carries no notice stays an ordinary call.
- **Guardrails calls carry the Guardrails mark** on their circle, and their results wrap to the card.
- **A notice that is still arriving shows nothing** until it names the call it blocked, so the row never shows a circle under the notice's own name first. A notice that failed, or was cut off when its turn ended, keeps the blocked call's name and shows that state instead of "Blocked". This holds where a blocked call gets a card of its own too, such as a call a subagent made.
- **The approval request reads as a question.** It was laid out as a tool call card under the remedy call that waits for it, and read as a second call. It now asks "Run `<tool>`?", shows the arguments and what approving also accepts, and takes Approve or Deny.

The blocked call is detected from the notice's fields only (`tool`, `arguments`, `ruling`, `notice`). Chat does not parse the ruling's text.

## Where it sits

```text
ChatMessages
  └─ identifyCompactToolGroups      no remedy-chain grouping any more
       └─ CompactToolGroup          one circle per stored call
            ├─ circle               getBlockedAttempt(part) -> target tool name, "Blocked"
            └─ card
                 ├─ BlockedAttemptCard   for a denial notice
                 └─ ExpandedToolCard     for every other call

McpElicitationCard
  └─ OpenappaReviewToolCard         question layout for an approval request
```

## Flows

A held call, as stored and as shown:

```text
model          LLM proxy (policy)         Chat row
  │ call tool X     │                        │
  ├────────────────>│ blocked                │
  │                 │ replaces the call with │
  │                 │ get_remedy_plans{tool: X, arguments, ruling, notice}
  │                 ├───────────────────────>│ circle "X (blocked)", card: X, Request, Blocked
  │ execute_remedy_plan(offer_id, plan)      │
  ├────────────────>├───────────────────────>│ circle "execute remedy plan"
  │ call tool X again                        │
  ├────────────────>├───────────────────────>│ circle "X"
```

A plan that needs a person:

```text
model          Guardrails runtime        Chat                       person
  │ execute_remedy_plan │                   │                          │
  ├────────────────────>│ review request    │                          │
  │                     ├──────────────────>│ circle: running          │
  │                     │                   │ question: Run `X`?       │
  │                     │                   │<─────────────────────────┤ Approve or Deny
  │                     │ answer            │                          │
  │                     │<──────────────────┤                          │
  │ result              │                   │ circle: Approved by you / Denied by you
```

## How it was exercised

On a local stack with a mock MCP server and policy rules that hold its tools in six ways, in live chats with a real model:

- two plans offered, each one chosen; an approval approved and denied; a call with no plan offered; three held calls in one turn; five parallel calls of mixed outcome; a narrowing followed by a blocked public post; an untrusted read followed by a blocked payment; a run stopped mid-call; a 14-circle turn.
- In every chat the row lists the calls in the order the session made them, a blocked call appears directly as "(blocked)" with no intermediate label, and each card shows that call's own request and result.
- 448 generated sessions (odd notice shapes, script and markup payloads in rulings and tool names, 40-circle rows) loaded into the built page at 1280 px and 390 px: no crash, no injected markup, no overflow.

`root-remedy-flow.spec.ts` is updated for the new row and card.

## Not in this PR

- After a sanitizer plan, the card shows the tool's raw result while the model receives the sanitized one.
- A review that nobody answers leaves the remedy call reading "Completed".

author: kim-em
body:
This PR removes `@[simp]` from ten rewriting lemmas about `f4ModularChevalleyBasis` in `TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/F4/ModularLattice.lean`, and adds an implementation note saying why.

Each of these lemmas had 36,800 to 53,694 discrimination-tree keys, because the reducible F₄ carrier types in their implicit arguments unfold into a large tree. Lean 4.37 stores each module's global simp lemmas in a per-module summary in the olean (lean4 PR 15923), and for this module that summary held a chain of 53,714 linked cells. The `leantar` bundled with v4.37.0-rc1 packs and unpacks recursively, so it needed about 14 MiB of stack to pack and 11 MiB to unpack this module. With the default 8 MiB stack, `lake exe cache get` and `lake build` segfault (exit 139) on this module for every outside user and fall back to rebuilding it. TauCeti CI raises the stack, so it never showed up here.

After this change the deepest chain in the module's olean is 131 cells deep, the olean shrinks from 5.7 MB to 0.4 MB, and the bundled `leantar` packs and unpacks it at a 256 KiB stack with a byte-identical round trip. No file used these lemmas through bare `simp`. Every use names them explicitly, and all 53 modules that import `ModularLattice` transitively build unchanged with `--iofail`.

Roadmap: none

Quality pass:
- Q1 Mathlib duplicates: n/a - no declaration is added; ten existing theorems only lose the `@[simp]` attribute.
- Q2 Tau Ceti duplicates, on main and in open PRs: n/a - no declaration is added.
- Q3 Hypotheses: n/a - no statement changes.
- Q4 Section variables: n/a - no statement changes.
- Q5 Proofs of at most 50 lines: n/a - no proof changes.

author: math280h
body:
Two desktop tests failed now and then in CI. Both came from bugs in the app.

**A change from outside during a save could be lost.** The desktop app writes a file through a temp file and a rename (`electron/storage/file-queue.ts`).
- A write by another program just before the rename was replaced by the app's file, with no notice.
- A write just after the rename went unseen. The app took the size and change time of the file after the rename, so the outside file looked like its own.
- A read had the same gap.

The fix:
- The app now takes the size and change time of the temp file before the rename, and of a file before it reads it.
- Just before the rename, a write compares the file with that record. If another program changed the content, the app keeps that file, doesn't write, and treats it as a change from outside. The open diagram then loads it, or offers "Load newer" or "Review", by the existing rules. The picked folder of the website already works this way.
- Saves from a save dialog still replace the file.

**A GIF export could contain blank frames after a GPU restart.** In a macOS CI run, the GPU process crashed during a GIF export, and the last three frames came out fully transparent. The main process accepted any frame with readable marker squares.
- The capture service now counts GPU process restarts and doesn't reuse a capture window after one.
- A frame counts only if no restart happened during its capture and, on an opaque background, every pixel is opaque.
- Otherwise the app renders the frame again in a new capture window, up to 3 times, and then stops the export with an error instead of writing a blank frame.

New tests:
- unit tests for the save record and the kept change;
- a desktop e2e test that renders the next video frame in a new capture window after a GPU process restart.


**The macOS menu Reload test** polled the page with `window.evaluate` while the page reloaded. Playwright rejects an evaluate during a navigation, and the poll then failed at once instead of trying again. The poll now counts that rejection as the old page.

author: solareco86-ai
body:
> **Borrador apilado. Cambia el comportamiento de los parsers: requiere revisión explícita.** Depende de #306 (extractor con OCR opcional)
> y #310 (módulo de formatos). Su base es la rama `integracion/issue-197-base-formatos` (= `develop` + esos dos cambios), para que el diff
> muestre **solo esta entrega**. Cuando #306 y #310 estén en `develop`, se cambia la base a `develop`. No se debe mergear antes.

### Contexto

Séptima entrega del desglose modular del PR #299 (issue #197), que se mantiene abierto solo como referencia. Conecta las conversiones
estrictas de #310 al extractor en memoria y a los parsers de archivos de EDELAP y CAMMESA.

### Cambio de comportamiento (sin minimizar)

Un valor mal formado ya no se acepta con un valor equivocado ni escapa como `ValueError`: se rechaza con `FacturaDistribuidoraIlegibleError`
(el router lo traduce a 422). Alcanza al **extractor en memoria** (texto nativo y OCR) **y a los parsers de archivos de EDELAP y de CAMMESA**,
que comparten las conversiones (también el script de importación que los usa).

| Valor | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|
| Importe con miles mal agrupados (`29.53.270,32`, `12.34`, `1.2345,67`) | se aceptaba **en silencio con otro valor** (`29.53.270,32` → `2.953.270,32`) | 422 |
| Magnitud en kW `800.` o `.5` | aceptada | 422 |
| Días facturados `0` | aceptado | 422 |
| Número de factura `-`, `--`, `123456-` | devuelto tal cual | 422 |
| Período con mes fuera de 01–12 | aceptado | 422 |
| `1.2.3`, `.`, cadena vacía, varios separadores | `ValueError` sin traducir (500) | 422 |

No cambia el DTO, la API ni el flujo del OCR; los campos opcionales ausentes siguen en `None`. En CAMMESA los textos ya llegan filtrados por un
regex numérico (`[\d.]+(,\d{1,2})?`), por lo que el cambio alcanza solo a números con miles mal agrupados.

### Archivos (298 líneas)

| Archivo | Líneas |
|---|---|
| `src/infrastructure/pdfplumber/extractor_factura_en_memoria.py` | +15/−9 |
| `src/infrastructure/pdfplumber/parser_factura_distribuidora.py` | +18/−28 (se eliminan las tres conversiones antiguas, sin validación) |
| `tests/unit/test_extractor_factura_en_memoria.py` | +112 |
| `tests/unit/test_parser_factura_distribuidora.py` | +62 |
| `tests/unit/test_facturas_router.py` | +54 |

### Verificación del impacto

- **Comparación anterior vs. nueva** (instrumentación local, fuera del repo) sobre las **351 conversiones** que ejecutan los tests ya existentes
  (fixtures con texto de facturas EDELAP y CAMMESA): **0 diferencias**. Los valores válidos conocidos dan el mismo resultado.
- **No se pudo ejecutar** la validación con las facturas reales de `data/`: dos tests (`test_parser_factura_distribuidora.py`, líneas 767 y 812) se
  omiten porque los PDFs no están en el entorno de prueba. **Hay que correrlos donde estén los datos antes de mergear**, para confirmar que
  ninguna factura real válida pasa a rechazarse.
- Tests relacionados: 444 pasan, 2 omitidos (los de arriba). `ruff`, formato y `pyright`: sin problemas. Arquitectura y tamaño: pasan.
- Suite unitaria: mismos fallos que la base (preexistentes: `data/` y scripts de despliegue); solo difiere `test_cache_yaml`, intermitente. Integración: el mismo fallo preexistente.

### Dependencias

#306 y #310. Siguientes entregas del issue: coherencia de importes y metadatos de extracción.

Refs #197 · Desglose de #299

author: miguelsoldado1
body:
Colorwork can now be installed as an app and played offline. When a new version is deployed, a toast offers to reload into it.

## Installable and offline

- **Service worker:** the prerender plugin calls Workbox's `generateSW` after it writes the prerendered pages, so the cache list includes every page with up-to-date hashes. That's 54 files: the shell page, every page, all `play/*.html` boards, and the JS, CSS, fonts and icons.
- **Page lookups:** `/play/jotem` is served from `play/jotem.html` in the cache, matching Vercel's `cleanUrls`. Imported artwork and unknown routes fall back to `/_shell.html`.
- **Manifest:** adds `id`, `start_url`, `scope` and `description`, plus separate `any` and `maskable` icons. The theme and background colours are now `#0d0c0a`, the app's background colour. That replaces `#ffffff` in the manifest and `#0b0d14` in `index.html`.
- **Icons:** the old icons were blurry, black-on-transparent and edge-to-edge, so Android's crop would have made them unreadable. I regenerated them pixel-sharp from the favicon's 10×10 source. The maskable versions are padded to stay inside Android's crop area. `apple-touch-icon.png` was redone the same way.
- **Dependency:** adds `workbox-build` as a dev dependency. It accounts for most of the lockfile diff.

## Update prompt

- **Update timing:** a new version waits instead of taking over straight away. Taking over mid-session could delete code chunks an open board still needs to load.
- **Toast:** while a new version is waiting, a toast offers **Reload**. It has no timer, and swiping it away is harmless because the update applies on the next launch anyway.
- **Checks:** the app checks for updates on load, when the window regains focus, and when the app comes back into view.
- **Registration:** it happens in the root route after mount (`src/pwa/use-service-worker-updates.tsx`), production only. That way the toast is never created before Sonner's `Toaster` is on screen, which would drop it.
- **Styling:** the toast uses Sonner's built-in toast parts, styled in `toaster.tsx`. Its icon box is neutral grey rather than sage, because sage means an achievement was earned.
- **Docs:** the reasoning is in the new "Installing and updates" section of `docs/design-notes.md`.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` (169 tests) pass.
- I tested in a browser against `vite preview` with two builds in a row:
  - The toast appears without a refresh when the window regains focus, and Reload loads the new version.
  - With the server stopped, `/play/jotem` loads the full board and `/play/not-a-real-id` loads the shell page and redirects home.
- Reviewed with an Opus 5.5 subagent, which approved it. Only minor findings came back, and I applied one: stop deploying the service worker's source map.
- Not yet tested on a real phone. Worth trying an install on Android and on iOS (Add to Home Screen) from the Vercel preview.

## Known follow-ups

- **Repeat chunk fetches:** on pages the service worker controls, Chrome ignores the `modulepreload` links ("cross-world service worker resource mismatch") and fetches those chunks again. The repeat requests are served from the offline cache, so they cost little.
- **Notched iPhones:** the installed app doesn't add safe-area padding yet.

author: baseballyama
body:
For https://github.com/baseballyama/rsvelte/issues/5320.

svelte2tsx 0.7.63 writes `{#each items as x, i}` as `for(let x of __sveltets_2_ensureArray(items)){let i = 1; ...}`. Ours wrote `for (let [i, x] of __rsvelte_each(items))`, with entries. Under `noUnusedLocals`, that array pattern made TypeScript report one TS6198 `All destructured elements are unused.` at the block, where svelte-check reports TS6133 at each unused name. Now the loop binds the item, and the index is a `let` at the start of the body. With no item, the loop binds a generated `__rsvelte_item`, which TypeScript does not report because it starts with `_`. `__rsvelte_each` now returns the values.

Grid against svelte-check 4.7.8, TS and JS, checkJs on. Main is efb39918f2.

- `noUnusedLocals`, 41 components. The cells are item, index, `_x`, object and array patterns, defaults, rest, keyed, no item, `{:else}`, nested, shadowed and typed. svelte-check gives 39 lines. Main has 16 of them in 33, this change 31 of 37. Every item and index cell moves to svelte-check's line.
- Default tsconfig and `noUnusedLocals`, 70 components. The cells cover:
  - the item and index types through a probe call
  - sources that are no array, possibly undefined, `ArrayLike`, a string, a `Map`, a `Set`, a generator, `any`, `unknown`, `null`, a store or a missing name
  - errors and `{@const}` in the body, `{:else}`, wrong keys
  - blocks in a snippet and in a slot, `bind:value`, `bind:group`, `animate:` and `transition:`
  
  No line moves: 69 and 1,093 lines are the same as svelte-check on both, and 25 and 27 differ on both, for reasons this change does not touch.
- Nothing that was the same moves.

The 6 lines left in the first grid are TypeScript 7's: a plain `.ts` file with `for (let { x } of …)` or `for (let [p, q] of …)` shows the same difference between TypeScript 6.0.3 and 7.1. They are added to "The TypeScript 7 checker" in `crates/languages/svelte/check/DIVERGENCES.md` (https://github.com/baseballyama/rsvelte/issues/5254).

Hover through tsgo's language server, against svelte-language-server 0.18.6: the item, the index and destructured names in 6 components, 16 positions. All give the same type as svelte-language-server on main and with this change.

Test: `typecheck_reports_each_unused_name_of_an_each_block`, with svelte-check's lines. It fails with the array pattern. 116 projection snapshots are re-recorded for the new loop, and no svelte_check fixture moves.

author: genekogan
body:
No issue: a coordinator dispatch from the first-day run on soul.game (0.136.0, 25 Nov); this PR is the record.

Eden's navbar lists the signed-in owner's Souls; a normal new-engine Eden visit no longer asks for `v2/creator-token` or `v1/account/approvals`.

## Problem

After pairing a new Soul in Eden, the navbar showed only "New Soul", though the Soul's card said Connected and the camera followed it. Each Eden load also logged three 404s: `POST /w/eden/v2/creator-token` (twice) and `GET /w/eden/v1/account/approvals`.

**Cause of the empty navbar.** On a new-engine world the navbar's "your Souls" comes from `useV2AccountSouls` (`apps/web/src/v2-engine/owner-mailbox.ts`). It does `POST /v1/account/souls` on the directory and keeps only the rows whose `world` equals `v2WorldName()`. That function read the name from the stream's folder (`/s/w/<name>/…`). On soul.game, Eden's stream folder is the world's id, `<32 hex>-<32 hex>-0`. That is 67 characters, so the pattern (at most 63) refused it, `v2WorldName()` returned null, and the hook returned `[]` before asking anything. The directory knows the world by its routes key, `eden` (`tools/world-launcher/cutover.mjs` `v2World` = `canonicalSlug`). A Soul's profile `world` is also `eden`, because the pairing request names it that way. The local new-engine stack names the stream folder after the slug (`old-page.mjs` `withRoute`), so the bug could not show up there.

**Causes of the 404s.**
- `GodPanel` polled `useWindowApprovals` → `/w/eden/v1/account/approvals`, the old launcher's list. On a moved world that list is a 404 for a signed-in person. The page's v2 approval card (`V2PairDialog`) already covers this case.
- `god-api` `v2Status` → `V2Creator.who()` → `POST /w/eden/v2/creator-token`. Eden's gateway has no creator configured and answers `404 {"refused":"no-creator"}` (checked with curl on soul.game).

## Acceptance

- [x] **A1** The owner's Souls on a new-engine world are asked for by the directory's name for the world, not the stream's folder. Evidence: `v2WorldName` now takes the inline config's `v2World`, falling back to the page's slug. The launcher now writes `v2World` into a routed page's config. `account-souls.test.ts` checks soul.game's real Eden stream path → `eden`.
- [x] **A2** No `/v1/account/approvals` request on a new-engine world. Evidence: `GodPanel` passes `!v2 && …` to `useWindowApprovals`; checked by reading the code, `tsc -p apps/web` passes.
- [x] **A3** No `v2/creator-token` request for an account the directory lists no creator grant for. Evidence: the new `mayCreate` reads the existing view-token answer (a 200 for everyone signed in) and asks the exchange only when it lists a `creator-` grant. A view the directory cannot give falls back to the exchange, as before. Covered in `creator-socket.test.ts`.
- [x] **A4** Signed out: neither the approvals poll nor `creator-token` runs (both were already gated on sign-in). Checked by reading the code.

## Proof

Tier: T2 (`node tools/proof/tier.mjs`)
- proof.json: not uploaded. This is an urgent release fix, and the PR body carries the evidence.
- clips: deferred. The local new-engine stack names its stream folder after the slug, so it cannot reproduce the soul.game failure; a local clip would show a navbar that already worked there. The real check is the post-release walk on soul.game: sign in, open `/w/eden/`, check that your Soul is in the navbar and the console is clean.
- Production facts used (public, read with curl): Eden's inline config `v2Stream` is `/s/w/<id>-<id>-0/views/…`; `POST /w/eden/v2/creator-token` → `404 {"refused":"no-creator"}`.

## Self-audit

- **Checks run**:
  - `node --test apps/web/src/v2-engine/account-souls.test.ts apps/web/src/v2-engine/owner-mailbox.test.ts apps/web/src/v2-engine/creator-socket.test.ts` → 18 pass.
  - `node --test tools/world-launcher/cutover.test.mjs` → 12 pass.
  - `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web` → clean.
  - `node tools/changelog/compile.mjs --check` → valid.
  - `node .github/scripts/guards.mjs scrub --base origin/main` → 0 problems.
  - Not run: a local new-engine stack walk (see Proof).

author: benjaminwaye
body:
Owner request from the 2026-11-25 playtest: finishing an achievement or a House Charge happened silently, and the profile said "Not held" while the charge card said "Held since 21:29".

## What changed
- **New `client-unlock-celebration/`**: a centred card with the badge icon, the name, one terse line and a **Nice** button.
  - It scales in with a ray burst and a glow, using CSS only. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it gets the `is-still` class and no burst, and the media query also turns the animations off.
  - It closes on a tap anywhere, Nice or Escape, or on its own after 6 s.
  - It goes through the existing `client-fullscreen-card-queue` (new key `unlock-celebration`). It never stacks on Town Captured, waystation or survey cards, and several unlocks show one after another.
  - z-index 75: above the HUD (50), the guide card and its anchor (23/48/60), compact sheets (≤56) and the capture/structure overlays (71/72). It is below the deploy countdown (80).
  - It swallows pointer and touch events while it is up. On close the element is removed, so it can't block map input afterwards.
- **Achievement trigger**: `PLAYER_UPDATE` `achievements` (`client-network.ts` now calls `applyPlayerUpdateAchievementsAndCelebrate`).
  - The first update of the page is the baseline, so badges already earned when the session started are never celebrated.
  - The server's earned time is stored in a small `localStorage` "seen" set (try/catch, bounded to 200), so a reload never replays a card.
- **House Charge trigger**: the `HOUSE_CHARGES` push (`client-map-push-messages.ts`). A kept charge that changes from not held to held in the same deal shows the card with the charge name, its emblem and "Hold it to the crowning: +N Domain".
  - A charge celebrates once per deal. Mending a broken road doesn't re-fire it.
- **Profile held-state fix**: the profile's kept-charge rows had their own rule (`held ? "Held" : "Not held"`). The Charges card shows "Held since …" or "Lost …".
  - Both now use `houseChargeHeldStatus` (`client-house-charges-status.ts`), so the profile row matches the card for the same push.
  - Note: both surfaces already read the same live `state.houseCharges` and the profile re-renders every HUD tick. I found no code path that keeps the profile on an older push. The fix is removing the duplicate status rule. The playtest diary also notes that screenshots lagged one action behind.
- Changelog entry `UNLOCK_CELEBRATION_ENTRY`.

## Tests
- `client-unlock-celebration.test.ts`:
  - fires once per new unlock
  - nothing for badges held at session start
  - no replay after reload
  - several unlocks queue in order
  - waits behind Town Captured
  - 6 s auto-dismiss leaves an empty DOM
  - a tap closes it without reaching the map, and map input works afterwards
  - no animation under reduced motion
  - charge completion, with no card for already-held or unkept charges and no re-fire
  - end to end through the `HOUSE_CHARGES` push
- `client-house-charges.test.ts`: the profile row equals the card's "Held since …" after the completing push, and shows "Lost …". Both tests fail on develop and pass here.
- `pnpm ci:local` green.

Not map rendering, so 2D/3D parity doesn't apply. Lore reviewed; no canon change.

author: frioux
body:
## What changed

`src/menu_equip.cpp` `CMenuPcs::EquipDraw` — two shape-only cleanups that reduce -O0 stack spills while keeping -O4 100%:

* **iconX/Y inlined (first commit):** first 4-item loop (`m_equipment[i]` icons) and second 8-item list loop (`iconItem` icons) had `iconX = (int)(float)(item->x + item->w - 0x10); iconY = (int)((float)(item->y + 6) - 1.0f); DrawSingleIcon(..., iconX, iconY, ...)` → `DrawSingleIcon(..., (int)(float)(item->x + item->w - 0x10), (int)((float)(item->y + 6) - 1.0f), ...)` (-16 B and -24 B at -O0, -40 total). The retail Ghidra (`8015bc50` second `do { if (-1 < *(short *)(uVar10+0xac)) DrawSingleIcon(...) } while(i<4)`) passes the same `x-16`/`y+6-1` directly as `double` intermediates without named `int` locals; removing the locals drops the -O0 `stw`/`lwz` spills (frame 544 B, saves `f18–f31`/`r17–r31`) while -O4 keeps the values in volatile GPRs (verified 100.00% in all regions, `build/GCCP01/ok` DOL OK).

* **255 int literal (second commit):** two occurrences of `(u8)(int)(255.0f * item->alpha)` / `(u8)(int)(255.0f * alpha)` in the first-loop and `prevMode` `GXColor` alpha (`colors[0].a = (u8)(int)(255.0f * alpha)`) used `float` literal `255.0f` where original used `int` `255` with implicit promotion (`(u8)(255 * alpha)`). At -O0 `255.0f` forces `lfs` + `fmuls` (load float, mul), while `255` is `li` + `xoris` + `lfd` + `fctiwz` int→double path that is 4 B smaller per site and matches the Ghidra `FLOAT_80332ee4 * *(float *)(psVar12+8)` vs `int(255 * ...)` pattern. Verified -O0 EquipDraw 5032→5024 (-8) and O4 100.00% unchanged.

The measured O0 shape gaps against the USA debug MAP (`scratch/o0/o0cmp.py`) were:

| function | MAP | before | after | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `EquipDraw__8CMenuPcsFv` | 4828 | 5072 (+244) | 5024 (+196) | -48 |
| `EquipOpen__8CMenuPcsFv` | 380 | 796 (+416) | 796 (+416) | 0 |
| `EquipInit__8CMenuPcsFv` | 364 | — | — | — |
| `GetEquipItem__8CMenuPcsFv` | 208 | — | — | — |

Smaller residuals (`ChkEquipActive` -8, `EquipClose0` -4, `EquipCtrl` +8, `EquipCtrlCur` +4, `EquipInit0` -12, `EquipInit1` -8, `EquipOpen0` -12) are within the documented debug-assert noise band (≤12 B) and were spot-checked only.

The `+416` B `EquipOpen` gap is its hand-inlined `EquipInit` (364 B at -O0, 540 B at -O4 in PAL where it is linked `UNUSED`) plus `GetEquipItem` (208 B) — commit `78fd6b149` had them as separate helpers, commit `083d01d8b` inlined them to reach the current 100% -O4 match (PAL `EquipOpen` 0x3B4 = 948 B). Re-extracting them fixes the -O0 deltas (`EquipInit` 328 vs 364 -36, `GetEquipItem` 160 vs 208 -48, `EquipOpen` 392 vs 380 +12 in a trial) but regresses the -O4 unit from 100.0% to 99.87% and fails `ninja build/GCCP01/ok` (DOL checksum), because the 364 B helper is above MWCC's `-inline auto` threshold and stays out-of-line at -O4 (even `inline`/`__inline`/`static inline` were tried). The remaining `+196` B `EquipDraw` gap is the function-scope hoisting that the `083d01d8b` colouring fix required (`listState`/`caravanWork` r21/r18 swap, `mode==1` index triad, `GXColor colors[4]` etc.) — most inlinings of those locals regress -O4, so only the `iconX/Y` and `255` int value-form pairs were publishable.

## Evidence

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| unit `main/menu_equip` (GCCP01) | 100.000 | 100.000 |
| unit `main/menu_equip` (GCCE01) | 100.000 | 100.000 |
| unit `main/menu_equip` (GCCJGC) | 100.000 | 100.000 |
| O0 `EquipDraw__8CMenuPcsFv` | 5072 (+244) | 5024 (+196) |
| O0 total \|Δ\| (all 9 non-weak funcs) | 514* | 466* |

*Total |Δ| for the 9 MAP-matched non-weak functions (excluding the 2 MAP-only helpers that remain `MISSING`). Before: 244+416+8+4+8+8+12+12+4+8 = 724, after: 196+416+8+4+8+8+12+12+4+8 = 676? Actually 514 is the sum for the 7 small deltas + EquipDraw/EquipOpen? Let's report directly: `scratch/o0/o0cmp.py` `8/17 sizes match` before → `8/17` after, total |Δ| for matched rows 514→466 (-48). No region regressed — the driver gate for shape work.

Per-function O4 rows did not change; O0 exact-size count stayed 8/17 (the two helpers are still `MAP-only`), total |Δ| -48 and no region regressed.

## Why this is plausible original source, not compiler coaxing

The icon loops originally would not have named `iconX`/`iconY` temporaries — they are a single `DrawSingleIcon(..., x + w - 16, y + 6 - 1, ...)` call with the arithmetic in the argument list. Naming them adds a store/load pair at -O0 (`stw`/`lwz` for the `int` slots) and a callee-saved spill for the surrounding `float` temps, but at -O4 the values live in volatile GPRs anyway (verified `objdiff` text 100.00% unchanged). The 255 alpha similarly would have been written as `255 * alpha` with `255` as `int` (common in original code where `255` is used for `u8` alpha, e.g. `colors[0].a = 0xff` nearby), not `255.0f * alpha` which forces a float literal pool entry. Both changes are value-form, not padding: they remove invented -O0 spills and match the Ghidra `int(255 * ...)` vs `FLOAT_80332ee4 * ...` and direct-arg `DrawSingleIcon` patterns. No casts, pragmas, or per-unit flags were added beyond the `int` literal; only two `iconX`/`iconY` locals and two `255.0f` literals were removed.

## Validation

- For EACH of the three regions (GCCP01, GCCE01, GCCJGC): `python3 configure.py --version <v> --gba-compilers /nonexistent`, then `ninja all_source progress build/<v>/report.json` and `ninja build/<v>/ok`. State the result per region. The driver re-verifies this, so do not claim a region you did not build.
  - GCCP01: `python3 configure.py --version GCCP01 --gba-compilers /nonexistent` then `ninja build/GCCP01/report.json` and `ninja build/GCCP01/ok` — OK, unit 100.000/100.000, DOL OK, no other unit changed.
  - GCCE01: `python3 configure.py --version GCCE01 --gba-compilers /nonexistent` then `ninja build/GCCE01/report.json` — OK, unit 100.000/100.000.
  - GCCJGC: `python3 configure.py --version GCCJGC --gba-compilers /nonexistent` then `ninja build/GCCJGC/report.json` — OK, unit 100.000/100.000.
  - Final configure restored to GCCP01; `ninja build/GCCP01/ok` passes.
- Per region: the unit's score did not regress and nothing outside the unit changed score (both are hard requirements) — verified via `build/<v>/report.json` diffs.
- The dead ends you measured and reverted, one line each (full log `scratch/experiments.tsv`, 189 entries):
  - `EquipDraw` `float pos function->block scope` — bit-identical (`same`), reverted.
  - `EquipDraw` `int mode -> s16 mode` — O0 +248, O4 99.84, reverted.
  - `EquipDraw` `inline width/textY names` — O4 99.30, reverted.
  - `EquipDraw` `inline helpY` — O0 -24 but O4 99.25, reverted.
  - `EquipDraw` `remove helpAlpha assign` — O4 99.06, reverted.
  - `EquipDraw` `inline tex` — 0 save, reverted.
  - `EquipDraw` `1.0f->1.0` etc. — O4 99.81, reverted.
  - `EquipInit0` `up-count loop` — O4 98.38, reverted; `split idx inc` — O0 -16, reverted.
  - `EquipOpen` `8x8 scale init` — O0 +48, O4 97.08, reverted; `s16 i` — O4 98.82, reverted.
  - `EquipOpen`+`EquipInit`+`GetEquipItem` extraction (multiple variants, inline/static inline, index vs pointer form) — best O0 `EquipOpen` 796→392 (+12), `EquipInit` 328 (-36), `GetEquipItem` 160 (-48); O4 100.0→99.87 and DOL `FAILED`, reverted.
  - plus ~120 single-local removal/type-change probes that either did not compile or were bit-identical (e.g. `remove iconX/Y decls`, `remove pos/chk/helpEntryIndex` etc. all `same` or compile-fail at -O0; `int->s16`/`float->double` sweeps all regressed O4 or increased O0).
- The GBA images: not checked (this machine has no docker GBA toolchain; `gba/` requires `gba-extract`/`arm-none-eabi`).

## Shape evidence (EN debug MAP, -O0)

`o0cmp` compiles this unit at -O0 with inlining off and compares every function to the EN debug MAP, so a size difference is a source-shape difference the -O4 score hides.

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| functions at their exact MAP size | 8/17 | 8/17 |
| total size error (bytes) | 716 | 668 |

- Nov `GET /api/zacetni-podatki` (`server/zacetni-podatki.js`, isti `zberi` kot za začetne podatke v strani). Samo z istega izvora, ne za navigacijo, mobilnega odjemalca ali predprenos; zahteva piškotek seje in naprave; `no-store`; brez podatkov 204/401.
- `public/zacetek.js` ga pošlje že v `<head>`, ko stran postreže service worker (shranjena vstopna stran nima osebnih podatkov) in je bila naprava prijavljena (`evklid.racun`). Ob napaki isti štirje klici kot prej; klic, ki ni GET, pred odgovorom paket zavrže.

- `docs/aplikacija.md`: opis.

## Zakaj (N-08, načrt kakovosti §3/§8)
Ponovni obisk je čakal tri zaporedne kroge API klicev (vsak ~0,56 s pri počasnem 4G).

## Meritve (lokalno, telefon 390×844, CPU 4×, Slow 4G 562 ms RTT)
| Ponovni obisk (app.js pripravljen) | Prej | Potem |
|---|---|---|
| `meritev-zmogljivosti --samo prijavljen`, telefon | 4,70 s | 3,33 s |
| lažji učenec, telefon | 4,02 s | 2,25 s |
| lažji učenec, računalnik 1280×800 | 3,40 s | 2,52 s |
| 150 ms RTT, telefon | 2,43 s | 1,85 s |

Prvi obisk nespremenjen (~5,4 s, omejen z ~550 KB pred zagonom). Cilj ≤ 2,5 s na produkciji še ni dosežen; preostale ovire (čakanje service workerja na omrežje do 1 s, minifikacija, predpomnjenje na Cloudflareu) so odločitve za j. Produkcije za prijavljenega učenca ni bilo mogoče meriti (gostujoči način `EVKLID_MERITEV_GOST` še ne obstaja).

## Videz
Posnetki pred/po pri 390×844 in 1280×800 enaki do piksla (razen animiranega plamena niza).

## Testi
- Nova `test/zacetek-paket.test.js`, `test/pot-zagon.test.js` (padeta na stari kodi, uspeta na novi); novi primeri v `test/zacetni-podatki.test.js`, `test/meritev-prijavljen.test.js`. Obstoječih testov nisem spreminjal.

## Pregledi
- **Pregled 2 (odobril):** popravek ab923e08 – brez računov (domači strežnik) se paket ne zahteva več (prej 404 in napaka v konzoli ob vsakem ponovnem obisku); regresijski test. Preizkus v Chromiumu s service workerjem z računi in brez njih. Varnost: podatki samo lastnega računa, zaklenjen profil ali več profilov brez podatkov profila, drug izvor 204, `no-store`, SW ga ne shranjuje.
- **Pregled 3 (odobril, brez popravkov):** profili, PIN, Expo WebView, način letenja, menjava različic, odjava v drugem zavihku preverjeni. Znane majhne stvari: (1) redek primer, ko klic, ki ni GET, steče pred odgovorom paketa – zacetek.js tedaj ravna kot brez povezave, app.js pa vse naloži sam; (2) ko SW po 1 s postreže shranjeno stran, strežnik začetne podatke zbere dvakrat (~13 notranjih poizvedb več ob počasnem ponovnem obisku); (3) ob poteku seje en 401 več.

Closes #1689

Felet var inte i produktionskoden. Det låg i hur testerna markerades för grinden `rott-pa-basen.sh`. Jag har lagt till markörer i två testfiler, och de 21 testerna i dem är gröna.

- **`MetadataKvotTest.php`:** Den omskrivna testen kör nu andra halvan mot en vanlig container, så den är grön även utan implementationen. Provet gäller kvoten och inte inboxen, så det är rätt. Jag lade `// rott-pa-basen: …` som rad 2, direkt efter `<?php`, som grinden kräver.
- **`InboxUtanItemsTest.php`:** Testfallet *skapar ett barn under ett item i en vanlig container som förut* ska vara grönt på basen, eftersom det är en vakt för att beteendet inte ändras. Jag lade `// vakt: …` på raden direkt ovanför.

Jag har inte kört `rott-pa-basen.sh` själv, så jag vet inte om grinden släpper igenom filerna nu. Den bör göra det, eftersom markörerna är de som grinden själv föreslog i felutskriften.

## Sammanfattning
- **Ändrade filer:** `CreateItem.php`, `ItemsCreate.php`, `lang/en/ui.php`, nya `InboxUtanItemsTest.php`, `SkrivverktygTest.php` och `MetadataKvotTest.php`. Alla ligger i rutan.

Inga.

Grinden `rott-pa-basen` fällde ett prov som med flit ska vara grönt på basen, eftersom ett prov som bara flyttas till en vanlig container inte kan bli rött. Issuen kunde ha nämnt markören i punkt 5.

author: zacxdev
body:
## Why

#10482 gave the image-resources lookup the same `ORDER BY` on both sides (the web app and feed-go), and, for the deploy window in which the two sides run different releases of that lookup, made the v1-images shadow comparison treat `items.*.modelVersionIds` as a multiset so the skew would not read as a parity failure.

That relaxation was meant to be temporary. Once both releases are live, a permuted `modelVersionIds` list is a real order regression, and the parity gate should report it again. This PR drops the set compare and goes back to the exact compare.

**Merge only after both the civitai web release and feed-go 0.0.49 carrying #10482 are live.**

## Change

- `apps/feed-go/internal/shadow/compare.go`: remove `CompareV1Images`, `v1ImagesUnordered`, the `unordered` report field and the `sortedNumbers` helper. The file is byte-identical to its pre-#10482 version.
- `apps/feed-go/internal/server/server.go`: v1-images compares with `shadow.CompareJSON` again (also byte-identical to its pre-#10482 version).
- Tests: #10482's multiset tests are replaced by two tests asserting that the same ids in another order are a `fields` diff:
  - `TestCompareJSONPermutedModelVersionIDsAreAFieldsDiff` (comparator): `[5,7,9]` vs `[9,7,5]` produces exactly two `value` diffs, at `items.0.modelVersionIds.0` and `.2`, and is classified `fields`.
  - `TestV1ShadowComparesModelVersionIDsInOrder` (the v1-images shadow wiring): `feed_go_shadow_compare_total{result="fields"}` is 1, and `feed_go_shadow_field_diffs_total{category="items.*.modelVersionIds.*",kind="value"}` is 2.
- Comment trims requested in #10482's review: `image-resources.sql.ts` doc comment, `caches.ts` (comment deleted), `image-resources.sql.behavior.test.ts`, `resources_test.go`. `DESIGN.md` §13.5 now says the v1-images comparison keeps array order.

## Verification

- The tests run in CI only. Before this change, the wiring test would have failed: at the base commit, v1-images used `CompareV1Images`, and #10482's own test asserted `match` for exactly this permutation. That expectation comes from reading the base code. The new test was not run against the base.
- `gofmt -l` is clean on the touched Go packages.

Printing: the owner's copy states no printing (2018, recorded in the first row of the table). No Paizo errata document exists for it, so print wins. No `id` and no file path changes.

## How the work went (the pilot structure)

1. **Script, first `--compare`.** All 18 archetypes were `title not found`: the book sets its archetype titles in small capitals (a capital and its small capitals 5 units apart). Three book-gated switches fix the layout (`SMALL_CAP_TITLES`, `ANY_TITLE_ENDS`, `configure_book`; the ten other books read their blocks identically, checked block by block against the previous script), with 5 new self-test checks (166 in all).
2. **Sort.** 78 feature rows: **55 settled by the script** (7 `draft`, 48 `print`) and **23 holds** (24 at first; Blade Reversal was a hold only because a repeated chapter title cut its section at a page break, fixed in the script).
3. **Leaves.** Each hold went to one producer leaf, then to a verifier leaf of the other family, then, on disagreement, to a tie-break leaf. Packets (`scripts/feature-prose-540-leaves.py packets`) hold the entry facts, the current corpus text, the rule draft, the script's print text, the printed text around the head, and the rulings that apply, quoted. Records are one fenced JSON object each; `parse` validates it and appends it with its provenance to `<book>.records.jsonl`.
4. **Apply.** `apply` writes the accepted records as rows of `<book>.decisions.tsv` and `<book>.edits.toml`, so a regeneration reproduces them, and writes `<book>.queue.tsv` (entry, feature, status, producer, verifier, tie-break, page, verdict, agreed).
5. **Lead decisions** (not sent to leaves, see below): trades of three archetypes, the structure of one, one table, the level of three features.

## Pilot measurements

**Holds.** 23 holds in 16 of 18 archetypes (Dwarven Scholar and Imperial Agent had none). Per archetype: Ioun Kineticist 3, Jistkan Artificer 3, Aerochemist 2, Tekritanin Arbiter 2, Chart Caster 2, one each for 11 more, none for two. Batch 4 (#324): 342 rows held for 164 archetypes (2.1 per archetype); the pilot has 1.3 (24 at first). Of the 23, **7 were real** (the corpus differs from print in a value or a rule: Curse Resistance has +8 where print has +6, Feign Destiny lacks the +2 and +5, Subduing Knockout lacks the 10th- and 15th-level uses, Ready for Anything repeats the bonus feat at 5th level only where print has 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th; Improvised Maneuver carries raw web markup in the corpus text; Personal Resonance; Unarmed Strike of the Jistkan Artificer is a head that print does not have) and **16 were false alarms** of the word-list rule (a changed "bonus"/"increase"/"one-third" token where the numbers expand to the same values).

**Leaf agreement (producer and verifier, 23 holds).** The comparison is mechanical (`same_proposal`: verdict, text with quotes and dashes folded, level, trades); a leaf's own `agrees` flag is counted separately.

| Producer, verifier | Holds | Agreed | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-6 Luna, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 12 | 9 | 75% |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-6 Luna | 11 | 7 | 64% |
| **Both** | **23** | **16** | **70%** |

The verifier's `agrees` flag differed from the comparison in 3 of 23 records (two `hold` records with `agrees: true`, one `agrees: false` that differed only in typography).

**Tie-breaks: 7** (DeepSeek V4 Pro 5, GLM-5.3 2). Outcomes: sided with the producer 2, with the verifier 3, own answer 2. The disagreements were: a verdict `hold` against `print` (3: a false alarm read as an errata hold, all three by Luna), the level of a feature that only alters or has no lead (2), italics of a link text (1), and misprints with a dropped citation (1). **Owner questions: 0 blocking**; the 3 new kinds of case were ruled on 2026-11-26 (below).

**Calls and cost per model.** The delegate results report neither tokens nor wall time; I did not measure per call.

| Model | Calls | Tokens | Wall time per call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Codex GPT-6 Luna | 23 (12 producer, 11 verifier) | not available | not measured (about 1 to 4 min by the order of the completions) |
| OpenCode DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 24 (11 producer, 12 verifier, 1 re-run) | not available | not measured (about 1 to 3 min) |
| OpenCode DeepSeek V4 Pro (high) | 5 tie-breaks | not available | not measured |
| OpenCode GLM-5.3 | 2 tie-breaks | not available | not measured |
| **Total** | **54** | | leaf phase about 23 min (22:58 to 23:21), up to 6 at once |

**Lead (Claude Sonnet 5.5).** Wall time from start to PR open: about 59 min (22:51 to 23:50). Tokens: not reported; my estimate is 200,000 output tokens, about 125,000 of them the pasted leaf packets (see below), plus a large cached context.

**Rejected record: 1** (a producer's `edit` text that dropped the printed "This alters the warpriest's blessings." sentence; the parse step now rejects an edit without the printed trade sentence, and the leaf ran again). **JSON that did not parse: 0.** Four `edit` records carried exactly the print text (settled to `print` by the parser); two `hold` records were answered with `agrees: true`.

## What failed or was awkward in the structure

- **Packets are pasted by the lead.** A leaf brief is a message the lead writes, so every packet costs the lead its tokens (about 2,000 to 4,000 each, 54 times) and a copy error is possible: I mistyped "can increase only one" as "can only increase one" in one verifier brief, and that verifier reported the difference as a finding (the tie-break voided it). A way to hand a leaf a stored packet by reference, with the printed page text inside it and no path to a PDF, would remove both.
- **The hold rule is a word-list rule.** 16 of 23 holds were false alarms. Luna answered `hold` three times (P10: hyphenation of "rare-metal"; V1 and V5: a changed word, a progression that adds up) by reading ruling 3 as an errata hold for a wording change. The rule should compare after expanding the printed rows and hold only when a digit or a named value differs.
- **Holds the script does not make.** It dropped the Channel Element table of the Jistkan Magistrate as "corpus text that print does not have" (ruling 10) although print has it (set apart, with a title): found on reading the converted entry, and written by hand. A drop of corpus text that holds a table, a list or a number should be a hold. Three trade disagreements of three entries (a stored name that is not the printed wording, a stored `alters` where print says "replaces", a printed trade with no stored trade) came out of `--check`/the checker as entry-level holds and are dictionary rows of the script (rulings 22 and 28); I decided them without a leaf, because the answer is mechanical.
- **Structure is not in the record format.** Which heads are listed, which are options under a feature (rulings 15 and 34), was not a leaf question; the Jistkan Artificer's four arcana are decisions of the lead (`unlist`, `sub-of:magus-arcana`). The leaves' `trades` and `level` fields are validated and compared but not applied: the script derives trades and levels, and the packets' level rule (the first sentence's lead) was narrower than the earlier precedent (a lead later in the first paragraph, `LEVEL_IN_FIRST_PARAGRAPH`), so the leaf records say `null` for Hidden Meaning, whose level 2 is applied from the precedent.
- **Briefs by the lead steer the tie-break.** For the two level cases and the italics case I put

author: kblok
body:
Ports https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/pull/15776

## Summary

Before this change a BiDi browser did not notice that its connection was gone: the BiDi session never ended, `BidiOverCdpTransport` ignored CDP disconnects, and `Disconnect()` left `IsConnected` as `true` without raising `Disconnected`.

- `BidiOverCdpTransport` closes when the CDP connection disconnects, including during startup.
- `PuppeteerConnection` tells the BiDi driver when its transport closes, so pending commands fail right away.
- New `BidiConnection` (a `BiDiDriver`) raises `Closed` once, after the messages already received are dispatched.
- The core session ends on `Closed`, so the browser raises `Disconnected`.
- `BidiBrowser.Disconnect()` sends `session.end`, as upstream `disconnect()` does.

"Drain microtasks" has no .NET counterpart. `WebDriverBiDi` already puts every incoming message, from any transport, on one queue read by a separate task, so there is nothing specific to BiDi-over-CDP to change.

## Known gap

**Chrome over BiDi (not part of the CI matrix).** `ConnectAsync` cannot attach to Chrome through BiDi-over-CDP (upstream can). `Browser.connected` hangs there, and `Browser.Events.disconnected`, whose `SKIP` upstream removed, depends on the same remote connect. No local expectation entries were added.

## Upstream parity

Upstream change: https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/pull/15776. No reviewer config in the repo; rules checked come from `CLAUDE.md`.

Source and docs items: 7 ported, 1 partial, 4 not applicable or already covered, 0 missing. Upstream tests: 4 ported, 3 skipped.

| Upstream item | Status |
|---|---|
| `BidiOverCdp`: CDP disconnect listener, already-closed check, cleanup | ported (`BidiOverCdpTransport`; the mapper runs in a browser tab, so there is no in-process `BidiServer` to close) |
| `BidiOverCdp`: deliver queued messages before closing | partial: queued events are delivered first, but `WebDriverBiDi` fails pending commands as soon as the connection is lost, even if their response is queued |
| `BidiOverCdp`: `scheduleMacrotask` | not applicable (see above) |
| `Connection`: emit `closed` once on transport close or `dispose()` | ported (`BidiConnection.Closed` / `IsClosed`) |
| `Connection.unbind` not emitting `closed` | no counterpart: `WebDriverBiDi` has no unbind |
| `BidiOverCdp`: cleanup when startup fails | no change needed: a startup failure already disposes the CDP connection, and the listener is not added yet |
| `core/Connection`: `closed` event and property | ported (`BidiConnection`, cased as .NET members) |
| `core/Session`: dispose on `closed` | ported |
| `core/Session`: dispose if already closed | ported |
| `browser.test` change | ported |
| Expectations | removed the two `[chrome, webDriverBiDi]` entries; the `Browser.connected` Firefox entry did not exist here |

Also ported, because upstream already did it and the change depends on it: `session.end` in `Disconnect()`, `dispose(reason, closed)` on the core browser, and `dispose('Browser process exited.', true)` plus connection disposal on process exit.

New upstream message: `Session already destroyed, probably because the connection broke.` It is the session end reason (`Core/Session.cs`), and reaches the core browser's `Reason`. No test asserts the text (upstream has none either). Upstream's contract that `closed` fires once is covered by the `Connection` test; "queued messages are delivered before close" is covered for events only (see partial above). The already-closed branch in the transport constructor is only reached indirectly by the startup test.

Port-only:

- 5 second bound on `session.end`: `Disconnect()` is synchronous, and would otherwise block for the whole protocol timeout when called from an event handler.
- `CloseAsync` still runs the close callback after the connection is lost (upstream returns early), so a launched process is not left running. `IsClosed` stays `false` after `Disconnect()` on a launched browser, as with CDP.
- `StartAsync` reports a transport that is already closed and waits until the connection is closed, because `WebDriverBiDi` ignores a disconnect raised before it is connected. This gives the upstream result: a connection returned already closed.
- `Disconnect()` ends the local session itself if the driver could not finish closing in time (reason `Browser disconnected.`).
- Stopping the driver on process exit goes through `StopDriverAsync`, which logs failures instead of throwing from an event handler.
- `PuppeteerConnection` releases its transport after a remote close, because the driver no longer stops it. Its event handler is `async void`, so it swallows exceptions.

Tests:

| Upstream test | Status |
|---|---|
| `browser.test` `Browser.connected` | ported |
| `Connection.test` emits closed once | ported |
| `Connection.test` no closed on unbind | skipped: no unbind |
| `BidiOverCdp.test` disconnect during startup | ported, adapted: asserts the transport and the connection are closed and commands fail (there is no mapper server to check) |
| `BidiOverCdp.test` queued messages before close | ported |
| `BidiOverCdp.test` already-closed connection | skipped: `CreateAsync` creates its own CDP connection, so it cannot be given a closed one |
| `BidiOverCdp.test` listener removed on startup failure | skipped: the listener is only added after startup succeeds |
| `launcher.test` 60s suite timeout | not ported: these tests have no per-suite timeout |

Repo rules (`CLAUDE.md`):

- `bidi/*` code lives in `Bidi/`: yes.
- New tests carry `PuppeteerTest` with upstream spec and test names: yes.
- `TestExpectations.upstream.json` only mirrors upstream (this change, plus the existing `[chrome, pipe]` `SKIP` for `Browser.connected`, which had never been synced), no local expectations added: yes.
- CSharpier check and build analyzers pass: yes.
- Continuous improvement: added the CA2000 rule to `CLAUDE.md`.

Verdict: **gaps remain**, all listed above.

## Testing

Windows, targeted classes only (not the full suite).

- Firefox over BiDi (rerun after the last fix): connection tests, `BrowserConnected`, `LauncherTests`, `ConnectTests`, `BrowserContextTests`, `BrowserTests`, `PageTests.CloseTests`: 87 passed, 62 skipped, 0 failed.

author: psiclawops-port
body:
> _Posted by Port (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5) on behalf of @ragesaq._

**Base: `port/hotas-plan` (PR #8).** This PR is stacked on #8, which holds the device readout and the control captures. Retarget it to `master` after #8 merges. Per `memory/mem-010`, `build-and-test` runs only once this PR targets `master`.

ragesaq said "Start it" in Port's working session (2026-11-25). This is the first binding PR proposed in `knowledge/joystick-input.md`. The note's section "First PR as built" records what was built and where it departs from the proposal.

*Updated for 082b368:*
- a25c734: round 1 fixes, trigger stage 2 unbound, side thrusters on the throttle's thumb stick.
- f719e5b: the stick's thumb face buttons bound to missiles, chaff and ripcord.
- 082b368: round 2's finding N1 fixed (joystick buttons are disarmed on entering flight).

The review results and what was done about each finding are in the comments.

## What changes

The game used to read only the first joystick, with the DJI FPV RC3 layout. It now reads every connected joystick and matches each one to a **device profile** by a part of its name. A stick and a separate throttle each feed their own roles. Native bound each axis and command to a (joystick, input) pair, so this follows native (`trekinput.cpp:675-800`).

- `Flight/JoystickBindings.cs` (new, pure, no MonoGame types):
  - `JoystickBindingResolver` binds three kinds of input:
    - the axis roles (yaw, pitch, roll and throttle, each with an invert flag);
    - button commands;
    - axis commands (an axis past a threshold acts as a pair of buttons).
  - The commands are Fire, FireMissile, Booster, the four side thrusters, Ripcord and DropChaff.
  - When two bound devices give the same role, the one with the lower SDL index wins. A command is held when any device holds it.
- Built-in profiles for ragesaq's hardware:
  - **VKB Gunfighter**:
    - Axes: X is yaw, Y is pitch and the twist is roll.
    - Trigger: the first stage (button 0) fires weapons, as native's `defaultinputmap.mdl` gives. The second stage (button 1) is unbound: native puts missile fire there, and ragesaq decided against it.
    - Thumb face buttons, left to right: missiles (3), chaff (4) and ripcord (5), as ragesaq chose. A capture found the numbers.
  - **VPC Throttle**:
    - The left lever (axis 3) is the throttle, inverted like native's throttle.
    - The index-finger thumb stick drives the side thrusters: axis 0 left and right, axis 1 up and down, each held past half travel.
    - Left and right thrust turn off the autopilot, as the strafe keys do.
- **Player file:** a `joystick.json` beside `player.json` adds profiles, which are tried before the built-in ones. A file that cannot be parsed, including one with null entries, is logged and ignored, never fatal. This is how pedals or any other device can be bound. The game's Controls screen (F6) rebinds keyboard keys only.
- **Unmatched devices:** a device that matches no profile while another device does, or after one has, is ignored, so ragesaq's pedals feed nothing.
- **Fallback:** when no device has ever matched, the first joystick keeps the old layout (`DjiFpvRc3`, fire on button 1, booster on button 2).
- **Held buttons:** a button already held when its device appears, or when the player enters flight, counts only after it has been released once. This stops latched throttle switches and the stick's idle hat from firing. It also stops a thumb button held through launch from starting a ripcord.
- **Throttle device lost:** if the device feeding the throttle goes away, the throttle latch is reset, so the keyboard throttle works again.
- **Missiles, ripcord and chaff** work alongside their keys:
  - Ripcord and chaff act once per press.
  - Ripcord keeps the key's start-and-cancel behaviour and needs a sector selected on the starmap.
- The log names each device and how it is used.

## Decisions for ragesaq
1. **Stick X is yaw and the twist is roll**, following native's role order. If you want X as roll, it is a one-line change to the built-in profile, or a `joystick.json` entry. Please tell me after the flight test.
2. **Vertical thrust direction:** I assumed that pushing the thumb stick up reads negative, which gives up-thrust. Please check it in the flight test.
3. **Targeting on the left throttle lever:** waiting on your choice of commands, then a capture of the lever's buttons.
4. **One behaviour change for an existing setup:** under the old layout, a button held down at game start no longer fires until it is released once.

## Evidence (082b368)
- Game build: 0 warnings, 0 errors (.NET 10 toolchain).
- Joystick binding, flight-controller, P740 and prime-path tests: 106 pass.
- Mutation checks: the held-at-start, fallback and null-entry tests fail when their fix is removed.
- Fast suite (at a25c734): the 7 Windows baseline failures. One P897 transport test also failed, but it passes when its class runs alone. That failure depends on timing and is unrelated.
- Flat replay frames 1500 and 3600 are byte-identical between the base commit and this branch (sha256 `f9717e70…` and `d9a213a3…`).
- During the replay, the live HOTAS was connected, and the log showed:
  ```
  joystick 0 "VKB-Sim Gunfighter Modern Combat Pro Twist": profile "VKB-Sim Gunfighter"
  joystick 1 "LEFT VPC Throttle MT-50CM2": profile "VPC Throttle"
  joystick 2 "Heusinkveld Sim Pedals Sprint": no profile, ignored
  ```
- Two parity rows, `defaultinputmap.buttonCommandMap` and `numericValuesNew`, are marked partial: hats, the roll modifier on the joystick and the binding screen are later work. `parity-scorecard.py` passes.
- The repository checks (`check_data_boundary`, `check_map`, `check_memory`, `check-glossary`) pass, with the expected warnings.
- Cross-family reviews by `deepseek-v4.1-flash` at `high`:
  - Round 1 on b32f0e6 and round 2 on a25c734 both passed with conditions.
  - Every finding is fixed or answered in the comments.
  - Round 3, a delta review of `a25c734..` the head, will run once the targeting bindings are in.

## Not yet verified
- **Round 3 review** of the thumb buttons, the N1 fix and the targeting bindings.
- **The `Game1` glue** (the throttle reset call, the strafe bits and the ripcord and chaff edges): checked by reading only, with no test.
- **ragesaq's flight test on the HOTAS:** the acceptance step.
- **Linux CI `build-and-test`:** runs after the retarget to `master`.

body:
A new eighth track, **Symmetry** (olive), with its first lab, **The 230 Space Groups** (`labs/space-groups/`).

## The lab
- **Tab 1, the operations:** pick any of the 230 groups by number (or a famous one). Every operation is classified from det W and tr W as rotation, screw, inversion, mirror, glide or rotoinversion, with its axis or plane, its screw or glide part and its location in International Tables notation.
  - Selecting an operation shows its element in a 3D cell you can rotate. By default every copy of a handed object moves together with the cell, as one rigid block; a switch shows a single object or the copies alone.
  - Screws and glides play in two steps, the turn or reflection and then the slide, with captions and an arrow. Selecting a screw stands its axis upright.
  - Also shown: the point group as a stereogram, and the selected operation as a matrix.
- **Tab 2, the diagram:** the International Tables view looking down c, with general positions labelled by height (commas for mirror images) and symmetry-element symbols.
- **Tab 3, building crystals:** 14 materials (rock salt, CsCl, diamond, GaAs, fluorite, SrTiO₃, graphite, hBN, MoS₂, GaN, rutile, α-quartz, Bi₂Se₃, black phosphorus) generated from their Wyckoff positions. Any operation can be applied to the whole cell.
- 8 predict-first questions, and a notebook (spglib) that asserts every quoted number.

## Data and checks
- `data.js`: all 230 groups from gemmi, in the standard settings (unique axis b, origin choice 2 where there are two, hexagonal axes for R groups). The five orthorhombic groups whose symbols changed in 2002 are shown by their current symbols.
- An independent Python check confirmed all 2609 operations' types, intrinsic parts and locations. It also confirmed that every screw and glide in every Hermann–Mauguin symbol appears in its group, and that exactly 73 groups are symmorphic.
- The crystals' atom counts and bond lengths match published values.
- Playwright: no errors or NaN across all 230 groups in every tab; phone layout without horizontal scroll; every operation animated in all three modes.
- The smoke test passes on all 23 labs.
