body:
## Summary On phones the project-card Rubik cube ignores the first tap: it stays scrambled, solves on the second tap, rescrambles on the third. Now the first tap solves it. **Root cause** (`assets/js/rubik-cube.js`): a touch tap fires a compatibility `mouseenter` before `click`. The hover handler set `desiredMode = "solved"`, then the click handler saw "solved" and toggled straight back to scrambled. Proof: with only `mouseenter` suppressed on `master`, the same first tap solves the cube. **Fix:** hover is handled by `pointerenter`/`pointerleave` limited to `pointerType === "mouse"`, so touch activation goes only through the existing `click` handler. The click "lock" that blocks hover from re-solving is set only for mouse clicks. Desktop hover and click work as before. ![Before: still scrambled after first tap | After: solved on first tap](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..8YhuvWfKciacsoMNtS90GXYkcdNyBEV8J61qpu57F-w) ## Evidence Playwright on Chromium with the iPhone 13 touch profile against local Jekyll: ```text master: first tap -> Expected /\bis-solved\b/, Received "project-icon js-rubik-stage is-unsolved" (exit=1) fix: Touch passes: tap 1 solved, tap 2 scrambled, tap 3 solved. (also with reduced motion) fix: Desktop passes: hover solves, leave rescrambles, click cycles the scramble and solves again, re-entry solves. ``` **Try it:** `bundle exec jekyll serve --port 4000`, then open http://localhost:4000/projects/ in DevTools device mode and tap the cube. author: easingthemes
body:
A tool that starts a coordinator skill (a dashboard, a script, a hub) still had to guess: it matched a result to its run by time, hardcoded which progress file each skill writes, saw nothing while a run was going, and lost every run but the latest per id. This adds what it needs to stop guessing. All additive: schema stays `1`, readers that ignore unknown fields keep working.

## Changes
1. **Running marker**: `run-result.sh --start` writes `.ai/run-results/<skill>-<id>.running.json` (`status: running`, `started_at`, `run_id`, `progress_file`, `spec_dir`). The final write removes it, so a marker left after the session ended = interrupted run. Its name does not match `<skill>-<id>.json`, so existing readers skip it.
2. **Run id**: `run_id` from `--run-id`, else `DX_RUN_ID` in the environment, else the marker's. Validated to `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}`, anything else becomes `null` with a warning. The caller sets `DX_RUN_ID` and finds its own run.
3. **Duration**: the final result carries `started_at` over from the marker and adds `duration_s` (`null` without a marker). Portable date parsing (GNU and BSD `date`).
4. **History**: every final write is appended as one line to `.ai/run-results/history.jsonl`, trimmed to the last 1000 lines once past 2000 (`DX_RUN_HISTORY_MAX` / `_KEEP`).
5. **Skills**: `dx-agent-all`, `dx-bug-all` (local mode), `dx-prep` and `dx-pr-review` call `--start` right after parsing the id, with their progress file name (`dev-all-progress.md`, `bug-progress.md`, `req-progress.md`; none for review).
6. **Hub**: `dx-hub-dispatch` on the `copilot` engine starts each repo terminal with `DX_RUN_ID=<session id>`, so the repo's run result points back to that terminal.
7. **Docs**: `docs/reference/run-result.md` (new fields, marker, history, `DX_RUN_ID`), `shared/run-result.md` (Start / End), website file table.

## Verification
- `run-result.test.sh`: 42 passed (17 new checks: marker fields, run id from env / flag / marker, invalid id dropped, `--start` with `--status` rejected, duration, marker removed, history append and trim).
- `validate-agents/skills/stats/structure.sh` and every `data/lib` and skill suite pass locally.

author: cozygarage
body:
Proposal for #3910, docs only. It adds a clearly marked **Proposed amendment (not yet accepted)** section to ADR 0005. Nothing in the code changes, and the section says so.

The problem, grounded in the code: `OperationControl` carries one deadline from the connection or global query timeout, and `run_server_cancellable` treats it like a Stop, so a slow UPDATE or ALTER past the read timeout is cancelled mid-flight and can end in an unknown outcome (which disables governed writes, ADR 0056).

The proposed rule: the read deadline applies to reads, chosen by the caller from the policy statement class (writes, DDL and unparsable statements get none); an optional per-connection write timeout only stops waiting and reports an unknown outcome; Stop is unchanged; transactions follow the same split. The section lists consequences and three open questions (unparsable statements, whether the write timeout is needed at all, MCP and agentd limits).

To decide: merge this to accept the direction (the code and the per-engine tests are then separate PRs), or edit the section, or close the PR. #3910 stays open either way.

body: ## Problem `OpenConstructionEstimator.export_estimate` in `5_DDC_Innovative/open-construction-estimate/SKILL.md` writes the estimate table to Excel through pandas and openpyxl. openpyxl gives any string longer than one character that starts with `=` the formula type (`data_type == 'f'`) and writes it as a `` element. Element fields (id, IFC type, description) and matched price-book fields (code, description, unit) come from outside parties. So text in those fields was saved in the Details and By_Type sheets as live formulas. ## Fix A new helper, `store_formulas_as_text(workbook)`, runs on `writer.book` after every sheet has been written and before the workbook is saved. It turns every formula-typed cell back into a literal string cell and sets `quotePrefix` on it, so Excel also keeps the cell as text if someone edits it. The export never writes formulas of its own, so any formula cell must have come from the data. Cell values are kept exactly as they were (no apostrophe is added). Because the fix runs where the workbook is written, it covers every column and sheet, and both the TF-IDF and the embedding match paths. ## Tests [PR #200](https://github.com/FLINT-Builders/DDC_Skills_for_AI_Agents_in_Construction/pull/200) has the tests that prove the fix. They are not part of this PR. Versions: pandas 3.1.1, openpyxl 3.1.5, scikit-learn 1.9.1. - **PR #200 tests on unchanged `main` (ce45bbf):** 2 failed, 1 passed. `test_element_text_is_stored_as_literal_text` failed because Details!A2, B2, C2 and By_Type!A2 were stored as formulas. `test_matched_price_book_text_is_stored_as_literal_text` failed because Details!D2, E2 and G2 were stored as formulas. `test_ordinary_description_exports_as_text` passed. - **PR #200 tests with this fix:** all 3 passed, both on the tests branch and on this branch (pointed at this branch's `SKILL.md`). - **Retry with other payloads:** hyperlink, DDE-style, `=SUM(...)` and `==1` payloads, in every element and price-book text column. Run with both `use_embeddings=False` and the semantic path (using a stub embedder). Each workbook had 0 `` elements in its worksheet XML, every `=` cell came back with type `s`, the text was unchanged, and the totals were correct. - **Smoke export of ordinary data on this branch:** the Summary, Details and By_Type sheets were written with the expected values (total 324 with the `west_us` factor). This repo has no other tests for this skill. ## Still open (not changed here) - `OpenDatabaseManager.export_subset` in the same `SKILL.md` writes price-book rows to CSV with no formula neutralization. A CSV has no cell types, so the only fix is to change the values (for example, add a `'` prefix). author: thiesi
body:
A race on opening a brand-new world, and an admission.

## The admission

#30 was merged with the Windows job red on its last commit. My merge command waited for the checks and then merged whatever they said; it did not stop on a failure. Main has therefore carried a failing check since `82110d4`. The failing test is the one this PR fixes, and the fault it shows is older than #30. From here on the merge is conditional on the checks passing.

## The fault

`test_two_callers_creating_the_world_at_once` failed on Windows with `StoreError: ... is not a Fair Winds world` in one of six processes.

`Store._prepare` read a file's three marks (`application_id`, `user_version`, whether it has tables) one after another, outside any transaction. A caller arriving while another was creating the world could read the first before the creator's commit and the last after it: no application id, but tables. That is exactly what some other program's database looks like, so the world was refused. #30 added a second schema step, which made creation longer and the window wider, but the race was there since S10.

For a real node: two callers reaching a brand-new world at the same instant, and one of them is told the records cannot be read and is sent back to the BBS. Rare, once per world at most, and nothing is damaged; but wrong.

## The fix

The three marks are read inside one read transaction, so a world in the making is seen either not at all or whole.

## Tests

- `test_the_marks_of_a_world_are_read_as_one`: all three reads happen inside one transaction, and none is left open.
- `test_many_callers_creating_many_worlds_at_once`: eight processes create each of four worlds at once.
- The store tests ran three times in a row locally without a failure. The race is timing-dependent, so that is evidence, not proof; the first test is the one that pins the fix.

Local run on Windows: 540 tests, OK, 4 skipped.

author: akp5282-7655004
body:
Cut from `938857c` (main after #80). Owner report, Nov 25, on the live site with credits on the account:

- "figure out some of my competitors" → "There are no competitors on file. You can search the Meta Ad Library… `[Meta Ad Library](https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/)`"
- "do some research based on my zip code" → "The search timed out and I cannot reach results right now."

## Why

Chat had no way to find a competitor. `competitor_research` reads the names the owner typed into the profile. `web_search` and `browser_search` fetch DuckDuckGo's HTML results page from the server with a 6 to 8 second limit; on the live server that timed out. A search-results page fetched from a datacenter is not a dependable source, and this PR does not try to make it one by disguising the request.

## What changes

- **`src/research/localcompetitors.ts` (new).** `findLocalCompetitors({ trade, area, ownName, ownWebsite })` searches `"<trade> near <zip or first place>"` with the Places API (New) Text Search, and falls back to the older Text Search in `places.ts` when the new one refuses the key. It leaves the owner's own business out (same domain or same name), sorts most reviewed first, and returns up to eight: name, rating, review count, address, website. No key, no trade, no area, or a refused key returns a plain note and an empty list. The key is never in the result.
- **`find_local_competitors` chat tool** (read-only), wired in `tools.ts` and `chatReadersFor`. Empty arguments use the profile's trade and zip or service area. Step label: "Finding competitors near you...".
- **Prompt.** For "who are my competitors" and research by city or zip, call `find_local_competitors` first, answer with names, ratings and review counts, and do not send the owner to another site to look. It is also first in the research chain.
- **`plainSpeech`.** `[Name](https://…)` becomes `Name (https://…)`. The chat bubble is plain text, so the brackets were showing.
- **Launch check.** New warning line, "Competitors can be found by city or zip", when `GOOGLE_PLACES_KEY` is not set.
- `places.ts`: `searchCompetitors` takes the caller's `fetch` and has a 6 second limit. Existing callers are unchanged.

## Coordination

| Area | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Chat tools | Added one | `find_local_competitors`. No existing tool changed. `test/chatsnapshot.test.ts` lists the tool names, so it gains the new one. |
| `GOOGLE_PLACES_KEY` | Owner step | Not verified against the real Places API here: there is no key in this environment. Until the key is set on Render, the tool returns the "key is not set" note and Miles says so. |
| Web search | Not changed | `web_search` still fetches DuckDuckGo. It needs an official search API to be dependable; that is a decision for the owner (a free-tier key, or OpenRouter's paid web search). |
| Research feeding the campaign plan | Not in this PR | Gap 1 in #79. This tool is the piece that plan can read competitors from. |

## Tests

`test/localcompetitors.test.ts`, nine cases: the query uses the zip or the first place named; no key looks nothing up; a missing trade or area is asked for; results are sorted, the owner is left out, an unrated business has no made-up rating, and the key is not in the output; the older API is tried when the new one refuses, and both failing is said plainly; the tool is described to the model and passes its arguments; "figure out some of my competitors" through `/api/chat/ask` reaches Places with the profile's trade and zip; a markdown link is rewritten; the launch check line.

Full suite: 158 unit files, 1466 tests pass. Browser: 83 of 84 locally; the one miss is `checklist-rest-d-a11y` on `#modal-x`, which fails the same way on main with my local browser build and passes in CI.

author: matheusborgesdev
body:
Every posted transfer now writes a `transfer.posted` event to `outbox_events` in the same transaction as its ledger entries. Delivery is a separate concern and comes in a follow-up.

- The use case records the event through the ledger port; it has no way to reach the network. A structural test enforces that for the whole application layer.
- The payload is serialized once, so every delivery attempt will send and sign the same bytes. The row id is the event id.
- Database guarantee, both ways: the event references its transfer (no event without a transfer), and a deferred trigger rejects a transfer committed without its event.
- A replayed idempotent request writes nothing, so it produces no second event.
- New role `wallety_dispatch`: reads events and updates delivery state only. It cannot read the ledger or change what an event says.

Tests cover: one event per committed transfer, none for a rejected transfer, none when the transaction rolls back after the event was recorded, none on replay, and each database guarantee through direct SQL. Each guarantee was switched off in the test database to confirm the tests fail without it.

author: buluoray
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** The ssh-to-self and git/tar-to-self checks track a shell variable name
exactly as bash does, so the case of a variable name cannot change which value a
floor reads for it.

The two floors read a command lowercased and resolve a same-line variable
assignment on that lowercased text. Bash variable names are case-sensitive, so
two names that differ only in case are one name to the floors. A command can give
each spelling a different value and have the floor resolve the one bash does not.

## Why it matters

These floors stop an agent from reaching the host it runs on outside the
sandbox, so a reading that does not match bash's is a security weakness. This
change makes the variable-name reading match bash.

## What changed

The floors read the variable name in its submitted case, but only to ADD a
refusal. A reference takes its lowered value -- the value main reads -- unless
the exact-case value names this host, in which case the exact-case value is used.
So the floor refuses a self-dial the lowered read would miss, and the submitted
case can never turn a refusal main makes into an allow, whatever the line's
shape. A nested carried command, which has no submitted copy, keeps the lowered
read.

## Not a goal

- Program-name and host matching keep whatever case folding they already use
  (for example case-insensitive program paths on macOS). Only variable-name
  resolution changes.
- The false match in #42729 (a command with no git or tar refused) is a
  different symptom; it is not fixed here and is tracked by its own follow-up.

## Tests

`test/test_denied_commands_security_self_dial_var_case.py`:

- `test_a_self_dial_hidden_in_a_case_twin_is_refused`: a self-dial that relies on
  two case spellings of one name is refused for ssh, git and tar.
- `test_a_genuine_remote_stays_allowed`: a variable reassigned to a real remote,
  and a remote in the spelling actually used, stay allowed.
- `test_a_single_variable_self_dial_stays_refused`: a plain one-variable
  self-dial stays refused.
- A row per earlier-found shape that must keep its refusal: a non-pure-assignment
  segment, a second command or a builtin that assigns, a non-bash whitespace
  separator, an `IFS` reassignment, a special variable, and a value the parser
  cannot read.
- `test_head_deny_set_is_a_superset_of_mains`: a seeded property check that for
  random lines the submitted-case read refuses whenever the lowered (main) read
  refuses.

The whole security suite (`test/test_denied_commands_security*.py`,
`test/test_deny*.py`, `test/test_security_gate_liveness.py`) passes on this head.

## Verification

Checked by calling `kiro_crew.security.is_denied` only; no candidate command was
executed. Every line main refuses stays refused; on a case-twin self-dial the
submitted-case read adds the refusal main's lowered read missed.

## Related Issues

Part of #42729. This PR hardens the floors; it does not fix the usability false
match that #42729 reports (a separate PR does).

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: a security check that lowercases a whole command and then reasons about
shell variable names, which bash keeps case-sensitive. Reading the exact case can
be made safe without a shell grammar by judging both the lowered and the exact
reading and refusing on either, so the stricter reading only ever adds a refusal.

## Checklist

- [x] A Conventional Commits title
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

author: alexandrec90
body:
Runes had values, charts and ranked offers; nothing else did. Traders pay in Worldstone shards, keys, perfect gems, statues and essences all the time ("an Ist for 20 shards"), and there was no way to tell whether such a trade was fair.

## What changes

- **`goods.py`** values each good against the runes, after the rune model has run: every trade of a good for runes, or of a rune for one kind of good, is one reading of its value in Ist at that day's rune values. A good's readings feed `trend.fit_path`, as forum gold's do. Goods are not added to the joint rune model, so their noisier trades cannot blur rune values. Sales offering alternatives or paid in a mix are left out; a busy day is thinned to 12 readings across its spread, to keep the fit cheap.
- **`deals.py`** reads "20 deep shards + 1 pul" against "an ist", values both sides and returns the gain, its 95% interval and the break-even amount. Under 5% is fair; a gain the interval cannot tell from zero is "too close to call". Ambiguous names ("worldstone shards") list the options.
- **`/currencies`** page: each good charted by family, with its cheapest offers, plus the deal checker.
- **Collection:** a new `goods` job fetches each good's sales, asks and bids from Traderie every `GOODS_POLL_HOURS` (3): about 90 requests a market, so less often than runes. The `rates` job now stores measured goods values too, so watch valuations use them.
- **Runes page:** offers paid in measured goods are now valued; unmeasured goods' seeds are dropped from page valuations instead of being guessed.
- `GOODS_BY_FAMILY` in `currency.py` lists the goods, taken from what rune listings ask for in payment; `display_name` writes "Key of Terror" and "Worusk's End" properly everywhere.

Checked against the live database before landing: Deep shard comes out at 23.5 per Ist, so 20 shards for an Ist is about +18% for the buyer.

author: alphatownsman
body:
## Problem

Since the teal.fm history imports, `record` holds about 3.77M rows (8.5 GB). The server has been hung since 2026-11-19. py-spy showed 28 of 30 samples in `dashboard` calling `collect_stats()`, mostly in `SELECT count(*) FROM record WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. That count reads the whole file. `/` and `/stats` ran it synchronously in `async def` handlers, so each request blocked the event loop: every other request, the Jetstream consumer and delivery.

## What this changes

**1. Stats come from a cache.**
- A background loop recounts the dashboard figures every 5 min in a thread (`stats.refresh_stats`, `stats_refresh_loop`). `/` and `/stats` only read the cache.
- Each query in that pass reads an index or a small table.
- `records_active` needs a full pass over `record`. It is now counted in the existing 6 h usage pass, in the same scan that `active_month` already did.
- `last_event_at` stays live.

**2. No route queries the database on the event loop.**
- Routes that read the database are now plain `def`, so FastAPI runs them on its thread pool.
- Routes that must stay `async` (they await other work or create a task) send their database calls to `run_in_threadpool`.
- `/robots.txt`, nodeinfo, `/` and `/stats` stay `async` and run no query.
- The connection pool grows from 5 + 10 to 10 + 70 connections, to cover the thread pool.

**3. Public pages are bounded.**
- **Two new partial indexes** over the published, live Notes: `ix_record_author_posts (did, created_at)` and `ix_record_work_posts (work_key, created_at)`. The profile list, outbox, post count, catalog list and rating average each walk one of them.
- **The index is pinned** with `INDEXED BY`. SQLite's statistics hold one average per index, and the skew misleads the planner: published Notes cluster on popular works, so the partial index can look wider than `ix_record_work_key`. The planner then reads every row of the album. SQLAlchemy's SQLite compiler drops table hints, so `db._HintingCompiler` renders them, as the MySQL and MSSQL compilers already do.
- **The rating average** is cached per work for up to 10 min. Concurrent misses wait for one count, because a delivered Note brings a burst of link-preview fetches for the same catalog page. The cache key includes the work's Note count and newest Note, read from the index alone, so a retraction or opt-out drops out at once.
- **`/users/{ident}/posts/{rkey}`** finds the record by primary key, `at://did/<collection>/rkey`, once for each collection in the archive. The collections come from a recursive skip-scan of `ix_record_collection`. Before, `did = ? AND rkey = ?` read every row of the author. When two collections hold the rkey (a teal.fm tracker copying plays off the alpha namespace), the copy that holds the Note wins.
- **`/users/{ident}`** skips the post count for ActivityPub fetches.
- **The teal.fm holder lookup** is pinned to `ix_record_play_holder`. A database without statistics otherwise uses `ix_record_play_session` and walks the whole session for each play.

**4. Planner statistics are refreshed at startup only.**
- `PRAGMA optimize` only considers tables that queries on the same connection have used. It ran on a fresh pooled connection, so `sqlite_stat1` still said 356k rows.
- At server startup (the lifespan's `init_db(refresh_stats=True)`), `ANALYZE` runs on tables whose row count moved more than 2x from `sqlite_stat1`. The check is one `max(rowid)` seek per table.
- CLI commands skip that pass, because they can run beside a live server. A table that just got a new index is analyzed in every case.
- The daily loop is gone. Even with `analysis_limit`, `ANALYZE` walks every index in full while it holds the write lock: 1.6 s for one index of a 1M-row table, cold. Ingestion still writes from the event loop, so a pass beside it would stall every request.

**5. `compose.yml`:** the healthcheck calls `/robots.txt`.

## Deploy notes (read before merge)

- **First boot builds two indexes on `record`.**
  - Each build is one full pass over the 8.5 GB table, then `record` is analyzed.
  - Expect a few minutes before HTTP answers. At the observed 156 MB/s that is roughly 1 min per index uncached.
  - The log shows `building index ...` and `built index ... in Ns`.
  - The build runs before ingestion starts, so no event is lost. The Jetstream cursor resumes after it.
  - Do not restart the container during the build. The healthcheck `start_period` is 10 s, so Docker can mark the container unhealthy during this boot. That does not restart it.
- **Later boots** build nothing, and analyze only if a table has doubled or halved.
- **Deploy the server before you run any CLI command with the new image.** A CLI `init_db` would otherwise build the two indexes on the live database.
- **Rollback** to the previous image is safe. Old code ignores the extra indexes.

## Behaviour changes

- **`/stats`:**
  - Same keys as before, plus `stats_updated_at`.
  - Counts are `null` until the first refresh after a restart. The dashboard shows "...".
  - `records_active` is `null` until the first usage pass finishes (one full scan after startup), then up to 6 h old.
- **`/users/{ident}/outbox`:** now paged. The collection embeds its first `OrderedCollectionPage` (100 ids) under `first`, and `next` leads on with a `max_id` rowid cursor. `orderedItems` is no longer at the top level.
- **`/archive`:** lists by insertion order, not `updated_at`. `updated_at` has no index, so every request sorted the whole table. `?q=` searches only the newest 50,000 records, and the page says so.
- **Admin "Start import":** a lock covers the running check, the job row and the start. Two submissions can no longer queue two metered downloads. Cancel now marks only the job its task runs.
- **`/catalog`:** lists by `rowid`. `first_seen` is only ever its insert-time default, so the order does not change.

## Not in this PR

- **Ingest database work on the loop (point 4)**, deferred by agreement. Five routes still query on the loop through code they await, not in the route itself:
  - `POST /inbox`, `POST /actor/inbox`, `POST /users/{ident}/inbox` (`handle_inbox`)
  - `POST /manage/opt-out` (the opt-out purge)
  - `GET /oauth/callback` (the fanout of a refreshed profile)

  `tests/test_event_loop.py` lists these as known exceptions. The same code also runs for every ingested event.
- **Point 7**, not relaying very old teal.fm plays: a product decision, not taken here.

## Benchmark

**Setup.** File database at about quarter scale:
- 1.06M `record` rows (2.2 GB)
- one author with 700k plays and 34k Notes
- one album with 10k plays and 1,060 Notes
- `sqlite_stat1` taken at 350k rows

macOS with 32 GB RAM, so the OS cache was warm. Timings understate production's cold reads; the plans are what carry over.

| Endpoint | 9bb39bd | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | 491 ms, `SCAN record` | 5 ms (cache) |
| `/stats` | 479 ms, `SCAN record` | 0.8 ms (cache) |
| `/users/heavy` (HTML) | 88 ms, sorts 34k rows | 15 ms |
| `/users/heavy/outbox` | 302 ms, sorts and parses 34k Notes | 5 ms (first page) |
| `/users/heavy/posts/{rkey}` | 219 ms | 7 ms |
| `/users/heavy/posts/missing` | 211 ms | 1.3 ms |
| `/catalog/album/mb-popular` | 59 ms, sorts 10k rows | 51 ms (100 rows, plus the rating average once) |
| `/catalog` | 88 ms, sorts all works | 5 ms |
| `/archive` | 2,844 ms, sorts the whole table | 30 ms |
| `/archive?q=` | 1,324 ms, full LIKE scan | 29 ms |

**Loop blocking.** `/robots.txt` sent together with `/` waited 483 ms before, and 0.7 ms after. Sent with `/archive`, it waited 2,863 ms before, and 0.5 ms after.

**Startup on this database:**
- index builds: 4.9 s + 0.5 s
- `ANALYZE record` after the build: 0.1 s, with pages still warm from the build. On a cold copy, `ANALYZE` took 7.6 s and held off a concurrent write for all of it, so it never runs beside ingestion.
- background passes: stats 0.28 s, usage 0.53 s

**Production base image:** `python:3.13-slim` ships SQLite 3.46.1. It supports

author: lucacappelletti94
body: PostgreSQL checks only the `TRUNCATE` privilege and fires no row trigger for the rows a `TRUNCATE` removes. The replica emptied the tables with plain deletes. The guards holding the acting role to its `DELETE` grant and its policies refused them, and they fired every row `DELETE` trigger, as well as the `UPDATE` triggers a self-referencing `SET NULL` or `SET DEFAULT` key reaches. The deletes now run under a `pg_truncate` frame on the definer stack. The guards of a table the acting role or a definer owner may truncate let them through while that frame is innermost, and the row triggers a truncation can fire hold only outside it. In a trigger body the `TRUNCATE` pushes, deletes and pops in line. A `TRUNCATE` of its own runs the three in a temporary trigger that one insert fires, so a failing delete takes the frame with it. A batch that renames a table or a column, or drops a column, first drops what a failed `TRUNCATE` left, since SQLite refuses those while a trigger names a table that is gone.

author: edzondev
body:
## Por qué

Compromisos en el móvil deja los datos de ejemplo y lee y escribe en Convex con las reglas de la web y el diseño Android (F1, F2, F3 y O5). Es el PR B1; Ahorros y la edición desde Movimientos van en B2.

## Lo que pedí

- **Lista (F1, O5):** `commitments.list` con `useEnsureOpen(space, today)`, `useSuspenseQueries` y `LoadBoundary` (skeleton y «No pudimos cargar tus compromisos.» con «Reintentar»). Se quitó `SAMPLE_COMMITMENTS` de `home/sample.ts`. `SAMPLE_TODAY` y `SAMPLE_HOME` se quedan: los usan Ajustes, Plus y Progreso.
- **Nuevo y editar (F2):** «Cada mes | Una vez». «Vence» tiene las 4 reglas de la web en chips (Un día fijo, El último día del mes, Días antes del fin, En quincena (el 15)) y la línea «Este mes vence el …». «Una vez» abre el `DateTimePicker` de `@expo/ui`, que ya estaba instalado, desde hoy en adelante. Los errores de la web salen bajo cada campo desde el primer «Guardar».
- **Marcar pagado (F3):** monto editable, «Se registra un movimiento en {sobre}.» y `markPaid { amountCents }`. Quién puede pagar es `canPay` de la web: también Reservado y un «una vez» de Más adelante.
- **Tocar la fila** abre el compromiso en la hoja de editar («Editar compromiso» y «Guardar cambios»), con las acciones dentro, como la hoja de editar de Registrar:
  - «Este mes vence… › Día N», solo en mensuales: la lista de los días del mes del cargo, también los pasados. Se guarda al elegir y vuelve al formulario sin perder lo escrito.
  - «Borrar compromiso» en ámbar bajo el botón: confirmación en la misma hoja.
  - Un compromiso pagado no se edita (la web oculta «Editar»): se ve su nombre, «Pagado el …», el monto, «Este mes vence…» y «Borrar compromiso».
  - Los textos son los de la web.
- **«Volver al N»** bajo la fila cuando este mes se movió a mano (`clearDueThisMonth`).
- **Guardias:**
  - Personal sin plan: `<EmptyPersonal />`, sin abrir ciclo.
  - Nuestro espacio sin Plus: cada escritura abre `/plus?feature=space`, igual que `useReadOnlyGate`.
  - El cuerpo lleva `key={space-today}`: un cambio de espacio o de día cierra la hoja abierta.
- **Sin toasts:** vibra (`Success`) solo después de que la mutación responde bien. Doble toque: `lib/use-single-flight.ts`.
- **Shared:** `canPay`, `ruleDay`, `isAdjusted` y `dueMonthTitle` pasaron de `apps/web/.../commitment-view.ts` a `packages/backend/shared/commitments.ts`. La web los importa de ahí; su comportamiento no cambia.
- **`use-single-flight.ts`:** solo el `ref`. Lo usan `use-movement-actions.ts` y `use-commitment-actions.ts`. Queda anotado en `mobile.md` #16 por qué se permite.
- **`leer-w.mjs`:** corta en `class="scr"` exacto. Antes cortaba en `class="scrim"` y las hojas (F2, F3, G3–G7) salían vacías.

## Lo que agregué

- `dueMonthText` («Solo cambia noviembre. En diciembre vuelve al 28.») también pasó a `shared`. El móvil lo necesita en «Este mes vence…» y así no se copia.
- **Hoja y teclado:** `components/ui/bottom-sheet.tsx` aplica en Android el modifier `imePadding()` de `@expo/ui` (ya instalado), y la hoja sube con el teclado. `react-native-keyboard-controller` no sirve aquí: solo sigue el teclado de la ventana principal y del `Modal` de React Native (`ModalAttachedWatcher` escucha `topShow` de `ReactModalHostView`). La hoja de `@expo/ui` es otra ventana de Compose. Arregla también Registrar, la limitación del 19 nov.
- `components/ui/option-list.tsx`: la lista con scroll que vivía dentro de `DayList`, sacada para reusarla en «Día del mes», «Días antes del fin» y «Este mes vence…». `DayList` la usa sin cambiar lo que pinta.

## Qué cambia

- `packages/backend/shared/commitments.ts`: añade `canPay`, `ruleDay`, `isAdjusted`, `dueMonthTitle` y `dueMonthText`.
- `apps/web/src/modules/commitments/{commitment-view.ts, components/commitment-row.tsx, components/commitment-menu.tsx}`: solo imports.
- `apps/mobile/src/features/commitments/`:
  - `commitments-screen.tsx`: datos reales, guardias y una sola hoja que cambia de contenido.
  - `commitment-row.tsx`: toque, enlace de pago y `below`.
  - `commitment-text.ts`: `payLabel` con `canPay`, `payHeading` y `backToRuleLabel`.
  - Nuevos: `commitment-form.ts` (lógica pura del formulario), `commitment-sheet.tsx` (F2: nuevo, y editar con sus acciones), `pay-sheet.tsx` (F3), `paid-sheet.tsx` (compromiso pagado), `commitment-actions.tsx` («Este mes vence…» y borrar) y `use-commitment-actions.ts`.
- `apps/mobile/src/lib/use-single-flight.ts` (nuevo) y `features/register/use-movement-actions.ts`, que ahora lo usa.
- `apps/mobile/src/components/ui/option-list.tsx` (nuevo) y `features/cycle/day-list.tsx`.
- `apps/mobile/src/features/home/sample.ts`: sin `SAMPLE_COMMITMENTS`.
- `.claude/rules/mobile.md` (#16) y `.claude/skills/quipu-pantalla/leer-w.mjs`.

## Fuera de este PR

- B2: Ahorros (fondo, metas, aportar, retirar, meta del fondo) y editar o borrar ahorros y retiros desde Movimientos.
- Tarjeta (F4–F6) y En cuotas: no existen en el backend.
- Deslizar la fila para pagar.
- La línea «Hoy: X → Y» de F2: la web no la tiene.
- PR C a F.
- Los 4 pendientes del PR 120 y la limpieza de Convex.
- Ya estaba en `master`: la lista pinta con `.map` dentro de un `ScrollView`. El tope es de 100 compromisos; pasar a `SectionList` si alguien llega a más de unos 20.

## Checks

| Comando | Salida |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm typecheck` (backend, móvil y web) | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter web typecheck` (por el cambio de imports) | 0 |
| `pnpm lint` | 0 (2 avisos viejos en `convex/auth.ts`) |
| `pnpm --filter mobile test` | 0 · 97 tests en 6 archivos |
| `pnpm --filter @quipu/backend test` | 0 · 693 tests. La primera corrida dio 1: 4 tests de billing y migración superaron los 20 s. Al repetirlos solos pasaron 47 de 47 y la suite completa pasó |
| `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo export --platform android` | 0 · bundle de 7.4 MB |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt <archivos tocados>` | 0 |
| e2e | no corrido, diferido al final del proyecto |

**Cada regla nueva, rota a propósito:** se cambió la línea, se corrió `pnpm --filter mobile test` y se devolvió el archivo. Las 12 fallaron:

- `canPay`: pagar un «una vez» de Más adelante.
- `isAdjusted`: el ajuste es del mes del cargo.
- `ruleDay`: ignora el ajuste.
- `payLabel`: el texto de vencido.
- `payHeading`: «vencía» o «vence».
- `backToRuleLabel`: depende de `isAdjusted`.
- `commitmentFields`, cuatro casos: la fecha de un «una vez», el nombre recortado, el monto mayor que 0 y las reglas fuera de rango.
- `thisMonthLine`: sigue el ajuste del mes.
- `monthDayOptions`: los días que tiene el mes.
- `ruleAmountOptions`: «1 día».

## Verificación

Pendiente de Edzon en el dispositivo (Android, tema claro y oscuro, fuente del sistema al máximo, 360 dp):

1. **Personal con plan y sin compromisos:** sale O5. «Añadir compromiso» abre F2.
2. **F2 «Cada mes»:**
   - «Guardar compromiso» vacío muestra los 3 errores en ámbar, y se van al corregir.
   - Probar cada regla. «Día del mes» y «Días antes del fin» abren su lista con scroll dentro de la hoja.
   - La línea «Este mes vence el …» cambia con la regla.
   - Guardar: vibra, la hoja se cierra y la fila aparece.
3. **F2 «Una vez»:**
   - «Vence › Fecha» abre el calendario por encima de la hoja (primera vez dentro de una hoja: mirar que abra y que al elegir se cierre).
   - No deja días pasados.
4. **Teclado en la hoja:** con el teclado abierto en «Nombre» o en el monto, la hoja sube y «Guardar compromiso» se ve. Lo mismo en Registrar. Al cerrar el teclado, la hoja baja sin dejar un hueco.
5. **«Marcar pagado»:**
   - Aparece en Vencido (texto «Vencido · marcar pagado», ámbar), Próximo, Reservado y en un «una vez» de Más adelante. No aparece en un mensual de Más adelante.
   - F3 trae el monto. Cambiarlo a 0 apaga el botón.
   - Pagar: vibra y la fila pasa a Pagado. En Movimientos aparece un gasto nuevo en su sobre.
6. **Tocar una fila:**
   - Abre el compromiso con sus datos (un compromiso de la web con «último día» sigue así al guardar).
   - Cambiar el nombre y luego abrir «Este mes vence…»: la lista mue

body:
Closes #1738

## Why

「第2四半期（累計）の業績予想と実績値との差異に関するお知らせ」を、J-Quants は `EarnForecastRevision`・`CurPerType=FY`（年度末はいまの年度）の行にし、通期予想の欄に同じ日の 2Q 決算短信の累計の実績を入れている。共通の層（`forecast_points`）が通期の予想修正として読むので、次の決算短信まで、株価チャートの予想 EPS・概要の予想 PER・決算速報の修正履歴が実績の値になる。

94750（昭文社HD）はいまも続いている。2026-11-06 の `20261106567318` の通期予想の欄が売上 3,112・純利益 △148・EPS △8.26（2Q の実績）で、本当の通期予想は純利益 360・EPS 19.87。決算速報の詳細の累計の表は、開いている 2Q 短信の行の予想の欄を読むので 19.87 のまま、修正履歴だけ △8.26 になって食い違って見える。

## What

`config/market/statement_period_fixes.json` に次の 5 本を `"drop": true` と根拠付きで載せた。コードは変えていない（テストの件数だけ直した）。

| 銘柄 | 開示日 | 予想修正の行 | 同じ日の 2Q 決算短信 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 52680 | 2021-11-10 | 20211108427905 | 20211108427766 |
| 31360 | 2021-11-12 | 20211103423905 | 20211111432360 |
| 60590 | 2023-11-10 | 20231109583979 | 20231109583548 |
| 54910 | 2025-10-31 | 20251028580424 | 20251030583449 |
| 94750 | 2026-11-06 | 20261106567318 | 20261029558745 |

5 本とも、値のある欄は通期予想の欄（と 54910 の非連結の欄）に入った 2Q の実績だけで、配当予想や取り下げの印は無い。捨てて失う情報は無い。同じ日に 2Q の決算短信があるので、決算発表後のパフォーマンスの起点も変わらない。

本決算の日に出た同じ形の行（104 本）は、終わった年度の予想修正なので KAB-566 で予想に使っていない。載せていない。

## 本番での手順（人が流す）

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m tools.market.fix_statement_periods          # 書かない。この 5 本が drop、要約行は drop=5
.venv/bin/python -m tools.market.fix_statement_periods --write
```

## 確かめたこと

- `python -m pytest tests -q`: 2111 passed, 5 skipped

author: jaredwray
body:
## Summary

Snooze replaces Reply later in Mail. A snooze takes a conversation out of the inbox until a date and a time that the person picks. At that time, the conversation comes back to the top of the inbox.

No GitHub issue: the maintainer asked for this change in a session.

## What changed

**Contracts**

- The system label `SNOOZED` replaces `REPLY_LATER`.
- The new operation `mail.snooze_threads` takes `thread_ids` and `until`. It needs `mail.modify`.
- `ThreadSummary` and `Thread` have `snoozed_until`.
- `mail.modify_threads` cannot add `SNOOZED`, because a snooze needs a time. It can remove `SNOOZED`, and the time goes with the label.
- `in:snoozed` replaces `in:reply_later` in the search.

**Mailbox object**

- Migration 8 puts each thread of Reply later back at the top of the inbox, removes `REPLY_LATER`, and adds `threads.snoozed_until` and `threads.woke_at`.
- The alarm of the mailbox ends each snooze at its time: the thread loses `SNOOZED` and gets `INBOX`.
- A list has the order of the newest message that matches. A thread whose snooze ended at its time has the place of that time, so it shows at the top of the inbox.
- New mail in the inbox ends the snooze of its thread. A reply that the mailbox sends does not end it.

**Web app**

- **Snooze** in the toolbar opens a list of times under the button: **In 3 hours**, **Tomorrow** and **Next week**. One more click snoozes.
- The last option of the list, **Pick a date and time…**, opens a dialog with a field for a date and a time. The `b` key opens the dialog too.
- The sidebar shows **Snoozed** with a count. A row of a snoozed conversation shows its time.
- **Unsnooze** puts a conversation back in the inbox. Its Undo snoozes the conversation again until the time that it had.
- Focus has **Snooze** in the place of **Later**. Focus also works in the Snoozed list.

**Design decisions**

- The feature follows the snooze of Gmail: new mail ends a snooze, and a reply does not.
- A thread of Reply later has no time. So the migration puts it back at the top of the inbox, where the person sees it.
- The path `/mail/reply-later`, the query `in:reply_later` and the label id `REPLY_LATER` are gone, with no redirect. A stored call of an agent that uses them fails. The release notes must say so.
- The key changes from `l` to `b`, the key of Gmail for a snooze.
- The pile at the end of the inbox and the banner of the Reply later list are gone. Snoozed mail stays out of sight until its time.
- A thread that comes back sends no webhook event, because it is not new mail. The module README lists this event as not built.

## How it was verified

- `pnpm verify` is green on the head commit: 1777 tests pass, and lint, types, build, budgets, deploy dry run, spike builds and the license check pass.
- New workerd tests in `apps/dock/test/mail-ops.test.ts`: a snooze, a change of the time through the MCP tool, the time of the alarm, the alarm before and at the time, the place at the top of the inbox, a page cursor after that, the alarm after a restart, the end of a snooze by new mail, by a removed label and by a send to the mailbox itself, a reply that keeps the snooze, a merge of a snoozed thread, the refusals, and migration 8.
- I removed the code of two contracts for a moment (the alarm after a restart, and the snooze time of a merge). The two tests for them failed, and they pass with the code.
- `pnpm e2e` for `tests/snooze.spec.ts`: the 5 tests pass two times in a row against the built Worker in `wrangler dev`.
- I examined the Snooze list, the dialog and the Snoozed list in screenshots at desktop width and at 390px.

**Test audit**

- Deleted: `removes REPLY_LATER from the thread of a reply, and not for a forward or a new message` (`mail-send.test.ts`). The contract is gone: a reply does not change a snooze. The new test `ends a snooze for new mail in the thread and for a removed label, and keeps it after a reply` proves the new contract.
- Rewrote: the `Reply later` tests in `mail-ops.test.ts` and `team-mailboxes.test.ts` are now the `Snooze` tests, because the label and its rules changed.
- Rewrote: the first e2e test of `replyLater.spec.ts` is now two tests in `snooze.spec.ts`. The first covers Snooze. The second keeps each Focus check of the old test, in Starred.
- Changed for setup only: the three tests that put the schema of a mailbox back (`mail-screener`, `mail-recipients`, `mail-ops`) also remove the snooze columns. A column cannot be added two times.
- Kept after the gate: `apps/web/test/snooze.test.ts` (the times of the dialog and the date field) and the two undo tests in `actions.test.ts`.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Goal met
- [x] Tests: unit, workerd integration and e2e
- [x] Parity: `mail.snooze_threads` is in contracts, the tests call it through REST and MCP, and the UI uses it
- [x] Authorization: a person in the own mailbox and in a team mailbox (allow), an agent in a team mailbox without `mail.modify` (deny, REST and MCP), an owner and an admin in the mailbox of an agent (deny). No test of a delegated token: the scope check is the shared check of each `mail.modify` operation
- [x] Audit + domain events: each call writes an audit line. No domain event (see the design decisions)
- [x] Data inventory: the Snooze row in the README of the mail module. No blob
- [x] Idempotency: a second call with the same time changes nothing, and the alarm ends a snooze one time
- [x] Agent safety: no new content in the output. No `dry_run`: a snooze is not destructive, and `mail.modify_threads` ends it
- [ ] Observability: logs + metrics. N/A: the audit line only, no new metric
- [x] Security: the input schema checks the ids and the time, and the object refuses a time that is not later than now. No new surface in the threat model
- [x] UI quality: a labelled dialog with keyboard focus, an error state, and a narrow layout
- [x] Docs: the root README, the READMEs of the mail module, the web app and e2e, and `docs/agents.md`
- [x] `pnpm verify` green

## Review

impl-reviewer verdict: **approve**, with no blocking finding. It reviewed the first two commits.

- Fixed: the tests that it asked for (the alarm after a restart, the time of the alarm, the page cursor, a send to the mailbox itself, a merge).
- Fixed: the alarm reads the next snooze time from the index, not from a scan of `threads`.
- Fixed: migration 8 puts the threads of Reply later at the top of the inbox, and the version of the mailbox grows.
- Fixed: the undo of Unsnooze skips a thread whose time the page does not know.
- Fixed: the e2e test does not fail at midnight, and the Snooze list keeps the time that it showed when the day changes before the click.
- Not changed: a conversation that comes back during the same visit of Focus does not show again in that visit. It shows in the inbox list and in the next visit. This needs a follow-up issue.
- Not changed: no `try` around `wakeSnoozed`. Only a storage failure makes it throw, and the drains fail then too.
- Not changed: no second refusal of `SNOOZED` in `modifyThreads`. The input schema refuses it, and no other caller can reach the object.
- Not tested: an allow for an agent or a service account. The scope check is the shared check of each `mail.modify` operation.

Aikido left three medium comments on the first push. Each thread has a reply. One is fixed (a new snooze removes the place of an earlier one). Two are design decisions that the README of the mail module now records, and the maintainer decides them.

author: oddurs
body:
## Problem

`horsegirl draw` refused a lens that the card names but this version does not draw (`show matrix`) with a line of prose and no code. With `--json` that line was not a JSON object.

## Approach

- New code `E0302` in the catalogue (`codes.rs`), with rows in `docs/diagnostics.md` (generated) and `docs/reference.md`.
- `picture` returns a `Diagnostic` whose span is the lens name on the first `show` line. `draw` prints it through `report`, so the text form and `--json` follow the same path as every other diagnostic.
- The MCP `draw` tool maps the diagnostic to its message, so its error text is unchanged.
- No new dependency.

## Evidence

- `printf 'A -> B\nshow matrix\n' | horsegirl draw --json` printed one JSON line with `"code":"E0302"` and span 2:6 to 2:12. Standard output was empty.
- `scripts/task check` passed.
- New CLI test for the JSON form. The text-form test now checks the code, the span and the lens list.

## Where it is weakest

- E0302 is raised in `draw`, not in `check`. `check` still accepts `show matrix`, by design: the card names the lens. So `check` and `draw` can disagree on a clean file.
- The MCP `draw` tool still returns this refusal as an `isError` text, not as a diagnostic in its result. Changing that is a change of the tool contract, so I left it.
- Only the first `show` line is looked at, as before.

author: miguelhang
body:
Closes #86

## What changed
- After `Send` or `Retry`, the chat thread goes to its end, even when you were reading higher up. `Edit` does not count as a send.
- When an agent's message arrives, or grows, as the last entry while the thread is at its end (48 px margin), its start lands just under the sticky bar. A short message shows whole at the end. The thread never goes past the end and never back up.
- Reading higher up: an arriving answer does not move the thread. Opening a chat still goes to the end.
- The rules are in `src/lib/thread.ts`. `NavBar` hands its element to `Thread` through `ChatHeader` and `Agent`, to measure under it.

author: kotekompotek
body:
Fixes #2401.

In D3D12, `ID3D12Device::CreateDescriptorHeap` with `ppvHeap == NULL` is the documented parameter-validation call – the PC answers `S_FALSE` (`1`, which satisfies `hr >= 0`) and writes nothing. `dev_create_descriptor_heap_x` checked only `hr >= 0` and then read `*ppv` to register the heap's console bookkeeping: a NULL `ppv` (or a `*ppv` the PC left NULL) is a null-pointer read the moment the call "succeeds".

**What is in it**
- `hle/d3d12x/real.rs`: the heap-registration block now runs under `hr >= 0 && !ppv.is_null() && !(*ppv).is_null()` – the same guard the `creator!` macro and the other `_x` methods already apply. The HRESULT passes through untouched either way.
- `create_descriptor_heap_x_tests`: a fake adopted device (CLASSES entry + ext vtable stub, as `adopt()` records them) whose PC-side `CreateDescriptorHeap` answers `S_FALSE`. Calling `dev_create_descriptor_heap_x` with `ppv == NULL`, and with an out pointer the PC left NULL, returns `S_FALSE` instead of dereferencing it; the test aborts on the null read when the guard is reverted (checked).

**Tested**
- hardware (GPU + driver, CPU), Rust version, debug / release: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 (driver supports up to SM 6.5, no mesh shaders), DXC 1.8.2502.11 (10.0.26100.0), rustc 1.98.1 stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc; debug tests, release smoke builds
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` on the head commit: 1421 passed, 3 failed, 46 ignored (SKIPPED GPU tests: 355 – this adapter has no SM 6.6 / mesh shaders)
- the three lib failures are environmental on this machine, unrelated to the change: `gpu_retire_queue_holds_heap_until_blocked_queue_passes_mark` (driver refuses a sparse heap op, HRESULT 0x80070057), `stale_blob_cannot_bypass_the_offline_pipeline_cap` and `split_compute_program_prebuilds_and_caches_chain_pieces` (both build/dispatch cs_6_6, which this SM 6.5 adapter cannot run; the latter is a new upstream test with no capability gate)
- `a_null_ppv_validation_call_passes_the_pc_answer_through` aborts with a null-pointer dereference when the fix is reverted (checked by restoring `if hr >= 0`)

**Regression run**

The blocks above end it through `XCL_RUN_SECONDS=0` before that point – they cover host boot, game loading and shutdown, no frames, no shaders.
